examples.zh: 作为记录，我想澄清我同事之前所说的一些事情。

senses.def: used to emphasize a point that you are making, so that the person you are speaking to takes notice

examples.en: And, for the record, he would be the last person I'd ask.
examples.zh: 需要强调的是，他是我最不愿意去找的人。

senses.def: for no particular reason

examples.en: Don't get married just for the sake of it.
examples.zh: 不要为结婚而结婚。

senses.def: because of the possibility of something happening

examples.en: You'd better take the keys in case I'm out.
examples.zh: 你最好带上钥匙以防我不在家。

examples.en: You probably won't need to call—but take my number, just in case.
examples.zh: 你很可能无需打电话，不过还是记下我的电话号码吧，以防万一。

examples.en: In case (= if it is true that) you’re wondering why Jo’s here—let me explain…
examples.zh: 我来解释一下吧，免得你奇怪乔为什么在这儿。

senses.def: used to say that you do not want to discuss or think about something bad or unpleasant that has happened, but just accept it
senses.zh: 命中注定的事；难免的倒霉事；不可挽回的事

examples.en: It wasn't your fault. It was just one of those things.
examples.zh: 不是你的错。这是命中注定的事。

senses.def: used to emphasize a threat, warning or promise
senses.zh: （用以加强威胁、警告或允诺的语气）你就等着吧，你就等着瞧

examples.en: I'll be famous one day, just you wait!
examples.zh: 我有朝一日会出名的，你就等着瞧吧！

senses.def: locked up safely somewhere; in prison
senses.zh: 把…安全地锁起来；在押；被囚禁

examples.en: We keep our valuables under lock and key.
examples.zh: 我们把贵重物品锁起来收好了。

examples.en: I will not rest until the murderer is under lock and key.
examples.zh: 杀人凶手一天不关起来我一天不罢休。

examples.en: Prisoners are kept under lock and key 24 hours a day.
examples.zh: 囚犯一天 24 小时都被关押着。

(keep something/put something/be) under.word: (keep something/put something/be) under lock and key

(keep sth/put sth/be) under lock and key: @@@LINK=(keep something/put something/be) under lock and key

senses.def: used to tell somebody to try to stay cheerful even though they are in a difficult or unpleasant situation
senses.zh: 振作起来；不气馁；不灰心

examples.en: Chin up! Only two exams left.
examples.zh: 别泄气！只剩下两门考试了。

senses.def: to keep calm and hide your feelings when you are in pain or in a difficult situation
senses.zh: （面对痛苦或困境）不动声色，沉着而不外露

examples.en: He was taught to keep a stiff upper lip and never to cry in public.
examples.zh: 他被教导要保持​​上嘴唇紧绷，永远不要在公共场合哭泣。

examples.en: Their reaction contrasts sharply with the stiff upper lip of the English.
examples.zh: 他们的反应与英国人的僵硬的上唇形成鲜明对比。

senses.def: (know) what things are useful, important, etc.
senses.zh: （知道）什么事物有用（或重要等）

examples.en: She certainly knows what's what.
examples.zh: 她当然知道轻重缓急。

senses.def: used to talk about people who leave an organization, a company, etc. that is having difficulties, without caring about the people who are left
senses.zh: （比喻只顾自己而离开处于困境中的机构等）（像）逃离沉船（的老鼠）

senses.def: used to describe people who are going to do something dangerous without realizing it
senses.zh: （如同）羔羊被牵往屠宰场（指将遇危险而不自觉的人）

senses.def: easily controlled or influenced by another person
senses.zh: （像）某人手中的面团；任某人摆布；易受某人的影响

examples.en: She'll persuade him. He's like putty in her hands.
examples.zh: 她会说服他的。他就像她手里的面团一样。

senses.def: used to say that something, especially criticism, has no effect on somebody/something

examples.en: I can't tell my son what to do; it's water off a duck's back with him.
examples.zh: 我无法告诉我儿子该做什么，他根本听不进去。

(live) in a world of your own: @@@LINK=(be/live) in a world of your own

senses.def: to remove all the people or things from an organization that are thought to be unnecessary or need changing

examples.en: The new manager made a clean sweep of the department.
examples.zh: 新经理清除了部门中的冗员。

senses.def: to win all the prizes or parts of a game or competition; to win an election completely
senses.zh: （比赛或竞赛中）大获全胜，包揽（所有奖项）；获得选举全胜

examples.en: China made a clean sweep of the medals in the gymnastics events.
examples.zh: 中国队在体操比赛中包揽了所有的奖牌。

examples.en: The opinion poll suggests a clean sweep for the Democrats.
examples.zh: 民意测验表明民主党有可能大获全胜。

senses.def: to suddenly move or jump forward to do something or reach somebody/something
senses.zh: 迅速移动；猛然一跳；扑跃

examples.en: The goalkeeper made a dive for the ball.
examples.zh: 守门员一个鱼跃向球扑去。

examples.en: Paul made a dive for the fridge to get a drink.
examples.zh: 保罗冲向冰箱去拿饮料。

senses.def: to keep doing something as well as somebody else, even though they keep making it harder for you

examples.en: We’ve managed to match our closest competitors stride for stride as regards prices.
examples.zh: 在价格方面，我们已设法尽量不输给几个势均力敌的竞争对手。

senses.def: (more than) an amount of something that is considered to be reasonable or acceptable
senses.zh: （超过）合理的数量，恰当的数量

examples.en: He has more than his fair share of problems.
examples.zh: 他的问题过多。

examples.en: I've had my fair share of success in the past.
examples.zh: 过去我已经取得了应有的成功。

(more than) your fair share of something.word: (more than) your fair share of something

(more than) your fair share of sth: @@@LINK=(more than) your fair share of something

senses.def: (not) an easy or a pleasant situation
senses.zh: （并非）轻松的境况，令人愉快的情况

examples.en: Their life together hasn't exactly been a bed of roses.
examples.zh: 他们在一起的生活并不十分幸福。

senses.def: (not) pleased about a situation

examples.en: She wasn't a happy bunny at all.
examples.zh: 她一点儿都不满意。

senses.def: (not) having a healthy mind; (not) thinking clearly

examples.en: My dog behaves very oddly at times—I don't think he's quite all there.
examples.zh: 我的狗有时表现得很奇怪——我认为他不太正常。

senses.def: in any way; to any degree

examples.en: I didn't enjoy it at all.
examples.zh: 我一点也不喜欢。

senses.def: to (not) be as good as is expected or needed
senses.zh: （不）如预想的一般好；（不）像所需要的那么好

examples.en: He won't cut it as a professional singer.
examples.zh: 他的歌艺未达到专业歌手水平。

senses.def: to (not) be as good as expected or required
senses.zh: （不）如所期待的那么好；（不）符合要求

examples.en: I didn't cut the mustard as a hockey player.
examples.zh: 我不是一个合格的曲棍球手。

senses.def: (not) to be able to say anything because somebody else is speaking too much

examples.en: When Mary starts talking, no one else can get a word in edgeways.
examples.zh: 玛丽讲起话来，别人谁也插不上嘴。

senses.def: (not) to be able to say anything because somebody else is speaking too much

examples.en: When Mary starts talking, no one else can get a word in edgeways.
examples.zh: 玛丽讲起话来，别人谁也插不上嘴。

senses.def: (not) to get a chance to take part or succeed in something
senses.zh: （没）有参加的机会；（没）有成功的机会；（没）有份儿

examples.en: She talks so much that nobody else can get a look-in.
examples.zh: 她老是滔滔不绝，别人谁也插不上嘴。

examples.en: The issue of freedom of information did not get a look-in (= it was not even discussed).
examples.zh: 信息自由的问题没有得到关注（=甚至没有被讨论）。

senses.def: (not) in exactly the same words as somebody says were used
senses.zh: （并非）一字不差地，原原本本地

examples.en: ‘Did she say she was sorry?’ ‘Not in so many words.’
examples.zh: “她道歉了没有？”“没有直截了当地说。”

examples.en: He didn't approve of the plan and said so in as many words.
examples.zh: 他明确地说他不同意这计划。

examples.en: They told me in so many words that I was no longer needed.
examples.zh: 他们直截了当地告诉我已经不再需要我了。

senses.def: (not) thinking clearly; (not) able to make sensible decisions
senses.zh: （没有）想清楚；（不）能够做出明智的决定

examples.en: Who in their right mind would spend $50 000 on a pair of shoes?
examples.zh: 哪个心智正常的人会花 50 万美元买一双鞋？

senses.def: to (not) have your normal healthy appearance

examples.en: You're not looking yourself today (= you look tired or ill/sick).
examples.zh: 今天你看上去气色不太好。

senses.def: to (not) be able to identify what is wrong or different about a particular situation
senses.zh: 看（不）出（问题所在）；说（不）出（差别）

examples.en: There was something odd about him but I couldn't put my finger on it.
examples.zh: 他有些古怪，但我说不出到底是什么。

examples.en: You've put your finger on something there—we'll need to investigate that.
examples.zh: 你已经把手指放在了那里——我们需要对此进行调查。

senses.def: (not) something that you are interested in or good at

examples.en: Poetry isn't really my bag.
examples.zh: 我其实并不擅长诗歌。

senses.def: to (not) prevent somebody from doing something

examples.en: If you believe you can make her happy, I won't stand in your way.
examples.zh: 如果你相信你能使她幸福，我不会妨碍你的。

examples.en: He wanted to go to college and would let nothing stand in his way.
examples.zh: 他想上大学，不会让任何事情阻碍他的。

senses.def: extremely thin in a way that is not attractive or healthy

examples.en: The dog lost more and more weight, and was soon little more than skin and bone.
examples.zh: 这只狗越来越瘦，很快就皮包骨了。

examples.en: He's all skin and bone after his illness.
examples.zh: 他病后瘦得皮包骨头。

senses.def: used to introduce different points of view, ideas, etc., especially when they are opposites
senses.zh: （引出不同的，尤指对立的观点、思想等）一方面…，另一方面…

examples.en: On the one hand they'd love to have kids, but on the other, they don't want to give up their freedom.
examples.zh: 一方面，他们想要孩子，但另一方面，他们又不想放弃自由自在的生活。

(on the one hand…) on the other (hand)….word: (on the one hand…) on the other (hand)…

senses.def: used to talk about planning or calculating something in a way that is not detailed, exact or complete

examples.en: We added up our savings on the back of an envelope.
examples.zh: 我们把我们的积蓄写在信封背面。

examples.en: back-of-the-envelope calculations
examples.zh: 粗略计算

senses.def: supplied with the agreement that any item that is not sold can be sent back without having to be paid for
senses.zh: 剩货包退（任何未售出的商品均可退给供货商）

examples.en: The novels are delivered to outlets on a sale or return basis.
examples.zh: 这些小说发给各经销门店，余货包退。

senses.def: walking, rather than travelling by car, bus, etc.

examples.en: ‘How did you get here?’ ‘Shanks’s pony!’
examples.zh: “你是怎么到这里来的？”“香克斯的小马！”

senses.def: (considering) the evidence on both sides of an argument, to find the most likely reason for or result of something
senses.zh: （从）总的来说；（考虑）正反两方面；权衡双方证据

examples.en: The balance of evidence suggests the Liberal party's decline began before the First World War.
examples.zh: 综合证据表明，自由党的衰落始于第一次世界大战之前。

examples.en: The coroner thought that on the balance of probabilities, the pilot had suffered a stroke just before the crash.
examples.zh: 验尸官在分析各种可能性后认为，飞行员很有可能在空难发生之前突然中风。

senses.def: (considering) the evidence on both sides of an argument, to find the most likely reason for or result of something
senses.zh: （从）总的来说；（考虑）正反两方面；权衡双方证据

examples.en: The coroner thought that on the balance of probabilities, the pilot had suffered a stroke just before the crash.
examples.zh: 验尸官在分析各种可能性后认为，飞行员很有可能在空难发生之前突然中风。

senses.def: (to provide) the means of getting or reaching something; (to create) the opportunity for something
senses.zh: （为…提供）达到目的的手段；（为…创造）机会

examples.en: The agreement will open the door to increased international trade.
examples.zh: 此协议将会提供增进国际贸易的机会。

examples.en: Our courses are the door to success in English.
examples.zh: 我们的课程是通向掌握英语的成功之路。

senses.def: visiting restaurants, clubs, theatres, etc. for entertainment, especially at night

examples.en: a night on the town
examples.zh: 去娱乐场所作乐的夜晚

examples.en: How about going out on the town tonight?
examples.zh: 今晚出去痛痛快快地玩一玩怎么样？

senses.def: without a home; outside, not in a house or other building
senses.zh: 无家可归；流落街头；在外面大街上

examples.en: the problems of young people living on the streets
examples.zh: 年轻人流落街头的种种问题

examples.en: If it had been left to me I would have put him out on the street long ago.
examples.zh: 换了我，早就把他赶出家门了。

examples.en: She was thrown onto the street.
examples.zh: 她被赶到大街上。

senses.def: pressed tightly together in a way that is uncomfortable or unpleasant
senses.zh: 拥挤不堪；挤得水泄不通

examples.en: We were packed in like sardines.
examples.zh: 我们像沙丁鱼一样挤在一起。

senses.def: (to have) an unhappy or disappointed expression
senses.zh: 闷闷不乐；哭丧着脸；愁眉苦脸

examples.en: He took one look at her long face and said ‘What’s wrong?’
examples.zh: 他看了一眼她拉长的脸，说：“怎么了？”

examples.en: The news for the company isn't good, to judge from the long faces in the boardroom.
examples.zh: 从董事会里的表情来看，这家公司的消息并不好。

senses.def: (to say or express something) in a very clear way, using few words

examples.en: To put it in a nutshell, we're bankrupt.
examples.zh: 简单地说，我们破产了。

senses.def: at risk

examples.en: If we don't make a profit, my job is on the line.
examples.zh: 我们要是赚不了钱，我就有失业的危险。

senses.def: (to put somebody) at a disadvantage or in difficulty
senses.zh: （使某人）陷入不利局面，处于困境

examples.en: Advances in drone technology have caught lawmakers on the back foot.
examples.zh: 无人机技术的进步教立法者措手不及。

examples.en: The side that’s on the back foot, struggling to defend, will usually give away more penalties.
examples.zh: 处于劣势、防守困难的一方通常会判罚更多的点球。

examples.en: We'd like to put the fossil fuel industry on the back foot.
examples.zh: 我们想让化石燃料行业处于不利地位。

senses.def: (to reach) the point at which something can no longer continue in the same way

examples.en: A defeat in the second round marked the end of the line for last year's champion.
examples.zh: 第二局的失利表明去年的冠军得主已卫冕无望。

examples.en: The loss of this contract could signal the end of the line for the shipyard.
examples.zh: 失去这份合同可能意味着这个造船厂的倒闭。

examples.en: This latest disagreement could mean the end of the road for the band.
examples.zh: 最近出现的分歧可能意味着乐队要解散了。

senses.def: from the very beginning
at exactly the moment you expect or that is appropriate
senses.zh: 恰好在这时；就在这时候

examples.en: ‘Where is that boy?’ As if on cue, Simon appeared in the doorway.
examples.zh: “那男孩在哪里？”西蒙像是接到了信号一样刚好出现在门口。

examples.en: I can't just cry on cue!
examples.zh: 我不会说哭就哭！

senses.def: right from the beginning of a situation or an activity

examples.en: The trouble began right out of the gate.
examples.zh: 麻烦一出门就开始了。

examples.en: The Democrats had a clear advantage out of the gate.
examples.zh: 民主党一开始就有明显的优势。

senses.def: very suitable for you because it is something that you know a lot about or are very interested in

examples.en: A teaching job would be right up her alley.
examples.zh: 教学工作正合她的胃口。

senses.def: very suitable for you because it is something that you know a lot about or are very interested in

examples.en: This job seems right up your street.
examples.zh: 这工作看来对你正合适。

senses.def: to think about how you can make a lot of money from a situation or person

examples.en: Investors are seeing dollar signs.
examples.zh: 投资者正在看到美元迹象。

examples.en: She looked at the wealthy widower and saw only dollar signs.
examples.zh: 她看着那个有钱的鳏夫，一心想着如何从他身上大捞一笔。

examples.en: Many inventors with dollar signs in their eyes are eager to come up with the latest gadget.
examples.zh: 许多望眼欲穿想发财的发明家都迫不及待地想推出最新潮的小玩意。

senses.def: (to become) out of control

examples.en: She said nothing in case her temper slipped out of gear.
examples.zh: 她什么都没说，免得按捺不住情绪。

senses.def: used as a command to soldiers to tell them to stand with their feet apart and their hands behind their backs
completely crazy
(to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions
senses.zh: （走）中间道路；（取）中庸之道；（采取）折中办法

(steer, take, etc.) a middle course | (f.word: (steer, take, etc.) a middle course | (find, etc.) a/the middle way

senses.def: (still) only a boy

examples.en: I was still in short trousers at the time.
examples.zh: 我那时还在穿着短裤呢（还只是个小男孩）。

senses.def: young and without much experience
senses.zh: 乳臭未干；少不更事；没见过世面

examples.en: He was still wet behind the ears, politically.
examples.zh: 在政治上，他仍然一无所知。

senses.def: given by somebody who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate

(stuck) between a rock and a hard place: @@@LINK=(caught/stuck) between a rock and a hard place

senses.def: (to become used to something) very easily, without any problems or fears
senses.zh: 像鸭子入水般容易，轻而易举，毫不困难，毫无畏惧（习惯于某事）

examples.en: She has taken to teaching like a duck to water.
examples.zh: 她教起书来驾轻就熟。

(take to something) like a duck to water.word: (take to something) like a duck to water

(take to sth) like a duck to water: @@@LINK=(take to something) like a duck to water

senses.def: used to say that things often happen in a particular way, especially when it is not convenient
senses.zh: （表示经常如此，尤指不方便）总是这样，老是

senses.def: the advantages to be gained from doing something are not great enough, considering the effort or cost involved

examples.en: If the price goes up again, he may decide that the game’s not worth the candle.
examples.zh: 如果价格再次上涨，他可能会认为这款游戏得不偿失。

(the game is) not worth the candle.word: (the game is) not worth the candle

senses.def: used to refer to a point at which you start achieving less than the value of the time or money you put into something
senses.zh: 收益递减，回报递减（规律）

examples.en: Our efforts were producing diminishing returns.
examples.zh: 我们的努力产生的收益正在不断递减。

examples.en: In general, the more exercise you take, the greater the health benefit; but beyond a certain level you get diminishing returns.
examples.zh: 一般来说，锻炼越多，对健康的益处就越大；但超过一定水平，你的回报就会递减。

senses.def: the ability to keep moving ahead of your competitors, especially in politics
senses.zh: （尤指政治上领先对手的）势力，推动力

examples.en: In politics, momentum is known as the big mo.
examples.zh: 政治上，势头被视作重要的推动力。

examples.en: He's picking up a lot of support and has the big mo.
examples.zh: 他正得到越来越多的支持，势头很足。

senses.def: the present time; at the present time

examples.en: our obsession with the here and now
examples.zh: 我们对当前事物的痴迷

examples.en: We're going to settle this here and now.
examples.zh: 我们要马上解决这个问题。

senses.def: somebody suddenly understood or began to understand something

examples.en: I puzzled over the problem for ages before the light suddenly dawned.
examples.zh: 我对这个问题冥思苦想了很久才豁然开朗。

senses.def: a man who is chosen as having given the best performance in a game of football (soccer), cricket
senses.zh: （足球、板球等的）本场最佳球员

examples.en: Stokes was named man of the match.
examples.zh: 斯托克斯被评为本场最佳球员。

senses.def: on the next, first, etc. occasion that the same thing happens
senses.zh: 同样的事情下次（或第一次等）发生时

examples.en: He repeated none of the errors he'd made first time round.
examples.zh: 他没有重复过首次所犯下的任何错误。

examples.en: This time round it was not so easy.
examples.zh: 这一次这事可就不那么容易了。

(the) next, first, second, etc. time rou.word: (the) next, first, second, etc. time round

senses.def: used to ask somebody to serve you the same drink as before

examples.en: Same again, please!
examples.zh: 和刚才一样的，请再来一份！

senses.def: used to answer a greeting
senses.zh: （回应问候、冒犯的话等）你也一样

examples.en: ‘Happy Christmas!’ ‘And the same to you!’
examples.zh: “圣诞快乐！”“也祝你圣诞快乐！”

examples.en: ‘Get lost!’ ‘Same to you!’

senses.def: used to describe a situation that changes so often that it is difficult to understand or deal with it
the excitement that is involved in dangerous activities, especially sports
senses.zh: （危险活动，尤指体育运动的）紧张和刺激

senses.def: a novel (1859) by Charles Dickens

senses.def: to make sure that you know all the most recent facts about a subject
senses.zh: 了解最新情况；跟上（某事物的发展）

examples.en: It is almost impossible to keep abreast of all the latest developments in computing.
examples.zh: 要跟上计算机领域所有最新的发展几乎不可能。

examples.en: I like to keep abreast of current affairs.
examples.zh: 我喜欢紧跟时事。

examples.en: It’s important to keep abreast with the latest legislation.

senses.def: to make a book, play, etc. shorter by leaving parts out

examples.en: She has been asked to abridge the novel for radio.
examples.zh: 她被要求为广播节目删减小说。

senses.def: the process of making a book, play, etc. shorter by leaving parts out; a version of a book, play, etc. that has been made shorter in this way

examples.en: Abridgement of this complex text was extremely difficult.
examples.zh: 对这一复杂文本进行删节极为困难。

examples.en: an abridgement of Forster’s ‘Life of Dickens’
examples.zh: 福斯特的《狄更斯传》节录本

senses.def: in or to a foreign country

examples.en: to go/travel/live/study abroad
examples.zh: 出国；出国旅行；在外国居住；出国留学

examples.en: She worked abroad for a year.
examples.zh: 她在国外工作了一年。

examples.en: imports of cheap food from abroad
examples.zh: 国外廉价食物的进口

examples.en: He was famous, both at home and abroad (= in his own country and in other countries).
examples.zh: 他享誉国内外。

examples.en: For a holiday abroad you need a valid passport.
examples.zh: 出国度假需要有效护照。

senses.def: being talked about or felt by many people

examples.en: There was news abroad that a change was coming.
examples.zh: 盛传即将有一个变动。

senses.def: outside; outdoors
to officially end a law, an agreement, etc.
senses.zh: 废除，废止，撤销（法律、协议等）

examples.en: The rule has been abrogated by mutual consent.
examples.zh: 经双方同意，该规则已被废除。

senses.def: to fail to carry out a responsibility or duty

examples.en: We believe the board is abrogating its responsibilities.
examples.zh: 我们认为董事会在推卸责任。

senses.def: the fact of officially ending a law, an agreement, etc.
senses.zh: 废除，废止，撤销（法律、协议等）

examples.en: the abrogation of civil rights in the country
examples.zh: 在该国废除公民权利

senses.def: failure to carry out a responsibility or duty

examples.en: Refusing to vote may be considered an abrogation of your responsibility as a citizen.
examples.zh: 拒绝投票可被视为放弃作为公民的责任。

senses.def: sudden and unexpected, often in an unpleasant way

examples.en: an abrupt change/halt/departure
examples.zh: 突然改变；骤然停顿；突然离去

examples.en: The accident brought his career to an abrupt end.
examples.zh: 那起事故使他的职业生涯突然结束了。

senses.def: speaking or acting in a way that seems rude and unfriendly; not taking time to say more than is necessary
senses.zh: （言语、行为）粗鲁的，莽撞的，唐突的；生硬的

examples.en: an abrupt manner
examples.zh: 唐突的举止

examples.en: He indicated Isabel with an abrupt movement of his head.
examples.zh: 他晃了一下脑袋，头指向伊莎贝尔。

examples.en: She was very abrupt with me in our meeting.
examples.zh: 我们会面时，她跟我说话非常生硬。

senses.def: in a sudden, unexpected and often unpleasant way
senses.zh: 以一种突然的、意想不到的并且经常是不愉快的方式

examples.en: The interview ended abruptly.
examples.zh: 采访戛然而止。

senses.def: in a way that seems rude and unfriendly, without taking time to say more than is necessary
senses.zh: 以一种看起来很粗鲁和不友好的方式，不花时间说更多必要的东西

examples.en: ‘Come here!’ she said abruptly.
examples.zh: “过来！”她突然说道。

senses.def: the fact of being sudden, unexpected and often unpleasant

examples.en: The abruptness of the ending comes as a shock after the long slow build-up.
examples.zh: 在漫长而缓慢的铺垫之后，突然的结局令人震惊。

senses.def: the fact of being rude and unfriendly, without taking time to say more than is necessary

examples.en: Polite enquiries were met with abruptness and rudeness.
examples.zh: 礼貌的询问遭到了唐突和粗鲁的回应。

senses.def: the muscles of the abdomen
anti-lock braking system
a swollen

examples.en: a painful abscess on the gum
examples.zh: 牙龈上疼痛的脓肿

senses.def: the coordinate
to escape from a place that you are not allowed to leave without permission

examples.en: She absconded from every children’s home they placed her in.
examples.zh: 她从他们安置她的每个儿童之家潜逃。

senses.def: to leave secretly and take with you something, especially money, that does not belong to you

examples.en: He absconded with the company funds.
examples.zh: 他卷走公司的资金潜逃了。

senses.def: an act of going down a steep cliff
senses.zh: 绕绳下降（用绳缠绕着身体，双脚蹬陡坡或峭壁自己放绳下滑）

senses.def: to go down a steep cliff
senses.zh: 绕绳下降（用绳缠绕着身体，双脚蹬陡坡或峭壁自己放绳下滑）

senses.def: the fact of somebody being away from a place where they are usually expected to be; the occasion or period of time when somebody is away

examples.en: The decision was made in my absence (= while I was not there).
examples.zh: 这个决定是我不在的时候作出的。

examples.en: We did not receive any news during his long absence.
examples.zh: 我们在他长期离开的时候没有得到一点消息。

examples.en: absence from work
examples.zh: 缺勤

examples.en: repeated absences from school
examples.zh: 一再缺课

senses.def: the fact of somebody/something not existing or not being available; a lack of something

examples.en: I was surprised by the absence of any women on the board of directors.
examples.zh: 我真没想到董事会中竟然没有女性。

examples.en: The case was dismissed in the absence of any definite proof.
examples.zh: 此案因缺乏确凿证据而不予受理。

senses.def: used to say that when you are away from somebody that you love, you love them even more
not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there
senses.zh: （本应在场）因缺席而招人注意

examples.en: The meeting went well but Nigel was conspicuous by his absence.
examples.zh: 会议进行得很顺利，但奈杰尔因缺席而显眼。

items.idm: absence makes the heart grow fonder

senses.def: used to say that when you are away from somebody that you love, you love them even more
not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there
senses.zh: （本应在场）因缺席而招人注意

examples.en: The meeting went well but Nigel was conspicuous by his absence.
examples.zh: 会议进行得很顺利，但奈杰尔因缺席而显眼。

senses.def: used to say that when you are away from somebody that you love, you love them even more

absence makes the heart grow fonder.word: absence makes the heart grow fonder

senses.def: not in a place because of illness, etc.

examples.en: She was absent from work for two weeks.
examples.zh: 她已经两周没有上班了。

examples.en: Local people were conspicuously absent from the meeting.
examples.zh: 当地人都没有到会，这引起了人们的关注。

senses.def: not present in something

examples.en: Love was totally absent from his childhood.
examples.zh: 他童年时没有得到丝毫关爱。

examples.en: She now played with a passion that had been strangely absent from her previous performance.
examples.zh: 她现在的演奏充满了热情，而这是她之前的表演中奇怪地缺乏的。

senses.def: showing that you are not really looking at or thinking about what is happening around you

examples.en: an absent expression
examples.zh: 心不在焉的神情

senses.def: to not go to or be in a place where you are expected to be

examples.en: He had absented himself from the office for the day.
examples.zh: 这一天他没有去办公室上班。

senses.def: without

examples.en: Absent further evidence, the police had no choice but to release him without charge.
examples.zh: 由于没有进一步的证据，警方只好将他无指控释放。

senses.def: tending to forget things, perhaps because you are not thinking about what is around you, but about something else

examples.en: I'm very absent-minded and often forget to take my keys with me.
examples.zh: 我很心不在焉，经常忘记带钥匙。

examples.en: She's nothing like the popular stereotype of the absent-minded professor.
examples.zh: 她与人们对心不在焉的教授的普遍刻板印象完全不同。

senses.def: in a way that shows you are not thinking about what is around you, but about something else, and that may cause you to forget things
senses.zh: （人或其行为举止）心不在焉的，出神的

examples.en: She absent-mindedly twisted a strand of hair around her fingers.
examples.zh: 她心不在焉地将一缕头发盘绕在手指上。

senses.def: the fact of tending to forget things, especially because you are not thinking about what is around you, but about something else
a person who is not at a place where they were expected to be
a vote in an election that you can send when you cannot be present
a person who rents their property to somebody, but does not live in it and rarely visits it
senses.zh: 在外业主，在外地主（不在产业内居住也很少过来）

examples.en: The house has an absentee landlord, who visits the property once a year.
examples.zh: 这房子的房主不在这儿住，只是一年来查看一次房产。

senses.def: the fact of being frequently away from work or school, especially without good reasons
in a way that shows you are not looking at or thinking about what is happening around you

examples.en: He nodded absently, his attention absorbed by the screen.
examples.zh: 他全神注视着屏幕，心不在焉地点了点头。

senses.def: a very strong green alcoholic drink that tastes of aniseed
senses.zh: 苦艾酒（带茴香味的绿色烈性酒）

senses.def: total and complete

examples.en: I've joined a class for absolute beginners.
examples.zh: 我参加了一个专门为初学者开设的班。

examples.en: absolute confidence/trust/silence/truth
examples.zh: 充满信心；绝对信任；万籁俱寂；绝对真实

examples.en: ‘You're wrong,’ she said with absolute certainty.
examples.zh: “你错了。”她斩钉截铁地说。

examples.en: Clean water is an absolute necessity.
examples.zh: 洁净水是绝对的必需品。

examples.en: Around them the darkness was absolute, the silence oppressive.
examples.zh: 他们周遭一片漆黑，寂静得令人压抑。

senses.def: used, especially in spoken English, to give emphasis to what you are saying
senses.zh: （口语中尤用以强调）道地的，确实的，十足的

examples.en: We must keep costs to an absolute minimum.
examples.zh: 我们必须把成本控制到最低。

examples.en: This room is an absolute disgrace.
examples.zh: 这个房间太丢人了。

examples.en: They're talking absolute nonsense.
examples.zh: 他们完全是在胡说八道。

examples.en: He must earn an absolute fortune.
examples.zh: 他准是赚了一大笔钱。

senses.def: definite and without any doubt

examples.en: There was no absolute proof.
examples.zh: 没有确凿的证据。

examples.en: He taught us that the laws of physics were absolute.
examples.zh: 他教导我们说，物理定律是确实存在的。

examples.en: The story offers no clear message, no absolute truth.
examples.zh: 这个故事没有传递清晰的信息，也没有绝对的真理。

senses.def: (of a legal decision) final

examples.en: The divorce became absolute last week.
examples.zh: 离婚在上周已成定局。

senses.def: not limited in any way
senses.zh: 不受限制的；不受约束的

examples.en: absolute power/authority
examples.zh: 无上权力；绝对权威

examples.en: an absolute ruler/monarchy (= one with no limit to their power)
examples.zh: 独裁统治者；君主专制政体

senses.def: existing or measured independently and not in relation to something else

examples.en: Although prices are falling in absolute terms, energy is still expensive.
examples.zh: 尽管能源的绝对售价在下降，但仍然昂贵。

examples.en: Beauty cannot be measured by any absolute standard.
examples.zh: 美是不可能用任何绝对标准来衡量的。

senses.def: an idea or a principle that is believed to be true or relevant in any circumstances

examples.en: Right and wrong are, for her, moral absolutes.
examples.zh: 她认为，是与非是道德上的绝对准则。

senses.def: a form of ethanol
senses.zh: 无水乙醇，无水酒精（含水量少于 1%）

senses.def: a measure of how bright a star, planet, etc. is, as it would be seen at a standard distance from the earth
senses.zh: 绝对星等（假定天体在距地球标准距离的地方所测得的亮度等级）

senses.def: more than half of the total number of votes or winning candidates
senses.zh: 绝对多数（指超过半数的选票或竞选席位）

examples.en: 280 seats are needed for an absolute majority in the National Assembly.
examples.zh: 在国民议会取得绝对多数必须拥有280个席位。

senses.def: music for instruments that is not intended to tell a story, describe a scene, represent something else, etc.
temperature measured from absolute zero
the lowest temperature that is thought to be possible
used to emphasize that something is completely true
senses.zh: （强调真实无误）绝对地，完全地

examples.en: You're absolutely right.
examples.zh: 你完全正确。

examples.en: He made it absolutely clear.
examples.zh: 他把此事讲得一清二楚。

examples.en: I'm not absolutely certain I posted it.
examples.zh: 我也不确定是我发的。

examples.en: Are you absolutely sure?
examples.zh: 你绝对肯定吗？

examples.en: Training is absolutely essential in this business.
examples.zh: 在这个行业中，培训是绝对必要的。

examples.en: Don't delay for longer than absolutely necessary.
examples.zh: 不要拖延超过绝对必要的时间。

examples.en: The place was absolutely packed.
examples.zh: 那地方拥挤不堪。

examples.en: It was absolutely pouring with rain.
examples.zh: 正下着倾盆大雨。

senses.def: used to emphasize something negative

examples.en: That man does absolutely no work!
examples.zh: 那个人一丁点活儿也没干！

examples.en: There's absolutely nothing more the doctors can do.
examples.zh: 医生的确再也无计可施了。

senses.def: used with adjectives or verbs that express strong feelings or extreme qualities to mean ‘extremely’

examples.en: absolutely delighted/thrilled
examples.zh: 极其兴奋／激动

examples.en: We were absolutely devastated at the news.
examples.zh: 这个消息让我们彻底崩溃了。

examples.en: I absolutely love strawberries.
examples.zh: 我极其喜欢草莓。

examples.en: She absolutely adores you.
examples.zh: 她极为崇拜你。

examples.en: absolutely fantastic/amazing
examples.zh: 极其出色的／惊人的

examples.en: He's an absolutely brilliant cook.
examples.zh: 他的厨艺精湛至极。

senses.def: used to emphasize that you agree with somebody, or to give somebody permission to do something
senses.zh: （强调同意或允许）当然，对极了

examples.en: ‘They could have told us, couldn't they?’ ‘Absolutely!’
examples.zh: “他们本来可以告诉我们的，不是吗？”“当然！”

examples.en: ‘Can we leave a little early?’ ‘Absolutely!’
examples.zh: “我们可以早一点离开吗？”“完全可以！”

senses.def: used to emphasize that you strongly disagree with somebody, or to refuse permission
senses.zh: （强调坚决不同意或不允许）当然不，绝对不行

examples.en: ‘Was it any good?’ ‘No, absolutely not.’
examples.zh: “那有什么好处吗？”“绝对没有。”

examples.en: ‘Can I stay up late?’ ‘Absolutely not!’
examples.zh: “我可以熬夜吗？”“绝对不能！”

senses.def: not considered in relation to other things

examples.en: White-collar crime increased both absolutely and in comparison with other categories.
examples.zh: 无论是与其他类型犯罪相比，还是就其本身而言，白领犯罪的数量都有所增长。

senses.def: a British television comedy series that was very popular in the 1990s. It is about two women in the fashion business, Patsy and Edina. They spend most of their time drinking, smoking and taking drugs, and arguing with Edina's daughter, who is very serious and does not approve of their behaviour.
formal release from blame for doing something wrong

examples.en: She's looking for some kind of absolution for her crimes.
examples.zh: 她在为自己的罪行寻求某种赦免。

senses.def: a formal statement that a person is forgiven for what they have done wrong

examples.en: to seek absolution for your sins
examples.zh: 为你的罪孽寻求赦免

examples.en: He was granted absolution by the priest.
examples.zh: 他得到神父的赦免。

examples.en: Some people might go to church and seek absolution.
examples.zh: 有些人可能会去教堂寻求赦免。

senses.def: a political system in which a leader or government has total power at all times
belief in a political, religious or moral principle that is thought to be true in all circumstances
senses.zh: （政治、宗教、道德上的）绝对主义，绝对论，绝对原则

senses.def: a person who supports a political system in which a leader or government has total power at all times

examples.en: The absolutist, Joseph II (1780–90), who succeeded Maria Theresa, failed in his reforms.
examples.zh: 接替玛丽亚·特蕾莎的专制主义者约瑟夫二世（1780-90 年）的改革失败了。

senses.def: a person who believes that a political, religious or moral principle is true in all circumstances
senses.zh: （政治、宗教、道德上的）绝对主义，绝对论，绝对原则

examples.en: He was a moral absolutist with little patience for shades of grey—or for dissent.
examples.zh: 他是一个道德绝对主义者，对灰色阴影或异议缺乏耐心。

senses.def: supporting a political system in which a leader or government has total power at all times

examples.en: absolutist government/monarchy/power
examples.zh: 专制政府/君主制/权力

senses.def: believing that a political, religious or moral principle is true in all circumstances
senses.zh: （政治、宗教、道德上的）绝对主义，绝对论，绝对原则

examples.en: One absolutist ethical theory is the traditional view that right and wrong are God-given.
examples.zh: 一种绝对主义的伦理理论是传统观点，即对错是上帝赋予的。

senses.def: to state formally that somebody is not guilty or responsible for something

examples.en: The court absolved him of all responsibility for the accident.
examples.zh: 法院判定他对该事故不负任何责任。

senses.def: to give absolution

examples.en: I absolve you from all your sins.
examples.zh: 我赦免你所有的罪过。

senses.def: to take in a liquid, gas or other substance from the surface or space around

examples.en: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air.
examples.zh: 植物吸收空气中的二氧化碳。

examples.en: Let the rice cook until it has absorbed all the water.
examples.zh: 让米饭煮至吸收所有水分。

examples.en: The cream is easily absorbed into the skin.
examples.zh: 这种乳霜皮肤易吸收。

senses.def: to take in and keep heat, light, energy, sound, etc. instead of reflecting it

examples.en: Black walls absorb a lot of heat during the day.
examples.zh: 黑色墙壁在白天吸收大量的热。

senses.def: to reduce the effect of a physical impact or movement
senses.zh: 减轻（撞击、活动等的）作用

examples.en: This tennis racket absorbs shock on impact.
examples.zh: 这款网球拍能减轻撞击所产生的剧烈震动。

examples.en: The bats have graphite shafts that absorb the vibration.
examples.zh: 球棒的石墨轴可以吸收振动。

senses.def: to take something into the mind and learn or understand it

examples.en: It's a lot of information to absorb all at once.
examples.zh: 要一下子消化这些资料，真是很多。

examples.en: It took me several days to absorb the fact of her death.
examples.zh: 我花了好几天时间才接受她去世的事实。

examples.en: They spent a week in Paris just absorbing the atmosphere.
examples.zh: 他们在巴黎呆了一周，感受巴黎的氛围。

senses.def: to interest somebody very much so that they pay no attention to anything else
senses.zh: 吸引全部注意力；使全神贯注

examples.en: This work had absorbed him for several years.
examples.zh: 这项工作曾使他沉迷了好几年。

examples.en: Her work absorbed her completely.
examples.zh: 她的工作完全吸引了她。

senses.def: to make something smaller become part of something larger

examples.en: The town absorbs an influx of tourists every summer.
examples.zh: 每年夏天，游客会大量涌入该镇。

examples.en: The surrounding small towns have been absorbed into the city.
examples.zh: 四周的小城镇已并入这座城市。

examples.en: These committees were gradually absorbed into the local government machine.
examples.zh: 这些委员会被逐渐并入当地的政府机构中。

senses.group: make part of something larger 使并入

senses.def: to use up a large supply of something, especially money or time
senses.zh: 耗费，耗去（大量金钱、时间等）

examples.en: The new proposals would absorb $80 billion of the federal budget.
examples.zh: 这些新提案将耗费 800 亿美元联邦政府预算。

examples.en: My work absorbs a great deal of my time.
examples.zh: 我的工作占用了我大量的时间。

senses.def: to deal with changes, effects, costs, etc.
senses.zh: 承受，承担，对付（变化、结果、费用等）

examples.en: The company is unable to absorb such huge losses.
examples.zh: 公司无法承受如此巨大的损失。

senses.def: that can be absorbed
senses.zh: 可吸收的；（尤指）可被人体吸收的

examples.en: absorbable gases
examples.zh: 可吸收气体

senses.def: the ability of a substance to absorb
the quality of being able to take in something easily, especially liquid

examples.en: Cotton has high absorbency.
examples.zh: 棉的吸水性强。

senses.def: able to take in something easily, especially liquid

examples.en: absorbent paper/materials
examples.zh: 吸水纸；吸收性材料

senses.def: a soft mass of white material that is used for cleaning the skin or a wound
the process of a liquid, gas or other substance being taken in

examples.en: Vitamin D is necessary to aid the absorption of calcium from food.
examples.zh: 从食物中吸取钙需靠维生素 D 的帮助。

senses.def: the process of a smaller group, country, etc. becoming part of a larger group or country

examples.en: the absorption of the town into the Leeds City Region
examples.zh: 将该镇并入利兹城市地区

senses.def: the fact of somebody being very interested in something so that it takes all their attention
senses.zh: 专心致志；全神贯注；着迷

examples.en: His work suffered because of his total absorption in sport.
examples.zh: 他痴迷于体育运动而影响了工作。

senses.def: to choose not to use a vote, either in favour of or against something

senses.zh: 阿萨伊（南美洲棕榈树，果实可食用或制成果汁）

examples.en: açai berries
examples.zh: 巴西莓

senses.def: a plant that grows in warm regions and has long spikes
senses.zh: 老鼠簕属植物（分布于温暖地区，穗状花序；有多个品种，有的叶片具光泽，叶缘有锯齿）

senses.def: Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service
senses.zh: （英国）咨询调解与仲裁局（帮助雇主与雇员解决争议的机构）

senses.def: to agree to a request, proposal, etc.

examples.en: He acceded to demands for his resignation.
examples.zh: 他同意要他辞职的要求。

examples.en: Japan had little choice but to accede.
examples.zh: 日本别无选择，只能同意。

examples.en: The Planning Committee has finally acceded to growing pressure.
examples.zh: 在越来越大的压力下，规划委员会终于做出了让步。

senses.def: to achieve a high position, especially to become king or queen
senses.zh: 就任；就职；（尤指君主）即位

examples.en: Queen Victoria acceded to the throne in 1837.
examples.zh: 维多利亚女王于 1837 年即位。

senses.def: to become a member of an organization

examples.en: Croatia acceded to the EU in 2013.
examples.zh: 克罗地亚于 2013 年加入欧盟。

senses.def: part of a piece of music that gradually increases in speed
senses.zh: 速度逐渐加快的（地）；渐快的（地）

senses.def: gradually increasing in speed
senses.zh: 速度逐渐加快的（地）；渐快的（地）

senses.def: to happen faster or earlier; to make something happen faster or earlier

examples.en: Inflation continues to accelerate.
examples.zh: 通货膨胀不断加速。

examples.en: Exposure to the sun can accelerate the ageing process.
examples.zh: 暴露在日光下会加快老化过程。

senses.def: to start to go faster

examples.en: The runners accelerated smoothly around the bend.
examples.zh: 赛跑运动员在转弯处顺势加速。

examples.en: The car accelerated to overtake me.
examples.zh: 那辆汽车加速超过了我。

examples.en: The car purred into life and accelerated away.
examples.zh: 那辆轿车轰隆隆地发动起来，然后加速开走了。

senses.def: an increase in how fast something happens

examples.en: an acceleration in the rate of economic growth
examples.zh: 经济增长加速

senses.def: the rate at which a vehicle increases speed

examples.en: a car with good acceleration
examples.zh: 加速性能良好的汽车

examples.en: acceleration from 0–60 mph in 11.2 seconds
examples.zh: 0-60 英里/小时加速时间为 11.2 秒

examples.en: This model has the best acceleration of any available sports car.
examples.zh: 这款车的加速性能是现有跑车中最好的。

senses.def: the rate at which the velocity

examples.en: acceleration caused by gravity
examples.zh: 重力引起的加速度

senses.def: the pedal

examples.en: She put her foot on the accelerator and we sped through the traffic lights.
examples.zh: 她一踩油门，我们就冲过了红绿灯。

senses.def: a machine for making elementary particles
a circuit board
an instrument for measuring acceleration
a way of pronouncing the words of a language that shows which country, area or social class a person comes from; how well somebody pronounces a particular language

examples.en: a northern/Dublin/Scottish accent
examples.zh: 北方／都柏林／苏格兰口音

examples.en: a strong/broad accent (= one that is easy to notice)
examples.zh: 浓重的口音

examples.en: She spoke English with an accent.
examples.zh: 她说英语带有口音。

examples.en: The Americans had learned Korean and spoke with a good accent.
examples.zh: 这些美国人学会了韩国语，而且发音非常地道。

senses.def: the emphasis that you should give to part of a word when saying it

examples.en: In ‘today’ the accent is on the second syllable.
examples.zh: today 一词的重音在第二音节。

senses.def: a mark on a letter to show that it should be pronounced in a particular way

examples.en: Canapé has an accent on the ‘e’.
examples.zh: canapé 在 e 上面有尖音符号。

senses.def: a special importance that is given to something

examples.en: In all our products the accent is on quality.
examples.zh: 我们的全部产品都强调质量。

senses.def: to emphasize a part of something

examples.en: The women accent their eyes with make-up.
examples.zh: 女人们用化妆来突出她们的眼睛。

senses.def: to emphasize something or make it easier to notice

examples.en: Her short hair accentuated her huge eyes.
examples.zh: 她的短发凸显了她的大眼睛。

examples.en: The fundamental patterns of inequality have remained and have been accentuated by the war.
examples.zh: 不平等的基本形式仍然存在，并因战争而更加突出。

examples.en: When talks did occur, they tended to accentuate differences between the two groups.
examples.zh: 当会谈真的发生时，它们往往会加剧两组人之间的分歧。

senses.def: the fact of being emphasized or made easier to notice
to take willingly something that is offered; to say ‘yes’ to an offer, invitation, etc.

examples.en: He asked me to marry him and I accepted.
examples.zh: 他向我求婚，我答应了。

examples.en: Please accept our sincere apologies.
examples.zh: 请接受我们真诚的歉意。

examples.en: It was pouring with rain so I accepted his offer of a lift.
examples.zh: 天正下着瓢泼大雨，所以我领了他的情，搭了他的便车。

examples.en: I am unfortunately unable to accept your kind invitation.
examples.zh: 很遗憾，我不能接受您的盛情邀请。

examples.en: The board of directors accepted our proposal.
examples.zh: 董事会接受了我们的提议。

examples.en: She's decided not to accept the job.
examples.zh: 她决定不接受这项工作。

examples.en: Please accept this small token of my appreciation.
examples.zh: 请接受我的这份小小的谢意。

examples.en: He is charged with accepting bribes from a firm of suppliers.
examples.zh: 他被控收受了一家供应商的贿赂。

examples.en: She said she'd accept $15 for it.
examples.zh: 她说她要 15 美元才卖。

senses.def: to agree to or approve of something

examples.en: They accepted the court's decision.
examples.zh: 他们接受法院的判决。

examples.en: The judge refused to accept his evidence.
examples.zh: 法官拒绝采纳他的证词。

examples.en: He accepted all the changes we proposed.
examples.zh: 他同意我们提出的全部修改方案。

examples.en: Are you willing to accept the challenge?
examples.zh: 你愿意接受挑战吗？

examples.en: She won't accept advice from anyone.
examples.zh: 她不会接受任何人的忠告。

examples.en: My article has been accepted for publication.
examples.zh: 我的文章已获采用，准备发表。

senses.def: to take payment in a particular form

examples.en: This machine only accepts coins.
examples.zh: 这台机器只收硬币。

examples.en: Credit cards are widely accepted.
examples.zh: 很多地方都可以刷信用卡。

senses.def: to admit that you are responsible or to blame for something

examples.en: He accepts full responsibility for what happened.
examples.zh: 他承认对发生的事负全部责任。

examples.en: You have to accept the consequences of your actions.
examples.zh: 你得对你的行为后果负责。

senses.def: to continue in a difficult situation without complaining, because you realize that you cannot change it

examples.en: You just have to accept the fact that we're never going to be rich.
examples.zh: 你只得接受我们永远也富不起来这个事实。

examples.en: to be willing/prepared to accept something
examples.zh: 愿意接受某事

examples.en: Nothing will change as long as the workers continue to accept these appalling conditions.
examples.zh: 只要工人继续容忍这种恶劣的劳动条件，情况就不会有任何改变。

examples.en: They accept the risks as part of the job.
examples.zh: 他们甘冒风险，把这当成工作的一部分。

examples.en: He just refused to accept that his father was no longer there.
examples.zh: 他就是不肯接受他父亲已不在的现实。

senses.def: to make somebody feel welcome and part of a group

examples.en: It may take years to be completely accepted by the local community.
examples.zh: 也许需要多年方能被当地居民完全接纳。

examples.en: She had never been accepted into what was essentially a man's world.
examples.zh: 她从未被这个基本上属于男人的世界所接受。

examples.en: He never really accepted her as his own child.
examples.zh: 他一直没有真正接纳她为自己的女儿。

senses.def: to believe that something is true

examples.en: I don't accept his version of events.
examples.zh: 我不相信他对事件的说法。

examples.en: Can we accept his account as the true version?
examples.zh: 我们能相信他说的是事实吗？

examples.en: I accept that this will not be popular.
examples.zh: 我认为这是不会受欢迎的。

examples.en: I am not prepared to accept that this decision is final.
examples.zh: 我不准备接受这一决定是最终决定。

examples.en: It is generally accepted that people are motivated by success.
examples.zh: 普遍认为，成功催人奋进。

examples.en: Their workforce is widely accepted to have the best conditions in Europe.
examples.zh: 普遍认为他们的劳工拥有欧洲最好的工作条件。

senses.def: to allow somebody to join an organization, attend an institution, use a service, etc.
senses.zh: 接纳，接受（为成员、会员等）

examples.en: The college he applied to has accepted him.
examples.zh: 他申请的那所学院录取了他。

examples.en: She was disappointed not to be accepted into the club.
examples.zh: 她没有获准加入俱乐部，感到失望。

examples.en: The landlord was willing to accept us as tenants.
examples.zh: 房东愿意把房子租给我们住。

examples.en: She was accepted to study music.
examples.zh: 她获录取学习音乐。

senses.group: allow somebody to join 准许加入

synonyms.words: accept ▪ approve ▪ go along with somebody/​something ▪ consent

intro.en: These words all mean to say that you will do what somebody wants or that you will allow something to happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含答应、同意之义。

items.def: to say that you will do what somebody wants or that you will allow something to happen:
items.zh: 指答应、容许

examples.en: He agreed to let me go early.
examples.zh: 他容许我早走。

items.def: to be satisfied with something that has been done, decided or suggested:
items.zh: 指同意、接受、认可

examples.en: They accepted the court’s decision.
examples.zh: 他们接受法院的判决。

items.def: to officially agree to a plan, suggestion or request:
items.zh: 指批准、正式通过（计划、建议或要求）

examples.en: The committee unanimously approved the plan.
examples.zh: 委员会一致通过了计划。

items.def: (rather informal) to agree to something that somebody else has decided; to agree with somebody else’s ideas:
items.zh: 指赞同某事，同意某人的观点

examples.en: She just goes along with everything he suggests.
examples.zh: 他的一切建议她都赞同。

items.def: (rather formal) to agree to something or give your permission for something:
items.zh: 指同意、准许、允许

examples.en: She finally consented to answer our questions.
examples.zh: 她最终同意回答我们的问题。

senses.def: the degree to which something is agreed or approved of by most people in a society

examples.en: The social acceptability of smoking varies between countries.
examples.zh: 各国社会对吸烟的接受程度不同。

senses.def: the degree to which somebody agrees that something is good enough to use or allow

examples.en: The study aimed to assess the acceptability of the new system to patients.
examples.zh: 这项研究旨在评估病人对新系统的接受程度。

senses.def: agreed or approved of by most people in a society

examples.en: Children must learn socially acceptable behaviour.
examples.zh: 儿童必须学会社会上认可的行为举止。

examples.en: It is perfectly acceptable for you as an employee to say no.
examples.zh: 作为一名员工，你完全可以说 "不"。

senses.def: that somebody agrees is of a good enough standard or allowed
senses.zh: 可接受的；令人满意的；可容许的

examples.en: For this course a pass in English at grade B is acceptable.
examples.zh: 英语成绩达到 B 级就可以学习这门课程。

examples.en: Air pollution in the city had reached four times the acceptable levels.
examples.zh: 这座城市的空气污染程度曾高达可接受标准的四倍。

examples.en: We want a political solution that is acceptable to all parties.
examples.zh: 我们需要一个各方都可接受的政治解决方案。

examples.en: It is possible to find a solution that is acceptable to both sides.
examples.zh: 有可能找到双方都能接受的解决方案。

senses.def: not very good but good enough
senses.zh: 还可以的；尚可的；差强人意的

examples.en: The food was acceptable, but no more.
examples.zh: 食物还可以，但说不上很好。

examples.en: Inspectors found that teaching standards were acceptable, but could be improved.
examples.zh: 检查员发现教学标准可以接受，但还有待改进。

senses.def: in a way that somebody agrees is of a good enough standard or allowed
senses.zh: 可接受的；令人满意的；可容许的

examples.en: The campaign hopes to achieve an acceptably high standard of street cleanliness.
examples.zh: 该活动希望街道清洁达到可接受的高标准。

senses.def: in a way that is agreed or approved of by most people in a society

examples.en: children who fail to behave acceptably
examples.zh: 不听话的孩子

senses.def: the act of accepting a gift, an invitation, an offer, etc.

examples.en: Please confirm your acceptance of this offer in writing.
examples.zh: 请书面确认你接受这项建议。

examples.en: He made a short acceptance speech/speech of acceptance.
examples.zh: 他发表了简短的提名感言。

examples.en: Invitations have been sent out and 80 acceptances have already been received.
examples.zh: 请帖已经发出，目前收到了 80 份接受邀请的回复。

examples.en: So far we have had one refusal and three acceptances.
examples.zh: 迄今为止，我们收到一个回绝，三个接受。

senses.def: the act of agreeing with something and approving of it

examples.en: The new laws have gained widespread acceptance.
examples.zh: 新法律获得广泛赞同。

senses.def: the process of allowing somebody to join something or be a member of a group
senses.zh: 接纳，接受（为成员、会员等）

examples.en: Your acceptance into the insurance plan is guaranteed.
examples.zh: 你参加保险计划一事已有保证。

examples.en: Social acceptance is important for most young people.
examples.zh: 对大多数青年来说，为社会所接纳很重要。

examples.en: The group is now seeking formal acceptance.
examples.zh: 这个团体现正努力寻求官方的承认。

senses.def: the quality of being willing to accept an unpleasant or difficult situation
senses.zh: 无怨接受（逆境、困境等）；逆来顺受

examples.en: acceptance of death/suffering
examples.zh: 接受死亡／苦难

senses.def: the meaning that a word or expression is generally accepted as having
the opportunity or right to use something or to see somebody/something

examples.en: High-speed internet access has become a necessity.
examples.zh: 高速网络连接已经是必需品。

examples.en: You need a password to get access to the computer system.
examples.zh: 使用这个计算机系统需要密码。

examples.en: access to information/services/resources
examples.zh: 信息／服务／资源的获取

examples.en: access to healthcare/education
examples.zh: 享有医疗／接受教育的权利

examples.en: They are seeking increased access to markets overseas.
examples.zh: 他们正在寻求更多进入海外市场的机会。

examples.en: to provide/allow access to something/somebody
examples.zh: 提供/允许访问某物/某人

examples.en: to restrict/block access to something/somebody
examples.zh: 限制/阻止对某物/某人的访问

examples.en: Journalists were denied access to the President.
examples.zh: 记者被挡住，无法见到总统。

examples.en: Many divorced fathers only have access to their children at weekends (= they are allowed by law to see them only at weekends).
examples.zh: 很多离婚父亲只有在周末才有权见自己的孩子。

senses.def: a way of entering or reaching a place

examples.en: The police gained access through a broken window.
examples.zh: 警察从一扇破窗户钻了进去。

examples.en: Many paths have become overgrown, blocking access.
examples.zh: 许多小路杂草丛生，堵塞了通道。

examples.en: There is easy access by road.
examples.zh: 开车去那儿很方便。

examples.en: We welcome disabled visitors and there is wheelchair access to all parts of the park.
examples.zh: 我们欢迎残疾游客，公园的所有区域均设有轮椅通道。

examples.en: The only access to the farmhouse is across the fields.
examples.zh: 去那农舍的唯一通路是穿过田野。

senses.def: to open a computer file or use a computer system

examples.en: Most people use their phones to access the internet.
examples.zh: 大多数人用手机上网。

examples.en: to access a file/database
examples.zh: 存取（计算机）文件；访问数据库

examples.en: It has never been easier to access information.
examples.zh: 获取信息从未如此简单。

examples.en: All employees can access real-time data.
examples.zh: 所有员工都可以访问实时数据。

examples.en: You should regularly change the password you use to access your online accounts.
examples.zh: 您应该定期更改用于访问在线帐户的密码。

examples.en: Their website can be accessed via the link below.
examples.zh: 可以通过下面的链接访问他们的网站。

senses.def: to be able to have or use something, especially something that you have a right to

examples.en: Being informed is the first step towards accessing better health services.
examples.zh: 知情是获得更好卫生服务的第一步。

examples.en: States need to understand how to access the federal resources that are available.
examples.zh: 各州需要了解如何获取可用的联邦资源。

examples.en: Businesses often provide their products at a discount in order to access a potential market.
examples.zh: 企业经常以折扣价提供产品，以进入潜在市场。

senses.def: to reach, enter or use something

examples.en: The loft can be accessed by a ladder.
examples.zh: 搭梯子可以上阁楼。

examples.en: The balcony is accessed via French doors from the living room.
examples.zh: 从客厅可通过法式门进入阳台。

senses.def: a course of education that prepares students without the usual qualifications, so that they can study at university or college
senses.zh: 高考资格补习班（为不具备所需条件者而设）

examples.en: A popular weekly evening class is the Access Course, which is designed for those considering higher education.
examples.zh: 每周一门受欢迎的晚间课程是Access Course，它是为那些考虑接受高等教育的人设计的。

examples.en: an access course in science and technology
examples.zh: 科学技术入门课程

senses.def: a business company that provides a service to customers, especially one that connects customers to the internet
senses.zh: 服务供应商（尤指互联网服务供应商）

senses.def: a road used for driving into or out of a particular place

examples.en: an access road to an industrial estate
examples.zh: 通往工业区的道路

senses.def: the time taken to obtain data stored on a computer
senses.zh: 存取时间（取得计算机中存储的数据所用的时间）

examples.en: an average access time of less than 100 milliseconds
examples.zh: 平均访问时间小于100毫秒

senses.def: how easy something is to reach, enter, use, see, etc.
senses.zh: 可访问性：某事物到达，输入，使用，查看等的难易程度。

examples.en: Data accessibility and reliability are essential factors in today's business world.
examples.zh: 数据可访问性和可靠性是当今商业世界的重要因素。

examples.en: Accessibility to computers is vital.
examples.zh: 计算机的可访问性至关重要。

examples.en: Improving the accessibility of woodlands to the public is seen as a key issue.
examples.zh: 改善公众对林地的可达性被视为一个关键问题。

senses.def: how easy something is to reach, enter, use, etc. for somebody with a disability

examples.en: The building has limited wheelchair accessibility.
examples.zh: 该建筑的轮椅通道有限。

examples.en: This checklist will help you to evaluate the accessibility of a venue.
examples.zh: 该清单将帮助您评估场地的可达性。

senses.def: how easy something is to understand

examples.en: the accessibility of her poetry
examples.zh: 她的诗歌的易读性

senses.def: that can be reached, entered, used, seen, etc.
senses.zh: 可到达的；可进入的；可使用的；可见到的

examples.en: The remote desert area is accessible only by helicopter.
examples.zh: 只有乘直升机才能进入那偏远的荒漠地区。

examples.en: These documents are not accessible to the public.
examples.zh: 公众无法看到这些文件。

senses.def: that can be reached, entered, used, etc. by somebody who has problems walking
senses.zh: 行动不便者可到达（或可进入、可使用等）的

examples.en: accessible toilets for wheelchair users
examples.zh: 供坐轮椅的人使用的无障碍厕所

examples.en: The beach should be accessible to everyone.
examples.zh: 海滩应向所有人开放。

senses.def: easy to understand

examples.en: Her poetry is always very accessible.
examples.zh: 她的诗作总是非常通俗易懂。

examples.en: a programme making science more accessible to young people
examples.zh: 一项使科学更容易为年轻人所了解的计划

senses.def: easy to talk to and to get to know
senses.zh: 易接近的；易相处的；易打交道的

senses.def: the act of getting a position of rank or power

examples.en: the accession of Queen Victoria to the throne
examples.zh: 维多利亚女王即位

examples.en: Charles I’s accession to the throne
examples.zh: 查理一世即位

examples.en: on her accession to the leadership
examples.zh: 在她担任领导职务时

senses.def: the act of becoming part of an international organization

examples.en: the accession of new member states to the EU
examples.zh: 新成员国正式加入欧盟

examples.en: the new accession states of the EU
examples.zh: 正式加入欧盟的新成员国

senses.def: a thing that is added to a collection of objects, paintings, etc. in a library or museum
senses.zh: （图书馆、博物馆的）新增项目，新增藏品，新增藏书

senses.def: to add fashionable items or extra decorations to something, especially to your clothes
senses.zh: （尤指给衣服）加时髦配件，加装饰物

senses.def: an extra piece of equipment that is useful but not essential or that can be added to something else as a decoration

examples.en: We stock a large range of bicycle accessories.
examples.zh: 我们库存了各类自行车配件。

examples.en: Our catalogue now includes a range of furnishings and accessories for the home.
examples.zh: 我们的目录现在包括一系列家居家具和配件。

senses.def: a thing that you can wear or carry that matches your clothes, for example a belt or a bag

examples.en: fashion accessories to dress up your wardrobe
examples.zh: 装扮衣橱的时尚配饰

senses.def: a person who helps somebody to commit a crime or who knows about it and protects the person from the police

examples.en: He was charged with being an accessory to murder.
examples.zh: 他被控为谋杀罪的从犯。

examples.en: an accessory before/after the fact (= before/after the crime was committed)
examples.zh: 事前／事后从犯

senses.def: not the most important when compared to others

examples.en: the accessory muscles of respiration
examples.zh: 辅助呼吸肌

senses.def: the part of grammar that deals with the inflections
senses.zh: 语法中处理单词变形的部分

senses.def: an unpleasant event, especially in a vehicle, that happens unexpectedly and causes injury or damage
senses.zh: （交通）事故；意外遭遇；不测事件

examples.en: a car/road/traffic accident
examples.zh: 车祸；公路事故；交通事故

examples.en: He was killed in an accident.
examples.zh: 他死于车祸。

examples.en: One in seven accidents is caused by sleepy drivers.
examples.zh: 每七次交通事故就有一次是驾驶员困倦造成的。

examples.en: The accident happened at 3 p.m.
examples.zh: 事故发生于下午 3 点钟。

examples.en: to have an accident
examples.zh: 出事故

examples.en: a serious/minor accident
examples.zh: 严重／轻微事故

examples.en: a fatal accident (= in which somebody is killed)
examples.zh: 死亡事故

examples.en: Every year in the United Kingdom more than 4 000 people die in accidents in the home.
examples.zh: 在英国，每年有4000多人死于家庭事故。

examples.en: a climbing/riding accident
examples.zh: 登山／骑马意外

examples.en: Take out accident insurance before you go on your trip.
examples.zh: 你去旅行前要办理好意外保险。

examples.en: I didn't mean to break it—it was an accident.
examples.zh: 我不是故意打碎它的，这是个意外。

examples.en: Their boat sank in a freak accident.
examples.zh: 他们的船在一起反常的意外事故中沉没了。

examples.en: His son died in a tragic cycling accident.
examples.zh: 他的儿子死于一场悲惨的自行车事故。

examples.en: There are a number of accident blackspots (= places where lots of accidents happen) on that road.
examples.zh: 那条路上有许多事故多发点。

examples.en: We don't know the cause of the accident.
examples.zh: 我们不知道事故的原因。

examples.en: She was badly injured in a motorcycle accident.
examples.zh: 她在一场摩托车事故中受了重伤。

senses.def: something that happens by chance and without an obvious cause

examples.en: Their early arrival was just an accident.
examples.zh: 他们早到仅仅是偶然而已。

examples.en: It is no accident that lawn tennis was invented in England.
examples.zh: 草地网球在英国发明绝非偶然。

examples.en: an accident of birth/fate/history (= describing facts and events that are due to chance or circumstances)
examples.zh: 出生／命运／历史的偶然性

senses.def: a thing or person that is very likely to cause danger or a problem in the future because of the condition it is in or the way they behave

examples.en: Any one of these nuclear plants may be a disaster waiting to happen.
examples.zh: 这些核电厂中的任何一个都可能会成为灾难隐患。

senses.def: people say accidents will happen
in a way that is not planned or organized

examples.en: We met by accident at the airport.
examples.zh: 我们在机场不期而遇。

examples.en: Helen got into acting purely by accident.
examples.zh: 海伦当演员完全出于偶然。

examples.en: It happened, whether by accident or design, that Steve and I were the last two people to leave.
examples.zh: 不知是偶然还是事先安排，史蒂夫和我是最后离开的两个人。

senses.def: a series of unpleasant events caused by bad luck
senses.zh: 一连串的倒霉事；祸不单行

examples.en: The whole affair has been a chapter of accidents from start to finish.
examples.zh: 整个事件自始至终麻烦不断。

items.idm: an accident/a disaster waiting to happen
