examples.zh: 这是博物馆的博客链接。

examples.en: You can post a comment on my blog here.
examples.zh: 你可以在我的博客上发表评论。

examples.en: You can read about my trip in my blog.
examples.zh: 你可以在我的博客上阅读我的旅行故事。

examples.en: He writes a blog about living with diabetes.
examples.zh: 他有一个讲述糖尿病患者生活状况的博客。

senses.def: to keep a blog; to write something in a blog

examples.en: I will be blogging from the convention all week.
examples.zh: 整个一星期我都会写博客对大会进行报道。

examples.en: Here are some reactions to the story I blogged this morning.
examples.zh: 下面是对我今天上午所写博客文章的一些回应。

examples.en: He blogged that there wasn't much happening.
examples.zh: 他在博客中表示，没有发生太多事情。

examples.en: Make sure that the facts you blog about are accurate.
examples.zh: 确保您博客中的事实准确无误。

senses.def: a piece of writing that forms part of a blog

examples.en: I wrote a series of blog posts about my trip to Vietnam.
examples.zh: 我写了关于自己到越南旅行的系列博文。

examples.en: I read your previous blog post on this topic.
examples.zh: 我读过您之前关于这个主题的博客文章。

senses.def: interesting enough to be a topic for a blog
senses.zh: 可作博客话题的；可写博客的

examples.en: That’s definitely a bloggable topic.
examples.zh: 这绝对是一个可以写博客的话题。

examples.en: The film gave me a whole range of bloggable ideas.
examples.zh: 这部电影给了我各种写博客的点子。

examples.en: She was hoping to find some bloggable material.
examples.zh: 她希望找到一些可写博客的材料。

senses.def: a person who writes a blog
typical of a blog

examples.en: The article is quite bloggy, with lots of opinions rather than facts.
examples.zh: 这是颇为典型的博客文章，观点远多于事实。

senses.def: all the personal websites that exist on the internet, viewed as a network of people communicating with each other

examples.en: It's one of the top stories in the blogosphere.
examples.zh: 那件事是博客圈热门的话题之一。

examples.en: the growing influence of the political blogosphere
examples.zh: 政治博客世界与日俱增的影响力

examples.en: The story moved from the blogosphere to the mainstream press.
examples.zh: 这个故事从博客圈转移到了主流媒体。

examples.en: The blogs are part of a constantly expanding blogosphere.
examples.zh: 这些博客是不断扩大的博客圈的一部分。

senses.def: a list on a website of links to other websites that the website owner thinks are useful or interesting

examples.en: A blogroll can help your blog get more exposure.
examples.zh: 博客卷可以帮助您的博客获得更多曝光。

examples.en: Recent additions to the blogroll are highlighted.
examples.zh: 博客卷中最近添加的内容已突出显示。

senses.def: a man

examples.en: He seemed like a nice bloke.
examples.zh: 他看上去像个好人。

senses.def: behaving in a way that is supposed to be typical of men, especially men enjoying themselves in a group
senses.zh: 举止豪爽的，爷们般的（尤指喜欢成伙作乐）

examples.en: He is a popular politician with a blokeish image.
examples.zh: 他是一位颇受欢迎的政治家，形象酷似男性。

senses.def: pale gold in colour

examples.en: She had long blonde hair.
examples.zh: 她有一头金色长发。

examples.en: The child had short blond curls and large blue eyes.
examples.zh: 这个孩子有一头金色的短卷发和蓝色的大眼睛。

senses.def: having blonde hair

examples.en: a small, blond boy
examples.zh: 一个金发小男孩

examples.en: A blonde-haired girl walked in.
examples.zh: 一名金发少女走了进来。

senses.def: a person, especially a woman, with hair that is pale gold in colour

examples.en: I'm not a natural blonde (= my hair is not naturally blonde).
examples.zh: 我不是天生的金发女郎（=我的头发不是天生的金发女郎）。

senses.zh: 美国流行乐团，成立于1974年，由Deborah Harry担任歌手。他们最成功的唱片包括《玻璃心》（1978），《呼唤我》（1980），《潮高》（1980）和最近的《欢乐》（2017）。

senses.zh: 金发女郎：1930年首次出现在美国的一条流行漫画。主要角色是聪明的金发女郎和她经常感到困惑的丈夫达格伍德·邦斯特德。这些角色还被用于广播电视节目和一系列电影。

senses.def: the red liquid that flows through the bodies of humans and animals

examples.en: He lost a lot of blood in the accident.
examples.zh: 他在那场事故中流了很多血。

examples.en: Blood was pouring out of a cut on her head.
examples.zh: 血不断地从她头上的伤口中涌出。

examples.en: His hands were covered in blood.
examples.zh: 他双手沾满了血。

senses.zh: 布卢姆斯伯里：伦敦市中心地区。大英博物馆和伦敦大学的主要建筑都在布卢姆斯伯里，包括布卢姆斯伯里集团在内的许多名人都曾住过。

senses.def: to make a mistake
an embarrassing mistake that you make in public
a flower or a mass of flowers, especially on a fruit tree or bush
senses.zh: （尤指果树或灌木的）花朵，花簇

examples.en: cherry/orange/apple blossom
examples.zh: 樱桃花；橘子花；苹果花

examples.en: The trees are in blossom.
examples.zh: 树上鲜花盛开。

examples.en: She loved the spring, when the blossom was out.
examples.zh: 她喜欢花朵盛开的春天。

senses.def: to produce blossom

examples.en: The cherry trees blossomed early this year.
examples.zh: 樱桃树今年开花早。

senses.def: to become more healthy, confident or successful
senses.zh: 变得更加健康（或自信、成功）

examples.en: She has visibly blossomed over the last few months.
examples.zh: 她近几个月以来身体明显好多了。

examples.en: Their friendship blossomed into love.
examples.zh: 他们的友谊发展成了爱情。

senses.def: to remove liquid from a surface by pressing soft paper or cloth on it
to make a spot or spots of ink
to do something to damage the opinion that other people have of you
senses.zh: 做出有损形象的事；玷污名誉

senses.def: a spot or dirty mark on something, made by ink

examples.en: There were ink blots all over the paper.
examples.zh: 纸上墨渍斑斑。

senses.def: something that damages the opinion that other people have of you, or your happiness
senses.zh: 有损形象（或幸福）的事情；污点

examples.en: Her involvement in the fraud has left a serious blot on her character.
examples.zh: 她卷入了这桩欺诈案，在她的品格上留下了一个很大的污点。

examples.en: There was just a tiny blot on his happiness.
examples.zh: 他的幸福只是一点点污点。

senses.def: an object, especially an ugly building, that makes a place less beautiful
senses.zh: 影响景观的物体（尤指丑陋建筑物）

examples.en: The power station is a blot on the landscape.
examples.zh: 那个发电厂把景致都破坏了。

senses.def: to do something to damage the opinion that other people have of you
senses.zh: 做出有损形象的事；玷污名誉

senses.def: an object, especially an ugly building, that makes a place less beautiful
senses.zh: 影响景观的物体（尤指丑陋建筑物）

examples.en: The power station is a blot on the landscape.
examples.zh: 那个发电厂把景致都破坏了。

synonyms.words: stain ▪ fingerprint ▪ streak ▪ speck ▪ blot ▪ smear ▪ spot

intro.en: These are all words for a small area of dirt or another substance on a surface.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指污点、斑点、污迹。

items.def: a small area of dirt, a spot or a cut on a surface that makes it look less good:
items.zh: 污点；污渍；斑点；疤痕

examples.en: The kids left dirty marks all over the kitchen floor.
examples.zh: 孩子们把厨房的地板弄得污迹斑斑。

items.def: a dirty mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid:
items.zh: 指污点、污渍

examples.en: blood stains
examples.zh: 血迹

items.def: a mark on a surface made by the pattern of lines on the end of a person’s finger, often used by the police to identify criminals:
items.zh: 指指纹、指印

examples.en: Her fingerprints were all over the gun.
examples.zh: 那支枪上布满了她的指纹。

items.def: a long, thin mark or line that is a different colour from the surface it is on:
items.zh: 指条纹、条痕

examples.en: She had streaks of grey in her hair.
examples.zh: 她头上已是白发绺绺。

items.def: a very small mark, spot or piece of a substance on something:
items.zh: 指小点、污点

examples.en: There isn’t a speck of dust anywhere in the house.
examples.zh: 整间房子一尘不染。

items.def: a spot or dirty mark left on something by a substance such as ink or paint being dropped on a surface
items.zh: 指污点、墨渍

items.def: a mark made by something such as oil or paint being spread or rubbed on a surface
items.zh: 指污迹、油渍、污渍、污点

items.def: a small dirty mark on something:
items.zh: 指污迹、污渍、污点

examples.en: There were grease spots all over the walls.
examples.zh: 墙上满是油渍。

senses.def: to do something to damage the opinion that other people have of you
senses.zh: 做出有损形象的事；玷污名誉

senses.def: to cover or hide something completely

examples.en: Clouds blotted out the sun.
examples.zh: 云遮住了太阳。

senses.def: to deliberately try to forget an unpleasant memory or thought
senses.zh: 有意地忘记（不愉快的记忆或想法）；抹去

examples.en: He tried to blot out the image of Helen's sad face.
examples.zh: 他尽量不去想海伦的那张忧伤的脸。

examples.en: She just wanted to sleep and blot out the terrifying events of the day.
examples.zh: 她只想睡觉，忘掉当天发生的可怕事件。

senses.def: a mark, usually not regular in shape, on skin, plants, material, etc.
senses.zh: （皮肤、植物、物体等上面不规则的）斑点，污点

examples.en: He had come out in (= become covered in) dark red blotches.
examples.zh: 他身上长出了一块块深红色的斑。

senses.def: covered in blotches

examples.en: her blotchy and swollen face
examples.zh: 她的布满斑点的浮肿的脸

senses.def: a large piece of blotting paper
the record of arrests in a police district
soft thick paper used for drying ink

examples.en: a piece/sheet of blotting paper
examples.zh: 一张吸墨纸

senses.def: very drunk

examples.en: He got completely blotto at the party.
examples.zh: 他在聚会上喝得大醉。

senses.def: a piece of clothing like a shirt, worn by women
an offensive term for a weak man, who is not brave or confident
an offensive term for a weak man, who is not brave or confident
a short loose jacket that is gathered together at the middle part of the body
to talk or write in a way that shows that you think you know a lot and have something important to say, when in fact you do not know much and have nothing important to say

examples.en: All radio talk show hosts blab and bloviate about national security.
examples.zh: 所有广播脱口秀主持人都对国家安全大肆宣扬。

senses.def: to send out air from the mouth

examples.en: You're not blowing hard enough!
examples.zh: 你没有用劲吹！

examples.en: The policeman asked me to blow into the breathalyser.
examples.zh: 警察要我对着呼气酒精含量探测器吹气。

examples.en: He drew on his cigarette and blew out a stream of smoke.
examples.zh: 他含着烟卷吸了一口，接着吐出一股烟。

senses.def: when the wind or a current of air blows

examples.en: The birds were singing and a warm wind was blowing.
examples.zh: 鸟儿在歌唱，温暖的风吹过。

examples.en: A cold wind blew from the east.
examples.zh: 东边吹来一股冷风。

examples.en: It was blowing hard.
examples.zh: 刮着大风。

examples.en: It was blowing a gale (= there was a strong wind).
examples.zh: 狂风大作。

senses.def: to be moved by the wind, somebody’s breath, etc.; to move something in this way

examples.en: My hat blew off.
examples.zh: 我的帽子被风吹走了。

examples.en: The door blew open.
examples.zh: 门被风吹开了。

examples.en: I was almost blown over by the wind.
examples.zh: 我被风刮得快倒了。

examples.en: She blew the dust off the book.
examples.zh: 她吹掉了书上的灰尘。

examples.en: The ship was blown onto the rocks.
examples.zh: 强风使船撞上了礁石。

examples.en: The bomb blast blew two passers-by across the street.
examples.zh: 炸弹爆炸的强劲气流把两个行人刮到街的另一边去了。

examples.en: The wind blew the door shut.
examples.zh: 风把门吹关上了。

senses.group: move with wind/breath 风／口吹动

senses.def: if you blow
senses.zh: 吹，吹奏（哨子、乐器等）；（哨子、乐器等）吹奏出音

examples.en: the sound of trumpets blowing
examples.zh: 吹喇叭的声音

examples.en: The referee blew his whistle.
examples.zh: 裁判吹响了哨子。

senses.def: to clear your nose by blowing

examples.en: She grabbed a tissue and loudly blew her nose.
examples.zh: 她抓起了一张纸巾，大声地擤鼻子。

senses.def: to kiss your hand and then pretend to blow
to make or shape something by blowing
senses.zh: 吹出（某物）；把（某物）吹出形状

examples.en: to blow smoke rings
examples.zh: 吐烟圈

examples.en: to blow bubbles (= for example, by blowing onto a thin layer of water mixed with soap)
examples.zh: 吹泡泡

examples.en: to blow glass (= to send a current of air into melted glass to shape it)
examples.zh: 吹制玻璃器皿

senses.def: if a fuse
to break open or apart, especially because of pressure from inside; to make a tyre break in this way

examples.en: The car spun out of control when a tyre blew.
examples.zh: 车胎爆了一个，车随后失去了控制。

examples.en: The truck blew a tyre and lurched off the road.
examples.zh: 这辆卡车爆了一个胎，斜冲出了公路。

senses.def: to break something open with explosives

examples.en: The safe had been blown by the thieves.
examples.zh: 保险柜被窃贼炸开了。

senses.def: to make known something that was secret

examples.en: One mistake could blow your cover (= make your real name, job, intentions, etc. known).
examples.zh: 一不小心就会让你暴露身份。

examples.en: We’re going to blow his operation wide open.
examples.zh: 我们要彻底揭露他的行动。

senses.def: to spend or waste a lot of money on something

examples.en: He inherited over a million dollars and blew it all on drink and gambling.
examples.zh: 他继承了一百多万美元，全部挥霍在饮酒和赌博上了。

senses.def: to waste an opportunity

examples.en: She blew her chances by arriving late for the interview.
examples.zh: 她面试时迟到，结果错过了机会。

examples.en: You had your chance and you blew it.
examples.zh: 你本来有机会，却没有抓住。

senses.def: used to show that you are annoyed, surprised or do not care about something

examples.en: Blow it! We've missed the bus.
examples.zh: 真该死！我们错过了公交车。

examples.en: Well, blow me down! I never thought I'd see you again.
examples.zh: 啊，天哪！我以为再也见不到你了。

examples.en: I'm blowed if I'm going to (= I certainly will not) let him treat you like that.
examples.zh: 我绝不会允许他那么对待你。

examples.en: Let's take a taxi and blow (= never mind) the expense.
examples.zh: 我们乘出租车吧，别在意费用。

senses.def: to leave a place suddenly

examples.en: Let's blow this joint.
examples.zh: 咱们马上离开这家酒吧。

senses.def: to kill yourself/somebody by shooting yourself/them in the head

examples.en: He put a gun to his head and threatened to blow his brains out.
examples.zh: 他用枪指着他的头，威胁说要让他脑袋开花。

examples.en: While cleaning his shotgun he had accidentally blown his own brains out.
examples.zh: 他擦猎枪时意外走火，打烂了自己的脑袋。

senses.def: to vomit
to help somebody have a fresh, lively state of mind again
senses.zh: 使头脑清醒；使振作精神

examples.en: A brisk walk should blow the cobwebs away.
examples.zh: 轻快的散步可以使人头脑清醒。

senses.def: to get very angry
to tell something secret, especially by mistake
to change your opinion about something often
to produce a very strong feeling of pleasure or shock

examples.en: Wait till you hear this. It'll blow your mind.
examples.zh: 等着听听这个吧。它会让你大感意外的。

examples.en: a collection of photographs that will blow your mind
examples.zh: 将会冲击你大脑的一批照片

senses.def: to get rid of your energy, anger or strong emotions by doing something active or noisy
senses.zh: 释放精力；发泄怒气；宣泄感情

examples.en: I went for a long walk to let off steam.
examples.zh: 我走了很长一段路来发泄一下。

examples.en: I like blowing off steam and I like saying things that shock people.
examples.zh: 我喜欢发泄情绪，喜欢说一些令人震惊的话。

senses.def: to destroy somebody/something completely
to show that somebody/something is not good by being very much better than it/them
senses.zh: （以更加优异者）表明…不好，显得…差得多

examples.en: I like my old phone, but this new model blows it out of the water.
examples.zh: 我喜欢我的旧手机，但这个新款比它强多了。

senses.def: to praise your own abilities and achievements
to try to trick somebody or lie to somebody, particularly by saying something is better than it really is
to surprise or impress somebody very much
senses.zh: 使某人万分惊愕；给某人留下深刻印象

senses.def: used by somebody who does not want to do something because it involves too much effort

examples.en: Sod that for a lark! I'm not doing any more tonight.
examples.zh: 拉倒吧！我今晚再也不做了。

senses.def: to use bombs or other weapons to destroy somebody/something completely

examples.en: The plane was blown to pieces when the bomb exploded.
examples.zh: 炸弹爆炸了，飞机被炸成了碎片。

senses.def: to completely destroy somebody/something with an explosion

examples.en: The truck was blown to kingdom come.
examples.zh: 卡车被炸飞到了西天了。

senses.def: to get very angry
if a plan, etc. blows up in your face
to tell somebody in authority about something wrong or illegal that somebody is doing
no problem is so bad that it does not bring some advantage to somebody
senses.zh: 没有绝对的坏事；任何坏事都会有利于某些人

senses.def: to tell people unpleasant facts about something

examples.en: Her article lifts the lid on bullying in the workplace.
examples.zh: 她的文章揭露了职场霸凌的真相。

senses.def: to breathe quickly and loudly through your mouth after physical effort
senses.zh: 气喘吁吁；呼哧呼哧地喘

examples.en: Eventually, puffing and blowing, he arrived at the gate.
examples.zh: 最终，他气喘吁吁地来到了门口。

senses.def: to get an idea of what is likely to happen before deciding what to do
a hard hit with the hand, a weapon, etc.

examples.en: She received a severe blow on the head.
examples.zh: 她头上挨了重重的一击。

examples.en: He was knocked out by a single blow to the head.
examples.zh: 他头上只被打了一下便昏过去了。

examples.en: The two men were exchanging blows.
examples.zh: 那两个人在相互厮打。

examples.en: He landed a blow on Hill's nose.
examples.zh: 他对着希尔的鼻子来了一拳。

senses.def: a sudden event that hurts or damages somebody/something, causing the people affected to be sad or disappointed

examples.en: Losing his job came as a terrible blow to him.
examples.zh: 失业给他造成了沉重的打击。

examples.en: It was a shattering blow to her pride.
examples.zh: 那事彻底摧毁了她的自尊心。

examples.en: The new cuts will be seen as a crippling blow for people on low incomes.
examples.zh: 新的削减措施将被视为对低收入人群的沉重打击。

examples.en: The recent bomb attacks are a serious blow for the peace process.
examples.zh: 最近发生的炸弹袭击事件对和平进程造成严重打击。

examples.en: The blow came at a meeting on Saturday.
examples.zh: 打击是在周六的会议上来到的。

examples.en: The news came as a bitter blow to the staff.
examples.zh: 这个消息对员工是一个沉重的打击。

examples.en: a mortal blow to British industry
examples.zh: 对英国工业的致命打击

examples.en: Can you stay with Cathy tonight? She's had a bit of a blow.
examples.zh: 你今晚能陪陪凯茜吗？她受了点儿打击。

senses.def: the action of blowing

examples.en: Give your nose a good blow (= clear it completely).
examples.zh: 把你的鼻子擤干净。

examples.en: Try to put the candles out in one blow.
examples.zh: 试着一口气吹灭蜡烛。

examples.en: I’ll give three blows on the whistle as a signal.
examples.zh: 我会吹三声哨子作为信号。

senses.def: a description of an event that gives you all the details in the order in which they happen

examples.en: He insisted on giving us a blow-by-blow account of what had happened.
examples.zh: 他坚持要向我们详细讲述所发生的事情。

examples.en: She gave us a blow-by-blow account of the incident.
examples.zh: 她向我们详细讲述了这起事件。

senses.def: to start fighting because of something

examples.en: We almost came to blows over what colour the new carpet should be.
examples.zh: 为了新地毯的颜色，我们差点大打出手。

examples.en: The children came to blows over the new toy.
examples.zh: 孩子们为了争那件新玩具动起手来。

senses.def: to shock somebody/something very much; to be very harmful to somebody/something
senses.zh: 使震惊；给予沉重打击；使受到严重伤害

examples.en: Her sudden death dealt a blow to the whole country.
examples.zh: 她突然逝世，举国上下为之震惊。

senses.def: to hit somebody/something
to make something that is unpleasant seem less unpleasant and easier to accept

examples.en: I should try to soften the blow of this news.
examples.zh: 我应该设法缓解这消息带来的打击。

examples.en: The chancellor may try to soften the blow somewhat with a cut in interest rates.
examples.zh: 财政大臣可能会试图通过降低利率来稍微减弱这一打击。

senses.def: to do something in support of/against a belief, principle, etc.
senses.zh: 维护（或损害）某种信念或原则等

examples.en: He felt that they had struck a blow for democracy.
examples.zh: 他感觉他们维护了民主制度。

examples.zh: 哎呀！我给忘得一干二净了。

senses.def: in a war, used to describe an accident or attack in which people are hit by a bomb or weapon that is fired by their own side

examples.en: Look in the blue pages, under US Department of State.
examples.zh: 查看美国国务院下方的蓝页。

senses.def: a British children's television programme broadcast by the BBC
senses.zh: 自1958年以来，英国广播公司（BBC）播出的英国儿童电视节目。众所周知，它教孩子如何用他们在家里可以找到的物体做东西，并组织活动为慈善机构筹款。主持人还参加了激动人心的挑战。

senses.def: any of the round blue notices that are attached to the front walls of houses, especially in London, to show that a famous person once lived there.
senses.zh: 蓝色标牌（房屋正面墙上悬挂的圆形蓝色标牌，用以表示某位名人曾在此居住过，尤见于伦敦）

senses.def: an honour (sometimes in the form of a blue ribbon
senses.zh: 冠军荣誉，优胜者称号（有时以蓝绶带形式授予冠军得主）

examples.en: a blue-riband event (= a very important one)
examples.zh: 重大事件

senses.def: involving new and interesting ideas for things which are not yet possible or practical
senses.zh: 新颖而未可行的；未能付诸实行的

examples.en: The government has been doing some blue-sky thinking on how to improve school standards.
examples.zh: 就如何提高学校的水平，政府仍然在作一些漫无边际的构想。

examples.en: The laboratory tries to maintain a balance between applied research and blue-sky research.
examples.zh: 实验室试图在应用研究和蓝天研究之间保持平衡。

examples.en: A team of designers have been briefed to come up with blue-sky ideas to overhaul the company’s image.
examples.zh: 一组设计师接到通知，要提出一些大胆的想法来彻底改变公司的形象。

senses.def: a lively American song sometimes called 'Jimmy Crack Corn'. It was written before the American Civil War
senses.zh: 《蓝尾苍蝇》(美国歌曲，有时被称为“吉米开玉米”。这首歌是在美国内战前由丹尼尔·埃米特创作的，他还写过《迪克西》。这首歌在被奴役的人中间很受欢迎，因为它讲述了一个奴隶主的死亡。)

senses.def: a small European bird of the tit
senses.zh: 蓝山雀（欧洲小山雀，头顶、两翼及尾部呈蓝色，胸腹部黄色）

a garden or wild flower with a short stem
a dark blue berry
senses.zh: 越橘蓝色浆果，蓝莓（产于北美，可食）

senses.def: a small North American bird with blue feathers on its back or head
senses.zh: 蓝鸲（北美小鸟，背或头有蓝色羽毛）

a blue-coloured sea fish that is caught for sport and food

examples.zh: 他们在钓蓝鱼。

senses.def: a large North American bird with blue feathers on its back and a row of feathers (called a crest

senses.def: a player who must prevent the other team from scoring

examples.en: He rarely scores but is an incredibly effective blueliner.
examples.zh: 他很少进球得分，却是一名极为出色的防守球员。

senses.def: the quality of being blue in colour; the degree to which something is blue

examples.en: the blueness of the water

senses.def: a plan which shows what can be achieved and how it can be achieved

examples.en: a blueprint for the privatization of healthcare

senses.def: the pattern in every living cell, which decides how the plant, animal or person will develop and what it will look like

examples.en: DNA carries the genetic blueprint which tells any organism how to build itself.
examples.zh: 脱氧核糖核酸带有决定有机体形成方式的遗传型板。

senses.def: a type of slow sad music with strong rhythms, developed by African American musicians in the southern US
senses.zh: 布鲁斯音乐，蓝调（源于美国南部黑人，节奏感强、缓慢忧郁）

examples.en: a bluesy sound/voice

examples.en: Bluetooth-enabled devices

senses.def: to try to make somebody believe that you will do something that you do not really intend to do, or that you know something that you do not really know

examples.en: I don't think he'll shoot—I think he's just bluffing.
examples.zh: 我认为他不会开枪，我想他不过是在吓唬人。

senses.def: to get out of a difficult situation by continuing to tell lies, especially when people suspect you are not being honest
senses.zh: （受到怀疑后）继续蒙混过关，靠说谎摆脱困境

senses.def: an attempt to trick somebody by making them believe that you will do something when you really have no intention of doing it, or that you know something when you do not, in fact, know it

examples.en: It was just a game of bluff.
examples.zh: 那只不过是唬人的把戏。

examples.en: He said he would resign if he didn't get more money, but it was only a bluff.
examples.zh: 他说如果不给他加薪他就辞职，但那不过是虚张声势而已。

senses.def: a steep cliff
senses.zh: （尤指海边或河边的）峭壁，陡岸

senses.def: to tell somebody to do what they are threatening to do, because you believe that they will not be cruel or brave enough to do it
senses.zh: 要求…摊牌，要求…兑现其恫吓（因相信对方不至于或不敢这样做）

examples.en: She was tempted to call his bluff, hardly able to believe he’d carry out his threat.
examples.zh: 她很想逼他亮出底牌，并不相信他会做他威胁要做的事。

senses.def: very direct and cheerful, with good intentions, although not always very polite
senses.zh: 直率豪爽的（尽管有时不够礼貌）

examples.en: Beneath his bluff exterior he was a sensitive man.

examples.zh: 绿中带蓝的地毯

examples.en: to make a terrible blunder
examples.zh: 犯大错

examples.en: a series of political blunders
examples.zh: 一连串政治失误

examples.en: one of the greatest policy blunders in history
examples.zh: 历史上最大的政策失误之一

senses.def: to make a stupid or careless mistake
senses.zh: 犯愚蠢的（或粗心的）错误

examples.en: The government had blundered in its handling of the affair.
examples.zh: 政府在这件事的处理上犯了大错。

senses.def: to move around in a way that is not smooth or steady, knocking into things, as if you cannot see where you are going

examples.en: I could hear him blundering around the bathroom in the dark.
examples.zh: 我能听到他在黑暗中在浴室里跌跌撞撞地走来走去。

senses.def: to knock into something because you move carelessly or are not able to see
to find yourself in a difficult or unpleasant situation by accident
senses.zh: 无意中陷入（困境）；偶然遇到（尴尬事）

examples.en: She realized that she had blundered into a trap.
examples.zh: 她意识到自己掉进了陷阱。

senses.def: to continue doing something in a careless or stupid way
senses.zh: 一再粗心（或荒唐）地做某事；一错再错

examples.en: I wasn’t sure he understood what I was saying, but I blundered on with my explanation.
examples.zh: 我不确定他是否明白我在说什么，但我的解释还是错误的。

senses.def: an old type of gun with a wide end
without a sharp edge or point

examples.en: a blunt knife
examples.zh: 钝刀子

examples.en: This pencil's blunt!
examples.zh: 这支铅笔不尖了！

examples.en: The police said he had been hit with a blunt instrument.
examples.zh: 警方说他遭到了钝器袭击。

senses.def: very direct; saying exactly what you think without trying to be polite

examples.en: She has a reputation for blunt speaking.
examples.zh: 她说话出了名地直截了当。

examples.en: To be blunt, your work is appalling.
examples.zh: 坦率地说，你的活儿干得糟透了。

senses.def: to make something weaker or less effective

examples.en: Age hadn't blunted his passion for adventure.
examples.zh: 岁月没有冲淡他的冒险激情。

examples.en: Living alone in the country had blunted her wits.
examples.zh: 在乡下的独居生活使她的头脑不复敏锐。

senses.def: to make a point or an edge less sharp

synonyms.words: frank ▪ direct ▪ open ▪ outspoken ▪ straight ▪ blunt

intro.en: These words all describe people saying exactly what they mean without trying to hide feelings, opinions or facts.
intro.zh: 以上各词均形容人坦率、坦诚。

items.def: not hiding the truth about something:
items.zh: 指坦率的、坦诚的

examples.en: Thank you for being so honest with me.
examples.zh: 感谢你对我这么坦诚。

items.def: honest in what you say, sometimes in a way that other people might not like:
items.zh: 指坦率的、直率的（有时可能不讨人喜欢）

examples.en: To be frank with you, I think your son has little chance of passing the exam.
examples.zh: 坦白说，我认为你的儿子不大可能通过考试。

items.def: saying exactly what you mean in a way that nobody can pretend not to understand:
items.zh: 指直接的、直率的、坦率的

examples.en: You’ll have to get used to his direct manner.
examples.zh: 你得慢慢习惯他这种直率的方式。

items.def: (approving) (of a person) not keeping thoughts and feelings hidden:
items.zh: 指为人诚恳的、坦诚的、直率的

examples.en: He was quite open about his reasons for leaving.
examples.zh: 他对离开的原因完全未加隐瞒。

items.def: saying exactly what you think, even if this shocks or offends people:
items.zh: 指直率的、坦诚的、直言不讳的

examples.en: She was outspoken in her criticism of the plan.
examples.zh: 她对该计划的批评直言不讳。

items.def: honest and direct:
items.zh: 指坦诚的、直率的

examples.en: I don’t think you’re being straight with me.
examples.zh: 我觉得你没跟我坦诚相见。

items.def: saying exactly what you think without trying to be polite:
items.zh: 指嘴直的、直言不讳的

examples.en: She has a reputation for blunt speaking.
examples.zh: 她说话出了名地直截了当。

senses.def: a heavy object without a sharp edge or point, used as a weapon

examples.en: He died after being hit over the head with a blunt instrument.
examples.zh: 他遭钝器击打头部后死亡。

senses.def: a way of doing something that is not efficient or not sensitive to people's feelings
senses.zh: （做事方式）低效的，不顾他人感受的

examples.en: Low interest rates have become a blunt instrument for generating financial growth.
examples.zh: 低利率已无法高效促进财政增长。

senses.def: in a very direct way, without trying to be polite or kind

examples.en: To put it bluntly, I want a divorce.
examples.zh: 坦白地说，我要离婚。

examples.en: ‘Is she dead?’ he asked bluntly.
examples.zh: “她死了吗？”他冲口而出。

senses.def: the fact of being very direct and of saying exactly what you think without trying to be polite
the fact of being blunt
a shape that you cannot see clearly, often because it is moving too fast

examples.en: The hedges whizzed past in a green blur as we sped along.
examples.zh: 当我们快速行驶时，树篱在绿色模糊中呼啸而过。

examples.en: Everything is a blur when I take my glasses off.
examples.zh: 我摘掉眼镜什么都变得模糊不清。

senses.def: something that you cannot remember clearly

examples.en: The events of that day were just a blur.
examples.zh: 那天发生的事只剩一片模糊的记忆。

senses.def: if the shape or outline of something blurs

examples.en: The writing blurred and danced before his eyes.
examples.zh: 字迹变得一片模糊，在他眼前晃动。

examples.en: The mist blurred the edges of the buildings.
examples.zh: 建筑群在薄雾中若隐若现。

senses.def: if something blurs

examples.en: Tears blurred her eyes.
examples.zh: 泪水模糊了她的视线。

senses.def: to become or make it become difficult to recognize a clear difference between things

examples.en: The differences between art and life seem to have blurred.
examples.zh: 艺术和生活之间的差别似乎已变得模糊不清。

examples.en: The line between make-believe and reality became increasingly blurred.
examples.zh: 虚构与现实之间的界限逐渐模糊。

examples.en: She tends to blur the distinction between her friends and her colleagues.
examples.zh: 她往往将朋友和同事混淆起来。

examples.en: His work has blurred the boundaries between children’s and adults’ fiction.
examples.zh: 他的作品模糊了儿童小说和成人小说之间的界限。

senses.def: a British pop group, one of the most popular of the Britpop
senses.zh: 模糊乐队（英国流行乐团，是1990年代最流行的英国流行乐团之一。他们最成功的专辑包括 Parklife，The Great Escape 和 Think Tank）

senses.def: a short description of a book, a new product, etc., written by the people who have produced it, that is intended to attract your attention and make you want to buy it
senses.zh: （书、新产品等的）宣传语；（生产商等的）产品推介

examples.en: publisher’s blurbs
examples.zh: 出版商的宣传推介

examples.en: The blurb says that this is Tarantino’s greatest movie.
examples.zh: 影片简介上说这是塔兰蒂诺的最佳作品。

senses.def: without a clear outline; not clear

examples.en: blurry, distorted photographs
examples.zh: 模糊走样的照片

examples.en: a blurry policy
examples.zh: 不明确的政策

senses.def: to say something suddenly and without thinking carefully enough

examples.en: She blurted it out before I could stop her.
examples.zh: 我还没来得及制止，她已脱口而出。

examples.en: ‘She’s pregnant,’ Jack blurted.
examples.zh: “她怀孕了，”杰克脱口而出。

examples.en: He blurted out the question without thinking.
examples.zh: 这个问题他想都没想就脱口而出了。

synonyms.words: cry out ▪ exclaim ▪ blurt ▪ burst out

intro.en: These words all mean to shout or say something loudly or suddenly.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含突然大声喊叫、说话之义。

items.def: to shout or say something loudly to attract somebody’s attention:
items.zh: 指大声呼叫或说话以吸引注意

examples.en: I thought I heard someone calling.
examples.zh: 我仿佛听见有人在呼喊。

items.def: to shout something loudly, especially when you need help or are in trouble:
items.zh: 尤指需要帮助或陷入困境时大声呼喊

examples.en: She cried out for help.
examples.zh: 她大声呼救。

items.def: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially because of a strong emotion:
items.zh: 尤指因强烈的情感而突然大声说话

examples.en: ‘It isn’t fair!’ he exclaimed angrily.
examples.zh: “这不公平！”他气愤地喊道。

items.def: to say something suddenly and without thinking carefully enough:
items.zh: 指脱口而出

examples.en: I blurted out the answer without thinking.
examples.zh: 我想都没想就脱口说出了答案。

items.def: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially with a lot of emotion:
items.zh: 尤指突然激动地大声喊叫

examples.en: ‘He’s a bully!’ the little boy burst out.
examples.zh: “他欺负人！”小男孩突然大叫。

senses.def: to become red in the face because you are embarrassed or ashamed
senses.zh: （因尴尬或害羞）脸红，涨红了脸

examples.en: to blush with embarrassment/shame
examples.zh: 尴尬／羞愧得面颊绯红

examples.en: She blushed furiously at the memory of the conversation.
examples.zh: 她一想起那次谈话就气得满脸通红。

examples.en: He looked away, blushing.
examples.zh: 他移开了视线，脸红了。

examples.en: He blushed scarlet at the thought.
examples.zh: 他想起那事便面红耳赤。

senses.def: to be ashamed or embarrassed about something

examples.en: I blush to admit it, but I quite like her music.
examples.zh: 不好意思，但我得承认我很喜欢她的音乐。

examples.en: I blush to think of how I behaved the last time we met.
examples.zh: 我一想起上次我们见面时自己的表现就觉得羞愧。

senses.def: the red colour that spreads over your face when you are embarrassed or ashamed
senses.zh: （因难堪、羞愧）面部泛起的红晕

examples.en: She felt a warm blush rise to her cheeks.
examples.zh: 她感到双颊热辣辣的。

examples.en: He turned away to hide his blushes.
examples.zh: 他转过身去，不让人看见他脸红。

senses.def: a coloured cream or powder that some people put on their cheeks
to save somebody from an embarrassing situation
senses.zh: 不让某人难堪；免得某人丢面子

examples.en: A last minute goal spared their blushes.
examples.zh: 最后一刻的进球让他们没有脸红。

senses.def: to save somebody from an embarrassing situation
senses.zh: 不让某人难堪；免得某人丢面子

examples.en: A last minute goal spared their blushes.
examples.zh: 最后一刻的进球让他们没有脸红。

senses.def: a light pink wine
senses.zh: 玫瑰红葡萄酒；粉红葡萄酒

examples.en: a bottle of blush wine
examples.zh: 一瓶红酒

senses.def: a coloured cream or powder that some people put on their cheeks
to talk in an aggressive or threatening
senses.zh: 气势汹汹地说话，咄咄逼人，威吓（但效果不大）

examples.en: ‘I don't know what you're talking about,’ he blustered.
examples.zh: “我不知道你到底在说什么！”他气势汹汹地说。

examples.en: a blustering bully
examples.zh: 咄咄逼人的恶霸

senses.def: to blow violently

examples.en: Outside the wind was blustering.
examples.zh: 外面风声呼啸。

senses.def: talk that is aggressive and threatening

senses.zh: 鲍勃·弗斯（Bob Fosse）：（1927-87）美国电影导演，曾为卡巴雷特（Cabaret）赢得奥斯卡奖（1972）。他从百老汇开始担任舞者和编舞（为舞蹈设计步法和动作的人），并获得了九项托尼奖。他指导并设计了电影《甜蜜的慈善》（Sweet Charity，1969）和《全爵士》（All That Jazz，1979）（根据自己的生活）的舞蹈。1999年，根据他的最佳作品改编的百老汇音乐剧《福斯》获得了三项托尼奖。

senses.zh: 鲍勃·霍普（Bob Hope）：（1903-2003）美国喜剧演员和喜剧演员，出生于英国。他曾担任杂技演员，广播，电视和电影明星近70年。他以娱乐世界各地的美国士兵而闻名。他的许多电影包括七部“公路电影”系列（包括通往桑给巴尔的路和通往摩洛哥的路），其中他与宾·克罗斯比和多萝西·拉莫尔一起出现。霍普多年来一直在颁发奥斯卡颁奖典礼电视节目，并获得了几项特别的奥斯卡奖。他还于1969年获得总统自由勋章，并于1998年被英国政府授予荣誉骑士勋章。

senses.def: (1945-81) a Jamaican singer and writer of reggae
senses.zh: 鲍勃·马利（Bob Marley）：（1945-81）牙买加歌手和雷鬼音乐作家，他还弹过吉他。他于1965年成立了Wailers小组，使雷鬼音乐在世界范围内广为人知。他的歌曲受到他作为Rastafarian的宗教信仰和对黑人权力的支持的影响。他的专辑包括Burnin'（1973），Rastaman Vibration（1976），Exodus（1977）和Uprising（1980）。他的早逝是由癌症引起的。

senses.def: an animated
senses.zh: 建造者鲍勃（Bob the Builder）：一个动画电视剧，介绍有关鲍勃，建造者，他的朋友和他周围的人的幼儿电视连续剧。这些节目首先在BBC电视台上播出，现在已在30多个国家/地区以不同语言显示。

senses.def: (1902-71) a US golf player. He was the most successful amateur
senses.zh: 鲍比·琼斯（Bobby Jones）：（1902-71）美国高尔夫球手。他是有史以来最成功的业余球员，而且从未成为职业球员。他四次夺得美国公开赛冠军（1923、1926和1929-30）。在1930年，他成为唯一赢得四项主要比赛（美国和英国业余比赛和公开赛）的人。琼斯还帮助在佐治亚州的奥古斯塔建立了美国大师赛。

senses.def: (1941-93) one of the most famous English football players of all time, especially because he was captain of the England team which won the World Cup in 1966. For most of his career he played for the London club West Ham
senses.zh: 鲍比·摩尔（Bobby Moore）：（1941-93）有史以来最著名的英国足球运动员之一，尤其是因为他是1966年赢得世界杯足球赛的英格兰队队长。在他的职业生涯的大部分时间里，他效力于伦敦西汉姆俱乐部（1958-74）。1963年，他22岁，成为有史以来最年轻的英格兰队长。他总共为英格兰效力108次。

examples.en: For this job you will need a good knowledge of both Italian and Spanish.
examples.zh: 担任这项工作需要精通意大利语和西班牙语。

senses.def: to spend time and/or energy doing something

examples.en: ‘Shall I wait?’ ‘No, don't bother’.
examples.zh: “要我等一下吗？”“不，别费事了。”

examples.en: I don't know why I bother! Nobody ever listens!
examples.zh: 我不知道我干吗要浪费时间！根本没人听！

examples.en: If that’s all the thanks I get, I won’t bother in future!
examples.zh: 如果这就是我得到的所有感谢，我以后就不会打扰了！

examples.en: It's not worth bothering with (= using) an umbrella—the car's just outside.
examples.zh: 不必打伞，汽车就停在外面。

examples.en: I don't know why you bother with that crowd (= why you spend time with them).
examples.zh: 我弄不懂你为什么和那伙人浪费时间。

examples.en: He doesn’t bother much about his appearance.
examples.zh: 他不太在意自己的外表。

examples.en: He didn't even bother to let me know he was coming.
examples.zh: 他甚至连通知都没通知我他要来。

examples.en: He hadn't even bothered to read the crucial documents.
examples.zh: 他甚至懒得去阅读那些重要的文件。

examples.en: Doctors never bothered to check his blood pressure.
examples.zh: 医生从来没有费心去检查他的血压。

examples.en: Why bother asking if you're not really interested?
examples.zh: 如果你不是真的感兴趣，干吗费口舌打听呢？

examples.en: I didn't bother trying to explain my feelings.
examples.zh: 我没有费心去解释我的感受。

senses.def: to annoy, worry or upset somebody; to cause somebody trouble or pain
senses.zh: 使（某人）烦恼（或担忧、不安）；给（某人）造成麻烦（或痛苦）

examples.en: The thing that bothers me is…
examples.zh: 让我感到不安的是…

examples.en: That sprained ankle is still bothering her (= hurting).
examples.zh: 她那扭伤的脚踝还在隐隐作痛。

examples.en: She has been bothered by a leg injury.
examples.zh: 她一直受到腿部受伤的困扰。

examples.en: ‘I'm sorry he was so rude to you.’ ‘It doesn't bother me.’
examples.zh: “对不起，他对你太没礼貌。”“没关系。”

examples.en: I don't want to bother her with my problems at the moment.
examples.zh: 我此刻不想让她为我的事操心。

examples.en: Does it bother you that she earns more than you?
examples.zh: 她比你挣的钱多，你是不是觉得不自在？

examples.en: It bothers me to think of her alone in that big house.
examples.zh: 想到她孤零零地待在那所大房子里，我便坐立不安。

senses.def: to interrupt somebody; to talk to somebody when they do not want to talk to you

examples.en: Stop bothering me when I'm working.
examples.zh: 我工作时别来烦我。

examples.en: Let me know if he bothers you again.
examples.zh: 他要是再搅扰你，就告诉我。

examples.en: Sorry to bother you, but there's a call for you on line two.
examples.zh: 很抱歉打扰你一下，二号线有你的电话。

examples.en: Please stop bothering me with all these questions!
examples.zh: 请别拿这么多问题来烦我！

senses.def: to think that somebody/something is important
senses.zh: 认为（某人或某事）重要；关心（某人或某事）

examples.en: I'm not bothered about what he thinks.
examples.zh: 我不在乎他怎么想。

examples.en: ‘Where shall we eat?’ ‘I'm not bothered.’ (= I don't mind where we go.)
examples.zh: “我们去哪里吃饭？”“随便。”

senses.def: used to say that you do not want to spend time and/or energy doing something
senses.zh: （表示不想花时间精力做某事）

examples.en: I should really do some work this weekend but I can't be bothered.
examples.zh: 我这个周末真该做点事了，可我懒得做。

examples.en: All this has happened because you couldn't be bothered to give me the message.
examples.zh: 就是因为你嫌麻烦没通知我，才出了这事。

senses.def: in a state of worry or stress because you are under too much pressure, have a problem, are trying to hurry, etc.
senses.zh: （因压力过大、遇到困难、时间紧迫等）焦灼不安，心慌意乱

senses.def: to not spend time/effort on something, because it is not important or you are not interested in it
senses.zh: 不为某事花费时间（或精力）；不操心

senses.def: trouble or difficulty

examples.en: You seem to have got yourself into a spot of bother.
examples.zh: 你似乎惹上了点麻烦。

examples.en: I don't want to put you to any bother (= cause you any trouble).
examples.zh: 我不想给你添乱子。

examples.en: Don't go to the bother of tidying up on my account (= don't make the effort to do it).
examples.zh: 别为了我费事整理一番。

examples.en: ‘Thanks for your help!’ ‘It was no bother.’
examples.zh: “多谢你的帮助！”“没什么。”

examples.en: Call them and save yourself the bother of going round.
examples.zh: 给他们打个电话就免得你亲自去了。

examples.en: I don’t mind looking after the children; they aren’t any bother.
examples.zh: 我不介意照看这些孩子，他们不烦人。

examples.en: She’s been having a bit of bother with her car.
examples.zh: 她的车出了点问题。

senses.def: an annoying situation, thing or person
senses.zh: 令人烦恼的情况（或事物、人）

examples.en: I hope I haven't been a bother.
examples.zh: 希望我没烦扰你。

senses.def: used to express the fact that you are annoyed about something/somebody

examples.en: Bother! I've left my wallet at home.
examples.zh: 真烦人！我把钱包落在家里了。

examples.en: Oh, bother him! He's never around when you need him.
examples.zh: 哎呀，他可真讨厌！需要他的时候从来都找不到他。

senses.def: to think that somebody/something is important
senses.zh: 认为（某人或某事）重要；关心（某人或某事）

examples.en: I'm not bothered about what he thinks.

examples.zh: “我们去哪里吃饭？”“随便。”

examples.en: I should really do some work this weekend but I can't be bothered.
examples.zh: 我这个周末真该做点事了，可我懒得做。

examples.en: All this has happened because you couldn't be bothered to give me the message.
examples.zh: 就是因为你嫌麻烦没通知我，才出了这事。

senses.def: in a state of worry or stress because you are under too much pressure, have a problem, are trying to hurry, etc.
senses.zh: （因压力过大、遇到困难、时间紧迫等）焦灼不安，心慌意乱

a small building in Scotland for farm workers to live in or for people to shelter in
senses.zh: （苏格兰供农场工人居住或供人栖身的）茅屋，棚屋

examples.en: We spent the night in a shepherd’s bothy.
examples.zh: 我们在牧羊人的小屋里过夜。

senses.def: a group of computers that are controlled by malware
senses.zh: 僵尸网络（指受恶意软件控制的计算机群）

examples.en: The internet has been flooded with botnets, unnoticed by the public.
examples.zh: 互联网上充斥着不为公众关注的僵尸网络。

examples.en: Botnet attacks can be used to damage a competitor’s website.
examples.zh: 僵尸网络攻击可用于损坏竞争对手的网站。

senses.def: to treat somebody with Botox
senses.zh: 肉毒杆菌毒素：用肉毒杆菌毒素治疗某人

examples.en: Which celebrities do you think have been Botoxed?
examples.zh: 你认为哪些名人接受过肉毒杆菌毒素治疗？

senses.def: a substance that makes muscles relax. It is sometimes injected
senses.zh: 保妥适注射液（可用于除皱）

senses.def: a country in southern Africa and an independent member of the Commonwealth since 1966. Its capital city is Gaborone.
senses.zh: 博茨瓦纳（非洲南部国家）

senses.def: (a person) from Botswana
senses.zh: 博茨瓦纳人；博茨瓦纳的；博茨瓦纳人的

senses.def: a glass or plastic container, usually round with straight sides and a narrow neck, used especially for storing liquids

examples.en: a wine/beer/milk/water bottle
examples.zh: 酒瓶；啤酒瓶；奶瓶；水瓶

examples.en: Put the top back on the bottle.
examples.zh: 把瓶盖盖上。

examples.en: a plastic/glass bottle
examples.zh: 塑料/玻璃瓶

examples.en: To open the bottle, you twist and pull out the stopper.
examples.zh: 要打开瓶子，您需要扭转并拉出瓶塞。

examples.en: He threw his message in a bottle into the North Sea.
examples.zh: 他将他的信息装在瓶子里扔进了北海。

senses.def: the amount contained in a bottle

examples.en: We drank a whole bottle of wine.
examples.zh: 我们喝了一整瓶酒。

examples.en: She handed me a bottle of water.
examples.zh: 她递给我一瓶水。

senses.def: alcoholic drink

examples.en: After his wife died, he really hit the bottle (= started drinking heavily).
examples.zh: 他妻子死后，他就酗酒了。

senses.def: a bottle used to give milk to a baby; the milk from such a bottle (used instead of mother’s milk)
senses.zh: （婴儿）奶瓶；奶瓶里的奶（非母乳）

examples.en: It's time for her bottle.
examples.zh: 该给她用奶瓶喂奶了。

senses.def: courage or confidence, for example to do something that is dangerous or unpleasant

examples.en: It took a lot of bottle to do that.
examples.zh: 那样做需要很大的勇气。

examples.en: I didn’t think she’d have the bottle to ask him.
examples.zh: 我没想到她会有勇气问他。

senses.def: to do something that has a big effect and after which it is very difficult or impossible to go back to how things were before
senses.zh: 把魔鬼从瓶子里放出来（比喻引发难以遏制的灾难性后果）

examples.en: When guns were invented, the genie was let out of the bottle.
examples.zh: 当枪给发明出来的时候，便是不可控恶果的开始。

senses.def: to put a liquid into a bottle

examples.en: The wines are bottled after three years.
examples.zh: 那些酒是在三年之后装瓶的。

senses.def: to put fruit or vegetables into glass containers in order to preserve them
senses.zh: 把（水果或蔬菜等）装入玻璃瓶储存

examples.en: Keep your empty jam jars for bottling next year’s fruit.
examples.zh: 保留你的空果酱罐，用于装瓶明年的水果。

senses.def: to not do something, or not finish something, because you are frightened

note.en: This idiom can be expressed in various different ways. Other versions include the genie is out of the bottle and opposite form put the genie back in the bottle. Many people realized the genie was out of the bottle and that free music and movie downloads were here to stay. • The world has failed to put the nuclear genie back in the bottle.
note.zh: 可以用不同的方式来表达。其他版本包括 "the genie is out of the bottle"，以及相反的形式 "put the genie back in the bottle"。 "Many people realized the genie was out of the bottle and that free music and movie downloads were here to stay." （许多人意识到音乐和电影免费下载的风潮已经兴起，无法逆转）• "The world has failed to put the nuclear genie back in the bottle." （世界各国没能控制住核武器的扩散）

items.idm: let the genie out of the bottle

senses.def: to do something that has a big effect and after which it is very difficult or impossible to go back to how things were before
senses.zh: 把魔鬼从瓶子里放出来（比喻引发难以遏制的灾难性后果）

examples.en: When guns were invented, the genie was let out of the bottle.
examples.zh: 当枪给发明出来的时候，便是不可控恶果的开始。

senses.def: to not do something, or not finish something, because you are frightened
to not do something, or not finish something, because you are frightened
a large container in a public place where people can leave their empty bottles so that the glass can be used again (= recycled)
senses.zh: 玻璃瓶回收箱；玻璃瓶回收点

senses.def: artificially made to look blonde
a person whose hair has been artificially made to look blonde
to feed a baby with artificial milk from a bottle
a dark-green colour

examples.en: One woman was in red, the other in bottle green.
examples.zh: 一名女士穿着红色衣服，另一名女士则穿着深绿色衣服。

senses.def: dark green in colour

examples.en: a bottle-green coat
examples.zh: 一件深绿色的大衣

senses.def: a small tool for opening bottles with metal tops, for example beer bottles
to not do something that you had intended to do because you are too frightened
a party to which the people who have been invited are asked to bring a bottle, usually of wine
a shop that sells a variety of alcoholic drinks in bottles, cans, etc. to take away
to not allow other people to see that you are unhappy, angry, etc., especially when this happens over a long period of time
senses.zh: 长时间掩饰，遏制，隐瞒（不快等）

examples.en: Try not to bottle up your emotions.
examples.zh: 尽量不要压抑自己的情感。

senses.def: a narrow or busy section of road where the traffic often gets slower and stops
senses.zh: 瓶颈路段（常引起交通阻塞）

examples.en: He drove around the outside of the town to avoid the bottleneck in the centre.
examples.zh: 他开车绕过镇外，以避免市中心的交通堵塞。

examples.en: a traffic bottleneck
examples.zh: 交通瓶颈

examples.en: Opponents argue that the traffic lights would cause a bottleneck at the junction.
examples.zh: 反对者认为交通灯会在路口造成瓶颈。

senses.def: anything that delays development or progress, particularly in business or industry
senses.zh: （尤指工商业发展的）瓶颈，阻碍，障碍

examples.en: to create/eliminate bottlenecks in the manufacturing process
examples.zh: 创建/消除制造过程中的瓶颈

senses.def: the lowest part of something

examples.en: the bottom of the screen/stairs/hill
examples.zh: 屏幕底部；楼梯底部；山脚

examples.en: Footnotes are given at the bottom of each page.
examples.zh: 脚注附于每页的下端。

examples.en: The book I want is right at the bottom (= of the pile).
examples.zh: 我想要的书就压在（那堆书的）最下面。

examples.en: The wind blew through gaps at the top and bottom of the door.
examples.zh: 风从门顶部和底部的缝隙吹进来了。

examples.en: farmers who lived in the valley bottoms
examples.zh: 住在谷底的农民

senses.def: the part of something that faces downwards and is not usually seen

examples.en: The bottom of the pan was all sticky.
examples.zh: 锅底都粘住了。

examples.en: The ingredients are listed on the bottom of the box
examples.zh: 成分标注见盒底。

senses.def: the lowest surface on the inside of a container

examples.en: Line the bottom of the cage with newspaper.
examples.zh: 给笼子底部垫上报纸。

examples.en: I found some coins at the bottom of my bag.
examples.zh: 我在我的手提包底找到了几枚硬币。

senses.def: the ground below the water in a lake, the sea, a swimming pool, etc.

examples.en: I feel safe as long as I can touch the bottom.
examples.zh: 只要能触到底部我就感到安全。

examples.en: He dived in and hit his head on the bottom.
examples.zh: 他跳进水里，头撞到了池底。

examples.en: The boat sank to the bottom of the sea.
examples.zh: 船沉入海底。

senses.def: the lowest position in a class, on a list, etc.; a person, team, etc. that is in this position
senses.zh: （班级、名单等的）最末位置；排名最后的人（或团队等）

examples.en: When the list came out, my name was near the bottom.
examples.zh: 名单出来了，我的名字接近末尾。

examples.en: I was always bottom of the class in math.
examples.zh: 我的数学成绩总是班上最后一名。

examples.en: a battle between the teams at the bottom of the league
examples.zh: 联盟排名最后的几个队之间的较量

examples.en: You have to be prepared to start at the bottom and work your way up.
examples.zh: 你得准备好从最基层干起，努力向上。

senses.def: the part of the body that you sit on

examples.en: We sat on our bottoms on the damp grass.
examples.zh: 我们屁股坐在潮湿的草地上。

senses.group: part of body 身体部位

senses.def: the lower part of a set of clothes that consists of two pieces

examples.en: a pair of pyjama/tracksuit bottoms
examples.zh: 一条睡裤／运动裤

examples.en: a bikini bottom
examples.zh: 比基尼泳装的短裤

senses.def: the part of something that is furthest from you, your house, etc.

examples.en: There was a stream at the bottom of the garden.
examples.zh: 花园尽头有一条小溪。

examples.en: I went to the school at the bottom of our street.
examples.zh: 我在我们街尾的学校上学。

senses.def: the lower part of a ship that is below the surface of the water
having the type of bottom mentioned

examples.en: a flat-bottomed boat
examples.zh: 平底船

senses.def: used to say what somebody/something is really like
senses.zh: 归根结底；本质上；实际上

examples.en: Their offer to help was at bottom self-centred.
examples.zh: 他们提出要帮忙，这其实还是他们为自己考虑。

senses.def: high up/low down in the structure of an organization or a society
senses.zh: 在（机构或社会的）顶层／底层

examples.en: These workers are at the bottom of the economic heap.
examples.zh: 这些工人处在经济结构的底层。

senses.def: to be the original cause of something, especially something unpleasant
senses.zh: 是某事的根源（或起因、导火线）

examples.en: We need to find out what lies at the bottom of these fears.
examples.zh: 我们需要找出这些恐惧的根源是什么。

examples.en: I'd love to know what lies at the bottom of all this.
examples.zh: 我想知道这一切究竟是怎么一回事。

senses.def: people stop buying or using the products of a particular industry

examples.en: The bottom has fallen out of the travel market.
examples.zh: 旅游市场出现了萧条局面。

senses.def: in the least/most important position in a group of people or things
senses.zh: 处于无足轻重的／举足轻重的地位

examples.en: It’s been 20 years since a British player was top of the pile.
examples.zh: 自从英国球员成为顶尖球员以来，已有 20 年了。

examples.en: The government is doing little to help those at the bottom of the social pile.
examples.zh: 政府几乎没有采取任何措施来帮助那些处于社会底层的人。

senses.def: used to express good wishes when drinking alcohol, or to tell somebody to finish their drink
in a way that is sincere

examples.en: I beg you, from the bottom of my heart, to spare his life.
examples.zh: 我诚心诚意地恳求你饶他一命吧。

examples.en: It was clearly an offer that came from the heart.
examples.zh: 那很明显是由衷的提议。

examples.en: I could tell he spoke from the heart.
examples.zh: 我看得出他这番话是发自内心的。

senses.def: going to every part of a place in a very careful way

examples.en: We cleaned the house from top to bottom.
examples.zh: 我们把房子彻底打扫了一遍。

senses.def: to find out the real cause of something, especially something unpleasant

examples.en: I won’t rest until I’ve got to the bottom of this!
examples.zh: 在弄清楚这件事之前，我是不会休息的！

examples.en: The only way to get to the bottom of it is to confront the chairman.
examples.zh: 弄清事情真相的唯一方法就是跟主席对质。

senses.def: a situation in which companies and countries compete with each other to produce goods as cheaply as possible by paying low wages and giving workers poor conditions and few rights
senses.zh: 逐底竞争（企业或国家通过降低工资、劳动条件和工人权利以尽可能降低生产成本的竞争）

examples.en: They are caught in the cheap food syndrome, the race to the bottom, the chase for the lowest cost of production globally.
examples.zh: 他们陷入了廉价食品综合症、逐底竞争、追求全球最低生产成本的困境。

senses.def: to have to use things or people that are not the best or most suitable because the ones that were the best or most suitable are no longer available
to reach the ground at the bottom of an area of water

examples.en: I put my feet down and touched bottom.
examples.zh: 我把脚放下，触到了底部。

senses.def: to reach the worst possible state or condition
senses.zh: 到最坏境况；到最低点；跌到谷底

examples.en: Her career really touched bottom with that movie.
examples.zh: 那部电影真的使她的事业跌至谷底。

senses.def: in the lowest, last or furthest place or position

examples.en: your bottom lip
examples.zh: 下嘴唇

examples.en: the bottom line/row/edge
examples.zh: 底线；最下面一排；底部边缘

examples.en: on the bottom left/right of the page
examples.zh: 在这一页的左／右下角

examples.en: in the bottom corner of the screen
examples.zh: 在屏幕的下角

examples.en: on the bottom shelf
examples.zh: 在架子底层

examples.en: Their house is at the bottom end of Bury Road (= the end furthest from where you enter the road).
examples.zh: 他们的房子位于贝里路的尽头。

examples.en: Put your clothes in the bottom drawer.
examples.zh: 把你的衣服放在最下面的抽屉里。

examples.en: to go up a hill in bottom gear
examples.zh: 用低挡爬山

examples.en: She was sitting on the bottom step.
examples.zh: 她坐在最下面的台阶上。

senses.def: the lowest or last position in a scale or competition

examples.en: the bottom end of the price range
examples.zh: 最低价位

examples.en: We came bottom with 12 points.
examples.zh: 我们以 12 分垫底。

examples.en: We finished bottom of the league.
examples.zh: 我们在联赛中垫底。

examples.en: They finished six points ahead of bottom club Swindon.
examples.zh: 他们领先垫底俱乐部斯温顿六分。

examples.en: a cut in the bottom income-tax bracket from 15% to 10%
examples.zh: 将最低收入税率从 15% 削减至 10%

examples.zh: 爆炸的巨大力量震碎了所有的窗户。

examples.zh: 袋子在里面瓶子的重量下破裂了。

examples.zh: 她把盘子掉在地上打碎了。

examples.zh: 我的表坏了。

examples.zh: 我可能把洗衣机弄坏了。

examples.en: The dog bit me but didn't break the skin.
examples.zh: 那条狗咬了我，但没咬破皮肤。

examples.zh: 我触犯了法律，应该受到惩罚。

examples.en: People should not be allowed to break the rules.
examples.zh: 不应该允许人们违反规则。

examples.zh: 他违章超速驾驶。

examples.en: Let's break for lunch.
examples.zh: 我们休息一会儿，吃午饭。

examples.zh: 议会下周休会。

examples.zh: 我们很早就休息了，去喝了一杯。

examples.zh: 他们被街上的噪声吵醒了。

examples.zh: 我们途中在牛津停留了一下。

examples.en: She broke the silence by coughing.
examples.zh: 她的咳嗽声打破了寂静。

examples.zh: 他坠落时一棵树接住了他。

examples.zh: 电话铃响起来，打断了我的思路。

examples.zh: 突然有人笑了，咒语被打破了。

examples.zh: 试图冲破长达一年的围困

examples.zh: 资方未能使罢工终止。

examples.zh: 他断绝了与父母的一切关系。

examples.zh: 他终于设法逃脱了袭击他的人。

examples.en: to break somebody’s morale/resistance/resolve/spirit
examples.zh: 瓦解某人的士气／抵抗／决心／精神

examples.en: The government was determined to break the power of the trade unions.
examples.zh: 政府决心削弱工会的力量。

examples.en: The scandal broke him (= ruined his reputation and destroyed his confidence).
examples.zh: 这桩丑闻把他毁了。

examples.zh: 她经不住盘问，招认了一切。

examples.zh: 威廉姆斯五次破掉对手的发球局。

senses.zh: 使心碎；使十分悲伤；使孤寂

examples.zh: 妻子的死使他悲痛欲绝。

examples.zh: 第三天，天气变坏，下了一场猛烈的暴风雨。

examples.zh: 云开日出。

examples.zh: 当他的头浮出水面时，他大口吸了几口气。

senses.def: when the day or dawn

examples.zh: 他们终于离开时正是破晓时分。

senses.group: of day/dawn/storm 白天；黎明；风暴

senses.def: if a piece of news breaks

examples.en: There was a public outcry when the scandal broke.
examples.zh: 丑闻一传开，舆论一片哗然。

senses.zh: （第一个将坏消息向某人）公布，透露，说出

examples.zh: 由谁来把这事告诉她呢？

examples.zh: 我很难过，这消息得由我来告诉你。

examples.en: Just break the news to him gently.
examples.zh: 轻轻地把这个消息告诉他。

senses.def: if somebody’s voice breaks

examples.en: Her voice broke as she told us what had happened.
examples.zh: 当她告诉我们发生了什么事时，她的声音沙哑了。

examples.zh: 她打破了 100 米世界纪录。

examples.zh: 这部影片打破了所有的票房纪录。

examples.zh: 浪涛拍岸的声音

examples.zh: 海浪冲刷着破船的残骸。

examples.zh: 他只用了二十分钟就破解了密码。

examples.zh: 可以给我破开二十美元的钞票吗？

senses.def: a short period of time when you stop what you are doing and rest, eat, etc.

examples.zh: 她正在午休。

examples.zh: 喝咖啡时间；茶歇

examples.zh: 咱们休息会儿吧。

examples.zh: 午餐休息

examples.zh: 上厕所的休息时间

examples.zh: 我工作了一整天，没有休息。

examples.zh: 课间休息时来见我。

examples.zh: 雇员可以有长达一年的停职期。

examples.zh: 我日常生活中的一段小插曲

examples.zh: 他正在从成功的电视节目中休息一下。

examples.zh: 我需要暂停照料孩子，休息一段时间。

examples.zh: 暑假；寒假

examples.zh: 圣诞节/复活节假期

senses.zh: （穿插在电视或广播节目中的）广告时间

examples.zh: 大多数观众倾向于跳过广告时段。

examples.zh: 两／三晚的休息

senses.def: the moment when a situation or a relationship that has existed for a time changes, ends or is interrupted
senses.zh: （持续一段时间的状况或关系的）改变，终止，中断

examples.en: I wanted to leave but was nervous about making the break.
examples.zh: 我想离开，但又担心改变现状。

examples.en: He needed to make a complete break with the past.
examples.zh: 他得与过去彻底告别。

examples.en: a break with tradition (= a change from what is accepted, in something such as art, behaviour, etc.)
examples.zh: 对于传统的突破

examples.en: a break in the weather (= a change from one type of weather to a different one)
examples.zh: 天气的转变

examples.en: a break in diplomatic relations
examples.zh: 外交关系的中断

examples.en: This event represents a real break from tradition.
examples.zh: 这一事件代表着对传统的真正突破。

senses.group: change in situation 状况改变

senses.def: a space or an opening between two or more things

examples.en: We could see the moon through a break in the clouds.
examples.zh: 我们能从云缝里看到月亮。

examples.en: Wait for a break in the traffic before crossing the road.
examples.zh: 要等到暂无车辆来往时，再过马路。

examples.en: The track bends left through a break in the hedge.
examples.zh: 树篱上有一个缺口, 小路由此拐向左

senses.def: an opportunity to do something, usually to get something that you want or to achieve success

examples.en: I got my lucky break when I won a ‘Young Journalist of the Year’ competition.
examples.zh: 我时来运转，在“年度最佳青年记者”竞赛中取胜。

examples.en: We've had a few bad breaks (= pieces of bad luck) along the way.
examples.zh: 我们一路上遭遇了几次厄运。

examples.en: If you just give me a break, you won’t regret it.
examples.zh: 如果你让我休息一下，你就不会后悔。

examples.en: She's the director who gave him his first big break.
examples.zh: 她是给他带来第一次重大突破的导演。

examples.en: It's often difficult for talented newcomers to get the break they deserve.
examples.zh: 对于有才华的新人来说，获得他们应得的休息往往很困难。

senses.def: a place where something, especially a bone in your body, has broken

examples.en: The X-ray showed there was no break in his leg.
examples.zh: X 光照片显示他的腿没有骨折。

senses.def: a win in a game in which your opponent is serving

examples.en: It was her second break in the set.
examples.zh: 这是本盘比赛中她第二次破掉对手的发球局。

senses.def: a series of successful shots by one player; the number of points scored in a series of successful shots

examples.en: He's put together a magnificent break.
examples.zh: 他这杆球打得很不错。

examples.en: a 147 break (= the highest possible break in snooker)
examples.zh: 单杆 147 分（斯诺克中的单杆最高得分）

examples.en: The champion began with breaks of 74 and 58.
examples.zh: 冠军以74杆和58杆的成绩开始。

senses.def: the moment in the early hours of the morning when it begins to get light
a complete end to any connection with a person, an organization, a way of life, etc.
senses.zh: （与人、组织、生活方式等的）彻底决裂

examples.en: She wanted to make a clean break with the past.
examples.zh: 她想与过去完全断绝。

senses.def: a break in a bone in one place
to give somebody a chance; to not judge somebody too severely
senses.zh: 给某人一次机会；不苛求某人

examples.en: Give the lad a break—it's only his second day on the job.
examples.zh: 别苛求这小伙子，他上工才第二天。

senses.def: used when somebody wants somebody else to stop doing or saying something that is annoying, or to stop saying something that is not true
to run towards something in order to try and escape

examples.en: He suddenly leapt up and made a break for the door.
examples.zh: 他突然一跃而起，向门口逃窜。

examples.en: They decided to make a break for it (= to try and escape) that night.
examples.zh: 他们决定那天晚上逃跑。

note.en: Idioms containing break are at the entries for the nouns and adjectives in the idioms, for example break somebody’s heart is at heart.
note.zh: 含 break 的习语，都可在该等习语中的名词及形容词相关词条找到，如 break sb’s heart 在词条 heart 下。

senses.def: the moment in the early hours of the morning when it begins to get light
a complete end to any connection with a person, an organization, a way of life, etc.
senses.zh: （与人、组织、生活方式等的）彻底决裂

examples.en: She wanted to make a clean break with the past.
examples.zh: 她想与过去完全断绝。

senses.def: a break in a bone in one place
to give somebody a chance; to not judge somebody too severely
senses.zh: 给某人一次机会；不苛求某人

examples.en: Give the lad a break—it's only his second day on the job.
examples.zh: 别苛求这小伙子，他上工才第二天。

senses.def: used when somebody wants somebody else to stop doing or saying something that is annoying, or to stop saying something that is not true

items.idm: make a break for something/for it

senses.def: to run towards something in order to try and escape

examples.en: He suddenly leapt up and made a break for the door.
examples.zh: 他突然一跃而起，向门口逃窜。

examples.en: They decided to make a break for it (= to try and escape) that night.
examples.zh: 他们决定那天晚上逃跑。

synonyms.words: break ▪ respite ▪ time out ▪ breathing space

intro.en: These are all words for a short period of time spent relaxing.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示短暂的休息。

items.def: a period of relaxing, sleeping or doing nothing after a period of activity:
items.zh: 指休息、睡眠

examples.en: We stopped for a well-earned rest.
examples.zh: 我们停下来做个应有的休息。

items.def: a short period of time when you stop what you are doing and rest or eat:
items.zh: 指间歇、休息

examples.en: Let’s take a break.
examples.zh: 咱们休息会儿吧。

items.def: a short break from something difficult or unpleasant:
items.zh: 指从困境或不愉快、不舒适的状态中得到暂缓、暂停

examples.en: The drug brought a brief respite from the pain.
examples.zh: 药物暂时缓解了疼痛。

items.def: (especially North American English尤用于美式英语, informal) time for resting or relaxing away from your usual work or studies:
items.zh: 指暂停工作或学习的时间

examples.en: Take time out to relax by the pool.
examples.zh: 去游泳池边歇一歇吧。

items.def: a short rest in the middle of a period of mental or physical effort:
items.zh: 指脑力或体力活动期间的短暂休息、喘息时间

examples.en: This delay gives the party a breathing space in which to sort out its policies.
examples.zh: 这一延误使该党有了喘息之机来厘定其政策。

senses.def: used to wish somebody good luck, especially to an actor before they go on stage
senses.zh: 祝你好运；祝你演出成功

senses.def: to leave a place that you have been hiding in, usually at a high speed
senses.zh: 匆匆离开隐蔽处；冲出躲藏处

examples.en: The vehicles broke cover and headed towards the enemy’s headquarters.
examples.zh: 车辆冲破掩体，向敌军总部驶去。

examples.en: The deer broke cover as the hunters approached.
examples.zh: 猎人接近时，鹿从躲藏的地方跑了出来。

senses.def: to complete a piece of business, etc. without either losing money or making a profit

examples.en: The company just about broke even last year.
examples.zh: 这家公司去年接近收支平衡。

senses.def: to start digging for a new building project

examples.en: They broke ground for the new highway this month.
examples.zh: 他们本月为新高速公路破土动工。

senses.def: to make a new discovery or do something that has not been done before

examples.en: Her architectural designs have broken new ground.
examples.zh: 她的建筑设计开辟了新天地。

examples.en: She broke ground by being the first Black woman to win the award.
examples.zh: 她成为第一位获得该奖项的黑人女性，开创了先河。

senses.def: to make a new discovery or do something that has not been done before

examples.en: Her architectural designs have broken new ground.
examples.zh: 她的建筑设计开辟了新天地。

senses.def: the moment in the early hours of the morning when it begins to get light
to fail to remain in line

examples.en: The police broke ranks and started hitting people with their batons.
examples.zh: 警察散开队形并开始用警棍打人。

senses.def: to refuse to support the group or the organization of which they are members
senses.zh: 不支持所属团体（或组织）

examples.en: Large numbers of MPs felt compelled to break ranks over the issue.
examples.zh: 为数众多的下院议员觉得在这一问题上不得不表示反对。

examples.en: He broke ranks with his fellow Republicans and opposed the war.
examples.zh: 他离开自己的共和党阵营，加入反战行列。

senses.def: to stop somebody from falling onto something hard
senses.zh: 缓和某人的跌势；防止某人跌得很重

examples.en: Luckily, a bush broke his fall.
examples.zh: 幸亏有灌木接着，他摔得不重。

senses.def: to make somebody feel very unhappy

examples.en: She broke his heart when she called off the engagement.
examples.zh: 她取消婚约令他心碎。

examples.en: It breaks my heart to see you like this.
examples.zh: 看到你这个样子我很难过。

senses.def: to change the way you are walking so that you do not walk in the same rhythm as the people you are walking or marching

examples.en: The soldiers turned without once breaking step.
examples.zh: 士兵们转过身来，没有停下脚步。

senses.def: to use a lot of physical effort

examples.en: He hardly needed to break sweat to reach the final.
examples.zh: 他几乎不费劲儿就取得了决赛权。

examples.en: She beat me without even breaking (a) sweat.
examples.zh: 她不费吹灰之力就打败了我。

senses.def: to finish the largest or most important part of a task
senses.zh: 完成（任务等的）主要部分

examples.en: I want to break the back of this translation before the weekend.
examples.zh: 我想在周末之前把这篇翻译做完。

senses.def: to say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party, etc.
senses.zh: （尤指聚会等开始时，用言语或行动）打破隔阂；打头说话

examples.en: Jim organized a few party games to break the ice when people first arrived.
examples.zh: 当人们第一次到达时，吉姆组织了一些聚会游戏来打破僵局。

senses.def: to change what people expect from a situation, especially by acting in a dramatic and original way
senses.zh: 改变…的模式；打破…的模式

senses.def: to change what people expect from a situation, especially by acting in a dramatic and original way
senses.zh: 改变…的模式；打破…的模式

examples.en: She succeeded in breaking the mould of political leadership.
examples.zh: 她成功地打破了政治领导模式。

senses.def: to be the first to tell somebody some bad news
senses.zh: 最先（向…）透露坏消息；说出实情

examples.en: There's no easy way to break the news.
examples.zh: 这个消息不容易说得出口。

examples.en: The police had to break the news to the boy's parents.
examples.zh: 警方不得不向男孩的父母透露这个消息。

senses.def: to release gas from your bowels
to escape suddenly from somebody who is holding you or keeping you prisoner

examples.en: The prisoner broke away from his guards.
examples.zh: 犯人挣脱了看守。

senses.def: to leave a political party, state, etc., especially to form a new one
senses.zh: 脱离，背叛（政党、国家等，尤指为了组建新的）

examples.en: The people of the province wished to break away and form a new state.
examples.zh: 该省人民希望分裂出来，成立一个新国家。

senses.def: to move away from a crowd or group, especially in a race

examples.en: She broke away from the pack and opened up a two-second lead.
examples.zh: 她甩开所有其他赛跑者，以两秒领先。

senses.def: to stop working because of a fault

examples.en: The telephone system has broken down.
examples.zh: 电话系统瘫痪了。

examples.en: We (= the car) broke down on the freeway.
examples.zh: 我们的车在高速公路上抛锚了。

senses.def: to fail

examples.en: Negotiations between the two sides have broken down.
examples.zh: 双方谈判失败了。

examples.en: Their marriage had broken down irretrievably.
examples.zh: 他们的婚姻已破裂，不可挽回。

senses.def: to become very bad

examples.en: Her health broke down under the pressure of work.
examples.zh: 她因工作压力身体垮掉了。

senses.def: to lose control of your feelings and start crying

examples.en: He broke down and wept when he heard the news.
examples.zh: 听到这个消息，他不禁失声痛哭。

examples.en: She broke down in tears as she spoke to reporters.
examples.zh: 她向记者诉说时，忍不住哭了起来。

senses.def: to divide into parts to be analysed

examples.en: Expenditure on the project breaks down as follows: wages $10m, plant $4m, raw materials $5m.
examples.zh: 这项工程的支出费用分项列明如下：工资 1 000 万美元，设备 400 万美元，原料 500 万美元。

senses.def: to make something fall down, open, etc. by hitting it hard

examples.en: Firefighters had to break the door down to reach the people trapped inside.
examples.zh: 消防队员不得不破门而入，解救困在里面的人。

senses.def: to destroy something or make it disappear, especially a particular feeling or attitude that somebody has
senses.zh: 破坏，消除（尤指某种感情或态度）

examples.en: to break down resistance/opposition
examples.zh: 瓦解抵抗／反对

examples.en: to break down somebody’s reserve/shyness
examples.zh: 驱除某人的矜持／胆怯

examples.en: Attempts must be made to break down the barriers of fear and hostility which divide the two communities.
examples.zh: 必须设法消除造成这两个团体不和的恐惧和敌意。

senses.def: to divide something into parts in order to analyse it or make it easier to do

examples.en: Break your expenditure down into bills, food and other.
examples.zh: 把支出费用按账单、食物及其他分类列明。

examples.en: Each lesson is broken down into several units.
examples.zh: 每一课都分成几个单元。

senses.def: to make a substance separate into parts or change into a different form in a chemical process

examples.en: Sugar and starch are broken down in the stomach.
examples.zh: 糖和淀粉在胃里被分解。

senses.def: a time when a company or piece of business earns just enough money to pay for its costs

examples.en: The company expects to reach break-even next year.
examples.zh: 公司预期明年达到盈亏平衡。

examples.en: The group has promised a break-even performance in the second quarter.
examples.zh: 集团承诺第二季度的业绩实现收支平衡。

examples.en: We are closely monitoring costs to bring down the break-even point for the business.
examples.zh: 我们正在密切监控成本，以降低业务的收支平衡点。

senses.def: to suddenly run towards something when you are trying to escape
senses.zh: （试图逃脱时）突然冲向；向…挣脱

examples.en: She had to hold him back as he tried to break for the door.
examples.zh: 他试图向门口逃去，她只好拉住他。

senses.def: to enter a building by force

examples.en: Burglars had broken in while we were away.
examples.zh: 我们不在家时，窃贼闯进屋里了。

senses.def: to train somebody/something in something new that they must do

examples.en: to break in new recruits
examples.zh: 训练新人

examples.en: The young horse was not yet broken in (= trained to carry a rider).
examples.zh: 那匹刚长成的马还没被驯服。

senses.def: to wear something, especially new shoes, until they become comfortable
senses.zh: 把…穿得合身，使舒适自如（尤指新鞋）

senses.def: to interrupt something

examples.en: I longed to break in on their conversation but didn't want to appear rude.
examples.zh: 我很想打断他们的谈话，但又不想显得粗鲁。

examples.en: ‘I didn't do it!’ she broke in.
examples.zh: “不是我干的！”她插嘴说。

senses.def: an entry into a building using force, usually to steal something
senses.zh: 破门而入；闯入；入室偷窃

examples.en: Police were called to three break-ins in the same area last night.
examples.zh: 昨夜警方接到同一地区的三宗入室盗窃的报案。

senses.def: to enter a building by force; to open a car, etc. by force

examples.en: We had our car broken into last week.
examples.zh: 我们的车上周被撬了。

senses.def: to begin laughing, singing, etc. suddenly

examples.en: As the president's car drew up, the crowd broke into loud applause.
examples.zh: 总统的座驾停下时，人群中爆发出热烈的掌声。

senses.def: to suddenly start running; to start running faster than before

examples.en: He broke into a run when he saw the police.
examples.zh: 他看见警察，撒腿就跑。

examples.en: Her horse broke into a trot.
examples.zh: 她的马突然开始加速小跑。

senses.def: to be successful when you get involved in something

examples.en: The company is having difficulty breaking into new markets.
examples.zh: 该公司在打入新市场时遇到困难。

senses.def: to open and use something that has been kept for an emergency

examples.en: They had to break into the emergency food supplies.
examples.zh: 他们不得不动用应急食物储备。

senses.def: to use a banknote
senses.zh: 找开（大面值钞票买小额商品）

examples.en: I had to break into a £20 note to pay the bus fare.
examples.zh: 我只好找开一张 20 英镑的钞票买公共汽车票。

senses.def: to become separated from something as a result of force

examples.en: The back section of the plane had broken off.
examples.zh: 飞机尾部脱落了。

senses.def: to stop speaking or stop doing something for a time

examples.en: He broke off in the middle of a sentence.
examples.zh: 他一句话说了一半就不说了。

examples.en: She broke off abruptly when Jo walked in.
examples.zh: 当乔走进来时，她突然停了下来。

examples.en: I had to break off from the conversation to answer my phone.
examples.zh: 我不得不中断谈话去接电话。

senses.def: to separate something, using force

examples.en: She broke off a piece of chocolate and gave it to me.
examples.zh: 她掰了一块巧克力给我。

senses.def: to end something suddenly

examples.en: Britain threatened to break off diplomatic relations.
examples.zh: 英国威胁说要断绝外交关系。

examples.en: They've broken off their engagement.
examples.zh: 他们突然解除了婚约。

senses.def: to start suddenly

examples.en: They had escaped to America shortly before war broke out in 1939.
examples.zh: 1939 年战争爆发前不久他们逃到了美国。

examples.en: Fighting had broken out between rival groups of fans.
examples.zh: 双方球迷发生了打斗。

examples.en: Fire broke out during the night.
examples.zh: 夜间突然发生了火灾。

senses.def: to escape from a place or situation

examples.en: Several prisoners broke out of the jail.
examples.zh: 几名囚犯越狱了。

examples.en: She needed to break out of her daily routine and do something exciting.
examples.zh: 她需要从日常事务中解脱出来，找点有意思的事做。

senses.def: to suddenly be affected by an unpleasant feeling or problem on your skin

examples.en: Her face broke out in a rash.
examples.zh: 她脸上突然长出一片红疹。

examples.en: He broke out in a cold sweat (= for example, through fear).
examples.zh: 他突然冒出一身冷汗。

senses.def: the point where something, especially a computer program, is interrupted
senses.zh: （尤指计算机程序的）断点，中断点

senses.def: a point that the person who is serving
senses.zh: 破发点；破对方发球局的末点

senses.def: the time when problems become so great that a person, an organization or a system can no longer deal with them
to make new and important discoveries

examples.en: Scientists think they are beginning to break through in the fight against cancer.
examples.zh: 科学家认为他们在对抗癌症的研究中开始有所突破。

senses.def: to make a way through something using force

examples.en: Demonstrators broke through the police cordon.
examples.zh: 示威者冲破了警方的警戒线。

examples.en: The defending champions tried hard to stop the Yale attack, but they managed to break through and score.
examples.zh: 卫冕冠军奋力阻止耶鲁进攻，但最终成功突破得分。

senses.def: to appear from behind clouds

examples.en: The sun broke through at last in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午太阳终于拨云而出。

examples.en: At last the moon broke through the clouds and they could see their way.
examples.zh: 月亮终于冲破云层，他们看清了路。

senses.def: to succeed in dealing with an attitude that somebody has and the difficulties it creates

examples.en: He had finally managed to break through her reserve.
examples.zh: 他终于设法消除了她的拘谨。

senses.def: a period of time between lessons at school
to separate into smaller pieces

examples.en: The ship broke up on the rocks.
examples.zh: 船触礁撞碎了。

senses.def: to come to an end

examples.en: Their marriage has broken up.
examples.zh: 他们的婚姻已经破裂。

senses.def: to go away in different directions

examples.en: The meeting broke up at eleven o'clock.
examples.zh: 会议在十一点散会。

senses.def: to begin the holidays when school closes at the end of a term

examples.en: When do you break up for Christmas?
examples.zh: 你们什么时候放假过圣诞节？

senses.def: to become very weak

examples.en: He was breaking up under the strain.
examples.zh: 过度的劳累使他快要垮了。

senses.def: to laugh very hard

examples.en: She's so funny she just breaks me up.
examples.zh: 她太有趣了，简直让我心碎。

senses.def: when a person who is talking on a mobile phone breaks up
senses.zh: （打移动电话的人）声音不清（因信号受干扰）

senses.def: to make somebody feel upset

examples.en: The thought of hurting her just breaks me up.
examples.zh: 一想到要伤害她我就感到不安。

senses.def: to make something separate into smaller pieces; to divide something into smaller parts

examples.en: The ship was broken up for scrap metal.
examples.zh: 船被拆解成为废铁。

examples.en: Sentences can be broken up into clauses.
examples.zh: 句子可以分成从句。

examples.en: She broke the chocolate up into small pieces.
examples.zh: 她把巧克力弄成小块。

senses.def: to end a relationship, a company, etc.

examples.en: They decided to break up the partnership.
examples.zh: 他们决定拆伙。

senses.def: to make people leave something or stop doing something, especially by using force

examples.en: Police were called in to break up the fight.
examples.zh: 有人叫来了警察制止打斗。

senses.def: to end a relationship with somebody

examples.en: She's just broken up with her boyfriend.
examples.zh: 她刚刚和男朋友分手。

senses.def: the ending of a relationship or an association

intro.zh: 以上各词均形容人有才智、悟性强、聪明。

items.def: good at learning, understanding and thinking in a logical way about things; showing this ability:
items.zh: 指有才智的、悟性强的、聪明的

items.def: (especially North American English尤用于美式英语) quick at learning and understanding things; showing the ability to make good business or personal decisions:
items.zh: 指聪明的、机敏的、精明的

items.def: (sometimes disapproving, especially British English尤用于英式英语) quick at learning and understanding things; showing this ability:
items.zh: 指聪明的、聪颖的

items.def: extremely intelligent or showing a lot of skill:
items.zh: 指聪颖的、技艺高的

items.def: intelligent; quick to learn:
items.zh: 指聪明的、悟性强的

intro.en: These words all describe things that are shining or full of light or colours that are strong and easy to see.
intro.zh: 以上各词均形容事物明亮、光线充足、鲜艳夺目。

items.zh: 指光线充足的、明亮的、色彩鲜明的

examples.zh: 亮黄色的连衣裙

items.def: very bright:
items.zh: 指明亮的、鲜艳的

examples.en: The sky was a brilliant blue.
examples.zh: 天空一片蔚蓝。

items.def: (approving) (of colours) bright and strong:
items.zh: 指（颜色）耀眼的、鲜艳的、醒目的

examples.en: His eyes were a vivid green.
examples.zh: 他的眼睛碧绿。

items.def: (approving) (of colours) bright and strong:

examples.en: The room was decorated in vibrant blues and greens.
examples.zh: 那房间以鲜艳的蓝绿两色装饰。

in a way that is very impressive or shows a lot of skill
senses.zh: 出色地：以一种令人印象深刻或显示出很多技巧的方式

examples.en: to play/perform brilliantly
examples.zh: 出色地演奏/表演

examples.en: a brilliantly simple idea
examples.zh: 一个非常简单的想法

senses.def: very well; in an extremely successful way
senses.zh: 非常好 以极其成功的方式

examples.zh: 计划实施得十分顺利。

senses.def: very brightly; with a lot of light or colour

examples.zh: 两只斟满的酒杯

examples.en: I felt suddenly alive and full to the brim with enthusiasm.
examples.zh: 我突然感觉自己充满了活力，充满了热情。

examples.zh: 她从帽檐下注视着人群。

examples.zh: 宽帽檐草帽

senses.def: having the type of brim

senses.def: to be full of something; to fill something

examples.en: Tears brimmed in her eyes.
examples.zh: 她热泪盈眶。

examples.en: His eyes brimmed with tears.
examples.zh: 他的眼睛里充满了泪水。

examples.en: The team were brimming with confidence before the game.
examples.zh: 该队在赛前信心十足。

examples.en: a young man brimming with confidence
examples.zh: 一个充满自信的年轻人

senses.def: to be so full of a liquid that it flows over the edge

examples.en: My heart was brimming over with happiness.
examples.zh: 我的心里充满了幸福。

senses.def: completely full of something

examples.en: She's certainly brimful of energy.
examples.zh: 她的确精力充沛。

examples.en: a jug brimful of cream
examples.zh: 一满罐奶油

senses.def: the chemical element sulphur
