examples.zh: 我的马跑了最后一名。

senses.def: to become fashionable

examples.en: Long hair for men came in in the sixties.
examples.zh: 男子留长发在 60 年代流行开来。

senses.def: to become available

examples.en: We're still waiting for copies of the book to come in.
examples.zh: 我们仍然在等这本书进货。

senses.def: to have a part in something

examples.en: I understand the plan perfectly, but I can't see where I come in.
examples.zh: 我完全了解这项计划，可是不明白我能起什么作用。

senses.def: to arrive somewhere; to be received

examples.en: The train is coming in now.
examples.zh: 火车现正进站。

examples.en: News is coming in of a serious plane crash in France.
examples.zh: 刚收到的消息说法国发生了一起严重的坠机事故。

examples.en: She has over a thousand pounds a month coming in from her investments.
examples.zh: 她每月从自己的投资中得到超过一千英镑的收入。

senses.def: to take part in a discussion

examples.en: Would you like to come in at this point, Susan?
examples.zh: 苏珊，你愿意在此刻发表意见吗？

senses.def: to be introduced; to begin to be used
to become involved in something

examples.en: If you want to come in on the deal, you need to decide now.
examples.zh: 如果你要做这笔交易，你得现在作出决定。

senses.def: to receive something, especially something unpleasant

examples.en: The government's economic policies have come in for a lot of criticism.
examples.zh: 政府的经济政策遭到很多批评。

senses.def: to be left money by somebody who has died

examples.en: She came into a fortune when her uncle died.
examples.zh: 她在叔叔去世后继承了一大笔财产。

senses.def: to be important in a particular situation

examples.en: I've worked very hard to pass this exam—luck doesn't come into it.
examples.zh: 我为通过这次考试下了很大的苦功，运气不是主要的。

senses.def: to be the result of something
senses.zh: 是…的结果；起源于；根源是

examples.en: I made a few enquiries, but nothing came of it in the end.
examples.zh: 我做过一些查询，但到头来却毫无结果。

examples.en: That comes of eating too much!
examples.zh: 那是吃得太多的结果！

senses.def: to be able to be removed

examples.en: Does this hood come off?
examples.zh: 这风帽能卸下来吗？

examples.en: That mark won't come off.
examples.zh: 那污点去不掉。

senses.def: to take place; to happen

examples.en: Did the trip to Rome ever come off?
examples.zh: 去罗马的事最后成了吗？

senses.def: to be successful; to have the intended effect or result
senses.zh: 成功；达到预期效果（或结果）

examples.en: They had wanted it to be a surprise but the plan didn't come off.
examples.zh: 他们本想一鸣惊人，然而计划却流产了。

senses.def: to be successful/not successful in a fight, contest, etc.

examples.en: I thought they came off very well in the debate.
examples.zh: 我认为他们在辩论中表现非常出色。

senses.def: to fall from something

examples.en: to come off your bicycle/horse
examples.zh: 从自行车／马上跌下

senses.def: to become separated from something

examples.en: When I tried to lift the jug, the handle came off in my hand.
examples.zh: 我刚想提起水壶，壶把子就掉在我的手中了。

examples.en: A button had come off my coat.
examples.zh: 我的外套掉了一颗纽扣。

senses.def: to stop taking medicine, a drug, alcohol, etc.

examples.en: I've tried to get him to come off the tranquillizers.
examples.zh: 我试图说服他停止服用镇静剂。

senses.def: to give a particular impression

examples.en: She always comes off as a snob because she doesn't like to hang out with any of the others.
examples.zh: 她总是显得势利小人，因为她不喜欢和其他人一起出去玩。

examples.en: It came off like he was trying to control us.
examples.zh: 看起来他想控制我们。

senses.def: used to disagree with somebody rudely
senses.zh: （粗鲁地表示不同意）别胡扯，别胡说，住口

examples.en: Come off it! We don't have a chance.
examples.zh: 别胡扯了！我们没机会。

senses.def: used in orders to tell somebody to hurry or to try harder

examples.en: Come on! We don't have much time.
examples.zh: 快点！我们时间不多了。

examples.en: Come on! Try once more.
examples.zh: 加把劲！再试一次。

senses.def: to walk onto the stage
to join a team during a game

examples.en: Wilson came on for Kane ten minutes before the end of the game.
examples.zh: 终场前十分钟，威尔逊上场替下了凯恩。

senses.def: to improve or develop in the way you want

examples.en: The project is coming on fine.
examples.zh: 这项工程进展顺利。

senses.def: used to show that you know what somebody has said is not correct
senses.zh: （表示知道某人所说的话不正确）得了吧

examples.en: Oh, come on—you know that isn't true!
examples.zh: 咳，得了吧，你知道那不是真的！

senses.def: to begin

examples.en: I can feel a cold coming on.
examples.zh: 我觉得要感冒了。

examples.en: I think there's rain coming on.
examples.zh: 我看要下雨了。

examples.en: It came on to rain.
examples.zh: 天下起雨来了。

senses.def: to start

examples.en: What time does the news come on?
examples.zh: 新闻报道什么时候开始？

senses.def: to begin to operate

examples.en: Set the oven to come on at six.
examples.zh: 把烤箱设定在六点钟开始烘烤。

examples.en: When does the heating come on?
examples.zh: 什么时间来暖气？

senses.def: to meet or find somebody/something by chance
an object or action that is intended to attract somebody or to persuade them to do something

examples.en: She was definitely giving him the come-on (= trying to attract him sexually).
examples.zh: 她肯定是在勾引他。

senses.def: to behave in a way that shows somebody that you want to have a sexual relationship with them
senses.zh: 勾引，勾搭（想与其发生性关系）

senses.def: to start talking about a subject

examples.en: I'd like to come on to that question later.
examples.zh: 我想稍后再讨论那个问题。

senses.def: when the sun, moon or stars come out

examples.en: The rain stopped and the sun came out.
examples.zh: 雨停后太阳出来了。

senses.def: to open

examples.en: The daffodils came out early this year.
examples.zh: 水仙花今年开得早。

senses.def: to be produced or published

examples.en: When is her new novel coming out?
examples.zh: 她的新小说何时出版？

senses.def: to become known

examples.en: The full story came out at the trial.
examples.zh: 案情始末在审判时真相大白。

examples.en: It came out that he'd been telling lies.
examples.zh: 后来才知道他一直在说谎。

senses.def: to be shown clearly

examples.en: Her best qualities come out in a crisis.
examples.zh: 她的优秀品质在危难之际显示了出来。

senses.def: when words come out

examples.en: I tried to say ‘I love you,’ but the words wouldn't come out.
examples.zh: 我想说“我爱你”，但这话怎么也说不出口。

senses.def: to say publicly whether you agree or disagree with something
senses.zh: 公开表明（同意或不同意）

examples.en: He came out against the plan.
examples.zh: 他公开表示反对这个计划。

examples.en: In her speech, the senator came out in favour of a change in the law.
examples.zh: 这位参议员在她的讲话中公开赞成修改法律。

senses.def: to tell other people that you are gay

examples.en: My best friend came out when she was 18.
examples.zh: 我最好的朋友18岁时就出柜了。

senses.def: to stop work and go on strike

examples.en: On 10 August the railway workers came out on strike.
examples.zh: 8月10日，铁路工人举行罢工。

senses.def: if a photograph taken on film comes out

examples.en: In the 1950s photographs often didn't come out at all.
examples.zh: 在 20 世纪 50 年代，照片常常冲洗不出来。

senses.def: to be formally introduced into society
to be removed from a place where it is fixed

examples.en: This nail won't come out.
examples.zh: 这颗钉子拔不出来。

senses.def: to be removed from something by washing or cleaning

examples.en: These ink stains won't come out of my dress.
examples.zh: 我衣服上的这些墨水斑点洗不掉。

examples.en: Will the colour come out (= become faint or disappear) if I wash it?
examples.zh: 我若用水洗，它会掉色吗？

senses.def: to add up to a particular cost or sum

examples.en: The total bill comes out at £500.
examples.zh: 账单金额总计为 500 英镑。

senses.def: to become covered in spots, etc. on the skin

examples.en: Hot weather makes her come out in a rash.
examples.zh: 炎热的天气使她起了皮疹。

senses.def: to develop from something

examples.en: The book came out of his experiences in India.
examples.zh: 这本书取材于他在印度的经历。

examples.en: Rock music came out of the blues.
examples.zh: 摇滚乐起源于布鲁斯音乐。

senses.def: to relax and become more confident and friendly with other people
senses.zh: 精神放松、更加自信和友好地与他人交往

examples.en: It was when she started drama classes that she really came out of herself.
examples.zh: 她是在开始学习戏剧课程时才真正不再害羞。

senses.def: to say something, especially something surprising or rude
senses.zh: 说出（尤指令人吃惊或粗鲁的话）

examples.en: He came out with a stream of abuse.
examples.zh: 他讲了一连串的脏话。

examples.en: She sometimes comes out with the most extraordinary remarks.
examples.zh: 她有时说起话来语惊四座。

senses.def: to suddenly feel something

examples.en: to come over funny/dizzy/faint
examples.zh: 突然感到可笑／眩晕／昏眩

examples.en: I come over all shy whenever I see her.
examples.zh: 我每次看到她时都会突然感到很害羞。

senses.def: to be understood
to make a particular impression
senses.zh: 给人以…印象；使产生…印象

examples.en: He came over well in the interview.
examples.zh: 他在面试中给人留下了很好的印象。

senses.def: to come to a place, especially somebody’s house, in order to visit for a short time
to travel from one place to another, usually over a long distance

examples.en: Why don't you come over to England in the summer?
examples.zh: 你为何不在夏天来英格兰呢？

examples.en: Her ancestors came over from Ireland during the famine.
examples.zh: 她的祖先在饥荒期间从爱尔兰来到这里。

senses.def: to change from one side, opinion, etc. to another
to affect somebody

examples.en: A fit of dizziness came over her.
examples.zh: 她感到一阵头晕目眩。

examples.en: I can't think what came over me (= I do not know what caused me to behave in that way).
examples.zh: 我不知道我是怎么了。

senses.def: to become conscious again

examples.en: Your mother hasn't yet come around from the anaesthetic.
examples.zh: 你的母亲麻醉后还没有苏醒过来。

senses.def: to happen again

examples.en: My birthday seems to come around more quickly every year.
examples.zh: 我的生日似乎一年比一年来得快。

senses.def: to come to a place, especially somebody’s house, to visit for a short time

examples.en: Do come around and see us some time.
examples.zh: 务必抽空来看看我们。

senses.def: to change your mood or your opinion

examples.en: He'll never come around to my way of thinking.
examples.zh: 他绝不会改变观点与我的思路一致。

senses.def: to arrive by phone, radio, etc. or through an official organization
senses.zh: （用电话、无线电等或由官方机构）传来

examples.en: A message is just coming through.
examples.zh: 刚有消息传来。

senses.def: to get better after a serious illness or to avoid serious injury
senses.zh: （重病后）康复；避免受严重伤害

examples.en: With such a weak heart she was lucky to come through the operation.
examples.zh: 她的心脏很弱，手术后能活下来真是幸运。

senses.def: to successfully do or complete something that you have promised to do

examples.en: We were worried she wouldn't be able to handle it, but she came through in the end.
examples.zh: 我们担心她没有能力处理那件事，然而她最终说到做到了。

examples.en: The bank finally came through with the money.
examples.zh: 这家银行终于兑现了那笔钱。

senses.def: to become conscious again
to enter your mind

examples.en: The idea came to me in the bath.
examples.zh: 我泡澡时想出了这个主意。

examples.en: It suddenly came to her that she had been wrong all along.
examples.zh: 她突然意识到她一开始就错了。

senses.def: to add up to something

examples.en: The bill came to $30.
examples.zh: 账单金额总计为 30 美元。

examples.en: I never expected those few items to come to so much.
examples.zh: 我根本没想到就那么几件东西合计起来竟要花这么多钱。

senses.def: to reach a particular situation, especially a bad one
senses.zh: 达到（某状况，尤指坏的局面）

examples.en: The doctors will operate if necessary—but it may not come to that.
examples.zh: 必要时医生会施行手术，但也许还不至于此。

examples.en: Who'd have thought things would come to this (= become so bad)?
examples.zh: 谁会想到事情竟会变成这个样子？

senses.def: to return to your normal state
if two or more different people or things come together

examples.en: Three colleges have come together to create a new university.
examples.zh: 三所学院合并成了一所新的大学。

examples.en: Bits and pieces of things he'd read and heard were coming together, and he began to understand.
examples.zh: 他把读到和听到的零碎片段综合起来，便逐渐明白了。

senses.def: to be included in a particular group

examples.en: What heading does this come under?
examples.zh: 这该归入哪一个主题？

senses.def: to be a person that others are attacking or criticizing
senses.zh: 成为（攻击或批评的）目标

examples.en: The head teacher came under a lot of criticism from the parents.
examples.zh: 校长受到了家长的很多批评。

senses.def: to be controlled or influenced by something

examples.en: All her students came under her spell.
examples.zh: 她所有的学生都被她迷住了。

senses.def: to appear above the soil

examples.en: The daffodils are just beginning to come up.
examples.zh: 那些水仙花刚开始破土发芽。

senses.def: to rise

examples.en: We watched the sun come up.
examples.zh: 我们观看了日出。

senses.def: to happen

examples.en: I'm afraid something urgent has come up.
examples.zh: 恐怕有紧急事情发生。

examples.en: We'll let you know if any vacancies come up.
examples.zh: 一有空缺，我们就会通知你。

senses.def: to be mentioned or discussed

examples.en: The subject came up in conversation.
examples.zh: 谈话中提到了这个话题。

examples.en: The question is bound to come up at the meeting.
examples.zh: 会上一定会讨论这个问题。

senses.def: to be going to happen, arrive or be ready soon
senses.zh: 即将发生（或到来、准备好）

examples.en: Her birthday is coming up soon.
examples.zh: 她的生日就快到了。

examples.en: ‘Is lunch ready?’ ‘Coming up!’
examples.zh: “午餐准备好了吗？”“马上就好！”

senses.def: to be dealt with by a court

examples.en: Her divorce case comes up next month.
examples.zh: 她的离婚案在下月审理。

senses.def: if your number, name, ticket, etc. comes up
senses.zh: （在博彩游戏中指号码、名字、奖券等）被抽中，中奖

senses.def: to arrive at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, at the beginning of a term or in order to begin your studies
senses.zh: （大学开学时）到校上学（尤指牛津或剑桥）

senses.def: to come from one place to another, especially from the south of a country to the north or from a smaller place to a larger one
senses.zh: 从…到…（通常指从一国的南部到北部，或从小地方到大地方）

examples.en: Why don't you come up to Scotland for a few days?
examples.zh: 你为何不上苏格兰来住几天？

senses.def: to move towards somebody, in order to talk to them

examples.en: He came up to me and asked me the way to the station.
examples.zh: 他走到我跟前打听去车站的路。

senses.def: to be faced with or opposed by somebody/something

examples.en: We expect to come up against a lot of opposition to the plan.
examples.zh: 我们预料这个计划会遭到很多人的反对。

senses.def: to be considered for a job, an important position, etc.

examples.en: She comes up for re-election next year.
examples.zh: 她明年将再度参加竞选。

senses.def: to be reaching the time when something must be done

examples.en: His contract is coming up for renewal.
examples.zh: 他的合同快到续订期了。

senses.def: to reach as far as a particular point

examples.en: The water came up to my neck.
examples.zh: 水淹到了我的脖子。

senses.def: to reach an acceptable level or standard
senses.zh: 达到（认可的水平或标准）

examples.en: His performance didn't really come up to his usual high standard.
examples.zh: 他的表现没有真正达到他往常的高水平。

examples.en: Their trip to France didn't come up to expectations.
examples.zh: 他们的法国之行未尽如人意。

senses.def: to find or produce an answer, a sum of money, etc.
senses.zh: 找到（答案）；拿出（一笔钱等）

examples.en: She came up with a new idea for increasing sales.
examples.zh: 她想出了增加销售量的新主意。

examples.en: How soon can you come up with the money?
examples.zh: 你什么时候能拿出这笔钱？

senses.def: to meet or find somebody/something by chance
to meet or find somebody/something by chance
if you say that somebody comes/crawls out of the woodwork

examples.en: When he won the lottery, all sorts of distant relatives came out of the woodwork.
examples.zh: 他彩票中奖后，八杆子打不着的亲戚都突然来登门造访。

senses.def: to start being used

examples.en: When do the new regulations come into force?
examples.zh: 新规章什么时候开始执行？

examples.en: The new law comes into force as from midnight tomorrow.
examples.zh: 新法律从明天零点起开始生效。

senses.def: to begin to understand and deal with something difficult
senses.zh: 开始理解并着手处理难题

examples.en: I'm slowly getting to grips with the language.
examples.zh: 我慢慢开始掌握这种语言。

examples.en: They have so far failed to come to grips with the ecological problems.
examples.zh: 迄今为止，他们对生态问题的处理是失败的。

senses.def: to join in an activity for pleasure but without being seriously interested in it
senses.zh: 随大溜；凑凑热闹；逢场作戏

senses.def: to become less/more important or successful in society
senses.zh: 落泊；衰落；倒运；飞黄腾达；发迹；兴盛

senses.def: to be a normal and accepted part of a particular job, situation, etc.
senses.zh: 成为必然的部分（或结果）

examples.en: She has to work late most days, but in her kind of job that goes with the territory.
examples.zh: 她在大部分日子里都得加班，但根据她的工作性质，这是不可避免的。

senses.def: if something comes/springs to mind

examples.en: When discussing influential modern artists, three names immediately come to mind.
examples.zh: 讨论现代有影响力的艺术家时，有三个名字一下子出现在脑海中。

examples.en: I'm sure someone can help you, but no one immediately springs to mind.
examples.zh: 我相信一定有人能帮到你，但一时又想不起来有谁。

senses.def: if a person in public life makes a comeback

examples.en: an ageing pop star trying to stage a comeback
examples.zh: 试图重返歌坛的已经上了年纪的流行音乐歌星

examples.en: The player is on the comeback trail after a serious knee injury.
examples.zh: 这名运动员经历了严重的膝伤之后正准备复出。

senses.def: if a thing makes a comeback
senses.zh: 再度流行并变得时髦；再度获得成功

senses.def: a quick reply to a critical remark
senses.zh: （对批评迅速作出的）反驳，回应

senses.def: a way of holding somebody responsible for something wrong that has been done to you
senses.zh: 可因自身受到伤害而追究某人的责任

examples.en: You agreed to the contract, so now you have no comeback.
examples.zh: 你同意了这份合同，所以现在你不能追究他人的责任了。

senses.def: a ball that is hit back in the direction of the pitcher

examples.en: His arm was broken by a comebacker in the first game of the series.
examples.zh: 他的手臂在系列赛第一场被回击球打中骨折了。

senses.def: a putt

examples.en: She sent the putt about six feet past the hole, then made the comebacker for par.
examples.zh: 她推杆过洞约六英尺，然后回推保帕。

senses.def: a person whose job is to make people laugh by giving a funny performance, for example by telling jokes or funny stories

examples.en: He started out as a stand-up comedian in Liverpool.
examples.zh: 他在利物浦出道时是一个单口喜剧演员。

senses.def: a person who is funny or thinks they are funny

examples.en: The speaker was a bit of a comedian, so it was an amusing session.
examples.zh: 演讲者有点喜剧演员的味道，所以会议很有趣。

senses.def: connected with comedy

examples.en: Many comedic moments feel directed, not spontaneous.
examples.zh: 许多笑点都像是事先排演的，而不是现场发挥的。

senses.def: a woman whose job is to make people laugh, for example by telling jokes or funny stories; a female comedian
senses.zh: 女滑稽演员；女喜剧演员

senses.def: a situation in which a person is not as important as before, or does not get as much respect from other people

examples.en: It was a sad comedown for a band that was so popular only a year ago.
examples.zh: 对于一支一年前还如此受欢迎的乐队来说，这是一次悲伤的衰落。

senses.def: a play, film or TV show that is intended to be funny, usually with a happy ending; plays, films and TV shows of this type

examples.en: a romantic comedy
examples.zh: 浪漫喜剧

examples.en: a black comedy (= a play or film that deals with unpleasant or terrible things in a humorous way)
examples.zh: 黑色喜剧

examples.en: a slapstick comedy
examples.zh: 打闹喜剧

examples.en: He moved to Los Angeles to write comedy.
examples.zh: 他移居到洛杉矶写喜剧。

examples.en: a comedy about an eccentric family
examples.zh: 一部关于一个古怪家庭的喜剧

examples.en: She went on to star in a hit comedy series.
examples.zh: 她继续主演一部热门喜剧系列剧。

examples.en: His TV comedy shows ran during the 70s and 80s.
examples.zh: 他的电视喜剧节目在 70 年代和 80 年代播出。

examples.en: a comedy series/show
examples.zh: 喜剧系列／表演

senses.def: professional entertainment with jokes, short acts, etc. that is intended to be funny

examples.en: The show combines theatre with the best of stand-up and sketch comedy.
examples.zh: 该演出将单口喜剧和喜剧小品的精华融入戏剧。

senses.def: a humorous aspect of something

examples.en: Her imaginative interpretation of the script brought out the comedy inherent in it.
examples.zh: 她对剧本富有想象力的诠释，衬托出了其中固有的喜剧色彩。

examples.en: He didn't appreciate the comedy of the situation.
examples.zh: 他未领略到这种局面的滑稽可笑之处。

examples.en: The visual comedy of this scene is obvious.
examples.zh: 这一幕的视觉喜剧效果显而易见。

senses.def: a funny play, film or book that shows the silly behaviour of a particular group of people
senses.zh: 风俗喜剧，风尚喜剧（讽刺某群体行为的戏剧、电影或书籍）

senses.def: pleasant to look at
anyone who wants to take part in an activity or a competition
senses.zh: 所有申请者；所有想参加者

examples.en: The event is open to all comers.
examples.zh: 所有人均可参加这项比赛。

senses.def: a person who arrives somewhere

examples.en: Early comers can enjoy the festival warm-up act.
examples.zh: 早到者可以欣赏节日暖场演出。

examples.en: Feeding every comer is still a sacred duty.
examples.zh: 给每个来的人提供食物仍然是一项神圣的职责。

senses.def: a person who is likely to be successful
that can be eaten
an item of food
a mass of ice and dust that moves around the sun and looks like a bright star with a tail
the world's first commercial jet
senses.zh: 彗星：1952年由BOAC（英国海外航空公司）运营的世界上第一架商用喷气飞机。彗星的飞行速度几乎是早期飞机的两倍，但是其中三架在1953-54年坠毁，原因是它们所用的金属存在问题制作。他们停止飞行，直到1958年，一种改进型的彗星在大西洋上提供了第一架喷气机服务。

senses.def: a punishment for something bad that you have done, that other people feel you really deserve

examples.en: I was glad to see that the bad guy got his comeuppance at the end of the movie.
examples.zh: 我很高兴看到那个坏蛋在电影的结尾受到了应有的惩罚。

senses.def: a sweet consisting of a nut, seed or fruit covered with sugar
the state of being physically relaxed and free from pain; the state of having a pleasant life, with everything that you need

examples.en: The hotel offers a high standard of comfort and service.
examples.zh: 这家旅馆提供高标准的舒适享受和优质服务。

examples.en: I didn't want to leave the comfort of my bed.
examples.zh: 我不想离开舒适的床。

examples.en: They had enough money to live in comfort in their old age.
examples.zh: 他们有足够的钱舒舒服服地安度晚年。

examples.en: Watch the latest movies in the comfort of your own home.
examples.zh: 在自己家舒舒服服地看最新电影。

examples.en: From the comfort of your own armchair, you can witness all the action live.
examples.zh: 坐在舒适的扶手椅上，您可以现场见证所有活动。

examples.en: I dress for comfort rather than elegance.
examples.zh: 我穿衣服是为了舒适而不是为了优雅。

examples.en: These tennis shoes are designed for comfort and performance.
examples.zh: 这些网球鞋的设计以舒适为本，打起球来发挥更出色。

examples.en: He's beginning to find a comfort level with his teammates now.
examples.zh: 他和队友之间开始有了一定的默契度。

senses.def: a feeling of not suffering or worrying so much; a feeling of being less unhappy

examples.en: I tried to offer a few words of comfort.
examples.zh: 我试图说上几句安慰的话。

examples.en: His words were of little comfort in the circumstances.
examples.zh: 在这种情况下，他的话起不了什么安慰作用。

examples.en: to take comfort from somebody’s words
examples.zh: 从某人的话中得到安慰

examples.en: His family can draw some comfort from the fact that the two men accused of his murder have pleaded guilty.
examples.zh: 被指控谋杀他的两名男子已经认罪，他的家人可以得到一些安慰。

examples.en: We know that they will find comfort in the knowledge that she died doing the job she loved.
examples.zh: 我们知道，当他们知道她死于自己热爱的工作时，他们会感到安慰。

examples.en: The announcement of a few new jobs will provide scant comfort to their many recently redundant employees.
examples.zh: 一些新职位的宣布不会给许多最近被裁员的员工带来多少安慰。

examples.en: If it's any comfort to you, I'm in the same situation.
examples.zh: 我的情况也一样——如果这会让你好受些。

senses.def: a person or thing that helps you when you are suffering, worried or unhappy
senses.zh: 令人感到安慰的人（或事物）

examples.en: Her being with me was such a comfort.
examples.zh: 她和我在一起真是一种安慰。

examples.en: The children have been a great comfort to me through all of this.
examples.zh: 在我经历这一切的日子里，孩子们一直是我的莫大安慰。

examples.en: It's a comfort to know that she is safe.
examples.zh: 知道她安然无恙是令人宽慰的事。

examples.en: It was a comfort to her to know that I was never far away.
examples.zh: 知道我从未远离过她，这对她来说是一种安慰。

examples.en: In some ways it's a comfort that they died together.
examples.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们死在一起是令人宽慰的事。

examples.en: It will be a comfort to her family that justice has been done.
examples.zh: 正义得到了伸张，这对她的家人来说将是一种安慰。

senses.def: a thing that makes your life easier or more comfortable

examples.en: The hotel has all modern comforts/every modern comfort.
examples.zh: 这家旅馆拥有各种现代化的舒适设施。

examples.en: material comforts (= money and possessions)
examples.zh: 物质上的舒适条件（钱财）

examples.en: She desperately missed her home comforts while camping.
examples.zh: 野营时她极为想念家里的舒适。

examples.en: He is someone who would take the comforts of home over the bright lights of Hollywood.
examples.zh: 他是一个愿意享受家的舒适而不喜欢好莱坞的明亮灯光的人。

senses.def: so near that it is uncomfortable or dangerous
senses.zh: 距离过近而令人不适（或不安全）

examples.en: When she leaves the stage, the fans can get a little too close for comfort.
examples.zh: 当她离开舞台时，粉丝可能靠得很近，令她感到不舒服。

examples.en: They got the win but it was a tight match, definitely too close for comfort.
examples.zh: 他们取得了胜利，但这是一场激烈的比赛，绝对是太接近了，让人感到不舒服。

senses.def: to make somebody who is worried or unhappy feel better by being kind and showing sympathy to them

examples.en: The victim's widow was today being comforted by family and friends.
examples.zh: 受害人的遗孀今天正受到亲属和朋友的安慰。

examples.en: The idea that he was not alone comforted him greatly.
examples.zh: 想到自己并不是孤身一人，他舒心多了。

examples.en: I am comforted by the fact that Jamie died doing what he liked best.
examples.zh: 令我欣慰的是，杰米在做他最喜欢的事情时去世了。

examples.en: She comforted herself with the thought that it would soon be spring.
examples.zh: 她想到春天很快就要来临，以此来宽慰自己。

examples.en: He was comforted to know that most people in the class knew even less than he did.
examples.zh: 他很欣慰地知道班上大多数人知道的甚至比他还少。

examples.en: It comforted her to feel his arms around her.
examples.zh: 感受到他的拥抱使她得到安慰。

senses.def: so near that it is uncomfortable or dangerous
senses.zh: 距离过近而令人不适（或不安全）

examples.en: When she leaves the stage, the fans can get a little too close for comfort.
examples.zh: 当她离开舞台时，粉丝可能靠得很近，令她感到不舒服。

examples.en: They got the win but it was a tight match, definitely too close for comfort.
examples.zh: 他们取得了胜利，但这是一场激烈的比赛，绝对是太接近了，让人感到不舒服。

senses.def: a blanket
senses.zh: （儿童借以得到安全感的）安慰毯，安慰物

examples.en: You can't use food as a comfort blanket.
examples.zh: 你不能拿食物当安慰。

senses.def: a short period of time when you leave a meeting, stop on a journey or stop what you are doing in order to go to the toilet
senses.zh: （会议、旅途或工作中让人上洗手间的）短暂休息，休息时间

examples.en: There's time for a quick comfort break now—please be ready to start again in ten minutes.
examples.zh: 现在短暂休息一会儿，十分钟后我们再继续。

senses.def: the act of eating something to make yourself feel happier rather than because you are hungry

examples.en: Avoid unhealthy eating habits such as comfort eating or skipping meals.
examples.zh: 避免不健康的饮食习惯，例如舒适饮食或不吃饭。

senses.def: food that makes you feel better, often because it contains a lot of sugar, or because it reminds you of home
senses.zh: 抚慰人心的食物；疗愈食物

examples.en: As the days get colder, we long for comfort food—home-made cakes and chocolate biscuits.
examples.zh: 随着天气变冷，我们渴望舒适的食物——自制蛋糕和巧克力饼干。

examples.en: Chocolate is a great comfort food.
examples.zh: 巧克力是一种非常好的令人舒心的食物。

senses.def: a toilet

examples.en: There is an area for exercise and a comfort room.
examples.zh: 有一个锻炼区和一间舒适的房间。

senses.def: a room with a toilet in a public place, for example for people who are travelling
a place or situation in which you feel safe or comfortable, especially when you choose to stay in this situation instead of trying to work harder or achieve more
senses.zh: 舒适区，放松区，安乐窝（尤指自我放松、不追求更高成就的状态）

examples.en: Stepping outside your comfort zone and trying new things can be a great experience.
examples.zh: 走出你的安乐窝去尝试一下新事物会是个很棒的经历。

examples.en: We cannot afford to have anyone operating in a comfort zone.
examples.zh: 我们可用不起工作中贪图安逸不求上进的人。

senses.def: a state in which you feel confident and are performing at your best

examples.en: I knew if I could find my comfort zone I would be difficult to beat.
examples.zh: 我知道如果我能达到自己的最佳状态就难以被打败。

senses.def: making you feel physically relaxed; pleasant to wear, sit on, etc.

examples.en: It's such a comfortable bed.
examples.zh: 这床真舒服。

examples.en: These new shoes are not very comfortable.
examples.zh: 这双新鞋穿起来不太舒服。

examples.en: clothes that are comfortable to wear
examples.zh: 穿起来舒适的衣服

examples.en: a warm comfortable house
examples.zh: 温暖舒适的房子

examples.en: Let me slip into something more comfortable (= change into more comfortable clothing).
examples.zh: 让我换件比较舒服的衣服。

senses.def: feeling physically relaxed in a pleasant way; warm enough, without pain, etc.
senses.zh: 愉快放松的；舒服的；安逸的

examples.en: Are you comfortable?
examples.zh: 你感觉舒服吗？

examples.en: She shifted into a more comfortable position on the chair.
examples.zh: 她在椅子上换了个更舒适的姿势。

examples.en: Please make yourself comfortable while I get some coffee.
examples.zh: 我去冲咖啡，您别拘束。

examples.en: The patient is comfortable (= not in pain) after his operation.
examples.zh: 病人手术后感觉良好。

examples.en: This bed is lumpy—I just can't seem to get comfortable.
examples.zh: 这床凹凸不平，我怎么都感觉不舒服。

senses.def: confident about something and not worried or afraid

examples.en: She was clearly quite comfortable and relaxed.
examples.zh: 她显然感到非常舒服和放松。

examples.en: He's more comfortable with computers than with people.
examples.zh: 比起与人相处，他和电脑打交道更能应付自如。

examples.en: I was not entirely comfortable about the plans they had made.
examples.zh: 我有点儿担心他们制订的计划。

examples.en: I didn't feel comfortable about accepting the money.
examples.zh: 收这笔钱让我心里不安。

examples.en: She seems comfortable giving a speech without notes.
examples.zh: 她似乎很乐意在没有笔记的情况下发表演讲。

examples.en: He didn't look comfortable in his role as the vicar.
examples.zh: 他看起来不太适应自己担任牧师的角色。

examples.en: I never feel very comfortable in her presence.
examples.zh: 在她面前我一向不太自在。

examples.en: Students will become more comfortable in expressing their ideas.
examples.zh: 学生将更加自在地表达自己的想法。

senses.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying about the cost

examples.en: They're not millionaires, but they're certainly very comfortable.
examples.zh: 他们不是百万富翁，但也很富足。

examples.en: He makes a comfortable living.
examples.zh: 他过着舒适的生活。

examples.en: They come from comfortable middle-class families.
examples.zh: 他们来自舒适的中产阶级家庭。

examples.en: I had a relatively comfortable life in Brazil.
examples.zh: 我在巴西过得相对富足。

senses.def: quite large; allowing you to win easily

examples.en: The party won with a comfortable majority.
examples.zh: 该政党以明显的多数票获胜。

examples.en: a comfortable 2–0 win
examples.zh: 以 2:0 轻取

synonyms.words: wealthy ▪ prosperous ▪ affluent ▪ well off ▪ comfortable

intro.en: These words all describe somebody/​something that has a lot of money, property or valuable possessions.
intro.zh: 以上各词均用以形容人富有或地方富饶。

items.def: (of a person) having a lot of money, property or valuable possessions; (of a country or city) producing a lot of wealth so that many of its people can live at a high standard
items.zh: 指（人）富有的、富裕的，（国家或城市）富庶的、富饶的

items.def: rich
items.zh: 指富有的、富饶的

items.def: (rather formal) rich and successful
items.zh: 指繁荣的、成功的、兴旺的

items.def: (rather formal) rich and with a good standard of living:
items.zh: 指富裕的：

examples.en: affluent Western countries
examples.zh: 富裕的西方国家

items.def: (often used in negative sentences) rich:
items.zh: （常用于否定句中）指富裕、有钱：

examples.en: His family is not very well off.
examples.zh: 他家境不太宽裕。

items.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying about the cost:
items.zh: 指富裕、宽裕

examples.en: They’re not millionaires, but they’re certainly very comfortable.
examples.zh: 他们不是百万富翁，但也很富足。

senses.def: in a comfortable way

examples.en: All the rooms were comfortably furnished.
examples.zh: 所有的房间都配置了舒适的家具。

examples.en: If you're all sitting comfortably, then I'll begin.
examples.zh: 要是你们都坐好了，那么我就开始。

examples.en: You should be able to live comfortably on your allowance.
examples.zh: 你的津贴应该够你丰衣足食的了。

senses.def: with no problem

examples.en: He can comfortably afford the extra expense.
examples.zh: 他支付这些额外的费用毫无问题。

examples.en: They are comfortably ahead in the opinion polls.
examples.zh: 他们在民意测验中遥遥领先。

senses.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying too much about the cost

examples.en: They’re not millionaires, but they’re comfortably off.
examples.zh: 他们不是百万富翁，但生活还算宽裕。

senses.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying too much about the cost

examples.en: They’re not millionaires, but they’re comfortably off.
examples.zh: 他们不是百万富翁，但生活还算宽裕。

senses.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying too much about the cost

examples.en: They’re not millionaires, but they’re comfortably off.
examples.zh: 他们不是百万富翁，但生活还算宽裕。

senses.def: a person or thing that makes you feel calmer or less worried
senses.zh: 令人感到安慰（或慰藉）的人（或事物）

examples.en: She was hugging a pillow as a comforter.
examples.zh: 她抱着一个枕头作为被子。

senses.def: a type of thick cover for a bed
a large cloth bag that is filled with feathers or other soft material and that you have on top of you in bed to keep yourself warm
in a way that makes you feel calmer and less worried or unhappy

examples.en: She patted him comfortingly on the shoulder.
examples.zh: 她安慰地拍拍他的肩膀。

senses.def: without anything to make a place more comfortable

examples.en: a grey and comfortless room
examples.zh: 灰色且不舒适的房间

senses.def: a plant with large leaves covered with small hairs and small flowers that are like bells in shape
senses.zh: 聚合草（长细茸大叶，开铃状小花）

senses.def: comfortable

examples.en: a comfy armchair/bed
examples.zh: 舒适的扶手椅／床

examples.en: You’ll be nice and comfy in this room.
examples.zh: 您在这个房间里会感到愉快和舒适。

examples.en: There’s a terrace with comfy chairs where we can have a drink.
examples.zh: 有一个露台，配有舒适的椅子，我们可以在那里喝一杯。

examples.en: These slippers aren’t as comfy as my old ones.
examples.zh: 这双拖鞋没有我原来的舒服。

senses.def: humorous and making you laugh

examples.en: a comic monologue/story
examples.zh: 滑稽的长篇独白／故事

examples.en: The play is both comic and tragic.
examples.zh: 这部剧既滑稽又悲惨。

examples.en: She can always be relied on to provide comic relief (= something to make you laugh) at a boring party.
examples.zh: 在沉闷的聚会上，她总是能搞些笑料调剂气氛。

examples.en: He wore a red nose and novelty glasses for comic effect.
examples.zh: 他戴着红鼻子和一副新奇的眼镜，以达到滑稽的效果。

examples.en: a blackly comic futuristic fantasy
examples.zh: 具有黑色喜剧色彩的未来幻想作品

senses.def: connected with comedy (= entertainment that is funny and that makes people laugh)

examples.en: a comic opera
examples.zh: 滑稽歌剧

examples.en: a very fine comic actor
examples.zh: 优秀的喜剧演员

examples.en: Charlie Chaplin was a comic genius.
examples.zh: 查理·卓别林是一位喜剧天才。

senses.def: a magazine, usually for children, that tells stories through pictures

examples.en: superhero comics
examples.zh: 超级英雄漫画

senses.def: the section of a newspaper that contains comic strips
a person who makes people laugh by telling jokes or funny stories

synonyms.words: amusing ▪ entertaining ▪ witty ▪ humorous ▪ comic ▪ hilarious

intro.en: These words all describe somebody/​something that makes you laugh or smile.
intro.zh: 以上各词均用以形容人或事好笑的、滑稽的。

items.def: that makes you laugh:
items.zh: 指好笑的、滑稽的

examples.en: a funny story
examples.zh: 滑稽的故事

items.def: funny and giving pleasure:
items.zh: 指逗人笑的、有乐趣的、好笑的

examples.en: It’s a very amusing game to play.
examples.zh: 这种游戏玩起来非常有趣。

items.def: that you enjoy watching, listening to, doing or experiencing:
items.zh: 指有趣的、令人开心的、使人愉快的

examples.en: It was a very entertaining evening.
examples.zh: 那是一场非常令人开心的晚会。

items.def: clever and amusing; able to say or write clever and amusing things:
items.zh: 指机智的、巧妙的、妙趣横生的、言辞诙谐的

examples.en: a witty remark
examples.zh: 机智的话

items.def: funny and entertaining; showing a sense of humour:
items.zh: 指滑稽有趣的、有幽默感的

examples.en: a humorous look at the world of fashion
examples.zh: 对时装界幽默的审视

items.def: that makes you laugh:
items.zh: 指好笑的、滑稽的

examples.en: Many of the scenes in the book are richly comic.
examples.zh: 这本书里的许多情节都非常滑稽可笑。

items.def: extremely funny
items.zh: 指极其滑稽的

senses.def: a British charity organization that was started in 1985 by a group of comedy actors to raise money for poor people and people with special disadvantages. Once every two years there are comedy programmes on television in which the actors and presenters
senses.zh: 一家英国慈善组织，由一群喜剧演员于1985年成立，旨在为穷人和处境特殊的人们筹集资金。每两年一次在电视上播放喜剧节目，其中演员和主持人要求人们为各种慈善机构汇款。在同一天，人们会做一些愚蠢或有趣的事情来筹集资金。

senses.def: a series of drawings inside boxes that tell a story and are often published in newspapers
senses.zh: （常登载于报纸上的）连环漫画

examples.en: Charles Schulz's classic ‘Peanuts’ comic strip
examples.zh: 查尔斯·舒尔茨的经典漫画《花生漫画》

senses.def: funny, especially because it is strange or silly
senses.zh: 滑稽可笑的；奇特有趣的

examples.en: She is a faintly comical figure who fears being made fun of.
examples.zh: 她是一个有点滑稽的人物，害怕被人取笑。

examples.en: He is a slightly comical figure.
examples.zh: 他是个有点儿滑稽的人物。

examples.en: What made it so comical was that their hats kept falling off.
examples.zh: 使人感觉非常滑稽的是他们的帽子总往下掉。

senses.def: in a way that is funny, especially because it is strange or silly
senses.zh: 滑稽可笑的；奇特有趣的

examples.en: Her performance was almost comically bad.
examples.zh: 她的表现差得几乎可笑。

senses.def: the time when a person reaches the age at which they have an adult’s legal rights and responsibilities
the title of a well-known Scottish song. The words were written by the Scottish poet Robert Burns
senses.zh: 穿越黑麦：苏格兰著名歌曲的标题。这些词是由苏格兰诗人罗伯特·伯恩斯（Robert Burns）写的。

senses.def: the movement of people arriving at and leaving a particular place

examples.en: It's hard to keep track of the children's comings and goings.
examples.zh: 这些孩子来来往往，很难跟得上他们的行踪。

examples.en: There had been lots of comings and goings at the house.
examples.zh: 那座房子一直有许多人进进出出。

examples.en: From her window she could watch the comings and goings of visitors.
examples.zh: 她从窗户可以看到访客来来往往。

senses.def: respect between nations or organizations for each other's laws and customs

examples.en: the comity of nations
examples.zh: 国际礼让

examples.en: This administration pledges to do its best to foster comity and bipartisanship.
examples.zh: 本届政府承诺尽最大努力促进礼让和两党合作。

senses.def: comic
senses.zh: 漫画书，尤其是为成年人写的书

examples.en: the underground comix scene in the ’60s and ’70s
examples.zh: 60 年代和 70 年代的地下漫画场景

senses.def: the mark ( , ) used to separate the items in a list or to show where there is a slight break in a sentence

examples.en: The relative clause is separated by commas.
examples.zh: 关系从句以逗号分隔。

examples.en: You need to put a comma before ‘which’.
examples.zh: 您需要在“which”之前加一个逗号。

senses.def: an order given to a person or an animal

examples.en: Begin when I give the command.
examples.zh: 我发出命令时开始。

examples.en: You must obey the captain's commands.
examples.zh: 你必须服从船长的命令。

examples.en: He issued the command to retreat.
examples.zh: 他下令撤退。

examples.en: Police said he ignored their commands to stop.
examples.zh: 警方表示，他无视他们的停车命令。

senses.def: an instruction given to a computer

examples.en: The computer executes commands successively in the order they arrive.
examples.zh: 计算机按照指令送达的顺序依次执行。

examples.en: What is the startup command for the program?
examples.zh: 程序的启动命令是什么？

senses.def: control and authority over a situation or a group of people

examples.en: He has 1 200 men under his command.
examples.zh: 他掌管着 1 200 人。

examples.en: He has command of 1 200 men.
examples.zh: 有 1 200 人由他管辖。

examples.en: The police arrived and took command of the situation.
examples.zh: 警察到达后就控制了局势。

examples.en: In 1939 he assumed command of all French naval forces.
examples.zh: 1939 年他掌握了法国海军的全部指挥权。

examples.en: There were many disagreements over the command of the peacekeeping forces.
examples.zh: 在维和部队的指挥问题上存在许多分歧。

examples.en: Who is in command here?
examples.zh: 这里谁负责？

examples.en: For the first time in years, she felt in command of her life.
examples.zh: 多少年来第一次，她觉得生活掌握在自己的手里。

examples.en: He looked relaxed and totally in command of himself.
examples.zh: 他看起来很轻松，有绝对的自信完全能控制住自己。

examples.en: the chain of command
examples.zh: 指令串；

examples.en: a breakdown in the command structure
examples.zh: 指挥结构的崩溃

senses.def: a part of an army, air force
senses.zh: （陆军、空军等的）兵团，军区，指挥部，司令部

examples.en: Bomber Command
examples.zh: 轰炸机组的指挥部

senses.def: your knowledge of something; your ability to do or use something, especially a language
senses.zh: 知识；（尤指对语言的）掌握，运用能力

examples.en: Applicants will be expected to have (a) good command of English.
examples.zh: 申请人必须精通英语。

examples.en: She has an excellent command of French.
examples.zh: 她的法语棒极了。

senses.def: if you have a skill or an amount of something at your command

examples.en: With all the words at my command, I could not express how I felt.
examples.zh: 我无法用言语表达我的感受。

examples.en: The vast knowledge he has at his command will be invaluable in the job.
examples.zh: 他掌握着丰富的知识，对工作将会非常有用。

senses.def: to be ready to obey somebody
senses.zh: 听候某人的吩咐；服从某人的支配

examples.en: I'm at your command—what would you like me to do?
examples.zh: 我听从您的吩咐，您要我做什么？

senses.def: used to say that you are ready to do whatever somebody asks you to do
to tell somebody to do something

examples.en: He commanded his men to retreat.
examples.zh: 他命令手下撤退。

examples.en: She commanded the release of the prisoners.
examples.zh: 她下令释放囚犯。

examples.en: ‘Come here!’ he commanded (them).
examples.zh: “过来！”他命令（他们）道。

examples.en: ‘Get back to your room,’ she commanded.
examples.zh: “回你的房间去，”她命令道。

examples.en: The commission intervened and commanded that work on the building cease.
examples.zh: 委员会进行了干预，下令那栋大楼必须停建。

examples.en: The commission commanded that work on the building should cease.
examples.zh: 委员会下令那栋大楼必须停建。

senses.def: to be in charge of a group of people in the army, navy

examples.en: In March 1942 he was appointed to command US naval forces in Europe
examples.zh: 1942 年 3 月，他受命指挥驻欧美国海军。

examples.en: The troops were commanded by General Haig.
examples.zh: 部队由黑格将军统率。

senses.def: to deserve and get something because of the special qualities you have

examples.en: to command sympathy/support
examples.zh: 值得同情／支持

examples.en: She was able to command the respect of the class.
examples.zh: 她赢得了全班的尊敬。

examples.en: The headlines commanded her attention.
examples.zh: 那些标题引起了她的注意。

examples.en: As a top lawyer, he can expect to command a six-figure salary.
examples.zh: 作为首屈一指的律师，他可望拿到六位数的薪资。

senses.def: to be in a position from where you can see or control something

examples.en: The hotel commands a fine view of the valley.
examples.zh: 从这家旅馆俯瞰，下面的峡谷一览无余。

examples.en: They built a castle commanding the river crossing.
examples.zh: 他们建造了一座城堡，指挥渡河。

senses.def: to have control of something; to have something available for use
senses.zh: 控制；拥有…可供使用；掌管

examples.en: The party was no longer able to command a majority in Parliament.
examples.zh: 该党已不能在国会中再占有多数。

examples.en: the power and finances commanded by the police
examples.zh: 警方掌握的权力和资金

senses.def: if you have a skill or an amount of something at your command

examples.en: With all the words at my command, I could not express how I felt.
examples.zh: 我无法用言语表达我的感受。

examples.en: The vast knowledge he has at his command will be invaluable in the job.
examples.zh: 他掌握着丰富的知识，对工作将会非常有用。

senses.def: to be ready to obey somebody
senses.zh: 听候某人的吩咐；服从某人的支配

examples.en: I'm at your command—what would you like me to do?
examples.zh: 我听从您的吩咐，您要我做什么？

senses.def: used to say that you are ready to do whatever somebody asks you to do
operated by instructions, either from another program or from the user through the keyboard
an economy in which production, prices and incomes are decided and fixed by the central government
the letters, symbols, etc. that you use to give instructions to a computer program
senses.zh: （操纵计算机程序的）命令语言，指令语言

senses.def: a line of letters, symbols, etc. that you type to give an instruction to a computer
the part of a spacecraft
senses.zh: （航天器中载人和控制仪器的）指挥舱，指令舱

senses.def: a special performance, for example at a theatre, that is given for a head of state
senses.zh: （为国家元首举行的）专场演出，御前演出

senses.def: the place from which a military unit or other official operation is commanded

examples.en: Police have set up a command post outside the building.
examples.zh: 警方在大楼外面设立了指挥部。

senses.def: the officer in charge of a particular military group or institution

examples.en: the commandant of a prisoner of war camp
examples.zh: 战俘集中营的指挥官

examples.en: Commandant Macdonald
examples.zh: 麦克唐纳指挥官

senses.def: to take control of a building, a vehicle, etc. for military purposes during a war, or by force for your own use
senses.zh: （战争期间为军事目的而）强征，征用；强占

examples.en: The soldiers had commandeered the farm and the villa five months ago.
examples.zh: 五个月前士兵们就已征用了这个农场和这座别墅。

examples.en: A group of young men had commandeered a truck, and were driving around the town in it.
examples.zh: 一群年轻男子霸占了一辆卡车，正开着车在城里到处转。

senses.def: a person who is in charge of something, especially an officer in charge of a particular group of soldiers or a military operation
senses.zh: 负责人；（尤指）司令官，指挥官

examples.en: military/allied/field/flight commanders
examples.zh: 军事／盟军／战地／飞行指挥官

examples.en: the commander of the expedition
examples.zh: 探险队队长

examples.en: General Eisenhower was Supreme Allied Commander in Western Europe.
examples.zh: 艾森豪威尔将军是西欧盟军的最高指挥官。

examples.en: the commander of US forces in Iraq
examples.zh: 驻伊拉克的美军指挥官

senses.def: an officer of fairly high rank in the British or American navy
(in England) a London police officer of high rank
the officer who commands all the armed forces of a country or all its forces in a particular area

examples.en: commander-in-chief of the armed forces
examples.zh: 武装部队总司令

senses.def: a law given by God, especially any of the Ten Commandments
senses.zh: 戒条，圣诫（尤指基督教十诫中的一诫）

examples.en: to keep the Ten Commandments
examples.zh: 遵守十诫

examples.en: Someone brought to his notice the fifth commandment: honour thy father and thy mother.
examples.zh: 有人让他注意到第五条诫命：孝敬父母。

examples.en: You shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God.
examples.zh: 你要谨守耶和华你们的神的诫命。

senses.def: a soldier or a group of soldiers who are trained to make quick attacks in enemy areas
senses.zh: 突击手；突击队；突击队员

examples.en: a commando raid on the north of the island
examples.zh: 突击队袭击该岛北部

senses.def: to not wear underwear under your clothes
to not wear underwear under your clothes
traditional Italian theatre in which the same characters appeared in different plays
senses.zh: 即兴喜剧，假面喜剧（意大利的一种传统戏剧，相同的角色出现在不同的戏剧中）

senses.def: to remind people of an important event or person from the past with a special action or object; to exist to remind people of a person or an event from the past

examples.en: A series of movies will be shown to commemorate the thirtieth anniversary of his death.
examples.zh: 为纪念他逝世 30 周年，有一系列的电影将要上映。

examples.en: A plaque commemorates the battle.
examples.zh: 设了一块匾额来纪念那次战役。

senses.def: an action, or a ceremony, etc. that makes people remember and show respect for an important person or event in the past

examples.en: a commemoration service
examples.zh: 纪念仪式

examples.en: Protests and commemorations took place in several cities on the anniversary of the uprising.
examples.zh: 起义周年纪念日，多个城市举行了抗议和纪念活动。

examples.en: a statue in commemoration of a national hero
examples.zh: 纪念民族英雄的雕像

senses.def: intended to help people remember and respect an important person or event in the past

examples.en: commemorative stamps
examples.zh: 纪念邮票

examples.en: A commemorative plaque on the bridge records the name of the engineer.
examples.zh: 桥上的纪念牌上记录着这位工程师的名字。

senses.def: to begin to happen; to begin something

examples.en: The meeting is scheduled to commence at noon.
examples.zh: 会议定于午间召开。

examples.en: I will be on leave during the week commencing 15 February.
examples.zh: 我将从 2 月 15 日开始一周的休假。

examples.en: The day commenced with a welcome from the principal.
examples.zh: 那天由校长致欢迎词开始。

examples.en: She commenced her medical career in 1996.
examples.zh: 她于1996年开始了她的医疗生涯。

examples.en: The company commenced operations in April.
examples.zh: 公司4月份开业了。

examples.en: to commence bankruptcy proceedings against somebody
examples.zh: 对某人启动破产程序

examples.en: We commence building next week.
examples.zh: 我们下周破土动工。

examples.en: Operators commenced to build pipelines in 1862.
examples.zh: 运营商于 1862 年开始兴建管道。

synonyms.words: begin ▪ start off ▪ kick off ▪ commence ▪ open

intro.en: These words are all used to talk about things happening from the beginning, or people doing the first part of something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均用以指事情开始发生或开始做某事。

items.def: to begin to happen or exist; to begin in a particular way or from a particular point:
items.zh: 指开始发生或存在、以…开始、以…为起点

examples.en: When does the class start?
examples.zh: 什么时候上课？

items.def: to start to happen or exist; to start in a particular way or from a particular point; to start speaking:
items.zh: 指开始发生或存在、以…开始、以…为起点、开始讲话

examples.en: When does the concert begin?
examples.zh: 音乐会什么时候开始？

items.def: (rather informal) to start happening or doing something; to start by doing or being something:
items.zh: 指进行或开展起来、首先进行、一开始是

examples.en: The discussion started off mildly enough.
examples.zh: 讨论颇为温和地开展起来。

items.def: (informal) to start an event or activity, especially in a particular way; (of an event, activity, etc.) to start, especially in a particular way:
items.zh: 尤指以…开始（活动）、（活动）以…开始

examples.en: Tom will kick off with a few comments.
examples.zh: 汤姆讲话时要先发表几点意见。

items.def: (formal) to start happening:
items.zh: 指开始发生

examples.en: The meeting is scheduled to commence at noon.
examples.zh: 会议定于午间召开。

items.def: to start an event or activity in a particular way; (of an event, a film or a book) to start, especially in a particular way:
items.zh: 指以…开始（活动）、（活动、电影或书）以…开头／开篇

examples.en: The story opens with a murder.
examples.zh: 故事以一宗谋杀案作序幕。

senses.def: beginning

examples.en: the commencement of the financial year
examples.zh: 财政年度的开始

examples.en: You will be required to enrol at the commencement of each academic year.
examples.zh: 您需要在每个学年开始时注册。

senses.def: a ceremony at which students receive their academic degrees or diplomas
senses.zh: 学位授予典礼；毕业典礼

senses.def: to praise somebody/something, especially publicly

examples.en: She was commended on her handling of the situation.
examples.zh: 她因妥善处理了那个局面而受到表扬。

examples.en: His designs were highly commended by the judges (= they did not get a prize but they were especially praised).
examples.zh: 他的设计受到了评委的高度赞扬。

examples.en: His book was highly commended.
examples.zh: 他的书受到高度赞扬。

senses.def: to recommend somebody/something to somebody

examples.en: She is an excellent worker and I commend her to you without reservation.
examples.zh: 她工作出色，我毫无保留地把她推荐给你。

examples.en: The movie has little to commend it (= it has few good qualities).
examples.zh: 这部电影乏善可陈。

senses.def: if something commends

examples.en: His outspoken behaviour did not commend itself to his colleagues.
examples.zh: 他直言不讳的行为不受他同事的欢迎。

senses.def: to give somebody/something to somebody in order to be taken care of

examples.en: We commend her soul to God.
examples.zh: 我们把她的灵魂托付给上帝。

senses.def: deserving praise and approval

examples.en: They always conduct their affairs with commendable honesty.
examples.zh: 他们总是以值得称道的诚实来处理事务。

examples.en: She showed commendable loyalty to the family firm.
examples.zh: 她对家族企业表现出了值得称赞的忠诚。

senses.def: in a way that deserves praise and approval
praise; approval

examples.en: The film deserves the highest commendation.
examples.zh: 这部电影值得最高的赞扬。

senses.def: an award or official statement giving public praise for somebody/something

examples.en: a commendation for bravery
examples.zh: 因勇敢而受到的嘉奖

examples.en: There were 16 prize winners and 18 commendations.
examples.zh: 共有16名获奖者和18名表彰者。

senses.def: living on another animal or plant and getting food from the situation, but doing no harm

examples.en: commensal organisms
examples.zh: 共栖体

senses.def: the fact of an animal or plant living on another animal or plant and getting food from the situation, but doing no harm
matching something in size, importance, quality, etc.
senses.zh: （在大小、重要性、质量等方面）相称的，相当的

examples.en: Salary will be commensurate with experience.
examples.zh: 薪金将会与资历相称。

senses.def: in a way that matches something in size, importance, quality, etc.
senses.zh: （在大小、重要性、质量等方面）相称的，相当的

senses.def: something that you say or write that gives an opinion on or explains somebody/something

examples.en: She made helpful comments on my work.
examples.zh: 她对我的工作提出了有益的意见。

examples.en: thoughtful/interesting/insightful comments
examples.zh: 深思熟虑/有趣/有洞察力的评论

examples.en: snide/critical/derogatory comments
examples.zh: 讽刺/批评/贬损评论

examples.en: Have you any comment to make about the cause of the disaster?
examples.zh: 你对发生灾难的原因有何评论？

examples.en: He handed me the document without comment.
examples.zh: 他未作任何解释就把文件交给了我。

examples.en: The director was not available for comment.
examples.zh: 经理抽不出时间来发表评论。

examples.en: You have to register to post a comment.
examples.zh: 你必须注册才能发帖评论。

examples.en: Please leave a comment on our website.
examples.zh: 请在我们的网站上发表评论。

examples.en: Keep up to date with all the latest news and comment.
examples.zh: 及时了解最新的消息和评论。

examples.en: You can post a question in the comments section below.
examples.zh: 可在下面的评论区提问。

examples.en: What she said was fair comment (= a reasonable criticism).
examples.zh: 她所讲的是合乎情理的批评。

senses.def: criticism that shows the faults of something

examples.en: The results are a clear comment on government education policy.
examples.zh: 这些结果是对政府教育政策明显的批评。

examples.en: There was a lot of comment about his behaviour.
examples.zh: 对他的行为举止有很多的议论。

senses.def: I have nothing to say about that

examples.en: ‘Will you resign, sir?’ ‘No comment!’
examples.zh: “先生，你会辞职吗？”“无可奉告！”

examples.en: When asked about the allegations, the chairman replied ‘No comment’.
examples.zh: 当被问到有关传闻时，主席回答“无可奉告”。

senses.def: to express an opinion about something

examples.en: He refused to comment until after the trial.
examples.zh: 他拒绝在审判前作任何评论。

examples.en: She said she was unable to comment further.
examples.zh: 她说她无法作进一步评论。

examples.en: to comment on a case/report
examples.zh: 对案例／报告进行评论

examples.en: I don't feel I can comment on their decision.
examples.zh: 我觉得我无法对他们的决定作出评论。

examples.en: We were just commenting on how well you look.
examples.zh: 我们刚才正说你看起来多么健康。

examples.en: He said nothing when asked to comment on the allegations.
examples.zh: 当被要求对这些指控发表评论时，他没有说什么。

examples.en: She declined to comment about the current situation in the party.
examples.zh: 她拒绝对党内现状发表评论。

examples.en: A spokesperson commented that levels of carbon dioxide were very high.
examples.zh: 发言人称二氧化碳的含量很高。

examples.en: ‘Not his best performance,’ she commented to the woman sitting next to her.
examples.zh: “这不是他的最佳表现。”她对坐在她旁边的女士议论道。

senses.def: I have nothing to say about that

examples.en: ‘Will you resign, sir?’ ‘No comment!’
examples.zh: “先生，你会辞职吗？”“无可奉告！”

examples.en: When asked about the allegations, the chairman replied ‘No comment’.
examples.zh: 当被问到有关传闻时，主席回答“无可奉告”。

intro.en: These are all words for something that you say or write, especially something that gives information or an opinion.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指口头或书面的说明、宣布。

items.def: something that you say or write that gives information or an opinion, often in a formal way:
items.zh: 通常指正式的说明、声明、陈述、报告

examples.en: A government spokesperson made a statement to the press.
examples.zh: 政府发言人向新闻界发表了一份声明。

items.def: something that you say or write that gives an opinion on something or is a response to a question about a particular situation:
items.zh: 指议论、评论、意见

examples.en: She made helpful comments on my work.
examples.zh: 她对我的工作提出了有益的意见。

items.def: a spoken or written statement that informs people about something:
items.zh: 指公告、布告、通告

examples.en: the announcement of a peace agreement
examples.zh: 和平协议公告

items.def: something that you say or write that gives an opinion or thought about somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指谈论、言论、评述

examples.en: He made a number of rude remarks about the food.
examples.zh: 他对这食物作了许多无礼的评论。

items.def: (rather formal) an official or formal statement, especially one that states an intention, belief or feeling, or that gives information:
items.zh: 指官方或正式的公告、宣告、宣言、声明

examples.en: the declaration of war
examples.zh: 宣战

items.def: (rather formal) a comment, especially one based on something you have seen, heard or read:
items.zh: 尤指根据所见、所闻、所读而作的评论

examples.en: He began by making a few general observations about the report.
examples.zh: 开头他先对这个报告作了几点概括性的评论。

intro.en: These words all mean to say or write a fact or opinion.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指口头或书面说明事实或发表意见。

items.def: to express an opinion or give facts about something:
items.zh: 指发表意见或说明事实

examples.en: He refused to comment until after the trial.
examples.zh: 他拒绝在审判前作任何评论。

items.def: (rather formal) to mention something because it is important or interesting:
items.zh: 指特别提到或指出

examples.en: He noted in passing that the company’s record on safety issues was not good.
examples.zh: 他顺便提到该公司在安全方面的记录不好。

items.def: to say or write what you have noticed about a situation:
items.zh: 指说起、谈论、评论

examples.en: Critics remarked that the play was not original.
examples.zh: 评论家指出这部戏剧缺乏创意。

items.def: (formal) to say or write what you have noticed about a situation:
items.zh: 指说起、谈论、评论

examples.en: She observed that it was getting late.
examples.zh: 她说天色晚了。

senses.def: a spoken description of an event that is given while it is happening, especially on the radio or television
senses.zh: （尤指电台或电视台所作的）实况报道，现场解说

examples.en: a sports commentary
examples.zh: 体育实况报道

examples.en: I was listening to the radio commentary on the game.
examples.zh: 我在听电台的比赛实况解说。

examples.en: The station provided live commentary on the African Nations Cup.
examples.zh: 该台对非洲国家杯进行了实况报道。

senses.def: a written explanation or discussion of something such as a book or a play

examples.en: a critical commentary on the final speech of the play
examples.zh: 对这剧本结尾的台词所作的批判性评论

senses.def: a criticism or discussion of something

examples.en: The petty quarrels were a sad commentary on the state of the government.
examples.zh: 这些鸡毛蒜皮的争吵说明了政府的状况很糟糕。

examples.en: The movie is a biting commentary on contemporary life in a big city.
examples.zh: 这部电影是对大城市当代生活的尖锐评论。

examples.en: political commentary
examples.zh: 政治评论

senses.def: a place in a sports ground where the people who describe what is happening in a sports event for radio or television sit
senses.zh: （为电台或电视转播而设在体育赛事现场的）解说席

examples.en: They will be in the commentary box to broadcast live and exclusive coverage of the game.
examples.zh: 他们将在解说室现场直播并独家报道比赛。

examples.en: the reporters in the commentary box
examples.zh: 实况转播间里的记者

senses.def: to give a spoken description of an event as it happens, especially on television or radio
senses.zh: （尤指在电视台或电台上）做实况报道，做现场解说

examples.en: Who will be commentating on the game?
examples.zh: 谁来对这场比赛做现场解说？

senses.def: a person who describes an event while it is happening, especially on television or radio
senses.zh: （尤指电视台或电台的）现场解说员，实况播音员

examples.en: a television/sports commentator
examples.zh: 电视台／体育运动实况解说员

examples.en: He's one of the great sports commentators of our time.
examples.zh: 他是我们那个时代优秀的体育比赛解说员之一。

senses.def: a person who is an expert on a particular subject and talks or writes about it on television or radio, in a newspaper or on social media
senses.zh: （电视台、电台、报章或社交媒体的）评论员

examples.en: She's a political commentator for the BBC.
examples.zh: 她是英国广播公司的政治评论员。

senses.def: trade, especially between countries; the buying and selling of goods and services
senses.zh: （尤指国家间的）贸易；商业；商务

examples.en: Leaders of industry and commerce met at the summit in Paris.
examples.zh: 工商界领导人在巴黎首脑会议上会面。

senses.def: connected with the buying and selling of goods and services

examples.en: residential and commercial properties
examples.zh: 住宅和商业地产

examples.en: a commercial building/development
examples.zh: 商业建筑/开发项目

examples.en: commercial real estate
examples.zh: 商业房地产

examples.en: commercial activities
examples.zh: 商业活动

examples.en: They have offices in the commercial heart of the city.
examples.zh: 他们在城市的商业中心有办事处。

examples.en: She is developing the commercial side of the organization.
examples.zh: 她负责该机构在商业方面的发展。

examples.en: a commercial vehicle (= one that is used for carrying goods or passengers who pay)
examples.zh: 商用车辆

senses.def: making or intended to make a profit
senses.zh: 赢利的；以获利为目的的

examples.en: The movie was not a commercial success (= did not make money).
examples.zh: 这部电影票房收入不佳。

examples.en: Risks arise when state-owned enterprises begin operating as commercial entities.
examples.zh: 当国有企业开始以商业实体的形式经营时，就会出现风险。

examples.en: policies to attract new industrial or commercial enterprises
examples.zh: 吸引新的工商企业的政策

examples.en: They are keen to see the technology licensed for commercial use.
examples.zh: 他们渴望看到该技术获得商业用途许可。

examples.en: The data cannot be used for commercial purposes.
examples.zh: 这些数据不能用于商业目的。

examples.en: The newspaper is acting solely in its own commercial interests.
examples.zh: 该报纸的行为完全是为了自身的商业利益。

examples.en: commercial baby foods
examples.zh: 市面上的婴儿食品

examples.en: the first commercial flights across the Atlantic
examples.zh: 头几次横跨大西洋的商业飞行

senses.def: more interested in profit and being popular than in quality
senses.zh: 商业化的；热衷于名利的

examples.en: Their more recent music is far too commercial.
examples.zh: 他们最近的音乐过分商业化了。

examples.en: The show was unashamedly commercial, with little artistic merit.
examples.zh: 这场演出毫无耻辱地商业化，几乎没有什么艺术价值。

senses.def: paid for by the money charged for broadcasting advertisements
senses.zh: 由广告收入支付的；商业性的

examples.en: a commercial radio station/TV channel
examples.zh: 商业电台／电视频道

senses.def: an advertisement on television, on the radio or on a website
senses.zh: （电视、电台或网站上播放的）广告

examples.en: a TV/television commercial
examples.zh: 电视广告片

examples.en: a radio commercial
examples.zh: 广播广告

examples.en: a Republican campaign commercial
examples.zh: 共和党竞选广告

examples.en: The marketing campaign is starting with four online commercials.
examples.zh: 营销活动从四个在线广告开始。

examples.en: actors in commercials
examples.zh: 广告演员

examples.en: She began her career appearing in commercials.
examples.zh: 她的职业生涯始于广告。

examples.en: He did a number of commercials for major brands.
examples.zh: 他为几个大品牌制作过一些广告。

intro.en: These words all describe activities or situations that are connected with the use of money, especially by a business or country.
intro.zh: 以上各词尤用于企业或国家的经济活动或状况。

items.def: connected with the trade, industry and development of wealth of a country, an area or a society:
items.zh: 指国家、地区或社会经济的、经济上的、经济学的

examples.en: This book deals with the social, economic and political issues of the period.
examples.zh: 这本书论及了那个时期的社会、经济和政治问题。

items.def: connected with money and finance:
items.zh: 指财政的、财务的、金融的

examples.en: She had got into financial difficulties.
examples.zh: 她陷入了财务困境。

items.def: connected with the buying and selling of goods and services.
items.zh: 指贸易的、商业的

items.def: (formal or finance) connected with money, especially all the money in a country:
items.zh: 指货币的、钱的，尤指一国的货币

examples.en: closer European monetary union
examples.zh: 更为紧密的欧洲货币联盟

items.def: (finance) connected with a budget (= the money available or a plan of how it will be spent).
items.zh: 指财政预算的

intro.en: These words all describe somebody/​something that is making or is likely to make money.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指赚钱的、赢利的、有利可图的。

items.def: making a lot of money, especially by being popular:
items.zh: 指赚钱的、成功的

examples.en: The play was very successful on Broadway.
examples.zh: 那部剧在百老汇大获成功。

items.def: making a profit:
items.zh: 指有利润的、赢利的

examples.en: a highly profitable business
examples.zh: 一家赢利很高的企业

items.def: [only before noun] making or intended to make a profit:
items.zh: 指赢利的、以获利为目的的

examples.en: The movie was not a commercial success (= made no profit).
examples.zh: 这部电影票房收入不佳。

items.def: (of business or work) producing or paying a large amount of money; making a large profit:
items.zh: 指生意或工作赚大钱的、获利多的

examples.en: They do a lot of business in lucrative overseas markets.
examples.zh: 他们在利润丰厚的海外市场上生意很多。

items.def: (often used in negative sentences) (of a process, business or activity) producing enough profit to continue:
items.zh: （常用于否定句中）指（工序、业务或活动）有利可图的、可赚钱的、合算的

examples.en: Small local shops stop being economic when a supermarket opens up nearby.
examples.zh: 附近有超市开业的话，当地的小商店就没有利润可赚了。

intro.en: These are all words for a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指广告、启事。

items.def: a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service; an example of something that shows its good qualities; the act of advertising something and making it public:
items.zh: 指广告、宣传的实例、广告活动或广告宣传

examples.en: They ran advertisements on TV and on social media.
examples.zh: 他们在电视和社交媒体上推出了广告。

items.def: [U] the business of attracting the attention of the public to somebody/​something such as a company, book, film, film star or product; the things that are done to attract attention:
items.zh: 指宣传业、广告宣传工作或传播工作

examples.en: She works in publicity.
examples.zh: 她从事宣传工作。

items.def: (informal) a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service:
items.zh: 广告；启事

examples.en: We put an ad on that website.
examples.zh: 我们在那个网站刊登了一则广告。

items.def: an advertisement on television or on the radio.
items.zh: 指电视或电台播放的广告

items.def: a set of advertisements for a particular product or service; activities done in order to increase the sales of a product or service:
items.zh: 指广告宣传、促销活动

examples.en: a special promotion of local products
examples.zh: 当地产品的特别促销活动

items.def: (especially British English尤用于英式英语) a series of short scenes from a film or television programme, shown in advance to advertise it.
items.zh: 指电影或电视节目的预告片

senses.def: a bank that offers services to the general public and to businesses

examples.en: Authorities want commercial banks to cut interest rates to revive car sales.
examples.zh: 主管机构要求商业银行降低利率以重振汽车销售。

senses.def: a short period of time when a television or radio show stops for advertisements
senses.zh: （穿插在电视或广播节目中的）广告时间

examples.en: He fetched a plate of snacks during a commercial break.
examples.zh: 他在广告时段拿了一盘小吃。

examples.en: The movie was so full of commercial breaks it was impossible to enjoy.
examples.zh: 这部电影里插播了这么多广告，简直没法好好欣赏。

senses.def: a method of farming that produces crops or animals for sale, usually on a large scale and using modern methods and equipment
senses.zh: 一种生产农作物或出售动物的耕作方法，通常是大规模并使用现代方法和设备

senses.def: a sales rep
the fact of being more interested in making money than in the value or quality of things

examples.en: commercialism in the theatre
examples.zh: 剧院的商业主义

senses.def: the act of using something to try to make a profit, especially in a way that other people do not approve of

examples.en: to complain about the commercialization of Christmas
examples.zh: 抱怨圣诞节的商业化

senses.def: to use something to try to make a profit, especially in a way that other people do not approve of
senses.zh: （尤指不择手段地）利用…牟利；商业化

examples.en: Their music has become very commercialized in recent years.
examples.zh: 他们的音乐近几年非常商业化了。

examples.en: Christmas is far too commercialized now.
examples.zh: 圣诞节现在太商业化了。

senses.def: in a way that is connected with the buying and selling of goods and services

examples.en: commercially produced/grown/developed
examples.zh: 商业化生产的／种植的／开发的

examples.en: The product is not yet commercially available.
examples.zh: 这种产品还未上市。

senses.def: in a way that makes or is intended to make a profit
senses.zh: 赢利的；以获利为目的的

examples.en: His invention was not commercially successful.
examples.zh: 他的发明没有获得商业上的成功。

examples.en: Designers are becoming more and more commercially minded.
examples.zh: 设计师们变得越来越具有商业头脑。

senses.def: an offensive way of referring to somebody that you think has ideas similar to those of communists
senses.zh: （冒犯性用语）有共产思想的人，共党分子

senses.def: to mix two or more things together or to be mixed, especially when it is impossible for the things to be separated afterwards

examples.en: The fluid must be prevented from commingling with other fluids.
examples.zh: 一定要避免将这种液体与其他液体混合。

examples.en: The corn must be segregated so the two types of seed do not commingle.
examples.zh: 玉米必须分开，这样两种类型的种子就不会混合在一起。

examples.en: Campaign funds must not be commingled with other money.
examples.zh: 竞选经费切忌与其他款项合并。

senses.def: a junior cook who works in a kitchen
senses.zh: 在厨房工作的初级厨师

senses.def: to show somebody sympathy when they are upset or disappointed about something

examples.en: She commiserated with the losers on their defeat.
examples.zh: 她对失败的一方表示同情。

senses.def: an expression of sympathy for somebody who has had something unpleasant happen to them, especially not winning a competition
senses.zh: （尤指对某人未赢得比赛而表示的）同情

examples.en: I offered him my commiseration.
examples.zh: 我对他表示同情。

examples.en: Commiserations to the losing team!
examples.zh: 落败的队伍太可惜了！

senses.def: an officer of the Communist Party, especially in the past in the Soviet Union
senses.zh: （尤指苏联旧时的）政治委员，政委

senses.def: a department of the army that is responsible for food supplies
a government department in the Soviet Union before 1946
senses.zh: （1946 年以前苏联的）人民委员部

senses.def: a shop that sells food, etc. in a military base, a prison, etc.
senses.zh: （军事基地、监狱等处出售食品等的）杂货商店

senses.def: a restaurant for people working in a large organization, especially a film studio
senses.zh: （大型机构，尤指电影制片厂的）员工餐厅

senses.def: an official group of people who have been given responsibility to control something, or to find out about something, usually for the government
senses.zh: （通常为政府管控或调查某事的）委员会

examples.en: The commission is expected to report its findings next month.
examples.zh: 预计委员会将在下个月报告调查结果。

examples.en: The government has set up a commission of inquiry into the disturbances at the prison.
examples.zh: 政府成立了一个委员会来调查监狱骚乱事件。

examples.en: The election commission found that neither candidate received enough votes to avoid a run-off.
examples.zh: 选举委员会发现，两位候选人都没有获得足够的票数来避免决选。

examples.en: the British representative on the commission
examples.zh: 委员会中的英国代表

examples.en: The defendant will be brought to trial before a military commission.
examples.zh: 被告将接受军事委员会的审判。

examples.en: She was also a member of the commission on religious education.
examples.zh: 她还是宗教教育委员会的成员。

examples.en: a commission on human rights
examples.zh: 人权委员会

examples.en: The government appointed an independent commission to investigate the causes of the disaster.
examples.zh: 政府任命了一个独立委员会来调查灾难原因。

senses.def: an amount of money that is paid to somebody for selling goods and that increases with the amount of goods that are sold

examples.en: You get a 10 per cent commission on everything you sell.
examples.zh: 你可从你售出的每件商品中获得 10% 的佣金。

examples.en: He earned £2 000 in commission last month.
examples.zh: 他上个月挣了 2 000 英镑的佣金。

examples.en: In this job you work on commission (= are paid according to the amount you sell).
examples.zh: 你做这份工作按销售额提成。

senses.def: an amount of money that is charged by a bank, etc. for providing a particular service

examples.en: 1 per cent commission is charged for exchanging foreign currency.
examples.zh: 换外币收取 1% 的手续费。

examples.en: The bank charges a high commission on these transactions.
examples.zh: 银行对这些交易收取高额手续费。

senses.def: a formal request to somebody to design or make a piece of work such as a building or a painting; the fact of making such a request
senses.zh: （请某人作建筑设计或作画等的）正式委托

examples.en: Eventually she agreed to accept the commission.
examples.zh: 最后她同意接受委托。

examples.en: He received a commission to design the new parliament building.
examples.zh: 他收到设计新议会大厦的委托。

examples.en: Sometimes I take commissions for portraits.
examples.zh: 有时我会接受肖像画的委托。

examples.en: The exhibition was a success and brought commissions from wealthy patrons.
examples.zh: 展览取得了成功，并获得了富有赞助人的委托。

senses.group: for art/music, etc. 艺术、音乐等

senses.def: the position of an officer in the armed forces, typically with the rank of lieutenant
senses.zh: （通常指陆军中尉、海军上尉、空军上尉及以上的）军衔

examples.en: He resigned his commission when he got married.
examples.zh: 结婚后，他辞去了佣金。

senses.def: the act of doing something wrong or illegal

examples.en: the commission of a crime
examples.zh: 犯罪

senses.def: available/not available to be used

examples.en: Several of the airline's planes are temporarily out of commission and undergoing safety checks.
examples.zh: 这家航空公司有几架飞机暂时不能使用，正在接受安全检查。

senses.def: to officially ask somebody to write, make or create something or to do a task for you
senses.zh: 正式委托（谱写、制作、创作或完成）

examples.en: She has been commissioned to write a new national anthem.
examples.zh: 她已受委托谱写新国歌。

examples.en: to commission a study/report
examples.zh: 委托做一项研究／写一份报告

examples.en: a specially commissioned piece of music
examples.zh: 特别委托谱写的乐曲

examples.en: Publishers have commissioned a French translation of the book.
examples.zh: 出版商已委托人把这本书译成法语。

examples.en: The survey on consumer taste was commissioned by local stores.
examples.zh: 消费者口味调查是由当地商店委托进行的。

examples.en: The king commissioned portraits from foreign artists.
examples.zh: 国王委托外国艺术家创作肖像画。

examples.en: the first opera commissioned for television
examples.zh: 第一部委托电视制作的歌剧

senses.group: piece of art/music, etc. 艺术、音乐等作品

senses.def: to choose somebody as an officer in one of the armed forces

examples.en: She was commissioned in 2014.
examples.zh: 她于 2014 年被任命为军官。

examples.en: He has just been commissioned (as a) pilot officer.
examples.zh: 他刚被任命为空军少尉。

senses.def: available/not available to be used

examples.en: Several of the airline's planes are temporarily out of commission and undergoing safety checks.
examples.zh: 这家航空公司有几架飞机暂时不能使用，正在接受安全检查。

senses.def: a person in uniform whose job is to stand at the entrance to a hotel, etc. and open the door for visitors, find them taxis, etc.
senses.zh: （在旅馆等门口为来宾开门、叫出租车等的）穿制服的看门人，门童

senses.def: an officer in the armed forces who holds a commission
senses.zh: （通常指陆军中尉、海军上尉、空军上尉及以上的）军官

senses.def: a member of a commission

examples.en: the Church Commissioners (= the group of people responsible for controlling the financial affairs of the Church of England)
examples.zh: 英格兰国教会财政管理委员会委员

examples.en: European Commissioners
examples.zh: 欧洲委员会委员

senses.def: the head of a particular police force in some countries
the head of a government department in some countries

examples.en: the agriculture/health, etc. commissioner
examples.zh: 农业、卫生等厅长

examples.en: Commissioner Rhodes was unavailable for comment.
examples.zh: 罗兹局长无暇评论。

examples.en: The Economic Affairs Commissioner, Albert Johnson, resigned over the issue.
examples.zh: 经济事务专员阿尔伯特·约翰逊因该问题辞职。

examples.en: The merger has been referred to the European Competition Commissioner.
examples.zh: 这个并购项目已提交欧洲竞争委员会委员审查。

senses.def: (in the US) an official chosen by a sports association to control it
senses.zh: （美国体育协会的）总干事，主管人

examples.en: the baseball commissioner
examples.zh: 棒球协会总干事

examples.en: a commissioner for the Central Collegiate Hockey Association
examples.zh: 中部大学曲棍球协会委员

senses.def: a lawyer who has official authority to be present when somebody makes a formal promise that a written statement that they will use as evidence in court is true
senses.zh: 监誓官（得到正式任命在法庭上主持宣誓的律师）

senses.def: to do something wrong or illegal

examples.en: to commit a crime/an offence
examples.zh: 犯罪

examples.en: to commit murder/fraud/adultery
examples.zh: 犯谋杀罪／欺诈罪／通奸罪

examples.en: to commit an act of violence/terrorism
examples.zh: 实施暴力／恐怖主义行为

examples.en: to commit an error/a sin
examples.zh: 犯错/犯罪

examples.en: to commit atrocities
examples.zh: 犯下暴行

examples.en: appalling crimes committed against innocent children
examples.zh: 对无辜儿童犯下的骇人听闻的罪行

examples.en: Most crimes are committed by young men.
examples.zh: 多数罪行都是年轻人犯下的。

examples.en: The men are being held on suspicion of conspiracy to commit armed robbery.
examples.zh: 这些男子因涉嫌串谋武装抢劫而被拘留。

senses.def: to kill yourself deliberately

examples.en: Her father had committed suicide.
examples.zh: 她的父亲自杀了。

senses.def: to promise sincerely that you will definitely do something, keep to an agreement or arrangement, etc.
senses.zh: 承诺，保证（做某事、遵守协议或遵从安排等）

examples.en: They want to see the text of the proposed treaty before fully committing themselves.
examples.zh: 他们想在作出全面承诺之前看到拟议条约的文本。

examples.en: Making an application does not commit you to anything.
examples.zh: 提出申请并不要求您承担任何义务。

examples.en: Borrowers should think carefully before committing themselves to taking out a loan.
examples.zh: 借款人应当慎重考虑之后再行借贷。

examples.en: Both sides committed themselves to settle the dispute peacefully.
examples.zh: 双方承诺和平解决争端。

senses.group: promise/say definitely 承诺；肯定地说

senses.def: to give an opinion or make a decision openly so that it is then difficult to change it
senses.zh: （公开地）表达意见，作出决定（以致日后难以更改）

examples.en: You don't have to commit yourself now—just think about it.
examples.zh: 你不必现在表态，只需考虑一下这件事。

senses.group: promise/say definitely 承诺；肯定地说

senses.def: to stay with and completely support one person, organization, etc. or give all your time and effort to your work, an activity, etc.
senses.zh: 忠于（某个人、机构等）；全心全意投入（工作、活动等）

examples.en: Why is he so scared to commit? (= say he will stay with one person)
examples.zh: 为什么他如此害怕承诺？ (= 说他会和一个人在一起)

senses.def: to spend money or time on something/somebody

examples.en: The council has committed large amounts of money to housing projects.
examples.zh: 市政会在住宅项目上投入了大量资金。

examples.en: The University committed substantial funds to assisting mature students.
examples.zh: 大学投入了大量资金来帮助成年学生。

senses.def: to order somebody to be sent to a hospital, prison, etc.
senses.zh: （下令）把（某人）送进（医院或监狱等）

examples.en: She was committed to a psychiatric hospital.
examples.zh: 她被送进了精神病院。

senses.def: to send somebody for trial in court

examples.en: The attackers were committed for trial at Bristol Crown Court.
examples.zh: 袭击者已被送往布里斯托皇家法院受审。

senses.group: somebody for trial 某人受审

senses.def: to learn something well enough to remember it exactly

examples.en: She committed the instructions to memory.
examples.zh: 她把指令记得很牢。

senses.def: to write something down

senses.def: a promise to do something or to behave in a particular way; a promise to support somebody/something; the fact of committing yourself
senses.zh: 承诺；许诺；允诺承担；保证

examples.en: I'm not ready to make a long-term commitment.
examples.zh: 我还没准备好做出长期的承诺。

examples.en: They have failed to honour their commitments.
examples.zh: 他们没有履行自己的承诺。

examples.en: The company has shown a commitment to diversity over the years.
examples.zh: 多年来，该公司表现出对多元化的承诺。

examples.en: He questioned the government's commitment to public services.
examples.zh: 他对政府在公共服务上作出的承诺提出质疑。

examples.en: We're looking for a firm commitment from both sides.
examples.zh: 我们期待双方都能作出坚定的承诺。

examples.en: This project demonstrates our commitment to improving the quality of the city's green spaces.
examples.zh: 这个项目表明了我们对提高城市绿地质量的承诺。

examples.en: They reaffirmed their commitment to work for peace.
examples.zh: 他们重申致力于和平的承诺。

examples.en: Australia is determined to meet its commitments under the agreement.
examples.zh: 澳大利亚决心履行其在该协定下的承诺。

senses.def: the desire to work hard and give your energy and time to a job or an activity
senses.zh: （对工作或活动的）献身，奉献，投入

examples.en: He has demonstrated exceptional commitment and dedication.
examples.zh: 他表现出非凡的投入和奉献精神。

examples.en: commitment to education/democracy/social justice
examples.zh: 致力于教育／民主／社会公正

examples.en: Not everyone will be happy with this level of commitment.
examples.zh: 并不是每个人都会对这种程度的承诺感到满意。

examples.en: She was criticized for her lack of commitment.
examples.zh: 她因缺乏承诺而受到批评。

senses.def: a thing that you have promised or agreed to do, or that you have to do
senses.zh: 已承诺（或同意）的事；不得不做的事

examples.en: He's busy for the next month with filming commitments.
examples.zh: 他正忙于准备已经承诺下个月接拍的电影。

examples.en: Parents very often have to juggle work with their family commitments.
examples.zh: 父母常常必须兼顾工作和家庭责任。

examples.en: I don't want to take on any more commitments.
examples.zh: 我不想再承担任何义务。

senses.def: a promise to pay for something, especially regularly; a promise to use resources in order to achieve something
