intro.en: These are all words for areas away from towns and cities, with fields, woods and farms.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指远离城镇，有田野、树林和农场的地区。

items.def: (often the country) an area that is away from towns and cities, especially one with particular natural features:
items.zh: （常作 the country）尤指具有自然特征的乡下、乡村

examples.en: She lives in the country.
examples.zh: 她住在乡下。

items.def: everything that you can see when you look across a large area of land, especially in the country:
items.zh: 尤指乡村的风景或景色

examples.en: This pattern of woods and fields is typical of the English landscape.
examples.zh: 这种林地与田野的格局是典型的英格兰乡村景色。

items.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods and farms. Countryside is usually used when you are talking about the beauty or peacefulness of a country area:
items.zh: countryside 通常用于强调乡村地区的美丽或宁静

items.def: (formal) land. Terrain is used when you are describing the natural features of an area, for example if it is rough, flat, etc:
items.zh: terrain 用于描述某地区的地形或地势

items.def: (usually the land) the countryside; the way people live in the country as opposed to in towns and cities:
items.zh: （通常作 the land）指与城镇相对的农村、农村生活方式

examples.en: Many younger people are leaving the land to find work in the cities.
examples.zh: 许多较年轻的人陆续离开农村到城市去找工作。

items.def: the natural features of an area, such as mountains, valleys, rivers and forests, especially when these are attractive to look at:
items.zh: 指自然风景、景色、风光

examples.en: We stopped on the mountain pass to admire the scenery.
examples.zh: 我们在山口停下来欣赏风景。

senses.def: a type of popular music in the style of the traditional music of the southern US, with singing and dance tunes played on violin

examples.en: a country and western singer
examples.zh: 乡村与西部音乐歌手

senses.def: a person from the countryside who seems stupid
a club in the country, or on the edge of a town, where people can play sports and go to social events
senses.zh: （体育运动和社交的）乡村俱乐部

senses.def: a person from the country who does not know much about life in the city, and who dresses or behaves in a way that shows this
a type of traditional dance, especially one in which couples dance in long lines or circles
senses.zh: 乡村舞，土风舞（尤为长排对舞或圆圈舞）

senses.def: a traditional type of dancing, especially one in which couples dance in long lines or circles
senses.zh: 乡村舞，土风舞（尤为长排对舞或圆圈舞）

senses.def: a large house in the country, especially one that belongs or used to belong to a rich important family
senses.zh: （尤指有地位富人家庭的）乡间宅第，别墅

examples.en: He used to entertain the politicians of the day at his country house.
examples.zh: 他以前经常在乡间别墅里招待时政要人。

senses.def: a British magazine, published every week, about houses, gardens, country sports and social life in the country. Many people associate it with rich people who own large houses in the country. It was first published in 1897.
senses.zh: 乡村生活：每周出版的一本英国杂志，介绍该国的房屋，花园，乡村体育和社交生活。许多人把它与在该国拥有大房子的富人联系起来。它于1897年首次出版。

senses.def: a long distance

examples.en: He won the race by a country mile.
examples.zh: 他遥遥领先赢了比赛。

examples.en: Their views are a country mile apart.
examples.zh: 他们的观点相差十万八千里。

examples.en: We missed the target by more than the proverbial country mile.
examples.zh: 我们与目标的差距超过了众所周知的乡村里程。

senses.def: a type of popular music in the style of the traditional music of the southern US, with singing and dance tunes played on violin
an area of the countryside that has been preserved for the public to enjoy
a large house in the country that belongs to a member of the upper class

examples.en: Espenson Hall has been the country seat of the Earls of Kendrick for seven generations.
examples.zh: 埃斯彭森庄园 (Espenson Hall) 一直是肯德里克伯爵七代人的乡间别墅。

senses.def: not made by a professional person

examples.en: a countrymade pistol
examples.zh: 土制手枪

senses.def: a person born in or living in the same country as somebody else

examples.en: The champion looks set to play his fellow countryman in the final.
examples.zh: 看来这位冠军在决赛中会遇上他的同胞。

senses.def: a man living or born in the country, not in the town

examples.en: Even after thirty years living in the country, I fear I am not a proper countryman. I don’t farm for a living or go tramping across drenched fields, gun in hand.
examples.zh: 即使在乡下生活了三十年，我也担心自己不是一个合格的乡下人。我不以务农为生，也不手持枪徒步穿越湿透的田野。

senses.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, etc.

examples.en: The surrounding countryside is windswept and rocky.
examples.zh: 这周围的乡村风多石头多。

examples.en: magnificent views over open countryside
examples.zh: 开阔乡村的壮丽景色

examples.en: the beautiful countryside of Wales
examples.zh: 威尔士美丽的乡村

examples.en: Everyone should enjoy the right of access to the countryside.
examples.zh: 人人都应享有进入乡村的权利。

examples.en: the quieter pace of life in the countryside
examples.zh: 乡间更为悠闲的生活节奏

intro.en: These are all words for areas away from towns and cities, with fields, woods and farms.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指远离城镇，有田野、树林和农场的地区。

items.def: (often the country) an area that is away from towns and cities, especially one with particular natural features:
items.zh: （常作 the country）尤指具有自然特征的乡下、乡村

examples.en: She lives in the country.
examples.zh: 她住在乡下。

items.def: everything that you can see when you look across a large area of land, especially in the country:
items.zh: 尤指乡村的风景或景色

examples.en: This pattern of woods and fields is typical of the English landscape.
examples.zh: 这种林地与田野的格局是典型的英格兰乡村景色。

items.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods and farms. Countryside is usually used when you are talking about the beauty or peacefulness of a country area:
items.zh: countryside 通常用于强调乡村地区的美丽或宁静

items.def: (formal) land. Terrain is used when you are describing the natural features of an area, for example if it is rough, flat, etc:
items.zh: terrain 用于描述某地区的地形或地势

items.def: (usually the land) the countryside; the way people live in the country as opposed to in towns and cities:
items.zh: （通常作 the land）指与城镇相对的农村、农村生活方式

examples.en: Many younger people are leaving the land to find work in the cities.
examples.zh: 许多较年轻的人陆续离开农村到城市去找工作。

items.def: the natural features of an area, such as mountains, valleys, rivers and forests, especially when these are attractive to look at:
items.zh: 指自然风景、景色、风光

examples.en: We stopped on the mountain pass to admire the scenery.
examples.zh: 我们在山口停下来欣赏风景。

senses.def: over the whole of a country
senses.zh: 遍及全国地；在全国范围

examples.en: a countrywide mail-order service
examples.zh: 全国性的邮购服务

examples.en: The film will be released in London in March and countrywide in May.
examples.zh: 这部电影将于三月在伦敦发行，五月在全国发行。

senses.def: a woman born or living in the same country as somebody else

examples.en: She defeated her fellow countrywoman in the final.
examples.zh: 她在决赛中击败了她的同胞。

senses.def: a woman living or born in the country, not the town

examples.en: Although I live in London now, I'm a countrywoman at heart.
examples.zh: 虽然我现在住在伦敦，但我本质上是一个乡下妇女。

senses.def: one of a number of areas that some countries are divided into, each with its own local government

examples.en: rural counties west of the Mississippi
examples.zh: 密西西比西部的乡村县

examples.en: Oxfordshire and neighbouring counties
examples.zh: 牛津及附近各郡

examples.en: the southern/northern counties
examples.zh: 南部/北部各县

examples.en: Orange County
examples.zh: 奥兰治县

examples.en: Originally, county boundaries often followed the course of a river.
examples.zh: 起初，郡的边界常沿河道划分。

examples.en: the most dangerous stretch of road in the county
examples.zh: 全县最危险的路段

examples.en: Most towns and villages throughout the county have experienced a population increase.
examples.zh: 全县大部分乡镇和村庄的人口都出现了增长。

examples.en: Children from schools across the county will be taking part.
examples.zh: 来自全县学校的孩子们将参加。

examples.en: Public meetings are being planned at various locations around the county.
examples.zh: 正在计划在全县各地举行公开会议。

senses.def: typical of English upper-class people
senses.zh: 典型英格兰上流社会人物的；世家子弟的

senses.def: (in the US) an elected county official who is responsible for elections and who keeps records of who owns buildings in the county, etc.
senses.zh: （美国负责选举及房产登记等的）县政官员

senses.def: (in England and Wales) a group of people elected to the local government of a county
senses.zh: （英国的）郡政务委员会，郡议会

examples.en: a member of Lancashire County Council
examples.zh: 兰开夏郡政务委员会委员

examples.en: The county council is/are voting on the proposals today.
examples.zh: 县议会今天正在对这些提案进行投票。

senses.def: (in England and Wales) the organization that provides services in a county, for example education, housing, etc.
senses.zh: 郡政务委员会服务机构；郡议会服务机构

examples.en: He works for the county council.
examples.zh: 他在郡议会服务机构工作。

examples.en: Many county councils are now controlled by the Conservatives.
examples.zh: 保守党现在控制着许多郡的政务委员会。

examples.en: The county council needs/need to improve this service.
examples.zh: 县议会需要/需要改进这项服务。

senses.def: a person elected to a county council
senses.zh: （英国的）郡政务委员会，郡议会

senses.def: a local court. In the UK county courts
senses.zh: 郡法院（在英国受理私人纠纷）；县法院（在美国受理私人纠纷和刑事案件）

senses.def: the county of Durham
senses.zh: 达勒姆郡（位于英格兰东北部，行政中心是达勒姆市）

senses.def: a large building in London, on the south bank of the Thames
senses.zh: 县政厅：伦敦的一幢大建筑，位于泰晤士河南岸，国会大厦对面。直到1986年大伦敦理事会被废止之前，它一直是伦敦地方政府的主要办公室。然后卖给了一家私人公司。现在大楼中有两家酒店，一家餐厅，一个水族馆和其他娱乐场所。

senses.def: the border of a county

examples.en: The car chase finally ended just across the county line.
examples.zh: 追车最终在刚跨过县界后停止。

senses.def: used to refer to the system used by drug dealers
senses.zh: 跨区域贩毒，跨地区毒品交易

examples.en: Vulnerable young people are often drawn into the drug trade by county lines gangs.
examples.zh: 弱势青少年经常被跨区域贩毒团伙拉入毒品交易。

examples.en: The programme seeks to educate people about the dangers of county lines.
examples.zh: 该节目旨在教育人们了解跨地区毒品交易的危险。

senses.def: the main town of a county, where its government is

examples.en: Trowbridge is the county town of Wiltshire.
examples.zh: 特罗布里奇是威尔特郡的首府。

senses.def: over the whole of a county
senses.zh: 遍及全郡（或全县）的；在全郡（或全县）范围的

senses.def: over the whole of a county
senses.zh: 遍及全郡（或全县）的；在全郡（或全县）范围的

senses.def: a sudden change of government that is illegal and often violent

examples.en: He seized power in a military coup in 2008.
examples.zh: 他在 2008 年的军事政变中夺取了政权。

examples.en: to stage/mount a coup
examples.zh: 发动政变

examples.en: He was sentenced to death for his part in the attempted coup.
examples.zh: 他因参与未遂政变而被判处死刑。

examples.en: a failed/an abortive coup
examples.zh: 失败的／流产的政变

examples.en: She lost her position in a boardroom coup (= a sudden change of power among senior managers in a company).
examples.zh: 她在董事会的人事突变中失去了职位。

senses.def: the fact of achieving something that was difficult to do

examples.en: Getting this contract has been quite a coup for us.
examples.zh: 把这份合同争取到手让我们费了很大力气。

examples.en: He pulled off a major diplomatic coup by winning agreement from all the warring factions on a permanent ceasefire.
examples.zh: 说服交战各方同意签署永久停火协议是他在外交上取得的重大成就。

senses.def: a sudden change of government that is illegal and often violent
an action or event that finally ends something that has been getting weaker or worse

examples.en: My disastrous exam results dealt the coup de grâce to my university career.
examples.zh: 我考试考得一塌糊涂，这就断送了我的大学生涯。

senses.def: a hit or shot that finally kills a person or an animal, especially to stop them from suffering
something very dramatic and surprising that happens, especially in a play
a play, show, etc. which is very successful
senses.zh: 非常成功的戏剧（或演出等）

senses.def: a car with two doors and usually a sloping back
two people or things

examples.en: I saw a couple of men get out.
examples.zh: 我看见有两个男人出去了。

senses.def: a small number of people or things

examples.en: We went there a couple of years ago.
examples.zh: 我们几年前去过那里。

examples.en: a couple of minutes/hours/days/weeks/months
examples.zh: 几分钟/几小时/几天/几周/几个月

examples.en: a couple of people/friends/guys
examples.zh: 几个人／朋友／伙计

examples.en: I've seen her a couple of times before.
examples.zh: 我以前见过她几次。

examples.en: I'll be with you in a minute. There are a couple of things I have to do first.
examples.zh: 请稍等一下，我有几件事情得先处理一下。

examples.en: We can do it in the next couple of weeks.
examples.zh: 我们可在今后几个星期里完成这件事。

examples.en: There have been some new developments in the past couple of days.
examples.zh: 过去几天里有一些新的进展。

examples.en: The last couple of years have been difficult.
examples.zh: 最近的几年一直是困难重重。

examples.en: There are a couple more files to read first.
examples.zh: 还有几份档案要先看一看。

senses.def: two people who are seen together, especially if they are married or in a romantic or sexual relationship

examples.en: married couples
examples.zh: 几对夫妇

examples.en: same-sex/gay/lesbian couples
examples.zh: 同性／男同性／女同性夫妇

examples.en: a young couple
examples.zh: 年轻夫妻

examples.en: an elderly couple
examples.zh: 老年夫妇

examples.en: The royal couple will visit New Zealand next year.
examples.zh: 这对皇室夫妇将于明年访问新西兰。

examples.en: Several couples were on the dance floor.
examples.zh: 有几对情侣在跳舞。

examples.en: The couple was/were married in 2022.
examples.zh: 这对夫妇于 2022 年结婚。

examples.en: We met a couple from Chicago, who were travelling with their three children.
examples.zh: 我们遇到了一对来自芝加哥的夫妇，他们带着三个孩子一起旅行。

senses.def: very soon

examples.en: We’ll be there in a couple of shakes.
examples.zh: 我们很快就会到达那里。

senses.def: to join together two parts of something, for example two vehicles or pieces of equipment

examples.en: The two railway trucks had been coupled together.
examples.zh: 这两节铁道货运车厢给连在了一起。

examples.en: This energy is converted into electrical energy by the generator that is coupled to the turbine.
examples.zh: 这种能量由与涡轮机相连的发电机转换成电能。

senses.def: to have sex

items.idm: in two shakes | in a couple of shakes

senses.def: very soon

examples.en: We’ll be there in a couple of shakes.
examples.zh: 我们很快就会到达那里。

senses.def: to join to form a pair, especially to have a romantic or sexual relationship
senses.zh: 配成一对；（尤指）成为情侣，发生性关系

examples.en: Two of the world's most beautiful people have coupled up.
examples.zh: 世界上最美丽的两个人已经结婚了。

examples.en: Jess decided Jordan wasn't for her and decided to couple up with Josh.
examples.zh: 杰西认为乔丹不适合她，并决定与乔什在一起。

senses.def: to be linked to another thing, situation, etc.

examples.en: Overproduction, coupled with falling sales, has led to huge losses for the company.
examples.zh: 生产过剩加上销售下降使这家公司遭受巨大损失。

senses.def: two lines of poetry of equal length one after the other
senses.zh: 对句（相连的两行长度相等的诗句）；对联

examples.en: a poem written in rhyming couplets
examples.zh: 用押韵对句写成的诗

senses.def: a small piece of printed paper or an electronic code that you can exchange for something or that gives you the right to buy something at a cheaper price than normal
senses.zh: 配给券；（购物）票证，优惠券

examples.en: discount coupons
examples.zh: 折扣券

examples.en: clothing coupons
examples.zh: 服装票

examples.en: an international reply coupon
examples.zh: 国际通用预付回信邮资券

senses.def: a printed form, often cut out from a newspaper, that is used to enter a competition, order goods, etc.
senses.zh: （常为剪自报章的）参赛表，订货单

examples.en: Fill in and return the attached coupon.
examples.zh: 填写所附上的参赛表并寄回。

senses.def: the practice of collecting and using coupons

examples.en: Couponing is a good way to save on groceries, but it means you can't favour brands.
examples.zh: 收集使用优惠券是节约食品杂货开销的好办法，但这也意味着不能有品牌偏好。

senses.def: the ability to do something dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear

examples.en: He showed great courage and determination.
examples.zh: 他表现得十分勇敢和果断。

examples.en: moral/physical courage
examples.zh: 道德勇气；不怕身体受苦的勇气

examples.en: They had the courage to stand up and fight for what they believed in.
examples.zh: 他们有勇气挺身而出，为捍卫自己的信仰而战。

examples.en: He couldn't find the courage to tell his daughters what had happened.
examples.zh: 他没有勇气告诉女儿们发生了什么事。

examples.en: Many said that the women's stories gave them the courage to pursue their goals
examples.zh: 许多人表示，这些女性的故事给了她们追求目标的勇气

examples.en: I haven't yet plucked up the courage to ask her.
examples.zh: 我还鼓不起勇气去问她。

examples.en: It takes courage to sing in public.
examples.zh: 在公共场合唱歌需要勇气。

examples.en: His courage in battle won him a promotion.
examples.zh: 他在战斗中的勇气为他赢得了晋升。

examples.en: She displayed remarkable courage in the face of danger.
examples.zh: 她展现了面对危险时的非凡胆量。

examples.en: I admire your courage in saying what you think.
examples.zh: 我佩服你怎么想就怎么说的勇气。

examples.en: They fought with courage, but were no match for the enemy.
examples.zh: 他们勇敢地战斗，但不是敌人的对手。

senses.def: to be/not be brave enough to do what you feel to be right
senses.zh: 有／没有勇气做自己认为正确的事

examples.en: You need to have the courage of your convictions.
examples.zh: 你需要有勇气做自己认为正确的事。

senses.def: to force yourself to be brave enough to do something

examples.en: I finally screwed up my courage and went to the dentist.
examples.zh: 我终于鼓起勇气，去看了牙医。

senses.def: to begin to feel happier and more confident because of something
to make yourself do something that you are afraid of
senses.zh: 鼓起勇气（做自己害怕做的事）；敢作敢为

examples.en: Taking her courage in both hands, she opened the door and walked in.
examples.zh: 她壮着胆打开门，走了进去。

items.idm: have/lack the courage of your convictions

senses.def: to be/not be brave enough to do what you feel to be right
senses.zh: 有／没有勇气做自己认为正确的事

examples.en: You need to have the courage of your convictions.
examples.zh: 你需要有勇气做自己认为正确的事。

senses.def: to force yourself to be brave enough to do something

examples.en: I finally screwed up my courage and went to the dentist.
examples.zh: 我终于鼓起勇气，去看了牙医。

senses.def: to begin to feel happier and more confident because of something

items.idm: take your courage in both hands

senses.def: to make yourself do something that you are afraid of
senses.zh: 鼓起勇气（做自己害怕做的事）；敢作敢为

examples.en: Taking her courage in both hands, she opened the door and walked in.
examples.zh: 她壮着胆打开门，走了进去。

senses.def: showing courage

examples.en: a very courageous decision
examples.zh: 十分勇敢的决定

examples.en: I hope people will be courageous enough to speak out against this injustice.
examples.zh: 我希望人们能敢于说出来，反对这种不公。

senses.def: in a way that shows courage

examples.en: The crew acted courageously in staying with the ship until all the passengers had been taken to safety.
examples.zh: 船员们勇敢地留在船上，直到所有乘客都被带到安全的地方。

senses.def: a long vegetable with dark green skin that is white inside

examples.en: Slice each courgette down the middle and remove the flesh.
examples.zh: 将每个西葫芦从中间切成薄片，去掉果肉。

senses.def: a person or company whose job is to take packages or important papers somewhere
senses.zh: （递送包裹或重要文件的）信使，通讯员，专递公司

examples.en: We sent the documents by courier.
examples.zh: 我们派了信使送交这些文件。

examples.en: I’ll send a courier with the blueprints.
examples.zh: 我会派人把设计图送达。

examples.en: Urgent deliveries of medicine may be sent by motorcycle courier.
examples.zh: 需紧急递送的药物可以通过摩托车投递员送。

senses.def: a person who is employed by a travel company to give advice and help to a group of tourists on holiday
to send a package, important papers, etc. by courier
senses.zh: （递送包裹或重要文件的）信使，通讯员，专递公司

examples.en: Courier that letter—it needs to get there today.
examples.zh: 那封信必须今天到达，用专递寄吧。

senses.def: a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject
senses.zh: （有关某学科的系列）课程，讲座

examples.en: a French/chemistry course
examples.zh: 法语课；化学课

examples.en: He took a course in Russian language and literature.
examples.zh: 他选修了俄语语言和文学课程。

examples.en: I want to do a course in art and design.
examples.zh: 我想修读艺术和设计课程。

examples.en: The department offers short courses in drama, fiction and poetry.
examples.zh: 本系开设戏剧、小说和诗歌短期课程。

examples.en: She teaches a course on internet crime.
examples.zh: 她教授有关网络犯罪的课程。

examples.en: My boss has been on a course this week.
examples.zh: 我的老板这周参加了一个课程。

examples.en: You need to go on a management training course.
examples.zh: 您需要参加管理培训课程。

examples.en: He has recently completed the five-week course.
examples.zh: 他最近完成了为期五周的课程。

examples.en: The college runs specialist language courses.
examples.zh: 这所学院开设有专门语言课程。

examples.en: I enrolled in a ten-week online course.
examples.zh: 我参加了为期十周的在线课程。

senses.def: a period of study at a college or university that leads to an exam or a qualification
senses.zh: （大学中要进行考试或取得资格的）课程

examples.en: What degree course did you choose?
examples.zh: 你选择了什么学位课程？

examples.en: a two-year postgraduate course leading to a master’s degree
examples.zh: 两年制硕士研究生课程

examples.en: He was able to design his own course of study.
examples.zh: 他能够设计自己的学习课程。

senses.def: a large area of land that is designed for playing golf on

examples.en: He set a new course record.
examples.zh: 他创下了高尔夫球的新纪录。

senses.def: an area of land or water where races are held
senses.zh: 比赛场地；跑道；赛船水道；泳道

examples.en: She was overtaken on the last stretch of the course.
examples.zh: 她在最后一个直道上被超过。

examples.en: Only ten yachts completed the course.
examples.zh: 只有 10 艘快艇赛完了全程。

senses.def: any of the separate parts of a meal

examples.en: a four-course dinner
examples.zh: 有四道菜的正餐

examples.en: The main course was roast duck.
examples.zh: 主菜是烤鸭。

examples.en: We had chicken for our main course.
examples.zh: 鸡肉是我们的主菜。

senses.def: a direction or route followed by a ship or an aircraft

examples.en: He radioed the pilot to change course.
examples.zh: 他用无线电通知飞行员改变航向。

examples.en: The plane was off course (= not going in the right direction).
examples.zh: 飞机偏离了航向。

examples.en: We're on course for our destination.
examples.zh: 我们正前往目的地。

senses.def: the general direction in which somebody’s ideas or actions are moving or in which things are developing
senses.zh: 方针；行动方向；发展方向

examples.en: The president appears likely to change course on some key issues.
examples.zh: 总统看起来可能要在某些重要问题上改变方针。

examples.en: The dollar fell sharply for two days, and then reversed course.
examples.zh: 美元快速下跌两天，然后开始反弹。

examples.en: Her career followed a similar course to her sister's.
examples.zh: 她的职业发展与她姐姐类似。

examples.en: Politicians are often obliged to steer a course between incompatible interests.
examples.zh: 政治家常常被迫在互不相容的利益集团之间开辟航道。

senses.def: a way of acting in or dealing with a particular situation

examples.en: There are various courses open to us.
examples.zh: 我们有多种处理方法可采取。

examples.en: What course of action would you recommend?
examples.zh: 你想推荐什么办法呢？

examples.en: It was the best course of action to take in the circumstances.
examples.zh: 这是在当时情况下能采取的最佳方法。

examples.en: The wisest course would be to say nothing.
examples.zh: 最明智的对策是缄口不语。

senses.def: the way something develops or should develop

examples.en: This was an event that changed the course of history.
examples.zh: 这是一次改变了历史进程的事件。

examples.en: The unexpected course of events aroused considerable alarm.
examples.zh: 意外的事态发展引起了相当大的恐慌。

examples.en: She repeatedly raised the issue during the course of the campaign.
examples.zh: 在竞选期间，她一再提起这个问题。

senses.def: the direction a river moves in

examples.en: The path follows the course of the river.
examples.zh: 小路沿河道延伸。

senses.def: a series of medical treatments, tablets, etc.

examples.en: to prescribe a course of antibiotics
examples.zh: 开一个疗程抗生素的处方

examples.en: She's been put on a course of injections.
examples.zh: 她接受了一个疗程的针剂治疗。

examples.en: When taking antibiotics it is important to finish the course.
examples.zh: 服用抗生素时，完成疗程很重要。

senses.def: a continuous layer of brick

examples.en: A new damp-proof course could cost £1 000 or more.
examples.zh: 新的防潮层可花掉 1 000 英镑以上。

senses.def: to be in a situation that is almost certain to cause an argument
senses.zh: 几乎发生冲突（或争端、纠纷）

examples.en: I was on a collision course with my boss over the sales figures.
examples.zh: 我和我的老板在销售数字问题上差点发生争执。

senses.def: to be moving in a direction in which it is likely that you will crash into somebody/something
senses.zh: 朝着可能会碰撞的方向移动；有可能相撞的趋势

examples.en: A giant iceberg was on a collision course with the ship.
examples.zh: 巨大的冰山朝着可能与船相撞的方向漂移。

senses.def: to be just what you would expect to happen or expect somebody to do in a particular situation

examples.en: Starting early and working long hours is par for the course in this job.
examples.zh: 开工早、工时长是这份工作的常态。

senses.def: the act of matching people with suitable jobs or tasks
going through a particular process

examples.en: The new textbook is in course of preparation.
examples.zh: 新的教科书正在准备之中。

senses.def: during

examples.en: He's seen many changes in the course of his long life.
examples.zh: 他在漫长的一生中目睹了许许多多的变化。

examples.en: The company faces major challenges over the course of the next few years.
examples.zh: 这家公司今后几年将面临重大的挑战。

senses.def: when enough time has passed

examples.en: It is possible that in the course of time a cure for cancer will be found.
examples.zh: 治疗癌症的方法终有一天能找到。

examples.en: In the course of time, I began to understand.
examples.zh: 终于我开始明白了。

senses.def: at the right time and not before
senses.zh: 在适当的时候；到一定的时候

examples.en: Your request will be dealt with in due course.
examples.zh: 你的要求将在适当的时候予以处理。

senses.def: as things usually happen
senses.zh: 按通常情况；在一般情况下；通常

examples.en: In the normal course of things we would not treat her disappearance as suspicious.
examples.zh: 在一般情况下，她不露面，我们也不会觉得有什么可疑之处。

examples.en: In the normal course of events, you should get a reply by Monday.
examples.zh: 按通常情况，你最迟在星期一就应该得到答复。

senses.def: to allow natural processes to happen, without trying to stop or change them (used especially in the context of illness)

examples.en: The midwife must judge when to let nature take its course and when to intervene.
examples.zh: 助产士必须判断何时顺其自然，何时进行干预。

examples.en: When the dog responded so badly to the treatment, we decided to let nature take its course.
examples.zh: 这条狗经过治疗后也没什么起色，于是我们就决定放弃治疗，听其自然。

senses.def: (as) the usual and correct thing to do
senses.zh: （作为）理所当然的事；（当作）常规

examples.en: We always check people's addresses as a matter of course.
examples.zh: 我们总是照例核对一下人们的地址。

senses.def: (to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions
senses.zh: （走）中间道路；（取）中庸之道；（采取）折中办法

senses.def: used to emphasize that what you are saying is true or correct
senses.zh: （强调所说的话属实或正确）当然

examples.en: ‘Don't you like my mother?’ ‘Of course I do!’
examples.zh: “难道你不喜欢我母亲？”“当然喜欢！”

examples.en: ‘Will you be there?’ ‘Course I will.’
examples.zh: “你会去那里吗？”“当然会。”

senses.def: used as a polite way of giving somebody permission to do something
senses.zh: （允许某人做某事的客气说法）当然

examples.en: ‘Can I come, too?’ ‘Course you can.’
examples.zh: “我也可以来吗？”“当然可以。”

examples.en: ‘Can I have one of those pens?’ ‘Of course—help yourself.’
examples.zh: “我能在那些笔中拿一支吗？”“当然，自己拿吧。”

senses.def: used as a polite way of agreeing with what somebody has just said
senses.zh: （礼貌地同意某人刚说的话）当然

examples.en: ‘I did all I could to help.’ ‘Of course,’ he murmured gently.
examples.zh: “我尽全力帮忙了。”“当然。”他轻声低语道。

senses.def: used to show that what you are saying is not surprising or is generally known or accepted
senses.zh: （表示所说的事不令人惊讶或具有普遍性）当然，自然

examples.en: Ben, of course, was the last to arrive.
examples.zh: 本当然是最后一个到的。

examples.en: Of course, there are other ways of doing this.
examples.zh: 当然还有别的方法做这件事。

senses.def: used to emphasize the fact that you are saying ‘no’

examples.en: ‘Are you going?’ ‘Of course not.’
examples.zh: “你要去吗？”“当然不去。”

examples.en: ‘Do you mind?’ ‘No, of course not.’
examples.zh: “你介意吗？”“不，当然不介意。”

senses.def: likely to achieve or do something because you have already started to do it
senses.zh: （因为已开始做而）很可能做成（或做）

examples.en: The American economy is on course for higher inflation than Britain by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 美国经济很可能在今年年底前出现比英国高的通货膨胀。

examples.en: Victory in Saturday’s match will put them on course to qualify for the European championships.
examples.zh: 周六比赛的胜利将使他们有望获得欧洲锦标赛的参赛资格。

senses.def: to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
to develop in the usual way and come to the usual end

examples.en: Sometimes it is better to simply let stress and grief run their course.
examples.zh: 有时，最好是让压力和悲伤顺其自然。

examples.en: With minor ailments the best thing is often to let nature take its course.
examples.zh: 对于小病，往往最好是听其自然。

senses.def: to continue doing something until it has finished or been completed, even though it is difficult

examples.en: Very few of the trainees have stayed the course.
examples.zh: 极少受训者坚持到底。

examples.en: He insists that he will not quit but will stay the course.
examples.zh: 他坚称自己绝不半途而废，将坚持到底。

senses.def: to move or flow quickly

examples.en: He stopped talking and tears coursed down his cheeks.
examples.zh: 他不再说话，泪水顺着脸颊流下来。

examples.en: They walked on, the river coursing slowly next to them.
examples.zh: 他们继续前行，河水在他们身边缓缓流过。

examples.en: The company faces major challenges over the course of the next few years.
examples.zh: 这家公司今后几年将面临重大的挑战。

examples.en: It is possible that in the course of time a cure for cancer will be found.
examples.zh: 治疗癌症的方法终有一天能找到。

examples.en: In the course of time, I began to understand.
examples.zh: 终于我开始明白了。

senses.def: at the right time and not before
senses.zh: 在适当的时候；到一定的时候

examples.en: Your request will be dealt with in due course.
examples.zh: 你的要求将在适当的时候予以处理。

items.idm: in the ordinary, normal, etc. course of events, things, etc.

senses.zh: 按通常情况；在一般情况下；通常

examples.zh: 在一般情况下，她不露面，我们也不会觉得有什么可疑之处。

examples.en: In the normal course of events, you should get a reply by Monday.
examples.zh: 按通常情况，你最迟在星期一就应该得到答复。

senses.zh: （作为）理所当然的事；（当作）常规

examples.en: We always check people's addresses as a matter of course.
examples.zh: 我们总是照例核对一下人们的地址。

items.idm: (steer, take, etc.) a middle course | (find, etc.) a/the middle way

senses.def: (to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions
senses.zh: （走）中间道路；（取）中庸之道；（采取）折中办法

examples.zh: “难道你不喜欢我母亲？”“当然喜欢！”

examples.en: ‘Will you be there?’ ‘Course I will.’
examples.zh: “你会去那里吗？”“当然会。”

senses.zh: （允许某人做某事的客气说法）当然

examples.zh: “我也可以来吗？”“当然可以。”

senses.zh: （礼貌地同意某人刚说的话）当然

examples.zh: “我尽全力帮忙了。”“当然。”他轻声低语道。

senses.def: used to show that what you are saying is not surprising or is generally known or accepted
senses.zh: （表示所说的事不令人惊讶或具有普遍性）当然，自然

examples.en: Ben, of course, was the last to arrive.
examples.zh: 本当然是最后一个到的。

examples.en: Of course, there are other ways of doing this.
examples.zh: 当然还有别的方法做这件事。

senses.def: used to emphasize the fact that you are saying ‘no’

examples.en: ‘Are you going?’ ‘Of course not.’
examples.zh: “你要去吗？”“当然不去。”

examples.en: ‘Do you mind?’ ‘No, of course not.’
examples.zh: “你介意吗？”“不，当然不介意。”

items.idm: on course for something/to do something

senses.def: likely to achieve or do something because you have already started to do it
senses.zh: （因为已开始做而）很可能做成（或做）

examples.en: The American economy is on course for higher inflation than Britain by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 美国经济很可能在今年年底前出现比英国高的通货膨胀。

examples.en: Victory in Saturday’s match will put them on course to qualify for the European championships.
examples.zh: 周六比赛的胜利将使他们有望获得欧洲锦标赛的参赛资格。

senses.def: to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
to develop in the usual way and come to the usual end

examples.en: Sometimes it is better to simply let stress and grief run their course.
examples.zh: 有时，最好是让压力和悲伤顺其自然。

examples.en: With minor ailments the best thing is often to let nature take its course.
examples.zh: 对于小病，往往最好是听其自然。

senses.def: to continue doing something until it has finished or been completed, even though it is difficult

examples.en: Very few of the trainees have stayed the course.
examples.zh: 极少受训者坚持到底。

examples.en: He insists that he will not quit but will stay the course.
examples.zh: 他坚称自己绝不半途而废，将坚持到底。

senses.def: a way of acting in or dealing with a particular situation
a book for studying from, used regularly on a particular course of study
computer programs that are designed to be used to teach a subject
work that students do during a course of study, not in exams, that is included in their final mark

examples.en: Coursework accounts for 40 per cent of the final marks.
examples.zh: 课程作业占最后总成绩的 40%。

senses.def: the place where legal trials take place and where crimes, etc. are judged

examples.en: the civil/criminal courts
examples.zh: 民事／刑事法庭

examples.en: Her lawyer made a statement outside the court.
examples.zh: 她的律师在法庭外面发表了一份声明。

examples.en: Relatives of the victims were in court.
examples.zh: 受害者亲属出庭受审。

examples.en: She will appear in court tomorrow.
examples.zh: 她明天出庭。

examples.en: They took their landlord to court for breaking the contract.
examples.zh: 因为房东毁约，他们把他告上了法庭。

examples.en: The case took five years to come to court (= to be heard by the court).
examples.zh: 那案件历时五年才被法庭受理。

examples.en: There wasn't enough evidence to bring the case to court (= start a trial).
examples.zh: 没有足够的证据可把此案提交法庭。

examples.en: The case was settled out of court (= a decision was reached without a trial).
examples.zh: 这案件已庭外和解。

examples.en: He won the court case and was awarded damages.
examples.zh: 他胜诉得到了赔偿金。

examples.en: She can't pay her tax and is facing court action.
examples.zh: 她缴不起税，将面临法庭诉讼。

examples.en: During the court hearing, the prosecutor said she would seek maximum prison sentences.
examples.zh: 在法庭听证会上，检察官表示她将寻求最高刑期。

senses.def: the people in a court
senses.zh: 全体出庭人员；（尤指）全体审判人员

examples.en: Please tell the court what happened.
examples.zh: 请向法庭陈述事情的经过。

examples.en: The court heard how the man collapsed after being stabbed.
examples.zh: 法庭听取了这男子被刺伤后倒下的过程。

examples.en: The court ruled in favour of her claim.
examples.zh: 法院判决支持她的诉讼请求。

examples.en: This is not a case to be decided by the courts.
examples.zh: 这不是一个需要由法院裁决的案件。

examples.en: This evidence was not put before the court.
examples.zh: 这个证据没有提交法庭。

examples.en: Airlines could face huge compensation bills following a court ruling on flight delays.
examples.zh: 在法庭对航班延误作出裁决后，航空公司可能面临巨额赔偿。

senses.def: a place where games such as tennis and basketball are played

examples.en: a tennis/squash/basketball court
examples.zh: 网球场；壁球场；篮球场

examples.en: He won after only 52 minutes on court.
examples.zh: 他上场仅 52 分钟就赢得了胜利。

examples.en: The players are good friends off court and train together.
examples.zh: 这些选手球场下是好朋友，而且一起训练。

senses.def: the official place where kings and queens live

examples.en: the court of Queen Victoria
examples.zh: 维多利亚女王的宫廷

examples.en: He was presented to the queen at court.
examples.zh: 他进入宫廷，被引见给女王。

senses.def: the king or queen, their family, and the people who work for them and/or give advice to them

examples.en: The painting shows the emperor with his court.
examples.zh: 这幅画画的是皇帝和皇宫里的人。

senses.def: an open space that is partly or completely surrounded by buildings and is usually part of a castle, a large house, etc.
senses.zh: （通常为城堡、大宅第等的）庭院，院子，天井

senses.def: used in the names of blocks of flats or apartment buildings, or of some short streets; (in the UK) used in the names of some large houses
senses.zh: （用于套房、公寓或某些短街区的名称）公寓大楼，短街；（英国用于某些大型宅第的名称）宅第，邸宅

examples.en: The building is situated in a medieval court at the top of Edinburgh's royal mile.
examples.zh: 该建筑位于爱丁堡皇家大道顶部的中世纪宫廷内。

senses.def: a large open section of a building, often with a glass roof
senses.zh: 建筑物的开阔部分（常有玻璃房顶）；大厅；馆

senses.def: it is your/somebody’s responsibility to take action next
senses.zh: （球已经丢给你了）下一步就看你的了

examples.en: They've offered me the job, so the ball's in my court now.
examples.zh: 他们已答应把那份工作给我，下一步就看我怎么办了。

senses.def: to entertain people by telling them interesting or funny things
senses.zh: （讲趣闻或笑话）使人快乐，逗人乐

examples.en: I met Giles holding court with some tourists in a cafe.
examples.zh: 我在一家咖啡馆遇到了贾尔斯和一些游客。

senses.def: to completely reject an idea, a story, etc. that you think is not worth taking seriously at all
senses.zh: 对（某主意、说法等）一笑置之；置之不理；不屑一顾

examples.en: All his attempts at explanation were simply laughed out of court.
examples.zh: 他所有的解释尝试都只是在法庭外被嘲笑。

senses.def: to treat somebody with great respect in order to gain favour with them
to say that something is completely wrong or not worth considering, especially in a trial
senses.zh: （尤指在法庭上）指明完全错误，不予考虑，不予受理

examples.en: The charges were thrown out of court.
examples.zh: 这些指控未予受理。

examples.en: Well that's my theory ruled out of court.
examples.zh: 唉，那就是我遭到摒弃的意见。

senses.def: to try to please somebody in order to get something you want, especially the support of a person, an organization, etc.
senses.zh: （为有所求，尤指为寻求支持而）试图取悦，讨好，争取

examples.en: Both candidates have spent the last month courting the media.
examples.zh: 两位候选人在过去的一个月里都在取悦媒体。

senses.group: try to please 试图取悦

senses.def: to try to obtain something

examples.en: He has never courted popularity.
examples.zh: 他从不追求名望。

senses.group: try to get 试图得到

senses.def: to do something that might result in something unpleasant happening
senses.zh: 招致，酿成，导致（不愉快的事）

examples.en: to court danger/death/disaster
examples.zh: 招致危险／死亡／灾难

examples.en: As a politician he has often courted controversy.
examples.zh: 作为政治人物，他常常招致争议。

senses.group: invite something bad 招致灾祸

senses.def: to have a romantic relationship with somebody that you hope to marry

examples.en: He had been courting Jane for six months.
examples.zh: 他追求简已有六个月之久。

examples.en: At that time they had been courting for several years.
examples.zh: 当时他们已经谈了好几年的恋爱了。

examples.en: Your grandfather and I were still courting at the time.
examples.zh: 当时你的祖父和我仍在谈恋爱。

senses.def: (of a male bird or other animal) to try to attract a female

items.idm: the ball is in your/somebody’s court

senses.def: it is your/somebody’s responsibility to take action next
senses.zh: （球已经丢给你了）下一步就看你的了

examples.en: They've offered me the job, so the ball's in my court now.
examples.zh: 他们已答应把那份工作给我，下一步就看我怎么办了。

senses.def: to entertain people by telling them interesting or funny things
senses.zh: （讲趣闻或笑话）使人快乐，逗人乐

examples.en: I met Giles holding court with some tourists in a cafe.
examples.zh: 我在一家咖啡馆遇到了贾尔斯和一些游客。

senses.def: to completely reject an idea, a story, etc. that you think is not worth taking seriously at all
senses.zh: 对（某主意、说法等）一笑置之；置之不理；不屑一顾

examples.en: All his attempts at explanation were simply laughed out of court.
examples.zh: 他所有的解释尝试都只是在法庭外被嘲笑。

senses.def: to treat somebody with great respect in order to gain favour with them
to say that something is completely wrong or not worth considering, especially in a trial
senses.zh: （尤指在法庭上）指明完全错误，不予考虑，不予受理

examples.en: The charges were thrown out of court.
examples.zh: 这些指控未予受理。

examples.en: Well that's my theory ruled out of court.
examples.zh: 唉，那就是我遭到摒弃的意见。

senses.def: a playing card
senses.zh: 人头牌，花牌（纸牌的 K、Q 或 J）

senses.def: the sum of money that somebody is ordered to pay for lawyers, etc. in a legal case

examples.en: She was ordered to pay £800 court costs.
examples.zh: 她被命令支付 800 英镑的法庭费用。

senses.def: a military court that deals with members of the armed forces who break military law; a trial at such a court
senses.zh: 军事法庭；军事法庭的审判；军法审判

examples.en: He was convicted at a court martial.
examples.zh: 他在军事法庭上被判有罪。

examples.en: All the men now face court martial.
examples.zh: 现在所有这些军人都面临军事法庭的审判。

senses.def: to hold a trial of somebody in a military court
senses.zh: （在军事法庭上）举行审判；以军法审判

examples.en: He was court-martialled for desertion.
examples.zh: 他因擅离职守受到了军法审判。

senses.def: a court that people can go to in order to try and change decisions that have been made by a lower court

examples.en: There is a right of appeal to the court of appeal.
examples.zh: 有向上诉法院上诉的权利。

senses.def: the highest court in England and Wales (apart from the Supreme Court
senses.zh: （英格兰和威尔士）上诉法院（仅次于最高法院的司法机构）

examples.en: The Court of Appeal dismissed the defendant’s appeal.
examples.zh: 上诉法院驳回被告的上诉。

senses.def: one of the courts in the US that can change decisions made by a lower court
a court in the US that hears claims made against the government
senses.zh: （美国）求偿法院（负责审理对政府的申诉案件）

senses.def: a special official group of people that investigates a particular problem
a room or building where legal cases are judged

examples.en: Such hearings are not as formal as a court of law.
examples.zh: 此类听证会不像法庭那么正式。

examples.en: There was nothing that could be proved in a court of law.
examples.zh: 在法庭上什么也没能证明。

examples.en: I don't think that argument would stand up in a court of law.
examples.zh: 我认为那个论据在法庭上是站不住脚的。

senses.def: in Scotland, the highest court that deals with civil
a decision that is made in court about what must happen in a particular situation

examples.en: He failed to meet four court orders to pay debts of £4 000.
examples.zh: 他未能履行四项法院命令，支付 4000 英镑的债务。

examples.en: She tried to get a court order to prevent him from coming near her.
examples.zh: 她试图争取法庭命令以阻止他接近自己。

senses.def: a person whose job is to create the official written record of what is said in court

examples.en: There is a court reporter who makes a transcript at the hearing.
examples.zh: 有一名法庭记录员在听证会上制作笔录。

senses.def: a journalist who goes to court to report on what happens there

examples.en: I started reporting general news and then became a court reporter for three years.
examples.zh: 我开始报道一般新闻，然后当了三年的法庭记者。

senses.def: a woman’s formal shoe that is plain and does not cover the top part of the foot
senses.zh: 船鞋，无带低帮女鞋，无带半高跟女鞋（正式场合穿的朴素女鞋）

senses.def: an old form of tennis
senses.zh: 庭院网球（使用硬球的旧式室内网球运动）

senses.def: polite, especially in a way that shows respect
senses.zh: 有礼貌的；客气的；（尤指）恭敬的，谦恭的

examples.en: a courteous young man
examples.zh: 彬彬有礼的年轻人

examples.en: The hotel staff are friendly and courteous.
examples.zh: 旅馆服务人员友好而有礼貌。

senses.def: in a polite way, especially in a way that shows respect
senses.zh: 有礼貌的；客气的；（尤指）恭敬的，谦恭的

examples.en: ‘I don’t think we have met,’ said the chairman courteously.
examples.zh: “我们好像没有见过面。”主席客气地说道。

senses.def: (in the past) a woman who had sexual relationships for money, especially one with rich customers
senses.zh: （旧时与富人或要人交往的）高级妓女，交际花

senses.def: polite behaviour that shows respect for other people

examples.en: I was treated with the utmost courtesy by the staff.
examples.zh: 我受到了工作人员极有礼貌的接待。

examples.en: We asked them, as a matter of courtesy, if we could photograph their house.
examples.zh: 出于礼貌，我们问他们是否可以拍摄他们的房子。

examples.en: It's only common courtesy to tell the neighbours that we'll be having a party (= the sort of behaviour that people would expect).
examples.zh: 告诉邻居我们要举行聚会，这是起码的礼貌。

senses.def: a polite thing that you say or do when you meet people in formal situations
senses.zh: （正式场合见面时的）客气话，礼貌

examples.en: an exchange of courtesies before the meeting
examples.zh: 会议开始前互致问候

examples.en: The prime minister was welcomed with the usual courtesies.
examples.zh: 按通常的礼仪欢迎那位总理的到来。

senses.def: with the official permission of somebody/something and as a favour

examples.en: The pictures have been reproduced by courtesy of the British Museum.
examples.zh: 承蒙大英博物馆惠允，复制了这些画。

senses.def: given as a prize or provided free by a person or an organization

examples.en: Win a weekend in Rome, courtesy of Fiat.
examples.zh: 赢了就可以获得菲亚特公司提供的到罗马度周末的机会。

senses.def: as the result of a particular thing or situation

examples.en: Viewers can see the stadium from the air, courtesy of a camera fastened to the plane.
examples.zh: 由于飞机上安装有摄像机，电视观众可从空中鸟瞰体育场。

senses.def: to be polite by doing the thing that is mentioned
senses.zh: （做提及的事）对某人表示礼貌

examples.en: Please do me the courtesy of listening to what I'm saying.
examples.zh: 请耐心听一听我的话。

examples.en: She might have done me the courtesy of replying to my letter.
examples.zh: 她本该给我回信以示礼貌。

senses.def: to know when you should do something in order to be polite
senses.zh: 知道何时该做…（以示礼貌）

examples.en: You think he'd at least have the courtesy to call to say he'd be late.
examples.zh: 谁都会觉得他至少应该懂得打个电话说一声他要晚来。

examples.en: You could at least have had the courtesy to let me know.
examples.zh: 你至少应该出于礼貌让我知道这件事吧。

senses.def: provided free, at no cost to the person using it

examples.en: A courtesy bus operates between the hotel and the beach.
examples.zh: 有一趟免费的公共汽车往返于旅馆和海滩之间。

examples.en: The dealer will provide you with a courtesy car while your vehicle is being repaired.
examples.zh: 车辆维修期间，经销商会为你提供免费使用的汽车。

(especially in the past) a person who is part of the court
extremely polite and full of respect, especially in an old-fashioned way
senses.zh: （尤指老式）极其恭敬有礼的，温文尔雅的

examples.en: He bowed in a very old-fashioned and courtly way.
examples.zh: 他以一种非常老式的、有礼貌的方式鞠了一躬。

examples.en: They learnt how to behave and how to speak in a courtly fashion.
examples.zh: 他们学会了如何以礼貌的方式行事和说话。

senses.def: a tradition in literature, especially in Medieval times, involving the love of a knight

senses.def: a room in which trials or other legal cases are held

examples.en: His lawyer read a statement outside the courtroom.
examples.zh: 他的律师在法庭外宣读了一份声明。

examples.en: She could face a bitter courtroom battle.
examples.zh: 她可能会面临一场激烈的法庭争斗。

senses.def: the time when two people have a romantic relationship before they get married; the process of developing this relationship

examples.en: They married after a short courtship.
examples.zh: 他们恋爱不久便结婚了。

examples.en: Mr Elton’s courtship of Harriet
examples.zh: 埃尔顿先生对哈丽雅特的追求

senses.def: the special way animals behave in order to attract a mate

examples.en: the elaborate courtship display of the pigeon
examples.zh: 鸽子尽心竭力的求偶表现

senses.def: the process or act of attracting a business partner, etc.

examples.en: the company’s courtship by the government
examples.zh: 政府向公司献殷勤

senses.def: the area around a tennis court, basketball court, etc.

examples.zh: 她的父母在球场边观赛。

senses.def: by the side of a tennis court, basketball court, etc.

examples.en: expensive courtside seats
examples.zh: 昂贵的球场边座位

examples.en: The couple were among celebrities sitting courtside.
examples.zh: 这对夫妇坐在球场边的名人中间。

senses.def: an open space that is partly or completely surrounded by buildings and is usually part of a castle, a large house, etc.
senses.zh: （通常为城堡、大宅第等的）庭院，院子，天井

examples.en: the central/inner courtyard
examples.zh: 中心／内庭院

senses.zh: （北非的）蒸粗麦粉，蒸粗麦粉菜肴

senses.def: a child of your aunt or uncle
senses.zh: 同辈表亲（或堂亲）；堂兄（或弟、姊、妹）；表兄（或弟、姊、妹）

examples.en: She's my cousin.
examples.zh: 她是我的表妹。

examples.en: We're cousins.
examples.zh: 我们是表亲。

examples.en: This is my cousin Richard.
examples.zh: 这是我的表弟理查德。

examples.en: He's a cousin once removed (= separated by one generation of our family).
examples.zh: 他是表兄弟的表亲（与我们家相隔一代）。

examples.en: She's a cousin of the bride.
examples.zh: 她是新娘的表亲。

examples.en: He claims to be a cousin to the King.
examples.zh: 他自称是国王的表弟。

senses.def: a person who is in your wider family but who is not closely related to you

examples.en: She's some sort of cousin, I think.
examples.zh: 我想她是一个远亲吧。

examples.en: He's a distant cousin of mine.
examples.zh: 他是我远房的一个表亲。

senses.def: a way of describing people from another country who are similar in some way to people in your own country
senses.zh: 兄弟的…国人民（对与本民族有某些类似的另一国家人民的说法）

examples.en: our American cousins
examples.zh: 我们兄弟的美国人民

senses.def: a way of describing things that are similar or related in some way

examples.en: Asian elephants are smaller than their African cousins.
examples.zh: 亚洲象比它们的非洲同类小些。

examples.en: These pigs are close cousins of the wild hog.
examples.zh: 这些猪和野猪是近亲。

senses.def: a son of your aunt or uncle; a male first cousin
a daughter of your aunt or uncle; a female first cousin

senses.def: the design and production of expensive and fashionable clothes; these clothes

examples.en: a couture evening dress
examples.zh: 昂贵时髦的晚礼服

examples.en: The House of Mattli is expanding from couture into ready-to-wear.
examples.zh: House of Mattli 正从高级时装扩展到成衣。

senses.def: a person who designs, makes and sells expensive, fashionable clothes
senses.zh: 时装设计师;时装销售商

senses.def: sharing a pair of electrons
tending to change with another variable
a small bay

examples.en: a secluded cove
examples.zh: 僻静的小海湾

senses.def: a man
a group or meeting of witches
a promise to somebody, or a legal agreement, especially one to pay a regular amount of money to somebody/something
senses.zh: 承诺；合同；协约；（尤指定期付款的）契约

examples.en: God’s covenant with Abraham in the Bible
examples.zh: 圣经中神与亚伯拉罕所立的约

examples.en: a covenant to a charity
examples.zh: 向慈善机构定期捐款的契约

senses.def: to promise or legally agree to do something or give somebody something, especially to pay a regular amount of money to somebody/something
senses.zh: 盟约：承诺或合法同意做某事或给予某人某物，特别是向某人/某物支付定期款项

examples.en: All profits are covenanted to medical charities.
examples.zh: 根据承诺所有利润都定期转给医疗慈善组织。

senses.def: any of a group of 17th-century Scottish Presbyterians
senses.zh: 盟约者：支持两个盟约（1638年和1643年）的17世纪苏格兰长老会中的任何一个。这些是捍卫长老会主义并抗议查理一世的宗教政策的正式声明，查理一世想与主教一起建立苏格兰教会，例如英格兰教会。盟约在英国内战中支持议会。

senses.def: a fashionable area in central London, that used to be London's main market for flowers, fruit and vegetables. In 1974 the market moved to New Covent Garden Market
senses.zh: 考文特花园（Covent Garden）：伦敦市中心的一个时尚地区，曾经是伦敦主要的花卉，水果和蔬菜市场。1974年，市场搬到了新科文特花园市场，市场广场上到处都是小商店和餐馆。这是一个深受游客欢迎的地方，街头表演者来招待他们。

examples.en: We spent all day shopping and sitting around in cafes in Covent Garden.
examples.zh: 我们花了一整天的时间购物并坐在考文特花园的咖啡馆里。

senses.def: another name for the Royal Opera House
senses.zh: 柯芬园（Covent Garden）：皇家歌剧院（Royal Opera House）的别称，它紧邻前柯芬园（Covent Garden）市场。最初的花卉市场大楼叫花厅，现在是歌剧院的一部分。

examples.en: We've got two tickets for ‘La Traviata’ at Covent Garden.
examples.zh: 我们有两张考文特花园《茶花女》的门票。

senses.def: an industrial city in the English Midlands
senses.zh: 考文垂（英格兰中部地区的工业城市，包括大教堂在内的许多建筑在二战中被炸毁。战后，在老教堂的废墟旁边修建了一座新的大教堂，由巴兹尔 · 斯彭斯设计）

senses.def: to refuse to speak to somebody, as a way of punishing them for something that they have done
senses.zh: 拒绝与某人交谈（作为惩罚）

senses.def: to refuse to speak to somebody, as a way of punishing them for something that they have done
senses.zh: 拒绝与某人交谈（作为惩罚）

senses.def: to place something over or in front of something in order to hide, protect or decorate it

examples.en: Cover the chicken loosely with foil.
examples.zh: 用锡箔把鸡肉松松地盖起来。

examples.en: She covered her face with her hands.
examples.zh: 她双手掩面。

examples.en: I covered my mouth to stifle a yawn.
examples.zh: 我捂着嘴憋住了哈欠。

examples.en: He laughed to cover (= hide) his nervousness.
examples.zh: 他哈哈大笑以掩饰他紧张的心情。

senses.def: to lie or spread over the surface of something

examples.en: Snow covered the ground.
examples.zh: 大雪覆盖了大地。

examples.en: Much of the country is covered by forest.
examples.zh: 森林覆盖着这个国家的大片土地。

examples.en: Its head, body, and tail are completely covered with brown fur.
examples.zh: 它的头、身体和尾巴全部覆盖着棕色的毛。

examples.en: His chest was covered in bruises.
examples.zh: 他的胸口满是瘀伤。

senses.def: to put or spread a layer of liquid, dust, etc. on somebody/something
senses.zh: 撒上，洒上，溅上（一层液体、尘土等）

examples.en: The wind blew in from the desert and covered everything with sand.
examples.zh: 风从沙漠那边吹来，把一切都蒙上了一层沙子。

examples.en: Soak the dried mushrooms by covering them in boiling water for a few minutes.
examples.zh: 将干蘑菇放入沸水中浸泡几分钟。

examples.en: The steps were now completely covered with water.
examples.zh: 台阶现在完全被水淹没了。

examples.en: The players were soon covered in mud.
examples.zh: 那些运动员很快就浑身溅满了泥。

senses.def: to include something; to deal with something

examples.en: The lectures covered a lot of ground (= a lot of material, subjects, etc.).
examples.zh: 这些讲座涉及的内容极为广泛丰富。

examples.en: The survey covers all aspects of the business.
examples.zh: 调查包括这家企业的各个方面。

examples.en: The articles cover a wide range of subjects.
examples.zh: 这些文章涵盖了广泛的主题。

examples.en: Each podcast covers a different topic.
examples.zh: 每个播客涵盖不同的主题。

examples.en: the sales team covering the northern part of the country (= selling to people in that area)
examples.zh: 负责这个国家北部地区的销售队伍

examples.en: Do the rules cover (= do they apply to) a case like this?
examples.zh: 这些规则适用于这样的情况吗？

examples.en: Don't worry. I've got it covered (= I'm dealing with it).
examples.zh: 别担心，我正处理这事呢。

senses.def: to be or provide enough money for something

examples.en: $100 should cover your expenses.
examples.zh: 100 美元该足够支付你的费用了。

examples.en: The show barely covered its costs.
examples.zh: 这场演出勉强够本。

examples.en: Your parents will have to cover your tuition fees.
examples.zh: 你的父母得支付你的学费。

senses.def: to travel the distance mentioned

examples.en: By sunset we had covered thirty miles.
examples.zh: 到日落时我们已走了三十英里。

examples.en: They walked for a long time and covered a good deal of ground.
examples.zh: 他们步行了很长时间，走了一大段路。

senses.def: to spread over the area mentioned

examples.en: The reserve covers an area of some 1 140 square kilometres.
examples.zh: 保护区占地面积大约 1 140 平方公里。

senses.def: to report on an event for television, a newspaper, etc.; to show an event on television

examples.en: She's covering the party's annual conference.
examples.zh: 她正在报道这个政党的年会新闻。

examples.en: The BBC will cover all the major games of the tournament.
examples.zh: 英国广播公司将报道这次锦标赛的所有重要赛事。

examples.en: The media has consistently refused to cover the story.
examples.zh: 媒体一直拒绝报道这个故事。

senses.def: to do somebody’s work or duties while they are away
senses.zh: 代替，顶替，替补（某人工作或履行职责）

examples.en: I'm covering for Jane while she's on leave.
examples.zh: 简休假时我来顶替她工作。

senses.def: to invent a lie or an excuse that will stop somebody from getting into trouble
senses.zh: （为免他人陷入麻烦而用谎话或借口）遮掩，掩盖，敷衍

examples.en: I have to go out for a minute—will you cover for me if anyone asks where I am?
examples.zh: 我得出去一会儿，假如有人问起我在哪里，你能为我搪塞一下吗？

senses.def: to protect somebody against loss, injury, etc. by insurance

examples.en: Are you fully covered for fire and theft?
examples.zh: 你是否买了足够的火险和盗窃险？

examples.en: Does this policy cover my husband to drive?
examples.zh: 这份保险单是否保我丈夫的驾车险？

senses.def: to take action in order to protect yourself against being blamed for something
senses.zh: 采取预防行动（以使自己免遭责备）

examples.en: Many firms put money aside to cover themselves against possible legal claims.
examples.zh: 许多公司存钱以应对可能的法律索赔。

senses.def: to protect somebody by threatening to shoot at anyone who tries to attack them

examples.en: Cover me while I move forward.
examples.zh: 掩护我前进。

examples.en: The artillery gave us covering fire (= shot to protect us).
examples.zh: 炮火掩护着我们。

senses.def: to aim a gun at a place or person so that nobody can escape or shoot

examples.zh: 警方用枪封锁了那栋大楼的出口。

examples.zh: 不许动！我们的枪口正对着你们！

examples.zh: 他们翻唱了滚石乐队的一首老歌。

senses.def: to consider and deal with all the things that could happen or could be needed when you are arranging something

examples.en: I am confident this contract covers all the bases.
examples.zh: 我确信这份合同涵盖了所有方面。

senses.def: to realize that you may be blamed or criticized for something later and take action to avoid this

examples.en: Get everything in writing in order to cover your back.

senses.def: to hide the real situation or facts when these are not good or pleasant

examples.zh: 爆炸发生以后，满街的人都奔跑躲避。

examples.zh: 他们寻找避风的地方。

examples.zh: 各种杂志的封面都有她的头像。

examples.zh: 他一挥手把眼镜摔到地上摔碎了。

examples.zh: 那家公司由于负债 5 000 万英镑而告破产。

examples.zh: 他们的网站在周二反复崩溃。

examples.zh: 流量激增使他们的服务器崩溃。

examples.zh: 我累极了，在沙发上就睡着了。

examples.zh: 他们喝了两箱啤酒。

senses.zh: 疯狂地：充满热情和活力

examples.zh: 他们疯狂地跳舞。

senses.zh: 疯狂地：以一种混乱和混乱的方式

examples.zh: 疯狂缠绕的电线

examples.zh: 演员们不得不疯狂尖叫。

senses.zh: 疯狂：愚蠢或不明智的行为或想法

senses.zh: 不理智的；疯狂的；愚蠢的；傻的

examples.zh: 你疯了？我们那样做会丧命的。

examples.en: I'd never do anything like that. That's just crazy.
examples.zh: 我绝不会做那样的事。那太疯狂了。

examples.zh: 他像白痴一样净把车往最不可思议的地方开。

examples.zh: 这个想法真荒唐！

examples.zh: “爱会让你做出疯狂的事情，”她说。

examples.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂，但也许行得通。

examples.zh: 她把钱借给他，一定是疯了。

examples.en: It's crazy to think he'll ever change.
examples.zh: 认为他会改变真是蠢到家了。

examples.zh: 那噪声吵得我快发疯了。

examples.zh: 里克对足球着了迷。

examples.zh: 她对足球很痴迷。

examples.en: I'm not crazy about jazz (= I don't like it very much).
examples.zh: 我对爵士乐不是很感冒。

senses.def: a place where babies and young children are taken care of while their parents are working, studying, shopping, etc.

examples.en: Younger children can be left in the crèche.
examples.zh: 小一点儿的孩子可以留在日托托儿所里。

senses.def: a model of the scene of Jesus Christ’s birth, placed in churches and homes at Christmas
senses.zh: 圣诞马槽（表现耶稣诞生的情景）

senses.def: a way of behaving and dressing that is acceptable to young people, especially those who live in cities and have experienced the problems of real life
senses.zh: 街头信誉，街头形象（青年人推崇的行为方式和着装风格，尤指城市青年）

senses.def: a quality that an idea or a story has that makes you believe it is true

examples.en: Historical evidence lends credence to his theory.
examples.zh: 史学根据使他的理论更为可信。

senses.def: belief in something as true

examples.en: They could give no credence to the findings of the survey.
examples.zh: 他们不相信这次调查的结果。

examples.en: Alternative medicine has been gaining credence (= becoming more widely accepted) recently.
examples.zh: 近来替代疗法越来越得到大众的认可。

senses.def: to be provided with credentials

examples.en: Faculty members needed to be properly credentialed in their respective disciplines.
examples.zh: 教师需要获得相关学科的资格证书。

senses.def: the quality that somebody/something has that makes people believe or trust them

examples.en: to gain/lack/lose credibility
examples.zh: 获取／缺乏／失去信任

examples.en: The prosecution did its best to undermine the credibility of the witness.
examples.zh: 控方竭力削弱证人的可信性。

examples.en: After the recent scandal, the government has lost all credibility.
examples.zh: 经过最近这次丑闻之后，政府完全失去了人们的信任。

examples.en: The media were talking of a credibility gap between what he said and what he did.
examples.zh: 媒体正在谈论他所说和所做的可信度差距。

senses.def: that can be believed or trusted

examples.en: a credible explanation/witness
examples.zh: 可信的解释／证人

examples.en: It is just not credible that she would cheat.
examples.zh: 她会行骗简直难以置信。

senses.def: that can be accepted, because it seems possible that it could be successful
senses.zh: （因看似可能成功而）可接受的

examples.en: Community service is seen as the only credible alternative to imprisonment.
examples.zh: 除监禁外，社区劳动被看作是唯一可接受的选择。

senses.def: in a way that is easy or possible to believe
senses.zh: 可信地；可靠地；令人信服地

examples.en: The 1920s period is portrayed very credibly.
examples.zh: 对 20 世纪 20 年代的描述非常可信。

examples.en: We can credibly describe the band's latest album as their best yet.
examples.zh: 我们完全可以说，这支乐队的最新专辑是他们迄今的最佳作品。

senses.def: an arrangement that you make, with a shop for example, to pay later for something you buy

examples.en: to get credit
examples.zh: 允许赊购

examples.en: We bought the dishwasher on credit.
examples.zh: 我们赊购了一台洗碗机。

examples.en: to offer interest-free credit (= allow somebody to pay later, without any extra charge)
examples.zh: 提供免息赊购

examples.en: Someone with a bad credit history is less likely to be lent money.
examples.zh: 有不良信用记录的人不容易获得贷款。

examples.en: a credit agreement
examples.zh: 信贷协定

examples.en: a credit facility
examples.zh: 信贷服务

examples.en: Your credit limit is now £2 000.
examples.zh: 你的信用额度现在为 2 000 英镑。

examples.en: He's a bad credit risk (= he is unlikely to pay the money later).
examples.zh: 他有欠账不还的危险。

examples.en: The credit crisis is far from over.
examples.zh: 信贷危机远未结束。

senses.def: money that you borrow from a bank; a loan

examples.en: The bank refused further credit to the company.
examples.zh: 银行拒绝再给那家公司提供贷款。

examples.en: Local lenders are more likely to extend credit (= lend money) to smaller, more marginal borrowers.
examples.zh: 当地放贷人更有可能向金额更小的边缘借款人提供贷款。

senses.def: the status of being trusted to pay back money to somebody who lends it to you

examples.en: Her credit isn't good anywhere now.
examples.zh: 她借钱不还，弄得声名狼藉。

senses.def: money that you have in your bank account; if you or your bank account are in credit

examples.en: You have a credit balance of £250.
examples.zh: 你有 250 英镑的存款余额。

examples.en: My account is in credit.
examples.zh: 我的账户里有余额。

senses.group: money in bank 银行存款

senses.def: a sum of money paid into a bank account; a record of the payment
senses.zh: （付入银行账户的）存款金额，贷记

examples.en: a credit of £50
examples.zh: 50 英镑的贷记

examples.en: You'll be paid by direct credit into your bank account.
examples.zh: 给你的付款将直接存入你的银行账户。

examples.en: I have three credits on my bank statement.
examples.zh: 我的银行结算单上有 3 笔存款。

senses.group: money in bank 银行存款

senses.def: the right to use a service up to a certain limit, paid for in advance

examples.en: My phone's run out of credit.
examples.zh: 我的电话欠费了。

examples.en: to add credit to your phone
examples.zh: 为您的手机充值

senses.group: money paid in advance 预付

senses.def: a payment that somebody has a right to for a particular reason

examples.en: The child tax credit is subject to strict income limitations.
examples.zh: 儿童税收抵免受到严格的收入限制。

examples.en: Export credits are granted to firms in low-income countries to give them a breathing space to pay for goods exported to them.
examples.zh: 向低收入国家的企业提供出口信贷，让它们有喘息的空间来支付出口到它们的货物。

senses.def: praise or approval because you are responsible for something good that has happened

examples.en: to get/deserve/receive/take/claim the credit
examples.zh: 获得／值得／接受／索取称赞

examples.en: He's a player who rarely seems to get the credit he deserves.
examples.zh: 他这个选手好像很少得到应得的赞扬。

examples.en: We did all the work and she gets all the credit!
examples.zh: 工作都是我们干的，而功劳却都归了她！

examples.en: I can't take all the credit for the show's success—it was a team effort.
examples.zh: 演出成功不能都算成我一个人的功劳，这是集体努力的结果。

examples.en: At least give him credit for trying (= praise him because he tried, even if he did not succeed).
examples.zh: 至少该表扬他尝试过。

examples.en: Credit will be given in the exam for good spelling and grammar.
examples.zh: 考试中拼写和语法出色者将受到表扬。

examples.en: His courage brought great credit to his regiment.
examples.zh: 他的勇气为他的团赢得了巨大的荣誉。

senses.def: a person or thing whose qualities or achievements are praised and who therefore earns respect for somebody/something else
senses.zh: 为…赢得荣誉的人（或事物）

examples.en: She is a credit to the school.
examples.zh: 她为学校赢得了荣誉。

examples.en: Your children are a great credit to you.
examples.zh: 您的孩子是您的一大功劳。

senses.def: the act of mentioning somebody who worked on a project such as a film or a television programme
senses.zh: （电影或电视节目演职人员的）片头字幕，片尾字幕

examples.en: She was given a programme credit for her work on the costumes for the play.
examples.zh: 她为这出戏准备服装，被列入剧目制作人员名单。

examples.en: The credits (= the list of all the people involved) seemed to last almost as long as the film!
examples.zh: 演职人员字幕持续的时间几乎与这部电影一样长！

examples.en: From the opening credits, the movie is non-stop action.
examples.zh: 从片头看，这部电影就是不间断的动作。

examples.en: The end credits came as a welcome relief.
examples.zh: 片尾字幕让人松了口气。

examples.en: We left before the final credits began to roll.
examples.zh: 片尾演职人员名单还未出现我们就退场了。

senses.group: movie/TV programme 电影；电视节目

senses.def: a film, play, television programme, etc. that somebody has worked on

examples.en: His film credits included ‘The Witches’ and ‘Halloween III’.
examples.zh: 他参与制作的电影包括《女巫》和《万圣节 3》。

senses.group: movie/TV programme 电影；电视节目

senses.def: a unit of study at a college or university (in the US, also at a school); the fact of having successfully completed a unit of study
senses.zh: （大学以及美国中小学的）学习单元，学分

examples.en: My math class is worth three credits.
examples.zh: 我的数学课为三个学分。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: if something does credit

examples.en: Your honesty does you great credit.
examples.zh: 你的诚实值得大大表扬。

examples.en: Your concern does you credit.
examples.zh: 你的关心给你赢得赞誉。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: to give somebody the praise they deserve, even if you do not really want to

examples.en: Give credit where credit is due—what the man does, he does well.
examples.zh: 有功必奖——这个人做事做得很好。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: to have achieved something

examples.en: He's only 30, and he already has four novels to his credit.
examples.zh: 他年仅 30，却已著有四部小说。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: used to introduce the good points about somebody/something, especially after the bad points have been mentioned
senses.zh: （尤用于提及缺点之后）就优点方面而言

examples.en: On the credit side, she’s always willing to work very late.
examples.zh: 从好的方面来说，她总是愿意工作到很晚。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: making somebody deserve praise or respect

examples.en: To his credit, Jack never told anyone exactly what had happened.
examples.zh: 杰克对发生的事守口如瓶，值得赞扬。

examples.en: It was to her credit that she managed to stay calm.
examples.zh: 值得赞扬的是，她能够保持冷静。

senses.group: unit of study 学习单元

senses.def: to add an amount of money to somebody’s bank account
senses.zh: （给银行账户）存入金额；把…记入贷方；贷记（银行账户）

examples.en: They credited my account two days later.
examples.zh: 两天后他们就记入我的账户了。

examples.en: Your account has been credited with $50 000.
examples.zh: 已把 5 万美元存入你的账户。

examples.en: The bank credited the oil company with $500 000.
examples.zh: 银行向那家石油公司提供 50 万美元信用贷款。

examples.en: $50 000 has been credited to your account.
examples.zh: 已把 5 万美元存入你的账户。

senses.group: put money in bank 往银行存钱

senses.def: to believe or say that somebody is responsible for doing something, especially something good

examples.en: All the contributors are credited on the title page.
examples.zh: 所有撰稿人的姓名均刊登在扉页上。

examples.en: She has been wrongly credited as the author.
examples.zh: 她一直被误认为是作者。

examples.en: The group has been widely credited with creating the sound of heavy metal.
examples.zh: 人们普遍认为这支乐队创造了重金属摇滚乐。

examples.en: The company is credited with inventing the industrial robot.
examples.zh: 发明工业机器人是那家公司的功劳。

examples.en: This therapy has long been credited with many benefits.
examples.zh: 长期以来，这种疗法一直被认为具有许多益处。

examples.en: Ray Charles is largely credited for creating soul music.
examples.zh: 雷·查尔斯 (Ray Charles) 因创作灵魂音乐而备受赞誉。

examples.en: Matthews was credited for the winning goal.
examples.zh: 马修斯因进球而获得胜利。

examples.en: The invention of the industrial robot is credited to the company.
examples.zh: 工业机器人的发明应归功于那家公司。

senses.def: to believe that somebody/something has a particular good quality or feature
senses.zh: 认为…有（良好的品质或特点）

examples.en: I credited you with a little more sense.
examples.zh: 我认为你更有见识。

examples.en: Credit me with some intelligence.
examples.zh: 相信我有一些智慧。

senses.def: to believe that somebody/something is of a particular type or quality

examples.en: The cheetah is generally credited as the world's fastest animal.
examples.zh: 普遍认为猎豹是世界上跑得最快的动物。

senses.def: to believe something, especially something surprising or unexpected
senses.zh: 相信（尤指令人惊奇或意外的事物）

examples.en: He's been promoted—would you credit it?
examples.zh: 他被擢升了，你相信吗？

items.idm: do somebody credit | do credit to somebody/something

senses.def: if something does credit

examples.en: Your honesty does you great credit.
examples.zh: 你的诚实值得大大表扬。

examples.en: Your concern does you credit.
examples.zh: 你的关心给你赢得赞誉。

items.idm: give credit where credit is due

senses.def: to give somebody the praise they deserve, even if you do not really want to

examples.en: Give credit where credit is due—what the man does, he does well.
examples.zh: 有功必奖——这个人做事做得很好。

senses.def: to have achieved something

examples.en: He's only 30, and he already has four novels to his credit.
examples.zh: 他年仅 30，却已著有四部小说。

senses.def: used to introduce the good points about somebody/something, especially after the bad points have been mentioned
senses.zh: （尤用于提及缺点之后）就优点方面而言

examples.en: On the credit side, she’s always willing to work very late.
examples.zh: 从好的方面来说，她总是愿意工作到很晚。

senses.def: making somebody deserve praise or respect

examples.en: To his credit, Jack never told anyone exactly what had happened.
examples.zh: 杰克对发生的事守口如瓶，值得赞扬。

examples.en: It was to her credit that she managed to stay calm.
examples.zh: 值得赞扬的是，她能够保持冷静。

senses.def: an arrangement with a shop or business to pay bills for goods or services at a later time, for example in regular amounts every month
a company that collects information about people's credit ratings

examples.en: Credit scores are compiled by the three major credit agencies, based on information provided by creditors.
examples.zh: 信用评分由三大信用机构根据债权人提供的信息编制。

senses.def: a company that collects information about people's credit ratings

examples.en: Most banks use scores calculated by credit bureaus to evaluate loan applications.
examples.zh: 大多数银行使用信用局计算的分数来评估贷款申请。

senses.def: a small plastic card that you can use to buy goods and services and pay for them later

examples.en: All major credit cards are accepted at our hotels.
examples.zh: 我们的旅馆接受所有主要的信用卡。

examples.en: The safest way to pay for goods ordered online is by credit card.
examples.zh: 在线订购商品付款最安全的方式是使用信用卡。

examples.en: I put the bill on my credit card.
examples.zh: 我把账记在信用卡上。

senses.def: an economic condition in which it suddenly becomes difficult and expensive to borrow money

examples.en: In a credit crunch, lenders stop lending and credit becomes tough to obtain.
examples.zh: 在信贷紧缩的情况下，贷方停止放贷，信贷变得难以获得。

examples.en: Consumer confidence is plunging as the credit crunch hits household budgets.
examples.zh: 随着信贷紧缩影响家庭预算，消费者信心正在大幅下降。

examples.en: Many companies will not survive the unfolding credit crunch.
examples.zh: 许多公司将无法在不断出现的信贷紧缩中幸存下来。

senses.def: an amount of money that a financial organization such as a bank is willing to lend to a person or organization
a letter that a shop gives you when you have returned something and that allows you to have goods of the same value in exchange
senses.zh: 贷项凭单（退货时发给的凭证，可换取等值的商品）

examples.en: If damaged items have to be returned, the manufacturer may issue a credit note.
examples.zh: 损坏的商品如需退回厂家，厂家可开具欠条。

senses.def: a judgement made by a bank, etc. about how likely somebody is to pay back money that they borrow, and how safe it is to lend money to them
senses.zh: （银行等作出的）信用等级评定

examples.en: He has a bad credit rating.
examples.zh: 他的还款信用很差。

senses.def: a number given to somebody to show how likely they are to pay back money that they borrow from a bank, a company, etc.

examples.en: Higher credit scores mean better interest rates and top treatment from all lenders.
examples.zh: 更高的信用评分意味着更好的利率和来自所有贷方的最高待遇。

examples.en: If you cannot repay a loan within an agreed time, your credit score may become worse.
examples.zh: 如果您无法在约定的时间内偿还贷款，您的信用评分可能会变得更糟。

senses.def: the system of allowing somebody to take completed units of study from one course to another so that they contribute to the final qualification

examples.en: Institutions need to develop processes for facilitating credit transfer for academically qualified students.
examples.zh: 机构需要制定促进学术合格学生学分转移的流程。

senses.def: the process of sending money from one person’s bank account to another’s

examples.en: Wages are paid by direct credit transfer to your bank account each month.
examples.zh: 工资每月通过直接转帐方式支付到您的银行帐户。

examples.en: The cost of credit transfers has increased.
examples.zh: 信用转移的成本增加了。

senses.def: an organization that lends money to its members at low rates of interest
senses.zh: 互助储金会，信用合作社（向会员提供低息贷款）

senses.def: of a quite good standard and deserving praise or approval
senses.zh: 值得赞扬的；应当认可的

examples.en: It was a very creditable result for the team.
examples.zh: 对这支队来说，这个比赛结果是十分值得称道的。

examples.en: The Green Party won a creditable 16 per cent of the vote.
examples.zh: 绿党赢得了令人瞩目的 16% 的选票。

examples.en: Although they struggled, they ended up coming a creditable second.
examples.zh: 虽然他们努力了，但最终获得了聊胜于无的第二名。

examples.en: The chairman welcomed the company’s creditable performance in the previous year.
examples.zh: 董事长对公司上一年的良好业绩表示赞赏。

senses.def: morally good

examples.en: There was nothing very creditable in what he did.
examples.zh: 他这事做得可实在不怎么样。

senses.def: well enough to deserve praise or approval
senses.zh: 值得赞扬地﹔应当认可地

examples.en: The team performed creditably.
examples.zh: 该队表现出色。

senses.def: in a way that is morally good

examples.en: They very creditably tried to help.
examples.zh: 他们非常值得信赖地试图提供帮助。

senses.def: a person, company, etc. that somebody owes money to

examples.en: The property will be sold to pay off their creditors.
examples.zh: 卖掉财产以偿债给他们的债主。

senses.def: the fact that somebody can be trusted to pay back money that is owed; the fact that somebody is safe to lend money to
senses.zh: 可信赖偿还欠款的；信誉好的；信用可靠的；借贷安全的

senses.def: able to be trusted to pay back money that is owed; safe to lend money to
senses.zh: 可信赖偿还欠款的；信誉好的；信用可靠的；借贷安全的

senses.def: a set of beliefs
the ability or the wish to believe that something is real or true

examples.en: The plot of the novel stretches credulity to the limit (= it is almost impossible to believe).
examples.zh: 这部小说的情节牵强得几乎令人无法相信。

senses.def: too ready to believe things and therefore easy to trick
a member of a native North American people, many of whom live in central Canada
senses.zh: 克里人（美洲土著，很多居于加拿大中部）

senses.def: a set of principles or religious beliefs
senses.zh: 信念；原则；纲领；宗教信仰

examples.en: We welcome people of all races, colours and creeds.
examples.zh: 我们欢迎所有种族、肤色和信仰的人们。

examples.en: discrimination on the basis of race, colour or creed
examples.zh: 基于种族、肤色或宗教信仰的歧视

examples.en: What is his political creed?
examples.zh: 他的政治信仰是什么？

senses.def: a statement of Christian belief that is spoken as part of some church services
a narrow area of water where the sea flows into the land

examples.en: They drove to the little creek where they kept their fishing boat.
examples.zh: 他们驱车来到小港湾，那里是他们停放渔船的地方。

senses.def: a small river or stream

examples.en: Sandy Creek
examples.zh: 桑迪溪

examples.en: He stood on the steep bank above Ray’s Creek.
examples.zh: 他站在雷河陡峭的岸上。

senses.def: in a difficult or bad situation

examples.en: If they won't accept my credit card, I'll really be up the creek.
examples.zh: 如果他们不接受我的信用卡，那我的麻烦就大了。

senses.def: a member of a native North American people, many of whom now live in the US state of Oklahoma
senses.zh: 克里克人（美洲土著，很多现居于美国俄克拉何马州）

senses.def: in a difficult or bad situation

examples.en: If they won't accept my credit card, I'll really be up the creek.
examples.zh: 如果他们不接受我的信用卡，那我的麻烦就大了。

senses.def: a basket
to move slowly, quietly and carefully, because you do not want to be seen or heard
senses.zh: 悄悄地缓慢行进；蹑手蹑脚地移动

examples.en: I crept up the stairs, trying not to wake my parents.
examples.zh: 为了尽量不吵醒父母，我蹑手蹑脚地上了楼。

examples.en: I heard someone creeping around the house.
examples.zh: 我听到有人在房子周围爬行。

senses.def: to move with your body close to the ground; to move slowly on your hands and knees
to move or develop very slowly
senses.zh: 非常缓慢地行进；不知不觉产生；渐渐出现

examples.en: Her arms crept around his neck.
examples.zh: 她的双臂慢慢地搂住了他的脖子。

examples.en: A slight feeling of suspicion crept over me.
examples.zh: 我渐渐地产生了一丝疑虑。

senses.def: to grow along the ground or up walls using long stems
to be too friendly or helpful to somebody in authority in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get an advantage from them

examples.en: He's always creeping to the boss.
examples.zh: 他总是偷偷摸摸地去找老板。

senses.def: to make you feel afraid or full of horror
senses.zh: 使起鸡皮疙瘩；令人毛骨悚然；使人汗毛直竖

examples.en: Just the sight of him makes my flesh creep.
examples.zh: 光是看到他就让我浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。

examples.en: The story made his flesh creep.
examples.zh: 这个故事让他毛骨悚然。

senses.def: a person that you dislike very much and find very unpleasant

examples.en: He's a nasty little creep!
