examples.en: He grew up during the Great Depression of the 1930s.
examples.zh: 他成长于20世纪30年代的经济大萧条时期。

senses.def: a part of a surface that is lower than the parts around it

examples.en: Rainwater collects in shallow depressions on the ground.
examples.zh: 雨水积在地上的浅坑里。

examples.en: From the air, the photos show a shallow depression on the planet's surface.
examples.zh: 从空中鸟瞰的照片显示行星表面有一处浅浅的凹陷。

senses.def: a weather condition in which the pressure of the air becomes lower, often causing rain

examples.en: an atmospheric depression moving east from the Atlantic
examples.zh: 从大西洋向东移动的低气压

senses.def: connected with the medical condition of depression

examples.en: depressive illness
examples.zh: 抑郁症

senses.def: a person who is affected by the medical condition of depression
an instrument for pressing something down
senses.zh: （检验或手术中用的）压板，压器

senses.def: the act of releasing the pressure inside a container or vehicle; the fact of pressure being released
senses.zh: 释放（容器或交通工具内的）压力；（使）减压，降压

senses.def: to release the pressure inside a container or vehicle; to lose pressure in this way
senses.zh: 释放（容器或交通工具内的）压力；（使）减压，降压

senses.def: the fact of not having something that you need, like enough food, money or a home; the process that causes this

examples.en: children living in poverty and deprivation
examples.zh: 生活在贫困和物资匮乏中的儿童

examples.en: a study of the effects of sleep deprivation
examples.zh: 睡眠缺失影响的研究

examples.en: the deprivation of war (= the suffering caused by not having enough of some things)
examples.zh: 战时的物品匮乏

examples.en: the deprivations and hardships resulting from the blockade
examples.zh: 封锁导致的物资匮乏和生活不便

senses.def: to prevent somebody from having or doing something, especially something important
senses.zh: 剥夺；使丧失；使不能享有

examples.en: They were imprisoned and deprived of their basic rights.
examples.zh: 他们遭到监禁并被剥夺了基本权利。

examples.en: Why should you deprive yourself of such simple pleasures?
examples.zh: 你为什么连这种简单的乐事也不让自己享受一下呢？

senses.def: (in writing) department
the distance from the top or surface to the bottom of something; a particular distance down from the surface of something

examples.en: What's the depth of the water here?
examples.zh: 这儿的水有多深？

examples.en: the depth of a cut/wound/crack
examples.zh: 划口／伤口／裂口深度

examples.en: Water was found at a depth of 30 metres.
examples.zh: 在 30 米深处找到了水。

examples.en: They dug down to a depth of two metres.
examples.zh: 他们挖到两米深。

examples.en: Many dolphins can dive to depths of 200 metres.
examples.zh: 许多海豚可潜到 200 米深。

examples.en: The oil well extended several hundreds of feet in depth.
examples.zh: 油井向下延伸了数百英尺。

examples.en: The camera must be strong enough to resist the immense water pressure at depth.
examples.zh: 照相机必须足够坚固，以抵抗深水区的巨大压力。

examples.en: Most earthquakes occur at much shallower depths, usually less than 30 kilometres.
examples.zh: 大多数地震发生在较浅的深度，通常小于 30 公里。

senses.def: the distance from the front to the back of something

examples.en: The depth of the shelves is 30 centimetres.
examples.zh: 书架的深度为 30 厘米。

senses.def: the strength and power of feelings

examples.en: the depth of her love
examples.zh: 她那爱情之深

examples.en: music of great emotional depth
examples.zh: 深情的音乐

senses.def: qualities that give somebody/something extra character and make them/it interesting

examples.en: The separate storylines really add depth and personality to the characters.
examples.zh: 独立的故事情节确实增加了人物的深度和个性。

examples.en: This film lacks the complexity or depth of his best movies.
examples.zh: 这部电影缺乏他最好的电影的复杂性或深度。

examples.en: Her paintings reveal hidden depths (= unknown and interesting things about her character).
examples.zh: 她的画表现出她内心深处的东西。

senses.def: the quality of knowing or understanding a lot of details about something; the ability to provide and explain these details

examples.en: a writer of great wisdom and depth
examples.zh: 有卓越智慧和洞察力的作家

examples.en: His ideas lack depth.
examples.zh: 他的想法缺乏深度。

examples.en: She has the ability to treat big subjects with breadth and depth.
examples.zh: 她有能力处理大课题的广度和深度。

examples.en: a job that doesn’t require any great depth of knowledge
examples.zh: 不需要多么高深知识的工作

examples.en: Younger students cannot be expected to have great depth of understanding.
examples.zh: 不能期求年轻学生有很深刻的理解力。

senses.def: the deepest, most extreme or serious part of something

examples.en: the depths of the ocean
examples.zh: 海洋深处

examples.en: to live in the depths of the country (= a long way from a town)
examples.zh: 住在偏远地区

examples.en: in the depths of winter (= when it is coldest)
examples.zh: 在隆冬季节

examples.en: She was in the depths of despair.
examples.zh: 她处于绝望的深渊。

examples.en: He gazed into the depths of her eyes.
examples.zh: 他深深凝视着她的眼睛。

senses.def: the strength of a colour

examples.en: Strong light will affect the depth of colour of your carpets and curtains.
examples.zh: 强烈的阳光会使你的地毯和窗帘褪色。

senses.def: the quality in a work of art or a photograph that makes it appear not to be flat
to be in water that is too deep to stand in with your head above water
senses.zh: 在水深没顶（或够不着底）的地方

examples.en: If you can't swim, don't go out of your depth.
examples.zh: 你若不会游泳,别走入水深过头的地方.

examples.en: I don't like going out of my depth in the sea.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢到海中水深没顶的深处。

senses.def: to be unable to understand something because it is too difficult; to be in a situation that you cannot control
senses.zh: 非某人所能理解；为某人力所不及

examples.en: He felt totally out of his depth in his new job.
examples.zh: 他感到自己根本不能胜任这新工作。

examples.en: The writer seems a little out of her depth when dealing with the emotional issue involved.
examples.zh: 在处理所涉及到的情感问题时这位女作家显得有点儿力不从心。

senses.def: in a detailed, careful and complete way

examples.en: I haven't looked at the report in depth yet.
examples.zh: 我还没有细看这份报告。

examples.en: an in-depth study
examples.zh: 深入研究

examples.en: I studied phonology in depth at college.
examples.zh: 我在大学里深入学习了音系学。

senses.def: to be or to experience an extreme example of something unpleasant
senses.zh: 陷入（痛苦等的）深渊；深入…深处

examples.en: His latest novel plumbs the depths of horror and violence.
examples.zh: 他最新的小说充斥着极端恐怖和暴力。

examples.en: It was at that stage in her life when she plumbed the depths of despair.
examples.zh: 正是在这个阶段，她陷入了绝望的深渊。

examples.en: The team's poor performances plumbed new depths last night when they lost 10–2.
examples.zh: 昨晚这个队的糟糕表现达到了新低纪录，以 2:10 输掉了。

examples.en: The story plumbed the depths of tabloid journalism.
examples.zh: 这个故事完全迎合了小报的低级趣味。

senses.def: the quality of being strong because you have a great variety of good people, ideas, etc. that can contribute to the success of something
senses.zh: 板凳深度深；团队无弱兵

examples.en: The French team does not have the strength in depth that the Australians have.
examples.zh: 法国队的板凳深度不如澳大利亚队。

senses.zh: 景深（照相机能同时清晰拍摄的最近和最远物体之间的距离）

senses.def: a small group of people who are asked or allowed to act or speak for others

examples.en: The mayor agreed to receive a deputation of local residents.
examples.zh: 市长同意接待当地居民代表团。

examples.en: Both sides in the dispute sent deputations to the prime minister's office.
examples.zh: 争端双方均派代表前往总理办公室。

examples.zh: 他获授权向委员会表达我们的观点。

examples.zh: 格林女士请我代表她出席会议。

senses.zh: 委托：赋予某人执行特定任务的权力，尤其是帮助警察的权力

examples.zh: 圣克拉拉警方派出约 100 名外地警官协助体育场巡逻。

examples.en: Volunteers were deputized to collect contact information from would-be supporters.
examples.zh: 志愿者被委托收集潜在支持者的联系信息。

senses.def: a person who is the next most important person below a business manager, a head of a school, a political leader, etc. and who does that person’s job when they are away

examples.en: I'm acting as deputy till the manager returns.
examples.zh: 我在经理回来之前代行他的职务。

examples.en: She was appointed deputy head of the school.
examples.zh: 她被任命为学校副校长。

senses.def: the name for a member of parliament in some countries

examples.en: 23 women were among the 77 deputies elected.
examples.zh: 当选的77名议员中有23名女性。

senses.def: (in the US) a police officer who helps the sheriff
senses.zh: （美国协助地方治安官办案的）警官

senses.def: to force somebody to leave their natural social, cultural or geographical
senses.zh: 迫使（某人）离开熟悉的环境；使背井离乡

senses.def: to leave the track; to make a train do this

examples.en: The train derailed and plunged into the river.
examples.zh: 火车脱轨栽进了河里。

examples.en: The rebels plotted to derail trains and blow up bridges.
examples.zh: 叛乱分子密谋使火车脱轨并炸毁桥梁。

senses.def: to stop a process from continuing in the way it was intended to

examples.en: This latest incident could derail the peace process.
examples.zh: 最近这个事件可能会扰乱和平进程。

examples.en: It is claims of financial irregularities which could ultimately derail his campaign.
examples.zh: 对财务违规行为的指控最终可能会破坏他的竞选活动。

examples.en: The company’s plans were initially derailed by problems with licence agreements.
examples.zh: 该公司的计划最初因许可协议问题而脱轨。

senses.def: a type of gear
senses.zh: 拨链器，变速器（自行车换挡装置）

examples.en: the derailment of a passenger train
examples.zh: 旅客列车脱轨

senses.zh: 脱轨：以某种方式阻止流程继续进行

examples.en: the derailment of the peace process
examples.zh: 和平进程脱轨

senses.def: unable to behave and think normally, especially because of a mental illness
senses.zh: 精神错乱的；精神失常的；疯狂的

examples.en: mentally deranged
examples.zh: 精神错乱

examples.en: a deranged attacker
examples.zh: 疯狂的攻击者

examples.en: At first I thought he was deranged.
examples.zh: 起初我以为他发疯了。

examples.en: The plan seemed to be the product of a deranged mind.
examples.zh: 这个计划像是精神错乱的人想出来的。

examples.en: Deranged with panic, I ran back and forth.
examples.zh: 我惊慌失措，来回奔跑。

senses.def: a condition in which somebody is unable to behave and think normally, especially because of a mental illness

examples.en: He seemed to be on the verge of total derangement.
examples.zh: 他似乎已濒临精神崩溃的边缘。

senses.def: a hard black hat with a curved brim
senses.zh: 常礼帽（英格兰旧时商人等戴）

senses.def: a sports competition between teams from the same area or town
senses.zh: 德比，同城大战（同地区两队间的比赛）

examples.en: a local derby between the two North London sides
examples.zh: 两支北伦敦队之间的一场同城德比

examples.en: a derby match
examples.zh: 地区体育比赛

senses.def: a race or sports competition

examples.en: a motorcycle derby
examples.zh: 摩托车大赛

senses.def: used in the name of several horse races that happen every year
senses.zh: 德比马赛（特指几个一年一度的马赛）

examples.en: the Epsom Derby
examples.zh: 埃普瑟姆马赛

examples.en: the Kentucky Derby
examples.zh: 肯塔基马赛

senses.def: a city in central England famous for its fine Crown Derby
senses.zh: 德比（英格兰中部城市，以精美的皇冠德比瓷器和劳斯莱斯汽车、飞机发动机及其他工程产品而闻名）

senses.def: a county in north central England. It contains the Peak District
senses.zh: 德比郡（英格兰中北部一郡，首府马特洛克）

senses.def: to use a piece of data to discover where another piece of data is held
to free a trade, a business activity, etc. from rules and controls
senses.zh: 撤销对（贸易、商业活动等）的管制；解除控制

examples.en: deregulated financial markets
examples.zh: 放宽了管制的金融市场

senses.def: the process of making a trade, business activity, etc. free from rules and controls
senses.zh: 撤销对（贸易、商业活动等）的管制；解除控制

examples.en: financial/economic deregulation
examples.zh: 金融/经济放松管制

senses.def: intended to free a trade, a business activity, etc. from rules and controls; connected with this process
senses.zh: 撤销对（贸易、商业活动等）的管制；解除控制

examples.en: deregulatory reforms
examples.zh: 撤销管制的改革

senses.def: a first name for boys
(1942-94) an English film director, artist and writer who was also known as a campaigner for gay
senses.zh: 德里克·贾曼（Derek Jarman）：（1942-94）是一位英国电影导演，艺术家和作家，也被称为同性恋权利运动者。他最著名的电影包括塞巴斯蒂安（1976），朋克电影周年（1978），暴风雨（1979），卡拉瓦乔（1986），英格兰末代（1987），花园（1990），爱德华二世（1991），布鲁（1993）和维特根斯坦（1993）。他还执导流行视频并写了几本书，其中包括《跳舞壁架》（1991年）。

senses.def: not used or cared for and in bad condition
senses.zh: 荒废的；被弃置的；破旧的

examples.en: derelict land/buildings/sites
examples.zh: 荒废的土地；被废弃的建筑物；破旧的遗址

examples.en: The canal has been derelict for many years.
examples.zh: 这条运河已废弃多年。

examples.en: The land lay derelict for ten years.
examples.zh: 这块地荒废了 10 年。

examples.en: a partially derelict mill
examples.zh: 一座部份被弃置的磨坊

senses.def: failing completely to do your duty or perform your obligations

examples.en: They have been grossly derelict in their duty.
examples.zh: 他们严重失职。

examples.en: She realizes that she's been derelict in her responsibilities as a mother.
examples.zh: 她意识到自己辜负了作为母亲的责任。

senses.def: a person without a home, a job or property
senses.zh: 无家可归者；乞丐；社会弃儿

examples.en: derelicts living on the streets
examples.zh: 流落街头的乞丐

senses.def: the state of land or buildings not being used or cared for and in bad condition

examples.en: industrial/urban dereliction
examples.zh: 工业／城市废墟

examples.en: a house in a state of dereliction
examples.zh: 破旧不堪的房屋

senses.def: the fact of deliberately not doing what you ought to do, especially when it is part of your job

examples.en: The police officers were found guilty of serious dereliction of duty.
examples.zh: 这些警察被判犯有严重渎职罪。

senses.def: to treat somebody/something as silly and not worth considering seriously

examples.en: His views were derided as old-fashioned.
examples.zh: 他的观点被当作旧思想受到嘲弄。

examples.en: The play was derided by the critics.
examples.zh: 该剧遭到评论家的嘲笑。

senses.def: a strong feeling that somebody/something is silly and not worth considering seriously, shown by laughing in an unkind way or by making unkind remarks

examples.en: Her speech was greeted with howls of derision.
examples.zh: 她的演讲受到阵阵嘲笑。

examples.en: He became an object of universal derision.
examples.zh: 他成了众人嘲弄的对象。

senses.def: unkind and showing that you think somebody/something is silly

examples.en: She gave a short, derisive laugh.
examples.zh: 她讥讽地笑了笑。

examples.en: His voice was savagely derisive.
examples.zh: 他的声音充满了野蛮的嘲讽。

senses.def: in an unkind way that shows you think somebody/something is silly
senses.zh: 嘲讽地：以一种不友善的方式表明你认为某人/某事很愚蠢

examples.en: He speaks derisively about modern pop music.
examples.zh: 他嘲笑现代流行音乐。

senses.def: too small or of too little value to be considered seriously
senses.zh: 少得可笑的；少得可怜的；不屑一顾的

examples.en: They offered us a derisory £50 a week.
examples.zh: 他们每周给我们 50 英镑，少得可怜。

senses.def: unkind and showing that you think somebody/something is silly
the origin or development of something, especially a word

examples.en: a word of Greek derivation
examples.zh: 源自希腊语的词

senses.def: the action of obtaining something from a source or origin

examples.en: the derivation of scientific laws from observation
examples.zh: 从观察中得出科学规律

senses.def: a word or thing that has been developed or produced from another word or thing
senses.zh: 派生词；衍生字；派生物；衍生物

examples.en: ‘Happiness’ is a derivative of ‘happy’.
examples.zh: happiness 是 happy 的派生词。

examples.en: Plastic is a derivative of petroleum.
examples.zh: 塑料是石油的衍生物。

senses.def: copied from something else; not having new or original ideas
senses.zh: 模仿他人的；缺乏独创性的

examples.en: a derivative design/style
examples.zh: 沿袭前人的设计／样式

examples.en: I found the novel thin and derivative. I had expected more.
examples.zh: 我发现这部小说单薄且衍生。我本来期待更多。

senses.def: to come or develop from something

examples.en: The word ‘politics’ is derived from a Greek word meaning ‘city’.
examples.zh: politics 一词源自希腊语，意思是 city。

senses.def: to get something from something

examples.en: He derived great pleasure from painting.
examples.zh: 他从绘画中得到极大的乐趣。

senses.def: to obtain a substance from something

examples.en: The new drug is derived from fish oil.
examples.zh: 这种新药是从鱼油中提炼出来的。

senses.def: a skin condition in which the skin becomes red, swollen
connected with skin diseases or the scientific study of skin diseases
a doctor who studies and treats skin diseases
senses.zh: 皮肤病医生；皮肤病专家

senses.def: the scientific study of skin diseases
the skin
the layer of living tissue

examples.en: He had a second-degree burn down to the dermis.
examples.zh: 他的真皮层被二级烧伤。

senses.def: a first name for boys
to state that something or somebody is without worth
to ignore a responsibility or duty

senses.zh: 下议院案头文箱（置于英国下议院中央的桌子上，大臣站在桌边发言）

senses.def: a man who does dangerous and criminal things without caring about himself or other people
feeling or showing that you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger to yourself or others
senses.zh: （因绝望而）不惜冒险的，不顾一切的，拼命的

examples.en: The prisoners grew increasingly desperate.
examples.zh: 犯人因绝望而越来越胆大妄为。

examples.en: Stores are getting desperate after two years of poor sales.
examples.zh: 两年来销路不畅，商店不惜冒起险来。

examples.en: Somewhere out there was a desperate man, cold, hungry, hunted.
examples.zh: 那外面有个男人又冷又饿，还有人抓他，走投无路了。

examples.en: I heard sounds of a desperate struggle in the next room.
examples.zh: 我听到隔壁房间里有拼命挣扎的声音。

senses.def: giving little hope of success; tried when everything else has failed
senses.zh: 绝望的；孤注一掷的；铤而走险的

examples.en: He made a desperate bid for freedom.
examples.zh: 他为获自由孤注一掷。

examples.en: She clung to the edge in a desperate attempt to save herself.
examples.zh: 为了活命，她拼命抓住边缘。

examples.en: His increasing financial difficulties forced him to take desperate measures.
examples.zh: 不断增加的经济困难迫使他采取了铤而走险的办法。

examples.en: Doctors were fighting a desperate battle to save the little girl's life.
examples.zh: 医生们不惜一切地奋力抢救小女孩的生命。

senses.def: needing or wanting something very much

examples.en: He was so desperate for a job he would have done anything.
examples.zh: 他当时太想找份工作了，什么事都愿意干。

examples.en: I'm desperate for a coffee.
examples.zh: 我太想喝咖啡了

examples.en: to be desperate for money/help/cash/attention
examples.zh: 迫切需要金钱/帮助/现金/关注

examples.en: I was absolutely desperate to see her.
examples.zh: 我极想见到她。

examples.en: She was desperate to escape small town life.
examples.zh: 她迫切地想逃离小镇生活。

senses.def: extremely serious or dangerous
senses.zh: 极严重的；极危险的；很危急的

examples.en: The children are in desperate need of love and attention.
examples.zh: 这些孩子非常需要爱心和关注。

examples.en: They face a desperate shortage of clean water.
examples.zh: 他们面临洁净水的严重短缺。

examples.en: His financial situation was desperate.
examples.zh: 他的经济状况陷入困境。

examples.en: He had died in desperate poverty.
examples.zh: 他是在极度贫困中死去的。

examples.en: American farmers are in desperate straits today.
examples.zh: 今天的美国农民正处于绝望的困境中。

senses.def: a character in the former British children's comic
senses.zh: 绝望的丹：前英国儿童漫画《丹迪》中的角色。他是一个很坚强的牛仔，下巴很大，不是很聪明，但性格温柔。他最喜欢的一餐是“牛派”。

senses.def: a very successful American television series shown on ABC
senses.zh: 《绝望的主妇》（非常成功的美国电视连续剧，在美国广播公司和英国的ITV上播出，讲述了四名妇女在郊区一条叫做Wisteria Lane的道路上的生活。第五名妇女，是其他四个人的朋友，在系列赛开始时刚刚自杀，并且听到她的声音对她去世后发生的事发表评论。该系列在2005年获得了两次金球奖。）

senses.def: in a way that shows you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger to yourself or others
senses.zh: （因绝望而）不惜冒险地，不顾一切地，拼命地

examples.en: She looked desperately around for a weapon.
examples.zh: 她在四下里找，急于弄到一件武器。

senses.def: extremely, especially when talking about bad situations
senses.zh: 极严重地；极危险地；很危急地

examples.en: desperately ill/unhappy/lonely
examples.zh: 病得厉害；极为不快；极其孤独

examples.en: He grew up desperately poor.
examples.zh: 他在极端贫困中长大。

senses.def: very much, especially when talking about difficult or bad situations

examples.en: They desperately wanted a child.
examples.zh: 他们非常想要一个孩子。

examples.en: He took a deep breath, desperately trying to keep calm.
examples.zh: 他深深地吸了口气，竭尽全力保持镇定。

senses.def: the state of being desperate

examples.en: In desperation, she called Louise and asked for her help.
examples.zh: 在走投无路的情况下，她给路易丝打了个电话请她帮忙。

examples.en: There was a note of desperation in his voice.
examples.zh: 听他的语气他急得要命。

examples.en: an act of sheer desperation
examples.zh: 完全不顾一切的行为

senses.def: very unpleasant or evil
senses.zh: 令人厌恶的；可鄙的；卑鄙的

examples.en: a despicable act/crime
examples.zh: 卑鄙的行为／罪行

examples.en: I hate you! You're despicable.
examples.zh: 我恨你！你真卑鄙。

senses.def: in a way that is very unpleasant or evil
senses.zh: 令人厌恶的；可鄙的；卑鄙的

examples.en: A small number of fans behaved despicably.
examples.zh: 少数粉丝行为卑劣。

examples.en: If the allegations are true, he has acted despicably.
examples.zh: 如果这些指控属实，那么他的行为就很卑鄙。

examples.en: It was a despicably vile racist tirade.
examples.zh: 这是一次卑鄙卑鄙的种族主义长篇大论。

examples.en: Despicably, they are using the incident to inspire hate.
examples.zh: 可耻的是，他们利用这一事件煽动仇恨。

senses.def: to dislike and have no respect for somebody/something

examples.en: She despised gossip in any form.
examples.zh: 她对任何形式的流言蜚语都嗤之以鼻。

examples.en: I don’t know why they despise me so much.
examples.zh: 我不知道他们为什么这么看不起我。

examples.en: He despised himself for being so cowardly.
examples.zh: 他为自己如此怯懦而自惭形秽。

examples.en: She thoroughly despised him for his weakness.
examples.zh: 她因为他的软弱而十分鄙视他。

synonyms.words: dislike ▪ can’t stand ▪ despise ▪ can’t bear ▪ loathe ▪ detest

intro.en: These words all mean to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含厌恶、讨厌、憎恶之义。

items.def: to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something. Although hate is generally a very strong verb, it is also commonly used in spoken or informal English to talk about people or things that you dislike in a less important way, for example a particular type of food:
items.zh: 尽管 hate 通常为语气很强的动词，但亦常用于口语或非正式英语中，谈论不太喜欢的人或物，如某种食物等

items.def: (rather formal) to not like somebody/​something. Dislike is a rather formal word; it is less formal, and more usual, to say that you don't like somebody/​something, especially in spoken English:
items.zh: dislike 为相当正式的用语，don’t like 则较非正式，而且较常用，尤其在英语口语中

items.def: (rather informal) used to emphasize that you really do not like somebody/​something:
items.zh: 强调不喜欢、受不了、不能容忍

examples.en: I can’t stand his brother.
examples.zh: 他弟弟让我受不了。

items.def: to dislike and have no respect for somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指鄙视、蔑视、看不起

examples.en: He despised himself for being so cowardly.
examples.zh: 他为自己如此怯懦而自惭形秽。

items.def: used to say that you dislike something so much that you cannot accept or deal with it:
items.zh: 指无法承受、应付不了

examples.en: I can’t bear having cats in the house.
examples.zh: 家里有猫我可受不了。

items.def: to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They loathe each other.
examples.zh: 他们相互讨厌。

items.def: (rather formal) to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They absolutely detest each other.
examples.zh: 他们完全是相互憎恨。

senses.def: used to show that something happened or is true although something else might have happened to prevent it

examples.en: Her voice was shaking despite all her efforts to control it.
examples.zh: 尽管她竭尽全力控制自己，声音仍然在颤抖。

examples.en: Despite applying for hundreds of jobs, he is still out of work.
examples.zh: 尽管他申请了数百个工作，但仍然在失业中。

examples.en: She was good at physics despite the fact that she found it boring.
examples.zh: 尽管她认为物理枯燥无味，她却学得很好。

senses.def: used to show that somebody did not intend to do the thing mentioned

examples.en: He had to laugh despite himself.
examples.zh: 他不想笑，但没法不笑。

senses.def: to steal something valuable from a place; to make a place less attractive by damaging or destroying it
a feeling of being sad and without much hope
senses.zh: 苦恼的；沮丧的；泄气的；失望的

examples.en: a mood of despondency
examples.zh: 沮丧的心情

examples.en: Life's not all gloom and despondency.
examples.zh: 生活并不都是悲观和失望。

examples.en: a situation of high unemployment and despondency about the future
examples.zh: 高失业率和对未来感到沮丧的情况

senses.def: sad, without much hope
senses.zh: 苦恼的；沮丧的；泄气的；失望的

examples.en: There are times when it is hard not to feel despondent.
examples.zh: 有时很难不感到沮丧。

examples.en: She was becoming increasingly despondent about the way things were going.
examples.zh: 她对事情的发展越来越失望。

senses.def: in a way that shows you are sad and without much hope
a leader with great power, especially one who uses it in a cruel way
senses.zh: 专制统治者；专制君主；暴君

examples.en: an enlightened despot (= one who tries to use his/her power in a good way)
examples.zh: 开明的专制君主

examples.en: It is the story of a military coup which brings a brutal despot to power.
examples.zh: 这就是那次军事政变的来龙去脉，它把一个残暴的专制统治者扶上了台。

senses.def: connected with or typical of a leader with great power, especially one who uses it in a cruel way
senses.zh: 专制统治者；专制君主；暴君

examples.en: despotic power/rule
examples.zh: 专制的权力；专制统治

senses.def: the rule of a despot
sweet food eaten at the end of a meal

examples.en: What's for dessert?
examples.zh: 餐后甜点吃什么？

examples.en: a rich chocolate dessert
examples.zh: 腻人的巧克力甜点

examples.en: the dessert trolley (= a table on wheels from which you choose your dessert in a restaurant)
examples.zh: （餐厅内）送甜点的手推车

senses.def: a sweet wine that is drunk with or after dessert
senses.zh: （用甜点时饮用的）甜点酒，甜食酒

examples.en: The chocolate mousse came with a glass of dessert wine.
examples.zh: 巧克力慕斯配有一杯甜酒。

examples.en: sweet dessert wines such as Sauternes
examples.zh: 甜酒，如苏玳 (Sauternes)

senses.def: a spoon of medium size
the amount a dessertspoon
the act of making a system, country, government, etc. become less well established or successful; the fact of being like this
senses.zh: 使（制度、国家、政府等）动摇；使不安定；使不稳定

examples.en: the economic and political destabilization of the country
examples.zh: 该国的经济和政治不稳定

senses.def: to make a system, country, government, etc. become less well established or successful
senses.zh: 使（制度、国家、政府等）动摇；使不安定；使不稳定

examples.en: Terrorist attacks were threatening to destabilize the government.
examples.zh: 恐怖袭击威胁着政府的稳定。

examples.en: The news had a destabilizing effect on the stock market.
examples.zh: 这消息引起了股市的动荡。

senses.def: a place to which somebody/something is going or being sent

examples.en: popular tourist/holiday destinations like the Bahamas
examples.zh: 像巴哈马那样深受大众喜爱的旅游／度假胜地

examples.en: to arrive at/reach your destination
examples.zh: 到达目的地

examples.en: Our luggage was checked all the way through to our final destination.
examples.zh: 我们的行李一直被托运到最终目的地。

senses.def: a hotel, store, etc. that people will make a special trip to visit
senses.zh: 作为目的地的（旅馆、商店、饭店等）

examples.en: Sun Valley Lodge was the first destination ski resort in the US.
examples.zh: 太阳谷酒店是美国第一个目的地滑雪度假区。

senses.def: a fee added to the price of a new car to cover the cost of transporting the vehicle from the factory where it was made to the place where it is to be sold
senses.zh: 目的地费用（新车价格中附加的从工厂到销售地的运输费用）

examples.en: The price that you pay for a new car in a dealership includes all kind of extra fees such as a destination charge and sales tax.
examples.zh: 你在汽车经销店支付的新车款包含目的地费用、销售税等所有附加费用。

senses.def: a wedding held in an exciting or unusual place in a foreign country where all the people who travel to the wedding can also have a holiday
senses.zh: 度假地婚礼，海外婚礼（在国外度假胜地举行，宾客可兼达旅游的目的）

examples.en: They had a destination wedding on a beach in Brazil.
examples.zh: 他们在巴西沙滩上举办了目的地婚礼。

senses.def: having a future that has been decided or planned at an earlier time, especially by fate
senses.zh: 预定；注定；（尤指）命中注定

examples.en: to be destined for greatness/stardom/success
examples.zh: 注定成为伟大/明星/成功

examples.en: He was destined for a military career, like his father before him.
examples.zh: 他命中注定要步父亲的后尘，过戎马生涯。

examples.en: We seem destined never to meet.
examples.zh: 我们似乎是命中注定无缘相见。

examples.en: She seemed destined to become a very rich woman.
examples.zh: 她似乎注定会成为富婆。

senses.def: on the way to or intended for a place

examples.en: goods destined for Poland
examples.zh: 运往波兰的货物

senses.def: what happens to somebody or what will happen to them in the future, especially things that they cannot change or avoid

examples.en: The destinies of five nations were decided at the peace conference.
examples.zh: 五个国家的命运在和平会议上决定了。

examples.en: He wants to be in control of his own destiny.
examples.zh: 他想要掌握自己的命运。

examples.en: The contemporary hero is one who stands out against the crowd to fulfil a personal destiny.
examples.zh: 当代英雄是在人群中脱颖而出、实现个人命运的人。

senses.def: the power believed to control events
senses.zh: 主宰事物的力量；命运之神

examples.en: I believe there's some force guiding us—call it God, destiny or fate.
examples.zh: 我总认为有某种力量在指引着我们，称之为上帝也罢，天意也罢，还是命运也罢。

examples.en: He was driven on by a strong sense of destiny.
examples.zh: 他被一种强烈的宿命感所驱使。

intro.en: These are all words for things that happen or the force that causes them to happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指机遇、命运、运气。

items.def: the force that causes good or bad things to happen to people:
items.zh: 指机遇、命运、运气

examples.en: This ring has always brought me good luck.
examples.zh: 这戒指总是给我带来好运。

items.def: the way that some things happen without any cause that you can see or understand:
items.zh: 指偶然、碰巧、意外

examples.en: The results could simply be due to chance.
examples.zh: 这结果可能纯属意外。

items.def: the fact of two things happening at the same time by chance, in a surprising way:
items.zh: 指出人意料的巧合、巧事

examples.en: They met through a series of strange coincidences.
examples.zh: 他们因一连串奇妙的巧合而相遇。

items.def: something that happens unexpectedly and is not planned in advance:
items.zh: 指意外、偶然的事

examples.en: Their early arrival was just an accident.
examples.zh: 他们早到仅仅是偶然而已。

items.def: the power that is believed to control everything that happens and that cannot be stopped or changed:
items.zh: 指命运、天数、定数、天意

examples.en: Fate decreed that she would never reach America.
examples.zh: 命中注定她永远到不了美国。

items.def: the power that is believed to control events:
items.zh: 指主宰事物的力量、命运之神

examples.en: I believe there’s some force guiding us—call it God, destiny or fate.
examples.zh: 我总认为有某种力量在指引着我们，称之为上帝也罢，天意也罢，还是命运也罢。

senses.def: without money, food and the other things necessary for life

examples.en: When he died, his family was left completely destitute.
examples.zh: 他死时家里一贫如洗。

examples.en: The war left her completely destitute.
examples.zh: 战争使她一贫如洗。

senses.def: people who are destitute
not having something

examples.en: They seem destitute of ordinary human feelings.
examples.zh: 他们似乎一点人情味都没有。

senses.def: the fact of having no money, food and the other things necessary for life

examples.en: homelessness and destitution
examples.zh: 无家可归且一无所有

senses.def: to reduce the amount of goods in a shop, the amount of materials kept available for making something in a factory, etc.
senses.zh: 减少存货；减少库存；去库存

senses.def: to damage something so badly that it no longer exists, works, etc.

examples.en: The building was completely destroyed by fire.
examples.zh: 这栋建筑物被大火彻底焚毁了。

examples.en: The earthquake damaged or destroyed countless homes.
examples.zh: 地震损坏或摧毁了无数房屋。

examples.en: Some of the habitat has already been totally destroyed.
examples.zh: 一些栖息地已经被完全破坏。

examples.en: They've destroyed all the evidence.
examples.zh: 他们销毁了一切证据。

senses.def: to take all the value and pleasure from somebody's life; to ruin

examples.en: Failure was slowly destroying him.
examples.zh: 失败渐渐地把他毁了。

examples.en: She threatened to destroy my reputation.
examples.zh: 她威胁要毁了我的名声。

examples.en: He wanted revenge on the man who had destroyed his life.
examples.zh: 他想报复那个毁了他一生的人。

examples.en: Their lives have been virtually destroyed by this tragedy.
examples.zh: 他们的生活事实上已被这一悲剧毁掉。

senses.def: to kill an animal deliberately, usually because it is sick or not wanted
senses.zh: （因动物有病或不再需要而）杀死，消灭，人道毁灭

examples.en: The injured horse had to be destroyed.
examples.zh: 这匹马受了伤，只好把它杀了。

senses.def: a small fast ship used in war, for example to protect larger ships
a person or thing that destroys

examples.en: Sugar is the destroyer of healthy teeth.
examples.zh: 糖会危害健康的牙齿。

senses.def: that can be destroyed

examples.en: Destructible environments allow you to exploit structural weaknesses to win fights swiftly.
examples.zh: 可破坏的环境让你能够利用结构性弱点来迅速赢得战斗。

examples.en: The terrain is fully destructible and can be obliterated throughout the course of the match.
examples.zh: 地形是完全可破坏的，并且可以在整个比赛过程中被摧毁。

senses.def: the act of destroying something; the process of being destroyed

examples.en: the destruction of the rainforests
examples.zh: 对热带雨林的破坏

examples.en: a tidal wave bringing death and destruction in its wake
examples.zh: 带来死亡与破坏的海啸

examples.en: The central argument is that capitalism sows the seeds of its own destruction (= creates the forces that destroy it).
examples.zh: 主要论点是资本主义播下了自我毁灭的种子。

senses.def: causing destruction
senses.zh: 引起破坏（或毁灭）的；破坏（或毁灭）性的

examples.en: The war demonstrated the destructive power of modern weapons.
examples.zh: 这次战争显示了现代武器的毁灭性力量。

examples.en: the destructive effects of anxiety
examples.zh: 焦虑的破坏性影响

examples.en: Opencast coal mining is among the most environmentally destructive activities carried out in Wales.
examples.zh: 露天煤矿开采是威尔士对环境最具破坏性的活动之一。

senses.def: negative or not helpful

examples.en: destructive behaviour/impulses/tendencies
examples.zh: 破坏性行为／冲动／倾向

examples.en: People have to learn how to handle destructive emotions like anger.
examples.zh: 人得学会控制愤怒等有害情绪。

examples.en: They don't think about how damaging and destructive their words are.
examples.zh: 他们不会考虑自己的言论有多么的破坏性和破坏性。

senses.def: in a way that causes destruction
senses.zh: 引起破坏（或毁灭）的；破坏（或毁灭）性的

senses.def: the fact of causing destruction
senses.zh: 引起破坏（或毁灭）的；破坏（或毁灭）性的

examples.en: the increasing destructiveness of tropical cyclones
examples.zh: 热带气旋的破坏力日益增强

senses.def: in a way that goes from one thing to another, without a definite plan and without enthusiasm
senses.zh: 漫无目的的；无条理的；随意的

senses.def: going from one thing to another, without a definite plan and without enthusiasm
senses.zh: 漫无目的的；无条理的；随意的

examples.en: I wandered about in a desultory fashion.
examples.zh: 我漫无目的地四处游荡。

examples.en: a desultory conversation
examples.zh: 漫无边际的谈话

senses.def: (in writing) detective

examples.en: Det Insp (= Inspector) Cox
examples.zh: 考克斯探长

senses.def: to remove something from something larger; to become separated from something

examples.en: You can detach the strap and carry the bag by the handle if you prefer.
examples.zh: 如果您愿意，可以拆下肩带并握住手柄拎包。

examples.en: One of the panels had become detached from the main structure.
examples.zh: 一块镶板已从主体结构上脱落。

examples.en: The skis should detach from the boot if you fall.
examples.zh: 要是你跌倒了，滑雪板就会脱离靴子。

senses.def: to leave or separate yourself from somebody/something

examples.en: She detached herself from his embrace.
examples.zh: 她挣脱了他的拥抱。

examples.en: I tried to detach myself from the reality of these terrible events.
examples.zh: 我尽力使自己从这些可怕事件的现实中摆脱出来。

examples.en: A figure in white detached itself from the shadows.
examples.zh: 一个穿白色衣服的人从阴影中走了出来。

senses.def: to send a group of soldiers, etc. away from the main group, especially to do special duties

examples.en: Five destroyers were detached to carry out a bombardment of the port.
examples.zh: 五艘驱逐舰被派出对港口进行轰炸。

senses.def: that can be taken off

examples.en: a coat with a detachable hood
examples.zh: 带有活风帽的外套

examples.en: The handle is detachable from the bag.
examples.zh: 手柄可以从包上取下来。

examples.en: The lid is fully detachable.
examples.zh: 这个盖子可以整个拿下来。

senses.def: the state of not being involved in something in an emotional or personal way

examples.en: He answered with an air of detachment.
examples.zh: 他回答时带着冷漠的神态。

examples.en: She felt a sense of detachment from what was going on.
examples.zh: 她对眼前发生的事感到很超然。

senses.def: the state of not being influenced by other people or by your own feelings

examples.en: In judging these issues a degree of critical detachment is required.
examples.zh: 在裁决这些争议时须要有一定程度的公正判断力。

examples.en: The judges show impartiality and detachment.
examples.zh: 这些法官表现得不偏不倚，冷静客观。

senses.def: a group of soldiers, ships, etc. sent away from a larger group, especially to do special duties
senses.zh: 分遣队；支队；特遣小分队

examples.en: a detachment of artillery
examples.zh: 炮兵支队

senses.def: the act of detaching

examples.en: to suffer detachment of the retina
examples.zh: 出现视网膜脱落

senses.def: a small individual fact or item; a less important fact or item

examples.en: an expedition planned down to the last detail
examples.zh: 计划详尽的探险

examples.en: The Ministry refused to reveal any more details of the attack.
examples.zh: 该部拒绝透露更多的袭击细节。

examples.en: Tell me the main points now; leave the details till later.
examples.zh: 现在把要点告诉我，细节留到以后再说。

examples.en: The finer details of the plan have still to be worked out.
examples.zh: 这个方案更详尽的细节还有待制订。

examples.en: These are all relatively minor details.
examples.zh: 这些都是相对较小的细节。

examples.en: ‘We had a terrible time—’ ‘Oh, spare me the details (= don't tell me any more).’
examples.zh: “我们倒霉透了 － ”“唉呀，别给我细说了。”

senses.def: the small facts or features of something, when you consider them all together

examples.en: The report was criticized for its lack of detail.
examples.zh: 这份报告因缺少细节而受到批评。

examples.en: Ensure that your diagrams contain the appropriate level of detail.
examples.zh: 要确保你的图表足够详细。

examples.en: This issue will be discussed in more detail in the next chapter.
examples.zh: 这个问题将在下一章详细论述。

examples.en: The making of the movie is explored in minute detail.
examples.zh: 对电影的制作进行了细致的探讨。

examples.en: The research has been carried out with scrupulous attention to detail.
examples.zh: 研究工作一丝不苟地完成了。

examples.en: He had an eye for detail (= noticed and remembered small details).
examples.zh: 他很善于发现并记住细节。

senses.def: information about something
senses.zh: 具体情况；（关于某事物的）资料，消息

examples.en: Please provide the following details: name, age and sex.
examples.zh: 请提供以下详情：姓名、年龄和性别。

examples.en: Can you send me your contact details?
examples.zh: 你能把联系方式发给我吗？

examples.en: For further details visit our website.
examples.zh: 请访问我们的网站了解详情。

examples.en: They didn't give any details about the game.
examples.zh: 他们没有提供这场比赛的具体情况。

senses.def: a small part of a picture or painting; the smaller or less important parts of a picture, pattern, etc. when you consider them all together
senses.zh: （照片、绘画等的）细部，局部，次要部分

examples.en: This is a detail from the 1844 Turner painting.
examples.zh: 这是透纳 1844 年画作的局部。

examples.en: a huge picture with a lot of fine detail in it
examples.zh: 一幅细致入微的巨型画作

senses.def: a group of soldiers given special duties
to explain something fully

examples.en: I can't go into details now; it would take too long.
examples.zh: 我现在不能细说，太费工夫。

senses.def: to give a list of facts or all the available information about something
senses.zh: 详细列举；详细说明；详述

examples.en: The brochure details all the hotels in the area and their facilities.
examples.zh: 这本小册子详细介绍了当地所有旅馆及其设施。

examples.en: In this lecture, I will detail the history of television from the beginning.
examples.zh: 在本次讲座中，我将从头开始详细介绍电视的历史。

examples.en: to detail your experiences/plans/activities
examples.zh: 详细描述您的经历/计划/活动

examples.en: Of the factors detailed above, supply and demand are the primary forces behind interest rate levels.
examples.zh: 在上述因素中，供给和需求是利率水平背后的主要力量。

senses.def: to give an official order to somebody, especially a soldier, to do a particular task

examples.en: Several of the men were detailed to form a search party.
examples.zh: 几个人被派组成一个搜索队。

senses.def: to clean a car carefully and completely

examples.en: He got work for a while detailing cars.
examples.zh: 他干了一段时间的清洗汽车的工作。

senses.def: to explain something fully

examples.en: I can't go into details now; it would take too long.
examples.zh: 我现在不能细说，太费工夫。

senses.def: to keep somebody in an official place, such as a police station, a prison or a hospital, and prevent them from leaving

examples.en: One man has been detained for questioning.
examples.zh: 一个男人被拘留审问。

senses.def: to delay somebody or prevent them from going somewhere

examples.en: I'm sorry—he'll be late; he's been detained at a meeting.
examples.zh: 对不起，他要晚点儿到，他因会议耽搁了。

examples.en: The minister was unavoidably detained in Lisbon on affairs of state.
examples.zh: 部长因国家事务不可避免地被拘留在里斯本。

senses.def: a person who is kept in prison, usually because of his or her political opinions
senses.zh: （通常因政治主张）被拘留者，被扣押者

examples.en: The detainee can make a formal complaint after release.
examples.zh: 被拘押者得到释放后可以提出正式控告。

senses.def: to discover or notice something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.

examples.en: The tests are designed to detect the disease early.
examples.zh: 这些检查旨在早期查出疾病。

examples.en: Only 8 per cent of regular cola consumers detected a difference.
examples.zh: 只有 8% 的普通可乐消费者发现了差异。

examples.en: The sensor detects changes in light level and temperature.
examples.zh: 传感器检测光照水平和温度的变化。

examples.en: a test that can detect the presence of calcium in the arteries
examples.zh: 可以检测动脉中是否存在钙的测试

examples.en: This is an instrument that can detect very small amounts of radiation.
examples.zh: 这是一种能检测到微量辐射的仪器。

examples.en: Do I detect a note of criticism?
examples.zh: 这好像带有批评的意味吧？

intro.en: These words all mean to see something, especially when you pay careful attention to it.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含看到、注意到之义。

items.def: to see, hear or become aware of somebody/​something; to pay attention to somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指看（或听）到、注意到、意识到、注意、留意

examples.en: The first thing I noticed about the room was the smell.
examples.zh: 我首先注意到的是屋子里的气味。

items.def: (rather formal) to notice or pay careful attention to something:
items.zh: 指注意、留意

examples.en: Please note (that) the office will be closed on Monday.
examples.zh: 请注意办事处星期一将关闭。

items.def: to discover or notice something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc:
items.zh: 指发现、查明、侦察出

examples.en: The tests are designed to detect the disease early.
examples.zh: 这些检查旨在早期查出疾病。

items.def: (formal) to see or notice somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指看到、注意到、观察到

examples.en: Have you observed any changes lately?
examples.zh: 最近你注意到什么变化没有？

items.def: (rather formal) to see something happen:
items.zh: 指当场看到、目击

examples.en: Police have appealed for anyone who witnessed the incident to contact them.
examples.zh: 警方呼吁目击这一事件的人与他们联系。

senses.def: that can be discovered or noticed

examples.en: The noise is barely detectable by the human ear.
examples.zh: 这声音人耳几乎觉察不到。

senses.def: the process of discovering or noticing something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.; the fact of being discovered or noticed

examples.en: crime prevention and detection
examples.zh: 犯罪的预防和侦查

examples.en: Last year the detection rate for car theft was just 13 per cent.
examples.zh: 去年汽车盗窃案的侦破率仅为 13%。

examples.en: Many problems, however, escape detection.
examples.zh: 然而许多问题却未被察觉。

examples.en: Early detection of cancers is vitally important.
examples.zh: 癌症的早期查出是极为重要的。

senses.def: a person, especially a police officer, whose job is to investigate crimes and catch criminals

examples.en: a police/homicide/undercover detective
examples.zh: 警方／凶杀案／卧底侦探

examples.en: Several objects were taken away by detectives from the anti-terrorist squad.
examples.zh: 反恐小组的侦探拿走了一些物品。

examples.en: Detective Inspector (Roger) Brown
examples.zh: （罗杰·）布朗探长

examples.en: a detective constable/sergeant/superintendent
examples.zh: 侦探警员/中士/警长

senses.def: a person employed by somebody to find out information about somebody/something
a story in which there is a murder or other crime and a detective who tries to solve it. The best-known British writers of detective stories include Arthur Conan Doyle
the activity of trying to discover more information about something

examples.en: He did some detective work and figured out what had happened to his bike.
examples.zh: 经过调查，他弄清楚了他的自行车出了什么问题。

senses.def: a piece of equipment for discovering the presence of something, such as metal, smoke, explosives

examples.en: a smoke detector
examples.zh: 烟雾检测器

senses.def: an improvement in the relationship between two or more countries which have been unfriendly towards each other in the past

examples.en: a new international climate of détente
examples.zh: 国际缓和新气氛

senses.def: the state of being kept in a place, especially a prison, and prevented from leaving

examples.en: They were sentenced to 12 months' detention in a young offender institution.
examples.zh: 他们被判留在少管所12 个月。

examples.en: police powers of arrest and detention
examples.zh: 警方的逮捕和拘留权

examples.en: allegations of torture and detention without trial
examples.zh: 拷打和未经审判便进行关押的指控

examples.en: Prisoners have the right to challenge their detentions.
examples.zh: 在押人员有权对拘留提出异议。

examples.en: a detention camp
examples.zh: 拘留营

senses.def: the punishment of being kept at school for a time after other students have gone home
senses.zh: 放学后留校，留堂（处罚学生）

examples.en: They can’t give me (a) detention for this.
examples.zh: 他们不能因为这事罚我课后留下来。

senses.def: a place where people who have entered a country without the necessary documents can be kept in detention
senses.zh: （尤指非法入境者的）收容所，拘留营

examples.en: They are confined in a detention centre for asylum seekers, and forced to prove their refugee status.
examples.zh: 他们被关押在寻求庇护者拘留中心，并被迫证明自己的难民身份。

senses.def: a prison for people who have been accused of a crime and are waiting for their trial or (in the UK in the past) for young people who have been found guilty of a crime
senses.zh: 拘留所；（英国旧时的）少年管教所

senses.def: a person who is held in prison, especially while waiting for trial
to make somebody decide not to do something or continue doing something, especially by making them understand the difficulties and unpleasant results of their actions

examples.en: I told him I wasn't interested, but he wasn't deterred.
examples.zh: 我已告诉他我不感兴趣，可他却不罢休。

examples.en: The high price of the service could deter people from seeking advice.
examples.zh: 这么高的服务费可能使咨询者望而却步。

senses.def: a liquid or powder that helps remove dirt, for example from clothes or dishes
to become worse

examples.en: Her health deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly afterwards.
examples.zh: 她的健康状况急剧恶化，不久便去世了。

examples.en: They had to cope with deteriorating weather conditions.
examples.zh: 他们必须应对日益恶化的天气条件。

examples.en: The discussion quickly deteriorated into an angry argument.
examples.zh: 这场讨论迅速演变成愤怒的争吵。

senses.def: the fact or process of becoming worse

examples.en: a serious deterioration in relations between the two countries
examples.zh: 两国关系的严重恶化

examples.en: her deterioration into severe depression
examples.zh: 她恶化为严重抑郁症

senses.def: that can be found out or calculated
senses.zh: 可确定的；可查明的；可计算出的

examples.en: During the third month of pregnancy the sex of the child becomes determinable.
examples.zh: 孩子的性别在妊娠期第三个月便可查明。

senses.def: a factor that decides whether or how something happens

examples.en: Interest rates are a major determinant of currency trends.
examples.zh: 利率是货币趋势的主要决定因素。

senses.def: fixed and definite

examples.en: a sentence with a determinate meaning
examples.zh: 具有确定意义的句子

senses.def: the quality that makes you continue trying to do something even when this is difficult

examples.en: fierce/grim/dogged determination
examples.zh: 坚强的／不屈不挠的／顽强的决心

examples.en: He fought the illness with courage and determination.
examples.zh: 他勇敢顽强地与疾病作斗争。

examples.en: They had survived by sheer determination.
examples.zh: 他们全凭坚强的决心幸存下来。

examples.en: I admire her determination to get it right.
examples.zh: 我赞赏她非把事情办好的决心。

senses.def: the process of deciding something officially

examples.en: factors influencing the determination of future policy
examples.zh: 影响未来决策的各种因素

senses.def: the act of finding out or calculating something

examples.en: Both methods rely on the accurate determination of the pressure of the gas.
examples.zh: 两种方法都依赖于对气体压力的准确测定。

senses.def: to discover the facts about something; to calculate something exactly

examples.en: An inquiry was set up to determine the cause of the accident.
examples.zh: 已展开调查以确定事故原因。

examples.en: Try to determine the extent of the problem.
examples.zh: 尝试确定问题的严重程度。

examples.en: We set out to determine exactly what happened that night.
examples.zh: 我们着手查明那天晚上发生的事情。

examples.en: It is difficult to determine when drama first appeared in India.
examples.zh: 很难确定戏剧何时首次出现在印度。

examples.en: It was determined that she had died of natural causes.
examples.zh: 已确认她是自然死亡。

senses.def: to make something happen in a particular way or be of a particular type

examples.en: Rural voters in key states will determine the outcome of the election.
examples.zh: 关键州的农村选民将决定选举结果。

examples.en: Upbringing plays an important part in determining a person's character.
examples.zh: 后天培养对于一个人性格的形成起着重要作用。

examples.en: Age and experience will be determining factors in our choice of candidate.
examples.zh: 年龄和经验是我们选择候选人的决定因素。

examples.en: The physical capabilities of a plant determine where it can and cannot live.
examples.zh: 植物的自身能力决定了它在某地能不能生存。

senses.def: to officially decide and/or arrange something

examples.en: A date for the meeting has yet to be determined.
examples.zh: 会议日期尚待确定。

examples.en: The court determined (that) the defendant should pay the legal costs.
examples.zh: 法庭裁决由被告支付诉讼费用。

senses.def: to decide definitely to do something

examples.en: They determined to start early.
examples.zh: 他们决定早点儿出发。

examples.en: The government determined on a change of policy.
examples.zh: 政府决定改变政策。

examples.en: From that moment, I determined that it should not happen again.
examples.zh: 从那一刻起，我就下定决心，不再让这样的事情发生。

senses.def: in a determined way

examples.en: a determinedly independent character
examples.zh: 坚决独立的性格

examples.en: determinedly resisting overwhelming force
examples.zh: 坚决抵抗压倒性的力量

senses.def: a word such as the
senses.zh: 限定词（置于名词前起限定作用，如 the、some、my 等）

senses.def: the belief that people are not free to choose what they are like or how they behave, because these things are decided by their environment and other things over which they have no control
senses.zh: 决定论（排除自由意志，认为个性或行为均由环境和自己不能控制的因素所决定）

senses.def: connected with the belief that people are not free to choose what they are like or how they behave, because these things are decided by their environment and other things over which they have no control
senses.zh: 决定论（排除自由意志，认为个性或行为均由环境和自己不能控制的因素所决定）

senses.def: the fact of making somebody less likely to do something

examples.en: His view is that prison sentences must be long enough to satisfy the requirements both of retribution and deterrence.
examples.zh: 他的观点是，监禁刑期必须足够长，才能满足报应和威慑的要求。

senses.def: something that makes somebody less likely to do something (= that deters

examples.en: Hopefully his punishment will act as a deterrent to others.
examples.zh: 对他的惩罚但愿能起到杀一儆百的作用。

examples.en: a deterrent against cheating
examples.zh: 防止作弊的威慑措施

senses.def: making somebody less likely to do something

examples.en: They were arguing about the deterrent effect of nuclear weapons.
examples.zh: 他们在争论核武器的威慑效果。

senses.def: to hate somebody/something very much

examples.en: They detested each other on sight.
examples.zh: 他们互相看着就不顺眼。

examples.en: They absolutely detest each other.
examples.zh: 他们完全是相互憎恨。

examples.en: I loathe and detest racism in any form.
examples.zh: 我厌恶并厌恶任何形式的种族主义。

examples.en: He detests having his photograph taken.
examples.zh: 他讨厌别人给他拍照。

synonyms.words: dislike ▪ can’t stand ▪ despise ▪ can’t bear ▪ loathe ▪ detest

intro.en: These words all mean to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含厌恶、讨厌、憎恶之义。

items.def: to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something. Although hate is generally a very strong verb, it is also commonly used in spoken or informal English to talk about people or things that you dislike in a less important way, for example a particular type of food:
items.zh: 尽管 hate 通常为语气很强的动词，但亦常用于口语或非正式英语中，谈论不太喜欢的人或物，如某种食物等

items.def: (rather formal) to not like somebody/​something. Dislike is a rather formal word; it is less formal, and more usual, to say that you don't like somebody/​something, especially in spoken English:
items.zh: dislike 为相当正式的用语，don’t like 则较非正式，而且较常用，尤其在英语口语中

items.def: (rather informal) used to emphasize that you really do not like somebody/​something:
items.zh: 强调不喜欢、受不了、不能容忍

examples.en: I can’t stand his brother.
examples.zh: 他弟弟让我受不了。

items.def: to dislike and have no respect for somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指鄙视、蔑视、看不起

examples.en: He despised himself for being so cowardly.
examples.zh: 他为自己如此怯懦而看不起自己。

items.def: used to say that you dislike something so much that you cannot accept or deal with it:
items.zh: 指无法承受、应付不了

examples.en: I can’t bear having cats in the house.
examples.zh: 家里有猫我可受不了。

items.def: to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They loathe each other.
examples.zh: 他们相互讨厌。

items.def: (rather formal) to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They absolutely detest each other.
examples.zh: 他们完全是相互憎恨。

senses.def: that deserves to be hated
senses.zh: 可憎的；可恨的；令人讨厌的

examples.en: All terrorist crime is detestable, whoever the victims.
examples.zh: 无论受害者是谁，一切恐怖主义罪行都是可憎的。

examples.en: ‘You’re detestable!’ she said, shaking.
examples.zh: “你真可恶！”她颤抖着说道。

senses.def: the feeling of hating somebody/something
to remove a king or queen from power; to remove somebody from a position of authority or power
senses.zh: 废黜（国王或女王）；撵下台；免（某人）的职；罢（某人）的官

senses.def: to explode, or to make a bomb or other device explode

examples.en: Two other bombs failed to detonate.
examples.zh: 另外两枚炸弹未引爆。

examples.en: The terrorists planned to detonate the device when the shop was empty.
examples.zh: 恐怖分子计划在商店空无一人时引爆装置。

examples.en: The bomb was detonated by remote control.
examples.zh: 那枚炸弹是遥控引爆的。

synonyms.words: blow up ▪ go off ▪ burst ▪ erupt ▪ detonate

intro.en: These are all words that can be used when something breaks apart violently, causing damage or injury.
intro.zh: 以上各词均可表示爆炸、爆破、爆裂。

items.def: to burst (= to break open or apart) loudly and violently, causing damage; to make something burst in this way:
items.zh: 指爆炸、爆破、爆裂、引爆

examples.en: The jet smashed into a hillside and exploded.
examples.zh: 喷气式飞机撞上山坡爆炸了。

items.def: to be destroyed by an explosion; to destroy something by an explosion:
items.zh: 指爆炸、（被）炸毁

examples.en: A police officer was killed when his car blew up.
examples.zh: 一名警员在其汽车爆炸时遇难。

items.def: (of a bomb) to explode; (of a gun) to be fired:
items.zh: 指（炸弹）爆炸、（枪）开火

examples.en: The bomb went off in a crowded street.
examples.zh: 炸弹在挤满人的大街上爆炸了。

items.def: to break open or apart, especially because of pressure from inside; to make something break in this way:
items.zh: 指（使）爆裂、胀开

examples.en: That balloon’s going to burst.
examples.zh: 那气球马上要爆了。

items.def: (of a volcano) to throw out burning rocks and smoke; (of burning rocks and smoke) to be thrown out of a volcano.
items.zh: 指（火山）爆发、（岩浆、烟）喷出

items.def: (rather formal) (of a bomb) to explode; to make a bomb explode:
items.zh: 指（炸弹）爆炸、使（炸弹）爆炸、引爆、起爆

examples.en: Two other bombs failed to detonate.
examples.zh: 另外两枚炸弹未引爆。

senses.def: an explosion; the action of making something explode
a device for making something, especially a bomb, explode
a longer route that you take in order to avoid a problem or to visit a place
senses.zh: 绕行的路；迂回路；兜圈子

examples.en: We had to make a detour around the flooded fields.
examples.zh: 我们只得绕道避开被洪水淹没的田野。

examples.en: It's well worth making a detour to see the village.
examples.zh: 绕道去参观一下这村子很是值得。

senses.def: a road or route that is used when the usual one is closed
to take a longer route in order to avoid a problem or to visit a place; to make somebody/something take a longer route

examples.en: The President detoured to Chicago for a special meeting.
examples.zh: 总统绕道到芝加哥参加一个特别会议。

examples.en: I would detour the endless stream of motor homes.
examples.zh: 我要绕过川流不息的度假房车。

examples.en: State troopers were detouring southbound trucks off Route 1 onto Route 16.
examples.zh: 州警正在将南行卡车从 1 号公路绕道至 16 号公路。

senses.def: the process of removing harmful substances from your body by only eating and drinking particular things
senses.zh: 排毒（通过控制饮食种类将有害物质排出体外）

examples.en: a 28-day detox plan
examples.zh: 28 天排毒计划

examples.en: I've tried numerous home detoxes.
examples.zh: 我尝试过多种家庭排毒方法。

senses.def: detoxification

examples.en: a detox clinic
examples.zh: 戒瘾（诊）所

examples.en: He's gone into detox.
examples.zh: 他进了戒毒所。

examples.en: I'd been waiting to get into the clinic for a detox.
examples.zh: 我一直在等待去诊所戒毒。

senses.def: to stop drinking alcohol or taking drugs; to make somebody do this

examples.en: He has checked into a hospital to detox, according to reports yesterday.
examples.zh: 据昨天报道，他已入院戒毒。

examples.en: The medication has a remarkable success rate in detoxing heroin addicts.
examples.zh: 该药物对海洛因成瘾者的戒毒具有显着的成功率。

senses.def: to attempt to remove harmful substances from your body by only eating and drinking certain things
senses.zh: 排毒（试图通过控制饮食种类将有害物质排出体外）

examples.en: This is where wealthy industrialists and film stars come to de-stress and detox.
examples.zh: 这是富有的实业家和电影明星减压和排毒的地方。

examples.en: Fasting is a great way to detox your body.
examples.zh: 禁食是给身体排毒的好方法。

senses.def: treatment given to people to help them stop drinking alcohol or taking drugs

examples.en: a detoxification unit
examples.zh: 戒毒所

senses.def: the process of improving the reputation of somebody/something that has been seen as morally bad

examples.en: The policy has been key to the successful detoxification of the party's brand.
examples.zh: 这项政策是党的品牌成功解毒的关键。

senses.def: the process of removing harmful substances or poisons from something

examples.en: the detoxification of formaldehyde
examples.zh: 去除甲醛毒害

senses.def: to remove harmful substances or poisons from something; to become free from harmful substances
senses.zh: 排毒；解毒；去毒；除去…的毒素

examples.en: She recommends bitter greens to cleanse and detoxify the body.
examples.zh: 她推荐苦菜来净化身体和排毒。

examples.en: You can help your body detoxify by cutting down on coffee.
examples.zh: 少喝咖啡有助于体内排毒。

senses.def: to stop drinking too much alcohol or taking drugs; to treat somebody in order to help them do this

examples.en: to detoxify from heroin addiction
examples.zh: 戒除海洛因成瘾

examples.en: He was twice detoxified from heroin.
examples.zh: 他受过两次戒除海洛因的治疗。

senses.def: to make something seem less good or fun

examples.en: He was determined not to let anything detract from his enjoyment of the trip.
examples.zh: 他下决心这次旅行不让任何事情影响他的兴致。

senses.def: a person who tries to make somebody/something seem less good or valuable by criticizing them/it
senses.zh: 诋毁者；贬低者；恶意批评者

examples.en: Detractors claim the building will be ugly and impractical.
examples.zh: 批评者声称这座建筑将丑陋且不切实际。

senses.def: to leave a train or make somebody leave a train
the act of causing harm or damage; something that causes harm or damage
senses.zh: 伤害；损害；造成伤害（或损害）的事物

examples.en: Wood accounts for 90% of energy production in some countries, with consequent environmental detriment.
examples.zh: 有些国家90%的能源产自木材，因而给环境造成了破坏。

examples.en: Too many tests are a detriment to good education.
examples.zh: 太多的考试不利于良好的教育。

senses.def: resulting in harm or damage to somebody/something

examples.en: He was engrossed in his job to the detriment of his health.
examples.zh: 他全身心地投入工作，结果损害了他的健康。

senses.def: not resulting in harm or damage to somebody/something

examples.en: This tax cannot be introduced without detriment to people’s living standards.
examples.zh: 这项税收政策一旦实施，将对人们的生活水平造成不利影响。

items.idm: to the detriment of somebody/something | to somebody's/something’s detriment

senses.def: resulting in harm or damage to somebody/something

examples.en: He was engrossed in his job to the detriment of his health.
examples.zh: 他全身心地投入工作，结果损害了他的健康。

senses.def: not resulting in harm or damage to somebody/something

examples.en: This tax cannot be introduced without detriment to people’s living standards.
examples.zh: 这项税收政策一旦实施，将对人们的生活水平造成不利影响。

senses.def: harmful

examples.en: the sun’s detrimental effect on skin
examples.zh: 日光对皮肤的伤害

examples.en: The policy will be detrimental to the peace process.
examples.zh: 这项政策将不利于和平进程。

examples.en: This move could be seriously detrimental to the economy.
examples.zh: 这个举措可能严重损害经济。

examples.en: Emissions from the factory are widely suspected of having a detrimental effect on health.
examples.zh: 人们普遍怀疑工厂的排放物对健康不利。

senses.def: in a way that is harmful
natural waste material that is left after something has been used or broken up
senses.zh: 碎屑；风化物；残渣；腐殖质

examples.en: organic detritus from fish and plants
examples.zh: 鱼和植物的有机碎屑

senses.def: any kind of rubbish that is left after an event or when something has been used

examples.en: the detritus of everyday life
examples.zh: 日常生活垃圾

examples.en: The kitchen table was still stacked with the detritus of the previous night.
examples.zh: 厨房的桌子上还堆满了前一天晚上的碎屑。

senses.def: the largest city in the US state of Michigan
senses.zh: 底特律（美国密歇根州最大城市）

senses.zh: 底特律（美国密歇根州最大城市）

examples.en: Detroit's fight against foreign brands
examples.zh: 底特律与外国品牌的斗争

senses.def: a strong liquid for killing bacteria, used for cleaning surfaces and for treating skin problems such as cuts, stings
senses.zh: 滴露（强效除菌液，用于清洁和消毒）

senses.def: a slow reduction in swelling
senses.zh: 消肿；退肿；（尤指）阴茎勃起消退

a playing card

senses.def: used in questions to show that you are annoyed
senses.zh: （用于问句中表示烦恼、厌恶）到底，究竟

examples.en: What the deuce is he doing?
examples.zh: 他到底在干什么？

senses.def: used for emphasis, especially when feeling angry, disappointed or surprised
senses.zh: （强调生气、失望、惊讶等感情）非常的，极其的

examples.en: The man's a deuced fool!
examples.zh: 那个男人真是个傻瓜！

senses.def: used to mean ‘very’, especially by somebody who is feeling angry, disappointed or surprised
senses.zh: （强调生气、失望、惊讶等感情）非常的，极其的

examples.en: It's deuced awkward.
examples.zh: 那事真令人难堪。

senses.def: in a confused state
an unexpected power or event that saves a situation that seems without hope, especially in a play or novel
senses.zh: （尤指剧本或小说中）机械降神，扭转乾坤的力量

senses.zh: 德国马克（德国货币单位，于 2002 年为欧元所取代）

senses.def: a male god
a god
a reduction in the value of the money of one country when it is exchanged for the money of another country
senses.zh: 将一个国家的货币换成另一个国家的货币时，货币贬值

examples.en: There has been a further small devaluation against the dollar.
examples.zh: 兑美元的比值继续小幅下跌。

senses.def: the act of giving a lower value to something or making it seem less important than it really is
senses.zh: 为某物赋予较低价值或使其显得不那么重要的行为

examples.en: the general devaluation of expertise in our culture
examples.zh: 我们的文化中专业知识普遍贬值

senses.def: to reduce in value when it is exchanged for the money of another country; to reduce the value of money in this way

examples.en: The local currency was rapidly devaluing.
examples.zh: 当地货币迅速贬值。

examples.en: The pound was devalued against the US dollar.
examples.zh: 英镑对美元贬值了。

senses.def: to give a lower value to something, making it seem less important than it really is

examples.en: Work in the home is often ignored and devalued.
examples.zh: 家务劳动常常被忽视和贬低。

senses.def: the alphabet used to write Sanskrit, Hindi and some other Indian languages
senses.zh: 天城体文字，伽里字母（用于梵语、印地语及其他印度语言）

senses.def: to completely destroy a place or an area

examples.en: The bomb devastated much of the old part of the city.
examples.zh: 这颗炸弹炸毁了旧城的一大片地方。

senses.def: to make somebody feel very shocked and sad
senses.zh: 使震惊；使极为忧伤；使极为悲痛

senses.def: in a way that causes a lot of damage and destruction
senses.zh: 破坏性极大的；毁灭性的

examples.en: America has become very good at fighting wars efficiently and devastatingly.
examples.zh: 美国已经变得非常擅长高效且具有毁灭性地进行战争。

senses.def: in a very impressive and powerful way
senses.zh: 给人印象深刻的；令人钦佩的；强有力的

examples.en: a devastatingly handsome man
examples.zh: 帅得迷死人的男子

examples.en: The play was devastatingly funny.
examples.zh: 这出戏非常有趣。

senses.def: used to say that a situation or fact makes you shocked and very sad

examples.en: Devastatingly, my mother died from cancer.
examples.zh: 不幸的是，我的母亲死于癌症。

senses.def: great destruction
senses.zh: （尤指大面积的）毁灭，破坏，蹂躏

examples.en: The bomb caused widespread devastation.
examples.zh: 炸弹造成大面积破坏。

examples.en: The cost of the devastation could run to £6 million.
examples.zh: 此次破坏造成的损失可能高达 600 万英镑。

senses.def: to gradually grow or become bigger, more advanced, stronger, etc.; to make something do this

examples.en: From birth to age 5, a child's brain develops rapidly.
examples.zh: 从出生到5岁，孩子的大脑发育迅速。

examples.en: Some children develop more slowly than others.
examples.zh: 有的儿童比其他儿童发育得慢。

examples.en: Gradually these settlements developed into cities.
examples.zh: 这些定居点逐渐发展成为城市。

examples.en: Human beings developed from earlier species of animals.
examples.zh: 人类是从早期的动物物种发展而来的。

examples.en: The place has rapidly developed from a small fishing community into a thriving tourist resort.
examples.zh: 这地方由原来的小渔村迅速发展成一个繁荣的旅游胜地。

examples.en: The aim is to develop your personal skills.
examples.zh: 目的是提升你的个人技能。

examples.en: She developed the company from nothing.
examples.zh: 她白手起家创办了这家公司。

examples.en: The competition helps entrants develop ideas into business concepts.
examples.zh: 竞赛帮助参赛者将想法转化为商业概念。

senses.def: to start to have a skill, ability, quality, etc. that becomes better and stronger; to become better and stronger

examples.en: He's developed a real flair for management.
examples.zh: 他在管理方面已经变得很有一套。

examples.en: Their relationship has developed over a number of years.
examples.zh: 多年来他们的情谊日益深厚。

senses.def: to think of or produce a new idea, product, etc. and make it successful

examples.en: The company develops and markets new software.
examples.zh: 这家公司开发并销售新软件。

examples.en: It takes time to develop new technology.
examples.zh: 开发新技术需要时间。

examples.en: We are developing products for different parts of the industry.
examples.zh: 我们正在为行业的不同部分开发产品。

examples.en: to develop a strategy/system/programme
examples.zh: 制定战略/系统/计划

examples.en: to develop a method/model/technique
examples.zh: 开发方法/模型/技术

examples.en: A new type of painkilling drug has recently been developed.
examples.zh: 最近刚研制出一种新的止痛药。

senses.group: new idea/product 新思想；新产品

senses.def: to begin to have something such as a disease or a problem; to start to affect somebody/something
senses.zh: 患（病）；出现（问题）；（疾病）开始侵袭；（问题）开始影响

examples.en: She developed lung cancer at the age of sixty.
examples.zh: 她六十岁时患上肺癌。

examples.en: Her son developed asthma when he was two.
examples.zh: 她的儿子两岁时患了哮喘。

examples.en: The car developed engine trouble and we had to stop.
examples.zh: 汽车发动机出了故障，我们只好停下来。

examples.en: If symptoms develop, seek help quickly.
examples.zh: 如果出现症状，请迅速寻求帮助。

examples.en: Problems can develop unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 问题可能会出乎意料地发展。

senses.def: to start to happen or change, especially in a bad way
senses.zh: （尤指开始向坏的方面）发展，变化

examples.en: A crisis was rapidly developing in the Gulf.
examples.zh: 海湾危机迅速加剧。

examples.en: We need more time to see how things develop before we take action.
examples.zh: 我们采取行动之前需要有更多时间观察情况的发展。

examples.en: The conflict quickly developed into full-scale war.
examples.zh: 冲突很快发展成全面战争。

examples.en: The situation is developing into a crisis.
examples.zh: 局势正在发展成为危机。

senses.def: to build new houses, factories, etc. on an area of land, especially land that was not being used effectively before

examples.en: The site is being developed by a French company.
examples.zh: 这块地正由一家法国公司开发利用。

senses.def: to build or improve a building or other facilities

examples.en: The company is developing a chain of hotels.
examples.zh: 公司正在创建连锁酒店。

examples.en: He is enthusiastic about plans to develop the leisure facilities at the site.
examples.zh: 他对在该地点开发休闲设施的计划充满热情。

senses.group: create/improve facilities 建造／改善设施

senses.def: to become economically and socially more advanced

examples.en: For a country to develop, a good road network is essential.
examples.zh: 一个国家要发展，良好的道路网络必不可少。

examples.en: Their economy was developing at an incredible pace.
examples.zh: 他们的经济正在以令人难以置信的速度发展。

senses.group: become economically advanced 发展经济

senses.def: to add further explanation or details to an idea, story or musical theme
senses.zh: 阐明（思想）；展开（故事或音乐主题）

examples.en: She develops the theme more fully in her later books.
examples.zh: 她在后来写的书中更详尽地阐明了这个主题。

examples.en: The piano then takes up the melody and develops it.
examples.zh: 然后钢琴会吸收旋律并发展它。

examples.en: He began to develop these ideas in a series of paintings.
examples.zh: 他开始在一系列绘画作品中展现这些思想。

senses.group: idea/story/musical theme 想法；叙述；音乐主题

senses.def: to treat film that has been used to take photographs with chemicals so that the pictures can be seen
senses.zh: 使（胶卷）显影；显像；冲洗（胶片）

examples.en: When Lewis developed the film, he was astonished by what he saw.
examples.zh: 当刘易斯冲洗胶片时，他对所看到的感到惊讶。

synonyms.words: do ▪ create ▪ develop ▪ produce ▪ generate ▪ form

intro.en: These words all mean to make something from parts or materials, or to cause something to exist or happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含制造、使产生之义。

items.def: to create or prepare something by combining materials or putting parts together; to cause something to exist or happen:
items.zh: 指制造、做、组装、使产生

examples.en: She makes her own clothes.
examples.zh: 她自己做衣服。

items.def: (rather informal) to make or prepare something, especially something artistic or something to eat:
items.zh: 指制作、准备（尤指艺术品或食品）

examples.en: He did a beautiful drawing of a house.
examples.zh: 他画了一栋漂亮的房子。

items.def: to make something exist or happen, especially something new that did not exist before:
items.zh: 指创造、创作、创建

examples.en: Scientists disagree about how the universe was created.
examples.zh: 科学家对宇宙是怎样形成的有分歧。

items.def: (used especially in business contexts) to think of and produce a new product:
items.zh: （尤用于商务语境）指开发、研制（产品）

examples.en: to develop new software
examples.zh: 开发新软件

items.def: to make things to be sold; to create something using skill:
items.zh: 指生产、制造（商品），（运用技巧）制作、造出

examples.en: a factory that produces microchips
examples.zh: 微芯片制造厂

items.def: to produce or create something, especially power, money or ideas:
items.zh: 指创造、产生（电、财富或主意）

examples.en: to generate electricity
examples.zh: 发电

items.def: [often passive] to make something from something else; to make something into something else:
items.zh: 指制作、组成、制成

examples.en: Rearrange the letters to form a new word.
examples.zh: 重新排列字母，组成另一单词。

senses.def: a person or company that buys land or buildings in order to build new houses, shops, etc., or to improve the old ones, and makes a profit from doing this

examples.en: property developers
examples.zh: 房地产开发商

senses.def: a person or a company that designs and creates new products

examples.en: a software developer
examples.zh: 软件开发人员

examples.en: Canada has emerged as the world's leading developer of hit board games.
examples.zh: 加拿大已初露头角，成为世界上热门棋类游戏的主要研发国。

senses.def: a chemical substance that is used for developing photographs from a film
the steady growth of something so that it becomes more advanced, stronger, etc.

examples.en: a baby’s development in the womb
examples.zh: 胎儿在子宫内的发育

examples.en: This is a perfectly normal stage of development.
examples.zh: 这是一个十分正常的发展阶段。

examples.en: the development of basic skills such as literacy and numeracy
examples.zh: 诸如识字与识数等基本技能的发展

examples.en: The company can offer a number of opportunities for career development.
examples.zh: 该公司能提供一些职业发展的机会。

senses.def: the growth of the economy of a country or region through increased business activity

examples.en: Increased tourism will promote job creation and economic development.
examples.zh: 旅游业的增长将促进创造就业机会和经济发展。

examples.en: International policies should support, not inhibit, sustainable development.
examples.zh: 国际政策应支持而不是抑制可持续发展。

examples.en: He described women as the backbone of rural development worldwide.
examples.zh: 他将妇女描述为全世界农村发展的支柱。

examples.en: community development projects
examples.zh: 社区发展项目

examples.en: a development plan/programme
examples.zh: 发展计划

senses.def: the process of producing or creating something new or more advanced; a new or advanced product or idea
senses.zh: 开发；研制；研制成果；开发创意

examples.en: the development of new technology
examples.zh: 新技术的开发

examples.en: Pete is head of product development.
examples.zh: 皮特是产品开发负责人。

examples.en: A more powerful version of this electric bus is currently in development.
examples.zh: 这种电动巴士的更强大版本目前正在开发中。

examples.en: A new vaccine is under development.
examples.zh: 一种新疫苗正在研发中。

examples.en: This drug is an exciting new development.
examples.zh: 这种药是一项令人兴奋的新成果。

examples.en: developments in aviation technology
examples.zh: 航空技术的开发成果

senses.group: new product or idea 新产品／想法

senses.def: a new event or stage that is likely to affect what happens in a continuing situation
senses.zh: （新的）发展势态，进展情况，发展阶段

examples.en: Have there been any further developments?
examples.zh: 有新的进展吗？

examples.en: We welcome the recent positive developments.
examples.zh: 我们欢迎最近的积极进展。

examples.en: the latest developments in the war
examples.zh: 战争的最新进展情况

examples.en: There have been some interesting new developments in the case.
examples.zh: 案件有了一些有趣的新进展。

senses.def: a piece of land with new buildings on it

examples.en: I live in a brand-new housing development.
examples.zh: 我住在一个全新的住宅开发区。

examples.en: a mixed residential and business development
examples.zh: 住宅和商业混合开发

examples.zh: 这棵树的叶子显示出白蜡树枯梢病的迹象。

examples.en: Dieback is killing trees in many areas of Auckland.
examples.zh: 奥克兰许多地区的树木因枯梢病而死亡。

senses.def: a person who strongly opposes change and new ideas

examples.en: A few diehards are trying to stop the reforms.
examples.zh: 几个顽固派分子试图阻止改革。

senses.def: strongly opposing change and new ideas
senses.zh: 顽固的；因循守旧的；死硬的

examples.en: diehard supporters of the exiled king
examples.zh: 顽固支持流亡国王的人

examples.zh: 柴油汽车／机车／火车

senses.def: a vehicle that uses diesel

examples.en: Our new car is a diesel.
examples.zh: 我们的新车是柴油车。

senses.def: the food and drink that you eat and drink regularly

examples.en: to eat a healthy, balanced diet
examples.zh: 吃健康均衡的食物

examples.en: I loved the Japanese diet of rice, vegetables and fish.
examples.zh: 我喜欢米饭、蔬菜和鱼这些日本人常吃的食物。

examples.en: a vegetarian/vegan diet
examples.zh: 素食/纯素饮食

examples.en: The traditional Mediterranean diet is fairly high in fat.
examples.zh: 传统的地中海饮食脂肪含量相当高。

examples.en: to receive advice on diet
examples.zh: 接受饮食建议

senses.def: a limited variety or amount of food that you eat for medical reasons or because you want to lose weight; a time when you only eat this limited variety or amount
senses.zh: 规定饮食（为健康或减肥等目的）；规定饮食的时期

examples.en: He followed a strict low-fat diet.
examples.zh: 他严格坚持低脂饮食。

examples.en: I decided to go on a diet (= to lose weight) before my holiday.
examples.zh: 我决定在休假前节食。

examples.en: She is trying to lose weight through diet and exercise.
examples.zh: 她想通过节食和运动减肥。

examples.en: diet drinks (= with fewer calories than normal)
examples.zh: 低热量饮料

examples.en: Lose pounds with our new diet plan!
examples.zh: 采用我们的新饮食方案瘦身吧！

senses.def: a large amount of a limited range of activities

examples.en: Children today are brought up on a diet of video games and TV on demand.
examples.zh: 如今的孩子是在打电子游戏和看点播电视片中长大的。

senses.def: to eat less food or only food of a particular type in order to lose weight

examples.en: She's always dieting but she never seems to lose any weight.
examples.zh: 她总是在节食，但体重好像并未减少。

senses.def: connected with or contained in the food that you eat and drink regularly

examples.en: dietary advice/changes/habits
examples.zh: 饮食建议／变化／习惯

examples.en: dietary supplements
examples.zh: 营养补充剂

examples.en: dietary fibre
examples.zh: 饮食纤维素

examples.en: her dietary intake of calcium
examples.zh: 她的膳食钙摄入量

senses.def: a person who is trying to lose weight on a diet
connected with diet and healthy eating

examples.en: dietetic advice
examples.zh: 饮食建议

senses.def: the scientific study of diet and healthy eating
a person whose job is to advise people on what kind of food they should eat to keep healthy
