examples.zh: 他们大约五年前首次发现这种蛋白质。

examples.en: She recently discovered two fungi that were new to science.
examples.zh: 她最近发现了两种对科学来说是新的真菌。

senses.def: to find somebody/something that was hidden or that you did not expect to find

examples.en: Police discovered a large stash of drugs while searching the house.
examples.zh: 警方搜查这栋房子时发现里面藏着一大批毒品。

examples.en: We discovered this beach while we were sailing around the island.
examples.zh: 我们在围绕这个海岛航行时发现了这个海滩。

examples.en: His body was discovered in the lake near his house.
examples.zh: 他的尸体在他家附近的湖里被发现。

examples.en: He was discovered hiding in a shed.
examples.zh: 人们发现他原来藏在棚屋里。

examples.en: She was discovered dead at her home in Leeds.
examples.zh: 人们发现她死在利兹的家里。

senses.def: to find out about something; to find some information about something

examples.en: She was determined to discover the truth about her neighbours.
examples.zh: 她决心弄清她邻居的真相。

examples.en: to discover a secret
examples.zh: 发现一个秘密

examples.en: I've just discovered hang-gliding!
examples.zh: 我刚知道有悬挂式滑翔运动！

examples.en: Discover the joys of yoga!
examples.zh: 发现瑜伽的乐趣！

examples.en: It was a shock to discover (that) he couldn’t read.
examples.zh: 得知他不识字真令人震惊。

examples.en: We never did discover why she gave up her job.
examples.zh: 我们一直弄不清楚她为什么辞职。

examples.en: It was later discovered that the diaries were a fraud.
examples.zh: 后来查明这些日记完全是伪造的。

examples.en: He was later discovered to be seriously ill.
examples.zh: 后来才了解到他患了重病。

senses.def: to be the first person to realize that somebody is very good at singing, acting, etc. and help them to become successful and famous

examples.en: The singer was discovered while still at school.
examples.zh: 这个歌唱家在上学的时候就受到赏识了。

examples.en: There's great talent out there just waiting to be discovered.
examples.zh: 伟大的天才并非不存在，只是等着大家去发现。

senses.def: the quality of being able to be found by searching or able to be found easily

examples.en: the algorithms that govern the discoverability of online content
examples.zh: 控制在线内容可发现性的算法

senses.def: that you can find by searching or find easily

examples.en: Annual demand for oil and gas amounts to less than 1% of estimates of the world's remaining discovered and discoverable resources.
examples.zh: 石油和天然气的年需求量不到世界剩余已发现和可发现资源估计值的 1%。

examples.en: The theses have been catalogued and are discoverable through the Libraries website.
examples.zh: 这些论文已被编目，可以通过图书馆网站找到。

senses.def: the first person to become aware that a particular place or thing exists

examples.en: Sir Alexander Fleming, the discoverer of penicillin
examples.zh: 青霉素的发现者亚历山大·弗莱明爵士

senses.def: a person who finds somebody/something that was hidden or that they did not expect to find

examples.en: I was the lucky discoverer of a very valuable painting.
examples.zh: 我很幸运地发现了一幅非常有价值的画作。

senses.def: an act or the process of finding somebody/something, or learning about something that was not known about before

examples.en: Researchers in this field have made some important new discoveries.
examples.zh: 这个领域的研究人员有了一些重大的新发现。

examples.en: New scientific discoveries are being made all the time.
examples.zh: 新的科学发现无时无刻不在发生。

examples.en: the discovery of antibiotics in the twentieth century
examples.zh: 二十世纪抗生素的发现

examples.en: The discovery of a child's body in the river has shocked the community.
examples.zh: 在河里发现一个孩子的尸体，使社区大为震惊。

examples.en: the discovery of new talent in the art world
examples.zh: 艺术界新秀的发现

examples.en: He saw life as a voyage of discovery.
examples.zh: 他把人生看成一次发现新事物的旅程。

examples.en: The film takes us on a journey of discovery to different parts of the globe.
examples.zh: 这部电影带我们踏上探索地球不同地区的旅程。

examples.en: She was shocked by the discovery that he had been unfaithful.
examples.zh: 她发觉他不忠时感到非常震惊。

examples.en: In 1974 Hawking made the discovery (= he discovered) that black holes give off radiation.
examples.zh: 1974 年霍金发现黑洞会发出辐射。

senses.def: a thing, fact or person that is found or learned about for the first time
senses.zh: 被发现的事物（或真相、人）

examples.en: The drug is not a new discovery—it's been known about for years.
examples.zh: 这种药并不是什么新发现，多年前便为人所知。

examples.en: one of the most important scientific discoveries of all time
examples.zh: 有史以来最重要的科学发现之一

examples.en: potentially the biggest archaeological discovery in Norway for fifty years
examples.zh: 可能是挪威50 年来最大的考古发现

examples.en: recent discoveries about sleep
examples.zh: 关于睡眠的新发现

senses.def: a major US cable and satellite television channel, started in 1985, which originally only offered programmes on history, technology, nature and adventure. It now also broadcasts programmes which are more typical of reality TV
senses.zh: 发现频道（Discovery Channel）：美国主要的有线和卫星电视频道，始于1985年，最初仅提供有关历史，技术，自然和冒险的节目。现在，它还播放真人电视更典型的节目。

senses.def: to make people stop respecting somebody/something
senses.zh: 败坏…的名声；使丧失信誉；使丢脸

examples.en: The photos were deliberately taken to discredit the president.
examples.zh: 这些蓄意拍摄的照片旨在败坏总统的名声。

examples.en: a discredited government/policy
examples.zh: 名声扫地的政府；失去信誉的政策

senses.def: to make people stop believing that something is true; to make something appear unlikely to be true

examples.en: These theories are now largely discredited among linguists.
examples.zh: 这些理论现已大多受到语言学家的质疑。

examples.en: This new evidence discredits earlier findings.
examples.zh: 这个新证据推翻了早期的研究结果。

examples.en: These ideas have now been completely discredited.
examples.zh: 这些想法现在已经完全不可信了。

senses.def: damage to somebody’s/something's reputation; loss of respect
senses.zh: 名誉丧失；信誉丧失；丢脸

examples.en: Violent football fans bring discredit on the teams they support.
examples.zh: 狂暴的足球迷败坏了他们所支持球队的声誉。

examples.en: My brother’s behaviour did great discredit to the family.
examples.zh: 我弟弟的行为大大败坏了家族的名誉。

examples.en: Britain, to its discredit, did not speak out against these atrocities.
examples.zh: 英国没有公开反对这些残暴行为，因而名誉扫地。

senses.def: a person or thing that causes damage to somebody's/something's reputation or loss of respect

examples.en: They were a discredit to their country.
examples.zh: 他们是国家的耻辱。

senses.def: bad and unacceptable; causing people to lose respect
senses.zh: 不光彩的；有损尊严的；丢脸的

senses.def: careful in what you say or do, in order to keep something secret or to avoid causing difficulty for somebody or making them feel embarrassed
senses.zh: （言行）谨慎的，慎重的；考虑周到的

examples.en: He was always very discreet about his love affairs.
examples.zh: 他对两性关系一贯谨小慎微。

examples.en: You ought to make a few discreet enquiries before you sign anything.
examples.zh: 你应该审慎地询问清楚再签字。

examples.en: A discreet glance at the clock told me the interview had lasted an hour.
examples.zh: 仔细地看了一眼时钟，我知道采访已经持续了一个小时。

senses.def: in a careful way, in order to keep something secret or to avoid causing difficulty for somebody or making them feel embarrassed

examples.en: She coughed discreetly to announce her presence.
examples.zh: 她小心地咳嗽了一声，让大家知道她来了。

senses.def: a difference between two or more things that should be the same

examples.en: wide discrepancies in prices quoted for the work
examples.zh: 这项工作的报价出入很大

examples.en: What are the reasons for the discrepancy between girls' and boys' performance in school?
examples.zh: 女生和男生在学校表现不同的原因何在呢？

senses.def: separate and different from other things of the same type

examples.en: The organisms can be divided into discrete categories.
examples.zh: 有机体可分为许多互不关联的种类。

senses.def: in a way that is independent of other things of the same type

examples.en: Goldstein discusses these issues jointly rather than discretely.
examples.zh: 戈德斯坦共同而不是离散地讨论这些问题。

senses.def: the quality of being independent of other things of the same type
the freedom or power to decide what should be done in a particular situation
senses.zh: 自行决定的自由；自行决定权

examples.en: I'll leave it up to you to use your discretion.
examples.zh: 我把这件事留给你自己斟酌决定。

examples.en: How much to tell terminally ill patients is left to the discretion of the doctor.
examples.zh: 晚期病人的病情让本人知道多少由医生自行决定。

senses.def: care in what you say or do, in order to keep something secret or to avoid causing difficulty for somebody or making them feel embarrassed; the quality of being discreet

examples.en: This is confidential, but I know that I can rely on your discretion.
examples.zh: 这是机密，不过我知道你靠得住。

examples.en: Jane is the soul of discretion (= you can trust her).
examples.zh: 简是谨慎的灵魂（=你可以信任她）。

examples.en: Use the utmost discretion when you talk to her.
examples.zh: 与她交谈时请务必谨慎行事。

senses.def: according to what somebody decides or wishes to do
senses.zh: 由某人斟酌决定；按照某人的意愿

examples.en: Bail is granted at the discretion of the court.
examples.zh: 由法庭决定准予保释。

examples.en: There is no service charge and tipping is at your discretion.
examples.zh: 不收服务费，给不给小费由你自行决定。

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.zh: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

senses.def: according to what somebody decides or wishes to do
senses.zh: 由某人斟酌决定；按照某人的意愿

examples.en: Bail is granted at the discretion of the court.
examples.zh: 由法庭决定准予保释。

examples.en: There is no service charge and tipping is at your discretion.
examples.zh: 不收服务费，给不给小费由你自行决定。

items.idm: discretion is the better part of valour

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.zh: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.zh: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

discretion is the better part of valour.word: discretion is the better part of valour

senses.def: decided according to the judgement of a person in authority about what is necessary in each particular situation; not decided by rules
senses.zh: 自行决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的

examples.en: You may be eligible for a discretionary grant for your university course.
examples.zh: 读大学课程可能会有资格获得学校自行决定是否发放的助学金。

examples.en: The court has a discretionary power to appoint a receiver in such circumstances.
examples.zh: 在这种情况下，法院有酌情权指定接管人。

senses.def: to recognize that there is a difference between people or things; to show a difference between people or things

examples.en: The computer program was unable to discriminate between letters and numbers.
examples.zh: 这计算机程序不能辨别字母与数字。

examples.en: When do babies learn to discriminate voices?
examples.zh: 婴儿什么时候学会辨别嗓音呢？

examples.en: A number of features discriminate this species from others.
examples.zh: 有些特征使这一物种与其他物种区别开来。

senses.def: to treat one person or group worse/better than another in an unfair way

examples.en: practices that discriminate against women and in favour of men
examples.zh: 重男轻女的做法

examples.en: It is illegal to discriminate on the grounds of race, gender or religion.
examples.zh: 因种族、性别或宗教信仰而实行歧视是非法的。

senses.def: the practice of treating somebody or a particular group in society less fairly than others

examples.en: age/racial/gender/sex discrimination (= because of somebody’s age, race, gender or sex)
examples.zh: 年龄／种族／性别歧视

examples.en: discrimination against the elderly
examples.zh: 歧视老人

examples.en: discrimination in favour of the young
examples.zh: 厚待年轻人

examples.en: They alleged discrimination by the authorities.
examples.zh: 他们声称受到当局的歧视。

examples.en: to prohibit/outlaw/ban discrimination on the basis of race, gender or sexual orientation
examples.zh: 禁止／立法禁止／明令禁止基于种族、性别或性取向的歧视

examples.en: legislation to ban discrimination on the grounds of age
examples.zh: 立法禁止年龄歧视

senses.def: the ability to judge what is good, true, etc.

examples.en: He showed great discrimination in his choice of friends.
examples.zh: 他在择友方面颇具慧眼。

senses.def: the ability to recognize a difference between one thing and another; a difference that is recognized

examples.en: to learn discrimination between right and wrong
examples.zh: 学会分辨是非

examples.en: Young children find it difficult to make fine discriminations.
examples.zh: 小孩子很难作出细微的区分。

examples.en: It takes a lot of experience to make such fine discriminations.
examples.zh: 做出如此精细的辨别需要大量的经验。

senses.def: unfair; treating somebody or one group of people worse than others
senses.zh: 区别对待的；不公正的；歧视的

examples.en: discriminatory practices/rules/measures
examples.zh: 不公正的做法／规定／措施

examples.en: sexually/racially discriminatory laws
examples.zh: 性别／种族歧视性法律

senses.def: moving from one point to another without any strict structure
senses.zh: 东拉西扯的；离题的；不着边际的

examples.en: the discursive style of the novel
examples.zh: 这部小说的散漫风格

examples.en: Poetry is closer to music than to the more extended and discursive literary forms.
examples.zh: 相对于更宽泛和散漫的文学形式，诗歌更接近音乐。

examples.en: The meetings were informal, discursive, even gossipy.
examples.zh: 会议是非正式的、漫无目的的，甚至是八卦的。

senses.def: a heavy flat round object thrown in a sporting event

examples.en: She hurled the discus across the field.
examples.zh: 她把铁饼扔过田野。

senses.def: the event or sport of throwing a discus

examples.en: He regained his discus title after a few years.
examples.zh: 几年后，他重新获得了铁饼冠军头衔。

examples.en: Her foot landed outside the discus circle and she was disqualified.
examples.zh: 她的脚落在铁饼圈外，她被取消资格。

senses.def: to talk about something with somebody, especially in order to decide something

examples.en: Have you discussed the problem with anyone?
examples.zh: 你与谁商量过这个问题吗？

examples.en: I'm not prepared to discuss this on the phone.
examples.zh: 我不想在电话里谈论此事。

examples.en: to discuss the issue/matter/topic
examples.zh: 讨论问题／事项／主题

examples.en: to discuss a plan/proposal
examples.zh: 讨论计划／提案

examples.en: They met to discuss the possibility of working together.
examples.zh: 他们会面讨论了合作的可能性。

examples.en: We need to discuss when we should go.
examples.zh: 我们需要商量一下什么时候动身。

examples.en: We briefly discussed buying a second car.
examples.zh: 我们草草商量了再买一辆汽车的事儿。

examples.en: They discussed the whole family possibly travelling together.
examples.zh: 他们讨论了全家人一起旅行的可能性。

senses.def: to write or talk about something in detail, showing the different ideas and opinions about it

examples.en: This topic will be discussed at greater length in the next chapter.
examples.zh: 这个题目将在下一章里详细论述。

examples.en: The author discusses the economic impact of these changes.
examples.zh: 作者讨论了这些变化的经济影响。

examples.en: The article discusses how teachers can use technology in their classrooms.
examples.zh: 本文讨论了教师如何在课堂上运用技术。

examples.en: The novel's main theme is ‘You reap what you sow’. Discuss. (= in an essay question)
examples.zh: 小说的主题是“一分耕耘，一分收获”。讨论。 （= 在问答题中）

intro.en: These words all mean to share news, information, ideas or feelings with another person or other people, especially by talking with them.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含交流、交谈之义。

items.def: to speak in order to give information, express feelings or share ideas:
items.zh: 指说话、讲话、谈话

examples.en: We talked on the phone for over an hour.
examples.zh: 我们在电话里谈了一个多小时。

items.def: (rather formal) to talk and share ideas on a subject or problem with other people, especially in order to decide something:
items.zh: 指谈论、讨论、商量

examples.en: Have you discussed the problem with anyone?
examples.zh: 你与谁商量过这个问题吗？

items.def: to talk to somebody about something; to have a conversation with somebody:
items.zh: 指谈话、交谈

examples.en: I’ve spoken to the manager about it.
examples.zh: 那件事我已经和经理谈过了。

items.def: (rather formal) to exchange information or ideas with somebody:
items.zh: 指与某人交流信息或意见

examples.en: We only communicate by email.
examples.zh: 我们只通过电子邮件进行交流。

items.def: to discuss something, especially formally, before making a decision or finding a solution:
items.zh: （尤指正式）讨论、辩论

examples.en: Politicians will be debating the bill later this week.
examples.zh: 政界将在本周晚些时候讨论这项议案。

items.def: (rather formal) to discuss something with somebody in order to get their permission for something, or to help you make a decision:
items.zh: 指（与某人）商议、商量（以得到许可或帮助决策）

examples.en: You shouldn’t have done it without consulting me.
examples.zh: 你不该不和我商量就做。

intro.en: These words all mean to think about, study or describe somebody/​something carefully, especially in order to understand them, form an opinion of them or make a decision about them.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含思量、审查、调查、研究之义。

items.def: to think about, study or describe an idea, subject or piece of work very carefully:
items.zh: 指审查、调查、考查、考察

examples.en: These ideas will be examined in more detail in Chapter 10.
examples.zh: 这些观点将在第 10 章做更为详细的探讨。

items.def: to examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it:
items.zh: 指分析

examples.en: The job involves gathering and analysing data.
examples.zh: 这项工作需要搜集和分析资料。

items.def: to examine something again, especially so that you can decide if it is necessary to make changes:
items.zh: 指复查、检讨，以做必要的修改

examples.en: The government will review the situation later in the year.
examples.zh: 政府将在今年晚些时候重新检讨形势。

items.def: to examine somebody/​something in order to understand them or it:
items.zh: 指研究、调查

examples.en: We will study the report carefully before making a decision.
examples.zh: 我们将认真研究这份报告，然后再作决定。

items.def: to write or talk about something in detail, showing the different ideas and opinions about it:
items.zh: 指详述、论述

examples.en: This topic will be discussed at greater length in the next chapter.
examples.zh: 这个题目将在下一章里详细论述。

senses.def: a conversation about somebody/something; the process of discussing somebody/something

examples.en: I discovered something interesting during a family discussion.
examples.zh: 在一次家庭讨论中我发现了一些有趣的事情。

examples.en: We'll continue this discussion some other time.
examples.zh: 我们另外安排时间继续讨论。

examples.en: We had a discussion with them about the differences between Britain and the US.
examples.zh: 我们和他们讨论了英美两国的不同之处。

examples.en: A lively discussion followed about whether he should be allowed to join the club.
examples.zh: 接下来就是否应该允许他加入俱乐部进行了热烈的讨论。

examples.en: The pair held informal discussions on a number of topics.
examples.zh: 两人就多个话题进行了非正式讨论。

examples.en: The exhibition offers opportunities for frank discussions around sensitive issues.
examples.zh: 该展览提供了围绕敏感问题进行坦诚讨论的机会。

examples.en: We want to encourage public discussion of mental health issues.
examples.zh: 我们想鼓励公众讨论心理健康问题。

examples.en: There was some discussion among reviewers about this film.
examples.zh: 评论家们对这部电影进行了一些讨论。

examples.en: The plans have been under discussion (= being talked about) for a year now.
examples.zh: 这些计划至今已讨论一年了。

examples.en: a list of topics for discussion
examples.zh: 讨论话题清单

examples.en: to stimulate/provoke discussion
examples.zh: 刺激/引发讨论

examples.en: to initiate/start/spark a discussion
examples.zh: 发起/开始/引发讨论

examples.en: a panel/group/round-table discussion
examples.zh: 小组/圆桌讨论

senses.def: a speech or a piece of writing that discusses many different aspects of a subject

examples.en: I have chosen to focus my discussion on a single work.
examples.zh: 我决定集中讨论一部作品。

examples.en: Her article is a discussion of the methods used in research.
examples.zh: 她这篇文章论述的是研究中使用的方法。

examples.en: See chapter 15 for a detailed discussion of the approach used.
examples.zh: 有关所用方法的详细讨论，请参阅第 15 章。

synonyms.words: conversation ▪ dialogue ▪ talk ▪ debate ▪ consultation ▪ chat ▪ gossip

intro.en: These are all words for an occasion when people talk about something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示交谈、谈论。

items.def: a detailed conversation about something that is considered to be important:
items.zh: 指重要事情的讨论、谈论、商讨

examples.en: Discussions are still taking place between the two leaders.
examples.zh: 两位领导人仍在进行讨论。

items.def: a talk, usually a private or informal one, involving two people or a small group; the activity of talking in this way:
items.zh: 通常指私下的或非正式的交谈、谈话

examples.en: a telephone conversation
examples.zh: 电话交谈

items.def: conversations in a book, play or film:
items.zh: 指书、戏剧或电影中的对话、对白

examples.en: The novel has long descriptions and not much dialogue.
examples.zh: 这部小说描述多，对话少。

examples.en: The President told waiting reporters there had been a constructive dialogue.
examples.zh: 总统告诉等候的记者，刚才进行了一次富有建设性的对话。

items.def: a conversation or discussion, often one about a problem or something important for the people involved:
items.zh: 常指对有关人员就某个问题或重要的事情进行的交谈、谈话、讨论、商讨

examples.en: I had a long talk with my boss about my career prospects.
examples.zh: 我和老板就我的事业前景进行了一次长谈。

items.def: a formal discussion of an issue at a public meeting or in a parliament. In a debate two or more speakers express opposing views and then there is often a vote on the issue:
items.zh: 指公共集会上或议会里就某问题进行的、常以表决结束的辩论

examples.en: a debate on prison reform
examples.zh: 关于监狱制度改革的辩论

items.def: a formal discussion between groups of people before a decision is made about something:
items.zh: 指团体间在决策前进行的咨询、商讨、磋商

examples.en: There have been extensive consultations between the two countries.
examples.zh: 两国之间进行了广泛磋商。

items.def: a friendly informal conversation; informal talking. The countable use of chat is especially British English:
items.zh: chat 作可数名词尤用于英式英语

items.def: a conversation about other people and their private lives:
items.zh: 指关于他人及其私生活的闲谈、闲聊、说长道短

examples.en: We had a good gossip about the boss.
examples.zh: 我们讲了好一会儿老板的闲话。

senses.def: a place on the internet where people can exchange ideas and opinions about a topic
a place on the internet where people can exchange ideas and opinions about a topic

examples.en: Join us on the discussion forum and share your views.
examples.zh: 加入我们的网络论坛，分享你的观点。

senses.def: a meeting at which people can exchange ideas and opinions about a topic

examples.en: Several well-attended public discussion forums were held in the community.
examples.zh: 社区内举办了数场参与者甚多的公众讨论会。

senses.def: the feeling that somebody/something is not good enough to deserve your respect or attention

examples.en: She treated him with disdain.
examples.zh: 她对他很鄙视。

examples.en: He turned his head away in disdain.
examples.zh: 他不屑地把头转过去。

examples.en: a disdain for the law
examples.zh: 对法律的藐视

senses.def: to think that somebody/something does not deserve your respect or interest

examples.en: She disdained his offer of help.
examples.zh: 他提出要帮忙，遭到她的鄙弃。

examples.en: He disdains experts and gets his information from popular media.
examples.zh: 他蔑视专家并从大众媒体获取信息。

examples.en: She is a disruptive artist who disdains convention.
examples.zh: 她是一位蔑视传统的颠覆性艺术家。

examples.en: He disdained all people less well educated than himself.
examples.zh: 他鄙视所有没有受过良好教育的人。

senses.def: to refuse to do something because you think that you are too important to do it

examples.en: He disdained to turn to his son for advice.
examples.zh: 他不屑向自己的儿子请教。

senses.def: showing the feeling that somebody/something is not good enough to deserve your respect or attention

examples.en: She's always been disdainful of people who haven't been to college.
examples.zh: 她总是瞧不起那些没有上过大学的人。

senses.def: in a way that shows the feeling that somebody/something is not good enough to deserve your respect or attention
an illness affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection

examples.en: heart/lung/liver disease
examples.zh: 心脏病；肺病；肝病

examples.en: In 19th-century England, infectious diseases were the principal cause of death.
examples.zh: 在 19 世纪的英国，传染病是主要的死亡原因。

examples.en: chronic diseases such as obesity and diabetes
examples.zh: 肥胖和糖尿病等慢性疾病

examples.en: health measures to prevent the spread of disease
examples.zh: 预防疾病传播的保健措施

examples.en: Smoking increases the risk of heart disease.
examples.zh: 吸烟会增加患心脏病的风险。

examples.en: It is not known what causes the disease.
examples.zh: 这种病的起因不明。

examples.en: He suffers from a rare blood disease.
examples.zh: 他患有一种罕见的血液病。

examples.en: Sailors who ate no fresh food contracted the disease.
examples.zh: 不吃新鲜食物的水手患了这种病。

examples.en: It's better to prevent disease by ensuring a clean water supply.
examples.zh: 更好的方法是通过确保供给洁净水来预防疾病。

examples.en: to treat/cure a disease
examples.zh: 治疗／治愈疾病

examples.en: to spread/transmit a disease
examples.zh: 传播疾病

examples.en: Cattle had to be slaughtered after an outbreak of the disease.
examples.zh: 疾病爆发后，牛不得不被宰杀。

examples.en: patients with coronary heart disease
examples.zh: 冠心病患者

examples.en: cardiovascular/pulmonary/respiratory disease
examples.zh: 心血管/肺部/呼吸系统疾病

senses.def: something that is very wrong with people’s attitudes, way of life or with society

examples.en: Greed is a disease of modern society.
examples.zh: 贪婪是现代社会的恶疾。

synonyms.words: illness ▪ disorder ▪ infection ▪ condition ▪ ailment ▪ bug

intro.en: These are all words for a medical problem.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示健康问题。

items.def: a medical problem affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection:
items.zh: 常指人、动植物感染的病、疾病

examples.en: He suffers from a rare blood disease.
examples.zh: 他患有一种罕见的血液病。

items.def: a medical problem, or a period of suffering from one:
items.zh: 指病、疾病或患病期

examples.en: She died after a long illness.
examples.zh: 她久病不愈而亡。

items.def: (rather formal) a condition that causes problems with the way part of the body or brain works:
items.zh: 失调症（disorder）一种导致身体或大脑部分工作方式出现问题的病症：

examples.en: a rare disorder of the liver
examples.zh: 一种罕见的肝病

items.def: an illness that is caused by bacteria or a virus and that affects one part of the body:
items.zh: 指由细菌或病毒引起的身体某部位的感染或传染疾病

examples.en: a throat infection
examples.zh: 喉部感染

items.def: a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it:
items.zh: 指因不可治愈而长期患有的疾病

examples.en: a heart condition
examples.zh: 心脏病

items.def: (rather formal) an illness that is not very serious:
items.zh: 指轻病、小恙

examples.en: childhood ailments
examples.zh: 儿童期小病

items.def: (informal) an infectious illness that is usually fairly mild:
items.zh: 指轻微的传染病、小病

examples.en: a stomach bug
examples.zh: 胃病

senses.def: suffering from a disease

examples.en: diseased tissue
examples.zh: 有病的组织

examples.en: the diseased social system
examples.zh: 病态的社会制度

senses.def: to leave a vehicle, especially a ship or an aircraft, at the end of a journey; to let or make people leave a vehicle

examples.en: We will be disembarking at midday.
examples.zh: 我们将在中午下船。

examples.en: They had just disembarked from their tour bus after a 12-hour journey.
examples.zh: 他们经过 12 个小时的旅程，刚从旅游巴士上下来。

examples.en: The heat hit us as soon as we disembarked the plane.
examples.zh: 一下飞机，我们就感到热浪袭来。

examples.en: The passengers were disembarked safely.
examples.zh: 乘客们安全地下了船。

senses.def: the act of leaving a vehicle, especially a ship or an aircraft, at the end of a journey

examples.en: Please assemble on the deck for disembarkation.
examples.zh: 请在甲板上集合下船。

senses.def: coming from a person or place that cannot be seen or identified
senses.zh: 从看不到的人（或地方）发出的

examples.en: a disembodied voice
examples.zh: 不见其人的说话声

senses.def: separated from the body

examples.en: disembodied spirits
examples.zh: 游魂

senses.def: to take the stomach, bowels
the removal

examples.en: a form of ritual suicide by disembowelment
examples.zh: 一种通过剖腹自杀的仪式

examples.en: The movie is full of beheadings and disembowelments.
examples.zh: 这部电影充满了斩首和剖腹的场面。

senses.def: no longer feeling enthusiasm for somebody/something; not believing something is good or worth doing
senses.zh: 不再着迷的；不再抱幻想的

examples.en: He was becoming disenchanted with his job as a lawyer.
examples.zh: 他对自己的律师工作渐渐地不抱幻想了。

examples.en: Many in the party had become disenchanted with the reforms.
examples.zh: 该党的许多人对这些改革都已不再抱幻想。

senses.def: the state of no longer feeling enthusiasm for somebody/something; a lack of belief that something is good or worth doing
senses.zh: 不再着迷的；不再抱幻想的

examples.en: a growing sense/feeling of disenchantment with his job
examples.zh: 他对工作渐渐失去热情

senses.def: to take away somebody’s rights, especially their right to vote
senses.zh: 剥夺（某人）的权利（尤指选举权）

examples.en: Many disabled people were effectively disenfranchised because of lack of access.
examples.zh: 由于缺乏机会，很多残疾人的权利实际上被剥夺了。

examples.en: Mr Mandela was the symbolic leader of the disenfranchised black majority.
examples.zh: 曼德拉先生是被剥夺公民权的黑人多数派的象征性领袖。

senses.def: to free somebody/something from the person or thing that is holding them or it; to become free

examples.en: She gently disengaged herself from her sleeping son.
examples.zh: 她轻轻地放下怀中熟睡的儿子。

examples.en: They wished to disengage themselves from these policies.
examples.zh: 他们希望能摆脱这些政策的束缚。

examples.en: to disengage the clutch (= when driving a car)
examples.zh: （开车时）松开离合器

examples.en: We saw the booster rockets disengage and fall into the sea.
examples.zh: 我们看到火箭助推器脱落后坠入大海。

senses.def: if an army disengages
the fact of no longer being involved with somebody/something or interested in them/it

examples.en: young people's disengagement from politics
examples.zh: 年轻人不参与政治

examples.en: A level of public disengagement is already evident in society.
examples.zh: 公众对社会事务漠不关心的现象已经很明显了。

senses.def: the act of stopping fighting and moving away

examples.en: the disengagement of forces from the region
examples.zh: 军队从该地区撤离

senses.def: to separate different arguments, ideas, etc. that have become confused
senses.zh: 理顺，分清，清理出（混乱的论据、想法等）

examples.en: It's not easy to disentangle the truth from the official statistics.
examples.zh: 从官方统计资料中理出真实情况并不容易。

examples.en: It is important to disentangle all the factors that may be causing your stress.
examples.zh: 把可能给你带来压力的那些因素理清楚，这一点很重要。

examples.en: trying to disentangle fact from fiction
examples.zh: 试图区分事实与虚构

senses.def: to free somebody/something from something that has become wrapped or twisted

examples.en: He tried to disentangle his fingers from her hair.
examples.zh: 他竭力将手指从她的头发中挣脱出来。

examples.en: She has just disentangled herself from a painful relationship.
examples.zh: 她刚刚摆脱一段痛苦的感情。

senses.def: to get rid of the twists

examples.en: He was sitting on the deck disentangling a coil of rope.
examples.zh: 他坐在甲板上解开一捆绳索。

senses.def: a loss or lack of balance in a situation
to end the official status of something, especially a national Church
senses.zh: 废除（国教等）的法定地位

examples.en: a campaign to disestablish the Church of England
examples.zh: 废除英格兰圣公会国教地位的运动

senses.def: the act of ending the official status of something, especially a national Church
the feeling that you do not like or approve of somebody/something

examples.en: They looked upon the new policy with disfavour.
examples.zh: 他们对新政策持不满态度。

examples.en: She seems to have fallen into disfavour with the director.
examples.zh: 她似乎不喜欢主任。

senses.def: to damage the appearance of a person, thing or place
senses.zh: 损毁…的外形；使变丑；毁容

examples.en: Her face was disfigured by a long red scar.
examples.zh: 她脸上一条红色的长疤使她破相了。

examples.en: An ugly power station disfigures the landscape.
examples.zh: 一座丑陋的发电站破坏了景观。

senses.def: the act of damaging the appearance of a person, thing or place; a damaged appearance of this kind
senses.zh: 毁容：破坏人，物或地方外观的行为；这种损坏的外观

examples.en: He suffered permanent disfigurement in the fire.
examples.zh: 那场火灾令他永久毁容。

examples.en: people with facial disfigurements
examples.zh: 面部有缺陷的人

senses.def: to pour something out in large quantities

examples.en: The pipe disgorges sewage into the sea.
examples.zh: 这管道将污水排入大海。

senses.def: if a vehicle or building disgorges

examples.en: The bus disgorged a crowd of noisy children.
examples.zh: 公共汽车上涌下来一群叽叽喳喳的孩子。

senses.def: the loss of other people’s respect and approval because of the bad way somebody has behaved

examples.en: Her behaviour has brought disgrace on her family.
examples.zh: 她的行为使家人蒙羞。

examples.en: The swimmer was sent home from the Olympics in disgrace.
examples.zh: 这位游泳运动员很不光彩地从奥运会上被遣送回国。

examples.en: Sam was in disgrace with his parents.
examples.zh: 萨姆已失宠于他的父母。

examples.en: There is no disgrace in being poor.
examples.zh: 贫穷不是耻辱。

senses.def: a person or thing that is so bad that people connected with them or it feel or should feel ashamed
senses.zh: 令人感到羞耻的人（或事）

examples.en: Your homework is an absolute disgrace.
examples.zh: 你的作业太丢人了。

examples.en: The state of our roads is a national disgrace.
examples.zh: 我们的道路状况是国家的耻辱。

examples.en: That sort of behaviour is a disgrace to the legal profession.
examples.zh: 那种行为是法律界的耻辱。

examples.en: You are a disgrace to this school.
examples.zh: 你是这所学校的耻辱。

examples.en: It's a disgrace that (= it is very wrong that) they are paid so little.
examples.zh: 他们的报酬如此微薄，太不像话了。

senses.def: to behave badly in a way that makes you or other people feel ashamed

examples.en: She disgraced herself by losing her temper and storming out.
examples.zh: 她发脾气并愤然离去，这让自己丢脸了。

examples.en: He had disgraced the family name.
examples.zh: 他玷污了家族的名声。

senses.def: to lose the respect of people, usually so that you lose a position of power
senses.zh: 使名誉扫地；使失势；使失去地位

examples.en: He was publicly disgraced and sent into exile.
examples.zh: 他被当众贬谪，放逐异乡。

senses.def: very bad or unacceptable; that people should feel ashamed about
senses.zh: 不光彩的；可耻的；丢脸的

examples.en: His behaviour was absolutely disgraceful!
examples.zh: 他的行为真可耻！

examples.en: It's disgraceful that none of the family tried to help her.
examples.zh: 家里竟无人肯帮助她，太不像话了。

examples.en: a disgraceful waste of money
examples.zh: 可耻的金钱浪费

senses.def: in a way that is very bad or unacceptable; in a way that people should feel ashamed about
senses.zh: 不光彩的；可耻的；丢脸的

examples.en: She has behaved disgracefully towards him.
examples.zh: 她对他的行为很不光彩。

examples.en: The healthcare system has been disgracefully neglected.
examples.zh: 医疗保健系统一直被可耻地忽视。

senses.def: annoyed or disappointed because something has happened to upset you

examples.en: disgruntled employees
examples.zh: 不满的雇员

examples.en: I left feeling disgruntled at the way I'd been treated.
examples.zh: 我受到如此对待，因而愤然离去。

senses.def: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you

examples.en: The hijackers were heavily disguised.
examples.zh: 劫持者伪装得严严实实。

examples.en: They got in disguised as security guards.
examples.zh: 他们装扮成保安人员混了进去。

examples.en: She was cleverly disguised as a policewoman.
examples.zh: 她巧妙地扮成警察。

examples.en: She disguised herself as a boy.
examples.zh: 她女扮男装。

senses.def: to hide something or change it, so that it cannot be recognized

examples.en: She made no attempt to disguise her surprise.
examples.zh: 她根本不曾掩饰自己惊奇的心情。

examples.en: It was a thinly disguised attack on the president.
examples.zh: 不难看出这是在攻击总统。

examples.en: She couldn't disguise the fact that she felt uncomfortable.
examples.zh: 她无法掩饰她那不安的心情。

examples.en: He tried to disguise his accent.
examples.zh: 他竭力掩饰自己的口音。

senses.def: something that you wear or use to change your appearance so that people do not recognize you

examples.en: She wore glasses and a wig as a disguise.
examples.zh: 她用眼镜和假发伪装起来。

examples.en: The star travelled in disguise (= wearing a disguise).
examples.zh: 这位明星化了装去旅行。

senses.def: the art of changing your appearance so that people do not recognize you

examples.en: He is a master of disguise.
examples.zh: 他是伪装能手。

senses.def: a way of hiding the true nature of something

examples.en: His angelic look is just a disguise.
examples.zh: 他天使般的外表只是一种伪装。

examples.en: State regulation often served as a thin disguise for corruption.
examples.zh: 国家规定常常成为腐败遮羞布。

examples.en: Her books can be history lessons in disguise.
examples.zh: 她的书是改头换面的历史教科书。

senses.def: something that seems to be a problem at first, but that has good results in the end

examples.en: Losing your job might turn out to be a blessing in disguise.
examples.zh: 失去工作可能会因祸得福。

senses.def: something that seems to be a problem at first, but that has good results in the end

examples.en: Losing your job might turn out to be a blessing in disguise.
examples.zh: 失去工作可能会因祸得福。

senses.def: a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/something that you feel is unacceptable, or for something that looks, smells, etc. unpleasant

examples.en: The idea fills me with disgust.
examples.zh: 这个想法实在令我恶心。

examples.en: I can only feel disgust for these criminals.
examples.zh: 对这些罪犯我只感到憎恶。

examples.en: She expressed her disgust at the programme in a tweet.
examples.zh: 她发推特表达了对这个节目的反感。

examples.en: He walked away in disgust.
examples.zh: 他厌恶地走开了。

examples.en: She wrinkled her nose in disgust at the smell.
examples.zh: 她闻到那气味，恶心地皱起了鼻子。

examples.en: He regarded the cubes of fat with disgust.
examples.zh: 他厌恶地看着那些肥肉块。

examples.en: Much to my disgust, they refused to help.
examples.zh: 他们不肯帮忙，令我极其愤慨。

senses.def: if something disgusts

examples.en: The level of violence in the film really disgusted me.
examples.zh: 影片中的暴力程度实在让我反感。

examples.en: The feel of it, all cold and slimy, disgusted him.
examples.zh: 那东西摸着冰凉凉、黏糊糊的，让他觉得恶心。

senses.def: a humorous name for an angry middle-class
senses.zh: 滕布里奇·威尔斯（Tunbridge Wells）感到恶心：这是一个生气的中产阶级老年人的幽默名字，他向报纸等撰写强烈的关于现代行为的投诉信。该名称来自这样的人可能会在信末加上而不是写下他或她的名字的签名。Tunbridge Wells是肯特镇。

senses.def: in a way that shows disgust
senses.zh: 令人厌恶的：以某种方式表现出厌恶

examples.en: ‘This champagne is warm!’, he said disgustedly.
examples.zh: “这香槟酒是温的！”他厌恶地说。

senses.def: extremely (in a way that other people feel jealous
senses.zh: 极其，极端，非常（以致使人忌妒）

examples.en: He looked disgustingly healthy when he got back from the Bahamas.
examples.zh: 他从巴哈马群岛回来时看上去健康得令人眼红。

senses.def: in a way that makes people feel shocked, upset or angry
senses.zh: 令人恶心地；令人气愤地

examples.en: disgustingly dirty
examples.zh: 脏得令人作呕

senses.def: a flat shallow container for cooking food in or serving it from

examples.en: a baking/serving dish
examples.zh: 烤盘；上食物的盘子

examples.en: a casserole dish
examples.zh: 砂锅菜

examples.en: Bake in a shallow dish for 45 mins.
examples.zh: 放在浅盘里烤 45 分钟。

examples.en: They helped themselves from a large dish of pasta.
examples.zh: 他们从一大盘意大利面食中自行取一些吃。

senses.def: the plates, bowls, cups, etc. that have been used for a meal and need to be washed

examples.en: I'll do the dishes (= wash them).
examples.zh: 我来洗碗。

examples.en: My first real job was washing dishes in a restaurant.
examples.zh: 我第一份真正的工作是在餐馆里洗盘子。

senses.def: food prepared in a particular way as part of a meal

examples.en: a vegetarian/fish/meat/pasta dish
examples.zh: 一盘素菜／鱼／肉／意面

examples.en: This makes an excellent hot main dish.
examples.zh: 这就是一道绝好的热主菜。

examples.en: I decided to cook his favourite dish.
examples.zh: 我决定做他最喜欢的菜。

examples.en: to prepare/serve a dish
examples.zh: 准备/上菜

examples.en: a savoury dish of curried rice and lamb
examples.zh: 美味的咖喱羊肉饭

examples.en: I can recommend the chef's dish of the day.
examples.zh: 我可推荐今天的主厨特餐。

senses.def: any object that is like a dish or bowl in shape

examples.en: a soap dish
examples.zh: 肥皂盘

senses.def: a sexually attractive person

examples.en: What a dish!
examples.zh: 真性感！

senses.def: to tell people unkind or unpleasant things about somebody, especially about their private life
senses.zh: 说（某人）的闲话；揭（某人）的短

examples.en: She loves to dish the dirt on her sisters.
examples.zh: 她喜欢说她姐妹们的坏话。

senses.def: to criticize other people

examples.en: He enjoys dishing it out, but he really can't take it (= cannot accept criticism from other people).
examples.zh: 他喜欢指责别人，而自己却一点批评都接受不了。

senses.def: to tell people unkind or unpleasant things about somebody, especially about their private life
senses.zh: 说（某人）的闲话；揭（某人）的短

examples.en: She loves to dish the dirt on her sisters.

examples.zh: 他被控以欺骗手段谋取财产。

examples.zh: 五名公务员因不诚实的行为和渎职而遭免职。

examples.zh: 她的行为败坏了这个行业的声誉。

examples.en: He was given a dishonourable discharge (= an order to leave the army for unacceptable behaviour).
examples.zh: 他被开除了军籍。

senses.def: in a way that does not deserve respect; in a way that is unacceptable or morally wrong

examples.zh: 我实在不愿把实情告诉你，但并非人人都像你那样诚实。

senses.def: the state of being disillusioned

examples.zh: 人们对政治制度的幻想日益幻灭。

senses.def: the state of being disillusioned
senses.zh: 醒悟；不再抱幻想；幻想破灭

examples.en: There is widespread disillusionment with the present government.
examples.zh: 人们对现政府普遍感到失望。

examples.en: Disillusionment among the young is worrying for schools.
examples.zh: 年轻人的幻灭令学校担忧。

examples.zh: 年轻人普遍感到失望。

examples.zh: 起薪低是失业者重返工作岗位的强烈阻碍。

senses.def: to remove the advantages of doing something, so that people no longer want to do it
senses.zh: 取消激励：消除做某事的优势，使人们不再希望这样做

examples.zh: 更高的税收会抑制工作积极性吗？

examples.zh: 政府发起了一场政治宣传和释放假消息的运动。

examples.zh: 你为什么那么讨厌他呢？

examples.en: She disliked her boss intensely.
examples.zh: 她极其厌恶她的老板。

examples.en: There are very few foods that I actively dislike.
examples.zh: 没有几样食物是我真正反感的。

examples.en: I dislike being away from my family.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢同家人分开。

examples.en: Much as she disliked going to funerals (= although she did not like it at all), she knew she had to be there.
examples.zh: 尽管她很不喜欢参加葬礼，但她知道她必须去。

examples.en: He disliked her staying away from home.
examples.zh: 他不愿意让她住在外面。

examples.zh: 他讨厌她在他母亲面前举止失当。

examples.zh: 他没有掩饰自己对上司的反感。

examples.zh: 他们几乎无法掩饰对彼此的厌恶。

examples.zh: 我喜欢什么，不喜欢什么，都对你说了。

synonyms.words: dislike ▪ can’t stand ▪ despise ▪ can’t bear ▪ loathe ▪ detest

intro.en: These words all mean to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含厌恶、讨厌、憎恶之义。

items.def: to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something. Although hate is generally a very strong verb, it is also commonly used in spoken or informal English to talk about people or things that you dislike in a less important way, for example a particular type of food:
items.zh: 尽管 hate 通常为语气很强的动词，但亦常用于口语或非正式英语中，谈论不太喜欢的人或物，如某种食物等

items.def: (rather formal) to not like somebody/​something. Dislike is a rather formal word; it is less formal, and more usual, to say that you don't like somebody/​something, especially in spoken English:
items.zh: dislike 为相当正式的用语，don’t like 则较非正式，而且较常用，尤其在英语口语中

items.def: (rather informal) used to emphasize that you really do not like somebody/​something:
items.zh: 强调不喜欢、受不了、不能容忍

examples.en: I can’t stand his brother.
examples.zh: 他弟弟让我受不了。

items.def: to dislike and have no respect for somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指鄙视、蔑视、看不起

examples.en: He despised himself for being so cowardly.
examples.zh: 他为自己如此怯懦而看不起自己。

items.def: used to say that you dislike something so much that you cannot accept or deal with it:
items.zh: 指无法承受、应付不了

examples.en: I can’t bear having cats in the house.
examples.zh: 家里有猫我可受不了。

items.def: to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They loathe each other.
examples.zh: 他们相互讨厌。

items.def: (rather formal) to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They absolutely detest each other.
examples.zh: 他们完全是相互憎恨。

senses.def: the act of putting a bone out of its normal position in a joint

examples.zh: 肩关节脱臼

senses.def: a state in which the usual organization of something is disturbed

examples.zh: 这些政策可能会引起严重的经济和社会混乱。

examples.en: There is often a sense of dislocation in their music.
examples.zh: 他们的音乐中常常有一种错位感。

senses.def: to force or knock something out of its position

examples.en: The wind dislodged one or two tiles from the roof.
examples.zh: 大风从屋顶上刮下了一两片瓦来。

examples.zh: 叛乱分子至今未能把总统赶下台。

examples.zh: 他被指控对政府不忠。
