senses.zh: 不成功的；差劲的；不怎么样的

examples.en: The singer gave a dismal performance of some old songs.
examples.zh: 那歌手唱了几首老歌，唱得不怎么样。

examples.en: Their recent attempt to increase sales has been a dismal failure.
examples.zh: 他们最近努力提高销售量，全是白费劲。

examples.en: Last year's results were fairly dismal.
examples.zh: 去年的结果相当令人失望。

senses.def: without skill or success
senses.zh: 沮丧地：没有技巧或成功

examples.en: The party performed dismally in the election.
examples.zh: 该党在选举中表现惨淡。

examples.en: I tried not to laugh but failed dismally (= was completely unsuccessful).
examples.zh: 我想尽量忍着不笑，但根本忍不住。

senses.def: in a way that causes or shows the feeling of being sad

examples.en: She shook her head dismally.
examples.zh: 她沮丧地摇摇头。

senses.def: to take apart a machine or structure so that it is in separate pieces

examples.en: I had to dismantle the engine in order to repair it.
examples.zh: 我得把发动机拆开来修理。

examples.en: The steel mill was dismantled piece by piece.
examples.zh: 钢厂已经被一块块拆散了。

senses.def: to end an organization or a system gradually in an organized way

examples.en: The government was in the process of dismantling the state-owned industries.
examples.zh: 政府正在着手逐步取消国有企业。

senses.def: the process of ending something or taking it apart in an organized way
senses.zh: 拆解：以某种方式结束某件事或将其拆散的过程

examples.en: the dismantlement of the country's nuclear weapons programme
examples.zh: 废除该国的核武器计划

senses.def: a worried, sad feeling after you have received an unpleasant surprise

examples.en: She could not hide her dismay at the result.
examples.zh: 她无法掩饰自己对这一结果的惶恐不安。

examples.en: He looked at her in dismay.
examples.zh: 他诧异地看着她。

examples.en: I read of her resignation with some dismay.
examples.zh: 我看到她辞职的消息时有些沮丧。

examples.en: The news has been greeted with dismay by local business leaders.
examples.zh: 当地商界领袖听到这消息都感到很丧气。

examples.en: To her dismay, her name was not on the list.
examples.zh: 使她难过的是，名单上没有她的名字。

senses.def: to make somebody feel shocked and disappointed

examples.en: Their reaction dismayed him.
examples.zh: 他们的反应使他感到惊愕。

senses.def: to cut or tear the dead body of a person or an animal into pieces

examples.en: Police say the body had been dismembered.
examples.zh: 警方称尸体已被肢解。

senses.def: to divide a country, an organization, etc. into smaller parts

examples.en: The British railway network has gradually been dismembered.
examples.zh: 英国铁路网逐渐被肢解。

senses.def: the act of cutting or tearing the dead body of a person or an animal into pieces

examples.en: He was found guilty of the murder and dismemberment of two men.
examples.zh: 他被判犯有谋杀和肢解两名男子的罪名。

senses.def: the act or process of dividing a country, an organization, etc. into smaller parts

examples.en: This conflict led to the permanent dismemberment of the kingdom.
examples.zh: 这场冲突导致王国永久分裂。

senses.def: to decide that somebody/something is not important and not worth thinking or talking about
senses.zh: 不予考虑；摒弃；对…不屑一提

examples.en: to dismiss a suggestion/a claim/an idea
examples.zh: 驳回建议／要求／想法

examples.en: The criticisms were summarily dismissed by the government.
examples.zh: 这些批评立即遭到政府驳斥。

examples.en: Rob is quick to dismiss the notion that his trip was horrific.
examples.zh: 罗布很快就否认了他的旅行是可怕的。

examples.en: I think we can safely dismiss their objections.
examples.zh: 我认为我们对他们的异议完全可以不予理会。

examples.en: He dismissed the opinion polls as worthless.
examples.zh: 他认为民意测验毫无用处而不予理会。

examples.en: His supporters dismissed the allegations as politically motivated.
examples.zh: 他的支持者驳斥这些指控是出于政治动机。

examples.en: Vegans are no longer dismissed as cranks.
examples.zh: 素食者不再被视为有怪癖的人。

examples.en: The suggestion should not be dismissed out of hand (= without thinking about it).
examples.zh: 这建议不应当直接就被摒弃。

senses.def: to put thoughts or feelings out of your mind
senses.zh: 去除，消除，摒除（思想、感情等）

examples.en: Dismissing her fears, she climbed higher.
examples.zh: 她排除了恐惧，爬得更高了。

examples.en: He dismissed her from his mind.
examples.zh: 他挥去了对她的思念。

senses.def: to officially remove somebody from their job

examples.en: She claims she was unfairly dismissed from her post.
examples.zh: 她声称自己被无理免职。

senses.def: to send somebody away or allow them to leave
senses.zh: 让（某人）离开；把（某人）打发走；解散

examples.en: At 12 o'clock the class was dismissed.
examples.zh: 12 点下课了。

senses.def: to say that a trial or legal case should not continue, usually because there is not enough evidence

examples.en: The judge dismissed the case for lack of evidence.
examples.zh: 法官以证据不足驳回了此案。

examples.en: to dismiss an appeal/application
examples.zh: 驳回上诉/申请

examples.en: The court dismissed all the charges against her.
examples.zh: 法院驳回了对她的所有指控。

senses.def: to end the innings
senses.zh: 使（球员或球队）退场；使出局

senses.def: the act of dismissing somebody from their job; an example of this

examples.en: He still hopes to win his claim against unfair dismissal.
examples.zh: 他仍然希望赢得无理解雇的索赔。

examples.en: The dismissals followed the resignation of the chairman.
examples.zh: 董事长辞职后紧接着就是解雇人员。

senses.def: the failure to consider something as important
senses.zh: 不予考虑；不予理会；摒弃

examples.en: Her casual dismissal of the threats seemed irresponsible.
examples.zh: 她对这些威胁毫不在乎而不予理会，似乎很不负责任。

examples.en: Dismissal of the last piece of evidence as unreliable would severely affect our case.
examples.zh: 如果最后一项证据不可靠而被驳回，将会严重影响我们的案件。

senses.def: the act of not allowing a trial or legal case to continue, usually because there is not enough evidence

examples.en: the dismissal of the appeal
examples.zh: 驳回上诉

senses.def: the act of sending somebody away or allowing them to leave
the end of the innings
showing that you do not believe a person or thing to be important or worth considering

examples.en: a dismissive gesture/tone
examples.zh: 轻蔑的手势／语调

examples.en: She was always dismissive of other women in the office.
examples.zh: 她总是对办公室里的其他女性不屑一顾。

examples.en: Other critics were equally dismissive.
examples.zh: 其他评论家同样目中无人。

examples.en: She was very dismissive of his achievements.
examples.zh: 她对他的成就非常不屑。

senses.def: in a way that shows that you do not believe a person or thing to be important or worth considering

examples.en: to shrug/wave dismissively
examples.zh: 轻蔑地耸耸肩／挥挥手

senses.def: to get off a horse, bicycle or motorcycle

examples.en: She brought her horse to a halt and dismounted.
examples.zh: 她停下马，下了马。

examples.en: The cyclists were made to dismount and show their documents.
examples.zh: 骑自行车的人被要求下车并出示他们的证件。

senses.def: a move in which a gymnast
senses.zh: （体操运动员）跳下器械，结束一套动作

examples.en: She performed a backflip and finished with a perfect dismount.
examples.zh: 她完成了一个后空翻，并以完美的下马结束了比赛。

senses.def: the popular name for Walt Disney World™, the famous US amusement park
senses.zh: 迪士尼世界：沃尔特·迪士尼世界™（Walt Disney World™）的流行名称，这是美国佛罗里达州奥兰多附近的著名游乐园。它于1971年开放，尽管它具有类似的功能，例如迪士尼活人物，美国主街，边境和冒险乐园，但它比迪士尼乐园大得多。它的面积大约是曼哈顿的两倍，并且正在不断发展。它包括魔术王国，迪斯尼动物王国，EPCOT和迪斯尼好莱坞影城。

senses.def: the original US amusement park
senses.zh: 迪士尼乐园原为华特•迪斯尼于1955年在加利福尼亚州阿纳海姆开办的美国游乐园，现称迪士尼乐园。分为不同的“园区”，如探险世界、边域世界和明日世界等。周边还有酒店、餐馆和剧院，整个地区称为迪士尼乐园度假村。后来兴建的类似游乐园有1971年开业的迪士尼世界、东京迪士尼乐园（1983年）、巴黎迪士尼乐园（1992年）、香港迪士尼乐园（2005年）及上海迪士尼乐园（2016年）。

senses.def: the act of failing or refusing to obey

examples.en: His behaviour was seen as another act of disobedience.
examples.zh: 他的这一行为被视作又一次反叛。

examples.en: their disobedience to the king
examples.zh: 他们对国王的违抗

examples.en: their disobedience to authority
examples.zh: 他们对当局的违抗

senses.def: failing or refusing to obey
senses.zh: 不服从的；不顺从的；违抗的

examples.en: a disobedient child
examples.zh: 不听话的孩子

examples.en: I was very disobedient to my father.
examples.zh: 我对父亲很不顺从。

senses.def: to refuse to do what a person, a law, an order, etc. tells you to do; to refuse to obey

examples.en: He was punished for disobeying orders.
examples.zh: 他因违抗命令而受到惩罚。

examples.en: How dare you disobey me!
examples.zh: 你竟敢不听我的！

examples.en: She sighed deeply but dared not disobey.
examples.zh: 她深深地叹了口气，却又不敢违抗。

senses.def: deliberately not helpful

examples.en: a disobliging manner
examples.zh: 不合作的态度

senses.def: a condition or illness that causes problems with the way part of the body or brain works

examples.en: a blood/bowel disorder
examples.zh: 血液病；闹肚子

examples.en: He was diagnosed with an anxiety disorder.
examples.zh: 他被诊断患有焦虑症。

examples.en: This is a rare disorder of the liver.
examples.zh: 这是一种罕见的肝功能紊乱。

examples.en: help for people with alcohol use disorder
examples.zh: 为酒精使用障碍患者提供帮助

senses.def: an untidy state; a lack of order or organization

examples.en: The room was in a state of disorder.
examples.zh: 房间凌乱不堪。

examples.en: His financial affairs were in complete disorder.
examples.zh: 他的财务完全是一笔糊涂账。

examples.en: Everyone began shouting at once and the meeting broke up in disorder.
examples.zh: 大家一下子全都喊叫起来，会议秩序大乱而被迫中断。

senses.def: violent behaviour of large groups of people

examples.en: an outbreak of rioting and public disorder
examples.zh: 暴乱和公众骚乱的爆发

examples.en: Twenty people were arrested after a night of civil disorder.
examples.zh: 一夜的内乱后，二十人被捕。

synonyms.words: illness ▪ disorder ▪ infection ▪ condition ▪ ailment ▪ bug

intro.en: These are all words for a medical problem.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示健康问题。

items.def: a medical problem affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection:
items.zh: 常指人、动植物感染的病、疾病

examples.en: He suffers from a rare blood disease.
examples.zh: 他患有一种罕见的血液病。

items.def: a medical problem, or a period of suffering from one:
items.zh: 指病、疾病或患病期

examples.en: She died after a long illness.
examples.zh: 她久病不愈而亡。

items.def: (rather formal) a condition that causes problems with the way part of the body or brain works:
items.zh: 失调症（disorder）一种导致身体或大脑部分工作方式出现问题的病症：

examples.en: a rare disorder of the liver
examples.zh: 一种罕见的肝病

items.def: an illness that is caused by bacteria or a virus and that affects one part of the body:
items.zh: 指由细菌或病毒引起的身体某部位的感染或传染疾病

examples.en: a throat infection
examples.zh: 喉部感染

items.def: a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it:
items.zh: 指因不可治愈而长期患有的疾病

examples.en: a heart condition
examples.zh: 心脏病

items.def: (rather formal) an illness that is not very serious:
items.zh: 指轻病、小恙

examples.en: childhood ailments
examples.zh: 儿童期小病

items.def: (informal) an infectious illness that is usually fairly mild:
items.zh: 指轻微的传染病、小病

examples.en: a stomach bug
examples.zh: 胃病

senses.def: showing a lack of order or control

examples.en: disordered hair
examples.zh: 乱七八糟的头发

examples.en: a disordered state
examples.zh: 混乱状态

examples.en: He looked round the disordered kitchen.
examples.zh: 他环顾杂乱的厨房。

examples.en: It is likely that the universe started out in a chaotic and disordered state.
examples.zh: 宇宙初始的状态可能是混乱无序的。

senses.def: affected by a medical disorder

examples.en: Anorexia or other disordered eating over a long period can cause lasting damage.
examples.zh: 长期厌食或其他饮食失调会造成持久损害。

senses.def: showing lack of control; publicly noisy or violent
senses.zh: 难驾驭的；目无法纪的；骚乱的

examples.en: disorderly behaviour
examples.zh: 不守秩序的行为

examples.en: A disorderly crowd had gathered outside the embassy.
examples.zh: 一群不守秩序的人聚集在大使馆外面。

senses.def: untidy

examples.en: newspapers in a disorderly pile by the door
examples.zh: 门边乱七八糟的一堆报纸

senses.def: behaving in a noisy or violent way in a public place because you are drunk

examples.en: Police arrested him for being drunk and disorderly.
examples.zh: 他因醉酒妨害治安被警方逮捕。

senses.def: behaving in a noisy or violent way in a public place because you are drunk

examples.en: Police arrested him for being drunk and disorderly.
examples.zh: 他因醉酒妨害治安被警方逮捕。

senses.def: the crime of behaving in a noisy or violent way in a public place

examples.en: He has been charged with disorderly conduct.
examples.zh: 他被指控妨害治安。

senses.def: a brothel
the fact of being badly planned; a lack of ability to plan or organize well
senses.zh: 计划不周的；缺乏组织的；杂乱无章的

examples.en: The high level of disorganization at the hospital is inexcusable.
examples.zh: 医院的高度混乱是不可原谅的。

senses.def: badly planned; not able to plan or organize well
senses.zh: 计划不周的；缺乏组织的；杂乱无章的

examples.en: It was a hectic disorganized weekend.
examples.zh: 这个周末忙乱得一塌糊涂。

examples.en: She's so disorganized.
examples.zh: 她太缺乏条理了。

examples.en: Don’t expect him to get there on time—he’s completely disorganized.
examples.zh: 别指望他能准时到达那里——他完全没有条理。

senses.def: to make somebody unable to recognize where they are or where they should go

examples.en: The darkness had disoriented him.
examples.zh: 黑暗让他迷失了方向。

senses.def: to make somebody feel confused
senses.zh: 使迷惘；使不知所措；使无所适从

examples.en: Ex-soldiers can be disoriented by the transition to civilian life.
examples.zh: 退伍军人可能会因过渡到平民生活而迷失方向。

senses.def: to make somebody unable to recognize where they are or where they should go

examples.en: The darkness had disorientated him.
examples.zh: 黑暗使他迷失了方向。

senses.def: to make somebody feel confused
senses.zh: 使迷惘；使不知所措；使无所适从

examples.en: Ex-soldiers can be disorientated by the transition to civilian life.
examples.zh: 退伍军人转而去过平民生活可能会感到茫然。

senses.def: a feeling of not being able to recognize where you are or where you should go

examples.en: At the top of the hill I had a brief moment of disorientation.
examples.zh: 在山顶上，我有短暂的迷失方向的时刻。

senses.def: a feeling of being confused or not able to think clearly
senses.zh: 迷失方向：感到困惑或无法清晰思考的感觉

examples.en: She went through a period of shock and disorientation following her husband's death.
examples.zh: 丈夫去世后，她经历了一段震惊和迷失方向的时期。

senses.def: to decide that you no longer want to be connected with or responsible for somebody/something
senses.zh: 与…断绝关系；否认对…的责任

examples.en: Her family disowned her for marrying him.
examples.zh: 她的家人因为她嫁给了他而与她断绝关系。

examples.en: Later he publicly disowned the rebellion.
examples.zh: 后来，他公开否认对叛乱负责。

examples.en: They have never disowned their humble roots.
examples.zh: 他们从未否认自己卑微的出身。

senses.def: to suggest that somebody/something is not important or valuable

examples.en: I don't mean to disparage your achievements.
examples.zh: 我并不想贬低你的成就。

senses.def: the act of suggesting that somebody/something is not important or valuable

examples.en: I use the word without disparagement.
examples.zh: 我使用这个词并没有贬义。

senses.def: in a way that suggests that somebody/something is not important or valuable

examples.en: He spoke disparagingly of his colleagues.
examples.zh: 他言辞之中很是看不起同事。

senses.def: made up of parts or people that are very different from each other
senses.zh: 由不同的人（或事物）组成的

examples.en: a disparate group of individuals
examples.zh: 三教九流的一帮人

senses.def: so different from each other that they cannot be compared or cannot work together
senses.zh: 迥然不同的；无法比较的；不相干的

examples.en: a critical study that aims to cover such disparate forms as Anglo-Saxon poetry and the modern novel.
examples.zh: 旨在涵盖盎格鲁撒克逊诗歌和现代小说等不同形式的批判性研究。

senses.def: a difference, especially one connected with unfair treatment
senses.zh: （尤指因不公正对待引起的）不同，不等，差异，悬殊

examples.en: The wide disparity between rich and poor was highlighted.
examples.zh: 特别强调了贫富差距悬殊的问题。

examples.en: growing regional disparities in economic prosperity
examples.zh: 经济繁荣的地区差距日益扩大

examples.en: There are growing regional disparities in economic prosperity.
examples.zh: 在经济繁荣方面，区域差别越来越大。

senses.def: not influenced by emotion
senses.zh: 不感情用事的；冷静的；不带偏见的

examples.en: taking a calm, dispassionate view of the situation
examples.zh: 以冷静、客观公正的观点看待形势

examples.en: a dispassionate observer
examples.zh: 冷静的旁观者

senses.def: in a way that is not influenced by emotion
senses.zh: 不动感情的；冷静的；不带偏见的

examples.en: The case needs to be examined dispassionately at a public inquiry.
examples.zh: 该案需要在公开调查中冷静地审查。

senses.def: to send somebody/something somewhere, especially for a special purpose

examples.en: Troops have been dispatched to the area.
examples.zh: 部队已派往那个地区。

examples.en: A courier was dispatched to collect the documents.
examples.zh: 已派快递员去取文件。

senses.def: to send a letter, package or message somewhere
senses.zh: 发出，发送（邮件、包裹、信息）

examples.en: Goods are dispatched within 24 hours of your order reaching us.
examples.zh: 订单到达我方 24 小时内发货。

examples.en: Weir dispatched 50 messages back to base.
examples.zh: 威尔向基地发送了 50 条消息。

senses.def: to deal or finish with somebody/something quickly and completely
senses.zh: 迅速处理；迅速办妥；迅速完成

examples.en: He dispatched the younger player in straight sets.
examples.zh: 他连续几盘迅速击败了那位比他年轻的选手。

senses.def: to kill a person or an animal
the act of sending somebody/something somewhere

examples.en: More food supplies are ready for immediate dispatch.
examples.zh: 更多的食品供应已备妥即刻发运。

senses.def: a message or report sent quickly from one military officer to another or between government officials
senses.zh: （军事人员或政府官员之间的）急件，快信

examples.en: The latest dispatch was held up for three hours at the border.
examples.zh: 最新的派遣在边境滞留了三个小时。

examples.en: He was mentioned in dispatches (= for brave acts in war).
examples.zh: 他在电报中被提及（=战争中的勇敢行为）。

senses.def: a report sent to a newspaper by a journalist who is working in a foreign country
senses.zh: （驻外国记者发给报社的）新闻报道，电讯

examples.en: dispatches from the war zone
examples.zh: 从战区发来的报道

senses.def: quickly and efficiently

examples.en: He carries out his duties with efficiency and dispatch.
examples.zh: 他高效而迅速地履行职责。

senses.def: quickly and efficiently

examples.en: He carries out his duties with efficiency and dispatch.
examples.zh: 他高效而迅速地履行职责。

senses.def: a container for carrying official documents
a box on a table in the centre of the House of Commons in the British parliament, which ministers stand next to when they speak
senses.zh: 下议院案头文箱（置于英国下议院中央的桌子上，大臣站在桌边发言）

senses.def: a person whose job is to carry messages or packages by motorcycle
a person whose job is to send vehicles to where they are needed

examples.en: an Emergency Medical Dispatcher
examples.zh: 紧急医疗调度员

senses.def: to make something, especially a feeling or belief, go away or disappear
senses.zh: 驱散，消除（尤指感觉或信仰）

examples.en: His speech dispelled any fears about his health.
examples.zh: 他的发言消除了人们对他身体健康的担心。

senses.def: not necessary; that can be got rid of
senses.zh: 不必要；可有可无；不重要

examples.en: They looked on music and art lessons as dispensable.
examples.zh: 他们认为音乐课和美术课是可有可无的。

senses.def: a place in a hospital, shop, etc. where medicines are prepared for patients
a place where patients are treated, especially one run by a charity
senses.zh: （尤指慈善机构的）医务室，诊所

senses.def: special permission to do something that is not usually allowed or legal

examples.en: She needed a special dispensation to remarry.
examples.zh: 她需要得到特准才能再婚。

examples.en: The sport's ruling body gave him dispensation to compete in national competitions.
examples.zh: 体育运动管理机构特许他参加全国性的体育比赛。

senses.def: the act or process of providing something, especially by somebody in authority

examples.en: the dispensation of justice
examples.zh: 执法

senses.def: a political or religious system that operates in a country at a particular time
senses.zh: （某一国家某一时期的政治、宗教）制度

senses.def: to give out something to people

examples.en: The machine dispenses a range of drinks and snacks.
examples.zh: 这台机器发售各种饮料和小吃。

examples.en: He dispensed hospitality lavishly in an effort to win votes.
examples.zh: 他慷慨地款待以赢得选票。

senses.def: to provide something, especially a service, for people

examples.en: The organization dispenses free healthcare to those who need it.
examples.zh: 该组织向有需要的人提供免费医疗服务。

examples.en: to dispense justice/advice
examples.zh: 执法；给予忠告

senses.def: to prepare medicine and give it to people, as a job

examples.en: A pharmacist will never dispense a prescription unless they know it is genuine.
examples.zh: 除非药剂师知道处方是真的，否则他们绝不会开出处方。

examples.en: to dispense medicine
examples.zh: 发药

examples.en: The ethanol should be available from any dispensing chemist.
examples.zh: 乙醇应该可以从任何配药化学家处获得。

senses.def: to stop using somebody/something because you no longer need them or it

examples.en: Debit cards dispense with the need for cash altogether.
examples.zh: 有借记卡就完全不需要用现金了。

examples.en: I think we can dispense with the formalities (= speak openly and naturally to each other).
examples.zh: 我想我们就免去客套吧。

senses.def: a machine or container holding money, drinks, paper towels, etc. that you can obtain quickly, for example by pulling a handle or pressing buttons
senses.zh: 自动取款机；自动售货机；自动取物器

examples.en: a soap dispenser
examples.zh: 皂液瓶

senses.def: a person who provides something for people

examples.en: He saw himself as a dispenser of justice.
examples.zh: 他认为自己是正义的使者。

senses.def: a person who prepares medicines in a dispensary

examples.en: drug prescribers and dispensers
examples.zh: 药物处方者和配药者

senses.def: a person whose job is to prepare and sell medicines, and who works in a shop
a person whose job is to make and supply glasses, but who does not test people's eyes
the process of sending somebody/something in different directions; the process of spreading something over a wide area

examples.en: police trained in crowd dispersal
examples.zh: 在疏散人群方面受过训练的警察

examples.en: the dispersal of seeds
examples.zh: 种子的传播

senses.def: to move apart and go away in different directions; to make somebody/something do this

examples.en: The fog began to disperse.
examples.zh: 雾开始散了。

examples.en: The crowd dispersed quickly.
examples.zh: 人群很快便散开了。

examples.en: Police dispersed the protesters with tear gas.
examples.zh: 警察用催泪瓦斯驱散了抗议者。

senses.def: to spread or to make something spread over a wide area

examples.en: The seeds are dispersed by the wind.
examples.zh: 这些种子由风传播。

senses.def: the process by which people or things are spread over a wide area

examples.en: population dispersion
examples.zh: 人口疏散

examples.en: the dispersion of light
examples.zh: 光的散射

senses.def: having no hope or enthusiasm
senses.zh: 气馁的；垂头丧气的；心灰意懒的

examples.en: She looked tired and dispirited.
examples.zh: 她显得疲倦而且神情沮丧。

senses.def: making somebody lose their hope or enthusiasm
senses.zh: 令人沮丧的；使人气馁的

examples.en: a dispiriting experience/failure
examples.zh: 令人沮丧的经历／失败

senses.def: in a way that causes somebody to lose hope or enthusiasm

examples.en: a dispiritingly dull and predictable movie
examples.zh: 一部令人沮丧、乏味且可预测的电影

examples.en: Dispiritingly, nothing seems to have changed since I was last here.
examples.zh: 令人沮丧的是，自从我上次来这里以来，一切似乎都没有改变。

senses.def: to take the place of somebody/something

examples.en: Gradually factory workers have been displaced by machines.
examples.zh: 工厂的工人已逐渐被机器取代。

senses.def: to force people to move away from their home to another place

examples.en: Around 10 000 people have been displaced by the fighting.
examples.zh: 大约 1 万人因战争而背井离乡。

examples.en: If the dam is built it will displace 100 000 people.
examples.zh: 如果大坝建成，将导致10万人口流离失所。

senses.def: to move something from its usual position

examples.en: Check for roof tiles that have been displaced by the wind.
examples.zh: 检查一下屋顶上是否有瓦被风刮得挪了位。

senses.def: to remove somebody from a job or position

examples.en: displaced workers
examples.zh: 辞退的工人

senses.def: to take the place of an amount of liquid when put or floating in it, used as a way of measuring size

examples.en: The ship displaces 58 000 tonnes.
examples.zh: 这艘船的排水量是 5.8 万吨。

senses.def: a person who has been forced to leave their country or home, because of war, a natural disaster, etc.
the act of forcing somebody/something away from their home or position
senses.zh: 迫使流亡；迫使迁移；移位

examples.en: the largest displacement of civilian population since World War Two
examples.zh: 自第二次世界大战以来最大规模的平民迁移

senses.def: the amount of a liquid moved out of place by something floating or put in it, especially a ship floating in water

examples.en: a ship with a displacement of 10 000 tonnes
examples.zh: 排水量为 1 万吨的船

senses.def: things that you do in order to avoid doing what you are supposed to be doing
behaviour in animals or humans that does not seem to be useful in the situation in which it is performed, resulting from the presence of two opposing desires that cannot be resolved
senses.zh: 替换活动，移代活动（人或动物由于对立的驱力而表现出不相宜的行为）

senses.def: a unit of measure for the amount of water displaced
senses.zh: （船舶的）排水吨（相当于 1 吨）

senses.def: to put something in a place where people can see it easily; to show something to people

examples.en: The exhibition gives local artists an opportunity to display their work.
examples.zh: 这次展览为当地艺术家提供了展示自己作品的机会。

examples.en: His football trophies were prominently displayed in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 他的足球奖杯陈列在厨房里，很显眼。

examples.en: She displayed her bruises for all to see.
examples.zh: 她将自己身上青一块紫一块的伤痕露出来给大家看。

examples.en: She proudly displayed her certificate to her parents.
examples.zh: 她自豪地向父母展示了她获得的证书。

senses.def: to show a quality, feeling, skill or type of behaviour; to show signs of something
senses.zh: 显示，显露，表现（特性、情感、技能、行为等）

examples.en: I have rarely seen her display any sign of emotion.
examples.zh: 我难得见到她将喜怒形于色。

examples.en: He displays amazing skill with a golf club.
examples.zh: 他展示了惊人的高尔夫球杆技巧。

examples.en: The supporting cast displays real acting talent.
examples.zh: 配角们展现了真正的表演天赋。

examples.en: These statistics display a definite trend.
examples.zh: 这些统计数据表现出一种明显的趋势。

examples.en: Many animals in stressful conditions display this behaviour.
examples.zh: 许多处于压力条件下的动物都会表现出这种行为。

examples.en: From 1811 until his death in 1820, George III displayed symptoms of insanity.
examples.zh: 从 1811 年到 1820 年去世，乔治三世都表现出了精神错乱的症状。

senses.def: to show information

examples.en: Giant screens displayed images of cheering crowds.
examples.zh: 大屏幕上显示的是欢呼人群的画面。

examples.en: ways of displaying information on screen
examples.zh: 在屏幕上显示信息的方式

senses.def: to show a special pattern of behaviour that is intended to attract a female bird or animal
an arrangement of things in a public place to inform or entertain people or advertise something for sale

examples.en: a beautiful floral display
examples.zh: 美丽的花卉展览

examples.en: The window display changes once a month.
examples.zh: 橱窗展示品每月更换一次。

examples.en: a display of photographs
examples.zh: 照片展示

examples.en: a display window/stand/board
examples.zh: 展示窗/展台/展板

senses.def: an act of performing a skill or of showing something happening, in order to entertain

examples.en: They put on a spectacular firework display.
examples.zh: 他们举行了场面壮观的烟花燃放。

examples.en: The team produced an impressive display.
examples.zh: 该团队做出了令人印象深刻的展示。

examples.en: We watched a stunning display of aerobatics.
examples.zh: 我们观看了令人惊叹的特技飞行表演。

examples.en: They gave a dazzling display of football and deserved their victory.
examples.zh: 他们展现了令人眼花缭乱的足球表现，理应获得胜利。

senses.def: an occasion when you show a particular quality, feeling or ability by the way that you behave
senses.zh: （特性、情感或能力的）显示，表现，表露

examples.en: a display of affection/emotion/skill
examples.zh: 爱／情感的流露；才能的展示

examples.en: an ostentatious display of wealth
examples.zh: 炫富

examples.en: an impressive display of strength and courage
examples.zh: 令人印象深刻的力量和勇气的展示

senses.def: the words, pictures, etc. shown on a computer screen; the process of showing words, pictures, etc. on a computer screen

examples.en: a high-resolution colour display
examples.zh: 高分辨率彩色显示

examples.en: the processing and display of high volumes of information
examples.zh: 大量信息的处理和显示

senses.def: an electronic device for presenting words, pictures, etc.

examples.en: The colour display now costs £400.
examples.zh: 彩色显示器现在的价格是 400 英镑。

senses.def: a special pattern of behaviour by male birds and animals of some species that is intended to attract a female bird or animal

examples.en: Males perform courtship displays to attract mates.
examples.zh: 雄性进行求偶炫耀以吸引配偶。

examples.en: The male performs a magnificent courtship display.
examples.zh: 雄性展示了出色的求偶炫耀行为。

senses.def: put in a place where people can look at it

examples.en: Designs for the new sports hall are on display in the library.
examples.zh: 新体育馆的设计图展示在图书馆里。

examples.en: to put something on temporary/permanent display
examples.zh: 临时／长期展出某物

senses.def: put in a place where people can look at it

examples.en: Designs for the new sports hall are on display in the library.
examples.zh: 新体育馆的设计图展示在图书馆里。

examples.en: to put something on temporary/permanent display
examples.zh: 临时／长期展出某物

senses.def: a box in a shop for displaying goods, especially goods whose prices have been reduced
senses.zh: （商店）陈列柜；（尤指）减价货品柜

senses.def: a cupboard made or partly made of glass, for displaying items in a shop, museum, etc.

examples.en: She asked to try on a necklace that was in the display case.
examples.zh: 她要求试戴展示柜里的一条项链。

senses.def: to make somebody feel upset, annoyed or not satisfied

examples.en: The tone of the letter displeased her.
examples.zh: 来信的语气使她不快。

senses.def: the feeling of being upset and annoyed

examples.en: She made no attempt to hide her displeasure at the prospect.
examples.zh: 她没有掩饰自己对前景并不乐观。

examples.en: The incident has heightened public displeasure with the authorities.
examples.zh: 这一事件加剧了公众对当局的不满。

senses.def: to enjoy yourself by doing something active
the fact that something is intended to be thrown away after use or after a short time
senses.zh: 一次性性：打算在使用后或短时间后丢弃

examples.en: the disposability of modern appliances
examples.zh: 现代电器的一次性使用

senses.def: the fact of being not essential or not serious
senses.zh: 一次性性：不是必需的或不严重

examples.en: I love these shows but they have a kind of disposability.
examples.zh: 我喜欢这些节目，但它们有一种一次性的性质。

senses.def: the fact that something is available

examples.en: An extension of the employment depends on the disposability of funding.
examples.zh: 就业的延长取决于资金的可支配性。

senses.def: made to be thrown away after use
senses.zh: 用后即丢弃的；一次性的

examples.en: disposable gloves/razors
examples.zh: 一次性手套／剃刀

examples.en: disposable nappies
examples.zh: 一次性尿布

examples.en: disposable diapers
examples.zh: 一次性尿布

senses.def: (of people or ideas) that you can easily stop employing or thinking about
senses.zh: (指人或者想法)你可以很容易地停止雇佣或者思考

examples.en: It is completely wrong for corporations to view workers as disposable.
examples.zh: 企业将员工视为可抛弃的人是完全错误的。

senses.def: available for use
senses.zh: 可动用的；可自由支配的

examples.en: disposable assets/capital/resources
examples.zh: 可支配资产／资本／资源

examples.en: a person’s disposable income (= money they are free to spend after paying taxes, etc.)
examples.zh: 个人可支配收入

senses.def: items such as nappies
senses.zh: 用后即丢弃的物品，一次性物品（如尿布、隐形眼镜片）

senses.def: the act of getting rid of something

examples.en: The council is responsible for waste disposal and street cleaning.
examples.zh: 市政局负责垃圾处理和街道清洁。

examples.en: sewage disposal systems
examples.zh: 污水处理系统

examples.en: the problems of the ultimate disposal of nuclear waste
examples.zh: 核废料最终处理的问题

senses.def: the sale of part of a business, property, etc.

examples.en: The next step is to think about disposal of your assets.
examples.zh: 下一步是考虑处置您的资产。

senses.def: a machine connected to the waste pipe of a kitchen sink
senses.zh: 食物垃圾处理器（安装于厨房水槽下方，可粉碎厨余垃圾）

senses.def: available for use as you prefer/somebody prefers
senses.zh: 任某人安排；供某人任意使用；由某人自行支配

examples.en: He will have a car at his disposal for the whole month.
examples.zh: 他将有一辆汽车归他使用一个月。

examples.en: Well, I'm at your disposal (= I am ready to help you in any way I can).
examples.zh: 好吧，我听候你的吩咐。

senses.def: available for use as you prefer/somebody prefers
senses.zh: 任某人安排；供某人任意使用；由某人自行支配

examples.en: He will have a car at his disposal for the whole month.
examples.zh: 他将有一辆汽车归他使用一个月。

examples.en: Well, I'm at your disposal (= I am ready to help you in any way I can).
examples.zh: 好吧，我听候你的吩咐。

senses.def: to arrange things or people in a particular way or position

examples.en: The visitors disposed themselves in a circle round the statue.
examples.zh: 参观者围着雕像围成一圈。

senses.def: to make somebody want to behave in a particular way
senses.zh: 使倾向于；使有意于；使易于

examples.en: a drug that disposes the patient towards sleep
examples.zh: 使病人想睡觉的药

examples.en: a drug that disposes the patient to sleep
examples.zh: 一种使病人入睡的药物

senses.def: to get rid of somebody/something that you do not want or cannot keep

examples.en: the difficulties of disposing of nuclear waste
examples.zh: 处理核废料的困难

examples.en: to dispose of stolen property
examples.zh: 销赃

examples.en: Radioactive waste must be disposed of safely.
examples.zh: 放射性废物必须安全处置。

senses.def: to deal with a problem, question or threat successfully

examples.en: That seems to have disposed of most of their arguments.
examples.zh: 这样就似乎把他们的大部分论点都驳倒了。

senses.def: to defeat or kill somebody

examples.en: It took her a mere 20 minutes to dispose of her opponent.
examples.zh: 她仅用了 20 分钟就击败了对手。

senses.def: the natural qualities of a person’s character

examples.en: to have a cheerful disposition
examples.zh: 性情开朗

examples.en: people of a nervous disposition
examples.zh: 神经质的人

senses.def: a quality of tending to behave in a particular way

examples.en: to have/show a disposition towards violence
examples.zh: 有／表现出暴力倾向

examples.en: Do people have a natural disposition to be good?
examples.zh: 人性本善吗？

senses.def: the way something is placed or arranged
a formal act of giving property or money to somebody
to take somebody’s property, land or house away from them
senses.zh: 剥夺，夺去（某人的财产、土地、房屋）

senses.def: the act of taking somebody's property or land away from them
senses.zh: 剥夺，夺去（某人的财产、土地、房屋）

examples.en: These people suffered colonial conquest and dispossession.
examples.zh: 这些人民遭受了殖民征服和剥夺。

senses.def: the state of two things not being at an equally high or low level; an example of this
senses.zh: 不相称；不均衡；不成比例；不相称（或不均衡、不成比例）的东西

examples.en: the disproportion between the extra responsibilities and the small salary increase
examples.zh: 额外的责任与小幅增加的薪金之间的不相称

examples.en: a profession with a high disproportion of male to female employees
examples.zh: 男女雇员比例严重失调的职业

senses.def: too large or too small when compared with something else
senses.zh: 不成比例的；不相称的；太大（或太小）的

examples.en: The area contains a disproportionate number of young middle-class families.
examples.zh: 这一区年轻的中产阶级家庭特别多。

senses.def: in a way that is too large or too small when compared with something else
senses.zh: 以一种与其他事物相比过大或过小的方式

examples.en: The lower-paid spend a disproportionately large amount of their earnings on food.
examples.zh: 低薪者把收入的很大部分花在购买食物上。

senses.def: to show that something is wrong or false

examples.en: The theory has now been disproved.
examples.zh: 这一理论现已证明是错误的。

senses.def: that can or should be questioned or argued about
senses.zh: 可质疑的；有争辩余地的；可商榷的

senses.def: a discussion about something that people cannot agree on
an argument between two people, groups or countries; discussion about a subject on which people disagree

examples.en: industrial/pay disputes
examples.zh: 劳资／工资纠纷

examples.en: a dispute between the two countries about the border
examples.zh: 两国间的边界争端

examples.en: the latest dispute over fishing rights
examples.zh: 最近关于捕鱼权的争端

examples.en: The union is in dispute with management over working hours.
examples.zh: 工会与资方在工时问题上发生纠纷。

examples.en: The cause of the accident was still in dispute (= being argued about).
examples.zh: 事故的原因仍在争议之中。

examples.en: These are not the issues under dispute.
examples.zh: 这些不是有争议的问题。

examples.en: The matter was settled beyond dispute by the court judgment (= it could no longer be argued about).
examples.zh: 此问题已由法庭判决，不容争辩。

examples.en: His theories are open to dispute (= can be disagreed with).
examples.zh: 他的理论值得商榷。

senses.def: to question whether something is true or legally or officially acceptable
senses.zh: 质疑（某事是否属实、合法或应该接受）

examples.en: These figures have been disputed.
examples.zh: 有人对这些数字提出了质疑。

examples.en: to dispute a decision/claim
examples.zh: 对某项决定／权利要求提出异议

examples.en: The family wanted to dispute the will.
examples.zh: 家属想对遗嘱提出质疑。

examples.en: No one is disputing that there is a problem.
examples.zh: 没有人否认现在有问题。

examples.en: It is disputed whether the law applies in this case.
examples.zh: 有人质疑这项法律是否适用于这个案例。

senses.def: to argue or disagree strongly with somebody about something, especially about who owns something

examples.en: I tried to dispute the bill with the waiter.
examples.zh: 我试图与服务员争论账单。

examples.en: The United Nations recognizes the area as a disputed territory.
examples.zh: 联合国承认该地区为有争议的领土。

examples.en: The issue remains hotly disputed.
examples.zh: 这个问题至今仍在激烈的辩论中。

examples.en: He taught and disputed with local poets.
examples.zh: 他教授当地的诗人并和他们进行讨论。

senses.def: to fight to get control of something or to win something

examples.en: On the last lap three runners were disputing the lead.
examples.zh: 在最后一圈，三名赛跑者在争夺领先地位。

senses.def: a situation in which somebody is stopped from doing something because they have broken a rule
senses.zh: （因犯规）取消资格（disqualification 的缩略式）

examples.en: The skier suffered two disqualifications in two separate events.
examples.zh: 该滑雪运动员在两次不同的比赛中两次被取消资格。

examples.en: Any form of cheating means automatic disqualification.
examples.zh: 如有任何形式的作弊将自动失去资格。

senses.def: a fact that makes somebody unsuitable for an activity or position
senses.zh: 失格：使某人不适合某项活动或职位

examples.en: Lack of integrity should be a disqualification for any high office.
examples.zh: 缺乏诚信应该成为任何高级职位的取消资格。

senses.def: to stop somebody from doing something because they have broken a rule
senses.zh: 因违规而取消（某人）的资格

examples.en: He was disqualified from the competition for cheating.
examples.zh: 他因作弊而被取消比赛资格。

examples.en: You could be disqualified from driving for up to three years.
examples.zh: 你可能会被取消驾驶资格达三年之久。

senses.def: to make somebody unsuitable for an activity or position

examples.en: A heart condition disqualified him for military service.
examples.zh: 心脏病使他不符合服兵役的条件。

senses.def: feelings of worry and unhappiness about something

examples.en: There is considerable public disquiet about the safety of the new trains.
examples.zh: 公众对新型列车的安全深感忧虑。

senses.def: causing worry and unhappiness
senses.zh: 令人不安的；使人忧虑的

examples.en: Everything about her seemed perfect apart from one disquieting fact.
examples.zh: 除了一个令人不安的事实之外，她的一切似乎都很完美。

senses.def: a long complicated speech or written report on a particular subject
senses.zh: 专题演讲；专题论文；专题报告

senses.def: to not consider something; to treat something as unimportant

examples.en: The board completely disregarded my recommendations.
examples.zh: 董事会完全无视我的建议。

examples.en: Safety rules were disregarded.
examples.zh: 安全规定被忽视了。

examples.en: He totally disregarded all the advice he was given.
examples.zh: 他完全无视别人给他的所有建议。

examples.en: You cannot disregard the fact that heart disease is the biggest killer in the Western world.
examples.zh: 你不能忽视心脏病是西方世界最大杀手的事实。

senses.def: the act of treating somebody/something as not important and not caring about them/it

examples.en: their reckless disregard for human life
examples.zh: 他们对生命的无视

examples.en: She shows a total disregard for other people's feelings.
examples.zh: 她丝毫不顾及别人的感受。

senses.def: a building, road, etc. that is in a state of disrepair

examples.en: The station quickly fell into disrepair after it was closed.
examples.zh: 车站关闭后很快便破败不堪。

examples.en: The castle was in such a state of disrepair that they decided not to spend money on it.
examples.zh: 城堡已破败不堪，他们决定不在上面花钱了。

senses.def: that people do not respect or trust; considered to be bad, dangerous or dishonest
senses.zh: 名声不好的；不名誉的；不光彩的

examples.en: She spent the evening with her disreputable brother Stefan.
examples.zh: 她同声名狼藉的弟弟斯蒂芬一起度过了这个晚上。

examples.en: a disreputable area of the city
examples.zh: 城里名声不好的地方

examples.en: This approach remains intellectually disreputable even now.
examples.zh: 即使现在这种做法理智一点儿说也是不光彩的。

senses.def: the fact that somebody/something loses the respect of other people

examples.en: The players' behaviour on the field is likely to bring the game into disrepute.
examples.zh: 球员在赛场上的表现很可能使这场比赛臭名远扬。

senses.def: a lack of respect for somebody/something

examples.en: disrespect for the law/the dead
examples.zh: 藐视法律；对死者的不敬

examples.en: No disrespect intended, sir. It was just a joke.
examples.zh: 先生，绝无不敬之意。这不过是个玩笑而已。

senses.def: to speak about or treat somebody/something without respect

examples.en: They were accused of disrespecting the country's flag.
examples.zh: 他们被控亵渎国旗。

examples.en: He denied disrespecting the disaster victims.
examples.zh: 他否认不尊重灾难受害者。

examples.en: The teachers’ dedication has been ignored or disrespected.
examples.zh: 教师的奉献精神被忽视或不尊重。

examples.en: Don’t disrespect what I believe in.
examples.zh: 不要不尊重我的信仰。

senses.def: showing a lack of respect for somebody/something

examples.en: I did not mean to be disrespectful to the memory of those who died.
examples.zh: 我无意对死者的记忆不敬。

senses.def: in a way that shows a lack of respect for somebody/something

examples.en: You shouldn't speak disrespectfully about them.
examples.zh: 你不应该对他们说不尊重的话。

senses.def: to take off your or somebody else’s clothes; to take off clothes worn for an official ceremony
senses.zh: 脱去（某人）的衣服；脱衣服；脱去制服（或礼服）

examples.en: She went behind the screen to disrobe.
examples.zh: 她到屏风后面去换装。

senses.def: to make it difficult for something to continue in the normal way

examples.en: Demonstrators succeeded in disrupting the meeting.
examples.zh: 示威者成功地扰乱了会议。

examples.en: Bus services will be disrupted tomorrow because of the bridge closure.
examples.zh: 明日公共汽车服务将因大桥暂时封闭而受影响。

senses.def: to cause significant change in an industry or market by means of innovation
senses.zh: 改变行业传统运作方式，颠覆

examples.en: Our radical new printing technology is disrupting traditional manufacturing.
examples.zh: 我们革新性的印刷技术正在颠覆传统制造业。

senses.def: a situation in which it is difficult for something to continue in the normal way; the act of stopping something from continuing in the normal way

examples.en: We aim to help you move house with minimum disruption to yourself.
examples.zh: 我们的宗旨是助您轻松搬家，将搬家一事带给您的不便降到最低。

examples.en: disruptions to rail services
examples.zh: 对铁路交通的干扰

examples.en: The strike caused serious disruptions.
examples.zh: 罢工造成了严重的混乱。

senses.def: significant change to an industry or market due to innovation
senses.zh: （使用新方法或技术对传统行业或市场的）颠覆

examples.en: The banking industry is primed for major disruption.
examples.zh: 银行业已准备好迎接巨变。

senses.def: causing problems, noise, etc. so that something cannot continue normally
senses.zh: 引起混乱的；扰乱性的；破坏性的

examples.en: She had a disruptive influence on the rest of the class.
examples.zh: 她搅扰了班上其他学生。

senses.def: new and original, in a way that causes major changes to how something is done
senses.zh: 颠覆性的；创新而引起巨变的

examples.en: Printing in 3D is a disruptive technology which may transform manufacturing.
examples.zh: 3D 打印是一项颠覆性技术，可能会改变制造业。

examples.en: Innovative and disruptive companies are changing the service economy.
examples.zh: 创新和颠覆性公司正在改变服务经济。

senses.def: a company, person or form of technology that causes significant change in an industry or market by means of innovation
senses.zh: 颠覆者（能为商业格局带来巨变的新创公司）

examples.en: Small high-tech companies with low overheads have often been among the main disruptors in the industry.
examples.zh: 营运费用低的小型高科技公司往往是行业的主要颠覆者。

examples.en: In recent years mobile technology has acted as a disruptor of traditional business models.
examples.zh: 近年来，移动技术已经成为传统商业模式的颠覆者。

senses.def: a thing that significantly alters the structure or function of a gene
senses.zh: 干扰物（能干扰生物的基因或激素的结构或功能）

examples.en: There are a number of new drugs that show great potential as DNA disruptors in cancer cells.
examples.zh: 若干新药表现出在癌细胞中作为 DNA 干扰物的巨大潜力。

senses.def: to show a lack of respect for somebody, especially by saying offensive things to them
a feeling that you are not pleased or satisfied

examples.en: Many people have expressed their dissatisfaction with the arrangement.
examples.zh: 许多人表示对这一安排不满。

senses.def: something that causes you to feel dissatisfied

examples.en: The characters struggle with their own personal dissatisfactions and frustrations.
examples.zh: 角色们与自己的个人不满和挫折作斗争。

senses.def: not happy or satisfied with somebody/something
senses.zh: （对…）不满的，不高兴的，不满意的

examples.en: dissatisfied customers
examples.zh: 不满的顾客

examples.en: If you are dissatisfied with our service, please contact our customer service department.
examples.zh: 对于服务如有不满，请联系客户服务部。

senses.def: to cut up a dead person, animal or plant in order to study it

examples.en: The biology students had to dissect a rat.
examples.zh: 生物系的学生必须解剖一只老鼠。

examples.en: dissecting instruments
examples.zh: 解剖仪器

senses.def: to study something closely and/or discuss it in great detail
senses.zh: 仔细研究；详细评论；剖析

examples.en: Her latest novel was dissected by the critics.
examples.zh: 评论家对她最近出版的一部小说作了详细剖析。

senses.def: to divide something into smaller pieces, areas, etc.

examples.en: The city is dissected by a network of old canals.
examples.zh: 古老的运河网将这座城市分割开来。

senses.def: the act of cutting up a dead person, animal or plant in order to study it

examples.en: anatomical dissection
examples.zh: 解剖分析

senses.def: the act of studying something closely and/or discussing it in great detail
senses.zh: 仔细研究；详细评论；剖析

examples.en: Your enjoyment of a novel can suffer from too much analysis and dissection.
examples.zh: 看小说时剖析过度会减少阅读的乐趣。

senses.def: to hide your real feelings or intentions, often by pretending to have different ones
senses.zh: 掩盖，掩饰（真实感情或意图）

examples.en: She was a very honest person who was incapable of dissembling.
examples.zh: 她是一个非常诚实的人，不会伪装。

senses.def: a person who hides their real feelings or intentions, often by pretending to have different ones
senses.zh: 掩盖，掩饰（真实感情或意图）

examples.en: They're all liars and dissemblers.
examples.zh: 他们都是骗子和伪装者。

senses.def: to spread information, knowledge, etc. so that it reaches many people

examples.en: Their findings have been widely disseminated.
examples.zh: 他们的研究成果已经广为传播。

senses.def: the act of spreading information or knowledge so that it reaches many people

examples.en: the internet's role in the dissemination of knowledge
examples.zh: 互联网在知识传播中的作用

senses.def: disagreement
senses.zh: 意见分歧；（派性）纷争；不和

examples.en: These issues caused bitter dissension in the party.
examples.zh: 这些问题在党内引起了激烈的争论。

examples.en: dissension within the government
examples.zh: 政府内部的意见分歧

examples.en: dissensions between rival factions
examples.zh: 敌对派系之间的争端

senses.def: the fact of having or expressing opinions that are different from those that are officially accepted

examples.en: political/religious dissent
examples.zh: 政治观点／宗教信仰上的分歧

examples.en: Voices of dissent began to rise against the established authority in the 1950s and 1960s.
examples.zh: 20世纪50年代和1960年代，反对既定权威的反对声音开始兴起。

examples.en: Stability only exists in the country because dissent has been suppressed.
examples.zh: 只有当异议受到压制时，国家才会存在稳定。

senses.def: the offence of openly disagreeing with the referee

examples.en: He was sent off for dissent.
examples.zh: 他因不服裁判被罚下场。

senses.def: a judge’s statement giving reasons why they disagree with a decision made by the other judges in a court case
senses.zh: （诉讼案中某法官对其他法官判决的）异议，不同意见

senses.def: to have or express opinions that are different from those that are officially accepted

examples.en: Only two ministers dissented from the official view.
examples.zh: 只有两位部长与官方持不同的观点。

senses.def: a person who does not agree with opinions that are officially or generally accepted
senses.zh: （对官方或普遍认可的意见）持异议者，持不同意见者

examples.en: The dissenters at the meeting were shouted down.
examples.zh: 会议上的反对者被大声喊倒。

senses.def: a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree
senses.zh: 专题论文；（尤指）学位论文

examples.en: He wrote his Master's dissertation on rats.
examples.zh: 他的硕士论文写的是关于老鼠的问题。

examples.en: Students can either do a dissertation or take part in a practical project.
examples.zh: 学生可以做学位论文，也可以参加实践项目。

senses.def: to do something that harms somebody and the opinion that other people have of them

examples.en: The minister’s comments do teachers a great disservice.
examples.zh: 部长的评论对教师大为不利。

senses.def: the act of strongly disagreeing with and criticizing your government, especially in a country where this kind of action is dangerous
a person who strongly disagrees with and criticizes their government, especially in a country where this kind of action is dangerous

examples.en: political dissidents
examples.zh: 政治异见人士

examples.en: regimes that murder political opponents and imprison dissidents
examples.zh: 谋杀政治对手并监禁异见人士的政权

examples.en: Dissidents were often imprisoned by the security police.
examples.zh: 持不同政见者常被安全警察关进监狱。

senses.def: strongly disagreeing with and criticizing your government, especially in a country where this kind of action is dangerous

examples.en: the suppression of dissident views
examples.zh: 压制不同意见

senses.def: not the same
senses.zh: 不一样的；不同的；不相似的

examples.en: These wines are not dissimilar (= are similar).
examples.zh: 这些葡萄酒都差不多。

examples.en: The two languages are completely dissimilar from each other.
examples.zh: 这两种语言彼此完全不同。

senses.def: the fact of not being the same as somebody/something else; a feature that things or people have that makes them different from one another
senses.zh: 不相似：与某人不同的事实；事物或人拥有的一种功能，使它们彼此不同

examples.en: research on the dissimilarity of languages
examples.zh: 语言差异性研究

examples.en: It is easy to point out dissimilarities between the two cases.
examples.zh: 很容易指出这两个案例之间的不同之处。

senses.def: to hide your real feelings or intentions, often by pretending to have different ones
senses.zh: 掩盖，掩饰（真实感情或意图）

senses.def: the act of hiding your real feelings or intentions, often by pretending to have different ones
senses.zh: 掩盖，掩饰（真实感情或意图）

examples.en: He was capable of great dissimulation and hypocrisy.
examples.zh: 他擅于假装与伪善。

senses.def: to gradually become or make something become weaker until it disappears

examples.en: Eventually, his anger dissipated.
examples.zh: 他的愤怒终于平息了。

examples.en: Her laughter soon dissipated the tension in the air.
examples.zh: 她的笑声很快消除了紧张气氛。

senses.def: to waste something, such as time or money, especially by not planning the best way of using it
senses.zh: 挥霍，浪费，消磨（时间、金钱等）

examples.en: She was determined to achieve results and not to dissipate her energies.
examples.zh: 她决心取得成果，而不是浪费精力。

senses.def: the process of disappearing or of making something disappear

examples.en: the dissipation of energy in the form of heat
examples.zh: 以热量形式耗散的能量

senses.def: the act of wasting money or spending money until there is none left

examples.en: concerns about the dissipation of the country’s wealth
examples.zh: 对挥霍国家财富的忧虑

senses.def: behaviour that is fun but has a harmful effect on you
to say or do something to show that you are not connected with or do not support somebody/something; to make it clear that something is not connected with a particular plan, action, etc.
senses.zh: 否认同…有关系；声明不支持；表明无关

examples.en: He tried to dissociate himself from the party's more extreme views.
examples.zh: 他极力表明自己并不赞成该党较为偏激的观点。

examples.en: They were determined to dissociate the UN from any agreement to impose sanctions.
examples.zh: 他们决心阻止联合国同意实施制裁。

senses.def: to think of two people or things as separate and not connected with each other
senses.zh: 把…分开（或看作是无关联的）

examples.en: She tried to dissociate the two events in her mind.
examples.zh: 她试图从思想上将这两件事分开。

senses.def: the fact of being separate or not connected

examples.en: the dissociation of political and moral ideas
examples.zh: 政治观念与道德观念的分离

senses.def: the act of showing that you do not support or agree with something
senses.zh: 分离：表明您不支持或不同意某件事的行为

examples.en: Dissociation from Cabinet decisions by individual ministers is unacceptable.
examples.zh: 个别部长脱离内阁决定是不可接受的。

senses.def: a mental illness in which somebody feels uncertain about who they are and feels that they have more than one separate identity, each one having its own name, voice, memories, personality, etc.
senses.zh: 分离性身份识别障碍;分离性人格障碍

senses.def: enjoying immoral
senses.zh: 放纵的；放荡的；道德沦丧的

senses.def: the act of officially ending a marriage, a business agreement or a parliament; the act of breaking up an organization, etc.
senses.zh: （婚姻关系的）解除；（商业协议的）终止；（议会等组织的）解散

examples.en: The company was set up following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
examples.zh: 这家公司是在苏联解体之后成立的。

senses.def: the process in which something gradually disappears

examples.en: the dissolution of barriers of class and gender
examples.zh: 阶级和性别障碍的消除

senses.def: to mix with a liquid and become part of it

examples.en: Salt dissolves in water.
examples.zh: 盐溶解于水。

examples.en: Heat gently until the sugar dissolves.
examples.zh: 慢慢加热直到糖溶解为止。

examples.en: The aspirin hasn't dissolved completely yet.
examples.zh: 阿司匹林还没有完全溶解。

senses.def: to make a solid become part of a liquid

examples.en: Dissolve the tablet in water.
examples.zh: 把药片溶于水中。

senses.def: to officially end a marriage, business agreement or parliament
senses.zh: 解除（婚姻关系）；终止（商业协议）；解散（议会）

examples.en: Their marriage was dissolved in 2019.
examples.zh: 他们的婚姻于2019年解除。

examples.en: The election was announced and parliament was dissolved.
examples.zh: 宣布选举后，议会解散了。

senses.def: to disappear; to make something disappear

examples.en: When the ambulance had gone, the crowd dissolved.
examples.zh: 救护车离开后人群便散开了。

examples.en: The lights in the windows faded and the house dissolved into darkness again.
examples.zh: 窗户里的灯光暗了下去，房子再次陷入黑暗。

examples.en: His calm response dissolved her anger.
examples.zh: 他平静的回答化解了她的怒气。

senses.def: to suddenly start laughing, crying, etc.
senses.zh: 禁不住（笑起来或哭起来等）

examples.en: When the teacher looked up, the children dissolved into giggles.
examples.zh: 教师抬头看时，孩子们不禁咯咯地笑起来。

examples.en: Every time she heard his name, she dissolved into tears.
examples.zh: 每当听到他的名字时，她都禁不住泪流满面。

senses.def: to remove or destroy something, especially by a chemical process; to be destroyed in this way
senses.zh: （尤以化学手段）除去，毁掉；（被）破坏

examples.en: a new detergent that dissolves stains
examples.zh: 新型去污洗涤剂

examples.en: All the original calcium had dissolved away.
examples.zh: 所有原始钙都被破坏了。

examples.en: The limestone has simply dissolved away.
examples.zh: 石灰石就这么溶解掉了。

senses.def: a combination of musical notes that do not sound pleasant together
lack of agreement
not sounding pleasant together
senses.zh: 不协和的；不和谐的；刺耳的

examples.en: dissonant chords/notes/music
examples.zh: 不和谐和弦/音符/音乐

senses.def: not in agreement

examples.en: There were a few dissonant voices.
examples.zh: 现场响起了一些不和谐的声音。

examples.en: The first dissonant note of the debate came from the Opposition leader.
examples.zh: 辩论中第一个不和谐的声音来自反对党领袖。

senses.def: to persuade somebody not to do something

examples.en: I tried to dissuade him from giving up his job.
examples.zh: 我劝过他不要放弃自己的工作。

examples.en: They were going to set off in the fog, but were dissuaded.
examples.zh: 他们原打算在雾中出发，但被劝阻了。

examples.en: She made no attempt to dissuade him.
examples.zh: 她没有试图劝阻他。

senses.def: a stick that was used in the past for holding wool when it was spun
senses.zh: （旧时手工纺纱用的）纺纱杆，绕线杆

senses.def: female or relating to women

examples.en: ‘Thelma and Louise’ was a distaff buddy movie with a strong feminist agenda.
examples.zh: 《末路狂花》是一部带有强烈女权主义议程的员工电影。

senses.def: on the woman’s side of the family
on the woman’s side of the family
located away from the centre of the body or at the far end of something

examples.en: the distal end of the tibia
examples.zh: 胫骨远端

senses.def: the amount of space between two places or things

examples.en: a short/long distance
examples.zh: 短距离；长距离

examples.en: Paul has to drive very long distances as part of his job.
examples.zh: 保罗不得不长途驾车，这是他工作的一部分。

examples.en: to travel/cover a distance of 200 kilometres
examples.zh: 行走 200 公里的距离

examples.en: She walked the short distance to her apartment.
examples.zh: 她走了一小段路回到公寓。

examples.en: Once she was a safe distance from the shop, Gina stopped.
examples.zh: 当吉娜离开商店一段安全距离后，就停了下来。

examples.en: the distance of the earth from the sun
examples.zh: 太阳到地球的距离

examples.en: What’s the distance from New York City to Boston?
examples.zh: 纽约市离波士顿有多远？

examples.en: What’s the distance between New York City and Boston?
examples.zh: 纽约市离波士顿有多远？

examples.en: The wind carries pollen over considerable distances.
examples.zh: 风能把花粉带到相当远的地方。

examples.en: The beach is within walking distance of my house (= you can walk there easily).
examples.zh: 海滩离我家很近，走几步路就到了。

examples.en: The house is within easy commuting distance of town.
examples.zh: 这所房子距离城镇很近。

examples.en: In the US, distance is measured in miles.
examples.zh: 在美国，测量距离以英里作单位。

examples.en: Our parents live some distance away (= quite far away).
examples.zh: 我们的父母住的地方相当远。

examples.en: a distance (= long-distance) runner/swimmer
examples.zh: 长跑运动员/游泳运动员

senses.def: being far away in space or in time
senses.zh: （空间的）遥远；（时间的）久远，间隔

examples.en: Distance is no problem on the internet.
examples.zh: 在互联网上距离根本不是问题。

examples.en: They don't see their family because of geographical distance.
examples.zh: 由于地理距离的原因，他们见不到家人。

examples.en: The car put physical distance between people and their places of work.
examples.zh: 汽车拉开了人们与其工作地点之间的物理距离。

senses.def: a point that is a particular amount of space away from something else

examples.en: You'll never get the ball in from that distance.
examples.zh: 你绝不可能从那么远的地方把球投进去。

examples.en: The cat sat and watched us from a safe distance.
examples.zh: 那只猫待在安全距离之外瞅着我们。

examples.en: Visitors can only view the painting from a distance of three metres.
examples.zh: 参观者只能从 3 米远的地方欣赏这幅油画。

examples.en: She followed them at a discreet distance.
examples.zh: 她跟在他们的后面，谨慎地保持着距离。

examples.en: A digital camera was positioned at a distance of 1.5 metres from the subject.
examples.zh: 一台数码相机放置在离拍摄对象 1.5 米远的地方。

senses.def: a difference or lack of a connection between two things

examples.en: The distance between fashion and art remains as great as ever.
examples.zh: 时尚与艺术之间的差别之大依然如故。

examples.en: The government is keen to put some distance between itself and these events (= show that there is no connection between them).
examples.zh: 政府急于表示自身与这些事件无关。

examples.en: Sociologists must maintain critical distance from the ideas of society at any particular time.
examples.zh: 社会学家必须在任何特定时间与社会观念保持审慎距离。

examples.en: Eddie is, by some distance (= by a great amount), the funniest character in the show.
examples.zh: 埃迪显然是这个节目中最有趣的人物。

senses.def: a situation in which there is a lack of friendly feelings or of a close relationship between two people or groups of people

examples.en: The coldness and distance in her voice took me by surprise.
examples.zh: 她话语中透出的冷淡和疏远使我感到意外。

examples.en: There was a growing distance between the two sides of the family.
examples.zh: 两家人之间的距离越来越远。

examples.en: He worried about the increasing distance between his children and himself.
examples.zh: 他对自己与子女之间关系的日益疏远感到担忧。

examples.en: He felt a sense of distance from the others.
examples.zh: 他感到自己与其他人关系疏远。

senses.def: from a place or time that is not near; from far away
senses.zh: 离一段距离；从远处；遥远地；久远地

examples.en: She had loved him at a distance for years.
examples.zh: 她曾经暗恋他好多年。

senses.def: to continue playing in a competition or sports contest until the end

examples.en: Nobody thought he would last 15 rounds, but he went the full distance.
examples.zh: 谁都以为他坚持不到 15 个回合，可是他却打完了全场。

senses.def: far away but still able to be seen or heard

examples.en: We saw lights in the distance.
examples.zh: 我们看到了远处的点点灯光。

examples.en: Alice stood staring into the distance.
examples.zh: 艾丽斯站着凝视远方。

examples.en: Five miles of sand stretched away into the distance.
examples.zh: 五英里的沙子一直延伸到远处。

senses.def: to refuse to be friendly with somebody; to not let somebody be friendly towards you
senses.zh: 对…冷淡；同…疏远；与…保持一定距离

examples.en: The manager prefers to keep employees at a distance.
examples.zh: 经理更喜欢与员工保持距离。

senses.def: to make sure you are not too near somebody/something
to avoid getting too friendly or involved with a person, group, etc.
senses.zh: 疏远；避免（与…）亲近；避免介入

examples.en: She was warned to keep her distance from Charles if she didn't want to get hurt.
examples.zh: 有人告诫她说，如果不想受到伤害，就离查尔斯远一点。

senses.def: very close

examples.en: We came within touching distance of winning the cup.
examples.zh: 我们离赢得奖杯已经很近了。

examples.en: We live within spitting distance of the bus station.
examples.zh: 我们住的地方离公交车站很近。

senses.def: to become less involved or connected with somebody/something

examples.en: When he retired, he tried to distance himself from politics.
examples.zh: 退休后，他便尽量使自己置身于政治之外。

examples.en: The company has tried to distance itself from the remarks made by some of its employees.
examples.zh: 该公司试图与部分员工的言论保持距离。

examples.en: It's not always easy for nurses to distance themselves emotionally.
examples.zh: 对护士来说，使自己不动感情有时并不容易。

senses.def: to make somebody/something less involved or connected with somebody/something

examples.en: Her mother wished to distance her from the rough village children.
examples.zh: 她母亲希望她远离那些粗野的乡下孩子。

examples.en: These narrative techniques actually distance the reader from the story.
examples.zh: 这些叙事技巧实际上拉开了读者与故事的距离。

senses.def: from a place or time that is not near; from far away
senses.zh: 离一段距离；从远处；遥远地；久远地

examples.en: She had loved him at a distance for years.
examples.zh: 她曾经暗恋他好多年。

senses.def: to continue playing in a competition or sports contest until the end

examples.en: Nobody thought he would last 15 rounds, but he went the full distance.
examples.zh: 谁都以为他坚持不到 15 个回合，可是他却打完了全场。

senses.def: far away but still able to be seen or heard

examples.en: We saw lights in the distance.
examples.zh: 我们看到了远处的点点灯光。

examples.en: Alice stood staring into the distance.
examples.zh: 艾丽斯站着凝视远方。

examples.en: Five miles of sand stretched away into the distance.
examples.zh: 五英里的沙子一直延伸到远处。

senses.def: to refuse to be friendly with somebody; to not let somebody be friendly towards you
senses.zh: 对…冷淡；同…疏远；与…保持一定距离

examples.en: The manager prefers to keep employees at a distance.
examples.zh: 经理更喜欢与员工保持距离。

senses.def: to make sure you are not too near somebody/something
to avoid getting too friendly or involved with a person, group, etc.
senses.zh: 疏远；避免（与…）亲近；避免介入

examples.en: She was warned to keep her distance from Charles if she didn't want to get hurt.
examples.zh: 有人告诫她说，如果不想受到伤害，就离查尔斯远一点。

senses.def: very close

examples.en: We came within touching distance of winning the cup.
examples.zh: 我们离赢得奖杯已经很近了。

examples.en: We live within spitting distance of the bus station.
examples.zh: 我们住的地方离公交车站很近。

senses.def: a system of education in which people study at home with the help of special internet sites and send or email work to their teachers

examples.en: distance education courses
examples.zh: 远程教育课程

examples.en: Technology allows distance education to occur at all levels.
examples.zh: 科技使人们可以获得各种层次的远程教育。

senses.def: a system of education in which people study at home with the help of special internet sites and send or email work to their teachers

examples.en: a distance learning programme/package
examples.zh: 远程学习计划/套餐

examples.en: I got my degree through a distance learning programme.
examples.zh: 我通过远程学习计划获得了学位。

examples.en: The Open University offers a wide range of distance learning programmes.
examples.zh: 开放大学开设一系列远程学习课程。

senses.def: far away in space or time

examples.en: the distant sound of music
examples.zh: 远处的音乐声

examples.en: distant stars/planets
examples.zh: 遥远的恒星／行星

examples.en: The time we spent together is now a distant memory.
examples.zh: 我们一起度过的时光现已成为久远的记忆。

examples.en: The airport was about 20 kilometres distant.
examples.zh: 机场在大约 20 公里远的地方。

examples.en: a star 30 000 light years distant from the Earth
examples.zh: 离地球 3 万光年远的恒星

examples.en: Peace was just a distant hope (= not very likely).
examples.zh: 和平只是遥不可及的希望而已。

senses.def: not like something else

examples.en: Their life seemed utterly distant from his own.
examples.zh: 他们的生活与他自己的生活似乎完全不同。

examples.en: The medieval mind can seem impossibly distant.
examples.zh: 中世纪的思想似乎遥不可及。

senses.def: related to you but not closely

examples.en: a distant cousin/aunt/relative
examples.zh: 远房堂兄弟／姑母／亲戚

senses.def: not friendly; not wanting a close relationship with somebody
senses.zh: 不友好的；冷淡的；疏远的

examples.en: Pat sounded very cold and distant on the phone.
examples.zh: 从电话里听起来帕特非常冷淡和疏远。

examples.en: He became emotionally distant from his friends and family after the illness.
examples.zh: 患病后，他在情感上与朋友和家人变得疏远。

senses.def: not paying attention to something but thinking about something completely different
senses.zh: 心不在焉的；恍惚的；出神的

examples.en: There was a distant look in her eyes; her mind was obviously on something else.
examples.zh: 她眼神恍惚，显然心里在想着别的什么事儿。

examples.en: He seemed distant and distracted.
examples.zh: 他显得冷淡而心不在焉。

senses.def: a long time ago

examples.en: stories from the dim and distant past
examples.zh: 遥远过去的故事

examples.en: In the distant past this land was covered in forests.
examples.zh: 在遥远的过去，这片土地被森林覆盖。

senses.def: not a long time in the future but fairly soon

examples.en: I hope we’ll see each other again in the not too distant future.
examples.zh: 我希望我们能在不久的将来再次见面。

senses.def: a long time ago

examples.en: stories from the dim and distant past
examples.zh: 遥远过去的故事

examples.en: In the distant past this land was covered in forests.
examples.zh: 在遥远的过去，这片土地被森林覆盖。

items.idm: in the not too distant future

senses.def: not a long time in the future but fairly soon

examples.en: I hope we’ll see each other again in the not too distant future.
examples.zh: 我希望我们能在不久的将来再次见面。

senses.def: far away in space or time

examples.en: Somewhere, distantly, he could hear the sound of the sea.
examples.zh: 他能听到在远处某个地方的海浪声。

senses.def: not closely

examples.en: We're distantly related.
examples.zh: 我们是远亲。

examples.en: The way I speak only distantly resembles the way I write.
examples.zh: 我说话的方式与我写作的方式只是有些相似。

senses.def: in a way that does not show real emotion because you are thinking about something else
senses.zh: 遥远的：以一种不会表现出真实情感的方式，因为您正在思考其他事情

examples.en: Holly smiled distantly.
examples.zh: 霍利恍惚地笑了笑。

senses.def: a feeling that somebody/something is unpleasant or offensive

examples.en: He looked around the filthy room in distaste.
examples.zh: 他厌恶地环视着这肮脏的房间。

examples.en: a distaste for politics of any sort
examples.zh: 对任何形式的政治的反感

examples.en: She couldn't hide her distaste at having to sleep in such squalid conditions.
examples.zh: 她无法掩饰自己对不得不在如此肮脏的条件下睡觉的厌恶。

senses.def: unpleasant or offensive
senses.zh: 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的

examples.en: The bad language in the film was distasteful and unnecessary.
examples.zh: 电影中的脏话令人反感且没有必要。

senses.def: a disease of animals, especially dogs, that causes a high temperature and coughing
senses.zh: 瘟热（尤指狗等动物的传染病）

senses.def: a type of paint that is mixed with glue
senses.zh: 刷墙水粉；水浆涂料；水性墙漆

senses.def: to swell

examples.en: He tied a piece of cloth around his upper arm to impede circulation and distend the veins.
examples.zh: 他在上臂绑了一块布，以阻碍血液循环并扩张静脉。

senses.def: the fact of swelling

examples.en: distension of the stomach
examples.zh: 胃胀

senses.def: to make a liquid pure by heating it until it becomes a gas, then cooling it and collecting the drops of liquid that form

examples.en: to distil fresh water from seawater
examples.zh: 用蒸馏法从海水中提取淡水

examples.en: distilled water
examples.zh: 蒸馏水

senses.def: to make something such as a strong alcoholic drink in this way

examples.en: The factory distils and bottles whisky.
examples.zh: 这家工厂用蒸馏法酿造瓶装威士忌酒。

senses.def: to get the essential meaning or ideas from thoughts, information, experiences, etc.

examples.en: The notes I made on my travels were distilled into a book.
examples.zh: 我的旅行笔记精选汇编成了一本书。

senses.def: a substance that is formed by distilling
the process of distilling

examples.en: the distillation process
examples.zh: 蒸馏过程

senses.def: the process or result of getting the essential meaning, ideas or information from something

examples.en: The movie is a perfect distillation of adolescence.
examples.zh: 这部电影是青春期的完美升华。

senses.def: a person or company that produces spirits
senses.zh: （采用蒸馏法的）酿酒者，酿酒公司

senses.def: a factory where strong alcoholic drink is made by the process of distilling
easily or clearly heard, seen, felt, etc.
senses.zh: 清晰的；清楚的；明白的；明显的

examples.en: There was a distinct smell of gas.
examples.zh: 有一股明显的煤气味。

examples.en: His voice was quiet but every word was distinct.
examples.zh: 他说话声音不大，但字字清晰。

senses.def: clearly different or of a different kind
senses.zh: 截然不同的；有区别的；不同种类的

examples.en: The results of the survey fell into two distinct groups.
examples.zh: 调查结果分为截然不同的两组。

examples.en: Jamaican reggae music is quite distinct from North American jazz or blues.
examples.zh: 牙买加的雷鬼乐完全不同于北美的爵士乐或布鲁斯音乐。

examples.en: We are talking about rural areas, as distinct from major cities.
examples.zh: 我们现在谈论的是乡村，与大城市截然不同。

senses.def: used to emphasize that you think an idea or situation definitely exists and is important
senses.zh: 确定无疑的；确实的；确切的

examples.en: Being tall gave Tony a distinct advantage.
examples.zh: 托尼个子高是个明显的优势。

examples.en: I had the distinct impression I was being watched.
examples.zh: 我确实感到有人在监视我。

examples.en: A strike is now a distinct possibility.
examples.zh: 目前罢工确有可能发生。

senses.def: a clear difference or contrast especially between people or things that are similar or related

examples.en: distinctions between traditional and modern societies
examples.zh: 传统社会和现代社会的差别

examples.en: Philosophers did not use to make a distinction between arts and science.
examples.zh: 哲学家过去不把人文科学和自然科学区别开来。

examples.en: We need to draw a distinction between the two events.
examples.zh: 我们得把两起事件区别开来。

senses.def: the act of separating people or things into different groups

examples.en: The new law makes no distinction between adults and children (= treats them equally).
examples.zh: 这项新法规对成人和孩子同样适用。

examples.en: All groups are entitled to this money without distinction.
examples.zh: 所有团体一律有权得到这笔款项。

senses.def: the quality of being something that is special

examples.en: She had the distinction of being the first woman to fly the Atlantic.
examples.zh: 她不同凡响，是第一个飞越大西洋的女子。

senses.def: the quality of being excellent or important

examples.en: a writer of distinction
examples.zh: 优秀作家

senses.def: a special mark or award that is given to somebody, especially a student, for excellent work
senses.zh: （尤指给学生的）优等评分，荣誉，奖赏

examples.en: Naomi got a distinction in maths.
examples.zh: 娜奥米的数学得了优等。

examples.en: He graduated with distinction.
examples.zh: 他以优异成绩毕业。

senses.def: a point that somebody wants to suggest is a difference when in fact it is not different at all

examples.en: His government did not brand them terrorists, but rather ‘an entity that supports terrorism’. That may prove to be a distinction without a difference.
examples.zh: 他的政府并没有将他们称为恐怖分子，而是将他们称为“支持恐怖主义的实体”。这可能被证明是一种没有区别的区别。

senses.def: a point that somebody wants to suggest is a difference when in fact it is not different at all

examples.en: His government did not brand them terrorists, but rather ‘an entity that supports terrorism’. That may prove to be a distinction without a difference.
examples.zh: 他的政府并没有将他们称为恐怖分子，而是将他们称为“支持恐怖主义的实体”。这可能被证明是一种没有区别的区别。

senses.def: having a quality or characteristic that makes something different and easily noticed
senses.zh: 独特的；特别的；有特色的

examples.en: clothes with a distinctive style
examples.zh: 式样独特的衣服

examples.en: The male bird has distinctive white markings on its head.
examples.zh: 雄鸟的头上有明显的白色斑纹。

senses.def: in a way that shows a quality that is easy to recognize

examples.en: a distinctively nutty flavour
examples.zh: 特别的坚果味道

senses.def: in a way that is easily or clearly heard, seen, felt, etc.
senses.zh: 清晰的；清楚的；明白的；明显的

examples.en: I distinctly heard someone calling me.
examples.zh: 我清楚地听到有人在叫我。

examples.en: He could remember everything very distinctly.
examples.zh: 他什么事都能记得清清楚楚。

senses.def: in a way that shows a quality that is easy to recognize

examples.en: a distinctly Australian accent
examples.zh: 明显的澳大利亚口音

examples.en: The two techniques are distinctly different.
examples.zh: 这两种技术明显不同。

senses.def: definitely or extremely
senses.zh: 明显地：绝对地或极端地

examples.en: It is distinctly possible that she will lose.
examples.zh: 她显然有可能会输。

examples.en: He looked distinctly uncomfortable.
examples.zh: 他看起来明显不舒服。

senses.def: the quality of being clearly different or of a different kind
senses.zh: 截然不同的；有区别的；不同种类的

examples.en: their sense of cultural distinctness
examples.zh: 他们的文化独特感

senses.def: the quality of being easily or clearly heard, seen, felt or remembered
senses.zh: 鲜明：容易或清晰地听到，看到，感觉或记住的质量

examples.en: I remember that dream with extraordinary distinctness.
examples.zh: 我对那个梦的记忆异常清晰。

senses.def: to recognize the difference between two people or things

examples.en: At what age are children able to distinguish between right and wrong?
examples.zh: 儿童到什么年龄才能明辨是非？

examples.en: English law clearly distinguishes between murder and manslaughter.
examples.zh: 英国法律明确区分谋杀和过失杀人。

examples.en: It was hard to distinguish one twin from the other.
examples.zh: 很难分辨出那对双胞胎谁是谁。

examples.en: Sometimes reality and fantasy are hard to distinguish.
examples.zh: 有时候现实和幻想很难区分。

examples.en: We can distinguish five meanings of the word ‘mad’.
examples.zh: 我们可以区分“疯狂”这个词的五个含义。

senses.def: to be a characteristic that makes two people, animals or things different
senses.zh: 成为…的特征；使具有…的特色；使有别于

examples.en: What was it that distinguished her from her classmates?
examples.zh: 是什么使得她有别于班上其他同学呢？

examples.en: The male bird is distinguished from the female by its red beak.
examples.zh: 雄鸟喙红色，有别于雌鸟。

examples.en: The adult bird can be readily distinguished by its orange bill.
examples.zh: 成鸟很容易根据橘黄色喙识别出来。

examples.en: Does your cat have any distinguishing marks?
examples.zh: 你的猫有什么特殊记号吗？

examples.en: The power of speech distinguishes human beings from animals.
examples.zh: 语言能力使得人类有别于动物。

senses.def: to be able to see or hear something

examples.en: I could not distinguish her words, but she sounded agitated.
examples.zh: 我听不清她说的话，但听得出她很激动。

examples.en: She could not distinguish the make and colour of the car in the fading light.
examples.zh: 在昏暗的灯光下，她无法辨别汽车的品牌和颜色。

senses.def: to do something so well that people notice and admire you
senses.zh: 使出众；使著名；使受人青睐

examples.en: She has already distinguished herself as an athlete.
examples.zh: 作为运动员她已享有盛名。

senses.def: that can be recognized as different from somebody/something else
senses.zh: 有区别的;可区分的;易辨别的

examples.en: The male bird is easily distinguishable from the female.
examples.zh: 这种鸟很容易辨认雌雄。

senses.def: that can be seen or heard

examples.en: The coast was barely distinguishable in the mist.
examples.zh: 在雾中很难看清海岸。

senses.def: to change the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear

examples.en: a fairground mirror that distorts your shape
examples.zh: 露天游乐场的哈哈镜

examples.en: The loudspeaker seemed to distort his voice.
examples.zh: 他的声音从喇叭里传出来好像失真了。

senses.def: to change facts, ideas, etc. so that they are no longer correct or true

examples.en: Newspapers are often guilty of distorting the truth.
examples.zh: 报章常犯歪曲事实的错误。

senses.def: a change in the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear

examples.en: modern alloys that are resistant to wear and distortion
examples.zh: 耐磨、防变形的新型合金

examples.en: Distortion of sound is a common problem with cheap amps.
examples.zh: 声音失真是廉价放大器的常见问题。

senses.def: a change in facts, ideas, etc. that makes them no longer correct or true

examples.en: a distortion of the facts
examples.zh: 对事实的歪曲

examples.en: His views are represented here without distortion or exaggeration.
examples.zh: 他的观点在这里得到了体现，没有扭曲或夸大。

senses.def: to take somebody’s attention away from what they are trying to do
senses.zh: 转移（注意力）；分散（思想）；使分心

examples.en: You're distracting me from my work.
examples.zh: 你使我不能专心工作。

examples.en: Don't talk to her—she's very easily distracted.
examples.zh: 不要同她讲话，她的注意力很容易分散。

examples.en: It was another attempt to distract attention from the truth.
examples.zh: 这又是企图分散人们对事实真相的注意力。

examples.en: He’s easily distracted from his work
examples.zh: 他工作时注意力很容易分散。

examples.en: an attempt to distract attention away from the real problems in the country
examples.zh: 把注意力从国家的实际问题上转移开的企图

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are not paying attention to somebody/something because you are worried or thinking about something else
senses.zh: 注意力分散的；思想不集中的

examples.en: I walked up and down distractedly, waiting for news.
examples.zh: 我心不在焉地走来走去，等待消息。

senses.def: a thing that takes your attention away from what you are doing or thinking about
senses.zh: 分散注意力的事物；使人分心的事物

examples.en: I find it hard to work at home because there are too many distractions.
examples.zh: 我发觉在家里工作很难，因为使人分心的事太多。

examples.en: cinema audiences looking for distraction
examples.zh: 寻求解闷的电影观众

senses.def: a feeling of not being able to trust somebody/something

examples.zh: 他们心怀戒备地看着对方。

examples.zh: 他对所有现代技术都深表怀疑。

examples.zh: 他一向不信任权威。

examples.zh: 对不起，打扰你一下，我能跟你谈一会儿吗？

examples.zh: 如果你起得早，尽量不要打扰别人。

examples.zh: 请勿打扰（旅馆房间、办公室等门上的提示牌）

examples.zh: 她被闹腾了一夜，很早就醒了。

examples.zh: 只有海鸟的叫声打破了宁静。

examples.zh: 这封信使我感到震惊和不安。

examples.zh: 他被指控在比赛结束后制造骚乱。

examples.zh: 弗洛伊德说，梦是睡眠的守护者，而不是睡眠的干扰者。

examples.zh: 我总觉得历史像沟水一样乏味。

examples.zh: 作为指挥家，他是一位真正的天后，但作为朋友，他却不是。

examples.zh: 他从桥上跳了下去。

examples.zh: 萨姆走到游泳池的深水区，一头扎进水里。

examples.zh: 潜水采珠

examples.zh: 他到希腊度假的主要目的就是去潜水。

examples.zh: 我们进行了一次深潜，看看能否找到残骸。

examples.zh: 飞行员似乎难以使飞机停止俯冲。

examples.zh: 飞机开始陡直俯冲。

senses.def: a bar, music club, etc. that is cheap, and perhaps dark or dirty

examples.en: The band played in every smoky dive in town.
examples.zh: 乐队在镇上每一次烟雾缭绕的潜水中演奏。

senses.def: a deliberate fall that a player makes when somebody tackles
senses.zh: （遇到阻截时的）假摔，故意跌倒

examples.en: Kane's dive won England a penalty.
examples.zh: 凯恩的假摔为英格兰赢得了一个点球。

senses.def: to suddenly move or jump forward to do something or reach somebody/something
senses.zh: 迅速移动；猛然一跳；扑跃

examples.en: The goalkeeper made a dive for the ball.
examples.zh: 守门员一个鱼跃向球扑去。

examples.en: Paul made a dive for the fridge to get a drink.
examples.zh: 保罗冲向冰箱去拿饮料。

senses.def: to suddenly get worse

examples.en: Profits really took a dive last year.
examples.zh: 去年利润确实跌得很厉害。

senses.def: to suddenly move or jump forward to do something or reach somebody/something

examples.zh: 守门员一个鱼跃向球扑去。

examples.en: Paul made a dive for the fridge to get a drink.
examples.zh: 保罗冲向冰箱去拿饮料。
