examples.en: evocative smells/sounds/music
examples.zh: 引起回忆的气味／声音／音乐

examples.en: Her new book is wonderfully evocative of village life.
examples.zh: 她的新书唤起人们对乡村生活的美好感情。

senses.def: in a way that makes you think of or remember a strong image or feeling, in a pleasant way
senses.zh: 引起记忆的；唤起感情的

examples.en: He writes evocatively about his upbringing.
examples.zh: 他以令人回味的方式写下了自己的成长经历。

senses.def: to bring a feeling, a memory or an image into your mind
senses.zh: 引起，唤起（感情、记忆或形象）

examples.en: The music evoked memories of her youth.
examples.zh: 这乐曲勾起了她对青年时代的回忆。

examples.en: His case is unlikely to evoke public sympathy.
examples.zh: 他的情况不大可能引起公众的同情。

senses.def: the slow steady development of plants, animals, etc. during the history of the earth, as they adapt to changes in their environment

examples.en: the evolution of the human species
examples.zh: 人类的进化

examples.en: Darwin’s theory of evolution
examples.zh: 达尔文的进化论

examples.en: Finally it was legal to teach evolution everywhere in America.
examples.zh: 最终，在美国各地教授进化论是合法的。

senses.def: the slow steady development of something

examples.en: In politics Britain has preferred evolution to revolution (= slow steady development to sudden violent change)
examples.zh: 英国在政治上倾向于渐进而不愿革命。

examples.en: cultural trends and evolutions
examples.zh: 文化趋势和演变

senses.def: in a way that is connected with evolution
senses.zh: 进化的；演变的；逐渐发展的

examples.en: an evolutionarily advanced group of insects
examples.zh: 进化先进的昆虫类群

senses.def: connected with evolution
senses.zh: 进化的；演变的；逐渐发展的

examples.en: evolutionary theory
examples.zh: 进化论

examples.en: evolutionary change
examples.zh: 逐渐演变

senses.def: belief in the theories of evolution
a person who believes in the theories of evolution
relating to the theories of evolution
to develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complicated form; to develop something in this way
senses.zh: （使）逐渐形成，逐步发展，逐渐演变

examples.en: The idea evolved from a drawing I discovered in the attic.
examples.zh: 这种想法是从我在阁楼里发现的一幅画得到启发的。

examples.en: The company has evolved into a major chemical manufacturer.
examples.zh: 这家公司已逐步发展成一家大型的化工厂。

examples.en: Each school must evolve its own way of working.
examples.zh: 每所学校必须发展出自己的办学方式。

senses.def: to develop over time, often many generations, into forms that are better adapted to survive changes in their environment

examples.en: The three species evolved from a single ancestor.
examples.zh: 这三种生物从同一祖先进化而来。

examples.en: The dolphin has evolved a highly developed jaw.
examples.zh: 海豚已经进化出高度发达的下颌。

senses.def: a female sheep
a large jug
senses.zh: （旧时提水用的）大口水壶，大口水罐

senses.def: the way of writing the sound that people make when they think that something is horrible or unpleasant
senses.zh: 唷，呃，咦呀（书写形式，表示恶心或厌恶时发出的声音）

examples.en: Eww! There’s a fly in my lemonade!
examples.zh: 呃！我的柠檬水里有只苍蝇！

senses.def: a person’s former wife, husband or partner
senses.zh: 前妻；前夫；以前的性伴侣

examples.en: The children are spending the weekend with my ex and his new wife.
examples.zh: 孩子们与我的前夫及其新夫人在一起度周末。

senses.def: not including something

examples.en: The price is £1 500 ex VAT.
examples.zh: 价格为 1 500 英镑，不含增值税。

senses.def: former

examples.en: ex-wife
examples.zh: 前妻

examples.en: ex-president
examples.zh: 前总裁

senses.def: out

examples.en: exodus
examples.zh: 离去

examples.en: export
examples.zh: 出口

senses.def: speaking or said with the authority of your position
senses.zh: 以职位的权威发言的；权威性地

examples.en: The Pope was speaking ex cathedra.
examples.zh: 教皇以宗座权威发表讲话。

examples.en: This papal judgement is not ex cathedra.
examples.zh: 教皇的这一判决并非前大教堂判决。

senses.def: not listed in the public phone book and not available through directory enquiries
senses.zh: 未列入电话号码簿的（经用户要求电话公司不向询问人提供其电话号码）

examples.en: an ex-directory number
examples.zh: 未列入电话簿的电话号码

examples.en: She's ex-directory.
examples.zh: 她的名字未列入电话号码簿。

senses.def: as a gift or favour, not because there is a legal duty to do it
senses.zh: 作为礼物的；作为恩惠的

examples.en: The sum was paid ex gratia.
examples.zh: 这笔钱是特惠金。

senses.def: given or done as a gift or favour, not because there is a legal duty to do it
senses.zh: 作为礼物的；作为恩惠的

examples.en: ex gratia payments
examples.zh: 通融付款

senses.def: written in the front of a book before the name of the person the book belongs to
senses.zh: （写于书前页的藏书者姓名前）…的藏书，…的藏本

examples.en: ex libris David Harries
examples.zh: 戴维 · 哈里斯藏书

senses.def: because of your job, rank or position
senses.zh: 出于工作（或职位、职权）的；（由于工作、职位或职权而成为的）当然的

examples.en: He was present at the meeting ex officio.
examples.zh: 他出于职务需要出席了会议。

senses.def: included or allowed because of your job, position or rank
senses.zh: 出于工作（或职位、职权）的；（因工作、职位或职权而）当然的

examples.en: an ex officio member of the committee
examples.zh: 委员会的当然委员

senses.def: having previously been a member of the army, navy

examples.en: ex-service personnel
examples.zh: 退伍人员

senses.def: a man who used to be in the army, navy

examples.en: an organization for ex-servicemen
examples.zh: 退役军人组织

senses.def: a woman who used to be in the army, navy

examples.en: exajoule
examples.zh: 百亿亿焦耳

senses.def: to make something worse, especially a disease or problem

examples.en: His aggressive reaction only exacerbated the situation.
examples.zh: 他的挑衅行为只会使情况恶化。

examples.en: The symptoms may be exacerbated by certain drugs.
examples.zh: 这些症状可能会因为某些药物而加重。

senses.def: the act of making something worse, especially a disease or problem
senses.zh: 使事情变得更糟的行为，尤指疾病或问题

examples.en: the exacerbation of religious tensions
examples.zh: 宗教紧张局势加剧

examples.en: Over the next two years, Gary experienced numerous acute exacerbations of his illness.
examples.zh: 在接下来的两年里，加里的病情多次急剧恶化。

senses.def: correct in every detail

examples.en: The new palace is an exact replica of the original building.
examples.zh: 新宫殿是原建筑一模一样的复制品。

examples.en: It is an exact copy of the original document.
examples.zh: 它是原始文件的精确副本。

examples.en: The model is exact in every detail.
examples.zh: 模型在每一个细节上都很精确。

examples.en: For now they are keeping the exact date and location of the wedding a secret.
examples.zh: 目前他们对婚礼的确切日期和地点保密。

examples.en: The exact nature of her illness (= precisely what her illness is) has not been made public.
examples.zh: 她的确切病情尚未公开。

examples.en: Her second husband was the exact opposite of her first (= completely different).
examples.zh: 她的第二任丈夫与第一任截然不同。

examples.en: The colours were an almost exact match.
examples.zh: 颜色几乎完全一致。

examples.en: She's in her mid-thirties—thirty-six to be exact.
examples.zh: 她三十五岁左右，确切地说是三十六岁。

examples.en: I had the exact same problem as you when I first started.
examples.zh: 刚开始的时候我和你有完全一样的问题。

examples.en: What were his exact words?
examples.zh: 他的原话是什么？

examples.en: A clear definition requires very exact wording.
examples.zh: 明确的定义需要非常精确的措辞。

examples.en: Nobody knows the exact number of people affected, but it is over 10 000.
examples.zh: 没有人知道受影响的确切人数，但已经超过 10 万人。

examples.en: He started to phone me at the exact moment I started to phone him (= at the same time).
examples.zh: 他给我拨电话时，我也正好在给他拨电话。

senses.def: very accurate and careful about details
senses.zh: 严谨的；严格的；一丝不苟的

examples.en: He was very exact about everything he did.
examples.zh: 他对自己所做的一切都非常精确。

senses.def: using accurate measurements and following set rules

examples.en: Assessing insurance risk can never be an exact science.
examples.zh: 估定承保的风险永远不会成为一门精确的科学。

senses.def: to demand and get something from somebody

examples.en: She was determined to exact a promise from him.
examples.zh: 她决意要他作出许诺。

examples.en: No doubt they will exact payment in due course.
examples.zh: 毫无疑问，他们会在适当的时候要求付款。

senses.def: to make something bad happen to somebody

examples.en: He exacted (= took) a terrible revenge for their treatment of him.
examples.zh: 他因受他们的虐待而痛加报复。

examples.en: Stress can exact a high price from workers (= can affect them badly).
examples.zh: 压力可能迫使工人付出昂贵的代价。

senses.def: an act of demanding and getting something from somebody

examples.en: rising tax exactions
examples.zh: 不断增加的税收

examples.en: the exaction of tolls at various ports
examples.zh: 各港口征收通行费

senses.def: an act of making something bad happen to somebody

examples.en: the exactions imposed by military law
examples.zh: 军事法强加的勒索

senses.def: the quality of being very accurate and exact

examples.en: scientific exactitude
examples.zh: 科学的精确性

senses.def: used to emphasize that something is correct in every way or in every detail

examples.en: It's exactly nine o'clock.
examples.zh: 现在是九点整。

examples.en: It happened almost exactly a year ago.
examples.zh: 这事情发生差不多正好一年了。

examples.en: Your answer is exactly right.
examples.zh: 你的回答完全正确。

examples.en: It was a warm day, if not exactly hot.
examples.zh: 这一天即使算不上热，也是一个暖和的日子。

examples.en: I know exactly how she felt.
examples.zh: 我完全清楚她的感受。

examples.en: It's impossible to say exactly what happened.
examples.zh: 不可能确切地说出发生了什么。

examples.en: Do exactly as I tell you.
examples.zh: 严格按照我说的办。

examples.en: You haven't changed at all—you still look exactly the same.
examples.zh: 你一点没变，看上去依然是老样子。

examples.en: His words had exactly the opposite effect.
examples.zh: 他的话产生了截然相反的效果。

senses.def: used to ask for more information about something
senses.zh: （要求得到更多信息）究竟，到底

examples.en: Where exactly did you stay in France?
examples.zh: 你究竟待在法国什么地方？

examples.en: Exactly what are you trying to tell me?
examples.zh: 你到底想对我说什么？

senses.def: used as a reply, agreeing with what somebody has just said, or emphasizing that it is correct
senses.zh: （答语，表示赞同或强调正确）一点不错，正是如此，完全正确

examples.en: ‘You mean somebody in this room must be the murderer?’ ‘Exactly.’
examples.zh: “你的意思是这屋子里肯定有人是凶手？”“正是。”

senses.def: used when you are saying the opposite of what you really mean
senses.zh: （说反话时用）根本不，决不，一点也不

examples.en: He wasn't exactly pleased to see us—in fact he refused to open the door.
examples.zh: 他根本不愿见我们，事实上他连门都不开。

examples.en: It's not exactly beautiful, is it? (= it's ugly)
examples.zh: 这一点也不美，是吗？

senses.def: used when you are correcting something that somebody has said
senses.zh: （纠正对方刚说过的话）不完全

examples.en: ‘So he told you you'd got the job?’ ‘Not exactly, but he said they were impressed with me.’
examples.zh: “如此看来，他对你说你得到这份工作了？”“不完全是这样，不过他说我给他们留下了深刻的印象。”

senses.def: used when you are saying the opposite of what you really mean
senses.zh: （说反话时用）根本不，决不，一点也不

examples.en: He wasn't exactly pleased to see us—in fact he refused to open the door.
examples.zh: 他根本不愿见我们，事实上他连门都不开。

examples.en: It's not exactly beautiful, is it? (= it's ugly)
examples.zh: 这一点也不美，是吗？

senses.def: used when you are correcting something that somebody has said
senses.zh: （纠正对方刚说过的话）不完全

examples.en: ‘So he told you you'd got the job?’ ‘Not exactly, but he said they were impressed with me.’
examples.zh: “如此看来，他对你说你得到这份工作了？”“不完全是这样，不过他说我给他们留下了深刻的印象。”

senses.def: the quality of being correct and accurate in every detail

examples.en: Most people remember with vivid exactness just where they were when the news came through.
examples.zh: 大多数人都清楚地记得消息传来时他们在哪里。

senses.def: the quality of being very accurate and careful about details
senses.zh: 严谨的；严格的；一丝不苟的

senses.def: to make something seem larger, better, worse or more important than it really is

examples.en: The hotel was really filthy and I'm not exaggerating.
examples.zh: 我不是夸张，这旅店真的很脏。

examples.en: He tends to exaggerate the difficulties.
examples.zh: 他往往夸大困难。

examples.en: I'm sure he exaggerates his Irish accent (= tries to sound more Irish than he really is).
examples.zh: 我肯定他故意把爱尔兰口音说得很重。

examples.en: Demand for the product has been greatly exaggerated.
examples.zh: 对这项产品的需求给过分夸大了。

senses.def: in a way that makes something seem larger, better, worse or more important than it really is or needs to be
senses.zh: 夸张的；夸大的；言过其实的

examples.en: Some hotels even cut their exaggeratedly high rates by half.
examples.zh: 一些酒店甚至将过高的房价降低了一半。

senses.def: a statement or description that makes something seem larger, better, worse or more important than it really is; the act of making a statement like this

examples.en: a slight/gross/wild exaggeration
examples.zh: 有点／明显的／过于夸张

examples.en: It would be an exaggeration to say I knew her well—I only met her twice.
examples.zh: 说我非常了解她不免言过其实，我只见过她两次。

examples.en: It's no exaggeration to say that most students have never read a complete Shakespeare play.
examples.zh: 说大多数同学从未读过一部完整的莎士比亚戏剧一点也不夸张。

examples.en: He told his story simply and without exaggeration.
examples.zh: 他简单扼要、毫不夸张地讲述了自己的故事。

senses.def: to make somebody rise to a higher rank or position, sometimes to one that they do not deserve
senses.zh: 提拔，提升（有时指不该得到的职位）

examples.en: His son was exalted to a high position in the government through family connections.
examples.zh: 他的儿子通过家族关系在政府中获得了很高的职位。

senses.def: to praise somebody/something very much

examples.en: She was exalted as a pillar of the community.
examples.zh: 她被尊崇为社区的栋梁。

senses.def: a feeling of very great joy or happiness

examples.en: a moment of extreme joy and exaltation
examples.zh: 极度喜悦和兴奋的时刻

senses.def: an act of raising something/somebody to a high position or rank

examples.en: the exaltation of emotion above logical reasoning
examples.zh: 把情感提高到逻辑推理之上

senses.def: a formal written, spoken or practical test, especially at school or college, to see how much you know about a subject, or what you can do

examples.en: to take an exam
examples.zh: 参加考试

examples.en: to pass/fail an exam
examples.zh: 考试合格／不合格

examples.en: I hate doing exams.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢考试。

examples.en: to sit an exam
examples.zh: 参加考试

examples.en: to mark an exam
examples.zh: 阅卷评分

examples.en: to grade an exam
examples.zh: 阅卷评分

examples.en: I failed the college entrance exam (= to get a place at college).
examples.zh: 我没有通过大学入学考试。

examples.en: Every term we would have exams in maths, English, French, etc.
examples.zh: 每学期我们都有数学、英语、法语等考试。

examples.en: She did well in her exams.
examples.zh: 她考试考得好。

examples.en: She did well on her exams.
examples.zh: 她考试考得好。

examples.en: an exam paper
examples.zh: 试卷

examples.en: I got my exam results today.
examples.zh: 我今天得知了考试成绩。

examples.en: A lot of students suffer from exam nerves.
examples.zh: 许多学生考试怯阵。

senses.def: a medical test of a particular part of the body
senses.zh: （对身体特定部位进行的）检查；体检

examples.en: an eye exam
examples.zh: 眼睛检查

senses.def: a formal written, spoken or practical test, especially at school or college, to see how much you know about a subject, or what you can do

examples.en: successful candidates in GCSE examinations
examples.zh: 通过普通中等教育证书考试的考生

examples.en: to sit an examination in mathematics
examples.zh: 参加数学考试

examples.en: In 1864 he passed the examination for the Indian Civil Service.
examples.zh: 1864 年，他通过了印度公务员考试。

examples.en: Applicants are selected for jobs on the results of a competitive examination.
examples.zh: 竞聘者按遴选考试结果择优录用。

senses.def: the act of looking at or considering something very carefully

examples.en: Careful examination of the ruins revealed an even earlier temple.
examples.zh: 仔细考察这片废墟后发现了一座更为古老的庙宇。

examples.en: The issue needs further examination.
examples.zh: 这个问题需要进一步考查。

examples.en: The review is the most detailed examination of policing since 1992.
examples.zh: 此次审查是自 1992 年以来对警务工作最详细的审查。

examples.en: The chapter concludes with a brief examination of some of the factors causing family break-up.
examples.zh: 本章结束时简要考查了引起家庭破裂的某些因素。

examples.en: After a thorough examination, they announced that the suspicious device was harmless.
examples.zh: 经过彻底检查，他们宣布可疑装置无害。

examples.en: On closer examination it was found that the signature was not genuine.
examples.zh: 经过进一步认真检查发现签名是伪造的。

examples.en: Your proposals are still under examination.
examples.zh: 你的提议仍在审查之中。

examples.en: The party would open up the issue to examination by a Senate Committee.
examples.zh: 该党将把这个问题开放给参议院委员会审查。

senses.def: a close look at something/somebody, especially to see if there is anything wrong or to find the cause of a problem

examples.en: a medical/physical examination
examples.zh: 健康检查

examples.en: a post-mortem/forensic examination
examples.zh: 尸检/法医检查

examples.en: Regular breast examination is advised.
examples.zh: 建议定期进行乳房检查。

examples.en: A specialist should carry out an examination of the patient.
examples.zh: 应由专家对这名患者做一次检查。

examples.en: Diagnosis can be made only by direct examination of affected brain tissue.
examples.zh: 只能通过直接检查受影响的脑组织才能做出诊断。

examples.en: Further examination by an orthopaedic surgeon will be needed today.
examples.zh: 今天需要由骨科医生进行进一步检查。

senses.def: to consider or study an idea, a subject, etc. very carefully

examples.en: This study sets out to examine in detail the possible effects of climate change.
examples.zh: 这项研究旨在详细考察气候变化可能带来的影响。

examples.en: Her new show critically examines the relationship between the arts and popular culture.
examples.zh: 她的新节目对艺术和流行文化之间的关系进行了批判性研究。

examples.en: This important issue must be carefully examined.
examples.zh: 这个重要问题须仔细研究。

examples.en: Only recently have historians begun to examine the impact and influence of these changes.
examples.zh: 直到最近，历史学家才开始研究这些变化的影响和影响。

examples.en: It is necessary to examine how the proposals can be carried out.
examples.zh: 有必要调查一下怎样才能实施这些方案。

examples.en: The weather gave researchers an opportunity to examine what happens to insect numbers when temperatures rise.
examples.zh: 天气使研究人员有机会研究气温升高时昆虫数量的变化。

senses.def: to look at somebody/something closely, to see if there is anything wrong or to find the cause of a problem

examples.en: The doctor examined her carefully but could find nothing wrong.
examples.zh: 医生给她认真做了检查，但没发现什么问题。

examples.en: to be examined by a doctor/psychiatrist/specialist/vet
examples.zh: 由医生/精神科医生/专家/兽医检查

examples.en: She examined herself closely in the mirror.
examples.zh: 她对着镜子仔细审视自己。

examples.en: The samples were examined under the microscope for the presence of damaged cells.
examples.zh: 在显微镜下检查样本是否存在受损细胞。

examples.en: The goods were examined for damage on arrival.
examples.zh: 货物到达时检查是否有破损。

examples.en: Investigators examined the room minutely for clues.
examples.zh: 调查人员仔细检查了房间以寻找线索。

senses.def: to give somebody a test to see how much they know about a subject or what they can do

examples.en: The students will be examined in all subjects at the end of term.
examples.zh: 期末时学生须要参加所有学科的考试。

examples.en: You are only being examined on this semester's work.
examples.zh: 现在只考你在本学期学的课程。

examples.en: The course is externally examined (= arranged and marked by somebody from outside a school, a university or an organization).
examples.zh: 这门课程受校外考核。

senses.def: to ask somebody questions formally, especially in court

examples.en: The prosecution examined 20 witnesses.
examples.zh: 检方询问了20名证人。

senses.def: to be crazy
to be crazy

intro.en: These words all mean to think about, study or describe somebody/​something carefully, especially in order to understand them, form an opinion of them or make a decision about them.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含思量、审查、调查、研究之义。

items.def: to think about, study or describe an idea, subject or piece of work very carefully:
items.zh: 指审查、调查、考查、考察

examples.en: These ideas will be examined in more detail in Chapter 10.
examples.zh: 这些观点将在第 10 章做更为详细的探讨。

items.def: to examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it:
items.zh: 指分析

examples.en: The job involves gathering and analysing data.
examples.zh: 这项工作需要搜集和分析资料。

items.def: to examine something again, especially so that you can decide if it is necessary to make changes:
items.zh: 指复查、检讨，以做必要的修改

examples.en: The government will review the situation later in the year.
examples.zh: 政府将在今年晚些时候重新检讨形势。

items.def: to examine somebody/​something in order to understand them or it:
items.zh: 指研究、调查

examples.en: We will study the report carefully before making a decision.
examples.zh: 我们将认真研究这份报告，然后再作决定。

items.def: to write or talk about something in detail, showing the different ideas and opinions about it:
items.zh: 指详述、论述

examples.en: This topic will be discussed at greater length in the next chapter.
examples.zh: 这个主题将在下一章里详细论述。

intro.en: These words all mean to look closely to make sure that everything is correct, in good condition, or acceptable.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含仔细检查、审查之义。

items.def: to look at something closely to make sure that everything is correct, in good condition, safe or acceptable:
items.zh: 指检查、审查、核查，以确保完好、正常和安全

examples.en: Check your work before handing it in.
examples.zh: 交作业前先检查一遍。

items.def: to look at somebody/​something closely to see if there is anything wrong or to find the cause of a problem:
items.zh: 指仔细检查或检验人或事物，以确认有无问题或找出问题所在

examples.en: The goods were examined for damage on arrival.
examples.zh: 货物到达时检查是否有破损。

items.def: to look at somebody/​something closely to make sure that everything is acceptable; to officially visit a school, factory, etc. in order to check that rules are being obeyed and that standards are acceptable:
items.zh: 指检查、查看、审视，以确保一切妥当；视察（学校、工厂等）

examples.en: Make sure you inspect the goods before signing for them.
examples.zh: 要确保在签收货物之前进行检验。

items.def: to check something carefully for mistakes, damage or anything dangerous:
items.zh: 指仔细检查是否有错误、损坏或危险

examples.en: Go over your work for spelling mistakes before you hand it in.
examples.zh: 交作业前仔细检查一下拼写错误。

senses.def: a person who is being tested to see how much they know about a subject or what they can do; a person who is taking an exam
a person who writes the questions for, or marks, a test of knowledge or ability

examples.en: The papers are sent to external examiners (= ones not connected with the students' school or college).
examples.zh: 试卷送到校外主考人那里。

senses.def: a person who has the official duty to check that things are being done correctly and according to the rules of an organization; a person who officially examines something

examples.en: He was the official examiner of electronic voting systems for Pennsylvania and Texas for 20 years.
examples.zh: 他担任宾夕法尼亚州和得克萨斯州电子投票系统的官方审查人达20年之久。

senses.def: something such as an object, a fact or a situation that shows, explains or supports what you say

examples.en: Let me give you an example.
examples.zh: 我给你举个例子。

examples.en: It is important to cite examples to support your argument.
examples.zh: 重要的是引用实例来证明你的论点。

examples.en: to provide/offer an example
examples.zh: 举个例子

examples.en: I shall take four different examples from contemporary literature to illustrate my point.
examples.zh: 我将从当代文学中举出四个不同的例子来说明我的观点。

examples.en: Can you show me an example of what you mean?
examples.zh: 你能给我举个实例来解释你的意思吗？

examples.en: This dictionary has many examples of how words are used.
examples.zh: 这部词典有许多关于词语用法的示例。

examples.en: Just to give you an example of his generosity—he gave me his old car and wouldn't take any money for it.
examples.zh: 且给你举个例子来说明他的慷慨吧 － 他把他的旧汽车给了我，而且分文不取。

examples.en: The progress the students have made serves as an example of the benefit of small class sizes.
examples.zh: 学生们取得的进步是小班制好处的一个例子。

examples.en: By way of example, we'll look at our most recent advertising campaign.
examples.zh: 我们通过实例来看看最近的广告活动。

senses.def: a thing that is typical of or represents a particular group or set

examples.en: This is a good example of the artist's early work.
examples.zh: 这是这位艺术家早期作品的范例。

examples.en: It is a perfect example of this type of architecture.
examples.zh: 这是这类建筑最典型的样本。

examples.en: Japan is often quoted as the prime example of a modern industrial nation.
examples.zh: 人们经常举例把日本作为现代工业国家的典范。

examples.en: It is a classic example of how not to design a new city centre.
examples.zh: 这对于如何设计新市中心是个绝佳的反面教材。

senses.def: a person or their behaviour that is thought to be a good model for others to copy

examples.en: Her courage is an example to us all.
examples.zh: 她的勇气是我们大家的榜样。

examples.en: He sets an example for the other students.
examples.zh: 他为其他学生树立了榜样。

examples.en: They are a shining example of the best of the human spirit.
examples.zh: 他们是人类精神最优秀的典范。

examples.en: He is a captain who leads by example.
examples.zh: 他是个以身作则的队长。

examples.en: Top management should be seen to lead by example.
examples.zh: 高层管理人员应该以身作则。

senses.def: a person’s behaviour, either good or bad, that other people copy

examples.en: It would be a mistake to follow his example.
examples.zh: 仿效他的做法是错误的。

examples.en: They started to plan protests, inspired by the example of their neighbours.
examples.zh: 受到邻居榜样的启发，他们开始策划抗议活动。

senses.def: used to emphasize something that explains or supports what you are saying; used to give an example of what you are saying

examples.en: There is a similar word in many languages, for example in French and Italian.
examples.zh: 在许多语言，譬如法语和意大利语中都有相似的词。

examples.en: The report is incomplete; it does not include sales in France, for example.
examples.zh: 这份报告不完整，例如在法国的销售情况就没包括进去。

examples.en: It is possible to combine computer science with other subjects, for example physics.
examples.zh: 将计算机科学与其他学科，如物理学，结合起来是可能的。

examples.en: An athlete, for example, might turn the pedals 80 times a minute.
examples.zh: 例如，一个运动员一分钟可能踏脚蹬 80 次。

senses.def: to punish somebody as a warning to others not to do the same thing
senses.zh: 惩罚某人以儆戒他人；用某人来杀一儆百

examples.en: The teacher made an example of him by suspending him from school.
examples.zh: 老师将他停学，以儆效尤。

senses.def: used to emphasize something that explains or supports what you are saying; used to give an example of what you are saying

examples.en: There is a similar word in many languages, for example in French and Italian.
examples.zh: 在许多语言，譬如法语和意大利语中都有相似的词。

examples.en: The report is incomplete; it does not include sales in France, for example.
examples.zh: 这份报告不完整，例如在法国的销售情况就没包括进去。

examples.en: It is possible to combine computer science with other subjects, for example physics.
examples.zh: 将计算机科学与其他学科，如物理学，结合起来是可能的。

examples.en: An athlete, for example, might turn the pedals 80 times a minute.
examples.zh: 例如，一个运动员一分钟可能踏脚蹬 80 次。

senses.def: to punish somebody as a warning to others not to do the same thing
senses.zh: 惩罚某人以儆戒他人；用某人来杀一儆百

examples.en: The teacher made an example of him by suspending him from school.
examples.zh: 老师将他停学，以儆效尤。

intro.en: These are all words for a thing or situation that is typical of a particular group or set, and is sometimes used to support an argument.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指事例、实例、例证。

items.def: something such as an object, a fact or a situation that shows, explains or supports what you say; a thing that is typical of or represents a particular group or set:
items.zh: 指实例、例证、典型、范例、样品

examples.en: Can you give me an example of what you mean?
examples.zh: 你能给我举个实例来解释你的意思吗？

items.def: a particular situation or a situation of a particular type; a situation that relates to a particular person or thing:
items.zh: 指具体情况、事例、实例、特定情况

examples.en: In some cases people have had to wait several weeks for an appointment.
examples.zh: 在某些情况下，人们必须等上好几周才能得到约见。

items.def: (rather formal) a particular situation or a situation of a particular type:
items.zh: 指例子、事例、实例

examples.en: The report highlights a number of instances of injustice.
examples.zh: 这篇报道重点列举了一些不公正的实例。

items.def: an example of something, especially an animal or plant:
items.zh: 尤指动植物的样品、实例

examples.en: The aquarium has some interesting specimens of unusual tropical fish.
examples.zh: 水族馆里有一些罕见的热带鱼，很有趣。

items.def: (rather formal) a story, an event or an example that clearly shows the truth about something:
items.zh: 指说明事实的故事、实例、示例

examples.en: The statistics are a clear illustration of the point I am trying to make.
examples.zh: 这些统计数字清楚地阐明了我要陈述的要点。

senses.def: to annoy somebody very much

examples.en: Her moods exasperated him.
examples.zh: 她的坏脾气让他很生气。

examples.en: She was clearly exasperated by all my questions.
examples.zh: 她显然对我问个没完感到恼火。

senses.def: in an extremely annoyed way, especially because you cannot do anything to improve a situation
the feeling of being extremely annoyed, especially because you cannot do anything to improve a situation

examples.en: a groan/look/sigh of exasperation
examples.zh: 愤怒的咕哝声／样子／叹息声

examples.en: He shook his head in exasperation.
examples.zh: 他愤怒地摇了摇头。

senses.def: the magic sword
senses.zh: 神剑：亚瑟王的魔剑。小时候，当没有其他人可以移动它时，他把它从石头上拉了下来。在他生命的尽头，他告诉他的一个人将其扔进湖中，在那里湖水被从湖中出来的那位女士的手抓住。根据故事的另一个版本，亚瑟还从湖中夫人那里获得了神剑。

senses.def: to dig in the ground to look for old buildings or objects that have been buried for a long time; to find something by digging in this way
senses.zh: 发掘，挖出（古建筑或古物）

examples.en: The site has been excavated by archaeologists.
examples.zh: 这个遗址已被考古学家发掘出来。

examples.en: The area has not yet been fully excavated.
examples.zh: 这个地方还没有被充分挖掘。

examples.en: pottery and weapons excavated from the burial site
examples.zh: 从墓葬挖掘出的陶器和兵器

senses.def: to make a hole, etc. in the ground by digging
senses.zh: 挖掘，开凿，挖空（洞、隧道等）

examples.en: The body was discovered when builders excavated the area.
examples.zh: 建筑工人挖地时发现了这具尸体。

senses.def: the activity of digging in the ground to look for old buildings or objects that have been buried for a long time
senses.zh: （对古建筑或古物的）发掘，挖掘

examples.en: Further archaeological excavations are now being carried out.
examples.zh: 更进一步的考古发掘正在进行。

examples.en: More discoveries were made as the excavation proceeded.
examples.zh: 挖掘期间陆续有所发现。

examples.en: The excavations took place between 1925 and 1939.
examples.zh: 发掘是在 1925 年到 1939 年间进行的。

examples.en: recent excavations of underground burial chambers
examples.zh: 最近对地下墓室的挖掘

senses.def: a place where people are digging to look for old buildings or objects

examples.en: The excavations are open to the public.
examples.zh: 发掘现场对公众开放。

senses.def: the act of digging, especially with a machine
a large machine that is used for digging and moving earth
a person who digs in the ground to look for old buildings and objects
to be greater than a particular number or amount

examples.en: The price will not exceed £100.
examples.zh: 价格不会超过 100 英镑。

senses.def: to do more than the law or an order, etc. allows you to do
senses.zh: 超越（法律、命令等）的限制

examples.en: She was exceeding the speed limit (= driving faster than is allowed).
examples.zh: 当时她超速驾驶。

examples.en: The officers had exceeded their authority.
examples.zh: 这些官员超越了他们的权限。

senses.def: to be better than expected

examples.en: His achievements have exceeded expectations.
examples.zh: 他的成就出乎预料。

examples.en: The amount raised has far exceeded our wildest expectations.
examples.zh: 筹集的金额远远超出了我们最疯狂的预期。

senses.def: extremely; very; very much
to be very good at doing something

examples.en: She has always excelled in foreign languages.
examples.zh: 她的外语从来都是出类拔萃。

examples.en: As a child he excelled at music and art.
examples.zh: 他小时候擅长音乐和美术。

examples.en: The team excels at turning defence into attack.
examples.zh: 这个队善于打防守反击。

senses.def: to do extremely well and even better than you usually do

examples.en: Rick's cooking was always good, but this time he really excelled himself.
examples.zh: 里克的烹饪技术一直不错，但这次简直是好上加好。

senses.def: the quality of being extremely good

examples.en: a reputation for academic excellence
examples.zh: 因学术上的杰出成就而获得的声誉

examples.en: The hospital is recognized as a centre of excellence in research and teaching.
examples.zh: 这所医院被确认为成就卓著的教学和研究中心。

senses.def: a title used when talking to or about somebody who has a very important official position, especially an ambassador
senses.zh: （对身居要职的人，尤其是大使的尊称）阁下

examples.en: Good evening, your Excellency.
examples.zh: 晚上好，阁下。

examples.en: their Excellencies the French and Spanish Ambassadors
examples.zh: 法国和西班牙大使阁下

senses.def: extremely good

examples.en: an excellent book/article
examples.zh: 优秀的书；出色的文章

examples.en: excellent results/work
examples.zh: 了不起的成绩／工作

examples.en: The meal looked and tasted excellent.
examples.zh: 这顿饭看起来和味道都很棒。

examples.en: Both the food and the service were truly excellent.
examples.zh: 食物和服务都非常棒。

examples.en: The performances of the cast are uniformly excellent throughout.
examples.zh: 演员们的表演自始至终都非常出色。

examples.en: She has done an excellent job of adapting the novel for the screen.
examples.zh: 她出色地把这部小说改编成了剧本。

examples.en: It is an excellent example of how a farm can work in harmony with nature.
examples.zh: 这是农场如何与自然和谐相处的一个很好的例子。

examples.en: The party provided an excellent opportunity to meet new people.
examples.zh: 这次聚会提供了结识新朋友的绝佳机会。

examples.en: The apartment is in excellent condition and is ready to move into.
examples.zh: 公寓状况非常好，可以随时入住。

examples.en: He was great at sport and excellent at art.
examples.zh: 他擅长运动，也擅长艺术。

examples.en: Our staff are excellent at advising small businesses.
examples.zh: 我们的员工擅长为小企业提供咨询。

examples.en: The experience was excellent for students' self-confidence.
examples.zh: 这种经历非常有助于提升学生的自信心。

examples.en: Ferns are excellent for planting in shady parts of the garden.
examples.zh: 蕨类植物非常适合种植在花园的阴凉处。

senses.def: used to show that you are very pleased about something or that you approve of something
senses.zh: （用以表示愉快或赞同）好极了，妙极了

examples.en: You can all come? Excellent!
examples.zh: 你们都能来？太好了！

examples.en: It's excellent to see so many people at today's event!
examples.zh: 很高兴在今天的活动中看到这么多人！

intro.en: These words all describe something that is extremely good.
intro.zh: 以上各词均形容某事物极好。

items.def: extremely good.
items.zh: 出色的；非凡的；非常棒的

items.def: extremely good. Outstanding is used especially about how well somebody does something or how good somebody is at something:
items.zh: outstanding 尤指在做某事上或某方面杰出

items.def: so good that it could not be better. Perfect is used especially about conditions or how suitable something is for a purpose:
items.zh: perfect 尤指条件状况极好或很合适

items.def: (informal) extremely good or impressive:
items.zh: 指极佳的、卓越的、出色的

examples.en: The facilities at the hotel are superb.
examples.zh: 旅馆的设施棒极了。

senses.def: extremely well; to a very high degree

examples.en: The story is excellently written.
examples.zh: 这个故事写得很好。

examples.en: Scandinavian trains are excellently clean.
examples.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚火车非常干净。

senses.def: used before you mention the only thing or person about which a statement is not true
senses.zh: （用于所言不包括的人或事物前）除…之外

examples.en: We work every day except Sunday.
examples.zh: 我们除星期天外每天都工作。

examples.en: They all came except Matt.
examples.zh: 除马特外他们都来了。

examples.en: I had nothing on except for my socks.
examples.zh: 我除了短袜什么都还没穿。

senses.def: used before you mention something that makes a statement not completely true

examples.en: I didn't tell him anything except that I needed the money.
examples.zh: 我什么都没告诉他，只是说我需要钱。

examples.en: Our dresses were the same except mine was red.
examples.zh: 我们的连衣裙是一样的，只是我的那件是红色。

senses.def: to not include somebody/something

examples.en: Children under five are excepted from the survey.
examples.zh: 五岁以下的儿童不在调查之列。

examples.en: Tours are arranged all year round (January excepted).
examples.zh: 全年都提供观光旅游（一月份除外）。

senses.def: used after being rude or critical about somebody to say that the people you are talking to are not included in the criticism
senses.zh: 在座诸位除外；与这里的各位无关

examples.en: The people in this office are so narrow-minded, present company excepted, of course.
examples.zh: 这个办公室里的人都是心胸狭隘的人，当然，现在的公司除外。

senses.def: used after being rude or critical about somebody to say that the people you are talking to are not included in the criticism
senses.zh: 在座诸位除外；与这里的各位无关

examples.en: The people in this office are so narrow-minded, present company excepted, of course.
examples.zh: 这个办公室里的人都是心胸狭隘的人，当然，现在的公司除外。

senses.def: a person or thing that is not included in a general statement
senses.zh: 一般情况以外的人（或事物）；例外

examples.en: Most of the buildings in the town are modern, but the church is an exception.
examples.zh: 城里大多是现代建筑，不过教堂是个例外。

examples.en: With very few exceptions, private schools get the best exam results.
examples.zh: 私立学校的考试成绩是最好的，很少有例外情况。

examples.en: Nobody had much money at the time and I was no exception.
examples.zh: 那时候谁都没有很多钱，我也不例外。

senses.def: a thing that does not follow a rule
senses.zh: 规则的例外；例外的事物

examples.en: Good writing is unfortunately the exception rather than the rule (= it is unusual).
examples.zh: 可惜优秀的文字作品真是可遇不可求。

examples.en: There are always a lot of exceptions to grammar rules.
examples.zh: 语法规则总是有很多例外。

senses.def: people say that something is the exception that proves the rule
senses.zh: 反证规律的例外；足以证明普遍性的例外

examples.en: Most electronics companies have not done well this year, but ours is the exception that proves the rule.
examples.zh: 今年多数电子公司都不景气，而我们公司却是普遍中的例外。

senses.def: to allow somebody not to follow the usual rule on one occasion or for one particular reason
senses.zh: 允许有例外；让…成为例外

examples.en: Children are not usually allowed in, but I'm prepared to make an exception in this case.
examples.zh: 儿童一般不允许入内，不过这次我可以破例。

examples.en: No parking is allowed, but an exception is made for disabled drivers.
examples.zh: 此处禁止停车，但对残疾驾车者例外。

examples.en: We are making a special exception for Emma because of her condition.
examples.zh: 因为艾玛的情况特殊，我们把她作为例外。

senses.def: to object strongly to something; to be angry about something

examples.en: I take great exception to the fact that you told my wife before you told me.
examples.zh: 你还没告诉我就先对我妻子讲了，为此我非常生气。

examples.en: No one could possibly take exception to his comments.
examples.zh: 任何人都不可能对他的意见提出异议。

senses.def: except; not including

examples.en: All his novels are set in Italy with the exception of his last.
examples.zh: 他的小说除最后一部外全是以意大利为背景。

examples.en: The whole of the island was flooded with the exception of a small area in the north.
examples.zh: 除了北部一小块地方以外，整个岛都被淹没了。

senses.def: used to emphasize that the statement you are making is always true and everyone or everything is included

examples.en: All students without exception must take the English examination.
examples.zh: 所有学生都必须参加英语考试，无一例外。

examples.en: Without exception, all employees must carry their identity card with them at all times.
examples.zh: 所有雇员无一例外地任何时候都要带着身分证。

items.idm: the exception that proves the rule

senses.def: people say that something is the exception that proves the rule
senses.zh: 反证规律的例外；足以证明普遍性的例外

examples.en: Most electronics companies have not done well this year, but ours is the exception that proves the rule.
examples.zh: 今年多数电子公司都不景气，而我们公司却是普遍中的例外。

senses.def: to allow somebody not to follow the usual rule on one occasion or for one particular reason
senses.zh: 允许有例外；让…成为例外

examples.en: Children are not usually allowed in, but I'm prepared to make an exception in this case.
examples.zh: 儿童一般不允许入内，不过这次我可以破例。

examples.en: No parking is allowed, but an exception is made for disabled drivers.
examples.zh: 此处禁止停车，但对残疾驾车者例外。

examples.en: We are making a special exception for Emma because of her condition.
examples.zh: 因为艾玛的情况特殊，我们把她作为例外。

senses.def: to object strongly to something; to be angry about something

examples.en: I take great exception to the fact that you told my wife before you told me.
examples.zh: 你还没告诉我就先对我妻子讲了，为此我非常生气。

examples.en: No one could possibly take exception to his comments.
examples.zh: 任何人都不可能对他的意见提出异议。

senses.def: except; not including

examples.en: All his novels are set in Italy with the exception of his last.
examples.zh: 他的小说除最后一部外全是以意大利为背景。

examples.en: The whole of the island was flooded with the exception of a small area in the north.
examples.zh: 除了北部一小块地方以外，整个岛都被淹没了。

senses.def: used to emphasize that the statement you are making is always true and everyone or everything is included

examples.en: All students without exception must take the English examination.
examples.zh: 所有学生都必须参加英语考试，无一例外。

examples.en: Without exception, all employees must carry their identity card with them at all times.
examples.zh: 所有雇员无一例外地任何时候都要带着身分证。

senses.def: unusually good

examples.en: At the age of five he showed exceptional talent as a musician.
examples.zh: 他五岁时就表现出非凡的音乐才能。

examples.en: The quality of the recording is quite exceptional.
examples.zh: 录音质量相当不错。

senses.def: very unusual

examples.en: This deadline will be extended only in exceptional circumstances.
examples.zh: 只有在特殊情况下才会延长最后期限。

senses.def: the belief that something, especially a country or its system of government, is unusually good or successful
senses.zh: 例外论，独特论，卓异主义（尤指认为某国或其政体与众不同，特别优秀）

examples.en: The belief in its own exceptionalism is at the root of many of the country's problems.
examples.zh: 该国自以为卓异独特，这一理念是其诸多问题的根源。

senses.def: used before an adjective or adverb to emphasize how strong or unusual the quality is
senses.zh: （用于形容词和副词之前表示强调）罕见，特别，非常

examples.en: The weather, even for January, was exceptionally cold.
examples.zh: 这种天气即使在一月份也算得上非常寒冷。

examples.en: I thought Bill played exceptionally well.
examples.zh: 我认为比尔的球打得特别好。

examples.en: There was an exceptionally high tide.
examples.zh: 发生了一次特别高的满潮。

examples.en: an exceptionally gifted child
examples.zh: 极具天赋的孩子

senses.def: only in unusual circumstances
senses.zh: 只有在特殊情况下；例外地

examples.en: Exceptionally, students may be accepted without formal qualifications.
examples.zh: 在特殊情况下，也可能接受无正式文凭的学生。

senses.def: a short piece of writing, music, film, etc. taken from a longer whole
senses.zh: 摘录；节选；（音乐、电影的）片段

examples.en: Read the following excerpt from one of Milton’s poems.
examples.zh: 阅读以下弥尔顿一首诗的摘录。

examples.en: They only played a short excerpt.
examples.zh: 他们只播放了一小段片段。

senses.def: to take a short piece of writing, music, film, etc. from a longer whole
senses.zh: 摘录；节选；（音乐、电影的）片段

examples.en: The document was excerpted from an unidentified FBI file.
examples.zh: 文件摘自来源不明的联邦调查局档案。

senses.def: more than is necessary, reasonable or acceptable

examples.en: You can throw away any excess.
examples.zh: 凡多余的你都可以扔掉。

examples.en: Are you suffering from an excess of stress in your life?
examples.zh: 你生活中的压力太大吗？

examples.en: In an excess of enthusiasm I agreed to work late.
examples.zh: 我一时热情过度答应了加班。

examples.en: He was now eating to excess as a result of stress.
examples.zh: 由于压力，他现在吃得过多。

examples.en: The increase will not be in excess of (= more than) two per cent.
examples.zh: 增加幅度不会超过百分之二。

senses.def: an amount by which something is larger than something else

examples.en: We cover costs up to £600 and then you pay the excess.
examples.zh: 我们最多支付 600 英镑的费用，超出的部分由你支付。

senses.def: the part of an insurance claim that a person has to pay while the insurance company pays the rest

examples.en: There is an excess of £100 on each claim under this policy.
examples.zh: 本保险单每次索赔均有 100 英镑的免赔额。

examples.en: Increasing the excess on home insurance from the standard £50 to £100 is likely to save 15%.
examples.zh: 将家庭保险的超额费用从标准的 50 英镑增加到 100 英镑可能会节省 15%。

senses.def: the fact of doing too much of something, especially eating or drinking

examples.en: He gave in to bouts of alcoholic excess.
examples.zh: 几次过量饮酒之后他就扛不住了。

senses.def: extreme behaviour that is unacceptable, illegal or morally wrong

examples.en: We need a free press to curb government excesses.
examples.zh: 我们需要新闻自由来遏制政府滥用权力。

examples.en: legislation to control the worst excesses of the press
examples.zh: 立法控制媒体最严重的过激行为

senses.def: in addition to an amount that is necessary, usual or legal
senses.zh: 超额的；额外的；附加的；过度的

examples.en: Excess food is stored as fat.
examples.zh: 多余的食物作为脂肪贮存起来。

examples.en: Driving with excess alcohol in the blood is a serious offence.
examples.zh: 血液里酒精含量过高时驾车是严重的违法行为。

examples.en: The book is hard to obtain, because of excess demand following the author’s appearance on TV.
examples.zh: 这本书很难买到，因为随着作者出现在电视上，需求过剩。

senses.def: required as extra payment

examples.en: The full excess fare had to be paid.
examples.zh: 必须支付全部超额车费。

senses.def: bags, cases, etc. taken on to a plane that weigh more than the amount each passenger is allowed to carry without paying extra

examples.en: If your luggage exceeds 23 kg you will have to pay for excess baggage.
examples.zh: 如果您的行李超过 23 公斤，您将需要支付超重行李费。

examples.en: Trying to lose weight? Here are some suggestions to help you get rid of that excess baggage.
examples.zh: 想减肥吗？这里有一些建议可以帮助您摆脱多余的包袱。

senses.def: greater than what seems reasonable or appropriate

examples.en: They complained about the excessive noise coming from the upstairs flat.
examples.zh: 他们抱怨楼上发出的噪音太大。

examples.en: The amounts she borrowed were not excessive.
examples.zh: 她借的数量没有超额。

examples.en: Excessive eating increases the risk of heart failure.
examples.zh: 过量饮食会增加心力衰竭的风险。

examples.en: He claimed that the police had used excessive force.
examples.zh: 他称警方过度使用武力。

senses.def: to a much greater level or degree than seems reasonable or appropriate

examples.en: excessively high prices
examples.zh: 过高的价格

examples.en: The country relies excessively on borrowing from abroad.
examples.zh: 该国过度依赖国外借款。

senses.def: an act of giving something to somebody or doing something for somebody and receiving something in return

examples.en: The exchange of prisoners took place this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上交换了俘虏。

examples.en: We need to promote an open exchange of ideas and information.
examples.zh: 我们需要促进思想和信息的公开交流。

examples.en: an exchange of glances/insults
examples.zh: 互换眼色；相互侮辱

examples.en: an exchange of fire (= between enemy soldiers)
examples.zh: 交火

examples.en: I buy you lunch and you fix my computer. Is that a fair exchange?
examples.zh: 我请你吃午饭，你给我修计算机，这算是公平交易吧？

examples.en: Wool and timber were sent to Egypt in exchange for linen or papyrus.
examples.zh: 羊毛和木材被运到埃及去交换亚麻布或纸莎草纸。

examples.en: I'll type your report if you'll babysit in exchange.
examples.zh: 如果你愿意代我照看孩子，我就把这个报告给你打出来。

senses.def: the process of changing an amount of one currency for an equal value of another

examples.en: currency exchange facilities
examples.zh: 货币兑换服务

examples.en: Where can I find the best exchange rate/rate of exchange?
examples.zh: 在什么地方才能获得最好的兑换价？

senses.def: an arrangement when two people or groups from different countries visit each other’s homes or do each other’s jobs for a short time
senses.zh: （不同国家人或团体之间的）交流，互访

examples.en: Our school does an exchange with a school in France.
examples.zh: 我们学校与法国的一所学校进行交流。

examples.en: trade and cultural exchanges with China
examples.zh: 与中国的贸易和文化交流

examples.en: Nick went on the French exchange.
examples.zh: 尼克到法国去作互访了。

senses.group: between two countries 两国之间

senses.def: a conversation or an argument

examples.en: There was only time for a brief exchange.
examples.zh: 只有简短的交谈时间。

examples.en: The prime minister was involved in a heated exchange with Opposition MPs.
examples.zh: 首相参与了和反对党议员的激烈争论。

examples.en: There was an angry exchange between the two players.
examples.zh: 两名选手互呛了几句。

senses.def: a building where business people met in the past to buy and sell a particular type of goods

examples.en: the old Corn Exchange
examples.zh: 古老的谷物交易所

senses.def: a place where phone calls are connected so that people can speak to each other
senses.zh: 电话交换台；总机；电话局

senses.def: to give something to somebody and at the same time receive the same type of thing from them

examples.en: to exchange news/information
examples.zh: 交换新闻/信息

examples.en: We use the forum to exchange ideas.
examples.zh: 我们利用这个论坛交流思想。

examples.en: Juliet and David exchanged glances (= they looked at each other).
examples.zh: 朱丽叶和戴维相互看了看对方。

examples.en: Everyone in the group exchanged email addresses.
examples.zh: 所有的组员都相互交换了电子邮件地址。

examples.en: The two men exchanged blows (= hit each other).
examples.zh: 两个男人相互殴打起来。

examples.en: I shook hands and exchanged a few words with the manager.
examples.zh: 我和经理握了握手，交谈了几句。

examples.en: He read the letters exchanged between Anna and her friend.
examples.zh: 他读了安娜和她的朋友之间的通信。

senses.def: to change an amount of one currency for an equal value of another

examples.en: Where can I exchange my money?
examples.zh: 我在哪里可以兑换货币？

examples.en: You can exchange your currency for dollars in the hotel.
examples.zh: 你可在旅馆把你的钱兑换成美元。

senses.def: to give or return something that you have and get something different or better instead

examples.en: If it doesn't fit, take it back and the store will exchange it.
examples.zh: 如果不合适就把它拿回来，商店将给你更换。

examples.en: I need to exchange this for a larger size.
examples.zh: 我需要把这个换成大一点的。

senses.def: when a buyer and seller exchange contracts
senses.zh: （尤指买卖房屋或土地时）订立契约

examples.en: The firm has just exchanged contracts on a nine-acre site.
examples.zh: 该公司刚刚就一块九英亩的土地交换了合同。

examples.en: We exchanged on the house last week.
examples.zh: 上周我们交换了房子。

senses.def: to have an argument with somebody

examples.en: We've had words.
examples.zh: 我们吵过架。

examples.en: Words were exchanged.
examples.zh: 发生过争吵了。

senses.def: to have an argument with somebody

examples.en: We've had words.
examples.zh: 我们吵过架。

examples.en: Words were exchanged.
examples.zh: 发生过争吵了。

senses.def: a former British magazine that consisted entirely of advertisements, mostly put in by individual people or small businesses. It was published every week and was started in 1868. In 2009 the magazine stopped being published, and now the advertisements, mainly for cars and other vehicles, only appear on the Exchange and Mart website.
senses.zh: 以前的英国杂志，完全由广告组成，大部分由个人或小型企业投放。该杂志每周出版一次，始于1868年。2009年该杂志停止出版，现在主要用于汽车和其他车辆的广告仅出现在Exchange and Mart网站上。

senses.def: that can be exchanged
senses.zh: 可交换的；可交易的；可兑换的；可更换的

examples.en: The vouchers are exchangeable for goods at selected stores.
examples.zh: 这些代金券可在定点商店兑换商品。

senses.def: the government department that controlled public money. This department is now called the Treasury
the public or national supply of money

examples.en: This resulted in a considerable loss to the exchequer.
examples.zh: 这使国库遭受了重大损失。

senses.def: a government tax on some goods made, sold or used within a country

examples.en: new excise duties on low-alcohol drinks
examples.zh: 低酒精饮料新的消费税

examples.en: a sharp increase in vehicle excise duty
examples.zh: 车辆消费税急剧增加

examples.en: an excise officer (= an official whose job is to collect excise)
examples.zh: 国内消费税务官

senses.def: to remove something completely

examples.en: Certain passages were excised from the book.
examples.zh: 书中某些段落已删去。

examples.en: He carefully excised any passages that might cause offence.
examples.zh: 他小心翼翼地删除了任何可能引起冒犯的段落。

examples.en: The sensor improves the precision with which surgeons can excise brain tumours.
examples.zh: 这种传感器提高了外科医生切除脑瘤的精确度。

senses.def: the act of removing something completely from something; the thing removed

examples.en: to demonstrate three types of surgical excision
examples.zh: 演示三种类型的手术切除

examples.en: The numerous excisions have destroyed the literary value of the text.
examples.zh: 大量的删减破坏了文本的文学价值。

senses.def: the fact of becoming excited easily

examples.en: His excitability is infectious.
examples.zh: 他的兴奋具有感染力。

senses.def: likely to become easily excited

examples.en: She had trouble controlling the class of excitable ten-year-olds.
examples.zh: 她很难管束班里这些易兴奋的十岁儿童。

senses.def: to make somebody feel very pleased, interested or enthusiastic, especially about something that is going to happen

examples.en: The prospect of a year in India greatly excited her.
examples.zh: 有望在印度待上一年使她激动万分。

senses.def: to make somebody nervous or upset and unable to relax

examples.en: Try not to excite your baby too much before bedtime.
examples.zh: 睡觉前尽量别使宝宝太兴奋。

examples.en: Don't excite yourself (= keep calm).
examples.zh: 别激动。

senses.def: to make somebody feel a particular emotion or react in a particular way

examples.en: to excite attention/curiosity/admiration
examples.zh: 引起注意／好奇心／爱慕

examples.en: The news has certainly excited comment (= made people talk about it).
examples.zh: 这消息已经使人们议论纷纷了。

examples.en: The advertising campaign failed to excite much interest in consumers.
examples.zh: 广告宣传未能引起消费者很大的兴趣。

senses.def: to make somebody feel sexual desire
to make a part of the body or part of a physical system more active
senses.zh: 使（身体部位或身体机能）活动；刺激…的活动

examples.en: The energy of an electron is sufficient to excite the atom.
examples.zh: 一个电子的能量已足以激发原子。

senses.def: in a happy and enthusiastic way

examples.en: She waved excitedly as the car approached.
examples.zh: 汽车开近时她激动地挥手。

senses.def: the state of feeling or showing happiness and enthusiasm

examples.en: The news caused great excitement among her friends.
examples.zh: 这消息使她的朋友们兴奋不已。

examples.en: The sport needs new stars to generate excitement.
examples.zh: 这项运动需要新的明星来激发激情。

examples.en: to feel a surge/thrill/shiver of excitement
examples.zh: 感到一阵激动

examples.en: There's a genuine sense of excitement because there is a British player in the final.
examples.zh: 因为决赛中有一位英国选手，所以我们真的很兴奋。

examples.en: He did not share their excitement about the project.
examples.zh: 他没有像他们一样为这个项目感到兴奋。

examples.en: I could hardly contain my excitement about going with Brandon.
examples.zh: 我几乎无法抑制与布兰登一起去的兴奋。

examples.en: She told of her excitement at the prospect of a new career as a pilot.
examples.zh: 她讲述了自己即将开启飞行员生涯的激动心情。

examples.en: He was unable to control his excitement at hearing this.
examples.zh: 听到这句话，他无法控制自己的兴奋。

examples.en: I can remember the excitement of winning that game.
examples.zh: 我记得赢得那场比赛时的激动心情。

examples.en: The app enables users to experience the excitement of space exploration.
examples.zh: 该应用程序使用户能够体验太空探索的兴奋。

examples.en: You'll jump up from your seat with excitement.
examples.zh: 你会兴奋得从座位上跳起来。

examples.en: The dog leapt and wagged its tail in excitement.
examples.zh: 狗兴奋得摇着尾巴跳来跳去。

examples.en: In her excitement she dropped her glass.
examples.zh: 她一激动把杯子摔了。

senses.def: something that you find exciting

examples.en: The new job was not without its excitements.
examples.zh: 这个新工作并非枯燥无味。

senses.def: the state of feeling sexual desire
in a way that causes great interest or excitement
senses.zh: 令人激动的；使人兴奋的

examples.en: an excitingly fast game
examples.zh: 令人兴奋的快速游戏

examples.en: Excitingly, the Olympics are yet to come.
examples.zh: 令人兴奋的是，奥运会还没有到来。

senses.def: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially because of strong emotion or pain
senses.zh: （尤因强烈的情感或痛苦而）惊叫，呼喊

examples.en: She opened her eyes and exclaimed in delight at the scene.
examples.zh: 看到这情景，她瞪着眼睛，高兴得大叫起来。

examples.en: ‘It isn't fair!’, he exclaimed angrily.
examples.zh: “这不公平！”他气愤地喊道。

examples.en: She exclaimed that it was useless.
examples.zh: 她大叫说这是无效的。

synonyms.words: cry out ▪ exclaim ▪ blurt ▪ burst out

intro.en: These words all mean to shout or say something loudly or suddenly.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含突然大声喊叫、说话之义。

items.def: to shout or say something loudly to attract somebody’s attention:
items.zh: 指大声呼叫或说话以吸引注意

examples.en: I thought I heard someone calling.
examples.zh: 我仿佛听见有人在呼喊。

items.def: to shout something loudly, especially when you need help or are in trouble:
items.zh: 尤指需要帮助或陷入困境时大声呼喊

examples.en: She cried out for help.
examples.zh: 她大声呼救。

items.def: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially because of a strong emotion:
items.zh: 尤指因强烈的情感而突然大声说话

examples.en: ‘It isn’t fair!’ he exclaimed angrily.
examples.zh: “这不公平！”他气愤地喊道。

items.def: to say something suddenly and without thinking carefully enough:
items.zh: 指脱口而出

examples.en: I blurted out the answer without thinking.
examples.zh: 我想都没想就脱口说出了答案。

items.def: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially with a lot of emotion:
items.zh: 尤指突然激动地大声喊叫

examples.en: ‘He’s a bully!’ the little boy burst out.
examples.zh: “他欺负人！”小男孩突然大叫。

senses.def: a short sound, word or phrase spoken suddenly to express an emotion. Oh!

examples.en: He gave an exclamation of surprise.
examples.zh: 他发出一声惊叹。

examples.en: She took his hand and uttered an exclamation of shock.
examples.zh: 她握住他的手，发出一声震惊的惊呼。

senses.def: the mark ( ! ) that is written after an exclamation
expressing surprise or strong feelings
to deliberately not include something in what you are doing or considering
senses.zh: 不包括；不放在考虑之列

examples.en: The cost of borrowing has been excluded from the inflation figures.
examples.zh: 通胀数字未包括借贷费用。

examples.en: Try excluding fat from your diet.
examples.zh: 平时用餐时试一试不吃含脂肪的食物。

examples.en: Buses run every hour, Sundays excluded.
examples.zh: 公共汽车每小时一班，星期天除外。

senses.def: to prevent somebody/something from entering a place or taking part in something
senses.zh: 防止…进入；阻止…参加；把…排斥在外

examples.en: Women are still excluded from some London clubs.
examples.zh: 伦敦有些俱乐部仍然拒绝妇女参加。

examples.en: Concern is growing over the number of children excluded from school (= not allowed to attend because of bad behaviour).
examples.zh: 大批儿童遭学校开除，人们对此越来越关注。

examples.en: She felt excluded by the other girls (= they did not let her join in what they were doing).
examples.zh: 她感到自己受到其他女孩子的排斥。

senses.def: to decide that something is not possible
senses.zh: 排除（…的可能性）；认为…不可能

examples.en: We should not exclude the possibility of negotiation.
examples.zh: 我们不应该排除谈判的可能性。

examples.en: The police have excluded theft as a motive for the murder.
examples.zh: 警方已排除这起谋杀案中有偷窃的动机。

examples.en: The possibility of error cannot be absolutely excluded.
examples.zh: 出错的可能性无法绝对排除。

senses.def: the act of preventing somebody/something from entering a place or taking part in something

examples.en: He was disappointed with his exclusion from the England squad.
examples.zh: 他对自己没有入选英格兰队感到失望。

examples.en: Exclusion of air creates a vacuum in the bottle.
examples.zh: 瓶子里的空气排除后就产生真空。

examples.en: Memories of the past filled her mind to the exclusion of all else.
examples.zh: 她满脑子全是对过去的回忆，其他事情都不想了。

senses.def: a person or thing that is not included in something
senses.zh: 不包括在内的人（或事物）；被排除在外的人（或事物）

examples.en: Check the list of exclusions in the insurance policy.
examples.zh: 检查一下保险单上的除外责任清单。

senses.def: the act of deciding that something is not possible

examples.en: the exclusion of robbery as a motive
examples.zh: 排除抢劫动机

senses.def: a situation in which a child is banned from attending school because of bad behaviour

examples.en: the exclusion of disruptive students from school
examples.zh: 把捣蛋的学生开除出学校

examples.en: Two exclusions from one school in the same week is unusual.
examples.zh: 一所学校在一周内就有两起开除学生的事是少有的。

examples.en: disciplinary measures including exclusion from school
examples.zh: 包括开除学籍在内的纪律措施

senses.def: an official order not to go to a particular place

examples.en: The judge placed an exclusion order on him, banning him from city centre shops.
examples.zh: 法官给他下了禁令，禁止他进入市中心的店铺。

senses.def: an area where people are not allowed to enter because it is dangerous or is used for secret activities

examples.en: Armed forces have set up an exclusion zone around the island.
examples.zh: 武装部队在该岛周围设立了禁区。

examples.en: An enemy plane was shot down after it violated the exclusion zone.
examples.zh: 一架敌机因违反禁区规定被击落。

senses.def: designed to prevent a particular person or group of people from taking part in something or doing something
only to be used by one particular person or group; only given to one particular person or group
senses.zh: （个人或集体）专用的，专有的，独有的，独占的

examples.en: The hotel has exclusive access to the beach.
examples.zh: 这家旅馆有通向海滩的专用通道。

examples.en: exclusive rights to televise the World Cup
examples.zh: 世界杯赛的独家电视播放权

examples.en: His mother has told ‘The Times’ about his death in an exclusive interview (= not given to any other newspaper).
examples.zh: 他的母亲在接受《泰晤士报》的独家采访时谈到他的死亡。

senses.def: not very willing to allow new people to become members, especially if they are from a lower social class
senses.zh: 排外的；不愿接收（较低社会阶层）新成员的

examples.en: He belongs to an exclusive club.
examples.zh: 他参加的是一个不轻易吸收新会员的俱乐部。

examples.en: Their clientele was exclusive and wealthy.
examples.zh: 他们的客户是独特且富有的。

senses.def: of a high quality and expensive and therefore not often bought or used by most people

examples.en: an exclusive hotel
examples.zh: 高级酒店

examples.en: exclusive designer clothes
examples.zh: 高档名牌服装

senses.def: not including anything else

examples.en: He had an exclusive focus on success and making money.
examples.zh: 他一心想的是成功和赚钱。

examples.en: This list is not exclusive.
examples.zh: 这张清单不排除其他项目。

senses.def: not including somebody/something

examples.en: The price is for accommodation only, exclusive of meals.
examples.zh: 此价只包括住宿，饭费除外。

senses.def: not able to exist or be a true statement at the same time as something else

examples.en: The two options are not mutually exclusive (= you can have them both).
examples.zh: 这两种选择并不相互排斥。

senses.def: an item of news or a story about famous people that is published in only one newspaper or magazine or broadcast on only one TV or radio station
senses.zh: 独家新闻；独家专文；独家报道

examples.en: We feature an exclusive on the mothers whose babies were swapped at birth.
examples.zh: 我们独家报道了婴儿出生时被交换的母亲。

examples.en: The paper printed a world exclusive on the presidential scandal.
examples.zh: 该报刊登了有关总统丑闻的全球独家报道。

senses.def: for only one particular person, group or use
senses.zh: （仅供某些人）专用地，独享地；仅作特定用途

examples.en: The resort caters almost exclusively for a high-society public.
examples.zh: 这个度假胜地几乎只接待上流社会的人。

examples.en: Some products are labelled exclusively for indoor or outdoor use.
examples.zh: 有些产品标明只供室内或室外使用。

senses.def: completely; without including anybody or anything else

examples.en: a charity that relies almost exclusively on voluntary contributions
examples.zh: 几乎全靠自愿捐赠的慈善机构

senses.def: the fact of being of a high quality and expensive and therefore not often bought or used by most people

examples.en: Many celebrities visit the resort, attracted by its exclusiveness.
examples.zh: 许多名人都被它的独特性所吸引而来到这里。

senses.def: the practice in a group or society of not allowing other people from different groups to become members or be included

examples.en: the exclusiveness of some social classes before 1914
examples.zh: 1914年之前某些社会阶层的排他性

examples.en: He described his experiences of exclusiveness and bullying at school.
examples.zh: 他描述了他在学校遭受排他和欺凌的经历。

senses.def: the fact of being of a high quality and expensive and therefore not often bought or used by most people

examples.en: The resort still preserves a feeling of exclusivity.
examples.zh: 这个度假胜地仍然保持着特有的情调。

examples.en: a designer whose clothes have not lost their exclusivity
examples.zh: 设计师的衣服并没有失去其独特性

senses.def: the practice in a group or society of not allowing other people from different groups to become members or be included

examples.en: The club has been criticized for its exclusivity and elitism.
examples.zh: 这个俱乐部因其排外及精英主义而受到批评。

senses.def: to punish somebody by officially stating that they can no longer be a member of a Christian Church
senses.zh: （尤指罗马天主教）开除…的教籍，把…逐出教会

senses.def: the act of punishing somebody by officially stating that they can no longer be a member of a Christian Church, especially the Roman Catholic Church

examples.en: They were threatened with excommunication.
examples.zh: 他们受到取消教籍的威胁。

senses.def: to make a person’s skin painful, and often red, so that it starts to come off
to criticize somebody/something severely
a medical condition in which a person's skin becomes painful, and often red, and so starts to come off; an area of skin that is affected by this condition
senses.zh: 切除：一个人的皮肤变得疼痛，往往发红，因此开始脱落的医疗状况;受此情况影响的皮肤区域

senses.def: the act of criticizing somebody/something severely
solid waste matter that is passed from the body through the bowels

examples.en: the pollution of drinking water by untreated human excrement
examples.zh: 未经处理的人体排泄物对饮用水的污染

examples.en: There was excrement smeared up the wall.
examples.zh: 墙上沾满了粪便。

senses.def: relating to excrement
an ugly part that has grown on a part of an animal’s body or on a plant, caused by disease or abnormality

examples.en: A hard, bony excrescence was visible above one of the animal’s hooves.
examples.zh: 在动物的一只蹄子上方可以看到一个坚硬的骨赘。

examples.en: The new office block is an excrescence (= it is very ugly).
examples.zh: 这座新办公楼很是煞风景。

senses.def: solid and liquid waste matter passed from the body

examples.en: human excreta
examples.zh: 人体排泄物

senses.def: to pass solid or liquid waste matter from the body
the act of passing solid or liquid waste matter from the body; the solid or liquid waste matter that is passed in this way

examples.en: the excretion of toxic substances through the skin
examples.zh: 有毒物质通过皮肤排出体外

examples.en: It's the corals' excretions that become the scaffolding of coral reefs.
examples.zh: 珊瑚的排泄物成为珊瑚礁的脚手架。

senses.def: connected with getting rid of waste matter from the body

examples.en: the excretory organs
examples.zh: 排泄器官

senses.def: extremely painful or bad
senses.zh: 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的

examples.en: The pain in my back was excruciating.
examples.zh: 我的背疼痛难忍。

examples.en: She groaned at the memory, suffering all over again the excruciating embarrassment of those moments.
examples.zh: 她在回忆中呻吟，又一次饱尝那时所经历的极度困窘。

examples.en: He rolled on the floor in excruciating agony.
examples.zh: 他痛苦地在地板上打滚。

examples.en: The process is painful, but not excruciating.
examples.zh: 整个过程是痛苦的，但并非难以忍受。

synonyms.words: sore ▪ raw ▪ inflamed ▪ excruciating ▪ burning ▪ itchy

intro.en: These words all describe something that causes you physical pain.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指使人肉体上疼痛的。

items.def: causing you physical pain. Painful can describe a part of the body, illness, injury, treatment or death:
items.zh: painful 可用于描述身体部位、疾病、受伤、治疗或死亡等

items.def: (of a part of the body) painful and often red, especially because of infection or because a muscle has been used too much:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）发炎疼痛的、肌肉酸痛的

examples.en: a sore throat
examples.zh: 咽喉疼

items.def: (of a part of the body) red and painful, for example because of an infection or because the skin has been damaged:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）红肿疼痛的、破损的、擦伤的

examples.en: The skin on her feet had been rubbed raw.
examples.zh: 她脚上的皮磨破了。

items.def: (of a part of the body) painful, red and hot because of an infection or injury:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）发炎的、红肿的

examples.en: The wound had become inflamed.
examples.zh: 伤口发炎了。

items.def: extremely painful. Excruciating can describe feelings, treatments or death but not parts of the body:
items.zh: excruciating 可用于描述情感、治疗或死亡，而非身体部位

items.def: painful and giving a feeling of being very hot:
items.zh: 指火辣辣地痛的

examples.en: She felt a burning sensation in her throat.
examples.zh: 她感到咽喉火辣辣的疼。

items.def: giving an uncomfortable feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch; having this feeling:
items.zh: 指发痒的

examples.en: an itchy rash
examples.zh: 发痒的皮疹

senses.def: in an extremely bad or painful way
senses.zh: 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的

examples.en: excruciatingly uncomfortable
examples.zh: 极不舒服

examples.en: excruciatingly painful/boring/embarrassing
examples.zh: 极其痛苦／乏味／难堪

senses.def: to prove or state officially that somebody is not guilty of something
senses.zh: 证明（或宣布）无罪；为（某人）开脱

examples.en: The defendant was able to exculpate himself from liability.
examples.zh: 被告能够为自己开脱责任。

senses.def: the act of proving or stating officially that somebody is not guilty of something
senses.zh: 证明（或宣布）无罪；为（某人）开脱

senses.def: a short journey made for pleasure, especially one that has been organized for a group of people

examples.en: They've gone on an excursion to York.
examples.zh: 他们到约克旅游去了。

examples.en: There are regular weekend excursions throughout the summer.
examples.zh: 整个夏季都会定期举办周末短途旅行。

senses.def: a short period of trying a new or different activity

examples.en: After a brief excursion into drama, he concentrated on his main interest, which was poetry.
examples.zh: 他短暂涉猎戏剧之后便把全部精力投入到他的主要兴趣——诗歌中去了。

examples.en: her first excursion into business
examples.zh: 她第一次涉足商务

synonyms.words: journey ▪ tour ▪ expedition ▪ excursion ▪ outing ▪ day out

intro.en: These are all words for an act of travelling to a place.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指旅行、旅游。

items.def: an act of travelling from one place to another, and usually back again:
items.zh: 通常指往返的旅行

examples.en: a business trip
examples.zh: 出差

items.def: an act of travelling from one place to another, especially when they are a long way apart:
items.zh: 尤指长途旅行

examples.en: a long and difficult journey across the mountains
examples.zh: 漫长而艰难的翻山旅行

items.def: a journey made for pleasure during which several different places are visited:
items.zh: 指游览多地的旅行、旅游

examples.en: a tour of Bavaria
examples.zh: 巴伐利亚之旅

items.def: an organized journey with a particular purpose, especially to find out about a place that is not well known:
items.zh: 指远征、探险、考察

examples.en: the first expedition to the South Pole
examples.zh: 首次去南极的探险

items.def: a short trip made for pleasure, especially one that has been organized for a group of people:
items.zh: 尤指集体远足、短途旅行

examples.en: We went on an all-day excursion to the island.
examples.zh: 我们到岛上去游览了一整天。

items.def: a short trip made for pleasure or education, usually with a group of people and lasting no more than a day:
items.zh: 指集体出外游玩或学习，通常不超过一天

examples.en: The children were on a day’s outing from school.
examples.zh: 孩子们离校游览了一天。

items.def: a trip to somewhere for a day, especially for pleasure:
items.zh: 指一日游

examples.en: We had a day out at the beach.
examples.zh: 我们在海滩玩了一天。

senses.def: that can be excused

examples.en: Doing it once was just about excusable—doing it twice was certainly not.
examples.zh: 这种事干一次还可以原谅，干两次就绝对不能了。

senses.def: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour

examples.en: Late again! What's your excuse this time?
examples.zh: 又迟到了！你这次有什么借口？

examples.en: I tried desperately to think of a good excuse.
examples.zh: 我绞尽脑汁想找个好理由。

examples.en: a lame/feeble/poor/flimsy excuse
examples.zh: 蹩脚/软弱/可怜/站不住脚的借口

examples.en: a reasonable/valid excuse
examples.zh: 合理/有效的借口

examples.en: I know I missed the deadline, but I have an excuse.
examples.zh: 我知道我没赶上截止日期，但我是有理由的。

examples.en: There's no excuse for such behaviour.
examples.zh: 这种行为说不过去。

examples.en: His excuse for forgetting her birthday was that he had lost his diary.
examples.zh: 他辩解说因为日记本丢了才忘了她的生日。

examples.en: You don't have to make excuses for her (= try to think of reasons for her behaviour).
examples.zh: 你不必为她辩解了。

examples.en: It's late. I'm afraid I'll have to make my excuses (= say I'm sorry, give my reasons and leave).
examples.zh: 时间不早了。很抱歉，我得告辞了。

senses.def: a good reason that you give for doing something that you want to do for other reasons

examples.en: Eating ice cream for a sore throat isn't really a cure, but I like it, so any excuse!
examples.zh: 吃冰淇淋治疗喉咙痛并不能真正治愈，但我喜欢它，所以有任何借口！

examples.en: It's just an excuse for a party.
examples.zh: 这只是聚会的一个借口。

examples.en: Any occasion is a good excuse for having a barbecue.
examples.zh: 任何场合都是烧烤的好借口。

examples.en: It gave me an excuse to take the car.
examples.zh: 这使我有理由开车去。

examples.en: He tried unsuccessfully to find an excuse to leave.
examples.zh: 他试图找借口离开，但没有成功。

examples.en: The demonstration was used as an excuse to impose martial law.
examples.zh: 示威被用作实施戒严的借口。

senses.def: a very bad example of something

examples.en: Why get involved with that pathetic excuse for a human being?
examples.zh: 为什么要与那个讨厌的家伙混在一起？

senses.def: a note written by a parent or doctor to explain why a student cannot go to school or somebody cannot go to work
senses.zh: 假条（家长或医生写明请假原因）

senses.def: to forgive somebody for something that they have done, for example not being polite or making a small mistake

examples.en: Please excuse the mess.
examples.zh: 这里凌乱不堪，请见谅。

examples.en: You must excuse my father—he's not always that rude.
examples.zh: 你一定要原谅我父亲，他并不总是那样粗鲁无礼。

examples.en: She had been excused for her actions.
examples.zh: 她的行为已得到原谅。

examples.en: I hope you'll excuse me for being so late.
examples.zh: 我来得这么晚，希望你能原谅。

examples.en: You might be excused for thinking that Ben is in charge (= he is not, but it is an easy mistake to make).
examples.zh: 你误以为是本在负责，这是情有可原的。

examples.en: Excuse me interrupting you.
examples.zh: 对不起，打扰你一下。

examples.en: Excuse my interrupting you.
examples.zh: 对不起，打扰你一下。

examples.en: If you'll excuse me pointing this out, I think you've made a mistake here.
examples.zh: 如果您能原谅我指出这一点，我认为您在这里犯了一个错误。

senses.def: to make your or somebody else’s behaviour seem less offensive by finding reasons for it

examples.en: Nothing can excuse such rudeness.
examples.zh: 如此粗鲁无礼不能原谅。

examples.en: He tried to excuse his behaviour as ‘a bit of harmless fun’.
examples.zh: 他试图为自己的行为辩解，说那是“无伤大雅的小玩笑”。

examples.en: I could try to excuse myself, but why bother?
examples.zh: 我可以设法为自己辩解，但何必找那麻烦呢？

examples.en: Should her previous good actions excuse her for the terrible things she is doing now?
examples.zh: 她以前的善行是否应该为她现在所做的可怕的事情辩护？

examples.en: He excused himself for being late by explaining that his flight had been delayed.
examples.zh: 他解释说他的航班延误了，以此为自己迟到找借口。

senses.def: to allow somebody to leave; to say in a polite way that you are leaving
senses.zh: 准许…离开；请求准予离开；（离开前）请求原谅

examples.en: Now if you'll excuse me, I'm a very busy man.
examples.zh: 如果可以，我先行一步了。我很忙。

examples.en: She excused herself and left the meeting early.
examples.zh: 她打了声招呼就提前离开了会场。

senses.def: to allow somebody to not do something that they should normally do

examples.en: She was excused from giving evidence because of her age.
examples.zh: 她因年龄关系获准免于作证。

examples.en: He was excused military service because of poor health.
examples.zh: 他因身体不好而免服兵役。

senses.def: used to say that you are sorry for swearing
senses.zh: 请原谅我说脏话了；不好意思，我骂人了

senses.def: used to politely get somebody’s attention, especially somebody you do not know
senses.zh: （引起尤其是陌生人的注意）劳驾，请原谅

examples.en: Excuse me, is this the way to the station?
examples.zh: 劳驾，这是去车站的路吗？

senses.def: used to politely ask somebody to move so that you can get past them
senses.zh: （客气地请人让路）对不起，劳驾，借光

examples.en: Excuse me, could you let me through?
examples.zh: 对不起，能让我过去吗？

senses.def: used to say that you are sorry for interrupting somebody or behaving in a slightly rude way
senses.zh: （因打扰别人或失礼表示歉意）对不起，请原谅

examples.en: Guy sneezed loudly. ‘Excuse me,’ he said.
examples.zh: 盖伊大声打了个喷嚏，然后说了声“对不起”。

senses.def: used to disagree politely with somebody
senses.zh: （婉转地表示不赞成）对不起，请原谅，很抱歉

examples.en: Excuse me, but I don't think that's true.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，我认为这不是真的。

senses.def: used to politely tell somebody that you are going to leave or talk to somebody else
senses.zh: （婉转地表示要离开或要与另外的人讲话）对不起，请原谅，抱歉

examples.en: ‘Excuse me for a moment,’ she said and left the room.
examples.zh: 她说了声“很抱歉，失陪一会儿”就离开了房间。

senses.def: used to say sorry for pushing somebody or doing something wrong
senses.zh: （因挤着别人或做错了事表示歉意）对不起，请原谅，很抱歉

examples.en: Oh, excuse me. I didn't see you there.
examples.zh: 啊呀，对不起，我没看到你在那里。

senses.def: used when you did not hear what somebody said and you want them to repeat it
senses.zh: （没听清楚，请对方再说一遍）对不起，请再说一遍

senses.def: used to say that you are sorry for swearing
senses.zh: 请原谅我说脏话了；不好意思，我骂人了

senses.def: used to politely get somebody’s attention, especially somebody you do not know
senses.zh: （引起尤其是陌生人的注意）劳驾，请原谅

examples.en: Excuse me, is this the way to the station?
examples.zh: 劳驾，这是去车站的路吗？

senses.def: used to politely ask somebody to move so that you can get past them
senses.zh: （客气地请人让路）对不起，劳驾，借光

examples.en: Excuse me, could you let me through?
examples.zh: 对不起，能让我过去吗？

senses.def: used to say that you are sorry for interrupting somebody or behaving in a slightly rude way
senses.zh: （因打扰别人或失礼表示歉意）对不起，请原谅

examples.en: Guy sneezed loudly. ‘Excuse me,’ he said.
examples.zh: 盖伊大声打了个喷嚏，然后说了声“对不起”。

senses.def: used to disagree politely with somebody
senses.zh: （婉转地表示不赞成）对不起，请原谅，很抱歉

examples.en: Excuse me, but I don't think that's true.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，我认为这不是真的。

senses.def: used to politely tell somebody that you are going to leave or talk to somebody else
senses.zh: （婉转地表示要离开或要与另外的人讲话）对不起，请原谅，抱歉

examples.en: ‘Excuse me for a moment,’ she said and left the room.
examples.zh: 她说了声“很抱歉，失陪一会儿”就离开了房间。

senses.def: used to say sorry for pushing somebody or doing something wrong
senses.zh: （因挤着别人或做错了事表示歉意）对不起，请原谅，很抱歉

examples.en: Oh, excuse me. I didn't see you there.
examples.zh: 啊呀，对不起，我没看到你在那里。

senses.def: used when you did not hear what somebody said and you want them to repeat it
senses.zh: （没听清楚，请对方再说一遍）对不起，请再说一遍

synonyms.words: explanation ▪ grounds ▪ basis ▪ excuse ▪ motive ▪ justification ▪ pretext

intro.en: These are all words for a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指事情发生或做某事的原因、理由、解释。

items.def: a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done; a fact that makes it right or fair to do something:
items.zh: 指某事发生或做某事的原因、理由、解释、道理

examples.en: He said no but he didn’t give a reason.
examples.zh: 他说不行，但没有说明原因。

items.def: a statement, fact or situation that tells you why something has happened; a reason given for something:
items.zh: 指解释、说明、阐述

examples.en: The most likely explanation is that his plane was delayed.
examples.zh: 最可能的解释是他的飞机晚点了。

items.def: (rather formal) a good or true reason for saying, doing or believing something:
items.zh: 指说、做或相信某事的充分理由、根据

examples.en: You have no grounds for complaint.
examples.zh: 你没有理由抱怨。

items.def: (rather formal) the reason why people take a particular action:
items.zh: 指原因、缘由

examples.en: On what basis will this decision be made?
examples.zh: 将基于何种原因作出这一决定呢？

items.def: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour; a good reason that you give for doing something that you want to do for other reasons:
items.zh: 指为自己行为所作的辩护、借口、理由

examples.en: Late again! What’s your excuse this time?
examples.zh: 又迟到了！你这次有什么借口？

items.def: a reason that explains somebody’s behaviour:
items.zh: 指动机、原因

examples.en: There seemed to be no motive for the murder.
examples.zh: 这起谋杀案看不出有什么动机。

items.def: (rather formal) a good reason why something exists or is done:
items.zh: 指事物存在或做某事的正当理由

examples.en: I can see no possible justification for any further tax increases.
examples.zh: 我看不出还能提出什么理由来加税了。

items.def: (rather formal) a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason:
items.zh: 指为掩盖做某事（通常为不好的事）的真正理由而找的借口、托辞

examples.en: He left the party early on the pretext of having to work.
examples.zh: 他借口有事要处理，早早离开了聚会。

senses.def: used to politely get somebody’s attention, especially somebody you do not know
senses.zh: （引起尤其是陌生人的注意）劳驾，请原谅

examples.zh: 劳驾，这是去车站的路吗？

senses.def: used to politely ask somebody to move so that you can get past them
senses.zh: （客气地请人让路）对不起，劳驾，借光

examples.zh: 对不起，能让我过去吗？

senses.zh: （因打扰别人或失礼表示歉意）对不起，请原谅

examples.zh: 盖伊大声打了个喷嚏，然后说了声“对不起”。

senses.zh: （婉转地表示不赞成）对不起，请原谅，很抱歉

examples.en: Excuse me, but I don't think that's true.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，我认为这不是真的。

examples.zh: 她说了声“很抱歉，失陪一会儿”就离开了房间。

examples.zh: 啊呀，对不起，我没看到你在那里。

senses.def: used when you did not hear what somebody said and you want them to repeat it
senses.zh: （没听清楚，请对方再说一遍）对不起，请再说一遍

senses.zh: 请原谅我说脏话了；不好意思，我骂人了

senses.def: an executive in a business

examples.zh: 工作室高管目前正在与编剧会面讨论剧本。

examples.zh: 首席执行官的作用是赋予团队权力。

to kill somebody, especially as a legal punishment

examples.en: He was executed for treason.
examples.zh: 他因叛国罪被处死。

examples.zh: 这些犯人已由行刑队枪决。

senses.def: to do a piece of work, perform a duty, put a plan into action, etc.

examples.zh: 他们制订并实施了一项降低燃料消耗的计划。

examples.zh: 这一犯罪活动实施得非常巧妙。

examples.zh: 检查一下计算机是否已执行指令。

examples.zh: 飞行员完成了一次完美着陆。

senses.def: to make or produce a work of art

examples.zh: 毕加索还在奥尔塔–德圣胡安画了几幅风景画。

senses.zh: 执行（法令）；使（法律文件）生效

examples.zh: 2008年，他的律师签署了他的遗嘱。

examples.zh: 这份协议已经如期执行。

examples.zh: 他因谋杀罪要以绞刑处死。

examples.zh: 去年执行了 200 多起死刑。

examples.zh: 他未能履行职责。

examples.zh: 这个主意倒不错，可实施情况不理想。

examples.zh: 公司对因建筑工程施工不当造成的任何损害承担责任。

examples.zh: 她把那段钢琴曲演奏得非常完美。

examples.zh: 拍得很差劲的电影

senses.def: the act of following the instructions in a legal document, especially those in somebody’s will

examples.zh: 律师正在着手执行她母亲的遗嘱。

senses.def: a delay in following the order of a court

examples.zh: 准予缓期执行

examples.zh: 这座混凝土塔楼将于下个月被拆除，死刑不会暂停，哀悼者也很少。

senses.def: a delay in following the order of a court

a person who has an important job as a manager of a company or an organization
