examples.zh: 她偷偷看了看表。

items.def: a long, steady look at somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指凝视、注视

examples.en: She felt embarrassed under his steady gaze.
examples.zh: 她在他凝视的目光下感到很尴尬。

items.def: a long look at somebody/​something, especially in a way that is unfriendly or that shows surprise:
items.zh: 尤指不友善或吃惊的盯、凝视、注视

examples.en: She gave the officer a blank stare and shrugged her shoulders.
examples.zh: 她面无表情地盯着那个军官，耸了耸肩。

items.def: a look at somebody/​something for a very short time, when you do not see the person or thing completely:
items.zh: 指一瞥、一看

examples.en: He caught a glimpse of her in the crowd.
examples.zh: 他一眼瞥见她在人群里。

items.def: a long, angry look at somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指长久的怒视、瞪眼

examples.en: She fixed her questioner with a hostile glare.
examples.zh: 她带着敌意瞪着向她提问的人。

intro.en: These words all mean to become aware of somebody/​something by using your eyes, especially suddenly or when it is not easy to see them/​it.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含看见、见到、看出之义，尤指突然发现或注意到。

items.def: to become aware of somebody/​something by using your eyes:
items.zh: 指看见、见到、看出

examples.en: She looked for him but couldn’t see him in the crowd.
examples.zh: 她在人群里找来找去，但没看见他。

items.def: to see or notice somebody/​something, especially suddenly or when they are not easy to see or notice:
items.zh: 指看见、看出，尤指突然发现或注意到

examples.en: I’ve just spotted a mistake on the front cover.
examples.zh: 我刚才在封面上发现了一处错误。

items.def: to see or notice something for a moment, but not clearly or completely:
items.zh: 指瞥见、察觉

examples.en: She caught sight of a car in the distance.
examples.zh: 她瞥见远处有一辆车。

items.def: (literary) to see somebody/​something for a moment, but not clearly or completely:
items.zh: 指瞥见、看一眼

examples.en: He’d glimpsed her through the window as he passed.
examples.zh: 他路过时透过窗户瞥见了她。

senses.def: to produce small bright flashes of light

examples.en: The sea glinted in the moonlight.
examples.zh: 月色中海面上波光粼粼。

examples.en: The sun glinted on the windows.
examples.zh: 太阳照在窗户上闪闪发光。

senses.def: if a person’s eyes glint
senses.zh: （眼睛）流露出（强烈情感）；（强烈情感在眼中）闪现

examples.en: Her eyes glinted angrily.
examples.zh: 她眼睛里闪射着愤怒的目光。

examples.en: Hostility glinted in his eyes.
examples.zh: 他眼睛里流露出敌意。

senses.def: a sudden flash of light or colour shining from a bright surface

examples.en: the glint of the sun on the water
examples.zh: 太阳照在水上的闪光

examples.en: golden glints in her red hair
examples.zh: 她的红发上闪着的金光

examples.en: She saw a glint of silver in the grass.
examples.zh: 她看到草地上银光闪亮。

senses.def: an expression in somebody’s eyes showing a particular emotion, often a negative one
senses.zh: （眼睛里某种感情，常指负面感情的）闪现

examples.en: He had a wicked glint in his eye.
examples.zh: 他眼睛里闪着邪恶的神色。

examples.en: a glint of anger
examples.zh: 愤怒的目光

synonyms.words: gleam ▪ glow ▪ sparkle ▪ glisten ▪ shimmer ▪ glitter ▪ twinkle ▪ glint

intro.en: These words all mean to produce or reflect light.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含发光、反光之义。

items.def: to produce or reflect light, especially brightly:
items.zh: 指发光、反光、照耀

examples.en: The sun was shining and the sky was blue.
examples.zh: 阳光灿烂，天空一片蓝。

items.def: to shine with a clear bright or pale light, especially a reflected light:
items.zh: 指闪烁、隐约闪光、微光反射

examples.en: Moonlight gleamed on the water.
examples.zh: 月光照在水面上泛起粼粼波光。

items.def: (often of something hot or warm) to produce a steady light that is not very bright:
items.zh: 常指热的物体发出稳定而微弱的光

examples.en: The end of his cigarette glowed red.
examples.zh: 他的烟头发着微弱的红光。

items.def: to shine brightly with small flashes of light:
items.zh: 指闪烁、闪耀

examples.en: The diamonds sparkled in the light.
examples.zh: 钻石在灯光下闪闪发亮。

items.def: (of something wet) to shine:
items.zh: 指湿物闪光、闪亮

examples.en: The road glistened wet after the rain.
examples.zh: 雨后的道路润泽闪亮。

items.def: to shine with a soft light that seems to shake slightly:
items.zh: 指发出微弱的闪光、闪烁

examples.en: Everything seemed to shimmer in the heat.
examples.zh: 在高温下所有的东西都好像在闪光。

items.def: to shine brightly with small flashes of reflected light:
items.zh: 指闪亮、闪耀

examples.en: The ceiling of the cathedral glittered with gold.
examples.zh: 大教堂的天花板金光闪闪。

items.def: to shine with a light that changes rapidly from bright to faint to bright again:
items.zh: 指一明一暗地闪耀、闪烁

examples.en: Stars twinkled in the sky.
examples.zh: 星星在天空中闪烁。

items.def: to give small bright flashes of reflected light:
items.zh: 指微微闪光、闪亮、反光

examples.en: The blade of the knife glinted in the darkness.
examples.zh: 刀刃在黑暗中亮了亮。

senses.def: a way of playing a series of notes so that each one slides into the next, making a smooth continuous sound
to shine

examples.en: Her eyes were glistening with tears.
examples.zh: 她眼里闪着晶莹的泪花。

examples.en: Sweat glistened on his forehead.
examples.zh: 他额头上的汗珠晶莹发亮。

examples.en: The road glistened wet after the rain.
examples.zh: 雨后的道路润泽闪亮。

senses.def: not everything that seems good, attractive, etc. is actually good, etc.
senses.zh: 闪闪发光的未必都是金子；中看未必中用

items.idm: all that glitters/glistens/glisters is not gold

senses.zh: 闪闪发光的未必都是金子；中看未必中用

senses.zh: 闪闪发光的未必都是金子；中看未必中用

senses.def: a small problem or fault that stops something working successfully

examples.en: A few technical glitches forced us to postpone the demonstration.
examples.zh: 一些技术故障迫使我们推迟了演示。

examples.en: It was only a temporary glitch but it could have put people’s lives in danger.
examples.zh: 这虽然是个暂时性的小毛病，但却可能威胁到人的生命。

examples.en: The new system has too many bugs and glitches to be trusted.
examples.zh: 新系统有太多错误和故障，值得信任。

senses.def: a type of electronic music that uses sound recordings and electronic instruments that have been made to work incorrectly
senses.zh: 毛刺：一种电子音乐，使用的录音和电子乐器无法正常工作，因此声音中存在故意的毛刺

examples.en: Their style embraces everything from hip hop and funk to techno and glitch.
examples.zh: 他们的风格涵盖了从嘻哈、放克到电子和故障的一切。

senses.def: (of a machine or system) to suffer a sudden fault and fail to work correctly

examples.en: The screen glitched.
examples.zh: 屏幕出了故障。

examples.en: The instrument panel began glitching back in March.
examples.zh: 仪表板从三月份开始出现故障。

senses.def: tending to glitch

examples.en: The game is so buggy and glitchy it is barely playable.
examples.zh: 这个游戏缺陷和故障很多，只能勉强玩。

senses.def: in the style of electronic glitch
senses.zh: 小故障：电子小故障音乐的风格

examples.en: her combination of raw, bluesy vocals and glitchy electronics
examples.zh: 她将原始的蓝调歌声和故障电子产品结合在一起

senses.def: to shine brightly with little flashes of light, like a diamond

examples.en: The ceiling of the cathedral glittered with gold.
examples.zh: 大教堂的天花板金光闪闪。

examples.en: The water glittered in the sunlight.
examples.zh: 水面在阳光下闪闪发光。

senses.def: to shine brightly with a particular emotion, usually a strong one

examples.en: His eyes glittered with greed.
examples.zh: 他眼睛里闪现出贪婪的神色。

senses.def: not everything that seems good, attractive, etc. is actually good, etc.
senses.zh: 闪闪发光的未必都是金子；中看未必中用

senses.def: bright light consisting of many little flashes

examples.en: the glitter of diamonds
examples.zh: 钻石的光彩

senses.def: a bright expression in somebody’s eyes showing a particular emotion
senses.zh: （眼睛里某种感情的）闪现，流露

examples.en: There was a triumphant glitter in his eyes.
examples.zh: 他眼睛里闪烁着胜利的光辉。

senses.def: the attractive, exciting qualities that somebody/something, especially a rich and famous person or place, seems to have

examples.en: the superficial glitter of show business
examples.zh: 演艺业表面上的光彩迷人

examples.en: Behind all the glitter, life in the theatre can be very hard.
examples.zh: 在所有的光鲜亮丽的背后，剧院的生活可能非常艰难。

senses.def: very small shiny pieces of thin metal or paper that are stuck to things as a decoration

examples.en: gold/silver glitter
examples.zh: 金色的／银色的闪光装饰物

examples.en: Jane wore pink eye glitter to the party.
examples.zh: 简戴着粉红色的眼睛闪闪发光的衣服参加聚会。

senses.def: not everything that seems good, attractive, etc. is actually good, etc.

senses.def: (used in newspapers) fashionable, rich and famous people
senses.zh: （报章用语）时髦人物，风云人物，知名人士

examples.en: Up-and-coming actors mingled with the glitterati of the film world.
examples.zh: 崭露头角的演员与电影界的名流交往。

senses.def: shining brightly with many little flashes of light
senses.zh: 灿烂夺目的；闪闪发光的；华丽的

examples.en: a glittery suit
examples.zh: 一套华丽的服装

senses.def: the fact of appearing very attractive, exciting and impressive, in a way that is not always real

examples.en: the glitz and glamour of the music scene
examples.zh: 表面光辉灿烂的乐坛

senses.def: appearing very attractive, exciting and impressive, in a way that is not always real

examples.en: a glitzy, Hollywood-style occasion
examples.zh: 好莱坞式的盛大场面

senses.def: to show that you are happy about your own success or somebody else’s failure, in an unpleasant way
senses.zh: 扬扬得意；沾沾自喜；幸灾乐祸

examples.en: She was still gloating over her rival's disappointment.
examples.zh: 她仍在为对手的失望而幸灾乐祸。

examples.en: Having lost a large percentage of the vote, they were in no position to gloat.
examples.zh: 由于失去了很大比例的选票，他们没有资格幸灾乐祸。

examples.en: I hope you haven’t just come here to gloat.
examples.zh: 我希望你来这里不仅仅是为了幸灾乐祸。

examples.en: He didn't want to hear her gloating at his misfortune.
examples.zh: 他不想听到她对他的不幸幸灾乐祸。

senses.def: a small amount of a liquid or substance in a round shape

examples.en: thick globs of paint on the floor
examples.zh: 地板上一滴滴黏稠的油漆

senses.def: covering or affecting the whole world

examples.en: This year the global economy will grow by about 4 per cent.
examples.zh: 今年全球经济将增长 4% 左右。

examples.en: a global financial/economic crisis
examples.zh: 全球金融／经济危机

examples.en: the struggle to stay competitive in global markets
examples.zh: 在全球市场保持竞争力的奋争

examples.en: the country's ability to compete on a global scale
examples.zh: 这个国家的全球竞争力

examples.en: global trade/capitalism
examples.zh: 全球贸易/资本主义

examples.en: the global war on terror
examples.zh: 全球反恐战争

examples.en: the global ban on commercial whaling
examples.zh: 全球商业捕鲸禁令

examples.en: a global network of 64 national, regional and international organizations
examples.zh: 由 64 个国家、区域和国际组织组成的全球网络

senses.def: considering or including all parts of something

examples.en: We need to take a more global approach to the problem.
examples.zh: 我们需要更全面地看这个问题。

examples.en: They sent a global email to all staff.
examples.zh: 他们向全体职员发了一封统一的电邮。

senses.def: operating or applying through the whole of a file, program, etc.

examples.en: We ran a global search on the database.
examples.zh: 我们在数据库中进行了全程检索。

senses.def: the economies of every country in the world considered as a single economic system

examples.en: The Covid-19 pandemic knocked the global economy into recession.
examples.zh: Covid-19 大流行使全球经济陷入衰退。

senses.def: the increase in temperature of the earth's atmosphere that is caused by the increase of particular gases, especially carbon dioxide
senses.zh: 全球热化（有人用该词代替 global warming 来强调当前大气升温迅速的严峻局面）

examples.en: The goal is to limit global heating to 1.5℃.
examples.zh: 目标是将全球热化控制在 1.5℃ 以内。

examples.en: The next 18 months will be critical in dealing with the global heating crisis.
examples.zh: 接下来的 18 个月将对处理全球热化危机至关重要。

senses.def: a system by which signals are sent from satellites to a special device, used to show the position of a person or thing on the surface of the earth very accurately
the whole world, looked at as a single community that is connected by electronic communication systems
senses.zh: 地球村（指整个世界作为一个由电子通信系统连接的单一集体）

examples.en: Television has helped to create a global village.
examples.zh: 电视帮助创建了一个地球村。

examples.en: Technology has turned the world into a global village.
examples.zh: 科技已经把世界变成了地球村。

senses.def: the increase in temperature of the earth’s atmosphere that is caused by the increase of particular gases, especially carbon dioxide
senses.zh: 全球（气候）变暖；地球大气层变暖

examples.en: a conference on global warming
examples.zh: 有关全球气候暖化的会议

senses.def: the belief that economic and foreign policy should be planned on a global basis, rather than serving the interests of individual countries
senses.zh: 全球主义（该理论认为经济和外交政策规划应基于全球，而非服务于个别国家的利益）

examples.en: Both political parties favour globalism, free trade and more open borders.
examples.zh: 两个政党都支持全球主义、自由贸易和更开放的边境政策。

senses.def: a person who supports the belief that economic and foreign policy should be planned on a global basis, rather than serving the interests of individual countries

examples.en: He is a globalist and considers himself a citizen of the world.
examples.zh: 他信奉全球主义，认为自己是世界公民。

senses.def: based on or supporting the belief that economic and foreign policy should be planned on a global basis, rather than serving the interests of individual countries
senses.zh: 全球主义的；支持全球主义的

examples.en: a globalist attitude to business
examples.zh: 全球主义的商业态度

senses.def: the fact that different cultures and economic systems around the world are becoming connected and similar to each other because of the influence of large multinational
senses.zh: 全球化，全世界化（世界各地的文化和经济体系日益关联）

senses.def: if something, for example a business company, globalizes
in a way that covers or affects the whole world

examples.en: We need to start thinking globally.
examples.zh: 我们需要开始从全球视角考虑问题。

examples.en: Locally successful companies must become globally competitive.
examples.zh: 本地成功的公司必须具有全球竞争力。

senses.def: in a way that considers or includes all parts of something

examples.en: It is important to approach the problem globally.
examples.zh: 从全球范围内解决这个问题非常重要。

senses.def: in a way that operates or applies through the whole of a file, program, etc.
senses.zh: 全局的：以在整个文件，程序等中运行或应用的方式

examples.en: The processing can be applied globally to all digital output signals.
examples.zh: 该处理可以全局应用于所有数字输出信号。

senses.def: the world (used especially to emphasize its size)
senses.zh: 地球，世界（尤用以强调其大）

examples.en: tourists from every corner of the globe
examples.zh: 来自世界各地的游客

senses.def: an object like a ball in shape with a map of the world on its surface, usually on a stand so that it can be turned

examples.en: A dusty old globe stood in the corner of the schoolroom.
examples.zh: 教室的角落里放着一个积满灰尘的旧地球仪。

examples.en: Find Laos on the globe.
examples.zh: 在地球仪上找出老挝。

examples.en: On his desk was a globe and several maps.
examples.zh: 他的桌子上有一个地球仪和几张地图。

senses.def: a thing that is like a ball in shape
a light bulb

examples.en: Halogen globes are being replaced with LEDs, which use 80 per cent less energy.
examples.zh: 卤素灯正在被 LED 灯取代，LED 灯的能耗可减少 80%。

examples.zh: 这次乘船游览时间过得很快。

senses.def: to stop existing; to be lost or stolen
senses.zh: 不复存在；不见了；丢失；失窃

examples.en: Has your headache gone yet?
examples.zh: 你还头痛吗？

examples.en: I left my bike outside the library and when I came out again it had gone.
examples.zh: 我把自行车放在图书馆外面，出来时它就不翼而飞了。

senses.def: to lead or extend in a particular direction

examples.en: Where does this road go?
examples.zh: 这条路通到哪里？

examples.en: The trail goes north at this point.
examples.zh: 这条路此时向北延伸。

examples.en: I want a rope that will go from the top window to the ground.
examples.zh: 我想要一根可从顶楼窗户垂到地面的绳子。

senses.def: to have as a usual or correct position; to be placed
senses.zh: 被放置，被置于，被安放（在通常或合适的位置）

examples.en: This dictionary goes on the top shelf.
examples.zh: 这部词典放在书架最上层。

examples.en: Where do you want the piano to go (= be put)?
examples.zh: 你想把钢琴放在什么地方？

senses.def: used to say that something does/did not fit into a particular place or space

examples.en: My clothes won't all go in that one suitcase.
examples.zh: 一个手提箱装不下我所有的衣服。

examples.en: He tried to push his hand through the gap but it wouldn't go.
examples.zh: 他试着把手伸进豁口，可就是伸不进去。

senses.def: used to talk about how well or badly something makes progress or succeeds

examples.en: ‘How did the interview go?’ ‘It went well, thank you.’
examples.zh: “面试情况如何？”“非常顺利，谢谢。”

examples.en: Did everything go smoothly?
examples.zh: 一切进行得都顺利吗？

examples.en: How's it going (= is your life enjoyable, successful, etc. at the moment)?
examples.zh: 近况可好？

examples.en: The way things are going, the company will be bankrupt by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 情况如此发展下去，到年底公司就得破产。

senses.def: used in many expressions to show that somebody/something has reached a particular state/is no longer in a particular state
senses.zh: 进入…状态；处于…状况；脱离…状态

examples.en: She went to sleep.
examples.zh: 她睡着了。

examples.en: The US and Mexico went to war in 1846.
examples.zh: 1846 年，美国和墨西哥开战。

examples.en: The law went into effect on 1 August.
examples.zh: 该法律于 8 月 1 日生效。

examples.en: Shares went on sale this morning.
examples.zh: 股票今天上午发售。

examples.en: They're threatening to go on strike again.
examples.zh: 他们威胁要再次罢工。

examples.en: That colour has gone out of fashion.
examples.zh: 那种颜色已不时兴了。

senses.def: to become different in a particular way, especially a bad way
senses.zh: （尤指朝坏的方面）变成，变为，变得

examples.en: to go crazy/mad/nuts/insane
examples.zh: 发狂；发疯；失去理智

examples.en: She's beginning to go blind.
examples.zh: 她开始变得失明。

examples.en: He suddenly went quiet.
examples.zh: 他突然安静了下来。

examples.en: The company went bankrupt last year.
examples.zh: 公司去年破产了。

examples.en: Our dog went missing over a week ago.
examples.zh: 我们的狗一个多星期前失踪了。

examples.en: Her hair is going grey.
examples.zh: 她的头发日渐花白。

examples.en: The children went wild with excitement.
examples.zh: 孩子们欣喜若狂。

senses.def: to live or move around in a particular state
senses.zh: （在某种状态下）生活，过活，移动

examples.en: to go naked/barefoot
examples.zh: 光着身子；赤着脚

examples.en: She cannot bear the thought of children going hungry.
examples.zh: 想到孩子们挨饿她就受不了。

senses.def: to spend a period of time in a particular way
senses.zh: 以特定方式度过一段时间

examples.en: They went for two weeks without receiving any news.
examples.zh: 他们两个星期没有收到任何消息。

senses.def: to not be noticed, reported, etc.

examples.en: Pippa's absence went unnoticed.
examples.zh: 皮帕的缺席没有引起人们的注意。

examples.en: Police are worried that many crimes go unreported.
examples.zh: 警方感到不安的是，许多罪行发生后无人报案。

examples.en: In these traditional stories, no crime goes unpunished.
examples.zh: 在这些传统故事中，犯罪必定会受到惩罚。

examples.en: Customer service calls went unanswered.
examples.zh: 客服电话无人接听。

senses.def: to make a particular sound or movement
senses.zh: 发出（某种声音）；做（某种动作）

examples.en: The gun went ‘bang’.
examples.zh: 枪“砰”的一声响了。

examples.en: She went like this with her hand.
examples.zh: 她用手这样比画着。

senses.def: to be sounded as a signal or warning

examples.en: The whistle went for the end of the game.
examples.zh: 比赛结束的哨声响了。

senses.def: if a number will go into

examples.en: 3 into 12 goes 4 times.
7 into 15 won’t go.
examples.zh: 7 除 15 除不尽。

examples.en: 7 into 15 doesn’t go.
examples.zh: 7 除 15 除不尽。

examples.en: 7 won’t go into 15.
examples.zh: 7 除不尽 15。

senses.def: to combine well with something
senses.zh: 与某物相配（或协调、和谐）

examples.en: Does this jacket go with this skirt?
examples.zh: 这件上衣与这条裙子相配吗？

examples.en: Those colours don’t really go (together).
examples.zh: 那些颜色并不十分协调。

senses.def: used to talk about what tune or words a song or poem has or what happens in a story
senses.zh: （歌曲）唱道；（诗歌）写道；（歌词或故事）内容是

examples.en: How does that song go?
examples.zh: 那首歌怎么唱？

examples.en: I forget how the next line goes.
examples.zh: 我忘记下一句台词怎么说了。

examples.en: The story goes that she's been married five times.
examples.zh: 据传她结过五次婚。

senses.def: to say

examples.en: I asked ‘How much?’ and he goes, ‘Fifty’ and I go, ‘Fifty? You must be joking!’
examples.zh: 我问：“多少钱？”他回答说：“五十。”我又说：“五十？你是在开玩笑吧！”

senses.def: to start an activity

examples.en: I'll say ‘One, two, three, go!’ as a signal for you to start.
examples.zh: 我喊“一、二、三，开始！”作为你开始的信号。

examples.en: As soon as he gets here we're ready to go.
examples.zh: 他一到我们就可以开始。

senses.def: if a machine goes

examples.en: This clock doesn't go.
examples.zh: 这钟不走了。

examples.en: What makes it go?
examples.zh: 是什么让它运转起来？

senses.def: used to talk about wanting to get rid of somebody/something
senses.zh: （必须或可以）辞掉（或扔掉、废弃）

examples.en: The old sofa will have to go.
examples.zh: 那旧沙发该扔掉了。

examples.en: He's useless—he'll have to go.
examples.zh: 他毫无用处，得辞掉他。

senses.def: to get worse; to become damaged or stop working correctly

examples.en: Her sight is beginning to go.
examples.zh: 她的视力开始下降。

examples.en: His mind is going (= he is losing his mental powers).
examples.zh: 他心智日衰。

examples.en: I was driving home when my brakes went.
examples.zh: 我正开车回家，突然刹车失灵了。

senses.def: to die. People say ‘
senses.zh: 走（委婉说法，与 die 同义）

examples.en: You can't take your money with you when you go.
examples.zh: 你不可能把钱带进棺材。

senses.def: when money goes

examples.en: I don't know where the money goes!
examples.zh: 我不知道钱都花到什么地方去了！

examples.en: Most of my salary goes on the rent.
examples.zh: 我大部分工资都花在房租上了。

examples.en: The money will go to finance a new community centre.
examples.zh: 这笔钱将用于新的社区活动中心。

senses.def: to be sold

examples.en: We won't let the house go for less than $200 000.
examples.zh: 这房子低于 20 万美元我们是不会卖的。

examples.en: There was usually some bread going cheap (= being sold cheaply) at the end of the day.
examples.zh: 在收市前常常有些面包降价出售。

senses.def: to be willing to pay a particular amount of money for something

examples.en: He's offered £3 000 for the car and I don't think he'll go any higher.
examples.zh: 他出价 3 000 英镑买这辆汽车，我看他不会愿意再多付了。

examples.en: I'll go to $1 000 but that's my limit.
examples.zh: 我愿意出 1 000 美元，这可是最大限度了。

senses.def: to help; to play a part in doing something

examples.en: This all goes to prove my theory.
examples.zh: 这一切都有助于证明我的说法是对的。

examples.en: It (= what has just happened) just goes to show you can't always tell how people are going to react.
examples.zh: 这正好说明你不可能总是知道人们会如何反应。

senses.def: to be available
senses.zh: 可得到；可买到；现成可用

examples.en: There just aren't any jobs going in this area.
examples.zh: 此地几乎没有工作可找。

senses.def: to use a toilet

examples.en: Do you need to go, Billy?
examples.zh: 你要上厕所吗，比利？

senses.def: anything that somebody says or does is accepted or allowed, even if it shocks or surprises people
senses.zh: 任何事都有可能发生；什么事都不新鲜

examples.en: Almost anything goes these days.
examples.zh: 这个年月几乎是无奇不有。

senses.def: in comparison with the average person, thing, etc.
senses.zh: 和一般人（或事物等）相比

examples.en: As teachers go, he's not bad.
examples.zh: 和一般教师相比，他是不错的。

senses.def: to be nearly a particular age, time or number
senses.zh: 接近（或将近、快到）某一年龄（或时间、数字）

examples.en: It was going on (for) midnight.
examples.zh: 快半夜了。

senses.def: used to show what somebody intends to do in the future

examples.en: We're going to buy a house when we've saved enough money.
examples.zh: 我们打算攒够钱后买所房子。

senses.def: used to show that something is likely to happen very soon or in the future
senses.zh: 快要发生某事；某事将要发生

examples.en: I think I'm going to faint.
examples.zh: 我看我快昏倒了。

examples.en: If the drought continues there's going to be a famine.
examples.zh: 如果旱灾继续下去很可能要发生饥荒。

senses.def: used to tell or warn somebody not to do something

examples.en: Don't go getting yourself into trouble.
examples.zh: 别惹麻烦。

senses.def: something that is enough for a short time
senses.zh: 暂且够用；足以应付一时

examples.en: £50 should be enough to be going on with.
examples.zh: 50 英镑该够应付一时半会儿的了。

senses.def: to make a very great effort to get something or do something
senses.zh: 竭力获取某物；全力以赴做某事；鼓足干劲做某事

senses.def: used to show that you are angry or annoyed that somebody has done something stupid
senses.zh: （对某人做了蠢事感到愤怒或烦恼）竟然干出某事，居然干出某事

examples.en: Trust him to go and mess things up!
examples.zh: 就知道他会把事情弄得一团糟！

examples.en: Why did you have to go and upset your mother like that?
examples.zh: 你干吗非得让你母亲那样伤心呢？

examples.en: You've really gone and done it (= done something very stupid) now!
examples.zh: 你竟然干出这样的事来！

senses.def: to suddenly become very angry

examples.en: Now and again she really goes off on one.
examples.zh: 偶尔她会发脾气。

senses.def: used to express the fact that you do not believe something, or that you think something is bad
senses.zh: （表示不相信或不赞同）去你的，我才不信呢

examples.en: Go on with you—you’re never forty. You don’t look a day over thirty.
examples.zh: 去你的吧─你哪有四十啊，你看上去决不超过三十岁。

senses.def: (to have) many/not many advantages
senses.zh: 有（或没有）很多有利条件

examples.en: You're young, intelligent, attractive—you have a lot going for you!
examples.zh: 你年轻、聪明、漂亮，有利条件可多啦！

senses.def: not possible or allowed

examples.en: If the bank won't lend us the money it's no go, I'm afraid.
examples.zh: 如果银行不愿贷款给我们，这恐怕就行不通了。

senses.def: used to say that you do not want to talk about something in any more detail because you do not even want to think about it
senses.zh: 不想细谈；甚至不愿想起

examples.en: Don't ask me to choose. I don't want to go there.
examples.zh: 别让我挑选。我连想都不愿想。

examples.en: ‘There was a problem with his parents, wasn't there?’ ‘Don't even go there!’
examples.zh: “他的父母有问题，是不是？”“别往下说了！”

senses.def: what you say to tell people to start a race
to start with; for now

examples.en: ‘One slice or two?’ ‘Just one to be going on with.’
examples.zh: “一片还是两片？”“只吃一片。”

senses.def: that remains; still left

examples.en: I only have one exam to go.
examples.zh: 我只剩一门考试了。

senses.def: if you buy cooked food to go
senses.zh: （食品）外带的；带出餐馆（或商店）吃的

examples.en: Two pizzas to go.
examples.zh: 来两份比萨饼，带走。

senses.def: the way somebody behaves towards other people will affect the way those people behave towards them in the future
senses.zh: 你怎么待人，人就怎么待你

senses.def: something that is not fashionable now will become fashionable again in the future
senses.zh: 现在过时的还会再时兴起来

senses.def: used to ask what action somebody should take, especially in order to improve the difficult situation that they are in
senses.zh: （尤指为了改变困境而询问）下一步该怎么办，往下怎么做呢

senses.def: used by a soldier who is guarding a place to order somebody to say who they are
senses.zh: （哨兵喝问对方身份用语）谁，什么人

examples.en: Halt, who goes there?
examples.zh: 站住，什么人？

senses.def: a person’s turn to move or play in a game or an activity

examples.en: Whose go is it?
examples.zh: 轮到谁了？

examples.en: It's your go.
examples.zh: 轮到你啦。

examples.en: ‘How much is it to play?’ ‘It's 50p a go.’
examples.zh: “玩这游戏多少钱？”“50 便士一回。”

examples.en: Can I have a go on your new bike?
examples.zh: 我能骑骑你的新自行车吗？

senses.def: an attempt at doing something

examples.en: It took three goes to get it right.
examples.zh: 试了三次才把它弄好。

examples.en: I doubt if he'll listen to advice from me, but I'll give it a go (= I'll try but I don't think I will succeed).
examples.zh: 我怀疑他是不是会听我劝，不过我想试试看。

senses.def: energy and enthusiasm

examples.en: Mary's always got plenty of go.
examples.zh: 玛丽总是精力充沛。

senses.def: in one single attempt or try

examples.en: She blew out the candles at one go.
examples.zh: 她一口气把蜡烛全吹灭了。

senses.def: to be very busy or full of activity
senses.zh: 忙得要命；事儿特别多；手忙脚乱

examples.en: It was all go in the office today.
examples.zh: 今天办公室里忙得要死。

senses.def: to be planned and possible or allowed

examples.en: I'm not sure if Friday's trip is a go.
examples.zh: 我说不准星期五是否能成行。

senses.def: to be very active and busy

examples.en: I've been on the go all day.
examples.zh: 我一整天忙得马不停蹄。

examples.en: Having four children keeps me on the go.
examples.zh: 有四个孩子让我一直忙碌。

senses.def: used to ask somebody to be reasonable
senses.zh: 可得到；可买到；现成可用

examples.en: I just wanted to say, ‘Hey mate, fair go!’
examples.zh: 我只想说，‘嘿伙计，公平吧！’

senses.def: (to give somebody/get) fair treatment that gives you the same chance as somebody else

examples.en: Are minority students getting a fair shake at college?
examples.zh: 少数族裔学生在大学得到公平对待吗？

examples.en: We need a government that cares about equity and a fair go for all.
examples.zh: 我们需要一个关心公平和所有人公平竞争的政府。

senses.def: at the first, second, etc. attempt
senses.zh: 第一次（或第二次等）尝试

examples.en: I passed my driving test first go.
examples.zh: 我考驾照一次就通过了。

senses.def: to attack somebody physically

examples.en: There were about seven of them standing round him, all waiting to have a go.
examples.zh: 他们大约有七个人把他围起来，个个都等着下手。

senses.def: to make an attempt to do something

examples.en: ‘I can't start the engine.’ ‘Let me have a go.’
examples.zh: “这发动机我发动不起来了。”“让我来试试。”

examples.en: I'll have a go at fixing it tonight.
examples.zh: 我今晚试着修一下。

examples.en: You should have a go at answering all the questions.
examples.zh: 你应该试着回答所有的问题。

senses.def: to criticize somebody or complain about somebody

examples.en: The boss had a go at me for being late for work.
examples.zh: 我上班迟到，老板剋了我一顿。

examples.en: The government are always having a go at teachers.
examples.zh: 政府总是对教师进行打击。

senses.def: to be in the middle of an activity or a project

examples.en: The award-winning novelist often has three or four books on the go at once.
examples.zh: 那位获奖小说家经常是三四部小说同时写的。

senses.def: all together on one occasion

examples.en: I'd rather do the journey in one go, and not stop on the way.
examples.zh: 我宁愿一次走完全程，中途不停。

examples.en: They ate the packet of biscuits all in one go.
examples.zh: 他们一下子把那包饼干全吃光了。

senses.def: to stop holding on to something

examples.en: Leave go of my arm—you're hurting me!
examples.zh: 放开我的手臂，你弄痛我了！

senses.def: to stop holding somebody/something

examples.en: Don't let go of the rope.
examples.zh: 别松开绳子。

examples.en: Don't let the rope go.
examples.zh: 别松开绳子。

examples.en: Let go! You're hurting me!
examples.zh: 放手！你把我弄疼了！

senses.def: to give up an idea or an attitude, or control of something
senses.zh: 放弃，摒弃（想法、态度或控制）

examples.en: It's time to let go of the past.
examples.zh: 该忘掉过去了。

examples.en: It's time to let the past go.
examples.zh: 该忘掉过去了。

senses.def: to stop holding somebody/something

examples.en: Don't let the rope go.
examples.zh: 别松开绳子。

examples.en: Don't let go of the rope.
examples.zh: 别松开绳子。

examples.en: Let go! You're hurting me!
examples.zh: 放手！你把我弄疼了！

senses.def: to give up an idea or an attitude, or control of something
senses.zh: 放弃，摒弃（想法、态度或控制）

examples.en: It's time to let the past go.
examples.zh: 该忘掉过去了。

examples.en: It's time to let go of the past.
examples.zh: 该忘掉过去了。

senses.def: to be successful in something
senses.zh: 在…方面成功（或有所成就）

examples.en: We've had a few problems in our marriage, but we're both determined to make a go of it.
examples.zh: 我们的婚姻有过一些问题，但现在我们俩都决心好好过日子。

note.en: Most idioms containing go are at the entries for the nouns and adjectives in the idioms, for example go it alone is at alone.
note.zh: 大多数含 go 的习语，都可在该等习语中的名词及形容词相关词条找到，如 go it alone 在词条 alone 下。

senses.def: anything that somebody says or does is accepted or allowed, even if it shocks or surprises people
senses.zh: 任何事都有可能发生；什么事都不新鲜

examples.en: Almost anything goes these days.
examples.zh: 这个年月几乎是无奇不有。

senses.def: in comparison with the average person, thing, etc.
senses.zh: 和一般人（或事物等）相比

examples.en: As teachers go, he's not bad.
examples.zh: 和一般教师相比，他是不错的。

senses.def: to be nearly a particular age, time or number
senses.zh: 接近（或将近、快到）某一年龄（或时间、数字）

examples.en: It was going on (for) midnight.
examples.zh: 快半夜了。

senses.def: used to show what somebody intends to do in the future

examples.en: We're going to buy a house when we've saved enough money.
examples.zh: 我们打算攒够钱后买所房子。

senses.def: used to show that something is likely to happen very soon or in the future
senses.zh: 快要发生某事；某事将要发生

examples.en: I think I'm going to faint.
examples.zh: 我看我快昏倒了。

examples.en: If the drought continues there's going to be a famine.
examples.zh: 如果旱灾继续下去很可能要发生饥荒。

senses.def: used to tell or warn somebody not to do something

examples.en: Don't go getting yourself into trouble.
examples.zh: 别惹麻烦。

items.idm: enough/something to be going on with

senses.def: something that is enough for a short time
senses.zh: 暂且够用；足以应付一时

examples.en: £50 should be enough to be going on with.
examples.zh: 50 英镑该够应付一时半会儿的了。

items.idm: go all out for something | go all out to do something

senses.def: to make a very great effort to get something or do something
senses.zh: 竭力获取某物；全力以赴做某事；鼓足干劲做某事

senses.def: used to show that you are angry or annoyed that somebody has done something stupid
senses.zh: （对某人做了蠢事感到愤怒或烦恼）竟然干出某事，居然干出某事

examples.en: Trust him to go and mess things up!
examples.zh: 就知道他会把事情弄得一团糟！

examples.en: Why did you have to go and upset your mother like that?

examples.zh: 她经常光着脚到处走。

examples.en: It's unprofessional to go about criticizing your colleagues.
examples.zh: 批评你的同事是不专业的。

senses.def: to spread from person to person

examples.en: There's a rumour going about that they're having an affair.
examples.zh: 有传言说他们有外遇。

senses.def: to continue to do something; to keep busy with something

examples.en: Despite the threat of war, people went about their business as usual.
examples.zh: 虽然有可能发生战争，人们照常忙着自己的事。

senses.def: to start working on something
senses.zh: 着手做某事；开始做某事

examples.en: You're not going about the job in the right way.
examples.zh: 你做这事的方法不对。

examples.en: How should I go about finding a job?
examples.zh: 我该怎样着手找工作呢？

senses.def: to run after or follow somebody
senses.zh: 追赶某人；跟在某人后面

examples.en: He went after the burglars.
examples.zh: 他追赶那些窃贼。

examples.en: She left the room in tears so I went after her.
examples.zh: 她流着泪离开了房间，于是我跟着追了出去。

senses.def: to try to get somebody/something
senses.zh: 追求某人；谋求某事（或某物）

examples.en: We're both going after the same job.
examples.zh: 我们俩都在谋求同一份工作。

senses.def: to not be in somebody’s favour or not to their advantage
senses.zh: 对某人不利；不利于某人

examples.en: The jury's verdict went against him.
examples.zh: 陪审团的裁定对他不利。

senses.def: to resist or oppose somebody/something
senses.zh: 反抗（或反对）某人（或某事）；与…相背

examples.en: He would not go against his parents' wishes.
examples.zh: 他不会违背父母的意愿。

senses.def: to be opposed to something; to not fit or agree with something

examples.en: Paying for hospital treatment goes against her principles.
examples.zh: 拿钱到医院治病有违她的原则。

examples.en: His thinking goes against all logic.
examples.zh: 他的想法完全不合情理。

senses.def: willing to try new ideas, methods, etc. and therefore likely to succeed
senses.zh: 有进取心的；有开拓精神的

examples.en: a go-ahead company
examples.zh: 开拓型公司

senses.def: to travel in front of other people in your group and arrive before them

examples.en: I'll go ahead and tell them you're on the way.
examples.zh: 我要先走一步，告诉他们你在路上。

senses.def: to happen; to be done

examples.en: The building of the new bridge will go ahead as planned.
examples.zh: 新桥的修建将按计划进行。

senses.def: to begin to do something, especially when somebody has given permission or has expressed doubts or opposition
senses.zh: （尤指经某人允许，或有人表示怀疑或反对后）开始做，着手干

examples.en: ‘May I start now?’ ‘Yes, go ahead.’
examples.zh: “我现在可以开始了吗？”“可以，开始吧。”

examples.en: The government intends to go ahead with its tax cutting plans
examples.zh: 政府拟开始实施减税计划。

senses.def: permission for somebody to start doing something

examples.en: The council has given the go-ahead to start building.
examples.zh: 地方议会已批准破土动工。

examples.en: Union leaders have now got the go-ahead for new talks with management.
examples.zh: 工会领导人现在已获准与资方进行新的谈判。

senses.def: to continue with an activity

examples.en: He made up the story as he went along.
examples.zh: 这个故事是他现编现讲的。

senses.def: to make progress; to develop

examples.en: Things are going along nicely.
examples.zh: 情况进展良好。

senses.def: to agree with somebody/something
senses.zh: 和某人观点一致；赞同某事

examples.en: I don't go along with her views on private medicine.
examples.zh: 在自费医疗的问题上，我不敢苟同她的观点。

senses.def: to turn round in a circle

examples.en: to go around in a circle
examples.zh: 转圈

senses.def: to be enough for everyone to have one or some
senses.zh: 足够分给每个人；够每人一份

examples.en: There aren't enough chairs to go around.
examples.zh: 椅子不够坐。

senses.def: to often be in a particular state or behave in a particular way
senses.zh: 习惯于（某种状态或行动方式）

examples.en: She often goes around barefoot.
examples.zh: 她常常光着脚。

examples.en: It's unprofessional to go around criticizing your colleagues.
examples.zh: 总是批评同事，这样做并不专业。

senses.def: to spread from person to person

examples.en: There's a rumour going around that they're having an affair.
examples.zh: 谣传他们之间关系暧昧。

senses.def: to visit somebody or a place that is near
senses.zh: 拜访（某人）；访问，参观（附近某处）

examples.en: I went around to the post office.
examples.zh: 我到邮局去了一趟。

examples.en: I'm going around to my sister's (= her house) later.
examples.zh: 我打算稍后到姐姐家去看看。

senses.def: a path taken by a plane after an unsuccessful attempt at landing, in order to get into a suitable position to try to land again
an argument
to spend time with somebody, especially in different places

examples.en: He goes around with some of the local lads.
examples.zh: 他和当地的一些小伙子有来往。

senses.def: to attack somebody

examples.en: They went at each other furiously.
examples.zh: 他们相互猛烈攻击。

senses.def: to make great efforts to do something; to work hard at something

examples.en: They went at the job as if their lives depended on it.
examples.zh: 他们干起活来好像性命攸关似的。

senses.def: to leave a person or place

examples.en: Just go away!
examples.zh: 走开！

examples.en: Go away and think about it, then let me know.
examples.zh: 到一边去想一想，然后再告诉我。

senses.def: to leave home for a period of time, especially for a holiday

examples.en: They've gone away for a few days.
examples.zh: 他们外出了，会在外待上几天。

examples.en: I'm going away on business.
examples.zh: 我要出趟差。

senses.def: to disappear

examples.en: The smell still hasn't gone away.
examples.zh: 气味还没散尽。

senses.def: if two people go back

examples.en: Dave and I go back twenty years.
examples.zh: 我和戴夫相识有二十年了。

senses.def: when the clocks go back
senses.zh: （在夏令时结束时钟表）回拨一小时

examples.en: Don't forget—the clocks go back tonight.
examples.zh: 别忘了今晚钟表要回拨一小时。

senses.def: to return to a place

examples.en: She doesn't want to go back to her husband (= to live with him again).
examples.zh: 她不想回到丈夫的身边了。

examples.en: This toaster will have to go back (= be taken or sent back to the shop it was bought from)—it's faulty.
examples.zh: 这烤面包机得退回去，它有毛病。

examples.en: Of course we want to go back some day—it's our country, our real home.
examples.zh: 我们当然希望有一天能回去，那是我们的祖国，我们真正的家。

senses.def: to consider something that happened or was said at an earlier time
senses.zh: 回忆起；回到（原来的话题）

examples.en: Can I go back to what you said at the beginning of the meeting?
examples.zh: 我想回到你在会议开始时所提的话题，行吗？

examples.en: Once you have made this decision, there will be no going back (= you will not be able to change your mind).
examples.zh: 你一旦作出这个决定就不能改变。

senses.def: to have existed since a particular time or for a particular period

examples.en: Their family goes back to the time of the Pilgrim Fathers.
examples.zh: 他们家族的渊源可追溯到清教徒前辈移民时代。

senses.def: to fail to keep a promise; to change your mind about something

examples.en: He never goes back on his word (= never fails to do what he has said he will do).
examples.zh: 他从不食言。

senses.def: to start doing something again that you had stopped doing

examples.en: The kids go back to school next week.
examples.zh: 孩子们下周开学。

examples.en: She's decided to go back to teaching.
examples.zh: 她已决定重新执教。

senses.def: a bag, packed with essential items, that is kept ready to take away and use if a person needs to leave their home in an emergency

examples.en: As soon as she heard the flood warning, she left the house with her Go bag and headed for higher ground.
examples.zh: 一听到洪水警报，她就拎着旅行包离开家，前往地势较高的地方。

senses.def: to exist or happen in an earlier time
senses.zh: 居先；先前存在；以往发生

examples.en: The present crisis is worse than any that have gone before.
examples.zh: 目前的危机比以往任何一次危机都严重。

senses.def: to be presented to somebody/something for discussion, decision or judgement
senses.zh: 提交给…讨论（或决定、裁决）

examples.en: My application goes before the planning committee next week.
examples.zh: 我的申请下周提交计划委员会审批。

senses.def: a person who takes messages between one person or group and another

examples.en: to act as (a) go-between
examples.zh: 做中间人

examples.en: A number of local church leaders have acted as go-betweens with the paramilitaries.
examples.zh: 几位地方教会领袖已担任那些非法军事组织之间的中间人。

senses.def: to be more than something

examples.en: This year's sales figures go beyond all our expectations (= are much better than we thought they would be).
examples.zh: 今年的销售额大大超过我们的预期。

senses.def: to pass

examples.en: Things will get easier as time goes by.
examples.zh: 随着时间的推移情况会有所改善。

examples.en: The weeks went slowly by.
examples.zh: 时间一周周慢慢地过去了。

examples.en: The days seemed to go by very slowly.
examples.zh: 日子似乎过得很慢。

senses.def: to be guided by something; to form an opinion from something
senses.zh: 遵循（或依照）某事；以某事来判断

examples.en: That's a good rule to go by.
examples.zh: 那是要遵守的好规则。

examples.en: If past experience is anything to go by, they'll be late.
examples.zh: 凭以往的经验看，他们会迟到的。

senses.def: to be known or called by a particular name

examples.en: He goes by the name of King Creole.
examples.zh: 他被称为硬汉歌王。

senses.def: a vehicle like a small low car with no roof or doors, used for racing
senses.zh: （无篷无门的）微型赛车；卡丁车

senses.def: if the price of something, the temperature, etc. goes down

examples.en: The price of oil is going down.
examples.zh: 油价正在下跌。

examples.en: Oil is going down in price.
examples.zh: 油价正在下跌。

senses.def: to fall to the ground

examples.en: She tripped and went down with a bump.
examples.zh: 她绊了一下，重重地倒在地上。

senses.def: if a ship, etc. goes down
when the sun or moon goes down
if food or drink will/will not go down
senses.zh: （食物、饮料）被吞下，被咽下，被喝下

examples.en: A cold drink would go down very nicely (= I would very much like one).
examples.zh: 喝一杯冷饮会很好喝（=我非常想要一杯）。

senses.def: to get worse in quality

examples.en: The neighbourhood has gone down a lot recently.
examples.zh: 近来这一带已远不如从前了。

senses.def: to stop working temporarily

examples.en: The system is going down in ten minutes.
examples.zh: 这个系统十分钟后要暂停运行。

senses.def: to happen

examples.en: You really don't know what's going down?
examples.zh: 你真的不知道发生了什么事？

senses.def: to be sent to prison

examples.en: She went down for ten years.
examples.zh: 她坐了十年牢。

senses.def: to leave a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, at the end of a term or after finishing your studies
senses.zh: （大学学期结束或毕业时）离校（尤指牛津或剑桥）

examples.en: She went down (from Cambridge) in 2018.
examples.zh: 她 2018 年（从剑桥大学）毕业。

senses.def: to be written in something; to be recorded or remembered in something

examples.en: It all goes down (= she writes it all) in her notebook.
examples.zh: 那些东西全记在她的笔记本上。

examples.en: He will go down in history as a great statesman.
examples.zh: 他将作为伟大的政治家名垂青史。

senses.def: to perform oral
to be defeated by somebody, especially in a game or competition

examples.en: Italy went down to Brazil by three goals to one.
examples.zh: 意大利队以一比三输给了巴西队。

senses.def: to go from one place to another, especially further south or from a city or large town to a smaller place
senses.zh: （从一处）到（另一处）（尤指南下或从城市、大城镇到小地方）

examples.en: They've gone down to Brighton for a couple of days.
examples.zh: 他们已南下到布赖顿去待几天。

senses.def: to be received in a particular way by somebody

examples.en: The suggestion didn't go down very well with her boss.
examples.zh: 她的老板对这个建议不太感兴趣。

examples.en: The novel went down well with the public.
examples.zh: 这部小说获得公众欢迎。

senses.def: to become ill with something

examples.en: Our youngest boy has gone down with chickenpox.
examples.zh: 我们的小儿子染上了水痘。

senses.def: coloured lines that can be stuck on the sides of cars
senses.zh: （可贴于车身侧面的）加速彩条

senses.def: features that are added to a product to attract attention but that actually have no practical use

examples.en: The expensive new version of the software is the same as the last one with go-faster stripes.
examples.zh: 该软件昂贵的新版本与上一个版本相同，但条纹速度更快。

senses.def: to attack somebody

examples.en: She went for him with a knife.
examples.zh: 她手持尖刀向他刺去。

senses.def: to apply to somebody/something

examples.en: What I said about Peter goes for you, too.
examples.zh: 我说的关于彼得的话也适用于你。

examples.en: They have a high level of unemployment—but the same goes for many other countries.
examples.zh: 他们的失业率很高，不过，其他许多国家也是如此。

senses.def: to go to a place and bring somebody/something back
senses.zh: 去带回某人；去取回某物

examples.en: She's gone for some milk.
examples.zh: 她买牛奶去了。

senses.def: to be attracted by somebody/something; to like or prefer somebody/something
senses.zh: 被…所吸引；（更）喜欢某人（或某事物）

examples.en: She goes for tall slim men.
examples.zh: 她喜欢瘦高的男人。

examples.en: I don't really go for modern art.
examples.zh: 我并不是很喜欢现代艺术。

senses.def: to choose something

examples.en: I think I'll go for the fruit salad.
examples.zh: 我想要水果色拉。

senses.def: to apply for a job

examples.en: I'm going for a job in sales.
examples.zh: 我在申请一份销售的工作。

senses.def: to put a lot of effort into something, so that you get or achieve something

examples.en: Go for it, John! You know you can beat him.
examples.zh: 努力争取吧，约翰！你知道你是可以打败他的。

examples.en: It sounds a great idea. Go for it!
examples.zh: 这听起来是个极好的主意。努力去实现吧！

senses.def: when the clocks go forward
senses.zh: （在夏令时开始时钟表）往前拨一小时

examples.en: Remember, the clocks go forward tonight.
examples.zh: 记住今晚钟表要向前拨一小时。

senses.def: a person who is determined to succeed, especially in business
senses.zh: （尤指商业上的）实干家，志在必得的人

senses.def: connected with a style of dancing to pop music in which the dancers wear very few clothes
senses.zh: 歌歌舞的（跳舞的女子衣着暴露）

examples.en: a go-go dancer
examples.zh: 歌歌舞舞女

senses.def: of a period of time when businesses are growing and people are making money fast

examples.en: the go-go years of the 1990s
examples.zh: 20 世纪 90 年代经济繁荣的岁月

senses.def: to enter a room, house, etc.

examples.en: Let's go in, it's getting cold.
examples.zh: 我们进屋去吧，天冷了。

senses.def: if the sun or moon goes in
to take an exam or enter a competition

examples.en: She's going in for the Cambridge B2 First exam.
examples.zh: 她要参加剑桥大学 B2 级的第一英语证书考试。

senses.def: to have something as an interest or a hobby

examples.en: She doesn't go in for team sports.
examples.zh: 她不喜欢团体运动。

senses.def: to join somebody in starting a business
senses.zh: 与某人合伙；与某人联合办企业

examples.en: My brothers are opening a garage and they want me to go in with them.
examples.zh: 我的几个兄弟要开办一个汽车修理厂，想让我与他们合伙干。

senses.def: to hit something violently

examples.en: The car skidded and went into a tree.
examples.zh: 汽车打滑，猛地撞到树上。

senses.def: to start moving in a particular way

examples.en: The plane went into a nosedive.
examples.zh: 飞机开始俯冲。

senses.def: to join an organization, especially in order to have a career in it
senses.zh: 加入某组织；从事某职业

examples.en: to go into the Army/the Church/Parliament
examples.zh: 参军；加入教会；当议会议员

examples.en: to go into teaching
examples.zh: 执教

senses.def: to begin to do something or behave in a particular way
senses.zh: （以某种方式）开始做某事，开始某种表现

examples.en: He went into a long explanation of the affair.
examples.zh: 他开始长篇大论地解释起那件事来。

senses.def: to examine something carefully

examples.en: We need to go into the question of costs.
examples.zh: 我们需要研究一下费用问题。

senses.def: to be spent on something or used to do something

examples.en: More government money needs to go into the project.
examples.zh: 政府需对此工程投入更多的资金。

examples.en: Years of work went into researching the book.
examples.zh: 多年的工夫全花在对这本书的研究上了。

senses.def: a vehicle like a small low car with no roof or doors, used for racing
senses.zh: （无篷无门的）微型赛车；卡丁车

senses.def: the sport of racing in go-karts
senses.zh: 微型赛车运动；卡丁车运动

examples.en: to go go-karting
examples.zh: 去开卡丁车

senses.def: to leave a place, especially in order to do something

examples.en: She went off to get a drink.
examples.zh: 她拿饮料去了。

senses.def: to be fired; to explode

examples.en: The gun went off by accident.
examples.zh: 枪走火了。

examples.en: The bomb went off in a crowded street.
examples.zh: 炸弹在挤满人的大街上爆炸了。

senses.def: if an alarm, etc. goes off
if a light, the electricity, etc. goes off

examples.en: Suddenly the lights went off.
examples.zh: 灯突然熄灭了。

examples.en: The heating goes off at night.
examples.zh: 暖气夜间停止供热。

senses.def: to go to sleep

examples.en: Hasn't the baby gone off yet?
examples.zh: 孩子还没睡着吗？

senses.def: if food or drink goes off
to get worse in quality

examples.en: Her books have gone off in recent years.
examples.zh: 她近年写的书质量下降了。

senses.def: to happen in a particular way

examples.en: The meeting went off well.
examples.zh: 会议进行得很好。

senses.def: to suddenly become angry with somebody

examples.en: He just went off on her and started yelling.
examples.zh: 他突然对她发火，大声叫嚷起来。

senses.def: to stop liking somebody/something or lose interest in them/it
senses.zh: 不再喜欢某人（或某事物）；对…失去兴趣

examples.en: Jane seems to be going off Paul.
examples.zh: 简好像不再喜欢保罗了。

examples.en: I've gone off beer.
examples.zh: 我对啤酒已不感兴趣。

senses.def: to leave your husband, wife, partner, etc. in order to have a relationship with somebody else
senses.zh: （抛弃原有伴侣等）另寻新欢与（另外的某人）相好；与某人私奔

examples.en: He went off with his best friend's wife.
examples.zh: 他和最要好的朋友的妻子走了。

senses.def: to take away from a place something that does not belong to you

examples.en: He went off with $10 000 of the company's money.
examples.zh: 他卷走了公司 1 万美元。

senses.def: when a performer goes on

examples.en: She doesn't go on until Act 2.
examples.zh: 她要到第 2 幕才出场。

senses.def: to join a team as a substitute
senses.zh: （比赛中）以替补队员身份上场

examples.en: Maguire went on in place of Cahill just before half-time.
examples.zh: 马奎尔在半场结束前替下了卡希尔。

senses.def: when a light, the electricity, etc. goes on

examples.en: Suddenly all the lights went on.
examples.zh: 突然所有的灯都亮了。

senses.def: to pass

examples.en: She became more and more talkative as the evening went on.
examples.zh: 夜渐深，她的话越来越多。

senses.def: to happen

examples.en: What's going on here?
examples.zh: 这儿出了什么事？

senses.def: if a situation goes on

examples.en: This cannot be allowed to go on.
examples.zh: 决不允许这种情况继续下去。

examples.en: How much longer will this hot weather go on for?
examples.zh: 这样炎热的天气还会持续多久？

examples.en: We can't go on like this—we seem to be always arguing.
examples.zh: 我们不能这样继续下去，我们似乎老是争吵不休。

examples.en: The flight just seemed to go on and on.
examples.zh: 飞行似乎永远也不会结束。

senses.def: to continue speaking, often after stopping for a short time

examples.en: She hesitated for a moment and then went on.
examples.zh: 她犹豫了一会儿，然后继续往下说。

examples.en: ‘You know,’ he went on, ‘I think my brother could help you.’
examples.zh: “嗯，”他接着说，“我想我哥哥可以帮助你。”

senses.def: used to encourage somebody to do something

examples.en: Go on! Have another drink!
examples.zh: 来吧！再喝一杯！

examples.en: Go on—jump!
examples.zh: 来呀，跳吧！

senses.def: to travel in front of somebody else

examples.en: You go on ahead—I'll catch you up in a few minutes.
examples.zh: 你先走，我一会儿就赶上来。

senses.def: to base an opinion or a judgement on something

examples.en: The police don't have much to go on.
examples.zh: 警方没多少依据。

senses.def: to talk about somebody/something for a long time, especially in a boring or complaining way

examples.en: He went on and on about how poor he was.
examples.zh: 他没完没了地哭穷。

examples.en: She does go on sometimes!
examples.zh: 她有时就是唠叨个没完！

examples.en: He goes on endlessly about his health problems.
examples.zh: 他喋喋不休地说他的健康问题。

senses.def: to complain to somebody about their behaviour, work, etc.
senses.zh: 向某人抱怨（或埋怨、发牢骚）

examples.en: She goes on at him continually.
examples.zh: 她老是责备他。

examples.en: Stop going on at me about that money.
examples.zh: 不要老是喋喋不休地跟我提那笔钱的事。

senses.def: to continue an activity, especially after a break
senses.zh: （尤指停顿或中断之后）继续做（某事）

examples.en: That's enough for now—let's go on with it tomorrow.
examples.zh: 现在就到这里，咱们明天再继续吧。

examples.en: We'll go on with the presentations after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后我们继续展示。

senses.def: to continue an activity without stopping

examples.en: He said nothing but just went on working.
examples.zh: 他什么都不说，只是不停地干活。

senses.def: to pass from one item to the next
senses.zh: 进而转入另外一件事；接着开始另一个项目

examples.en: Let's go on to the next item on the agenda.
examples.zh: 咱们接着进行下一项议程吧。

senses.def: to do something after completing something else

examples.en: The book goes on to describe his experiences in the army.
examples.zh: 本书继而描述了他在部队的经历。

examples.en: After her early teaching career she went on to become a doctor.
examples.zh: 在她早期的教学生涯结束后，她继续成为一名医生。

senses.def: to leave your house to go to a social event
senses.zh: 出门参加社交活动；外出交际；外出娱乐

examples.en: She goes out a lot.
examples.zh: 她经常外出参加社交活动。

examples.en: He goes out drinking most evenings.
examples.zh: 他大多数晚上都在外喝酒。

senses.def: when the tide
to be sent

examples.en: Have the invitations gone out yet?
examples.zh: 请柬发出去了吗？

senses.def: when a radio or television programme goes out
when news or information goes out

examples.en: Word went out that the director had resigned.
examples.zh: 局长已经辞职的消息公开了。

senses.def: if a fire or light goes out
to fail to reach the next stage of a competition, etc.

examples.en: She went out of the tournament in the first round.
examples.zh: 她在锦标赛的第一轮比赛中就被淘汰了。

senses.def: to be no longer fashionable or generally used

examples.en: Those skirts went out years ago.
examples.zh: 那些裙子多年前就不时兴了。

senses.def: to spend time with somebody and have a romantic or sexual relationship with them
senses.zh: 与某人谈恋爱（或有性关系）

examples.en: Tom has been going out with Lucy for six weeks.
examples.zh: 汤姆与露西相恋六周了。

examples.en: How long have Tom and Lucy been going out together?
examples.zh: 汤姆和露西相恋多久了？

senses.def: to be no longer present in somebody/something; to disappear from somebody/something
senses.zh: 在…中不复存在；从…中消失

examples.en: All the fight seemed to go out of him.
examples.zh: 他身上的所有斗志似乎都已丧失殆尽。

examples.en: The heat has gone out of the argument.
examples.zh: 辩论已不那么激烈了.

senses.def: if your thoughts, etc. go out to somebody
senses.zh: 对某人产生同情（及寄予良好的祝愿）

examples.en: Our hearts go out to all who have lost loved ones in this tragedy.
examples.zh: 我们的心与所有在这场悲剧中失去亲人的人同在。

senses.def: to spend time with somebody and have a romantic or sexual relationship with them
senses.zh: 与某人谈恋爱（或有性关系）

examples.en: Tom has been going out with Lucy for six weeks.
examples.zh: 汤姆与露西相恋六周了。

examples.en: How long have Tom and Lucy been going out together?
examples.zh: 汤姆和露西相恋多久了？

senses.def: to examine or check something carefully
senses.zh: 仔细检查（或审查、查阅）某事

examples.en: Go over your work before you hand it in.
examples.zh: 把作业仔细检查后再交。

senses.def: to study something carefully, especially by repeating it

examples.en: He went over the events of the day in his mind (= thought about them carefully).
examples.zh: 他心里反复琢磨白天发生的事。

senses.def: to move from one place to another, especially when this means crossing something such as a room, town or city

examples.en: He went over and shook hands with his guests.
examples.zh: 他走过去与客人们握手。

examples.en: Many Irish people went over to America during the famine.
examples.zh: 许多爱尔兰人在饥荒时期迁徙到美国。

senses.def: to be received in a particular way by somebody

examples.en: The news of her promotion went over well with her colleagues.
examples.zh: 她晋升的消息一传开，同事都为她高兴。

senses.def: to change to a different person or place for the next part of a broadcast
senses.zh: 切换到另一人物（或地点）

examples.en: We are now going over to the news desk for an important announcement.
examples.zh: 我们现在转换到新闻部宣布一则重要消息。

senses.def: to change from one side, opinion, habit, etc. to another
senses.zh: 转向另一立场（或见解、习惯等）

examples.en: Several Conservative MPs have gone over to Labour.
examples.zh: 一些保守党议员已经转向工党。

senses.def: to turn round in a circle

examples.en: to go around in a circle
examples.zh: 转圈

senses.def: to be enough for everyone to have one or some
senses.zh: 足够分给每个人；够每人一份

examples.en: There aren't enough chairs to go around.
examples.zh: 椅子不够坐。

senses.def: to often be in a particular state or behave in a particular way
senses.zh: 习惯于（某种状态或行动方式）

examples.en: She often goes around barefoot.
examples.zh: 她常常光着脚。

examples.en: It's unprofessional to go around criticizing your colleagues.
examples.zh: 总是批评同事，这样做并不专业。

senses.def: to spread from person to person

examples.en: There's a rumour going around that they're having an affair.
examples.zh: 谣传他们之间关系暧昧。

senses.def: to visit somebody or a place that is near
senses.zh: 拜访（某人）；访问，参观（附近某处）

examples.en: I went around to the post office.
examples.zh: 我到邮局去了一趟。

examples.en: I'm going around to my sister's (= her house) later.
examples.zh: 我打算稍后到姐姐家去看看。

senses.def: a path taken by a plane after an unsuccessful attempt at landing, in order to get into a suitable position to try to land again
an argument
to spend time with somebody, especially in different places

examples.en: He goes around with some of the local lads.
examples.zh: 他和当地的一些小伙子有来往。

senses.def: a protest that workers make by doing their work more slowly than usual
if a law, contract, etc. goes through
senses.zh: （法律、合同等正式）通过，接受，达成

examples.en: The deal did not go through.
examples.zh: 这笔交易未谈成。

senses.def: to look at or examine something carefully, especially in order to find something
senses.zh: 仔细察看某事物；检查某事物；审查某事物

examples.en: She went through the company's accounts, looking for evidence of fraud.
examples.zh: 她仔细审查公司的账目，寻找诈骗的证据。

senses.def: to study or consider something in detail, especially by repeating it
senses.zh: （尤指反复地）详细研究，仔细琢磨

examples.en: Let's go through the arguments again.
examples.zh: 咱们再详细研究一下这些论据吧。

examples.en: Could we go through (= practise) Act 2 once more?
examples.zh: 我们把第 2 幕戏再串一次好吗？

senses.def: to perform a series of actions; to follow a method or procedure
senses.zh: 执行某行动；实行某方法；履行某程序

examples.en: Certain formalities have to be gone through before you can emigrate.
examples.zh: 必须办理一定的手续方能移居他国。

senses.def: to experience or suffer something

examples.en: She's been going through a bad patch recently.
examples.zh: 她最近很不走运。

examples.en: He's amazingly cheerful considering all he's had to go through.
examples.zh: 经历了种种磨难，他还那么乐观，令人惊叹。

senses.def: to use up or finish something completely

examples.en: The boys went through two whole loaves of bread.
examples.zh: 这些男孩把整整两条面包吃得精光。

senses.def: to do what is necessary to complete a course of action, especially one that is difficult or unpleasant
senses.zh: 完成艰难（或令人不快）的事

examples.en: She decided not to go through with (= not to have) the operation.
examples.zh: 她决定不动手术。

senses.def: to be given to somebody/something

examples.en: Proceeds from the concert will go to charity.
examples.zh: 音乐会的收入将捐赠给慈善事业。

examples.en: All her property went to her eldest son (= when she died).
examples.zh: （她死后）她的全部财产由她的长子继承了。

senses.def: used to refer to the person or place that somebody goes to for help, advice or information
senses.zh: （指对象）寻求协助的，征询意见的

examples.en: He's my go-to guy for business advice.
examples.zh: 他是我寻求商业建议的首选人。

senses.def: to exist at the same time or in the same place as something; to be found together
senses.zh: 与某事同时（或同地）存在；与某事相伴而生

examples.en: Disease often goes with poverty.
examples.zh: 疾病与贫穷常常相伴而生。

examples.en: Disease and poverty often go together.
examples.zh: 疾病与贫穷常常相伴而生。

senses.def: to be used as part of the payment for something
senses.zh: 用于支付…的部分款项；作为对…的部分付款

examples.en: The money will go towards a new car.
examples.zh: 这笔钱将用于支付新车的部分款项。

examples.en: Part of my pay goes towards paying off my student loans.
examples.zh: 我的一部分工资用于偿还学生贷款。

senses.def: to sink below the surface
to become bankrupt

examples.en: The firm will go under unless business improves.
examples.zh: 生意若无起色，公司将会倒闭。

senses.def: to be known or called by a particular name

examples.en: He goes under the name of King Creole.
examples.zh: 他的名字是克里奥尔国王。

senses.def: if the price of something, the temperature, etc. goes up

examples.en: The price of oil is going up.
examples.zh: 石油价格正在上涨。

examples.en: Oil is going up in price.
examples.zh: 石油价格正在上涨。

senses.def: to be built

examples.en: New office buildings are going up everywhere.
examples.zh: 到处都在兴建新办公楼。

senses.def: when the curtain across the stage in a theatre goes up
to be destroyed by fire or an explosion

examples.en: The whole building went up in flames.
examples.zh: 整座楼房在大火中焚毁。

senses.def: to arrive at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, at the beginning of a term or in order to begin your studies
senses.zh: （大学开学时）到校上学（尤指牛津或剑桥）

examples.en: She went up (to Oxford) in 2023.
examples.zh: 她于 2023 年升入牛津大学。

senses.def: to go from one place to another, especially further north or to a city or large town from a smaller place
senses.zh: （从一处）到（另一处）（尤指北上或从小地方到城市或大城镇）

examples.en: When are you next going up to Scotland?
examples.zh: 你下次什么时候北上苏格兰？

examples.en: We went up to London last weekend.
examples.zh: 我们上周末上伦敦去了。

senses.def: used to say goodbye to somebody

examples.en: I hope you enjoy your holiday. Go well!
examples.zh: 祝你假期玩得愉快。再见！

senses.def: to have a sexual or romantic relationship with somebody
senses.zh: 与某人有性关系；与某人谈恋爱

senses.def: to have sex with somebody
to be included with or as part of something

examples.en: A car goes with the job.
examples.zh: 这份工作配有一辆汽车。

senses.def: to agree to accept something, for example a plan or an offer

examples.en: You're offering £500? I think we can go with that.
examples.zh: 你出价 500 英镑？我想我们可以接受。

senses.def: to exist at the same time or in the same place as something; to be found together
senses.zh: 与某事同时（或同地）存在；与某事相伴而生

examples.en: Disease often goes with poverty.
examples.zh: 疾病与贫穷常常相伴而生。

examples.en: Disease and poverty often go together.
examples.zh: 疾病与贫穷常常相伴而生。

senses.def: to manage without something that you usually have or need
senses.zh: 没有…而勉强应付；没有…也行

examples.en: There wasn't time for breakfast, so I had to go without.
examples.zh: 没有时间吃早饭，我只好不吃了。

examples.en: How long can a human being go (= survive) without sleep?
examples.zh: 人不睡觉能活多久？

examples.en: She went without eating for three days.
examples.zh: 她三天没吃东西。

senses.def: to think about the simple or most important ideas within a subject or an activity instead of new ideas or complicated details

examples.en: Managers should get back to basics and examine the kind of products people really want.
examples.zh: 管理层应当回归根本，认真考虑人们真正需要什么样的产品。

examples.en: It's time our education system got back to basics.
examples.zh: 我们的教育制度该回归到基础上了。

senses.def: to start to happen or to make something happen in the opposite way

examples.en: In 2008 economic growth went into reverse.
examples.zh: 2008 年，经济增长发生了逆转。

examples.en: Various problems have put the company’s expansion plans into reverse.
examples.zh: 各种问题使该公司的扩张计划陷入倒退。

senses.def: to become a sailor; to leave your home and family without permission to become a sailor
senses.zh: 当水手；当海员；离家出走去当水手

examples.en: He ran away to sea at the age of 13.
examples.zh: 他13岁时离家出走去当水手。

senses.def: to be felt in a strong way, especially for a long time

examples.en: Feelings about the death of a parent are bound to go deep.
examples.zh: 对于父母去世的感受必然会很深。

examples.en: Dignity and pride run deep in this community.
examples.zh: 尊严和骄傲已深深扎根于这个群体之中。

examples.en: This suspicion runs very deep among some government members.
examples.zh: 这种猜疑在一些政府成员中很强烈。

senses.def: to happen according to plan; to happen without difficulties or problems

examples.en: The operation went like clockwork.
examples.zh: 手术进行得极为顺利。

senses.def: to produce flowers and seeds as well as leaves

examples.en: The lettuces had all run to seed.
examples.zh: 生菜都结籽了。

examples.en: Cutting weeds before they go to seed will greatly reduce future weed problems.
examples.zh: 在杂草结籽前将其剪除会极大地减少将来的杂草问题。

senses.def: to become much less attractive or good because of lack of attention
senses.zh: 变得懒散颓废（或意志消沉）；衰败

examples.en: After his divorce, he let himself go to seed.
examples.zh: 离婚后，他自暴自弃。

senses.def: to be bought quickly or in great numbers
to do/start to do your work
senses.zh: 做（或着手做）自己的工作

examples.en: She went cheerfully about her work.
examples.zh: 她高高兴兴地做自己的工作。

senses.def: to stop being pleasant or working properly

examples.en: Their relationship soon went sour.
examples.zh: 他们的关系很快有了嫌隙。

senses.def: to get married
to work very well

examples.en: My new car goes like a dream.
examples.zh: 我的新汽车性能好极了。

senses.def: to happen without problems, in the way that you had planned
senses.zh: 毫无困难；非常顺利；完美

examples.en: The wedding celebrations went like a dream.
examples.zh: 婚礼庆典进行得像一场梦。

senses.def: to keep annoying somebody/something until they react

examples.en: Goaded beyond endurance, she turned on him and hit out.
examples.zh: 她被气得忍无可忍，于是转身向他猛击。

examples.en: He finally goaded her into answering his question.
examples.zh: 他终于激得她回答了他的问题。

examples.en: She felt a needle of annoyance goading her to hit back.
examples.zh: 她心生恼怒，起而反击。

senses.def: a pointed stick used for making cows, etc. move forwards
something that makes somebody do something, usually by annoying them
senses.zh: （意在惹恼某人而促其行动的）刺激，激励

examples.en: The offer of economic help is intended to act as a goad to political reform.
examples.zh: 提供经济援助旨在推动政治改革。

senses.def: to drive or encourage somebody to do something

examples.en: The boxers were goaded on by the shrieking crowd.
examples.zh: 拳击运动员听见观众的喊叫就来劲儿了。

examples.en: She was goaded on by fierce ambition.
examples.zh: 她被强烈的野心所驱使。

senses.def: a frame with a net into which players must kick or hit the ball in order to score a point

examples.en: He headed the ball into an open goal (= one that had nobody defending it).
examples.zh: 他把球顶进了空门。

examples.en: Nicky Roberts was outstanding in goal (= as goalkeeper).
examples.zh: 尼基·罗伯茨是一位非常出色的门将。

examples.en: The goalkeeper was injured so a defender had to go in goal.
examples.zh: 守门员受伤了，只好由一名防守队员来守门。

senses.def: the act of kicking or hitting the ball into the goal

examples.en: She scored twenty goals in her first season.
examples.zh: 她在第一个赛季进了二十个球。

examples.en: United conceded two goals in the first half.
examples.zh: 联队在上半场被攻入了两球。

examples.en: Liverpool won by three goals to one.
examples.zh: 利物浦队以三比一获胜。

examples.en: The winning goal came in the 71st minute.
examples.zh: 第 71 分钟迎来了制胜一球。

examples.en: a penalty goal
examples.zh: 点球罚中

senses.def: something that you hope to achieve

examples.en: to achieve/accomplish/reach a goal
examples.zh: 达到目标

examples.en: My job is to help businesses meet their goals.
examples.zh: 我的工作是帮助企业实现目标。

examples.en: You need to set yourself some long-term goals.
examples.zh: 你得为自己定一些长期目标。

examples.en: Their goal was to eradicate malaria.
examples.zh: 他们的目标是根除疟疾。

examples.en: Their primary goal is to make a profit.
examples.zh: 他们的首要目标是盈利。

examples.en: Our ultimate goal must be the preservation of the environment.
examples.zh: 我们的最终目的必须是保护好环境。

examples.en: We are all working towards a common goal.
examples.zh: 我们都在朝着一个共同的目标努力。

intro.en: These are all words for something that you are trying to achieve.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指目标、目的。

items.def: a result that you try to achieve:
items.zh: 指试图达到的目标、指标

examples.en: Set yourself targets that you can reasonably hope to achieve.
examples.zh: 给自己制订有望达到的指标。

items.def: (rather formal) something that you are trying to achieve:
items.zh: 指正努力达到的目标、目的

examples.en: What is the main objective of this project?
examples.zh: 这个项目的主要目标是什么？

items.def: something that you hope to achieve:
items.zh: 指希望达到的目标、目的

examples.en: He continued to pursue his goal of becoming an actor.
examples.zh: 他继续追求他成为演员的目标。

items.def: the purpose of something; something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指目的、目标、宗旨

examples.en: The object is to educate people about road safety.
examples.zh: 目的就是教育大众注意交通安全。

items.def: something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指计划达到的目的、目标

examples.en: He joined the society for political ends.
examples.zh: 他为了政治目的加入了这个协会。

senses.def: an area in front of the goal from which goal kicks

the difference between the number of goals that a team has scored and the number of goals that have been scored against them over a series of games, sometimes used to decide the team’s position in the league table

examples.en: Russia lead Group G on goal difference from Montenegro.
examples.zh: 俄罗斯队凭借净胜球优势领先于黑山队。

senses.def: a kick taken by one team after the ball has been kicked over their goal line
an attempt to kick a goal
the line at either end of a sports field on which the goal stands or which the ball must cross to score a goal or touchdown
an electronic system used to determine whether the ball has crossed the goal line
senses.zh: 门线技术（辅助判断进球是否有效的电子系统）

examples.en: Goal-line technology and VAR have now been introduced in some form in all major leagues.
examples.zh: 门线技术和视频助理裁判如今已以某种形式引入各大联赛。

senses.def: a player who waits near the opposite team’s goal in order to try to score if they get the ball
senses.zh: “禁区之王”（埋伏在对方球门附近伺机进攻）

senses.def: a game in which teams of three players try to roll a ball containing bells over a line at the end of a court
senses.zh: 盲人门球（视障人士参加的一种球类运动，比赛双方各有三名队员，力图将带铃铛的球滚入球场另一端的线内）

senses.def: a player whose job is to stop the ball from going into their own team’s goal

examples.en: He now plays as goalkeeper for Liverpool.
examples.zh: 目前他在利物浦队担任守门员。

examples.en: The England goalkeeper played brilliantly.
examples.zh: 英格兰队的守门员表现得很出色。

senses.def: the job of stopping the ball from going into your own team's goal

examples.en: goalkeeping techniques
examples.zh: 守门的技巧

senses.def: without either team scoring a goal

examples.en: The match ended in a goalless draw.
examples.zh: 比赛以零比零结束。

senses.def: the area directly in front of a goal
one of the two posts that form part of a goal
to change the rules for something, or conditions under which it is done, so that the situation becomes more difficult for somebody
senses.zh: 改变规则，改变条件（使某人为难）

examples.en: I manage to get on top of the job, and then they move the goalposts again.
examples.zh: 我成功地完成了工作，然后他们再次移动了球门柱。

a glass bowl for keeping fish in as pets
a situation in which people can see everything that happens and nothing is private
senses.zh: 金鱼缸（指众目睽睽之下毫无隐私的状况）

examples.zh: 生活在这种全无隐私可言的环境之下，最牢固的婚姻也会破裂。

senses.def: without extremes; just right

examples.en: The planet is in what astronomers call the Goldilocks zone: neither too hot, nor too cold.
examples.zh: 这颗行星位于天文学家所说的适居带，既不太热，也不太冷。

examples.en: a return to the Goldilocks economy when growth was just right
examples.zh: 当增长恰到好处时，回归金发姑娘经济

senses.def: a popular children's story. Goldilocks, a young girl with golden
senses.zh: 金发姑娘和三只熊：一个受欢迎的儿童故事。Goldilocks，一个有着金色卷发的年轻女孩，去了三只熊（母熊，父亲熊和小熊）生活的房子。熊不在家，戈迪洛克（Goldilocks）吃了一些稀饭，尝试了所有床铺，然后睡在其中的一只床上。熊回来了，看到有人去过那里，说：“谁在吃我的稀饭？” 和“谁在我的床上睡觉？” 直到他们找到她，她才逃脱。这个故事经常被用作英国哑剧的基础。

senses.def: a person who makes or repairs things made of gold
a strong alcoholic drink from Poland that contains very small pieces of gold

a machine that behaves like a human
a game played over a large area of ground using sticks with a special shape to hit a small hard ball (a golf ball

examples.en: I play golf every weekend.
examples.zh: 我每个周末都打高尔夫球。

examples.en: He enjoyed a round of golf on a Sunday morning.
examples.zh: 他喜欢星期天的上午打一场高尔夫球。

senses.def: a large bag used to carry golf clubs

examples.en: I always keep a set of waterproofs in my golf bag.
examples.zh: 我总是在高尔夫球杆袋里备一套防水衣物。

senses.def: a small vehicle, often without a roof or doors, used especially to carry players and equipment around a golf course

examples.en: You don't need a driver's license to drive a golf cart on the course.
examples.zh: 您不需要驾驶执照即可在球场上驾驶高尔夫球车。

examples.en: Most people walk or use golf carts to navigate the island.
examples.zh: 大多数人步行或使用高尔夫球车在岛上航行。

examples.en: a set of golf clubs
examples.zh: 一套高尔夫球杆

examples.en: You can borrow golf clubs if you want a game.
examples.zh: 如果你想打高尔夫球，可以借用球杆。

senses.def: an organization whose members play golf; the place where these people meet and play golf
senses.zh: 高尔夫球俱乐部（指组织或所在地）

examples.en: Pine Ridge Golf Club
examples.zh: 派恩里奇高尔夫球俱乐部

examples.en: We're going for lunch at the golf club.
examples.zh: 我们要去高尔夫球俱乐部吃午餐。

examples.en: She decided to join a golf club.
examples.zh: 她决定加入高尔夫球俱乐部。

a golf course

a person who plays golf

examples.zh: 超过标准杆数不多的高尔夫球手

senses.def: the activity of playing golf
senses.zh: 打高尔夫球的；与高尔夫球有关的

examples.en: a week’s golfing with friends
examples.zh: 和朋友一起打高尔夫球的一周

senses.def: playing golf; connected with golf

examples.en: a golfing holiday
examples.zh: 打高尔夫球的假期

examples.en: a Goliath of a man
examples.zh: 巨人一般高大的男子

examples.en: a Goliath of the computer industry
examples.zh: 计算机行业的巨头

senses.def: a doll
senses.zh: 黑脸黑短发布娃娃（现在常被认为会冒犯黑人）

senses.def: used to express surprise

examples.en: Golly, you're early!
examples.zh: 天哪，你好早哟！

senses.zh: 黑脸黑短发布娃娃（现在常被认为会冒犯黑人）

a long boat with a flat bottom and high parts at each end, used on canals
senses.zh: 威尼斯小划船；贡多拉；凤尾船

senses.def: the part on a cable car
the part of a hot air balloon
a person whose job is to move and control the direction of a gondola
senses.zh: 威尼斯小划船船夫；贡多拉船夫

senses.def: lost or destroyed
a popular US novel (1936) by Margaret Mitchell that won the Pulitzer Prize
senses.zh: 《乱世佳人》：玛格丽特·米切尔（Margaret Mitchell）所著的美国畅销小说（1936年），获得了普利策奖。1939年，这部影片成为有史以来最成功的电影之一，获得了10项奥斯卡奖。故事发生在佐治亚州，讲述了内战期间斯嘉丽·奥哈拉（Scarlett O'Hara）和瑞德·巴特勒（Rhett Butler）之间陷入困境的爱情，这改变了他们的生活。

senses.def: a person or animal who is going to die soon; somebody/something that cannot be saved from a dangerous situation
senses.zh: 垂死的人；快完蛋的人；无法挽救的人

examples.en: We were frantic. We thought you were a goner.
examples.zh: 我们急死了，以为你快没命了。

senses.def: a round piece of metal that hangs in a frame and makes a loud deep sound when it is hit with a stick. Gongs

examples.en: to bang/beat/sound a gong
examples.zh: 敲锣

examples.en: the breakfast/dinner gong
examples.zh: 早餐/晚餐锣

senses.def: an award or medal
a way of saying or writing ‘going to’ in informal speech, when it refers to the future
senses.zh: 即将，将要（非正式用语，即 going to）

examples.zh: 她现在要干什么？

senses.def: a disease of the sexual organs, caught by having sex with a person who already has the disease

examples.zh: 你不必住在佐治亚州就能种植出优秀的果子。
