senses.zh: 巴登·鲍威尔勋爵：罗伯特·斯蒂芬森·史密斯·巴登·鲍威尔（1857-1951）是一位英国士兵，以在布尔战争中保卫南非马菲金镇而闻名。后来他离开军队，于1908年成立了童子军组织（现称为童子军或童军协会），并与他的姐姐Agnes一起在1910年成立了女童军（现在称为女童军或在美国称为女童军）。 。

senses.def: born William Maxwell Aitken (1874-1964) a British newspaper owner and politician. He was born in Canada, but settled in Britain and became a Member of Parliament
senses.zh: 比弗布鲁克勋爵（Lord Beaverbrook）：出生于英国报纸所有者兼政治家威廉·麦克斯韦·艾特肯（William Maxwell Aitken，1874-1964年）。他出生于加拿大，但定居英国，并于1910年成为国会议员。在两次世界大战中，他都是内阁大臣。他购买了《每日快报》和《夜间标准》，并开始了《星期日快报》。他利用这些报纸试图使各种思想流行起来，例如他渴望保存大英帝国。

senses.def: born Frederick Edwin Smith (1872-1930) a British lawyer and conservative politician who was well known for the humorous things he said. He was Attorney General
senses.zh: 伯肯黑德勋爵（Lord Birkenhead）：弗雷德里克·埃德温·史密斯（Frederick Edwin Smith）（1872-1930）出生，他是英国律师兼保守派政治家，因他讲的幽默而出名。当他完善土地和财产法时，他是司法部长（1915-18），然后是总理大臣（1919-22）。

senses.def: William Cecil (1520-98) a British politician. He was one of the most important members of Queen Elizabeth I's
senses.zh: 伯格利勋爵：威廉·塞西尔（1520-98）英国政治家。他是伊丽莎白女王一世政府最重要的成员之一，曾任国务卿（1558-72）和司库（1572-98）。他负责使英格兰具有强大的军事和经济实力。他还负责许多宏伟的建筑，包括Burghley House。他于1551年被任命为骑士，并于1571年被任命为男爵。

senses.def: George Gordon Byron (1788-1824) an English poet whose life is as well known as his poetry. He had love affairs with many women, including Lady Caroline Lamb, and probably had a child by his half-sister
senses.zh: 拜伦勋爵：乔治·戈登·拜伦（George Gordon Byron，1788-1824年），一位英国诗人，其生活和他的诗歌一样出名。他与包括卡罗琳·兰姆夫人在内的许多妇女有过恋爱关系，并且可能由同父异母的妹妹生了一个孩子（异母的姐姐）。他是浪漫主义运动中的佼佼者，他本人过着浪漫的英雄生活，常常对恋爱不满，对周围的不公正政治和社会处境感到愤怒。他的作品，包括柴尔德·哈罗德的朝圣（1812-18）和唐·胡安（1818-20），常常表达出相同的感受。由于受到英国社会的拒绝，他一生的大部分时间都在国外度过，死于帮助希腊人对抗土耳其统治的斗争。

senses.def: James Brudenell (1797-1868) a British army officer, well known for leading the Charge of the Light Brigade
senses.zh: Cardigan勋爵：James Brudenell（1797-1868）英国陆军军官，以克里米亚战争期间领导轻旅的领导而闻名

senses.def: born Robert Stewart (1769-1822) a British Tory
senses.zh: 卡斯尔雷格勋爵（Lord Castlereagh）：出生于英国保守党政治家罗伯特·斯图尔特（Robert Stewart，1769-1822年），负责与爱尔兰的联合法案（1800）。1809年，他与对手坎宁（Canning）进行了决斗（为解决争吵而进行的枪战），并离开了政府。他以外交大臣的身份返回（1812-22）。拿破仑战争后，他试图保持欧洲国家之间的力量平衡。

senses.def: (1738-1805) a general in charge of British forces during the American Revolution
senses.zh: 查尔斯·康沃利斯勋爵（Lord Charles Cornwallis）：（1738-1805）美国大革命期间负责英军的将军。当他承认在约克镇战役中击败华盛顿时，战争结束了。康沃利斯后来被任命为印度总督。

senses.def: George Nathaniel Curzon (1859-1925) a British diplomat
senses.zh: 寇松勋爵：乔治·纳撒尼尔·寇松（1859-1925）英国外交官（代表海外国家的人）和政治家。他仅39岁就成为印度总督。后来（1919-24）他担任外交大臣。Curzon性格坚强，许多人认为他太骄傲了。关于他有一种流行的押韵：

senses.def: Henry Stuart (1545-67) the second husband of Mary, Queen of Scots
senses.zh: 达恩利勋爵（Lord Darnley）：亨利·斯图尔特（Henry Stuart）（1545-67），苏格兰女王玛丽的第二任丈夫，英国国王詹姆斯一世（苏格兰詹姆斯六世）的父亲。达恩利以1566年谋杀玛丽的秘书戴维·里齐奥（David Rizzio）而闻名。第二年，达恩利本人被谋杀，可能是博斯韦尔伯爵（Bothwell Earl）谋杀了，伯特利随后接任了达恩利（Darnley）作为玛丽的第三任丈夫的职位。

senses.def: born George Lascelles (1923-2011) an English earl
senses.zh: 哈伍德伍德勋爵（Lord Harewood）：出生于英国伯爵乔治·拉塞尔斯（George Lascelles，1923-2011年），曾是伊丽莎白二世女王的表弟。在他的一生中，他大部分时间都在英国从事音乐，尤其是歌剧。

senses.def: a novel (1900) by Joseph Conrad
senses.zh: 吉姆勋爵：约瑟夫·康拉德的小说（1900年）。它讲述了一个年轻的船军官离开一艘似乎正在下沉的船的故事，在船上所有其他乘客面前。后来，他为这种行为感到羞愧，并到国外生活，在那里他终于赢得了荣誉。

senses.def: Horatio Herbert Kitchener (1850-1916) a British soldier who commanded the army in the Sudan (1883-5), in South Africa during the Boer War
senses.zh: 基奇纳勋爵（Lord Kitchener）：霍拉克·赫伯特·基奇纳（Horatio Herbert Kitchener，1850-1916年），英国士兵，他在苏丹（1883-5年），布尔战争（1900-02年）的南非和印度（1902-9年）的军队中担任指挥。第一次世界大战开始时，他成为战争国务卿，负责鼓励更多的人参军。他出现在著名的海报上，告诉人们“您的国家需要您”。他于1914年成为伯爵，并在第一次世界大战期间在海上死亡。

senses.def: born William Hesketh Lever (1851-1925) an English businessman. He became rich by making soap, and often gave his money to benefit others. One of his best-known projects was the building of a 'model industrial village', Port Sunlight
senses.zh: 勒沃胡姆勋爵（Lord Leverhulme）：出生于英国商人威廉·赫斯基斯·勒沃（1851-1925）。他通过制造肥皂而致富，并经常捐出自己的钱使他人受益。他最著名的项目之一是在利物浦附近建造一个“工业村模范”，阳光港。他在1922年成为副总裁。他的公司后来成为联合利华。

senses.def: an official who represents the Queen or King in each county of the UK

examples.en: the Lord Lieutenant of Oxfordshire
examples.zh: 牛津郡治安长官

senses.def: the title of the mayor
senses.zh: 市长大人（伦敦城和英国、爱尔兰、澳大利亚、加拿大一些城市市长的称号）

senses.def: born William Lamb (1779-1848) a British Whig
senses.zh: 墨尔本勋爵（Lord Melbourne）：出生于英国辉格党政客威廉·兰姆（William Lamb，1779-1848年），曾两次出任总理（1834年和1835-41年）。尤其因他与维多利亚女王的亲密关系而被人们铭记，维多利亚女王年轻时掌权并欢迎他给她的建议，并因1812年他的妻子卡罗琳·兰姆夫人（Caroline Lamb）恋爱而引起公开丑闻与诗人拜伦勋爵。

senses.def: born Louis Mountbatten (1900-79) a British admiral
senses.zh: 蒙巴顿勋爵（Lord Mountbatten）：生于路易斯·蒙巴顿（Louis Mountbatten）（1900-79年），他是英国海军上将（高级海军军官），在第二次世界大战期间指挥了东南亚的盟军。在印度独立之前，他是印度的最后一个总督，并担任印度第一任总督。他在爱尔兰西海岸航行时被IRA炸弹炸死。蒙巴顿勋爵是维多利亚女王的曾孙，也是查尔斯王子的叔叔。他于1947年成为伯爵。

senses.def: born Horatio Nelson (1758-1805) an English admiral
senses.zh: 纳尔逊勋爵（Lord Nelson）：出生于Horatio Nelson（1758-1805），是一位英国海军上将（海军高级军官），他以在1790年代与法国人的海战中胜出而闻名。这些胜利增强了英国在海上的军事力量，并阻止了拿破仑的军队进攻英国。许多人都知道纳尔逊在不同的战斗中失去了右臂和右眼，还有一个著名的故事，他在去特拉法加（Trafalgar）死前曾对另一名军官说“ Kiss me，Hardy”。他于1801年成为子爵。

senses.def: born Alfred Charles William Harmsworth (1865-1922) a British newspaper publisher
senses.zh: 诺斯克里夫勋爵（Lord Northcliffe）：生于英国报纸出版商阿尔弗雷德·查尔斯·威廉·哈姆斯沃斯（1865-1922），出生于爱尔兰。他于1896年创建了《每日邮报》，并于1903年创建了《每日镜报》，介绍了当时英国不陌生的新闻风格。文章简短而生动，其中一些专为女性撰写，并且使用了更多标题。诺思克里夫还是1908年至1922年《泰晤士报》的所有者。在第一次世界大战期间，他帮助英国政府进行了宣传（即影响公众舆论的信息），并于1917年成为了副总统。他是一个很坚强的人，喜欢权力。他的弟弟哈罗德（后来的罗瑟米尔勋爵）是他早期职业的伙伴。

senses.def: born William Richard Morris (1877-1963) an English businessman who was the first person in Britain to mass-produce
senses.zh: 纳菲尔德勋爵（Lord Nuffield）：生于英国商人威廉·理查德·莫里斯（William Richard Morris，1877-1963年），他是英国第一位批量生产汽车的人。他在牛津开始从事自行车修理业务，不久便开始制造自行车和汽车。莫里斯汽车公司非常成功，莫里斯本人也变得非常富有。他把很多钱都捐给了医院和慈善机构，还捐给了牛津大学，以他的名字命名的纳菲尔德大学。

senses.def: a novel (1954) by William Golding
senses.zh: 蝇王：威廉·戈尔丁（William Golding）的小说（1954）。它讲述了一群飞机失事后留在岛上的男孩的故事。最初，他们试图以和平方式生活在一起，但后来彼此残酷并崇拜一个被发明的神，“苍蝇王”（被苍蝇遮住的猪头）。戈尔德（Golding）在写这本书时使用了一个较早的，非常不同的儿童故事中的角色的名字，即RM Ballantyne的《珊瑚岛》（1858年）。

senses.def: Henry John Temple, 3rd Viscount Palmerston (1784-1865) an English prime minister (1855-58 and 1859-65). He began his career as a Tory
senses.zh: 帕默斯顿勋爵：亨利·约翰·邓普（Henry John Temple），帕默斯顿三世子爵（1784-1865），英国总理（1855-58和1859-65）。他的职业生涯始于保守党，但在1830年，他成为辉格党政府的外交大臣。他以使用武装力量保护英国在其他国家的利益而闻名。他曾在克里米亚战争和印度叛变期间担任总理，几乎使英国卷入了美国内战。

senses.def: a character in several crime novels by Dorothy Sayers
senses.zh: 彼得·温西勋爵（Lord Peter Wimsey）：多萝西·塞耶斯（Dorothy Sayers）的几本犯罪小说中的角色。他是一位英国主人，是一位非常出色的业余侦探。

senses.def: the title given to Oliver Cromwell
senses.zh: 护国公英国内战后护国公时期（1653—1659）奥利弗·克伦威尔及其子理查德·克伦威尔（1626—1712）的称号。克伦威尔曾解散议会，父子俩先后统治英国。

senses.def: the Scottish equivalent
senses.zh: 市长大人（苏格兰大城市市长的称号）

senses.def: John Reith (1889-1971) a Scottish broadcaster
senses.zh: 瑞斯勋爵：约翰·瑞斯（John Reith，1889-1971年）是苏格兰广播公司，后来成为BBC的第一任总经理。他的职业生涯始于工业界，但于1922年加入英国广播公司。在担任总经理期间（1927-38年），他在公共广播服务方面设定了高标准，认为英国广播公司有责任向公众宣传，教育和娱乐。他还帮助其摆脱了政府的控制。赖斯（Reith）在第二次世界大战期间担任政府部长，并于1940年成为终身同伴。

senses.def: born Harold Sydney Harmsworth (1868-1940) an English businessman who owned several newspapers, including the Daily Mirror
senses.zh: 罗瑟米尔勋爵（Lord Rothermere）：生于英国商人哈罗德·悉尼·哈姆斯沃斯（Harold Sydney Harmsworth，1868-1940年），他拥有几份报纸，包括《每日镜报》和《每日邮报》。他的兄弟是诺思克里夫勋爵。他的孙子第三任罗瑟米尔勋爵（生于1925-1998年，是Vere Harold Esmond Harmsworth先生），于1971年从其父亲手中接过了《每日邮报》，并在《星期日和晚间标准报》上拥有该邮报。

senses.def: a famous English cricket
senses.zh: 洛德（Lord）：位于伦敦北部圣约翰伍德（St John's Wood）的一个著名的英国板球场，这里定期举行测试比赛。它以托马斯·洛德（1755-1832）的名字命名，托马斯·洛德（1755-1832）于1814年在这里建立了基地。MCC和英格兰和威尔士板球委员会都设在那儿，也是保存灰烬的地方。这也是米德尔塞克斯郡板球俱乐部的所在地。

senses.def: born Robert Gascoyne-Cecil 1830-1903 a British Conservative (1885-6, 1886-92 and 1895-1902). He helped to increase the power of the British Empire
senses.zh: 索尔兹伯里勋爵（Lord Salisbury）：罗伯特·加斯科因·塞西尔（Robert Gascoyne-Cecil）1830-1903年出生，是英国的保守党（1885-6、1886-92和1895-1902）。他帮助提高了大英帝国，特别是在非洲的力量，并支持塞西尔·罗德斯（Cecil Rhodes）等人的活动。在他执政的最后时期，他领导了布尔战争中的英国。

senses.def: Alfred Tennyson (1809-92) an English poet known especially for his long narrative poems (= ones that tell a story)
senses.zh: 坦尼森勋爵：阿尔弗雷德·坦尼森（Alfred Tennyson，1809-92年），一位英国诗人，以长篇叙事诗（讲故事的诗）而闻名。他以其在亲密的朋友亚瑟·哈拉姆（Arthur Hallam）突然去世后写的诗《纪念》而声名远扬，并于1850年出版。同年，他被任命为诗人桂冠。他的其他著名诗作包括《沙洛特夫人》，《莫德》，《国王的田园诗》和《轻旅》。1884年，他被封为男爵。

senses.def: born Archibald Percival Wavell (1883-1950) a senior military officer in charge of British forces in the Middle East from 1939 to 1941, during the Second World War
senses.zh: 韦维尔勋爵（Lord Wavell）：生于阿奇博尔德·珀西瓦尔·韦维尔（Archibald Percival Wavell，1883-1950年），他是第二次世界大战期间1939年至1941年负责中东英军的高级军事官。他后来在印度指挥英军，从1943年到1947年，他担任印度总督。1947年，他成为伯爵。

senses.def: behaving in a way that suggests that you think you are better than other people

examples.en: He dismissed us with a lordly gesture.
examples.zh: 他以一种威严的姿态让我们走开。

senses.def: large and impressive; suitable for a lord
senses.zh: 宏伟的；堂皇的；贵族气派的

examples.en: a lordly mansion
examples.zh: 富丽堂皇的宅第

senses.def: a title of respect used when speaking to or about a judge, a bishop
senses.zh: （对法官、主教或贵族的尊称）阁下，大人，爵爷

examples.en: His Lordship is away on business.
examples.zh: 爵爷有事出去了。

senses.def: a humorous way of talking to or about a boy or man that you think is trying to be too important
senses.zh: （对自以为了不起的男孩或男子幽默的称呼）阁下

examples.en: Can his lordship manage to switch off the TV?
examples.zh: 请阁下设法关掉电视机好不好？

senses.def: the power or position of a lord
senses.zh: 贵族的权力（或身份、地位）

senses.def: knowledge and information related to a particular subject, especially when this is not written down; the stories and traditions of a particular group of people
senses.zh: （尤指口头流传的）某一方面的学问；（某一群体的）传说，传统

examples.en: weather lore
examples.zh: 天气的知识

examples.en: Celtic lore
examples.zh: 凯尔特人的传说

senses.def: (1895-1943) a US writer of songs, who with Richard Rodgers
senses.zh: 洛伦兹·哈特（Lorenz Hart）：（1895-1943年）是美国的一位歌曲作家，他与理查德·罗杰斯（Richard Rodgers）共同创作了29部百老汇音乐剧，其中许多成为电影。哈特写了这句话，罗杰斯则写了音乐。他们的作品包括《武器中的宝贝》（Babes in Arms，1937年）和《 Pal Joey》（Pal Joey，1940年），以及他们创作的歌曲中的《 The Lady is Tramp》（1937年）和《 This Ca n't Be Love》（1938年）。

senses.def: an old-fashioned pair of glasses that you hold to your eyes on a long handle
a small bird found mainly in New Guinea
senses.zh: 吸蜜鹦鹉（主要见于新几内亚）

senses.def: a first name for girls
a romantic novel (1869) by the English author R D Blackmore (1825-1900). It is set on Exmoor
senses.zh: 英国作家RD Blackmore（1825-1900）创作的浪漫小说（1869）。它坐落于17世纪的埃克斯穆尔（Exmoor），讲述了一个年轻人爱上一个叫洛娜·杜恩（Lorna Doone）的女孩的故事。不幸的是，她来自谋杀父亲的家庭。这个时期的一些历史事件构成了故事的一部分。

senses.def: a large vehicle for carrying heavy loads by road

examples.en: a lorry driver
examples.zh: 卡车司机

examples.en: a lorry load of frozen fish
examples.zh: 装满一卡车的冷冻鱼

examples.en: Emergency food supplies were brought in by lorry.
examples.zh: 应急食物是用卡车运来的。

senses.def: goods that fell off the back of a lorry

items.idm: off the back of a lorry

senses.def: goods that fell off the back of a lorry
a small US town in northern New Mexico
senses.zh: 洛斯阿拉莫斯（Los Alamos）：新墨西哥州北部的美国小镇。第一个原子弹和氢弹是在1943年建立的美国政府核研究中心在那里开发的，而该镇则在该中心附近成长。洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室（LANL）为美国能源部运营，其教育和研究工作包括中子科学中心。

senses.def: the second largest city in the US and the largest in California
senses.zh: 洛杉矶（美国加利福尼亚州南部城市，位于太平洋沿岸，是美国第二大、加利福尼亚州最大城市）

senses.def: to be unable to find something/somebody

examples.en: I've lost my keys.
examples.zh: 我把钥匙丢了。

examples.en: The tickets seem to have got lost.
examples.zh: 那些票好像给弄丢了。

examples.en: She lost her husband in the crowd.
examples.zh: 她在人群中与丈夫走散了。

senses.def: to have something/somebody taken away from you, especially as a result of an accident, dying, etc.
senses.zh: （尤指因事故、死亡等）损失，丧失，失去

examples.en: She lost a leg in a car crash.
examples.zh: 她在一次车祸中失去了一条腿。

examples.en: Some families lost everything (= all they owned) in the flood.
examples.zh: 有些家庭的财产在洪水中损失得精光。

examples.en: She lost her baby (= had a miscarriage) three months into the pregnancy.
examples.zh: 她怀孕三个月时流产了。

examples.en: They lost both their sons (= they were killed) in the war.
examples.zh: 他们的两个儿子都被战争夺去了生命。

examples.en: The ship was lost at sea (= it sank).
examples.zh: 那条船沉没了。

examples.en: Many people lost their lives (= were killed).
examples.zh: 有许多人丧生。

senses.group: have something/somebody taken away 丧失

senses.def: to have to give up something; to fail to keep something/somebody

examples.en: He's lost his job.
examples.zh: 他失业了。

examples.en: You will lose your deposit if you cancel the order.
examples.zh: 如果撤销订单，订金将不予退还。

examples.en: Sit down or you'll lose your seat.
examples.zh: 坐下吧，要不这个座位就没啦。

examples.en: The government has lost control of the city.
examples.zh: 政府失去了对这个城市的控制。

examples.en: We cannot afford to lose any more senior members of staff.
examples.zh: 我们不能再失去更多高级员工了。

examples.en: The average business loses 20 per cent of its customers every year.
examples.zh: 企业平均每年失去 20% 的客户。

examples.en: You risk losing your house if you do not keep up the payments.
examples.zh: 如果您不继续付款，您将面临失去房屋的风险。

examples.en: The company has lost a lot of business to its competitors.
examples.zh: 公司的许多生意都被对手夺走了。

senses.group: have something/somebody taken away 丧失

senses.def: to no longer have something, or have less of something than you had before, especially as a result of getting older

examples.en: to lose your hair/teeth
examples.zh: 掉头发；掉牙齿

examples.en: to lose your sight/eyesight/hearing/memory
examples.zh: 视力／听力／记忆力减退

examples.en: There's new hope for people trying to lose weight.
examples.zh: 想减肥的人有了新的希望。

examples.en: I've lost ten pounds since I started this diet.
examples.zh: 这次节食开始以来我体重减了十磅。

senses.def: to have less and less of a quality or ability, especially until you no longer have any of it
senses.zh: 慢慢失去，渐渐丧失（品质或能力）

examples.en: She seemed to have lost interest in food.
examples.zh: 她好像对食物不感兴趣了。

examples.en: to lose faith/confidence
examples.zh: 失去信心

examples.en: He lost his nerve at the last minute.
examples.zh: 他在最后一刻失去了勇气。

examples.en: At that moment he lost his balance and fell.
examples.zh: 他在那一瞬间失去平衡摔倒了。

examples.en: The train was losing speed.
examples.zh: 火车当时正在减速。

examples.en: She never lost the ability to make people laugh.
examples.zh: 她从未失去让人们发笑的能力。

senses.def: to be defeated; to fail to win a competition, a court case, an argument, etc.; to cause somebody to be defeated
senses.zh: （使）被打败；输掉（比赛、诉讼案件、辩论等）

examples.en: So far they haven't lost a game.
examples.zh: 到目前为止，他们还没有输过一场比赛。

examples.en: to lose a race/an election/a battle/a war
examples.zh: 输掉赛跑／选举／战役／战争

examples.en: We lost to a stronger team.
examples.zh: 我们输给了一支实力更强的队。

examples.en: He lost by less than 100 votes.
examples.zh: 他以不到 100 张选票败北。

examples.en: We lost the game by three points.
examples.zh: 我们以三分之差输掉了比赛。

examples.en: They lost on penalties to (= because they scored fewer penalties than) Spain.
examples.zh: 他们在点球大战中输给了西班牙。

examples.en: Many believe the incident lost them the election.
examples.zh: 许多人认为这一事件导致他们选举失利。

senses.def: to fail to keep something you want or need, especially money; to cause somebody to fail to keep something
senses.zh: （使）失去（所需要的东西，尤指钱）

examples.en: The business is losing money.
examples.zh: 这家公司正在亏损。

examples.en: Poetry always loses something in translation.
examples.zh: 诗歌一经翻译总会失去某些东西。

examples.en: You have nothing to lose by telling the truth.
examples.zh: 你讲真话是不会吃亏的。

examples.en: What do we lose by working with them?
examples.zh: 与他们合作我们会失去什么？

examples.en: We lost on that deal.
examples.zh: 我们那笔交易做亏了。

examples.en: The company stands to lose financially if this deal falls through.
examples.zh: 如果这次交易落空，公司可能会有经济损失。

examples.en: His carelessness lost him the job.
examples.zh: 他粗枝大叶，丢了工作。

senses.def: to fail to get, hear or understand something

examples.en: His words were lost (= could not be heard) in the applause.
examples.zh: 他的讲话让掌声淹没了。

senses.group: not understand/hear 弄不懂；听不见

senses.def: to be no longer understood by somebody

examples.en: I'm afraid you've lost me there.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，我没听明白你的话。

senses.group: not understand/hear 弄不懂；听不见

senses.def: to escape from somebody/something

examples.en: We managed to lose our pursuers in the darkness.
examples.zh: 我们设法在黑暗中摆脱了追赶者。

senses.def: to waste time or an opportunity

examples.en: We lost twenty minutes changing a tyre.
examples.zh: 我们换轮胎耽误了二十分钟。

examples.en: Hurry—there's no time to lose!
examples.zh: 快点，抓紧时间吧！

examples.en: He lost no time in setting out for London.
examples.zh: 他赶紧启程去了伦敦。

senses.def: if a watch or clock loses

examples.en: This clock loses two minutes a day.
examples.zh: 这时钟每天慢两分钟。

senses.def: to become unable to control your emotions or behaviour

examples.en: Then she just lost it and started screaming.
examples.zh: 然后她再也控制不住，尖叫起来。

note.en: Most idioms containing lose are at the entries for the nouns and adjectives in the idioms, for example lose your bearings is at bearing.
note.zh: 大多数含 lose 的习语，都可在该等习语中的名词及形容词相关词条找到，如 lose your bearings 在词条 bearing 下。

senses.def: to become unable to control your emotions or behaviour

examples.en: Then she just lost it and started screaming.
examples.zh: 然后她再也控制不住，尖叫起来。

senses.def: to forget the total of something before you have finished counting it

examples.en: I lost count and had to start again.
examples.zh: 我数着数着忘了，不得不又从头开始数。

examples.en: She had lost count of the number of times she'd told him to be careful (= she could not remember because there were so many).
examples.zh: 她不知多少次告诉过他要小心。

examples.en: I've lost count of the times I've heard that joke.
examples.zh: 那个笑话我不知道听过多少遍了。

senses.def: to be less respected or look stupid because of something you have done

examples.en: Many leaders don't want to lose face by admitting failures.
examples.zh: 许多领导人为免丢脸，不愿承认失败。

senses.def: to stop hoping for something or trying to do something because you no longer feel confident
to become unable to control your emotions or behaviour

examples.en: Then she just lost it and started screaming.
examples.zh: 然后她再也控制不住，尖叫起来。

senses.def: to become no longer able to see somebody/something

examples.en: They finally lost sight of land.
examples.zh: 他们终于看不见陆地了。

senses.def: to stop considering something; to forget something

examples.en: We must not lose sight of our original aim.
examples.zh: 我们决不能忘记我们最初的目标。

senses.def: to not notice somebody/something or pay attention to somebody/something because of a confusing situation
senses.zh: 在混乱中没有注意到；忽略；遗失

examples.en: Middle children tend to get lost in the shuffle.
examples.zh: 排行居中的子女往往得不到充分的关注。

senses.def: to lose your ability to understand or deal with what is happening
to no longer have any contact with somebody/something

examples.en: I've lost touch with all my old friends.
examples.zh: 我与所有的老朋友都失去了联系。

senses.def: to no longer understand something, especially how ordinary people feel
senses.zh: 不再了解（尤指一般人的想法）

senses.def: to become angry or excited

examples.en: I lost my cool and shouted at them.
examples.zh: 我火冒三丈，对他们大吼了起来。

senses.def: to become unable to understand or control a situation
senses.zh: 失去（对…的）理解（或控制）；驾驭不住

examples.en: Sometimes I feel I'm losing my grip.
examples.zh: 有时我感到自己无能为力。

senses.def: to become unable to act in a calm or sensible way
to fall in love with somebody/something
to become mentally ill

examples.en: He feared he was losing his mind.
examples.zh: 他那时害怕自己会失去理智。

senses.def: to get angry
to become lost

examples.en: We lost our way in the dark.
examples.zh: 我们在黑暗中迷了路。

examples.en: She lost her way in the fog.
examples.zh: 她在大雾中迷了路。

senses.def: to forget or move away from the purpose or reason for something

examples.en: I feel that the project has lost its way.
examples.zh: 我觉得这个项目已经背离了原来的意图。

examples.en: This project seems to have lost its way.
examples.zh: 这个项目似乎背离了原来的意图。

senses.def: to not get something you wanted or feel you should have
senses.zh: 得不到（想要或觉得应有的东西）

examples.en: While the stores make big profits, it's the customer who loses out.
examples.zh: 商店赚大钱，而吃亏的是顾客。

senses.def: to not get business, etc. that you expected or used to get because somebody/something else has taken it

examples.en: Small businesses are losing out to the large chains.
examples.zh: 小商店被大型的连锁店抢了生意。

examples.en: Our company lost out to one that could offer a lower price.
examples.zh: 我们输给了报价更低的一家公司。

senses.def: to become so interested in something that it takes all your attention
to fail/manage to control your anger

examples.en: She lost her temper with a customer and shouted at him.
examples.zh: 她对一位顾客发了脾气，冲着他大喊大叫。

examples.en: I struggle to keep my temper with the kids when they misbehave.
examples.zh: 孩子们淘气时，我强捺住性子不发脾气。

senses.def: a person who is defeated in a competition

examples.en: winners and losers
examples.zh: 赢家与输家

examples.en: He’s a good/bad loser (= he accepts defeat well/badly).
examples.zh: 他是个输得起／输不起的人。

senses.def: a person who is regularly unsuccessful, especially when you have a low opinion of them
senses.zh: 屡屡失败的人（尤指评价较低者）

examples.en: She's one of life's losers.
examples.zh: 她是个生活的失败者。

examples.en: He's a born loser.
examples.zh: 他生来就是个失败者。

senses.def: a person who suffers because of a particular action, decision, etc.
senses.zh: （因某行为、决定等的）受损害者

examples.en: The real losers in all of this are the students.
examples.zh: 在这一切中真正受损害的是学生。

examples.en: If the teachers go on strike, the children are the ultimate losers.
examples.zh: 如果教师罢工，最终受害的将是孩子们。

senses.def: the state of no longer having something or as much of something; the process that leads to this

examples.en: I want to report the loss of a package.
examples.zh: 我要报告丢失了一个包裹。

examples.en: Insure your instrument against loss or damage.
examples.zh: 确保您的仪器免遭丢失或损坏。

examples.en: weight loss
examples.zh: 体重减少

examples.en: hearing/memory loss
examples.zh: 听力／记忆力减退

examples.en: We can help people with sight loss lead full and independent lives.
examples.zh: 我们可以帮助视力丧失的人过上充实而独立的生活。

examples.en: The closure of the factory will lead to a number of job losses.
examples.zh: 工厂倒闭会使许多人失业。

examples.en: When she died I was filled with a sense of loss.
examples.zh: 她去世后我心里充满了失落感。

examples.en: He suffered a loss of confidence.
examples.zh: 他失去了信心。

examples.en: loss of earnings/income (= the money you do not earn because you are prevented from working)
examples.zh: 收入损失

examples.en: The loss of her job was a terrible blow.
examples.zh: 失去工作对她来说是一个可怕的打击。

senses.def: money that has been lost by a business or an organization

examples.en: The company has announced net losses of $1.5 million.
examples.zh: 公司宣布净亏损 150 万美元。

examples.en: The banks incurred huge losses.
examples.zh: 银行遭受了巨大损失。

examples.en: We made a loss on (= lost money on) the deal.
examples.zh: 我们做那笔交易亏了。

senses.def: the death of a person

examples.en: He is mourning the loss of his wife.
examples.zh: 他在哀悼亡妻。

examples.en: the tragic loss of a child
examples.zh: 不幸丧子

examples.en: Enemy troops suffered heavy losses.
examples.zh: 敌军伤亡惨重。

examples.en: The drought caused widespread loss of life.
examples.zh: 旱灾导致了许多人的死亡。

senses.def: the disadvantage that is caused when somebody leaves, or when a useful or valuable object is taken away; a person who causes a disadvantage by leaving
senses.zh: （某人离开或重要物品被取走造成的）损失；因离去而造成损失者

examples.en: Her departure is a big loss to the school.
examples.zh: 她这一走对学校来说是一个巨大的损失。

examples.en: She will be a great loss to the company.
examples.zh: 她的离去对公司来说将是一个巨大的损失。

examples.en: She wouldn't be able to attend the lecture, which was no great loss.
examples.zh: 她没能去听讲座，其实也没有什么损失。

examples.en: His death is a sad loss to all who knew him.
examples.zh: 他的去世让所有认识他的人都痛惜不已。

senses.def: a failure to win a contest

examples.en: Brazil’s 2–1 loss to Argentina
examples.zh: 巴西对阿根廷 1:2 的落败

senses.def: not knowing what to say or do

examples.en: His comments left me at a loss for words.
examples.zh: 他的评论让我不知说什么才好。

examples.en: I'm at a loss what to do next.
examples.zh: 我对下一步做什么心里没谱。

examples.en: We are at a loss to understand his actions.
examples.zh: 我们对他的行动迷惑不解。

senses.def: in a way that loses you money

examples.en: We are now operating at a loss.
examples.zh: 我们现在是亏本经营。

senses.def: used to say that if somebody chooses not to do something, they will not obtain a benefit they could have had

examples.en: If people can't appreciate how great this film is, it's their loss.
examples.zh: 如果有人不懂得这部电影有多么伟大，那是他们的损失。

examples.en: I can see you don't trust me. Well, that's your loss
examples.zh: 我看得出你不信任我。好吧，那是你的损失

senses.def: to stop doing something that is not successful before the situation becomes even worse
senses.zh: 不成功就住手（免得情况更糟）；趁早罢手

examples.en: I decided to cut my losses and move back to England.
examples.zh: 我决定减少损失并搬回英国。

examples.en: He decided to cut his losses and sell the shares before they sank further.
examples.zh: 他决定在股票继续下跌之前卖出，以减少亏损。

senses.def: the state of being less respected by other people or looking stupid because of something you have done

examples.en: Failure to pass the exams means a massive loss of face for the students and their parents.
examples.zh: 考试不及格对学生和家长来说意味着巨大的颜面损失。

senses.def: not knowing what to say or do

examples.en: His comments left me at a loss for words.
examples.zh: 他的评论让我不知说什么才好。

examples.en: I'm at a loss what to do next.
examples.zh: 我对下一步做什么心里没谱。

examples.en: We are at a loss to understand his actions.
examples.zh: 我们对他的行动迷惑不解。

senses.def: in a way that loses you money

examples.en: We are now operating at a loss.
examples.zh: 我们现在是亏本经营。

senses.def: used to say that if somebody chooses not to do something, they will not obtain a benefit they could have had

examples.en: If people can't appreciate how great this film is, it's their loss.
examples.zh: 如果有人不懂得这部电影有多么伟大，那是他们的损失。

examples.en: I can see you don't trust me. Well, that's your loss
examples.zh: 我看得出你不信任我。好吧，那是你的损失

senses.def: to stop doing something that is not successful before the situation becomes even worse
senses.zh: 不成功就住手（免得情况更糟）；趁早罢手

examples.en: I decided to cut my losses and move back to England.
examples.zh: 我决定减少损失并搬回英国。

examples.en: He decided to cut his losses and sell the shares before they sank further.
examples.zh: 他决定在股票继续下跌之前卖出，以减少亏损。

senses.def: the state of being less respected by other people or looking stupid because of something you have done

examples.en: Failure to pass the exams means a massive loss of face for the students and their parents.
examples.zh: 考试不及格对学生和家长来说意味着巨大的颜面损失。

senses.def: the state of being less respected by other people or looking stupid because of something you have done

examples.en: Failure to pass the exams means a massive loss of face for the students and their parents.
examples.zh: 考试不及格对学生和家长来说意味着巨大的颜面损失。

senses.def: a person who works for an insurance company and whose job is to calculate how much money somebody should receive after they have lost something or had something damaged
senses.zh: （保险公司的）险损估价师，损失理算人，理赔员

senses.def: an item that a shop sells at a very low price, so that they lose money on it, in order to attract customers
not making a profit; losing money

examples.en: Support for loss-making state enterprises was a drain on the budget.
examples.zh: 对亏损国有企业的支持消耗了预算。

senses.def: involving no loss of data or electrical energy
senses.zh: （数据或电能）无损的；无损耗的

senses.def: involving the loss of data or electrical energy
senses.zh: （数据或电能）有损的；有损耗的

senses.def: the place where items that have been found are kept until they are collected
something that has failed or that cannot succeed
senses.zh: 业已失败的事情；没有希望的事情

examples.en: The game looked a lost cause when the score reached 6–0.
examples.zh: 当比分达到6-0时，比赛看起来已经失败了。

senses.def: items that have been found in public places and are waiting to be collected by the people who lost them

examples.en: a lost-property office
examples.zh: 失物招领处

senses.def: the place where items that have been found are kept until they are collected
a large number or amount

examples.en: ‘How many do you need?’ ‘A lot.’
examples.zh: “你需要多少？”“很多。”

examples.en: Have some more cake. There's lots left.
examples.zh: 再吃点蛋糕吧。还剩下好多呢。

examples.en: He has invited nearly a hundred people but a lot aren't able to come.
examples.zh: 他邀请了差不多一百人，但很多人都来不了。

examples.en: I have a lot to do today.
examples.zh: 我今天有很多事要做。

examples.en: She still has an awful lot (= a very large amount) to learn.
examples.zh: 她要学的还多着呢。

senses.def: a large number or amount of somebody/something

examples.en: What a lot of presents!
examples.zh: 礼品真多啊！

examples.en: A lot of people are coming to the meeting.
examples.zh: 有很多人要来参加这次会议。

examples.en: black coffee with lots of sugar
examples.zh: 不加奶多放糖的咖啡

examples.en: I saw a lot of her (= I saw her often) last summer.
examples.zh: 去年夏天我经常见到她。

senses.def: used with verbs to mean ‘a great amount’

examples.en: I care a lot about you.
examples.zh: 我非常在乎你。

examples.en: Thanks a lot for your help.
examples.zh: 非常感谢你的帮助。

examples.en: I play tennis quite a lot (= often) in the summer.
examples.zh: 我夏天常打网球。

senses.def: used with adjectives and adverbs to mean ‘much’
senses.zh: （与形容词和副词连用）很，非常

examples.en: I'm feeling a lot better today.
examples.zh: 我今天感觉好多了。

examples.en: I spend a lot more time with my family now.
examples.zh: 我现在和家人在一起的时间要多得多。

examples.en: I eat lots less than I used to.
examples.zh: 我比以前吃得少多了。

examples.en: Are you sure he 's not Mark ? He looks an awful lot like him.
examples.zh: 你确定他不是马克？他看起来非常像他。

examples.en: I got into the city centre a whole lot more quickly than expected.
examples.zh: 我到达市中心的速度比预想的要快得多。

senses.def: the whole number or amount of people or things

examples.en: He's bought a new laptop, microphone, printer—the lot.
examples.zh: 他买了新的笔记本电脑、麦克风、打印机，样样齐备。

examples.en: She bought the whole lot.
examples.zh: 她全部买了下来。

examples.en: Get out of my house, the lot of you!
examples.zh: 你们别待在我家里，通通给我滚出去！

examples.en: That's the lot! (= that includes everything)
examples.zh: 全都在这儿了！

examples.en: That's your lot! (= that's all you're getting)
examples.zh: 你的那份儿全在那儿了！

senses.def: a group or set of people or things

examples.en: The first lot of visitors has/have arrived.
examples.zh: 首批游客已经到达。

examples.en: I have several lots of essays to mark this weekend.
examples.zh: 这周末我有几批文章要批改。

examples.en: What do you lot want?
examples.zh: 你们这帮人想要怎么样？

examples.en: Shall I put this lot with the others?
examples.zh: 我把这些东西跟其他的放在一起可以吗？

senses.def: used to express sympathy for somebody

examples.en: Bad luck, Helen—you played very well.
examples.zh: 海伦，你表现得非常好，只是运气欠佳。

examples.en: It's hard luck on him that he wasn't chosen.
examples.zh: 他未被选中真是不幸。

examples.en: What rotten luck it had to happen now!
examples.zh: 现在竟然发生这样的事真是太倒霉了！

senses.def: to have no money because of a period of bad luck
senses.zh: 因一时不走运而没有钱；穷困潦倒

examples.en: In the movie they play two jazz musicians who are down on their luck.
examples.zh: 在电影中，他们扮演两位运气不佳的爵士音乐家。

items.idm: the best of luck (with something) | good luck (with something)

senses.def: used to wish somebody success with something

examples.en: The best of luck with your exams.
examples.zh: 祝你考试成功！

examples.en: Good luck! I hope it goes well.
examples.zh: 祝你交好运！我希望这事进展顺利。

examples.en: ‘I'm going to try giving up social media for a year.’ ‘Good luck with that (= I don't think you will succeed).’
examples.zh: “我打算尝试放弃社交媒体一年。”“祝你好运（=我认为你不会成功）。”

senses.def: used to encourage somebody who has not been successful at something
senses.zh: （鼓励未成功的人）祝下次好运

examples.en: Never mind— better luck next time.
examples.zh: 没关系，祝你下次好运。

examples.en: If you didn't win a prize, better luck next time.
examples.zh: 如果没获奖，愿你下次好运。

senses.def: because you believe it will bring you good luck, or because this is a traditional belief
senses.zh: 图个吉利；为了带来好运

examples.en: Take something blue. It's for luck.
examples.zh: 挑件蓝色的东西吧，求个吉利。

examples.en: I always carry it with me, just for luck.
examples.zh: 为讨吉利，我总是随身带着它。

senses.def: for no particular reason

examples.en: I gave the mixture one more stir for luck.
examples.zh: 我顺手又把混合物搅了一次。

senses.def: used to say that you do not mind what somebody does as it does not affect you, but you hope they will be successful
senses.zh: （与己无关而不介意某人的所为）祝某人成功，祝某人走运

examples.en: It's not something I would care to try myself but if she wants to, good luck to her.
examples.zh: 这件事我自己是不想做的，但如果她想试一试，祝愿她成功。

senses.def: used to tell somebody that you feel sorry for them

examples.en: ‘Failed again, I'm afraid.’ ‘Oh, hard luck.’
examples.zh: “恐怕我又失败了。”“哦，太不幸了。”

senses.def: used to show you are not surprised something bad has happened to you, because you are not often lucky
senses.zh: （对自己的遭遇并不惊讶）常不走运，就这运气

examples.en: Just my luck to arrive after they had left.
examples.zh: 我总是这样倒霉，他们离去后我才赶到。

examples.en: Just my luck to get the broken chair!
examples.zh: 我这把椅子是坏的，我总是那么倒霉！

senses.def: used to say that somebody has been lucky or successful

examples.en: On a Sunday I didn’t expect to find him at his desk but my luck was in.
examples.zh: 星期天我没指望在他的办公桌前找到他，但我运气真好。

senses.def: the fact that chance decides something, in a way that you cannot control

examples.en: To a large extent the life you have depends on who your parents were; it’s just the luck of the biological draw.
examples.zh: 在很大程度上，你的生活取决于你的父母是谁。这只是生物抽签的运气。

senses.def: used to show that you are disappointed because something you were hoping for did not happen
senses.zh: 没那么走运（所希望的事情没有发生而失望）

examples.en: ‘Were you chosen for the team?’ ‘No such luck!’
examples.zh: “你被选入球队了吗？”“没那么幸运！”

senses.def: when you take pot luck

examples.en: It's pot luck whether you get good advice or not.
examples.zh: 能不能得到好的指点那就全靠运气了。

examples.en: You're welcome to stay to supper, but you'll have to take pot luck (= eat whatever is available).
examples.zh: 欢迎你留下来吃晚饭，不过你得有什么就吃什么了。

senses.def: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
senses.zh: （由于过去的成功过关）再冒一次险，继续碰运气

examples.en: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!
examples.zh: 上次没被逮住，但你不要再心存侥幸了！

senses.def: used to show sympathy for somebody that something bad that has happened to

examples.en: ‘I failed by one point.’ ‘That's tough luck.’
examples.zh: “我差一分没及格。”“运气真不好。”

senses.def: used to show that you do not feel sorry for somebody who has a problem

examples.en: ‘If you take the car, I won't be able to go out.’ ‘Tough luck!’
examples.zh: “如果你把车开走，我就出不去了。”“该你倒霉！”

senses.def: to do something that involves risk or luck, hoping to succeed

examples.en: My grandparents emigrated to Canada to try their luck there.
examples.zh: 我的祖父母移民到加拿大去碰碰运气。

senses.def: used to show that you are disappointed about something

examples.en: I shall have to miss the party, worse luck!
examples.zh: 我参加不了这次聚会了，真倒霉！

intro.en: These are all words for things that happen or the force that causes them to happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指机遇、命运、运气。

items.def: the force that causes good or bad things to happen to people:
items.zh: 指机遇、命运、运气

examples.en: This ring has always brought me good luck.
examples.zh: 这戒指总是给我带来好运。

items.def: the way that some things happen without any cause that you can see or understand:
items.zh: 指偶然、碰巧、意外

examples.en: The results could simply be due to chance.
examples.zh: 这结果可能纯属意外。

items.def: the fact of two things happening at the same time by chance, in a surprising way:
items.zh: 指出人意料的巧合、巧事

examples.en: They met through a series of strange coincidences.
examples.zh: 他们因一连串奇妙的巧合而相遇。

items.def: something that happens unexpectedly and is not planned in advance:
items.zh: 指意外、偶然的事

examples.en: Their early arrival was just an accident.
examples.zh: 他们早到仅仅是偶然而已。

items.def: the power that is believed to control everything that happens and that cannot be stopped or changed:
items.zh: 指命运、天数、定数、天意

examples.en: Fate decreed that she would never reach America.
examples.zh: 命中注定她永远到不了美国。

items.def: the power that is believed to control events:
items.zh: 指主宰事物的力量、命运之神

examples.en: I believe there’s some force guiding us—call it God, destiny or fate.
examples.zh: 我认为有某种力量在指引着我们，称之为上帝也罢，天意也罢，或是命运也罢。

senses.def: to be lucky

examples.en: I guess I really lucked out when I met her.
examples.zh: 我想，我遇到她真是交了好运。

senses.def: by good luck

examples.en: Luckily for us, the train was late.
examples.zh: 我们运气不错，火车晚点了。

examples.en: Luckily, I am a good swimmer.
examples.zh: 幸好我是个游泳好手。

senses.def: having bad luck
senses.zh: 运气不好的；不走运的；不幸的

examples.en: the luckless victim of the attack
examples.zh: 遭到袭击的不幸受害者

examples.en: The luckless striker will be out for six weeks with his latest injury.
examples.zh: 这位不幸的前锋因最近的伤势将缺席六周。

senses.def: having good luck
senses.zh: 有好运的；运气好的；幸运的

examples.en: His friend was killed and he knows he is lucky to be alive.
examples.zh: 他的朋友丧了命，他知道自己还活着是侥幸。

examples.en: She was lucky enough to be chosen for the team.
examples.zh: 她很幸运被选中参加此队。

examples.en: You were lucky (that) you spotted the danger in time.
examples.zh: 幸好你及时发现了险情。

examples.en: In terms of my career I feel incredibly lucky.
examples.zh: 就我的职业生涯而言，我感到非常幸运。

examples.en: You can think yourself lucky you didn't get mugged.
examples.zh: 你未遭暴力抢劫，可算是万幸了。

examples.en: She counted herself lucky that she still had a job.
examples.zh: 她认为自己很幸运，仍有一份工作。

examples.en: Mark is one of the lucky ones—he at least has somewhere to sleep.
examples.zh: 马克是个幸运的人，他至少还有地方睡觉。

examples.en: the lucky winners
examples.zh: 幸运的获胜者

examples.en: He was among the lucky ones who escaped with only minor injuries.
examples.zh: 他是幸运逃脱的人之一，只受了轻伤。

senses.def: being the result of good luck

examples.en: It was lucky for us that we were able to go.
examples.zh: 我们能去是我们的运气好。

examples.en: Lucky for her, a police car was passing.
examples.zh: 幸运的是，一辆警车正从她身边驶过。

examples.en: It is lucky (that) neither was killed in the accident.
examples.zh: 幸运的是，两人都没有在事故中丧生。

examples.en: That was the luckiest escape of my life.
examples.zh: 那次逃脱是我一生中最大的幸运。

examples.en: a lucky guess
examples.zh: 侥幸猜中

examples.en: A lucky find on the edge of the Cotswolds is helping archaeologists discover what life was like in Roman Britain.
examples.zh: 科茨沃尔德边缘的一个幸运发现正在帮助考古学家了解罗马时期不列颠的生活。

examples.en: I had a lucky break when I left school getting a job on local radio.
examples.zh: 当我离开学校在当地电台找到一份工作时，我有一次幸运的突破。

senses.def: bringing good luck

examples.en: a lucky charm
examples.zh: 吉祥配饰

examples.en: The team thinks of me as their lucky mascot.
examples.zh: 团队认为我是他们的幸运吉祥物。

senses.def: to have good luck

examples.en: She hopes that some day she'll get lucky and win the jackpot.
examples.zh: 她希望有一天她能鸿运当头中大奖。

senses.def: to meet somebody new and have sex with them

examples.en: Mike's hoping to get lucky tonight.
examples.zh: 迈克希望今晚能走桃花运。

senses.def: used to show that you think somebody is lucky to have something, be able to do something, etc.

examples.en: ‘I'm off to Paris.’ ‘Lucky you!’
examples.zh: “我要去巴黎了。”“你真幸运！”

senses.def: to have good luck

examples.en: We certainly struck it lucky with the weather.
examples.zh: 我们真幸运，遇上了好天气。

senses.def: to feel very grateful and lucky about something

examples.en: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.
examples.zh: 感谢你的幸运星，你当时不在屋子里。

senses.def: used when you have failed to do something twice and hope that you will succeed the third time
senses.zh: （但愿）第三次交好运；过一过二不过三

senses.def: used to tell somebody that something that they are expecting probably will not happen
senses.zh: （告诉某人所期盼的事很可能不会发生）但愿你会走运

examples.en: ‘I was hoping to get a ticket for Saturday.’ ‘You'll be lucky.’
examples.zh: “我盼望弄到一张星期六的票。”“但愿你会走运。”

senses.def: used to tell somebody that they will probably not get what they are hoping for, and may not deserve it
senses.zh: （告诉某人所希望之物可能得不到，且本不该其得到）你不见得这么走运吧

examples.zh: 她希望有一天她能鸿运当头中大奖。

examples.zh: “我要去巴黎了。”“你真幸运！”

examples.zh: 我们真幸运，遇上了好天气。

examples.en: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.
examples.zh: 感谢你的幸运星，你当时不在屋子里。

senses.def: used when you have failed to do something twice and hope that you will succeed the third time
senses.zh: （但愿）第三次交好运；过一过二不过三

senses.def: used to tell somebody that something that they are expecting probably will not happen
senses.zh: （告诉某人所期盼的事很可能不会发生）但愿你会走运

examples.en: ‘I was hoping to get a ticket for Saturday.’ ‘You'll be lucky.’
examples.zh: “我盼望弄到一张星期六的票。”“但愿你会走运。”

items.idm: you, etc. should be so lucky

senses.def: used to tell somebody that they will probably not get what they are hoping for, and may not deserve it
senses.zh: （告诉某人所希望之物可能得不到，且本不该其得到）你不见得这么走运吧

senses.def: used to show that you think somebody is lucky to have something, be able to do something, etc.

examples.en: ‘I'm off to Paris.’ ‘Lucky you!’
examples.zh: “我要去巴黎了。”“你真幸运！”

senses.def: a game in which people choose a present from a container of presents without being able to see what it is going to be
a comic novel (1954) by Kingsley Amis
senses.zh: 幸运吉姆：金斯利·阿米斯（Kingsley Amis）的漫画小说（1954）。主角吉姆·迪克森（Jim Dixon）是一位年轻的大学老师，不喜欢工作，爱上了另一个男人的女朋友。书中最有趣的时刻是吉姆喝醉了，在高年级老师面前表现不好的时候。这本书是由Boulting兄弟于1957年制成的电影，并于2003年制成电视电影。

senses.def: (1897-1962) a US criminal, born in Sicily. He became the head of a powerful criminal organization in New York in the 1920s and probably ordered the murder of his rival
senses.zh: “幸运”卢西亚诺：（1897-1962年）美国罪犯，出生于西西里岛。他在1920年代成为纽约一个强大的犯罪组织的负责人，并可能在1935年下令谋杀了他的对手“荷兰人”舒尔茨（Dutch Schultz）。一年后，他被送入监狱，继续从监狱进行非法活动， 1946年，他被送回意大利。

senses.def: a cigarette first sold in the US in the early 1900s. Phrases used to advertise Lucky Strike cigarettes have included ‘
senses.zh: 卷烟在1900年代初首次在美国销售。用来宣传Lucky Strike卷烟的短语包括“ Reach for a Lucky”，“ LS / MFT”（Lucky Strike表示优质烟草）和“ Be Happy，Go Lucky”。

senses.def: a sweet orange-coloured drink which is advertised as giving energy to people who take part in sports. In the past it was sold as a way of helping people to get well after an illness.
senses.zh: 一种甜甜的橙色饮料，被广告宣传为参与运动的人们提供能量。在过去，它被出售来帮助人们生病后康复。

senses.def: producing a large amount of money; making a large profit

examples.en: a lucrative business/contract/market
examples.zh: 利润丰厚的生意／合同／市场

examples.en: Had the plan worked it would have proved highly lucrative.
examples.zh: 如果这个计划成功的话，将会带来丰厚的利润。

intro.en: These words all describe somebody/​something that is making or is likely to make money.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指赚钱的、赢利的、有利可图的。

items.def: making a lot of money, especially by being popular:
items.zh: 指赚钱的、成功的

examples.en: The play was very successful on Broadway.
examples.zh: 那部剧在百老汇大获成功。

items.def: making a profit:
items.zh: 指有利润的、赢利的

examples.en: a highly profitable business
examples.zh: 一家赢利很高的企业

items.def: [only before noun] making or intended to make a profit:
items.zh: 指赢利的、以获利为目的的

examples.en: The movie was not a commercial success (= made no profit).
examples.zh: 这部电影票房收入不佳。

items.def: (of business or work) producing or paying a large amount of money; making a large profit:
items.zh: 指生意或工作赚大钱的、获利多的

examples.en: They do a lot of business in lucrative overseas markets.
examples.zh: 他们在利润丰厚的海外市场上生意很多。

items.def: (often used in negative sentences) (of a process, business or activity) producing enough profit to continue:
items.zh: （常用于否定句中）指（工序、业务或活动）有利可图的、可赚钱的、合算的

examples.en: Small local shops stop being economic when a supermarket opens up nearby.
examples.zh: 附近有超市开业的话，当地的小商店就没有利润可赚了。

senses.def: in a way that produces a large amount of money
senses.zh: 有利可图的：以产生大量金钱的方式

senses.def: money, especially when it has been obtained in a way that is not honest or moral

examples.en: the lure of filthy lucre
examples.zh: 不义之财的诱惑

senses.def: a first name for girls, sometimes short for Lucinda
senses.zh: 露西（女子名，有时是Lucinda的简称）

senses.def: a person who is opposed to new technology or working methods
senses.zh: 反对新技术（或新工作方法）的人

senses.def: tending to play and have fun, make jokes, etc., especially when there is no particular reason for doing this
unreasonable; that you cannot take seriously

examples.en: a ludicrous suggestion
examples.zh: 荒谬的建议

examples.en: It was ludicrous to think that the plan could succeed.
examples.zh: 认为此计划会取得成功是荒唐的。

examples.en: He is paid a ludicrous amount of money.
examples.zh: 他的报酬高得荒唐。

senses.def: in a way that is unreasonable and impossible to take seriously
senses.zh: 荒唐的：以一种不合理，不可能荒谬地，认真地取而代之的方式

examples.en: ludicrously expensive
examples.zh: 贵得离谱

senses.def: the fact of being unreasonable and impossible to take seriously
senses.zh: 荒唐可笑：不合理且不可能严肃地认为荒谬

senses.def: a simple game played with dice
senses.zh: 卢多（一种用骰子和筹码在棋盘上玩的游戏，类似于美国的巴棋戏）

senses.def: (1919-2009) a Scottish television presenter
senses.zh: （1919-2009年）苏格兰电视节目主持人和作家。在1960年代，他介绍了许多新闻和时事节目，包括Panorama和This Week。他因调查被认为错误地入狱的人的案件而闻名，还因为他对安乐死的支持（使人们有权在希望死于重病的情况下死亡）。1994年，他被任命为骑士。

senses.def: (1886-1969) a US architect, born in Germany, who was known for his glass and steel skyscrapers
senses.zh: 路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗（Ludwig Mies van der Rohe）：（ 1886-1969年）美国建筑师，出生于德国，以玻璃和钢结构的摩天大楼（非常高的建筑物）而闻名。他帮助发展了现代建筑，被认为是20世纪的主要建筑师之一。他使用简单的设计，并说“少即是多”。他设计的美国建筑包括芝加哥的湖岸大道公寓（1948-51），以及菲利普·约翰逊（Philip Johnson），纽约的西格拉姆大厦（1954-58）。他还设计了家具。

senses.def: (1889-1951) an Austrian philosopher
senses.zh: 路德维希·维特根斯坦（1889-1951）是奥地利哲学家。第一次世界大战之前，他曾在Bertrand Russell领导下在英国学习。战争结束后，他移居英国，并于1938年成为英国公民。他从事语言和哲学理论的研究。在他的《逻辑哲学哲学》（Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus，1922年）中，他提出了一种理论，即语言根据既定的惯例（即普遍同意）表示事物的图片。后来，他认为这是错误的，并根据使用理论（即单词在语言中的使用方式）更为重要的理论进行研究。

senses.def: to carry or drag something heavy with a lot of effort
senses.zh: 吃力地搬运；用力拖；使劲拉

examples.en: I had to lug my bags up to the fourth floor.
examples.zh: 我只得费劲地把我的几个包拖上五楼。

examples.en: Leave your books here—you don’t want to lug those around with you all day.
examples.zh: 把你的书放在这里——你不想整天带着它们到处走。

senses.def: a part of something that sticks out, used as a handle or support
an ear
a small piece of metal with a hole through it that screws

examples.en: A slightly loose lug nut will grow looser as a wheel experiences greater pressures during turns.
examples.zh: 当车轮在转动过程中承受更大的压力时，稍微松动的凸耳螺母会变得更松。

senses.def: a type of sledge
senses.zh: 无舵雪橇，单雪橇（比赛用的单人或双人仰卧雪橇）

senses.def: the event or sport of racing down a track of ice on a luge
senses.zh: 无舵雪橇运动；单雪橇运动

senses.def: a type of small gun that was made in Germany
bags, cases, etc. that contain somebody's clothes and things when they are travelling

examples.en: There's room for one more piece of luggage.
examples.zh: 还有地方再放一件行李。

examples.en: You stay there with the luggage while I find a cab.
examples.zh: 你看着行李，我去找出租车。

senses.def: empty bags, cases, etc. for putting your clothes and things in when you are travelling

examples.en: a new set of luggage
examples.zh: 新旅行箱系列

examples.en: I need to buy some new luggage for my vacation next month.
examples.zh: 我需要为我下个月的度假旅行买个新的行李箱。

examples.en: The couple had matching luggage.
examples.zh: 这对夫妇有配套的行李。

senses.def: a shelf for bags above the seats in a train, bus, etc.
senses.zh: （火车、公共汽车等座位上方的）行李架

senses.def: a metal frame fixed to the roof of a car and used for carrying bags, cases and other large objects
a coach on a train for carrying passengers’ bags, cases, etc.

examples.zh: “你们出口到哪里？”“主要是法国。”

examples.zh: 澳大利亚国立大学保持了澳大利亚顶尖大学的位置。

examples.zh: 这两个国家一直保持着密切关系。

examples.en: Unemployment was the chief cause of poverty.
examples.zh: 失业是贫穷的主要原因。

items.def: [only before noun] (rather formal) most important; to be considered first:
items.zh: 指主要的、首要的

examples.en: My prime concern is to protect my property.
examples.zh: 我最关心的是保护自己的财产。

senses.def: a senior servant who manages a large house
an officer of very high rank in the army or the US air force

examples.en: Major General William Hunt
examples.zh: 陆军少将威廉·亨特

senses.def: to study something as your main subject at a university or college

examples.en: She majored in history at Stanford.
examples.zh: 她在斯坦福主修历史。

senses.def: a league of professional sports teams, especially in baseball, that play at the highest level
senses.zh: （尤指棒球）第一流的职业队伍联盟；大联盟

examples.en: By the time his dream of playing in the Major Leagues came true, he was over 40.
examples.zh: 当他在美国职业棒球大联盟打球的梦想实现时，他已经40多岁了。

senses.def: connected with teams that play in the major leagues, especially in baseball
senses.zh: （尤指棒球）职业球队联盟的，大联盟的

examples.en: a major-league team
examples.zh: 大联盟球队

senses.def: very important and having a lot of influence
senses.zh: 非常重要的；颇有影响力的

examples.en: a major-league business
examples.zh: 举足轻重的企业

senses.def: the highest level of professional baseball in the US. Major League Baseball
senses.zh: 美国职棒大联盟：美国职业棒球最高水平。美国职业棒球大联盟也是经营两个棒球联盟，国家联盟和美国联盟的组织。世界大赛™

senses.def: the highest level football (soccer) league in the US, which started in 1996 and is run by the United States Soccer Federation. The league is divided into Eastern and Western regions, with some Canadian teams playing in each. Soccer is less popular in the US than other sports, but became more popular after the national team reached the quarter-final
senses.zh: 职业足球大联盟（美国最高级别的足球联赛，始于 1996 年，由美国足联管理，分东西两区）

senses.def: to pay particular attention to one subject, issue, etc.
a girl in special brightly coloured clothes who walks in front of a marching band
senses.zh: （行进乐队中身着艳丽服装、舞动抛接指挥棒的）女领队

senses.def: the largest part of a group of people or things

examples.en: The majority of people interviewed prefer TV to radio.
examples.zh: 大多数接受采访的人都喜欢看电视多于听收音机。

examples.en: The majority was/were in favour of banning new coal mines.
examples.zh: 大多数人赞成禁止新煤矿。

examples.en: This treatment is not available in the vast majority of hospitals.
examples.zh: 绝大部分医院都不提供这种治疗。

examples.en: The overwhelming majority of participants were men.
examples.zh: 绝大多数参与者是男性。

examples.en: to represent/form/constitute/comprise the majority of somebody/something
examples.zh: 代表／形成／构成／组成某人／某事物的多数

examples.en: In the nursing profession, women are in the majority.
examples.zh: 女性在护理行业中占大多数。

examples.en: The drug provided significant pain relief in a majority of cases.
examples.zh: 在大多数情况下，该药物可以显着缓解疼痛。

examples.en: a majority decision (= one that is decided by what most people want)
examples.zh: 根据大多数人的意见作出的决定

examples.en: We make decisions by majority vote.
examples.zh: 我们以多数票作决定。

examples.en: the majority opinion/view
examples.zh: 多数人的意见／观点

senses.def: the number of votes by which one political party wins an election; the number of votes by which one side in a discussion, etc. wins

examples.en: She was elected by a majority of 749.
examples.zh: 她以 749 票的多数票当选。

examples.en: The resolution was carried by a huge majority.
examples.zh: 这项决议以绝大多数票赞成而获得通过。

examples.en: They had a large majority over their nearest rivals.
examples.zh: 他们所得的票数远远超出紧随其后的对手。

examples.en: They have a clear majority (= large majority) in Parliament.
examples.zh: 他们在议会中占绝对多数。

examples.en: to win/get/gain/secure a majority
examples.zh: 赢得／获得多数

senses.def: the difference between the number of votes given to the candidate who wins the election and the total number of votes of all the other candidates
senses.zh: 超出其余各方票数总和的票数

examples.en: Without this shift, Kerry would have had a popular majority of a million votes.
examples.zh: 如果没有这种改变，克里会比其他候选人得票数多出 100 万张。

senses.def: the age at which you are legally considered to be an adult

examples.en: The age of majority in Britain was reduced from 21 to 18 in 1970.
examples.zh: 1970年，英国的法定成年年龄从21岁降至18岁。

senses.def: the leader of the political party that has the majority in either the House of Representatives or the Senate in the US
senses.zh: （美国众议院或参议院的）多数派政党领袖

examples.en: a former US Senate majority leader
examples.zh: 前美国参议院多数派领袖

senses.def: a system in which power is held by the group that has the largest number of members

examples.en: Black majority rule in South Africa took many years to achieve.
examples.zh: 南非黑人占多数的统治花了很多年才实现。

senses.def: a decision made by a jury
senses.zh: 多数裁决（陪审团根据多数票作出）

senses.def: a member of the political party in Congress with the most representatives, who influences other party members to vote a particular way
senses.zh: 多数党党鞭（多数党中负责督导党员投票的组织秘书）

examples.en: The Republican majority whip in the Senate was quick to respond.
examples.zh: 参议院共和党多数党鞭迅速做出回应。

senses.def: very; extremely

examples.en: majorly disappointed
examples.zh: 无比失望

senses.def: a Hindu festival celebrated in various regions of India, marking the beginning of the harvest
a language system created for people who have difficulty communicating, especially people with learning disabilities
senses.zh: 为沟通有困难的人，特别是有学习障碍的人创建的语言系统，结合了语音、手势和图片

examples.en: I learned Makaton to help my son.
examples.zh: 我学习Makaton是为了帮助我的儿子。

examples.en: More than a million children and adults in the UK use Makaton signs and symbols.
examples.zh: 英国有超过一百万儿童和成人使用 Makaton 标志和符号。

senses.def: to create or prepare something by combining materials or putting parts together

examples.en: to make a table/dress/cake
examples.zh: 做桌子／连衣裙／蛋糕

examples.en: to make bread/cement/paper
examples.zh: 制作面包；生产水泥／纸张

examples.en: She makes her own clothes.
examples.zh: 她自己做衣服。

examples.en: How do you make that dish with the peppers and olives in it?
examples.zh: 那道有胡椒和橄榄的菜你是怎么做的？

examples.en: made in France (= on a label)
examples.zh: 法国制造

examples.en: What's your shirt made of?
examples.zh: 你的衬衣是用什么做的？

examples.en: Traditional Japanese houses were made of wood.
examples.zh: 传统的日本房屋是用木头建造的。

examples.en: What's your shirt made out of?
examples.zh: 你的衬衣是什么材质的？

examples.en: Wine is made from grapes.
examples.zh: 葡萄酒是用葡萄做的。

examples.en: The grapes are made into wine.
examples.zh: 这些葡萄用来做酒。

examples.en: She made coffee for us all.
examples.zh: 她给我们大家冲了咖啡。

examples.en: She made us all coffee.
examples.zh: 她给我们大家冲了咖啡。

senses.def: to write, create or prepare something

examples.en: These regulations were made to protect children.
examples.zh: 这些规章制度是为了保护儿童而制定的。

examples.en: My lawyer has been urging me to make a will.
examples.zh: 我的律师一直在催促我立遗嘱。

examples.en: She has made (= directed or acted in) several movies.
examples.zh: 她已经出了好几部电影。

examples.en: It is possible to make a hypothesis on the basis of this graph.
examples.zh: 以这张图表为基础作出假设是可能的。

examples.en: The Environment Secretary is to make a statement on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 环境大臣将于周二发表声明。

senses.def: to cause something to appear as a result of breaking, tearing, hitting or removing material

examples.en: The stone made a dent in the roof of the car.
examples.zh: 石头把车顶砸了个坑。

examples.en: The holes in the cloth were made by moths.
examples.zh: 布上的窟窿是虫子蛀的。

senses.group: cause to appear/happen/become/do 使出现／发生／成为／做

senses.def: to cause something to exist, happen or be done

examples.en: to make a noise/mess/fuss
examples.zh: 产生噪声；弄得一团糟；小题大做

examples.en: She tried to make a good impression on the interviewer.
examples.zh: 她努力给主持面试者留个好印象。

examples.en: I keep making the same mistakes.
examples.zh: 我总是犯同样的错误。

senses.group: cause to appear/happen/become/do 使出现／发生／成为／做

senses.def: to cause somebody/something to feel, show or have a particular quality; to cause somebody/something to be or become something

examples.en: The news made him very happy.
examples.zh: 这则消息使他非常高兴。

examples.en: She made her objections clear.
examples.zh: 她明确表示反对。

examples.en: Technology continues to make our lives easier.
examples.zh: 科技继续让我们的生活变得更加轻松。

examples.en: He made it clear that he objected.
examples.zh: 他明确表示反对。

examples.en: The full story was never made public.
examples.zh: 事情的完整情况从未公开。

examples.en: Can you make yourself understood in Russian?
examples.zh: 你能用俄语表达你的意思吗？

examples.en: She couldn't make herself heard above the noise of the traffic.
examples.zh: 车辆噪声很大，她无法让人听到她的声音。

examples.en: The terrorists made it known that tourists would be targeted.
examples.zh: 恐怖分子宣称游客将成为他们袭击的目标。

examples.en: Unrealistic deadlines may make targets difficult or impossible to achieve.
examples.zh: 不切实际的最后期限可能会使目标难以或不可能实现。

examples.en: Technology has made it possible to move many jobs away from high-cost locations.
examples.zh: 技术使许多工作岗位从高成本地区转移成为可能。

senses.group: cause to appear/happen/become/do 使出现／发生／成为／做

senses.def: to cause somebody/something to do something

examples.en: She always makes me laugh.
examples.zh: 她总是让我发笑。

examples.en: This dress makes me look fat.
examples.zh: 这衣服我穿着显胖。

examples.en: What makes you say that (= why do you think so)?
examples.zh: 你为什么这么说？

examples.en: Nothing will make me change my mind.
examples.zh: 什么也改变不了我的主意。

examples.en: We were made to feel extremely welcome.
examples.zh: 我们感到非常受欢迎。

senses.group: cause to appear/happen/become/do 使出现／发生／成为／做

senses.def: to cause somebody/something to be or become a particular kind of thing or person

examples.en: This isn't very important—I don't want to make an issue of it.
examples.zh: 这不太重要，我不想把它当回事儿。

examples.en: Don't make a habit of it.
examples.zh: 别养成习惯。

examples.en: You've made a terrible mess of this job.
examples.zh: 你把这活儿搞得一团糟。

examples.en: It's important to try and make something of (= achieve something in) your life.
examples.zh: 一生中努力有所成就是很重要的。

examples.en: We'll make a tennis player of you yet.
examples.zh: 早晚有一天，我们会让你成为一名网球选手的。

examples.en: I made painting the house my project for the summer.
examples.zh: 把房子粉刷了一遍，这就是我的夏季工程。

examples.en: She made it her business to find out who was responsible.
examples.zh: 她一定要查清楚到底是谁干的。

examples.en: These improvements will make the city a better place to live.
examples.zh: 这些改善将使这座城市成为一个更美好的居住地。

examples.en: He's made his firm a success.
examples.zh: 他使他的公司取得了成功。

senses.group: cause to appear/happen/become/do 使出现／发生／成为／做

senses.def: to arrange a bed so that it is neat and ready for use
to decide, guess, etc. something

examples.en: Come on! It's time we made a start.
examples.zh: 快点！我们该开始了。

examples.en: The plane was forced to make an emergency landing because of bad weather.
examples.zh: 飞机因恶劣天气被迫紧急着陆。

senses.group: a decision/guess/comment, etc. 决定、猜测、评论等

senses.def: to force somebody to do something

examples.en: They made me repeat the whole story.
examples.zh: 他们非让我把整个事件再说一遍。

examples.en: She must be made to comply with the rules.
examples.zh: 必须让她遵守规则。

examples.en: He never cleans his room and his mother never tries to make him.
examples.zh: 他从不收拾自己的房间，而他妈也从不要求他收拾。

senses.def: to represent somebody/something as being or doing something

examples.en: You've made my nose too big (= for example in a drawing).
examples.zh: 你把我的鼻子画得太大了。

examples.en: He makes King Lear a truly tragic figure.
examples.zh: 他把李尔王刻画成一个真正的悲剧人物。

senses.def: to elect or choose somebody as something

examples.en: She made him her assistant.
examples.zh: 她挑选他做她的助手。

senses.def: to become or develop into something; to be suitable for something

examples.en: She would have made an excellent teacher.
examples.zh: 她本可以成为一位出色的教师。

examples.en: This room would make a nice office.
examples.zh: 这间屋子做办公室挺不错。

senses.def: to add up to or equal something

examples.en: 5 and 7 make 12.
A hundred cents make one euro.
examples.zh: 一百分等于一欧元。

senses.def: to be a total of something

examples.en: That makes the third time he's failed his driving test!
examples.zh: 他这已经是第三次驾驶考试不及格了！

senses.def: to earn or gain money

examples.en: She makes $100 000 a year.
examples.zh: 她一年赚 10 万美元。

examples.en: to make a profit/loss
examples.zh: 获利；赔钱

examples.en: We need to think of ways to make money.
examples.zh: 我们需要想办法挣钱。

examples.en: He made a fortune on the stock market.
examples.zh: 他在股票市场发了大财。

examples.en: She makes a living as a stand-up comic.
examples.zh: 她以单口喜剧演员为生。

senses.def: to think or calculate something to be something

examples.en: What time do you make it?
examples.zh: 你估计现在几点了？

examples.en: I make that exactly $50.
examples.zh: 我算出正好是 50 美元。

senses.def: to manage to reach or go to a place or position

examples.en: Do you think we'll make Dover by 12?
examples.zh: 你觉得我们 12 点前能到多佛吗？

examples.en: I'm sorry I couldn't make your party last night.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，昨晚没能参加你们的聚会。

examples.en: He'll never make (= get a place in) the team.
examples.zh: 他绝不可能成为该队的队员。

examples.en: The story made (= appeared on) the front pages of the national newspapers.
examples.zh: 这件事登在了全国性报纸的头版。

examples.en: We just managed to make the deadline (= to finish something in time).
examples.zh: 我们总算勉强按期完成。

senses.def: to cause something to be a success

examples.en: Good company can make a meal.
examples.zh: 好的公司可以做一顿饭。

examples.en: The news really made my day.
examples.zh: 这消息确实使我一天都很愉快。

senses.def: to make a movement that makes it seem as if you are just going to do something

examples.en: He made as if to speak.
examples.zh: 他似乎要说点什么。

senses.def: to manage with something that is not really good enough

examples.en: We were in a hurry so we had to make do with a quick snack.
examples.zh: 我们很匆忙，只好将就着来了点小吃。

senses.def: to become rich and successful
to pay for, replace or repair something that has been lost or damaged

examples.en: She promised to make good the damage.
examples.zh: 她答应赔偿损失。

senses.def: to do something that you have promised, threatened, etc. to do
senses.zh: 履行，执行（曾承诺、威胁等的事）

senses.def: to be successful in your career

examples.en: He never really made it as an actor.
examples.zh: 他从来就不是一个成功的演员。

senses.def: to succeed in reaching a place in time, especially when this is difficult
senses.zh: （尤指在困难情况下）准时到达

examples.en: The flight leaves in twenty minutes—we'll never make it.
examples.zh: 再过二十分钟飞机就起飞了，咱们无论如何也赶不上了。

senses.def: to be able to be present at a place

examples.en: I'm sorry I won't be able to make it (= for example, to a party) on Saturday.
examples.zh: 很抱歉，星期六我出席不了。

senses.def: to survive after a serious illness or accident; to deal successfully with a difficult experience

examples.en: The doctors think he's going to make it.
examples.zh: 医生认为他能挺过去。

examples.en: I don't know how I made it through the week.
examples.zh: 我不知道自己是怎么熬过那个星期的。

senses.def: to have sex with somebody
to pretend to be, know or have something in order to impress people
senses.zh: （为给别人留下印象）假装，装出…样子

examples.en: He makes like he's the greatest actor of all time.
examples.zh: 他装模作样，仿佛自己是有史以来最棒的演员。

senses.def: to gain as much advantage, pleasure, etc. as you can from somebody/something

examples.en: It's my first trip abroad so I'm going to make the most of it.
examples.zh: 这是我第一次出国，我要充分利用这个机会。

examples.en: She doesn't know how to make the most of herself (= make herself appear in the best possible way).
examples.zh: 她不知道如何充分表现自己。

senses.def: to treat something/somebody as very important

examples.en: He always makes much of his humble origins.
examples.zh: 他总是非常在意他卑微的出身。

senses.def: to be the thing that makes somebody/something either a success or a failure

examples.en: This movie will make or break him as a director.
examples.zh: 这部电影将要决定他当导演是行还是不行。

examples.en: It's make-or-break time for the company.
examples.zh: 这是公司盛衰的关键时刻。

senses.def: to be successful in your life

examples.en: I wanted to study hard and really make something of myself.
examples.zh: 我想努力使自己学有所成。

senses.def: the name or type of a machine, piece of equipment, etc. that is made by a particular company

examples.en: What make of car does he drive?
examples.zh: 他开的是什么品牌的车？

examples.en: a Swiss make of watch
examples.zh: 一块瑞士表

examples.en: There are so many different makes to choose from.
examples.zh: 有很多不同的型号可供选择。

examples.en: We need to know the make, model and year of your car.
examples.zh: 我们需要知道你的汽车的品牌、型号和出厂年份。

senses.def: trying to get money or an advantage for yourself

note.en: Most idioms containing make are at the entries for the nouns and adjectives in the idioms, for example make merry is at merry.
note.zh: 大多数含 make 的习语，都可在该等习语中的名词及形容词相关词条找到，如 make merry 在词条 merry 下。

examples.zh: 他似乎要说点什么。

examples.zh: 他画了一栋漂亮的房子。

examples.zh: 科学家对宇宙是怎样形成的有分歧。

intro.en: These words all mean to make somebody believe something that is not true, especially in order to get what you want.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含使人误信之义，尤指有目的地这样做。

items.def: to make somebody believe something that is not true, especially in order to laugh at them or to get what you want:
items.zh: 指蒙骗、愚弄

examples.en: Just don’t be fooled into investing any money with them.
examples.zh: 别上当受骗，同他们一起搞什么投资。

items.def: to make somebody believe something that is not true, especially somebody who trusts you, in order to get what you want:
items.zh: 尤指利用别人的信任欺骗、蒙骗、诓骗

examples.en: She deceived him into handing over all his savings.
examples.zh: 她把他所有的积蓄都骗走了。

items.def: to hurt somebody who trusts you, especially by lying to or about them or telling their secrets to other people:
items.zh: 指辜负别人的信任、出卖

examples.en: She felt betrayed when she found out the truth about him.
examples.zh: 她发现他的真实情况时，感到受了欺骗。

items.def: [often passive] to make somebody believe something that is not true, usually in order to get what you want:

examples.zh: 我被她的花言巧语蒙骗了。

examples.en: No parking is allowed, but an exception is made for disabled drivers.

examples.en: We are making a special exception for Emma because of her condition.
examples.zh: 因为艾玛的情况特殊，我们把她作为例外。
