examples.en: We now know that solid objects are largely made up of empty space.
examples.zh: 我们现在知道固体大部分是由真空组成的。

examples.en: art objects from the ancient world
examples.zh: 来自古代世界的艺术品

senses.def: a person or thing that somebody desires
senses.zh: （极欲得到、研究、注意等的）对象

examples.en: He felt he was nothing more to her than an object of desire.
examples.zh: 他觉得对她来说自己不过是个性欲对象而已。

examples.en: Her objects of study are all paintings.
examples.zh: 她的研究对象都是绘画。

examples.en: an object of affection/ridicule/worship
examples.zh: 喜爱/嘲笑/崇拜的对象

senses.def: an aim or a purpose

examples.en: Her sole object in life is to become a travel writer.
examples.zh: 她人生的唯一目标就是当游记作家。

examples.en: The object is to educate people about road safety.
examples.zh: 目的是教育人们注意交通安全。

examples.en: The object of the game is to score points by combining cards.
examples.zh: 游戏的目的是通过组合纸牌来得分。

examples.en: If you're late, you'll defeat the whole object of the exercise.
examples.zh: 如果你迟到了，便不能达到整个活动的目的。

examples.en: He put together an army with the object of taking back the lost territory.
examples.zh: 他组建了一支军队，目的是夺回失去的领土。

senses.def: a noun, noun phrase or pronoun that refers to a person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb (called the direct object
senses.zh: 宾语（包括直接宾语、间接宾语）

senses.def: money is not something that needs to be considered, because there is plenty of it available

examples.en: She travels around the world as if money is no object.
examples.zh: 她周游世界，好像钱不是问题。

senses.def: to say that you disagree with or oppose something

examples.en: If nobody objects, we'll postpone the meeting till next week.
examples.zh: 如果没有人反对，我们就把会议推迟到下周。

examples.en: Members of the council strongly objected to plans to sell off the land.
examples.zh: 地方议会的议员强烈反对出售这块土地的计划。

examples.en: Many local people object to the building of the new airport.
examples.zh: 许多当地的居民反对兴建新机场。

examples.en: I really object to being charged for parking.
examples.zh: 我非常反对收停车费。

examples.en: Who could object to people having fun?
examples.zh: 谁会反对人们开心玩乐呢？

senses.def: to give something as a reason for opposing something
senses.zh: 提出…作为反对的理由；抗辩说

examples.en: He objected that the police had arrested him without sufficient evidence.
examples.zh: 他抗辩说警察没有充分的证据就逮捕了他。

examples.en: ‘But that's not fair!’ she objected.
examples.zh: “但这不公平！”她反对道。

senses.def: money is not something that needs to be considered, because there is plenty of it available

examples.en: She travels around the world as if money is no object.
examples.zh: 她周游世界，好像钱不是问题。

intro.en: These are all words for something that you are trying to achieve.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指目标、目的。

items.def: a result that you try to achieve:
items.zh: 指试图达到的目标、指标

examples.en: Set yourself targets that you can reasonably hope to achieve.
examples.zh: 给自己制订有望达到的指标。

items.def: (rather formal) something that you are trying to achieve:
items.zh: 指正努力达到的目标、目的

examples.en: What is the main objective of this project?
examples.zh: 这个项目的主要目标是什么？

items.def: something that you hope to achieve:
items.zh: 指希望达到的目标、目的

examples.en: He continued to pursue his goal of becoming an actor.
examples.zh: 他继续追求他成为演员的目标。

items.def: the purpose of something; something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指目的、目标、宗旨

examples.en: The object is to educate people about road safety.
examples.zh: 目的是教育人们注意交通安全。

items.def: something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指计划达到的目的、目标

examples.en: He joined the society for political ends.
examples.zh: 他为了政治目的加入了这个协会。

intro.en: These words all mean to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/​something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含对人或事物感到恼怒、不高兴或不满之义。

items.def: to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指抱怨、埋怨、投诉、发牢骚

examples.en: I’m going to complain to the manager about this.
examples.zh: 我要就这件事向经理投诉。

items.def: to say or do something to show that you disagree with something or think it is bad, especially publicly; to give something as a reason for protesting:
items.zh: 指公开反对、抗议或申辩

examples.en: Students took to the streets to protest against the decision.
examples.zh: 学生走上街头抗议这项决定。

items.def: to say that you disagree with something or think it is bad; to give something as a reason for objecting:
items.zh: 指不同意、不赞成、反对或抗辩

examples.en: If nobody objects, we’ll postpone the meeting till next week.
examples.zh: 如果没有人反对，我们就把会议推迟到下周。

items.def: (rather informal, disapproving) to complain about somebody/​something, especially something that is not really very serious:
items.zh: 尤指为不太严重的事情发牢骚、咕哝、嘟囔

examples.en: They kept grumbling that they were cold.
examples.zh: 他们不停地嘟囔着说冷。

items.def: (British English英式英语, rather informal, disapproving) to complain about somebody/​something in an annoying way:
items.zh: 指抱怨、埋怨

examples.en: What are you moaning about now?
examples.zh: 你在抱怨什么呢？

items.def: (rather informal, disapproving) to complain in an annoying, crying voice:
items.zh: 指哭哭啼啼或哭嚷着诉说

examples.en: Stop whining!
examples.zh: 别哭哭啼啼的！

senses.def: the language into which a program is translated using a compiler
senses.zh: （编译或汇编程序的）目标码，目标代码

senses.def: a language into which a text is being translated
senses.zh: （翻译的）目标语言，译文语言，译入语

senses.def: the language into which a program is translated using a compiler
senses.zh: （编译或汇编程序的）目标码，目标代码

senses.def: a practical example of what you should or should not do in a particular situation

examples.en: Her calm handling of the emergency was an object lesson to us all.
examples.zh: 她对紧急情况的冷静处理给我们所有人上了一个生动的教训。

senses.def: a way of programming computers so that information and instructions are stored together in units called objects
senses.zh: （编程方式）面向对象的，对象式的，物件导向的

examples.en: object-oriented languages/programming
examples.zh: 面向对象语言╱程序设计

examples.en: Java is object-oriented and well structured.
examples.zh: Java 语言是面向对象的，结构良好。

senses.def: a program into which another program is translated by a compiler
senses.zh: 目标程序；目标程式；目的程式

senses.def: the act of treating people as if they are objects, without rights or feelings of their own
senses.zh: 人格物化（把人当成没有权利或感情的物体）

senses.def: to treat somebody/something as an object, without rights or feelings of their own

examples.en: magazines that objectify women
examples.zh: 将女性人格物化的杂志

senses.def: a reason why you do not like or are opposed to something; a statement about this

examples.en: I'd like to come too, if you have no objection.
examples.zh: 如果你不反对，我也想来。

examples.en: They raised no objections at the time.
examples.zh: 他们当时没有提出异议。

examples.en: He did not know how to voice his objections.
examples.zh: 他不知道如何表达自己的反对意见。

examples.en: The main objection to the plan was that it would cost too much.
examples.zh: 反对这个计划的主要理由是费用过高。

examples.en: There was widespread objection to the proposals.
examples.zh: 这些提案遭到广泛反对。

examples.en: I have no objection to him coming to stay.
examples.zh: 我不反对他来小住。

examples.en: I have no objection to staying here.
examples.zh: 我不反对留在这里。

examples.en: The proposal will go ahead despite strong objections from the public.
examples.zh: 尽管公众强烈反对，这项提案仍将付诸实施。

examples.en: He dismissed the objection that the plan was too expensive.
examples.zh: 他没有理会认为该计划费用过高的反对意见。

senses.def: unpleasant or offensive
senses.zh: 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的

examples.en: objectionable people/odours
examples.zh: 讨厌的人／气味

examples.en: Why are you being so objectionable today?
examples.zh: 你今天怎么这么别扭？

examples.en: I myself didn’t find his behaviour objectionable.
examples.zh: 我本人并不觉得他的行为令人反感。

senses.def: something that you are trying to achieve

examples.en: the primary/principal/key objective
examples.zh: 首要／主要／关键目标

examples.en: The main objective of this meeting is to give more information on our plans.
examples.zh: 这次会议的主要目的是进一步介绍我们的规划。

examples.en: How does the project fit with our strategic objectives?
examples.zh: 该项目如何符合我们的战略目标？

examples.en: the government's policy objectives
examples.zh: 政府的政策目标

examples.en: to achieve/meet/accomplish your objectives
examples.zh: 实现／达到／完成目标

examples.en: to set/state/define your objectives
examples.zh: 设定/陈述/定义您的目标

examples.en: You must set realistic aims and objectives for yourself.
examples.zh: 你必须给自己订立切实可行的目标。

examples.en: What are the organization's goals and objectives?
examples.zh: 组织的目的和目标是什么？

senses.def: the lens
not influenced by personal feelings or opinions; considering only facts
senses.zh: 客观的；就事论事的；不带个人感情的

examples.en: an objective assessment of the situation
examples.zh: 对形势的客观评估

examples.en: objective truth/facts/reality
examples.zh: 客观真理／事实／现实

examples.en: objective criteria/measures/measurements
examples.zh: 客观标准／措施／测量值

examples.en: He doesn't even pretend to be impartial and objective.
examples.zh: 他甚至连个公正客观的样子都不装一下。

examples.en: It's hard to remain completely objective.
examples.zh: 很难保持完全客观。

senses.def: existing outside the mind; based on facts that can be proved
senses.zh: 客观存在的；基于事实的

examples.en: objective reality
examples.zh: 客观现实

senses.def: the objective

intro.en: These are all words for something that you are trying to achieve.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指目标、目的。

items.def: a result that you try to achieve:
items.zh: 指试图达到的目标、指标

examples.en: Set yourself targets that you can reasonably hope to achieve.
examples.zh: 给自己制订有望达到的指标。

items.def: (rather formal) something that you are trying to achieve:
items.zh: 指正努力达到的目标、目的

examples.en: What is the main objective of this project?
examples.zh: 这个项目的主要目标是什么？

items.def: something that you hope to achieve:
items.zh: 指希望达到的目标、目的

examples.en: He continued to pursue his goal of becoming an actor.
examples.zh: 他继续追求他成为演员的目标。

items.def: the purpose of something; something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指目的、目标、宗旨

examples.en: The object is to educate people about road safety.
examples.zh: 目的就是教育大众注意交通安全。

items.def: something that you plan to achieve:
items.zh: 指计划达到的目的、目标

examples.en: He joined the society for political ends.
examples.zh: 他为了政治目的加入了这个协会。

senses.def: considering only facts and without being influenced by personal feelings or opinions
senses.zh: 客观地；不带个人感情地

examples.en: Looked at objectively, the situation is not too bad.
examples.zh: 客观地看，局面并不算太糟。

examples.en: I was too upset to see things objectively.
examples.zh: 我太沮丧了，无法客观地看待事情。

senses.def: in a way that is based only on facts that can be proved

examples.en: Can these effects be objectively measured?
examples.zh: 这些作用能不能客观地衡量？

senses.def: the fact of not being influenced by personal feelings or opinions but considering only facts
senses.zh: 客观的；就事论事的；不带个人感情的

examples.en: There was a lack of objectivity in the way the candidates were judged.
examples.zh: 评价候选人的方法不够客观。

senses.def: the fact of something being based only on facts that can be proved
senses.zh: 客观存在的；基于事实的

examples.en: a high standard of scientific objectivity
examples.zh: 高标准的科学客观性

senses.def: a person who objects to something

examples.en: There were no objectors to the plan.
examples.zh: 没有人反对这个计划。

senses.def: a small artistic object, used for decoration
senses.zh: （装饰性的）小艺术品，小工艺品

senses.def: having a moral or legal duty to do something
senses.zh: （道义或法律上）有义务的，有责任的，必须的

examples.en: He felt obligated to help.
examples.zh: 他觉得有义务帮忙。

senses.def: the state of being forced to do something because it is your duty, or because of a law, etc.

examples.en: You are under no obligation to buy anything.
examples.zh: 你不必非买什么东西不可。

examples.en: She did not feel under any obligation to tell him the truth.
examples.zh: 她觉得没有义务告诉他实情。

examples.en: I don't want people coming to see me out of a sense of obligation.
examples.zh: 我不想让别人迫于无奈来看我。

examples.en: We will send you an estimate for the work without obligation (= you do not have to accept it).
examples.zh: 我们将寄上工程估算，仅供参考。

senses.def: something which you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.
senses.zh: （已承诺的或法律等规定的）义务，责任

examples.en: legal/professional/financial obligations
examples.zh: 法律／职业／财政义务

examples.en: They reminded him of his contractual obligations.
examples.zh: 他们提醒他注意合同规定的义务。

examples.en: The country has promised to comply with its international obligations.
examples.zh: 该国承诺遵守其国际义务。

examples.en: We have a moral obligation to protect the environment.
examples.zh: 我们有道义责任保护环境。

examples.en: I have an obligation under law to protect their confidentiality.
examples.zh: 根据法律规定，我有义务保护他们的机密。

examples.en: I felt that there was a moral obligation on me to tell the story.
examples.zh: 我觉得我有道德义务把这个事情讲出来。

examples.en: We want to fulfil our obligation to farmers and see they get a fair price.
examples.zh: 我们希望履行对农民的义务，并确保他们得到公平的价格。

examples.en: The company did not have enough money to meet its obligations.
examples.zh: 该公司没有足够的资金来履行其义务。

examples.en: We have an obligation to our consumers.
examples.zh: 我们有义务对消费者负责。

senses.def: an important part for an instrument in a piece of music which cannot be left out
that you must do because of the law, rules, etc.
senses.zh: （按法律、规定等）必须的，强制的

examples.en: The college authorities have now made these classes obligatory.
examples.zh: 学院管理部门现已将这些课程列为必修课。

examples.en: These classes are obligatory for all first-year students.
examples.zh: 这些课程是所有一年级学生的必修课。

examples.en: It is obligatory to report all cases of the disease to the authorities.
examples.zh: 有义务向当局报告所有疾病病例。

examples.en: It is obligatory for all employees to wear protective clothing.
examples.zh: 所有员工必须穿防护服装。

senses.def: that you do because you always do it, or other people in the same situation always do it
senses.zh: 习惯性的；随大溜的；赶时髦的

examples.en: In the mid-60s he took the almost obligatory trip to India.
examples.zh: 60 年代中期，他也赶时髦到印度一游。

senses.def: to force somebody to do something, by law, because it is a duty, etc.

examples.en: Parents are obliged by law to send their children to school.
examples.zh: 法律规定父母必须送子女入学。

examples.en: I felt obliged to ask them to dinner.
examples.zh: 我不得不请他们吃饭。

examples.en: He suffered a serious injury that obliged him to give up work.
examples.zh: 他受伤严重，不得已只好放弃工作。

examples.en: Libel plaintiffs are virtually obliged to go into the witness box.
examples.zh: 诽谤案的原告几乎是被迫进入证人席的。

senses.def: to help somebody by doing what they ask or what you know they want

examples.en: Call me if you need any help—I'd be happy to oblige.
examples.zh: 若有需要，尽管给我打电话。我很乐意帮忙。

examples.en: Would you oblige me with some information?
examples.zh: 拜托您给我透露些消息好吗？

examples.en: Oblige me by keeping your suspicions to yourself.
examples.zh: 拜托你不要把你的怀疑声张出去。

examples.en: The fans were looking for another goal and Kane duly obliged.
examples.zh: 球迷们正在寻找另一个进球，凯恩也顺从了这一点。

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are very willing to help
senses.zh: 乐于助人地，热心相助地

examples.en: ‘I’ll go for you,’ she said, obligingly.
examples.zh: “我替你去吧。”她热情地说。

examples.en: They had obligingly reserved a room for me.
examples.zh: 他们很热心地为我保留了一个房间。

senses.def: not expressed or done in a direct way
senses.zh: 间接的；不直截了当的；拐弯抹角的

examples.en: an oblique reference/approach/comment
examples.zh: 隐约提及；间接途径；婉转的评论

senses.def: sloping at an angle
greater or less than 90°

examples.en: The extension was built at an oblique angle to the house.
examples.zh: 扩建的部分与原本的房子形成斜角。

senses.def: the symbol (/) used to show alternatives, as in lunch and/or dinner
an angle that is not an angle of 90°

examples.en: The extension was built at an oblique angle to the house.
examples.zh: 扩建的部分与原本的房子形成斜角。

senses.def: in a way that is not direct

examples.en: He referred only obliquely to their recent problems.
examples.zh: 他只是间接提到了他们近期的问题。

senses.def: at an angle

examples.en: Always cut stems obliquely to enable flowers to absorb more water.
examples.zh: 一定要斜剪花茎，让花能多吸收些水分。

senses.def: to remove all signs of something, either by destroying or covering it completely

examples.en: The building was completely obliterated by the bomb.
examples.zh: 炸弹把那座建筑物彻底摧毁了。

examples.en: The snow had obliterated their footprints.
examples.zh: 白雪覆盖了他们的足迹。

examples.en: Everything that happened that night was obliterated from his memory.
examples.zh: 那天夜里发生的一切都从他的记忆中消失了。

senses.def: the act of removing all signs of something, either by destroying or covering it completely

examples.en: the obliteration of the city by aerial bombing
examples.zh: 空中轰炸摧毁了这座城市

examples.en: The party faces obliteration at the next general election.
examples.zh: 该党将在下次大选中面临被消灭的危险。

senses.def: a state in which you are not aware of what is happening around you, usually because you are unconscious or asleep

examples.en: He often drinks himself into oblivion.
examples.zh: 他常常喝酒喝得不省人事。

examples.en: Sam longed for the oblivion of sleep.
examples.zh: 萨姆恨不得一睡不醒，了无心事。

senses.def: the state in which somebody/something has been forgotten and is no longer famous or important

examples.en: An unexpected victory saved him from political oblivion.
examples.zh: 一次意外的胜利使得他在政治上不再默默无闻。

examples.en: Most of his inventions have been consigned to oblivion.
examples.zh: 他的大部分发明都湮没无闻了。

examples.en: a minor masterpiece, saved from oblivion
examples.zh: 免于湮灭的次要代表作

senses.def: a state in which something has been completely destroyed

examples.en: Hundreds of homes were bombed into oblivion during the first weeks of the war.
examples.zh: 在战争的最初几周内，数以百计的房屋被炸毁。

senses.def: not aware of something

examples.en: You eventually become oblivious to the noise.
examples.zh: 你终究会变得不在意吵闹声的。

examples.en: The couple seemed oblivious to what was going on around them.
examples.zh: 这对夫妇似乎对周围发生的事情浑然不觉。

examples.en: He drove off, oblivious of the damage he had caused.
examples.zh: 他驾车而去，没有注意到他所造成的损害。

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are not aware of something
senses.zh: 明显地：以某种方式表明你不知道某事

senses.def: a shape that has four straight sides, two of which are longer than the other two, and four angles of 90°
senses.zh: 有四条直边的形状，其中两条比另外两条长，四个角为90度

examples.en: a tiny oblong of glass in the roof
examples.zh: 房顶上的一小块长方形玻璃

senses.def: any shape that is longer than it is wide

examples.en: The leaves are narrow oblongs.
examples.zh: 叶子是窄长圆形的。

senses.def: an oblong
used to describe any shape that is longer than it is wide
senses.zh: 椭圆形的；椭圆体的；长方形的

examples.en: an oblong melon
examples.zh: 椭圆形的瓜

senses.def: strong public criticism
senses.zh: 公开的抨击；公开的谴责；辱骂

senses.def: loss of respect and honour
extremely unpleasant, especially in a way that offends people
senses.zh: 极讨厌的；可憎的；令人作呕的

examples.en: obnoxious behaviour
examples.zh: 讨厌的行为

examples.en: a thoroughly obnoxious man
examples.zh: 一个非常令人讨厌的人

examples.en: obnoxious odours
examples.zh: 难闻的气味

examples.en: The movie is loud and obnoxious.
examples.zh: 这部电影喧闹且令人讨厌。

examples.en: I find her really obnoxious.
examples.zh: 我觉得她很讨厌。

senses.def: in an extremely unpleasant way, especially in a way that offends people
senses.zh: 极讨厌的；可憎的；令人作呕的

examples.en: She was being obnoxiously loud as usual.
examples.zh: 她像往常一样大声说话，令人讨厌。

examples.en: his obnoxiously arrogant manner
examples.zh: 他令人讨厌的傲慢态度

senses.def: or best offer (used in small advertisements to show that something may be sold at a lower price than the price that has been asked)

examples.en: $800 obo
examples.zh: 800 美元（可议价）

senses.def: a musical instrument of the woodwind
a person who plays the oboe
connected with sex in a way that most people find offensive

examples.en: obscene gestures/language/books
examples.zh: 淫秽的姿势／语言／书籍

examples.en: an obscene phone call (= in which somebody says obscene things)
examples.zh: 色情骚扰电话

examples.en: The book was declared obscene.
examples.zh: 这本书被宣布为淫秽书刊。

senses.def: extremely large in size or amount in a way that most people find unacceptable and offensive
senses.zh: （数量等）大得惊人的，骇人听闻的

examples.en: He earns an obscene amount of money.
examples.zh: 他赚钱多得吓人。

examples.en: It's obscene to spend so much on food when millions are starving.
examples.zh: 当数以百万的人忍饥挨饿时，饮食上挥霍无度是天理难容的。

senses.def: in a way that is connected with sex and that most people find offensive

examples.en: She gestured obscenely at them.
examples.zh: 她对他们做了一个猥亵的手势。

senses.def: extremely, especially in a way that most people find unacceptable and offensive
senses.zh: （数量等）大得惊人的，骇人听闻的

examples.en: They have become obscenely rich.
examples.zh: 他们已经变得极其富有。

senses.def: obscene
senses.zh: 淫秽的语言；下流的行为

examples.en: The editors are being prosecuted for obscenity.
examples.zh: 几个编辑因刊载污秽文字而被起诉。

examples.en: the laws on obscenity
examples.zh: 禁止淫秽的言语及行为的法规

senses.def: an obscene

examples.en: She screamed a string of obscenities at the judge.
examples.zh: 她冲着法官高声骂了一连串的脏话。

senses.def: the practice of deliberately preventing somebody from understanding or discovering something
senses.zh: 故弄玄虚；蒙蔽主义；蒙骗政策

examples.en: Religious prejudice and scientific obscurantism have been closely entangled throughout the whole history of this debate.
examples.zh: 宗教偏见和科学蒙昧主义在这场争论的整个历史中一直紧密地纠缠在一起。

senses.def: that deliberately prevents somebody from understanding or discovering something
senses.zh: 故弄玄虚；蒙蔽主义；蒙骗政策

senses.def: not well known

examples.en: an obscure German poet
examples.zh: 一个名不见经传的德国诗人

examples.en: We went to see one of Shakespeare’s more obscure plays.
examples.zh: 我们去看了莎士比亚的一部比较不起眼的戏剧。

examples.en: He was born around 1650 but his origins remain obscure.
examples.zh: 他生于 1650 年前后，但身世不详。

examples.en: The origins of the tradition have become obscure.
examples.zh: 这个传统的起源已经不清楚了。

senses.def: difficult to understand

examples.en: I found her lecture very obscure.
examples.zh: 我觉得她的讲座非常费解。

examples.en: For some obscure reason, he failed to turn up.
examples.zh: 他莫名其妙地没有如期露面。

examples.en: The meaning of his comment was obscure to everyone but himself.
examples.zh: 除了他自己之外，每个人都不清楚他的评论的含义。

senses.def: to make it difficult to see, hear or understand something

examples.en: The view was obscured by fog.
examples.zh: 雾中景色朦胧。

examples.en: We mustn't let these minor details obscure the main issue.
examples.zh: 我们不能让枝节问题掩盖主要问题。

examples.en: A shadow fell across her face, obscuring her expression.
examples.zh: 一道阴影落在了她的脸上，遮住了她的表情。

senses.def: without being well known

examples.en: He lived obscurely for the remainder of his life.
examples.zh: 他的余生都过着默默无闻的生活。

senses.def: in a way that is difficult to understand

examples.en: an obscurely titled song
examples.zh: 一首名字晦涩的歌曲

examples.en: They were making her feel obscurely worried.
examples.zh: 他们让她无缘无故地担忧起来。

senses.def: the state in which somebody/something is not well known or has been forgotten

examples.en: The actress was only 17 when she was plucked from obscurity and made a star.
examples.zh: 这个演员受到提携从无名少女一跃成为明星时年仅 17 岁。

examples.en: He spent most of his life working in obscurity.
examples.zh: 他在默默无闻的工作中度过了大半生。

senses.def: the fact of being difficult to understand; something that is difficult to understand

examples.en: The course teaches students to avoid ambiguity and obscurity of expression.
examples.zh: 这门课程教学生避免表达上的模棱两可、含混不清。

examples.en: poems of impenetrable obscurity
examples.zh: 晦涩难懂的诗

examples.en: a speech full of obscurities
examples.zh: 一篇晦涩难懂的演说

senses.def: the state of being dark
ceremonies at a funeral

examples.en: state obsequies
examples.zh: 国葬

senses.def: trying too hard to please somebody, especially somebody who is important

examples.en: an obsequious manner
examples.zh: 谄媚的态度

examples.en: The waiters came hurrying forward with obsequious smiles on their faces.
examples.zh: 侍者们急忙上前，脸上都带着谄媚的笑容。

examples.en: The service in the restaurant was attentive without being obsequious.
examples.zh: 餐厅的服务很周到，但并不谄媚。

senses.def: in a way that shows you are trying too hard to please somebody, especially somebody who is important

examples.en: He was smiling obsequiously.
examples.zh: 他正谄媚地笑着。

senses.def: the fact of trying too hard to please somebody, especially somebody who is important; behaviour that shows this
senses.zh: 谄媚：努力讨好某人，尤其是重要人物的事实；表明这一点的行为

senses.def: that can be seen or noticed
senses.zh: 能看得到的；能察觉到的

examples.en: observable differences
examples.zh: 可以察觉到的差异

examples.en: Similar trends are observable in mainland Europe.
examples.zh: 类似的趋势在欧洲大陆也能见到。

examples.en: The political crisis seems to be having little observable effect on share prices.
examples.zh: 政治危机似乎对股价影响不大。

senses.def: in a way that can be seen or noticed
senses.zh: 能看得到的；能察觉到的

examples.en: All of her predictions were observably correct.
examples.zh: 她所有的预测显然都是正确的。

senses.def: the practice of obeying a law, celebrating a festival or behaving according to a particular custom
senses.zh: （对法律、习俗的）遵守，奉行；（节日的）庆祝

examples.en: observance of the law
examples.zh: 守法

examples.en: a strict observance of the Sabbath
examples.zh: 对安息日的严格遵守

examples.en: observance of traditional practices
examples.zh: 遵守传统习俗

senses.def: an act performed as part of a religious or traditional ceremony
senses.zh: 宗教（或传统节日）的仪式

examples.en: religious observances
examples.zh: 宗教仪式

senses.def: good at noticing things around you
senses.zh: 善于观察的；观察力敏锐的

examples.en: Observant walkers may see red deer along this stretch of the road.
examples.zh: 观察敏锐的步行者能在这一路段看到赤鹿。

examples.en: How very observant of you!
examples.zh: 你真有眼力！

examples.en: She keeps an observant eye on developments in education.
examples.zh: 她密切关注教育领域的发展。

examples.en: He was acutely observant of the poverty around him.
examples.zh: 他敏锐地观察到周围的贫困。

senses.def: careful to obey religious laws and customs
senses.zh: 谨慎遵守教规和习俗的

senses.def: the act of watching somebody/something carefully for a period of time, especially to learn something

examples.en: Most information was collected by direct observation of the animals' behaviour.
examples.zh: 大部分信息都是通过直接观察动物的行为收集到的。

examples.en: results based on scientific observations
examples.zh: 根据科学观测得来的结果

examples.en: We managed to escape observation (= we were not seen).
examples.zh: 我们设法避开了人们的注意。

examples.en: The suspect is being kept under observation (= watched closely by the police).
examples.zh: 嫌疑人正受到监视。

examples.en: She has outstanding powers of observation (= the ability to notice things around her).
examples.zh: 她有超人的观察力。

examples.en: an observation post/tower (= a place from where somebody, especially an enemy, can be watched)
examples.zh: 瞭望哨；瞭望塔

examples.en: an observation deck (= a room or platform at the top of a tall building which provides views of the surrounding area)
examples.zh: 观景台（=位于高层建筑顶部的房间或平台，可欣赏周围地区的景色）

examples.en: his close observations of animal life in its natural setting
examples.zh: 他对自然环境中动物生活的密切观察

senses.def: a comment, especially based on something you have seen, heard or read
senses.zh: （尤指据所见、所闻、所读而作的）评论

examples.en: May I make a personal observation?
examples.zh: 我可以做一下个人观察吗？

examples.en: He began by making a few general observations about the report.
examples.zh: 开头他先对这个报告作了几点概括性的评论。

examples.en: She has some interesting observations on possible future developments.
examples.zh: 她对未来可能的发展有一些饶有兴味的论述。

examples.en: her witty observations on life
examples.zh: 她对人生的睿智评论

intro.en: These are all words for something that you say or write, especially something that gives information or an opinion.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指口头或书面的说明、宣布。

items.def: something that you say or write that gives information or an opinion, often in a formal way:
items.zh: 通常指正式的说明、声明、陈述、报告

examples.en: A government spokesperson made a statement to the press.
examples.zh: 政府发言人向新闻界发表了一份声明。

items.def: something that you say or write that gives an opinion on something or is a response to a question about a particular situation:
items.zh: 指议论、评论、意见

examples.en: She made helpful comments on my work.
examples.zh: 她对我的工作提出了有益的意见。

items.def: a spoken or written statement that informs people about something:
items.zh: 指公告、布告、通告

examples.en: the announcement of a peace agreement
examples.zh: 和平协议公告

items.def: something that you say or write that gives an opinion or thought about somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指谈论、言论、评述

examples.en: He made a number of rude remarks about the food.
examples.zh: 他对这食物作了许多无礼的评论。

items.def: (rather formal) an official or formal statement, especially one that states an intention, belief or feeling, or that gives information:
items.zh: 指官方或正式的公告、宣告、宣言、声明

examples.en: the declaration of war
examples.zh: 宣战

items.def: (rather formal) a comment, especially one based on something you have seen, heard or read:
items.zh: 尤指根据所见、所闻、所读而作的评论

examples.en: He began by making a few general observations about the report.
examples.zh: 开头他先对这个报告作了几点概括性的评论。

senses.def: a coach on a train with large windows, designed to give passengers a good view of the passing landscape
senses.zh: 观光车厢，游览车厢（火车车厢，有大窗）

senses.def: connected with or based on the activity of watching somebody/something carefully for a period of time, especially to learn something

examples.en: The course helps drivers to improve their observational skills.
examples.zh: 该课程帮助驾驶员提高观察能力。

examples.en: an observational study of cancer patients
examples.zh: 对癌症患者的观察性研究

senses.def: a special building with a telescope
to see or notice somebody/something

examples.en: Have you observed any changes lately?
examples.zh: 最近你注意到什么变化没有？

examples.en: All the characters in the novel are closely observed (= seem like people in real life).
examples.zh: 小说中的人物个个栩栩如生。

examples.en: I want you to observe all the details.
examples.zh: 我希望你观察所有的细节。

examples.en: The patterns observed in our study may represent a general rule.
examples.zh: 我们的研究中观察到的模式可能代表了一般规则。

examples.en: The police observed a man enter the bank.
examples.zh: 警察注意到一个男人走进了银行。

examples.en: They observed him entering the bank.
examples.zh: 他们看见他走进银行。

examples.en: She observed that all the chairs were already occupied.
examples.zh: 她发现所有的椅子都有人坐了。

examples.en: He was observed to follow her closely.
examples.zh: 有人看到他紧跟着她。

senses.def: to watch somebody/something carefully, especially to learn more about them

examples.en: He observes keenly, but says little.
examples.zh: 他观察敏锐，但言语寥寥。

examples.en: I felt he was observing everything I did.
examples.zh: 我觉得他正在注视着我做的每一件事。

examples.en: The patients were observed over a period of several months.
examples.zh: 这些病人被观察了数月之久。

examples.en: an observed decrease in rainfall in the area
examples.zh: 观察到该地区降雨量减少

examples.en: The program provided an opportunity to observe the effects of treatment.
examples.zh: 该计划提供了观察治疗效果的机会。

examples.en: The cells were observed under a microscope.
examples.zh: 在显微镜下观察细胞。

examples.en: The patient should be observed for signs of an allergic reaction.
examples.zh: 应注意观察患者是否出现过敏反应的迹象。

examples.en: They observed how the parts of the machine fitted together.
examples.zh: 他们观看了机器零件的组装过程。

senses.def: to make a remark

examples.en: She observed that it was getting late.
examples.zh: 她说天色晚了。

senses.def: to obey rules, laws, etc.

examples.en: Will the rebels observe the ceasefire?
examples.zh: 叛乱者会遵守停火协议吗？

examples.en: The crowd observed a minute's silence (= were silent for one minute) in memory of those who had died.
examples.zh: 众人为死者默哀一分钟。

senses.def: to celebrate festivals, birthdays, etc.

examples.en: Religious festivals were always observed.
examples.zh: 人们总是庆祝宗教节日。

intro.en: These words all mean to say or write a fact or opinion.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指口头或书面说明事实或发表意见。

items.def: to express an opinion or give facts about something:
items.zh: 指发表意见或说明事实

examples.en: He refused to comment until after the trial.
examples.zh: 他拒绝在审判前作任何评论。

items.def: (rather formal) to mention something because it is important or interesting:
items.zh: 指特别提到或指出

examples.en: He noted in passing that the company’s record on safety issues was not good.
examples.zh: 他顺便提到该公司在安全方面的记录不好。

items.def: to say or write what you have noticed about a situation:
items.zh: 指说起、谈论、评论

examples.en: Critics remarked that the play was not original.
examples.zh: 评论家指出这部戏剧缺乏创意。

items.def: (formal) to say or write what you have noticed about a situation:
items.zh: 指说起、谈论、评论

examples.en: She observed that it was getting late.
examples.zh: 她说天色晚了。

intro.en: These words all mean to see something, especially when you pay careful attention to it.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含看到、注意到之义。

items.def: to see, hear or become aware of somebody/​something; to pay attention to somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指看（或听）到、注意到、意识到、注意、留意

examples.en: The first thing I noticed about the room was the smell.
examples.zh: 我首先注意到的是屋子里的气味。

items.def: (rather formal) to notice or pay careful attention to something:
items.zh: 指注意、留意

examples.en: Please note (that) the office will be closed on Monday.
examples.zh: 请注意办事处星期一将关闭。

items.def: to discover or notice something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc:
items.zh: 指发现、查明、侦察出

examples.en: The tests are designed to detect the disease early.
examples.zh: 这些检查旨在及早查出疾病。

items.def: (formal) to see or notice somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指看到、注意到、观察到

examples.en: Have you observed any changes lately?
examples.zh: 最近你注意到什么变化没有？

items.def: (rather formal) to see something happen:
items.zh: 指当场看到、目击

examples.en: Police have appealed for anyone who witnessed the incident to contact them.
examples.zh: 警方呼吁目击这一事件的人与他们联系。

intro.en: These words all mean to turn your eyes in a particular direction.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含看、观看之义。

items.def: to turn your eyes in a particular direction:
items.zh: 指看、瞧

examples.en: If you look carefully you can just see our house from here.
examples.zh: 你要是仔细看，从这里就可以看见我们的房子。

items.def: to look at somebody/​something for a time, paying attention to what happens:
items.zh: 指看、注视、观看、观察

examples.en: to watch television
examples.zh: 看电视

items.def: to watch a game, television programme, performance, etc.:
items.zh: 指观看（比赛、电视节目、演出等）

examples.en: In the evening we went to see a movie.
examples.zh: 晚上我们去看了一场电影。

items.def: (formal) to look at something, especially when you look carefully; to watch television, a film, etc.:
items.zh: 指看、观看（尤指仔细观察）；看（电视、电影等）

examples.en: People came from all over the world to view her work.
examples.zh: 观众从世界各地涌来欣赏她的作品。

items.def: (formal) to watch somebody/​something carefully, especially to learn more about them or it:
items.zh: 指观察、注视、监视

examples.en: The patients were observed over a period of several months.
examples.zh: 这些病人被观察了数月之久。

senses.def: the sport of riding a specially designed motorcycle or bicycle through a course that has objects on the ground, which is designed to test a rider's ability
senses.zh: 极限骑行运动（使用特制摩托车或自行车，考验骑行者通过障碍物的能力）

examples.en: Observed trials is/are a test of technique and balance.
examples.zh: 观察试验是对技术和平衡的测试。

senses.def: a person who watches somebody/something

examples.en: According to observers, the plane exploded shortly after take-off.
examples.zh: 据目击者说，飞机起飞后不久就爆炸了。

examples.en: To the casual observer (= somebody who does not pay much attention), the system appears confusing.
examples.zh: 乍看起来，这个系统好像条理不清。

examples.en: Most art forms require a contribution from the observer.
examples.zh: 大多数艺术形式都需要观察者的贡献。

senses.def: a person who attends a meeting, lesson, etc. to listen and watch but not to take part

examples.en: A team of British officials were sent as observers to the conference.
examples.zh: 一组英国官员被派去做大会观察员。

senses.def: a person who watches and studies particular events, situations, etc. and is therefore considered to be an expert on them

examples.en: a royal observer
examples.zh: 王室观察家

intro.en: These are all words for a person who sees something happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指目睹事情发生的人。

items.def: a person who sees something happen and is able to describe it to other people; a person who gives evidence in a court of law:
items.zh: 指目击者、见证人、证人

examples.en: Police have appealed for witnesses to the accident.
examples.zh: 警方呼吁这起事故的目击者出来作证。

items.def: a person who sees something happen:
items.zh: 指观察者、目击者

examples.en: According to observers, the plane exploded shortly after take-off.
examples.zh: 据目击者说，飞机起飞后不久就爆炸了。

items.def: a person who watches something that is happening but is not involved in it:
items.zh: 指旁观者

examples.en: A crowd of onlookers gathered at the scene of the crash.
examples.zh: 在撞车地点聚集了一大群围观者。

items.def: a person who is going past somebody/​something by chance, especially when something unexpected happens:
items.zh: 指路人、过路的人，尤指意想不到的事发生时碰巧路过的

examples.en: Police asked passers-by if they had witnessed the accident.
examples.zh: 警察询问过路的人是否目击了这次事故。

items.def: a person who is near and can see what is happening when something such as an accident or fight takes place:
items.zh: 指现场目击者、旁观者

examples.en: Three innocent bystanders were killed in the crossfire.
examples.zh: 三名无辜的旁观者在交火中丧生。

items.def: a person who has seen a crime or accident and can describe it afterwards.
items.zh: 指犯罪或事故现场的目击者、见证人

senses.def: to completely fill your mind so that you cannot think of anything else, in a way that is not reasonable or normal

examples.en: He's obsessed by computers.
examples.zh: 他迷上了电脑。

examples.en: She's completely obsessed with him.
examples.zh: 他让她神魂颠倒。

examples.en: The need to produce the most exciting newspaper story obsesses most journalists.
examples.zh: 大多数记者梦寐以求的就是要写出最撼动人心的新闻报道来。

senses.def: to be always talking or worrying about a particular thing, especially when this annoys other people

examples.en: I think you should try to stop obsessing about food.
examples.zh: 我看你该歇歇了，别没完没了地唠叨吃的东西。

senses.def: the state in which a person’s mind is completely filled with thoughts of one particular thing or person in a way that is not reasonable or normal

examples.en: Her fear of flying is bordering on obsession.
examples.zh: 她怕乘飞机几乎到了不可救药的地步。

examples.en: There's a national obsession with celebrity in England.
examples.zh: 在英格兰，有一股对名流痴迷的全民风潮。

examples.en: The media's obsession with the young prince continues.
examples.zh: 新闻媒体继续对小王子进行连篇累牍的报道。

senses.def: a person or thing that somebody thinks about too much

examples.en: Fitness has become an obsession with him.
examples.zh: 他迷上了健身。

senses.def: thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not reasonable or normal
senses.zh: 痴迷的；迷恋的；耿耿于怀的

examples.en: She is obsessional about cleanliness.
examples.zh: 她有洁癖。

examples.en: obsessional behaviour
examples.zh: 痴迷的行为

examples.en: Perfectionist and obsessional thoughts can increase stress.
examples.zh: 完美主义和强迫性的想法会增加压力。

examples.en: They were receiving medical treatment for obsessional symptoms.
examples.zh: 他们正接受强迫症症状的治疗。

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not reasonable or normal
senses.zh: 痴迷地；迷恋地；耿耿于怀地

senses.def: thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not reasonable or normal
senses.zh: 痴迷的；迷恋的；耿耿于怀的

examples.en: He's becoming more and more obsessive about punctuality.
examples.zh: 他对守时要求越来越过分了。

examples.en: an obsessive attention to detail
examples.zh: 过分注重细枝末节

senses.def: a person whose mind is filled with thoughts of one particular thing or person so that they cannot think of anything else
a mental illness in which somebody feels they have to repeat certain actions or activities to get rid of fears or unpleasant thoughts
in a way that shows that you are thinking too much about one particular person or thing, in a way that is not reasonable or normal
senses.zh: 痴迷地；迷恋地；耿耿于怀地

examples.en: obsessively jealous
examples.zh: 妒火中烧

examples.en: He worries obsessively about his appearance.
examples.zh: 他极其在意自己的外表。

senses.def: a type of dark rock that looks like glass and comes from volcanoes
the state of becoming old-fashioned and no longer useful

examples.en: products with built-in/planned obsolescence (= designed not to last long so that people will have to buy new ones)
examples.zh: 内置／计划性报废产品（故意设计成不耐用而迫使人汰旧换新的产品）

senses.def: becoming old-fashioned and no longer useful

examples.en: obsolescent equipment/technology
examples.zh: 陈旧的设备/技术

senses.def: no longer used because something new has been invented

examples.en: obsolete technology
examples.zh: 过时技术

examples.en: With technological changes many traditional skills have become obsolete.
examples.zh: 随着技术的革新，许多传统技艺已被淘汰。

senses.def: a situation, an event, etc. that makes it difficult for you to do or achieve something

examples.en: So far, we have managed to overcome all the obstacles that have been placed in our path.
examples.zh: 到目前为止，我们已设法排除了前进道路上的一切人为障碍。

examples.en: A lack of qualifications can be a major obstacle to finding a job.
examples.zh: 学历不足往往是谋职的主要障碍。

examples.en: The MP claims that there is now no obstacle to him standing at the next general election.
examples.zh: 这位议员声称，现在他参加下届大选没有任何障碍。

examples.en: The huge distances involved have proved an obstacle to communication between villages.
examples.zh: 遥远的距离成为乡村之间通讯的一个障碍。

senses.def: an object that is in your way and that makes it difficult for you to move forward

examples.en: The area was full of streams and bogs and other natural obstacles.
examples.zh: 此地遍布小溪、泥潭和其他天然障碍。

examples.en: He managed with difficulty to negotiate the obstacles strewn across the floor.
examples.zh: 他艰难地跨过地板上散落的障碍物。

senses.def: a fence, etc. for a horse to jump over

examples.en: This huge open ditch forms the biggest obstacle on the course.
examples.zh: 这条巨大的明沟成为途中最大的障碍。

senses.def: a series of objects that people taking part in a race have to climb over, under, through, etc.
a series of difficulties that people have to deal with in order to achieve a particular aim

examples.en: We assume that competent doctors emerge at the end of an obstacle course of traditional examinations based on facts.
examples.zh: 我们假设，在基于事实的传统考试的障碍过程结束后，有能力的医生就会出现。

senses.def: an area of land with many objects that are difficult to climb, jump over or go through, which is used, especially by soldiers, for improving physical skills and strength
a race in which the people taking part have to climb over, under, through, etc. various objects
connected with the branch of medicine that deals with the birth of children

examples.en: obstetric medicine
examples.zh: 产科学

senses.def: a doctor who is trained in obstetrics
the branch of medicine that deals with the birth of children
the attitude of somebody who refuses to change their opinions, way of behaving, etc. when other people try to persuade them to; behaviour that shows this
senses.zh: 顽固性：某人拒绝说服他人的态度，行为方式等，当其他人试图说服他们时； 表现这一点的行为

examples.en: an act of sheer obstinacy
examples.zh: 纯属固执的行为

senses.def: refusing to change your opinions, way of behaving, etc. when other people try to persuade you to; showing this

examples.en: He can be very obstinate when he wants to be!
examples.zh: 他的犟劲儿一上来，简直执拗得要命！

examples.en: her obstinate refusal to comply with their request
examples.zh: 她拒不服从他们的要求

examples.en: Their position remains one of obstinate denial, even in face of the new evidence.
examples.zh: 即使在新证据面前他们还是固执地持否定立场。

senses.def: difficult to get rid of or deal with
senses.zh: 棘手的；难以去除的；难以对付的

examples.en: the obstinate problem of unemployment
examples.zh: 失业这个棘手的问题

examples.en: an obstinate stain
examples.zh: 顽固斑渍

senses.def: in a way that shows that you refuse to change your opinions, way of behaving, etc. when other people try to persuade you to

examples.en: He obstinately refused to consider the future.
examples.zh: 他执意拒不考虑未来。

senses.def: noisy and difficult to control
senses.zh: 喧闹的；桀骜不驯的；任性的

senses.def: to block a road, an entrance, a passage, etc. so that somebody/something cannot get through, see past, etc.

examples.en: You can't park here, you're obstructing my driveway.
examples.zh: 你不能在这里停车，你挡住了我家的车道。

examples.en: First check that the accident victim doesn't have an obstructed airway.
examples.zh: 首先要确保事故受伤者的气道通畅。

examples.en: The pillar obstructed our view of the stage.
examples.zh: 柱子挡着，我们看不见舞台。

senses.def: to prevent somebody/something from doing something or making progress, especially when this is done deliberately

examples.en: They were charged with obstructing the police in the course of their duty.
examples.zh: 他们被指控妨碍警察执行公务。

examples.en: He accused terrorists of attempting to obstruct the peace process.
examples.zh: 他谴责恐怖分子企图阻碍和平进程。

senses.def: to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
to tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc. from finding out the truth about a crime
the fact of trying to prevent something/somebody from making progress

examples.en: the obstruction of justice
examples.zh: 妨碍司法公正

examples.en: He was arrested for obstruction of a police officer in the execution of his duty.
examples.zh: 他因妨碍警察执行公务而被逮捕。

examples.en: The asylum seekers had to contend with continued bureaucratic obstruction.
examples.zh: 寻求政治庇护的人得不断地应付官僚主义的层层阻挠。

senses.def: the fact of blocking a road, an entrance, a passage, etc.

examples.en: obstruction of the factory gates
examples.zh: 对工厂大门的堵塞

examples.en: The abandoned car was causing an obstruction.
examples.zh: 这辆被遗弃的汽车堵住了道路。

senses.def: something that blocks a road, an entrance, etc.

examples.en: It is my job to make sure that all pathways are clear of obstructions.
examples.zh: 保证所有的道路通畅是我的职责。

senses.def: something that blocks a passage or tube in your body; a medical condition resulting from this

examples.en: He had an operation to remove an obstruction in his throat.
examples.zh: 他做了手术，取出喉头的阻塞物。

examples.en: bowel/intestinal obstruction
examples.zh: 肠梗阻

senses.def: the offence of unfairly putting your body in front of a player of the other team so they cannot move to get the ball
the practice of trying to prevent a parliament or committee from making progress, passing laws, etc.
senses.zh: （对议会或委员会工作的）阻挠行为，妨碍

senses.def: a person who tries to prevent a parliament or committee from making progress, passing laws, etc.
senses.zh: （对议会或委员会工作的）阻挠行为，妨碍

senses.def: trying to prevent a parliament or committee from making progress, passing laws, etc.
senses.zh: （对议会或委员会工作的）阻挠行为，妨碍

senses.def: trying to prevent somebody/something from making progress

examples.en: Of course she can do it. She's just being deliberately obstructive.
examples.zh: 这事她当然能做。她只是在刻意阻挠罢了。

examples.en: He proved to be an obstinate and obstructive defendant.
examples.zh: 事实证明，他是一个固执且阻挠的被告。

senses.def: connected with a passage, tube, etc. in your body that has become blocked

examples.en: obstructive lung disease
examples.zh: 肺阻塞疾病

senses.def: to get something, especially by making an effort

examples.en: to obtain information/data/results
examples.zh: 获取信息／数据／结果

examples.en: I've been trying to obtain permission to publish this material.
examples.zh: 我一直在努力获取公开这一材料的许可。

examples.en: I finally managed to obtain a copy of the report.
examples.zh: 我终于设法弄到了这份报告的一个副本。

examples.en: Further details can be obtained by writing to the above address.
examples.zh: 详情可致信上述地址获取。

examples.en: To obtain the overall score, add up the totals in each column.
examples.zh: 要得出总计得分，就把各栏的小计加起来。

senses.def: to exist

examples.en: These conditions no longer obtain.
examples.zh: 这些条件不再适用。

senses.def: that can be obtained

examples.en: Full details are obtainable from any post office.
examples.zh: 详情可至任何邮局索取。

senses.def: to become or make something/yourself noticed, especially in a way that is not wanted

examples.en: Music from the next room obtruded upon his thoughts.
examples.zh: 隔壁的音乐声打扰了他的思绪。

examples.en: The design should not obtrude to the extent that it distracts the reader.
examples.zh: 设计不应过于突兀，以免分散读者的注意力。

examples.en: This overwhelming sense of despair obtruded itself on me at intervals.
examples.zh: 这种压倒性的绝望感时不时地向我袭来。

senses.def: easy to notice in an unpleasant way
senses.zh: 扎眼的；显眼而不好看的

examples.en: The sofa would be less obtrusive in a paler colour.
examples.zh: 沙发的颜色再浅一点就不那么扎眼了。

examples.en: They tried to ensure that their presence was not too obtrusive.
examples.zh: 他们尽量做到在场时不引人注目。

examples.en: The proposed development would form an obtrusive feature in the landscape.
examples.zh: 拟议的开发项目将在景观中形成一个引人注目的特征。

senses.def: in a way that is easy to notice and unpleasant

examples.en: Music played loudly but not too obtrusively.
examples.zh: 音乐播放得很大声，但又不太刺耳。

senses.def: slow or unwilling to understand something
senses.zh: 迟钝的；愚蠢的；态度勉强的

examples.en: Are you being deliberately obtuse?
examples.zh: 你是不是故意装傻？

examples.en: Perhaps I’m being obtuse, but what has all this got to do with me?
examples.zh: 也许是我太迟钝了，但这一切与我有什么关系呢？

examples.en: He was either completely ignorant or being wilfully obtuse.
examples.zh: 他要么完全无知，要么故意迟钝。

examples.en: She was the most obtuse person I’d ever met.
examples.zh: 她是我见过的最迟钝的人。

senses.def: between 90° and 180°
an angle between 90° and 180°
the fact of being slow or unwilling to understand something
senses.zh: 迟钝的；愚蠢的；态度勉强的

senses.def: obviously
the opposite of something

examples.en: The obverse of love is hate.
examples.zh: 爱的反面是恨。

senses.def: the side of a coin or medal
to remove a problem or the need for something

examples.en: This new evidence obviates the need for any further enquiries.
examples.zh: 这项新证据排除了继续调查的必要。

examples.en: Disaster was obviated by the opening of the reserve parachute.
examples.zh: 备用降落伞的打开避免了灾难。

senses.def: easy to see or understand
senses.zh: 明显的；显然的；易理解的

examples.en: I know you don't like her but try not to make it so obvious.
examples.zh: 我知道你不喜欢她，但尽量别表现得那么明显。

examples.en: He agreed with obvious pleasure.
examples.zh: 他同意了，显然很高兴。

examples.en: It soon became obvious that the machine did not work.
examples.zh: 机器故障很快就显现出来了。

examples.en: It's painfully obvious that the budget was low for this movie.
examples.zh: 很明显这部电影的预算很低。

examples.en: It's obvious a change is needed.
examples.zh: 显然需要做出改变。

examples.en: It was obvious to everyone that the child had been badly treated.
examples.zh: 人人一看便知那个孩子受过虐待。

examples.en: The lessons seem fairly obvious to anyone who doesn't work in the Administration.
examples.zh: 对于不在政府工作的人来说，这些教训似乎相当明显。

examples.en: It's obvious from what she said that something is wrong.
examples.zh: 根据她所说的，显然是出问题了。

examples.en: For obvious reasons, I'd prefer not to give my name.
examples.zh: 因为显而易见的原因，我不愿披露自己的姓名。

examples.en: The reasons for this decision were not immediately obvious.
examples.zh: 作出这一决定的理由暂时还不清楚。

examples.en: It is blindingly obvious that there is not enough money to finance this public spending programme.
examples.zh: 显而易见的是，没有足够的资金来资助这一公共支出计划。

examples.en: It was far from obvious how they were going to get off the island.
examples.zh: 很难看出他们将如何离开这座岛。

senses.def: that most people would think of or agree to

examples.en: She was the obvious choice for the job.
examples.zh: 她是这一工作的当然人选。

examples.en: There's no obvious solution to the problem.
examples.zh: 这个问题尚无公认的解决办法。

examples.en: This seemed the most obvious thing to do.
examples.zh: 这似乎是最顺理成章的做法。

examples.en: an obvious example/answer/question
examples.zh: 一个明显的例子/答案/问题

senses.def: not interesting, new or showing imagination; unnecessary because it is clear to everyone
senses.zh: 平淡无奇的；无创意的；因显而易见而不必要的

examples.en: The ending was pretty obvious.
examples.zh: 结尾十分平淡。

examples.en: I may be stating the obvious but without more money the project cannot survive.
examples.zh: 我这话可能多余，但是不投入更多资金，项目就难以为继。

intro.en: These words all describe something that is easy to see or understand.
intro.zh: 以上各词均形容事物显而易见、明白易懂。

items.def: easy to see or understand and leaving no doubts:
items.zh: 指显而易见的、明白易懂的、清楚的、明确的

examples.en: It was quite clear to me that she was lying.
examples.zh: 我十分清楚她在撒谎。

items.def: easy to see or understand:
items.zh: 指显而易见、明白易懂、显然

examples.en: It’s obvious from what he said that something is wrong.
examples.zh: 根据他所说的，显然是出问题了。

items.def: [not usually before noun] (rather formal) easy to see or understand:
items.zh: 指显而易见、明白易懂、显然

examples.en: It was apparent from her face that she was really upset.
examples.zh: 从面容上一眼就可以看出她确实心绪烦乱。

items.def: (rather formal) easy to see or understand:
items.zh: 指显而易见、明白易懂、显然

examples.en: The orchestra played with evident enjoyment.
examples.zh: 管弦乐队演奏得兴致勃勃。

items.def: easy to see or understand:
items.zh: 指显而易见、明白易懂、显然

examples.en: He made it very plain that he wanted us to leave.
examples.zh: 他明确表示要我们离开。

senses.def: used when giving information that you expect other people to know already or agree with
senses.zh: （用于陈述认为别人已知道或希望别人同意的事）显然，明显地

examples.en: Obviously, we don't want to spend too much money.
examples.zh: 很明显，我们不想花太多的钱。

examples.en: Diet and exercise are obviously important.
examples.zh: 显然，饮食和运动是重要的。

examples.en: I wanted to do well, obviously, but I wasn't nervous because I don't see exams as the be all and end all.
examples.zh: 显然，我想取得好成绩，但我并不紧张，因为我不认为考试就是一切。

examples.en: She responded 'Oh well, obviously I disagree with him'.
examples.zh: 她回答说“哦，好吧，显然我不同意他的观点”。

examples.en: This massive storm obviously had a huge impact on air travellers.
examples.zh: 这场巨大的风暴显然对航空旅客产生了巨大的影响。

senses.def: used to say that a particular situation or fact is easy to see or understand
senses.zh: （用于说明某种情况或事实）显而易见，明显，不言而喻

examples.en: He was obviously upset.
examples.zh: 他显然很不高兴。

examples.en: They're obviously not coming.
examples.zh: 他们显然不会来了。

examples.en: ‘I didn't realise it was a formal occasion.’ ‘Obviously!’ (= I can see by the way you are dressed)
examples.zh: “我没想到这是个正式场合。”“看得出来！”

examples.en: This story is so obviously false that Matthew doesn't bother to refute it.
examples.zh: 这个故事显然是错误的，马修懒得去反驳它。

senses.def: the fact of being easy to see or understand
senses.zh: 明显的；显然的；易理解的

examples.en: the obviousness of his injuries
examples.zh: 他的伤势显而易见

senses.def: the fact that most people would think of or agree to something

examples.en: Casey rolled her eyes at the obviousness of the question.
examples.zh: 凯西对这个显而易见的问题翻了个白眼。

senses.def: the fact of not being interesting, new or showing imagination
senses.zh: 明显性：没有兴趣，没有新意或没有想象力

examples.en: the obviousness of the show's humour
examples.zh: 节目的幽默感显而易见

senses.def: obviously
a small musical instrument like an egg in shape that you blow into, with holes for the fingers
senses.zh: 陶笛，奥卡里纳（管身椭圆形）

senses.def: a particular time when something happens

examples.en: on this/that occasion
examples.zh: 这次；那次

examples.en: I've met him on several occasions.
examples.zh: 我曾见过他几次。

examples.en: They have been seen together on two separate occasions.
examples.zh: 他们有两次被人看见在一起。

examples.en: On one occasion, she called me in the middle of the night.
examples.zh: 有一次她深更半夜打电话给我。

examples.en: Only on rare occasions do I go out socially.
examples.zh: 只有在极少数情况下我才会出去参加社交活动。

examples.en: I can remember very few occasions when he had to cancel because of ill health.
examples.zh: 我记得他因为健康不佳而被迫取消的情况极少。

examples.en: He used the occasion to announce further tax cuts.
examples.zh: 他利用这个机会宣布再次减税。

examples.en: I have stated on numerous occasions what options are open.
examples.zh: 我曾多次说过有哪些选择可供选择。

examples.en: Harry has mentioned this on many previous occasions.
examples.zh: 哈利之前曾多次提到过这一点。

senses.def: a special event, ceremony or celebration
senses.zh: 特别的事情（或仪式、庆典）

examples.en: a great/memorable/happy/momentous occasion
examples.zh: 一个伟大／难忘／快乐／重要的时刻

examples.en: Turn every meal into a special occasion.
examples.zh: 要把每一顿饭都弄得特别一些。

examples.en: They marked the occasion (= celebrated it) with an open-air concert.
examples.zh: 他们举办了露天音乐会来庆祝。

examples.en: Their wedding turned out to be quite an occasion.
examples.zh: 他们的婚礼办得相当隆重。

examples.en: We expect you to dress for the occasion.
examples.zh: 我们希望您着装适合这个场合。

examples.en: He was presented with the watch on the occasion of his retirement.
examples.zh: 他在退休仪式上获赠这块手表。

examples.en: Every good wish to them on the occasion of their 40th anniversary.
examples.zh: 在他们结婚 40 周年之际，向他们致以良好的祝愿。

senses.def: a suitable time for something

examples.en: It should have been an occasion for rejoicing, but she could not feel any real joy.
examples.zh: 原本应该是高兴的时刻，她却丝毫未感到快乐。

examples.en: These workshops provide an occasion for talking about art.
examples.zh: 这些研讨会提供了一个讨论艺术的机会。

examples.en: This is not a time for specifics, but an occasion for vision.
examples.zh: 现在不是讨论具体细节的时候，而是展现远见的时候。

examples.en: Festivals were occasions for great celebration.
examples.zh: 节日是盛大庆祝的场合。

examples.en: I’ll speak to him about it if the occasion arises (= if I get a chance).
examples.zh: 有机会的话，我要跟他谈谈这件事。

senses.def: a reason or cause

examples.en: I've had no occasion to visit him recently.
examples.zh: 我最近无缘去拜访他。

examples.en: She doesn’t have much occasion to speak French in her new job.
examples.zh: 她在新工作中没有太多机会说法语。

examples.en: Her death was the occasion of mass riots.
examples.zh: 她的逝世引发了大规模的骚乱。

examples.en: Art here is an occasion for education and entertainment.
examples.zh: 艺术在这里是教育和娱乐的场所。

examples.en: I'm willing to go to court over this if the occasion arises (= if it becomes necessary).
examples.zh: 如果必要的话，我愿意就此出庭。

senses.def: sometimes but not often

examples.en: He has been known on occasion to lose his temper.
examples.zh: 大家都知道他有时会发脾气。

senses.def: a feeling or understanding that an event is important or special

examples.en: Candles on the table gave the evening a sense of occasion.
examples.zh: 桌上点了一些蜡烛，使得那个晚上有一种特别的气氛。

senses.def: to cause something

examples.en: The flight delay was occasioned by the need for a further security check.
examples.zh: 这次航班的延误是由于必须做进一步的安全检查。

examples.en: The injury was believed to have occasioned his death.
examples.zh: 据信，这次受伤导致了他的死亡。

examples.en: The decision occasioned us much anxiety.
examples.zh: 这个决定让我们忧虑不堪。

senses.def: sometimes but not often

examples.en: He has been known on occasion to lose his temper.
examples.zh: 大家都知道他有时会发脾气。

senses.def: a feeling or understanding that an event is important or special

senses.zh: （某人的言行导致的）冒犯，不快，反感

examples.zh: 这张照片可能会引起一些人的反感。

examples.zh: 你若早退谁也不会介意的。

examples.zh: 别动不动就生气。

examples.zh: 许多读者对这篇文章很反感。

examples.zh: 我无意冒犯任何人。

examples.zh: 尼尔开那个玩笑并非想冒犯谁。

examples.zh: 他们决定把这份工作给乔。

examples.en: They decided to offer Jo the job.
examples.zh: 他们决定让乔做这件工作。

examples.en: I gratefully took the cup of coffee she offered me.
examples.zh: 我感激地接过她递来的一杯咖啡。

examples.en: Taylor offered him 500 dollars to do the work.
examples.zh: 泰勒愿出 500 美元雇他做这件工作。

senses.def: to say that you are willing to do something for somebody
senses.zh: 主动提出，主动分担（做某事）

examples.en: The kids offered to do the dishes.
examples.zh: 孩子们主动要求洗盘子。

examples.en: ‘I'll do it,’ she offered.
examples.zh: “这个我来做吧。”她提议道。

senses.def: to make something available for sale or use

examples.en: The hotel offers excellent facilities for families.
examples.zh: 本旅馆提供适合家庭的优良设施。

examples.en: Both companies offer a range of software.
examples.zh: 两家公司都提供一系列软件。

examples.en: Which lenders consistently offer the cheapest mortgages?
examples.zh: 哪些贷方始终提供最便宜的抵押贷款？

examples.en: The property will be offered for sale by auction on May 24.
examples.zh: 该房产将于 5 月 24 日拍卖。

senses.def: to provide the opportunity for something; to provide access to something

examples.en: The job didn't offer any prospects for promotion.
examples.zh: 这份工作没有任何升迁的希望。

examples.en: He did not offer any explanation for his behaviour.
examples.zh: 他没有对自己的行为作出任何解释。

examples.en: The program has offered her many opportunities for travel.
examples.zh: 该计划让她有了许多旅行的机会。

senses.def: to show that you are ready to resist or attack somebody/something
senses.zh: 表现出抵抗力（或攻击力）

examples.en: Universities offered little resistance to these changes.
examples.zh: 大学对这些变化几乎毫无抵抗力。

examples.en: He never lost his temper or offered violence to anyone.
examples.zh: 他从不发脾气，也不对人武力相向。

senses.def: to give something to God

examples.en: We offered up our prayers for the men's safe return.
examples.zh: 我们祈求上苍保佑他们平安归来。

senses.def: to have something available that somebody wants

examples.en: Oxford has a lot to offer visitors in the way of entertainment.
examples.zh: 牛津向来访者提供各式各样的娱乐活动。

examples.en: a young man with a great deal to offer (= who is intelligent, has many skills, etc.)
examples.zh: 一个多才多艺的年轻人

senses.def: to hold out your hand for somebody to shake
senses.zh: 伸出手（以便同别人握手）

senses.def: an act of saying that you are willing to do something for somebody or give something to somebody

examples.en: to receive a job offer
examples.zh: 收到聘用邀约

examples.en: to accept/reject/decline an offer
examples.zh: 接受／拒绝／谢绝邀约

examples.en: Thank you for your kind offer of help.
examples.zh: 谢谢你的好心帮助。

examples.en: I took him up on his offer of a loan.
examples.zh: 他主动借钱给我，我接受了。

examples.en: You can't just turn down offers of work like that.
examples.zh: 人家给你工作，你不能就那样一一谢绝呀。

examples.en: an offer of marriage
examples.zh: 求婚

examples.en: I accepted her offer to pay.
examples.zh: 她要付款，我同意了。

senses.def: an amount of money that somebody is willing to pay for something

examples.en: I've had an offer of $2 500 for the car.
examples.zh: 有人向我出价 2 500 美元买这辆汽车。

examples.en: The museum received an offer for the painting of $19 million.
examples.zh: 该博物馆收到了这幅画 1900 万美元的报价。

examples.en: They've decided to accept our original offer.
examples.zh: 他们已决定接受我们最初的报价。

examples.en: The offer has been withdrawn.
examples.zh: 那个报价已经撤销了。

examples.en: They made me an offer I couldn't refuse.
examples.zh: 他们提出了一个使我不好拒绝的报价。

examples.en: The original price was £3 000, but I'm open to offers (= willing to consider offers that are less than that).
examples.zh: 原价为 3 000 英镑，但价钱还可以商量。

senses.def: a reduction in the normal price of something, usually for a short period of time
senses.zh: （通常为短期的）减价，削价；处理价；特价

examples.en: This special offer is valid until the end of the month.
examples.zh: 这个特价优惠月底前有效。

examples.en: See next week's issue for details of more free offers.
examples.zh: 有关更多免费赠品的详情请见下期周刊。

examples.en: They have an offer on new phones at the moment.
examples.zh: 他们目前有新手机的报价。

senses.def: that can be bought, used, etc.

examples.en: The following is a list of courses currently on offer.
examples.zh: 以下是目前所开设课程的清单。

examples.en: Prizes worth more than £20 000 are on offer.
examples.zh: 优胜者奖品总值逾 20 000 英镑。

senses.def: on sale at a lower price than normal for a short period of time
senses.zh: 短期内打折销售；削价出售

examples.en: Italian wines are on (special) offer this week.
examples.zh: 意大利葡萄酒本周特价销售。

examples.en: We have a number of bargains on offer.
examples.zh: 我们有许多要出售的便宜货。

senses.def: if a house or other building is under offer
senses.zh: （房屋或其他建筑物）已有买主出价，在洽售中

examples.en: The property is currently under offer to a client.
examples.zh: 这处房产目前已有一位客户出价打算购买。

senses.def: to have something available that somebody wants

examples.en: Oxford has a lot to offer visitors in the way of entertainment.
examples.zh: 牛津向来访者提供各式各样的娱乐活动。

examples.en: a young man with a great deal to offer (= who is intelligent, has many skills, etc.)

senses.def: on sale at a lower price than normal for a short period of time
senses.zh: 短期内打折销售；削价出售

examples.en: Italian wines are on (special) offer this week.
examples.zh: 意大利葡萄酒本周特价销售。

examples.en: We have a number of bargains on offer.

senses.zh: （房屋或其他建筑物）已有买主出价，在洽售中

examples.en: The property is currently under offer to a client.
examples.zh: 这处房产目前已有一位客户出价打算购买。

senses.def: to hold out your hand for somebody to shake
senses.zh: 伸出手（以便同别人握手）

senses.def: the offering of bread and wine to God at a church service
senses.zh: 祭品（奉献给上帝的饼和酒）

senses.def: an offering or a collection of money during a church service
senses.zh: 献金（礼拜中收集的捐款）

senses.def: not showing much interest in somebody/something in a way that is rude or upsets somebody

examples.en: an offhand manner
examples.zh: 随随便便的态度

examples.en: He was very offhand with me.
examples.zh: 他完全是在敷衍我。

senses.def: without being able to check something or think about it
senses.zh: 未经核实地；不假思索地；即席地

examples.en: I don't know offhand how much we made last year.
examples.zh: 我一时还真说不清我们去年赚了多少钱。

senses.def: in a way that does not show much interest in somebody/something and is rude

examples.en: He spoke offhandedly, making it clear I had no say in the matter.
examples.zh: 他语气冷淡敷衍，清楚表明这件事不容我置喙。

senses.def: a room, set of rooms or building where people work, usually sitting at desks

examples.en: The company is moving to new offices on the other side of town.
examples.zh: 公司要迁往城另一边的新办公楼。

examples.en: Are you going to the office today?
examples.zh: 你今天去办公室吗？

examples.en: I'm sorry, Mr Anders is not in the office today.
examples.zh: 很遗憾，安德斯先生今天不在办公室。

examples.en: I've had a tough day at the office.
examples.zh: 我在办公室度过了艰难的一天。

examples.en: a regional/branch office
examples.zh: 区域/分支机构

examples.en: office workers
examples.zh: 办公室人员

examples.en: an office job
examples.zh: 办公室工作

examples.en: an office building
examples.zh: 办公楼

examples.en: The new development will include housing and office space.
examples.zh: 新开发项目将包括住房和办公空间。

examples.en: I'm going to be out of the office next week.
examples.zh: 下周我要离开办公室。

senses.def: a room in which a particular person works, usually at a desk

examples.en: Some people have to share an office.
examples.zh: 有些人只好合用一间办公室。

examples.en: Come into my office.
examples.zh: 到我的办公室里来。

senses.def: a place where a doctor, dentist or vet

examples.en: a doctor’s/dentist’s office
examples.zh: 诊室；牙医诊所

examples.en: the bill from an office visit to the doctor
examples.zh: 到医生诊室就诊的收费单

senses.def: a room or building used for a particular purpose, especially to provide information or a service
senses.zh: 办事处；（尤指）问询处，服务处

examples.en: a ticket office
examples.zh: 售票处

senses.def: used in the names of some British government departments
senses.zh: （用于英国某些政府部门的名称中）

examples.en: the Home Office
examples.zh: 内政部

examples.en: the Foreign and Commonwealth Office
examples.zh: 外交和联邦事务部

examples.en: the Office of Fair Trading
examples.zh: 公平贸易局

examples.en: a research project carried out by the Welsh Office
examples.zh: 威尔士办事处开展的一项研究项目

senses.def: an important position of authority, especially in government; the work and duties connected with this
senses.zh: 要职；重要官职；重要职务

examples.en: She held office as a cabinet minister for ten years.
examples.zh: 她担任内阁部长长达十年。

examples.en: How long has he been in office?
examples.zh: 他任职多久了？

examples.en: Perhaps she remained in office too long.
examples.zh: 也许她在位时间太长了。

examples.en: The scandal cast a shadow over his time in office.
examples.zh: 这桩丑闻给他的执政期蒙上了一层阴影。

examples.en: The party has been out of office (= has not formed a government) for many years.
examples.zh: 那个党已在野多年了。

examples.en: The present government took office in 2024.
examples.zh: 本届政府于2024年上任。

examples.en: He died three years after leaving office.
examples.zh: 他在卸任三年后去世。

examples.en: She has announced she will not run for office again.
examples.zh: 她已宣布不再竞选公职。

examples.en: He has never sought public office.
examples.zh: 他从未寻求过公职。

examples.en: She held the office of treasurer for five years.
examples.zh: 她担任财长五年。

senses.def: with somebody’s help
senses.zh: 经某人斡旋；承某人协助

senses.def: with somebody’s help
senses.zh: 经某人斡旋；承某人协助

senses.def: a large building that contains offices, usually belonging to more than one company
senses.zh: 办公大楼（通常为几家公司合用的）

examples.en: high-rise office blocks
examples.zh: 高层办公大楼

senses.def: a young man employed to do simple tasks in an office
a British government department which researches and publishes social and economic statistics, including trade figures and the Retail Price Index
senses.zh: 国家统计局：英国政府部门，负责研究和发布社会和经济统计数据，包括贸易数据和零售价格指数。它还发布了人口普查的结果。国家统计局独立于部长，而是通过英国统计局向议会以及苏格兰，威尔士和北爱尔兰政府报告。

senses.def: a young woman employed to do simple tasks in an office
a person who is in a position of authority, especially in the government or a government organization
the time when people in offices are normally working

examples.en: Our telephone lines are open during normal office hours.
examples.zh: 我们的电话在正常办公时间一直开通。

senses.def: a party, usually just before Christmas, for the people who work in a particular office or company
senses.zh: 办公室聚会：通常在圣诞节前的聚会，用于在特定办公室或公司工作的人们

senses.def: a person who works in the offices of a business or company
senses.zh: （公司、企业的）办事人员；公司职员；上班族

senses.def: a person who is in a position of authority in the armed forces or on a ship

examples.en: army/military/naval officers
examples.zh: 陆军军官；军官；海军军官

examples.en: senior officers in the Royal Air Force
examples.zh: 英国皇家空军高级军官

examples.en: The matter was passed on to me, as your commanding officer.
examples.zh: 这件事转到了你的指挥官我这里。

examples.en: He's a retired army intelligence officer.
examples.zh: 他是一名退役陆军情报官员。

senses.def: a member of the police

examples.en: the officer in charge of the case
examples.zh: 负责本案的警察

examples.en: the investigating officer
examples.zh: 进行调查工作的警察

examples.en: Yes, officer, I saw what happened.
examples.zh: 是，警察先生，我看到了发生的事。

examples.en: Officers arrested five suspects after a raid last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚的突袭后，警方逮捕了五名嫌疑人。

senses.def: a title for a police officer

examples.en: Officer Dibble
examples.zh: 迪布尔警官

senses.def: a person who is in a position of authority in the government or a large organization
senses.zh: （政府或大机构的）官员，高级职员

examples.en: an environmental health officer
examples.zh: 环境卫生官员

examples.en: a customs/prison/welfare officer
examples.zh: 海关／典狱／福利官员

examples.en: officers of state (= ministers in the government)
examples.zh: （政府各部）部长

examples.en: He was a former officer in the Secret Service.
examples.zh: 他曾是情报部门的一名官员。

senses.def: agreed to, said, done, etc. by somebody who is in a position of authority
senses.zh: 正式的；官方的；官方授权的

examples.en: an official announcement/decision/statement
examples.zh: 官方公告／决定／声明

examples.en: according to official figures/statistics
examples.zh: 根据官方数字／统计

examples.en: The news is not yet official.
examples.zh: 这消息尚未经官方证实。

examples.en: the official biography of the President
examples.zh: 总统的官方传记

examples.en: An official inquiry has been launched into the cause of the accident.
examples.zh: 当局已对事故的原因展开调查。

examples.en: The country's official language is Spanish.
examples.zh: 这个国家的官方语言为西班牙语。

examples.en: The film's official website is also very informative.
examples.zh: 这部电影的官方网站也有很详尽的介绍。

examples.en: I intend to lodge an official complaint (= to complain to somebody in authority).
examples.zh: 我打算正式提出申诉。

senses.def: connected with the job of somebody who is in a position of authority

examples.en: official duties/responsibilities
examples.zh: 公务

examples.en: the Prime Minister’s official residence
examples.zh: 首相官邸

examples.en: He attended in his official capacity as mayor.
examples.zh: 他以市长的官方身份莅临。

examples.en: This was her first official engagement.
examples.zh: 这是她的首桩公务。

examples.en: He made an official visit to Tokyo in March.
examples.zh: 他于三月到东京进行了一次公务访问。

senses.def: formal and attended by people in authority
senses.zh: 正式的；公务的；官方场合的

examples.en: an official function/reception
examples.zh: 官方活动／招待会

examples.en: The official opening is planned for October.
examples.zh: 正式开幕拟在十月。

senses.def: that is told to the public but may not be true
senses.zh: 公开的；公布的；据官方的

examples.en: I only knew the official version of events.
examples.zh: 我对事情的了解仅限于官方的版本。

examples.en: The official line is that the date for the election has not yet been decided.
examples.zh: 官方的说法是选举日期尚未确定。

examples.en: The official story has always been that they are just good friends.
examples.zh: 官方一直说他们只不过是好朋友。

senses.def: used to announce publicly something that you think is obvious or that everyone already knows
senses.zh: 官方：用于公开宣布你认为显而易见的或每个人都已经知道的事情

examples.en: It's official: this is the worst zombie film ever.
examples.zh: 官方消息：这是有史以来最糟糕的僵尸电影。

senses.def: a person who is in a position of authority in a large organization

examples.en: She is the government official in charge of the project.
examples.zh: 她是负责该项目的政府官员。

examples.en: a senior official in the State Department
examples.zh: 国务院的高级官员

examples.en: a bank/company/court official
examples.zh: 银行／公司／法院要员

examples.en: The newspaper quoted an unnamed FBI official as saying:…
examples.zh: 该报援引一位不愿透露姓名的联邦调查局官员的话称：……

examples.en: This is still one of its top sellers, according to company officials.
examples.zh: 据公司官员称，这仍然是其最畅销的产品之一。

senses.def: used to announce publicly something that you think is obvious or that everyone already knows
senses.zh: 官方：用于公开宣布你认为显而易见的或每个人都已经知道的事情

examples.en: It's official: this is the worst zombie film ever.
examples.zh: 官方消息：这是有史以来最糟糕的僵尸电影。

senses.def: a person who is chosen by a court to be in charge of a company that is bankrupt
senses.zh: （破产公司的）财产管理人，官方接管人

senses.def: (in the UK) a piece of information known only to the government and some of its employees, which it is illegal for them to tell anyone under the Official Secrets Act
senses.zh: 公务秘密（“公务秘密法”禁止政府工作人员泄露的信息）

senses.def: people who are in positions of authority in large organizations when they seem to be more interested in following rules than in being helpful

examples.en: The report is critical of attempts by officialdom to deal with the problem of homelessness.
examples.zh: 报告对处理无家可归者问题上的官僚作风提出批评。

senses.def: language used in official documents that is thought by many people to be too complicated and difficult to understand
senses.zh: 公文体（复杂而难以理解）

senses.def: publicly and by somebody who is in a position of authority

examples.en: The library will be officially opened by the local MP.
examples.zh: 图书馆将由当地下院议员正式揭幕。

examples.en: We haven't yet been told officially about the closure.
examples.zh: 我们尚未接到关闭的正式通知。

examples.en: The college is not an officially recognized English language school.
examples.zh: 那所学院不是官方认可的英语学校。

senses.def: according to a particular set of rules, laws, etc.

examples.en: Many of those living on the streets are not officially homeless.
examples.zh: 根据法律定义，许多流浪街头的人并非无家可归者。

examples.en: I'm not officially supposed to be here.
examples.zh: 按公事说，我是不该到这里来的。

senses.def: according to information that has been told to the public but that may not be true

examples.en: Officially, he resigned because of bad health.
examples.zh: 据官方说法，他是因健康状况不佳而辞职的。

senses.def: to act as an official in charge of something, especially a sports event
senses.zh: 主持（工作）；（尤指体育比赛）担任裁判

examples.en: A referee from a neutral country will officiate (at) the game.
examples.zh: 一名来自中立国的裁判将担任这场比赛的裁判。

senses.def: to do the official duties at a public or religious ceremony

examples.en: He baptized children and officiated at weddings.
examples.zh: 他给孩子们施洗礼, 也主持婚礼。

senses.def: too ready to tell people what to do or to use the power you have to give orders
senses.zh: 爱指手画脚的；爱发号施令的

examples.en: an officious traffic warden
examples.zh: 一位热心的交通督导员

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are too ready to tell people what to do or to use the power you have to give orders
senses.zh: 爱指手画脚的；爱发号施令的

examples.en: ‘You can't park here,’ he said officiously.
examples.zh: “此处不准停车。”他装腔作势地说。

senses.def: the fact of being too ready to tell people what to do or to use the power you have to give orders
senses.zh: 爱指手画脚的；爱发号施令的

senses.def: not directly controlled by or connected to a computer or to the internet
senses.zh: 未联机的；未连线的；脱机的；离线的

examples.en: For offline orders, call this number.
examples.zh: 离线订货请拨打这个号码。

senses.def: to talk about something on a later occasion, perhaps because it does not interest the other people who are present at a meeting
senses.zh: 以后再谈（可能因会议上其他人对该话题不感兴趣）

examples.en: Could you two take that offline so we can move onto the other items on the agenda?
examples.zh: 你们二位以后再谈这个话题好吗？这样我们就可以继续讨论议程上的其他事项了。

senses.def: without being directly controlled by or connected to a computer or to the internet
senses.zh: 未联机的；未连线的；脱机的；离线的

examples.en: How do I write an email offline?
examples.zh: 我如何在离线时写电子邮件？

senses.def: to talk about something on a later occasion, perhaps because it does not interest the other people who are present at a meeting

senses.zh: 奥利弗·克伦威尔（Oliver Cromwell）：（1599-1658）是一位英国将军和政治家，曾短暂统治过英格兰，苏格兰和爱尔兰。克伦威尔（Cromwell）是一位清教徒，他的政治生涯是1628年开始担任亨廷登议会议员的。他在1642年英国内战爆发时，他召集了当地士兵为议会而战，并很快成为新模式军和英国最伟大的士兵。他是1649年签署查理一世国王死刑令的人之一。作为英联邦的领导人，他负责对那些反对爱尔兰和苏格兰清教徒的人进行残酷对待。1653年，克伦威尔（Cromwell）罢免了议会，成为英格兰，苏格兰和爱尔兰的主要保护者，其权力几乎与国王相同。他得到了王冠，但拒绝了。在1658年，他死于疟疾，被葬在威斯敏斯特大教堂。克伦威尔（Cromwell）的儿子理查德（Richard）死后不久，就担任保卫勋爵（Lord Protector）的职位，但他没有父亲的恩赐作领导者。1660年，查理二世（Charles II）成为国王。奥利弗·克伦威尔（Oliver Cromwell）的尸体被挖了，他的头被放在威斯敏斯特（Westminster）一栋建筑物的屋顶上的一根杆子上，长达24年。克伦威尔（Cromwell）还因他对画家彼得·利利（Peter Lely）（1618-80）的著名讲话而被人们铭记。人们常常说某物或某人应该被显示出疣和所有东西，这意味着不应排除缺陷或不愉快的特征。奥利弗·克伦威尔（Oliver Cromwell）的尸体被挖了，他的头被放在威斯敏斯特（Westminster）一栋建筑物的屋顶上的一根杆子上，长达24年。克伦威尔（Cromwell）还因他对画家彼得·利利（Peter Lely）（1618-80）的著名讲话而被人们铭记。人们常常说某物或某人应该被显示出疣和所有东西，这意味着不应排除缺陷或不愉快的特征。奥利弗·克伦威尔（Oliver Cromwell）的尸体被挖了，他的头被放在威斯敏斯特（Westminster）一栋建筑物的屋顶上的一根杆子上，长达24年。克伦威尔（Cromwell）还因他对画家彼得·利利（Peter Lely）（1618-80）的著名讲话而被人们铭记。人们常常说某物或某人应该被显示出疣和所有东西，这意味着不应排除缺陷或不愉快的特征。

senses.zh: 奥利弗·萨克斯（Oliver Sacks）：（1933-2015）一位英国神经病学家（研究神经及其疾病的医生），他写了许多有关异常精神状况的书。他从1960年起居住在纽约，在那里担任神经病学教授。他与罗宾·威廉姆斯（Robin Williams）合作拍摄的关于“昏睡病”的书籍《觉醒》（Awakenings，1973年）成为1990年的电影。他的其他著作包括《戴帽子的妻子犯错的男人》（1985）和《火星人类学》（1995）。

senses.def: a novel (1838) by Charles Dickens
senses.zh: 《奥利弗·特威斯：一本小说》（1838年），由查尔斯·狄更斯（Charles Dickens）撰写，以对伦敦贫困地区和罪犯的真实描述而著称。奥利弗（Oliver）是一个贫穷的孤儿，他逃往伦敦。在那里，他加入了一群罪犯，包括法金（Fagin），狡猾的道奇（Artful Dodger）和比尔·西克斯（Bill Sikes），他们试图将他变成小偷。他由好人布朗洛先生救出，但被罪犯再次抓获。西克斯的女友南希（Nancy）试图帮助奥利弗（Oliver），并被西克斯（Sikes）杀死，西克斯在试图逃离警察时死亡。罪犯全部被捕，奥利弗与布朗洛先生住在一起。它是狄更斯最著名的书之一，并已成功地制作成电影和音乐剧《奥利弗！》（1960）。

senses.def: (1809-94) a US doctor and writer of stories and poems. In 1857, they began to be published in The Atlantic
senses.zh: 奥利弗·温德尔·福尔摩斯（Oliver Wendell Holmes）：（1809-94）是一位美国医生，也是故事和诗歌的作家。1857年，它们开始在《大西洋》杂志上出版，后来他著名的“早餐桌”对话被收录在几本书中。他的诗有《鹦鹉螺的房间》和《老铁边》。福尔摩斯还在哈佛大学（1847-82）教授医学。霍姆斯的儿子奥利弗·温德尔·霍姆斯（Oliver Wendell Holmes Junior）（1841-1935年）成为美国最高法院（1902-32年）最明智，最受尊敬的法官之一。

examples.zh: 你发誓你从未见过这个人。

senses.zh: 违则受到某种惩罚；违则以…论处

examples.en: They were required to cut pollution levels, on pain of a £10 000 fine if they disobeyed.
examples.zh: 他们被要求降低污染水平，违则罚款 1 万英镑。

masturbation
