senses.def: used to describe the situation that exists in the world now, rather than in the past or the future

examples.en: present-day fashions
examples.zh: 当今时尚

examples.en: present-day America
examples.zh: 当代美国

senses.def: the form of the verb that in English ends in -ing
looking clean and attractive and suitable to be seen in public

examples.en: I must go and make myself presentable before the guests arrive.
examples.zh: 趁客人还没到，我得去打扮一下好见人。

examples.en: I’ve got nothing presentable to wear.
examples.zh: 我没有什么像样的衣服可以穿。

examples.en: She was not exactly good-looking, but perfectly presentable.
examples.zh: 她并不是很漂亮，但是绝对上得了台面。

senses.def: acceptable

examples.en: You're going to have to do a lot more work on this essay before it's presentable.
examples.zh: 你的这篇文章还得多加润饰才能交得出手。

senses.def: a meeting at which something, especially a new product or idea, or piece of work, is shown to a group of people

examples.en: The sales manager will give a presentation on the new products.
examples.zh: 营销经理将举行一次新产品推介会。

examples.en: Several speakers will be making short presentations.
examples.zh: 几位演讲者将做简短的演讲。

examples.en: The conference will begin with a keynote presentation by a leading industry figure.
examples.zh: 本次会议开始时将由企业界的一位领军人物发表主旨讲话。

examples.en: a slide/video/multimedia presentation
examples.zh: 幻灯片/视频/多媒体演示

senses.def: the act of showing something or of giving something to somebody

examples.en: The trial was adjourned following the presentation of new evidence to the court.
examples.zh: 新证据呈到庭上后，审讯就宣告暂停。

examples.en: The presentation of prizes began after the speeches.
examples.zh: 讲话结束后就开始颁奖了。

examples.en: The Mayor will make the presentation (= hand over the gift) herself.
examples.zh: 市长将亲自颁发礼品。

examples.en: Members will be admitted on presentation of a membership card.
examples.zh: 会员出示会员证便可入场。

examples.en: a presentation copy (= a free book given by the author or publisher)
examples.zh: （出版者或作者免费提供的）赠阅本.

examples.en: a presentation ceremony/evening
examples.zh: 颁奖典礼/晚会

senses.def: the way in which something is offered, shown, explained, etc. to others
senses.zh: 提出（或展示、解释等）的方式

examples.en: Improving the product's presentation (= the way it is wrapped, advertised, etc.) should increase sales.
examples.zh: 改进产品的包装形式会提高销售量。

examples.en: I admire the clear, logical presentation of her arguments.
examples.zh: 我很欣赏她的论证，言辞清晰且有条理。

examples.en: The main emphasis of the training will be on presentation skills.
examples.zh: 培训将会首重演讲技巧。

senses.def: the series of computer slides (= images)

examples.en: I've put my presentation on a memory stick.
examples.zh: 我已经把我的幻灯片演示文件存在 U 盘里了。

senses.def: a ceremony or formal occasion during which a gift or prize is given

examples.en: the school's annual presentation evening
examples.zh: 学校一年一度的颁奖晚会

senses.def: a performance of a play, etc. in a theatre
the position in which a baby is lying in the mother’s body just before birth
connected with the act of showing, explaining or offering something to other people, especially a new product, a policy or a performance
senses.zh: 展示的；介绍的；提交的；表演的

examples.en: a course on developing presentational skills
examples.zh: 展示技巧训练课程

senses.def: the practice of spending more time at your work than you need to according to your contract, in order to appear to be working hard
a person who introduces the different sections of a radio or television programme

examples.en: a TV presenter
examples.zh: 电视节目主持人

examples.en: a BBC sports presenter
examples.zh: 英国广播公司体育节目主持人

examples.en: one of the presenters of Radio 4's 'Today' programme
examples.zh: 第四广播电台“Today”节目的主持人之一

senses.def: a person who makes a speech or talks to an audience about a particular subject

examples.en: conference presenters
examples.zh: 会议发言人

senses.def: a person who gives somebody a prize at a ceremony
a feeling that something is going to happen, especially something unpleasant

examples.en: a presentiment of disaster
examples.zh: 大难临头的预感

senses.def: at the time you are speaking or writing; now

examples.en: The crime is presently being investigated by the police.
examples.zh: 警方目前正在调查这起案件。

examples.en: These are the courses presently available.
examples.zh: 这些就是现有的课程。

senses.def: used to show that something happened after a short time

examples.en: Presently, the door opened again and three men stepped out.
examples.zh: 不久，门又打开了，走出来三个人。

senses.def: used to show that something will happen soon

examples.en: She'll be here presently.
examples.zh: 她马上就会到这儿。

senses.def: the act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition

examples.en: building/environmental/food preservation
examples.zh: 建筑物的维护；环境保护；食物的保存

examples.en: a preservation group/society
examples.zh: 环保团体

senses.def: the act of making sure that something is kept

examples.en: The central issue in the strike was the preservation of jobs.
examples.zh: 罢工的核心问题是工作职位的保留。

senses.def: the degree to which something has not been changed or damaged by age, weather, etc.
senses.zh: 保存的状况；保养的程度

examples.en: The paintings were in an excellent state of preservation.
examples.zh: 这些绘画保存得非常好。

senses.def: (in the UK) a document that makes it illegal to change or destroy a building, a tree or part of the countryside, because of its beauty or historical interest

examples.en: The council has placed a preservation order on the building.
examples.zh: 地方议会颁布了对这座建筑的保护令。

senses.def: a person who works to keep old buildings or areas of the countryside in their original condition and to prevent them from being destroyed
senses.zh: 文物保护者；环境保护者

senses.def: preventing food or wood from decaying

examples.en: the preservative effects of freezing
examples.zh: 冷冻的防腐保护作用。

senses.def: a substance used to prevent food or wood from decaying

examples.en: The juice contains no artificial preservatives.
examples.zh: 这种果汁不含人工防腐剂。

examples.en: (a) wood preservative
examples.zh: 木材防腐剂

senses.def: to keep a particular quality, feature, etc.; to make sure that something is kept

examples.en: He was anxious to preserve his reputation.
examples.zh: 他急于维护自己的名声。

examples.en: Efforts to preserve the peace have failed.
examples.zh: 维护和平的努力失败了。

examples.en: She managed to preserve her sense of humour under very trying circumstances.
examples.zh: 她在艰难的环境下依然不失幽默感。

examples.en: He was insistent on preserving the integrity of the brand.
examples.zh: 他坚持维护品牌的完整性。

senses.def: to keep something in its original state in good condition

examples.en: a perfectly preserved 14th-century house
examples.zh: 保存完好的 14 世纪宅第

examples.en: Is he really 60? He's remarkably well preserved.
examples.zh: 他真有 60 岁了吗？他真会保养啊。

examples.en: We need knowledgeable gallery curators to preserve great masterpieces for posterity.
examples.zh: 我们需要知识渊博的画廊策展人来为子孙后代保存伟大的杰作。

examples.en: This vase has been preserved intact.
examples.zh: 这个花瓶保存得完好无损。

senses.def: to prevent something, especially food, from decaying

examples.en: Wax polish preserves wood and leather.
examples.zh: 上光蜡可保护木材和皮革。

examples.en: preserved lemons
examples.zh: 柠檬罐头

examples.en: olives preserved in brine
examples.zh: 盐水橄榄

examples.en: an attempt to preserve the corpse from decomposition
examples.zh: 保存尸体使其免于腐烂的尝试

senses.def: to keep somebody/something alive, or safe from harm or danger

examples.en: The society was set up to preserve endangered species from extinction.
examples.zh: 成立这个协会是为了保护濒危物种不致灭绝。

senses.def: an activity, a job, an interest, etc. that is thought to be suitable for one particular person or group of people
senses.zh: （某人或群体活动、工作等的）专门领域

examples.en: Football is no longer the preserve of men.
examples.zh: 足球再也不是男人的专利了。

examples.en: I began my career in the days when nursing was a female preserve.
examples.zh: 我开始工作的时候，护理工作是女性专属的领域。

examples.en: Higher education is no longer the preserve of the wealthy.
examples.zh: 高等教育再也不是富人的专利了。

senses.def: a type of jam made by boiling fruit with a large amount of sugar
a type of pickle
a piece of land that is a protected area for animals, plants, etc.
an area of private land or water where animals and fish are kept for people to hunt

examples.en: He bought a 171-acre hunting preserve in upstate New York.
examples.zh: 他在纽约州北部购买了一块 171 英亩的狩猎保护区。

senses.def: a person who makes sure that a particular situation does not change

examples.en: The police are the preservers of law and order.
examples.zh: 警察负责维持治安。

senses.def: a substance used to prevent wood from decaying
to set the controls of a piece of electrical equipment so that it will start to work at a particular time

examples.en: You can preset the radiators to come on when you need them to.
examples.zh: 你可以预先调好暖气，使它在你需要的时候启动。

examples.en: to preset TV channels/radio stations (= to set the controls so that particular channels are selected when you press particular buttons)
examples.zh: 预调电视频道／广播电台

senses.def: to decide something in advance

examples.en: They kept to the preset route.
examples.zh: 他们沿着事先规划的路线前进。

senses.def: to lead or be in charge of a meeting, ceremony, etc.
senses.zh: 主持（会议、仪式等）；担任（会议）主席

examples.en: the presiding judge
examples.zh: 首席法官

examples.en: They asked if I would preside at the committee meeting.
examples.zh: 他们问我是否会主持委员会会议。

examples.en: The party presided over one of the worst economic declines in the country's history (= it was in power when the decline happened).
examples.zh: 该党执政时期，国家经历了历史上最严重的经济衰退。

senses.def: the job of being president of a country or an organization; the period of time somebody holds this job
senses.zh: 总统（或主席）的职位；总统（或主席）任期

examples.en: the current holder of the EU presidency
examples.zh: 现任欧盟主席

examples.en: She hopes to be the first woman elected to the presidency of the United States.
examples.zh: 她希望成为第一位当选美国总统的女性。

examples.en: He was a White House official during the Biden presidency.
examples.zh: 他在拜登担任总统期间担任白宫官员。

senses.def: the leader of a republic

examples.en: Several presidents attended the funeral.
examples.zh: 好几位总统参加了葬礼。

examples.en: the President of the United States
examples.zh: 美国总统

examples.en: President Biden visited the country twice.
examples.zh: 拜登总统两次访问该国。

examples.en: Do you have any comment, Mr President?
examples.zh: 总统先生，您有何评论？

examples.en: France elected a new president in 2017.
examples.zh: 2017年，法国选出了新总统。

examples.en: Ford became president following Nixon's resignation.
examples.zh: 尼克松辞职后，福特成为总统。

examples.en: She should run for president.
examples.zh: 她应该竞选总统。

examples.en: the former South African president, Nelson Mandela
examples.zh: 南非前总统纳尔逊·曼德拉

examples.en: He was sworn in as President on August 31.
examples.zh: 他于 8 月 31 日宣誓就职总统。

senses.def: the person in charge of some organizations, clubs, colleges, etc.
senses.zh: （机构、俱乐部、学院等的）会长，院长，主席

examples.en: to be made president of the students’ union
examples.zh: 当选学生会主席

examples.en: She travels extensively in her role as President of the World Wide Fund for Nature.
examples.zh: 作为世界自然基金会主席，她经常出差。

senses.def: the person in charge of a bank or a commercial organization
senses.zh: 银行行长；总经理；董事长；总裁

examples.en: the bank president
examples.zh: 银行行长

examples.en: the president of Columbia Pictures
examples.zh: 哥伦比亚影业公司董事长

senses.def: a person who has been elected to be president but who has not yet begun the job
connected with the position or activities of a president

examples.en: a presidential campaign/candidate/election
examples.zh: 总统竞选活动／候选人／选举

examples.en: a presidential system of government
examples.zh: 总统制政体

examples.en: a presidential year (= one in which the people vote for the next president of the country)
examples.zh: 总统选举年。

senses.def: a medal
senses.zh: 总统自由勋章（美国和平时期授予个人的最高奖章）

senses.def: (in the US) a legal holiday on the third Monday in February, in memory of the birthdays of George Washington and Abraham Lincoln
senses.zh: 总统日（美国法定假日，二月的第三个星期一，纪念美国总统乔治 · 华盛顿和亚伯拉罕 · 林肯的诞辰）

senses.def: an official in charge of a polling station

examples.en: Voters should report any irregularities to the presiding officer.
examples.zh: 投票人如发现违规行为，都应告知投票站主任。

senses.def: a permanent committee that makes important decisions as part of a government or large political organization, especially in communist
senses.zh: （尤指共产主义国家的）常务委员会，主席团

senses.def: newspapers and magazines
senses.zh: 报章杂志；报刊；平面媒体

examples.en: the local/national/foreign press
examples.zh: 地方／全国／外国报刊

examples.en: the popular/tabloid press (= newspapers with a lot of pictures and stories about famous people)
examples.zh: 通俗报刊；小报

examples.en: the music/sporting press (= newspapers and magazines about music/sport)
examples.zh: 音乐／体育报刊

examples.en: The mainstream press is/are ignoring this story.
examples.zh: 主流媒体正在忽略这个故事。

examples.en: Unlike the American, the British press operates on a national scale.
examples.zh: 与美国不同，英国报刊都是行销全国的。

examples.en: The case has been widely reported in the press.
examples.zh: 报刊广泛报道了这个案件。

examples.en: the freedom of the Press/press freedom (= the freedom to report any events and express opinions)
examples.zh: 新闻自由

examples.en: The event is bound to attract wide press coverage (= it will be written about in many newspapers).
examples.zh: 肯定会有很多报刊报道这件事。

examples.en: According to French press reports, three people have been killed.
examples.zh: 据法国媒体报道，已有三人死亡。

examples.en: a White House press briefing
examples.zh: 白宫新闻发布会

senses.def: the journalists and photographers who work for newspapers and magazines
senses.zh: 记者；新闻工作者；新闻界

examples.en: The Press was/were not allowed to attend the trial.
examples.zh: 庭审谢绝新闻采访。

examples.en: She has been harassed by the press, who desperately need a story.
examples.zh: 她受到了新闻界的骚扰，因为记者迫切想追到新闻。

examples.en: He told the press that there had been ‘further progress’.
examples.zh: 他告诉媒体，已经取得了“进一步进展”。

examples.en: She told them not to talk to the press.
examples.zh: 她告诉他们不要与媒体交谈。

senses.def: the type or amount of reports that newspapers write about somebody/something

examples.en: The airline has had a bad press recently (= journalists have written unpleasant things about it).
examples.zh: 这家航空公司最近受到新闻界的责难。

examples.en: The demonstration got very little press.
examples.zh: 新闻媒体对这次示威游行报道很少。

examples.en: His latest novel didn't get (a) very good press (= was not praised in the media).
examples.zh: 他新出版的小说没有得到新闻界的好评。

senses.def: a machine for printing books, newspapers, etc.; the process of printing them

examples.en: We were able to watch the books rolling off the presses.
examples.zh: 我们可以看到书本从印刷机上源源不断地印出。

examples.en: These prices are correct at the time of going to press.
examples.zh: 这些价格在付印时是准确无误的。

examples.en: a story that is hot off the press (= has just appeared in the newspapers)
examples.zh: 刚刚见报的新闻报道

senses.def: a business that prints and publishes books

examples.en: Oxford University Press
examples.zh: 牛津大学出版社

senses.def: a piece of equipment that is used for creating pressure on things, to make them flat or to get liquid from them

examples.en: a trouser press
examples.zh: 烫裤机

examples.en: an olive press
examples.zh: 橄榄压榨机

senses.group: equipment for pressing 挤压设备

senses.def: an act of pushing something with your hand or with a tool that you are holding

examples.en: He gave the bell another press.
examples.zh: 他又按了一下铃。

examples.en: Those shirts need a press (= with an iron).
examples.zh: 这些衬衣需要熨一熨。

senses.def: a large number of people or things competing for space or movement
senses.zh: 拥挤的人群（或大批事物）

examples.en: the press of bodies all moving the same way
examples.zh: 拥向同一方向的人群

examples.en: Among the press of cars he glimpsed a taxi.
examples.zh: 在拥挤的汽车中，他瞥见了一辆出租车。

senses.def: a large cupboard, usually with shelves, for holding clothes, books, etc.
to push part of a device, etc. in order to make it work

examples.en: to press a button/key
examples.zh: 按下按钮／按键

examples.en: He pressed the lid firmly shut.
examples.zh: 他把盖子盖得紧紧的。

examples.en: Press here to open.
examples.zh: 请按此处打开。

examples.en: She pressed down hard on the gas pedal.
examples.zh: 她用力踩下油门踏板。

senses.def: to push something closely against something; to be pushed in this way

examples.en: She pressed her face against the window.
examples.zh: 她把脸贴在窗子上。

examples.en: He pressed a handkerchief to his nose.
examples.zh: 他用手绢捂住鼻子。

examples.en: She pressed her lips together.
examples.zh: 她紧抿着双唇。

examples.en: Her lips softly pressed my cheek.
examples.zh: 她的双唇柔和地贴在我脸颊上。

examples.en: His body was pressing against hers.
examples.zh: 他的身体紧贴着她。

examples.en: She pressed down harder on the paper.
examples.zh: 她更加用力地按在纸上。

senses.def: to put something in a place by pushing it

examples.en: He pressed a coin into her hand and moved on.
examples.zh: 他把一枚硬币塞进她手里，然后继续向前走。

examples.en: She pressed a finger into the dough.
examples.zh: 她把一根手指按进面团里。

senses.def: to put gentle pressure on somebody’s hand or arm, especially to show care or kind feelings
senses.zh: 握，轻捏（某人的手或臂，以示关心或友好）

examples.en: He gently pressed her arm, then left.
examples.zh: 他轻轻按住她的手臂，然后就离开了。

senses.def: to move in the direction mentioned by pushing

examples.en: The photographers pressed around the royal visitors.
examples.zh: 摄影记者们在王室贵宾周围挤来挤去。

examples.en: A host of unwelcome thoughts were pressing in on him.
examples.zh: 一大堆恼人的心事涌上他的心头。

examples.en: The crowd pressed forward.
examples.zh: 人群向前挤。

senses.def: to make strong efforts to persuade or force somebody to do something

examples.en: If pressed, he will admit that he knew about the affair.
examples.zh: 如果逼问他，他就会承认对此事知情。

examples.en: The bank is pressing us for repayment of the loan.
examples.zh: 银行正在催我们偿还贷款。

examples.en: They are pressing us to make a quick decision.
examples.zh: 他们正催促我们尽快做决定。

examples.en: Don't let yourself be pressed into doing something you don't like.
examples.zh: 不要勉强自己做不喜欢的事情。

examples.en: I did not press him further on the issue.
examples.zh: 我没有在这一问题上再逼他。

examples.en: ‘Are you sure?’ she pressed gently.
examples.zh: “你能确定吗？”她温和地追问。

senses.def: to express or repeat something with force

examples.en: I don't want to press the point, but you do owe me $200.
examples.zh: 我不想老提这一点，但你确实欠我 200 美元。

examples.en: She is still pressing her claim for compensation.
examples.zh: 她仍然坚持索赔。

examples.en: They were determined to press their case at the highest level.
examples.zh: 他们决心把事情闹到最高层。

senses.def: to make something flat or smooth by using force or putting something heavy on top

examples.en: The easiest way to press flowers is between the pages of a book.
examples.zh: 压花最简单的方法是在书页之间压花。

examples.en: Press the soil flat with the back of a spade.
examples.zh: 用铁锹背把土拍平。

senses.def: to make clothes smooth using a hot iron

examples.en: My suit needs pressing.
examples.zh: 我的西服该熨了。

examples.en: his immaculately pressed suit
examples.zh: 他的熨烫得笔挺的西装

senses.def: to get the juice out of fruit or vegetables by using force or weight
to make something from a material, using pressure

examples.en: to press a CD
examples.zh: 压制一张光盘

examples.en: The car bodies are pressed out of sheets of metal.
examples.zh: 汽车车身是用钣金压制成的。

senses.def: to accuse somebody formally of a crime so that there can be a trial in court

examples.en: Police have brought a charge of dangerous driving against the man.
examples.zh: 警方以危险驾驶罪控告那名男子。

examples.en: Many victims of crime are reluctant to press charges against their attackers.
examples.zh: 许多罪案的受害者不愿意指控侵害他们的人。

examples.en: She laid charges against the firm for not complying with the regulations.
examples.zh: 她指控该公司不遵守规定。

senses.def: to do exactly the right things to please somebody
senses.zh: 投其所好；迎合众人／某人的喜好

examples.en: a new satirical comedy show that presses all the right buttons
examples.zh: 一部按下所有正确按钮的新讽刺喜剧节目

senses.def: to say hello to people by shaking hands
to get as much advantage as possible from a situation by attacking or arguing in a determined way

examples.en: to press home an attack/an argument/a point
examples.zh: 把进攻／论证／论点坚持到底

examples.en: Simon saw she was hesitating and pressed home his advantage.
examples.zh: 西蒙见她犹豫不决，便趁机占尽优势。

senses.def: to use somebody/something for a purpose that they were not trained or intended for because there is nobody or nothing else available

examples.en: Every type of boat was pressed into service to rescue passengers from the sinking ferry.
examples.zh: 为了营救正在下沉的渡轮上的旅客，各类船只都被临时征用了。

senses.def: to react in a sudden or extreme way to something unexpected that has frightened you
senses.zh: 惊慌失措；仓促行事；采取紧急行动

examples.en: The prime minister pressed the panic button yesterday as Britain’s economy plunged deeper into crisis.
examples.zh: 随着英国经济进一步陷入危机，首相昨天按下了恐慌按钮。

senses.def: to push the reset button

examples.en: When the game is over, press reset to start a new game.
examples.zh: 游戏结束后，按重置键开始新游戏。

senses.def: to make an important change in your life, career, etc. by starting again with a fresh approach

examples.en: Working from home during Covid gave many people a chance to press reset and make changes in their lives.
examples.zh: 新冠疫情期间居家工作使许多人有机会重新开始，改变自己的生活。

examples.en: Police have brought a charge of dangerous driving against the man.
examples.zh: 警方以危险驾驶罪控告那名男子。

examples.en: Many victims of crime are reluctant to press charges against their attackers.

senses.def: to say hello to people by shaking hands
to do exactly the right things to please somebody
senses.zh: 投其所好；迎合众人／某人的喜好

examples.en: a new satirical comedy show that presses all the right buttons
examples.zh: 一部按下所有正确按钮的新讽刺喜剧节目

senses.def: to push the reset button

examples.en: When the game is over, press reset to start a new game.
examples.zh: 游戏结束后，按重置键开始新游戏。

senses.def: to make an important change in your life, career, etc. by starting again with a fresh approach

examples.en: Working from home during Covid gave many people a chance to press reset and make changes in their lives.
examples.zh: 新冠疫情期间居家工作使许多人有机会重新开始，改变自己的生活。

senses.def: to use somebody/something for a purpose that they were not trained or intended for because there is nobody or nothing else available

examples.en: Every type of boat was pressed into service to rescue passengers from the sinking ferry.
examples.zh: 为了营救正在下沉的渡轮上的旅客，各类船只都被临时征用了。

senses.def: to get as much advantage as possible from a situation by attacking or arguing in a determined way

examples.en: to press home an attack/an argument/a point
examples.zh: 把进攻／论证／论点坚持到底

examples.en: Simon saw she was hesitating and pressed home his advantage.
examples.zh: 西蒙见她犹豫不决，便趁机占尽优势。

senses.def: an organization that collects news and supplies it to newspapers and television and radio companies
a person whose job is to supply information and advertising material about a particular actor, musician, theatre, etc. to newspapers, radio or television
senses.zh: （剧团等雇用的）广告宣传人员

senses.def: to continue doing something in a determined way; to hurry forward
senses.zh: 坚决继续进行；匆忙前进；加紧

examples.en: The company is pressing ahead with its plans for a new warehouse.
examples.zh: 这家公司正加紧推动设置新仓库的计划。

examples.en: ‘Shall we stay here for the night?’ ‘No, let's press on.’
examples.zh: “我们今晚在这里住下好吗？”“不，咱们继续走。”

senses.def: to continue doing something in a determined way; to hurry forward
senses.zh: 坚决继续进行；匆忙前进；加紧

examples.en: ‘Shall we stay here for the night?’ ‘No, let's press on.’
examples.zh: “我们今晚在这里住下好吗？”“不，咱们继续走。”

examples.en: The company is pressing ahead with its plans for a new warehouse.
examples.zh: 这家公司正加紧推动设置新仓库的计划。

senses.def: a special area or a room at a sports ground where sports journalists sit
senses.zh: （体育场的）新闻工作室，记者席

examples.en: We got to sit in the press box since my dad would be writing about the game.
examples.zh: 因为我爸爸要写比赛的情况，我们得坐在记者席上。

senses.def: a meeting at which somebody talks to a group of journalists in order to answer their questions or to make an official statement
senses.zh: 记者招待会；新闻发布会

examples.en: to hold/give a press conference
examples.zh: 举行／召开记者招待会

examples.en: The police called a press conference to appeal for witnesses.
examples.zh: 警方召开新闻发布会呼吁目击者提供线索。

senses.def: a group of journalists who work in or go to a particular place to report on an event

examples.en: The press corps had assembled for the morning news conference.
examples.zh: 记者团已聚集在一起参加上午的新闻发布会。

examples.en: the UN press corps
examples.zh: 联合国记者团

examples.en: The spokesman addressed an international press corps.
examples.zh: 这位发言人对国际记者团发表了谈话。

senses.def: an article or a story that you cut from a newspaper or magazine and keep

examples.en: He kept a scrapbook containing press cuttings of his concerts.
examples.zh: 他保存着一本自己音乐会的剪报簿。

senses.def: to keep asking for something

examples.en: They continued to press for a change in the law.
examples.zh: 他们不断要求修改这项法律。

senses.def: an area in a parliament building or a court for journalists to sit in
a group of people who were employed in the past to force men to join the army or navy
senses.zh: 抓丁团，拉夫队（旧时受雇抓人当兵）

senses.def: to force somebody to do something that they do not want to do
senses.zh: 迫使自己，勉强别人（做某事）

senses.def: the office of a large organization, political party or government department that answers questions from journalists and provides them with information
senses.zh: （组织、政党或政府的）新闻办公室

examples.en: The Buckingham Palace press office has denied rumours of another royal divorce.
examples.zh: 白金汉宫新闻办公室否认了王室再次离婚的传言。

examples.en: The company's press office did not return the call.
examples.zh: 该公司的新闻办公室没有回电话。

senses.def: a person who is in charge of or works for a press office
senses.zh: 新闻发言人；新闻发布官；新闻局长

senses.def: to continue doing something in a determined way; to hurry forward
senses.zh: 坚决继续进行；匆忙前进；加紧

examples.en: The company is pressing ahead with its plans for a new warehouse.
examples.zh: 这家公司正加紧推动设置新仓库的计划。

examples.en: ‘Shall we stay here for the night?’ ‘No, let's press on.’
examples.zh: “我们今晚在这里住下好吗？”“不，咱们继续走。”

senses.def: to try to make somebody accept something, especially food or drink, although they may not want it
senses.zh: 勉强某人接受；强迫某人吃（或喝）

examples.en: She kept pressing cake on us.
examples.zh: 她非要我们吃蛋糕不可。

senses.def: to continue doing something in a determined way; to hurry forward
senses.zh: 坚决继续进行；匆忙前进；加紧

examples.en: ‘Shall we stay here for the night?’ ‘No, let's press on.’
examples.zh: “我们今晚在这里住下好吗？”“不，咱们继续走。”

examples.en: The company is pressing ahead with its plans for a new warehouse.
examples.zh: 这家公司正加紧推动设置新仓库的计划。

senses.def: an official statement made to journalists by a large organization, a political party or a government department

examples.en: The company issued a press release to end speculation about its future.
examples.zh: 这家公司发布了新闻稿以结束外界对其前途的猜测。

senses.def: a person who works for a politician or a political organization and gives information about them to journalists, the newspapers, etc.
a type of button used for fastening clothes, consisting of two metal or plastic sections that can be pressed together
an exercise in which you lie on your stomach and raise your body off the ground by pressing down on your hands until your arms are straight

examples.en: He does 20 press-ups every morning before breakfast.
examples.zh: 他每天早上早餐前都会做 20 个俯卧撑。

senses.def: to react in a sudden or extreme way to something unexpected that has frightened you
senses.zh: 惊慌失措；仓促行事；采取紧急行动

examples.en: The prime minister pressed the panic button yesterday as Britain’s economy plunged deeper into crisis.
examples.zh: 随着英国经济进一步陷入危机，首相昨天按下了恐慌按钮。

senses.def: a present that you give somebody, for example for their birthday
a journalist
the act of trying to persuade or to force somebody to do something

examples.en: The pressure for change continued to mount.
examples.zh: 改革的呼声越来越高。

examples.en: We are determined to keep up the pressure on the other member states.
examples.zh: 我们决心继续向其他成员国施加压力。

examples.en: There is intense pressure on her to resign.
examples.zh: 要求她辞职的呼声非常高。

examples.en: In every society there is strong pressure to conform.
examples.zh: 每个社会都存在着巨大的顺应压力。

examples.en: Do you feel any pressure to dress in a certain way?
examples.zh: 您对以某种方式着装感到有压力吗？

examples.en: We must bring pressure to bear on our government to reverse this decision.
examples.zh: 我们必须向政府施压，使其撤回这个决定。

examples.en: The company is facing increasing pressure from shareholders
examples.zh: 公司面临股东压力越来越大

examples.en: The government eventually bowed to popular pressure (= they agreed to do what people were trying to get them to do).
examples.zh: 政府最终向群众的压力低头。

senses.def: difficulties and worries that are caused by the need to achieve or to behave in a particular way

examples.en: You need to be able to handle pressure in this job.
examples.zh: 做这工作要能承受压力。

examples.en: She was unable to attend because of the pressure of work.
examples.zh: 她因工作紧张不能出席。

examples.en: How can anyone enjoy the pressures of city life?
examples.zh: 怎么会有人喜欢都市生活的压力呢？

examples.en: The economic pressures on small businesses are intense.
examples.zh: 小企业承受的经济压力很大。

senses.def: the force or weight with which something presses against something else

examples.en: The nurse applied pressure to his arm to stop the bleeding.
examples.zh: 护士压住他的胳膊止血。

examples.en: The barriers gave way under the pressure of the crowd.
examples.zh: 拥挤的人群把路障推倒了。

examples.en: Last year he had brain surgery to relieve pressure from a blood clot.
examples.zh: 他去年做了脑部手术来缓解血栓造成的压力。

senses.def: the force produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a container or a limited space; the amount of this

examples.en: air/water pressure
examples.zh: 空气／水的压力

examples.en: Check the tyre pressure (= the amount of air in a tyre) regularly.
examples.zh: 要定期检查轮胎的气压。

examples.en: a pressure gauge (= an instrument used for measuring the pressure of a liquid or a gas)
examples.zh: 压力计

senses.def: the effect that something has on the way a situation develops, especially when this causes problems

examples.en: This puts upward pressure on prices.
examples.zh: 这会使价格上涨。

examples.en: The high unemployment rate was exerting downward pressure on wage growth.
examples.zh: 高失业率压制了工资增长。

examples.en: These measures are intended to relieve the pressure on the prison system.
examples.zh: 这些措施旨在缓解监狱系统的压力。

examples.en: They raised the starting threshold for income tax to ease the pressure on family budgets.
examples.zh: 他们提高了所得税起征点，以缓解家庭预算压力。

senses.def: the force of the atmosphere on the earth’s surface

examples.en: A band of high/low pressure is moving across the country.
examples.zh: 一股高／低气压正经过这个国家。

senses.def: to force or to try to persuade somebody to do something

examples.en: Advertisements put pressure on girls to be thin.
examples.zh: 广告给女孩施加了变瘦的压力。

senses.def: if a liquid or a gas is kept under pressure

examples.en: Draught beer is pumped out of the barrel under pressure.
examples.zh: 生啤酒在压力下从桶中泵出。

senses.def: being forced to do something

examples.en: The director is under increasing pressure to resign.
examples.zh: 要求总监辞职的呼声越来越高。

examples.en: Hospital staff are coming under pressure to work longer hours.
examples.zh: 医院员工正被迫延长工作时间。

senses.def: made to feel anxious about something you have to do
senses.zh: 承受着（急于完成某事的）压力

examples.en: The team performs well under pressure.
examples.zh: 这个队在压力下表现良好。

examples.en: He's felt under pressure since his wife had the operation.
examples.zh: 妻子做手术以来，他一直觉得压力很大。

senses.def: to persuade somebody to do something, especially by making them feel that they have to or should do it

examples.en: No one has the right to pressure you. You can always say no.
examples.zh: 没人有权逼你，你什么时候都可以说“不”。

examples.en: Don't let yourself be pressured into making a hasty decision.
examples.zh: 不要勉强自己仓促作决定。

examples.en: His father pressured him to accept a job in the bank.
examples.zh: 他的父亲向他施压，要求他接受银行的工作。

items.idm: put pressure on somebody (to do something)

examples.zh: 广告给女孩施加了变瘦的压力。

intro.en: These are all words for the feelings of worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指生活上的心理压力、精神紧张。

items.def: difficulties and feelings of worry that are caused by the need to achieve something or to behave in a particular way:
items.zh: 指为达到某一目标或有某种行为表现而产生的心理压力、紧张

examples.en: She was unable to attend because of the pressures of work.
examples.zh: 由于工作紧张，她不能出席。

items.def: pressure or worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life:
items.zh: 精神压力；心理负担；紧张

examples.en: stress-related illnesses
examples.zh: 与精神压力有关的疾病

items.def: a feeling of worry and stress that makes it impossible to relax:
items.zh: 指情绪上的紧张、烦躁

examples.en: nervous tension
examples.zh: 神经紧张

items.def: pressure on somebody/​something because they have too much to do or manage; the problems or worry that this produces:
items.zh: 指压力、重负、重压之下出现的问题、担忧

examples.en: I found it a strain looking after four children.
examples.zh: 我觉得照料四个孩子挺累的。

senses.def: a strong metal pot with a tight lid
a situation that is difficult or dangerous because people are likely to become anxious or violent
senses.zh: 一触即发的危险局势；剑拔弩张的形势

examples.en: I needed to get away from the pressure cooker atmosphere of the campus during finals week.
examples.zh: 在期末考试周期间，我需要摆脱校园高压锅的气氛。

examples.en: They performed wonders in keeping the lid on the pressure cooker of a rapidly rising jail population.
examples.zh: 他们创造了奇迹，为迅速增加的监狱人口提供了压力。

senses.def: a group of people who try to influence the government and ordinary people’s opinions in order to achieve the action they want, for example a change in a law
senses.zh: 压力集团（向政府和公众施加影响的团体）

examples.en: the environmental pressure group ‘Greenpeace’
examples.zh: “绿色和平”这个环保压力集团

senses.def: a long tube that is strong enough for liquid to pass through it at high pressure

examples.en: a pressure hose for agricultural spraying
examples.zh: 用于农业喷洒的压力软管

senses.def: a place on the surface of the body that is sensitive to pressure, for example where an artery
a place or situation where there is likely to be trouble

examples.en: a new political pressure point
examples.zh: 新的政治压力点

senses.def: a suit that can be filled with air, used to protect the person wearing it from low air pressure, for example while flying a plane very high in the atmosphere
senses.zh: 增压服，加压服（高空飞行等用）

senses.def: a machine that cleans things by spraying
senses.zh: 高压喷洗机；高压清洗机

examples.en: industrial pressure washers
examples.zh: 工业高压清洗机

examples.en: He used a pressure washer to clean the deck.
examples.zh: 他使用高压清洗机来清洁甲板。

senses.def: the act of keeping the air pressure in a submarine, an aircraft, etc. the same as it is on earth
senses.zh: 使（潜艇、飞机等内）保持正常气压

senses.def: to persuade somebody to do something, especially by making them feel that they have to or should do it

examples.en: Stop trying to pressurize me!
examples.zh: 别再逼我了！

examples.en: She was pressurized into accepting the job.
examples.zh: 她被迫接受了这份工作。

examples.en: He was pressurized into getting married.
examples.zh: 他迫于压力不得不结婚。

examples.en: He felt that he was being pressurized to resign.
examples.zh: 他觉得被迫要辞职。

senses.def: to keep the air pressure in a submarine
senses.zh: 使（潜艇、飞机等内）保持正常气压

examples.en: a pressurized cabin
examples.zh: 增压舱

senses.def: the respect and value that somebody/something has because of their social position, or what they have done

examples.en: personal prestige
examples.zh: 个人声望

examples.en: There is a lot of prestige attached to owning a car like this.
examples.zh: 拥有这样一部汽车会显得很气派。

examples.en: jobs with low prestige
examples.zh: 地位低微的工作

senses.def: that brings respect and importance
senses.zh: 令人敬仰的；受尊重的；重要的

examples.en: a prestige job
examples.zh: 体面的工作

senses.def: admired and respected because it looks important and expensive
senses.zh: 名贵的；贵重的；讲究派头的

examples.en: a prestige car
examples.zh: 豪华的汽车

examples.en: prestige items such as jewellery and silver
examples.zh: 珠宝和银器等珍贵物品

senses.def: respected and admired as very important or of very high quality

examples.en: a prestigious award
examples.zh: 赫赫有名的奖项

examples.en: a highly prestigious university
examples.zh: 名牌大学

examples.en: My parents wanted me to go to a more prestigious university.
examples.zh: 我的父母希望我能去一所更有名望的大学。

examples.en: the city’s most prestigious and exclusive hotel
examples.zh: 这座城市最负盛名、最独特的酒店

examples.en: The Gold Cup is one of the most prestigious events in the racing calendar.
examples.zh: 金杯赛是最负盛名的年度赛事之一。

senses.def: something that people say when they have just done something so quickly and easily that it seems to have been done by magic
senses.zh: 嘿，瞧（变魔术般迅速而轻松地做完某事时所说）

senses.def: something that people say just before they finish a magic trick
senses.zh: 变（变魔术完成之前所说）

senses.def: very quickly
a piece of music that should be performed very quickly
a city in north-west England
senses.zh: 普雷斯顿（英格兰西北部城市）

senses.def: a town on the western coast of Scotland, about 30 miles/50 kilometres south-west of Glasgow
senses.zh: 普雷斯蒂克（Prestwick）：位于苏格兰西海岸的一个城镇，位于格拉斯哥西南约30英里/ 50公里处。它有一个国际机场和港口，并以其高尔夫球场而闻名，在这里举行公开赛已经很多年了，直到1924年。

senses.def: used to say that you think that something is probably true

examples.en: Presumably this is where the accident happened.
examples.zh: 这大概就是事故现场。

examples.en: You'll be taking the car, presumably?
examples.zh: 想必您是要买这辆汽车了？

examples.en: I couldn't concentrate, presumably because I was so tired.
examples.zh: 我的精神集中不起来，大概是太累了吧。

examples.en: Presumably you’ll be leaving the children at home.
examples.zh: 你应该会把孩子们留在家里吧。

senses.def: to suppose that something is true, although you do not have actual proof

examples.en: They are very expensive, I presume?
examples.zh: 我想这些东西很贵吧？

examples.en: ‘Is he still abroad?’ ‘I presume so.’
examples.zh: “他还在国外吗？”“我想是吧。”

examples.en: I presumed (that) he understood the rules.
examples.zh: 我相信他明白这些规则。

examples.en: Little is known of the youngest son; it is presumed that he died young.
examples.zh: 对于最小的儿子所知甚少，据推测他夭折了。

examples.en: I presumed him to be her husband.
examples.zh: 我料想那就是她丈夫。

senses.def: to accept that something is true until it is shown not to be true, especially in court

examples.en: Twelve passengers are missing, presumed dead.
examples.zh: 有十二名旅客失踪，并已推定罹难。

examples.en: In English law, a person is presumed innocent until proved guilty.
examples.zh: 英国法律规定，一个人被证明有罪前假定为无罪。

examples.en: We must presume innocence until we have proof of guilt.
examples.zh: 在证实一个人有罪之前，我们必须假定其无罪。

examples.en: We must presume them to be innocent until we have proof of guilt.
examples.zh: 在证实他们有罪之前，我们必须假定其无罪。

senses.def: to accept something as true or existing and to act on that basis

examples.en: The course seems to presume some previous knowledge of the subject.
examples.zh: 这门课程似乎是以具备某些基础知识为前提的。

senses.def: to behave in a way that shows a lack of respect by doing something that you have no right to do

examples.en: I wouldn't presume to tell you how to run your own business.
examples.zh: 我不会僭越去指点你该如何经营你自己的事业。

senses.def: to make use of somebody’s friendship by asking them for more than you should
senses.zh: 利用（友谊）作过分的要求

examples.en: I felt it would be presuming on our personal relationship to keep asking her for help.
examples.zh: 我觉得总要她帮忙就是过分利用了我们的私人交情。

senses.def: to make use of somebody’s friendship by asking them for more than you should
senses.zh: 利用（友谊）作过分的要求

examples.en: I felt it would be presuming on our personal relationship to keep asking her for help.
examples.zh: 我觉得总要她帮忙就是过分利用了我们的私人交情。

senses.def: something that is thought to be true or likely

examples.en: There is a general presumption that the doctor knows best.
examples.zh: 一般人都以为医生最了解情况。

senses.def: behaviour that is too confident and shows a lack of respect for other people

examples.en: She was infuriated by his presumption in not consulting her first.
examples.zh: 她对他没有先咨询她的想法感到愤怒。

senses.def: the act of supposing that something is true, although it has not yet been proved or is not certain

examples.en: Everyone is entitled to the presumption of innocence until they are proved to be guilty.
examples.zh: 在被证明有罪之前，每个人都应被假定无罪。

senses.def: likely to be true, based on the facts that are available
senses.zh: 很可能的；假设的；推断的

examples.en: a presumptive diagnosis of bowel cancer
examples.zh: 肠癌的推定诊断

senses.def: too confident, in a way that shows a lack of respect for other people

examples.en: Would it be presumptuous of me to ask to borrow your car?
examples.zh: 我向你借车会不会太冒昧了？

examples.en: Isn’t it rather presumptuous of you to decide what he needs?
examples.zh: 他需要什么得你来定，这难道不是自以为是吗？

examples.en: It would be presumptuous to assume she will accept the offer.
examples.zh: 如果认为她会接受这个提议，那就太自以为是了。

senses.def: to accept something as true or existing and act on that basis, before it has been proved to be true

examples.en: Teachers sometimes presuppose a fairly high level of knowledge by the students.
examples.zh: 教师有时候假定学生的知识水平相当高。

senses.def: to depend on something in order to exist or be true

examples.en: His argument presupposes that it does not matter who is in power.
examples.zh: 他的论点前提是，谁掌权都无关紧要。

examples.en: This argument presupposes that all children start off life with equal advantages.
examples.zh: 这个论点的前提是，所有儿童生来都具有同等的优势。

senses.def: something that you believe to be true and use as the beginning of an argument even though it has not been proved; the act of believing it is true

examples.en: theories based on presupposition and coincidence
examples.zh: 基于假设和偶合的理论

senses.def: any of a chain of sandwich shops started in London in 1986 by Julian Metcalfe and Sinclair Beecham, which sell sandwiches that are made in the shops, as well as drinks and other food items that customers can eat in the shop or take away. There are now Pret
senses.zh: 装扮成马槽：1986年，朱利安·梅特卡夫（Julian Metcalfe）和辛克莱·比彻姆（Sinclair Beecham）在伦敦开设的任何三明治店链中的任何一家，都出售店里制造的三明治以及顾客可以在店里吃或拿的饮料和其他食品远。现在在英国以及美国，香港和巴黎都有Pret商店。该名称意为即食食品，是根据法语表达prêtàporter（即食）制成的。

senses.def: the act of behaving in a particular way, in order to make other people believe something that is not true

examples.en: Their friendliness was only pretence.
examples.zh: 他们的友善态度只不过是装出来的。

examples.en: By the end of the evening she had abandoned all pretence of being interested.
examples.zh: 到晚会结束时，她已将假装的兴趣抛得一干二净。

examples.en: He made no pretence of great musical knowledge.
examples.zh: 他未敢妄称音乐知识丰富。

examples.en: She was unable to keep up the pretence that she loved him.
examples.zh: 她无法继续假装爱他了。

senses.def: a claim that you have a particular quality or skill

examples.en: A judge should have at least some pretence to objectivity.
examples.zh: 法官至少应该有一定程度的客观性。

examples.en: I make no pretence to being an expert on the subject.
examples.zh: 我不敢自诩为这方面的专家。

senses.def: by pretending to be something that you are not, in order to gain some advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 靠欺诈手段；以虚假的借口

examples.en: She was accused of obtaining money under false pretences.
examples.zh: 她被控诈骗钱财。

senses.def: by pretending to be something that you are not, in order to gain some advantage for yourself
senses.zh: 靠欺诈手段；以虚假的借口

examples.en: She was accused of obtaining money under false pretences.
examples.zh: 她被控诈骗钱财。

senses.def: to behave in a particular way, in order to make other people believe something that is not true

examples.en: I'm tired of having to pretend all the time.
examples.zh: 我厌倦了常常要装假。

examples.en: Of course I was wrong; it would be hypocritical to pretend otherwise.
examples.zh: 当然是我错了，混充正确就是虚伪了。

examples.en: He pretended to his family that everything was fine.
examples.zh: 他对家人装出一切都好的样子。

examples.en: We pretended (that) nothing had happened.
examples.zh: 我们假装什么事情也没发生。

examples.en: She pretended (that) she was his niece.
examples.zh: 她冒充他的外甥女。

examples.en: I pretended to be asleep.
examples.zh: 我假装睡着了。

examples.en: He pretended not to notice.
examples.zh: 他假装没注意。

examples.en: She didn't love him, though she pretended to.
examples.zh: 她并不爱他，虽然她装出爱的样子。

examples.en: She pretended an interest she did not feel.
examples.zh: 她毫无兴趣却装作有。

senses.def: to imagine that something is true as part of a game

examples.en: They didn't have any real money so they had to pretend.
examples.zh: 他们没有真钱，就用假的代替。

examples.en: Let’s pretend (that) we’re astronauts.
examples.zh: 咱们假装是宇航员吧。

senses.def: to claim to be, do or have something, especially when this is not true

examples.en: I can't pretend to any great musical talent.
examples.zh: 我不能妄称自己多有音乐天赋。

examples.en: I don’t pretend (that) I know much about the subject, but…
examples.zh: 我不敢说自己对这个主题有多了解，但是…

examples.en: The book doesn't pretend to be a great work of literature.
examples.zh: 这本书并未自封为文学杰作。

senses.def: not real, imaginary

examples.en: pretend cakes
examples.zh: 假糕点

senses.def: a person who claims they have a right to a particular title even though other people disagree with them

examples.en: the pretender to the French throne
examples.zh: 法国王位觊觎者

examples.en: Their friendliness was only pretense.
examples.zh: 他们的友善只是假装的。

examples.en: By the end of the evening she had abandoned all pretense of being interested.
examples.zh: 到了晚上，她已经放弃了所有假装感兴趣的样子。

examples.en: He made no pretense of great musical knowledge.
examples.zh: 他并没有假装自己拥有渊博的音乐知识。

examples.en: She was unable to keep up the pretense that she loved him.
examples.zh: 她无法继续假装自己爱他。

senses.def: a claim that you have a particular quality or skill

examples.en: A judge should have at least some pretense to objectivity.
examples.zh: 法官至少应该有一定程度的客观性。

examples.en: I make no pretense to being an expert on the subject.
examples.zh: 我并不假装自己是该领域的专家。

senses.def: the act of trying to appear more important, intelligent, etc. than you are in order to impress other people

examples.en: intellectual pretensions
examples.zh: 装作有知识

examples.en: The play mocks the pretensions of the new middle class.
examples.zh: 这出戏讽刺了新中产阶级的装模作样。

examples.en: He spoke without pretension.
examples.zh: 他有话直说，不装相。

examples.en: a young couple with social pretensions
examples.zh: 一对有社交自负的年轻夫妇

examples.en: She was charmed by his lack of pretension.
examples.zh: 他不虚夸，不做作，这让她为之倾倒。

senses.def: a claim to be or to do something

examples.en: a building with no pretensions to architectural merit
examples.zh: 没有刻意表现建筑特色的楼房

examples.en: The movie makes no pretension to reproduce life.
examples.zh: 这部电影并未标榜重现了真实生活。

senses.def: trying to appear important, intelligent, etc. in order to impress other people; trying to be something that you are not, in order to impress
senses.zh: 炫耀的；虚夸的；自命不凡的

examples.en: That's a pretentious name for a dog!
examples.zh: 狗叫这个名字真够炫的！

examples.en: It was just an ordinary house—nothing pretentious.
examples.zh: 那只是一座普通的房子，没有故作特别。

examples.en: He's so pretentious!
examples.zh: 他太自命不凡了！

senses.def: in a way that tries to appear important, intelligent, etc. in order to impress other people; in a way that tries to be something that you are not, in order to impress
senses.zh: 炫耀的；虚夸的；自命不凡的

examples.en: The screen pretentiously displays a sombre quotation about war.
examples.zh: 屏幕上自命不凡地显示着一段关于战争的阴沉的引言。

senses.def: the fact of trying to appear important, intelligent, etc. in order to impress other people

examples.en: There was no hint of pretentiousness in her manner.
examples.zh: 她的举止中没有任何自命不凡的迹象。

senses.def: born or happening after a short pregnancy
senses.zh: 早产的，不满妊娠期的（尤指怀孕少于 37 周的）

examples.en: caring for low birthweight and preterm babies
examples.zh: 对体重不足和早产婴儿的护理

examples.en: a preterm birth/delivery
examples.zh: 早产

senses.def: after a short pregnancy
senses.zh: 早产的，不满妊娠期的（尤指怀孕少于 37 周的）

examples.en: Babies born preterm are at greater risk of needing hospitalization.
examples.zh: 早产儿需要住院治疗的风险较高。

senses.def: that does not seem natural; that cannot be explained by natural laws
senses.zh: 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的

examples.en: preternatural power
examples.zh: 超自然力量

senses.def: in a way that does not seem natural; in a way that cannot be explained by natural laws
senses.zh: 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的

examples.en: The city was preternaturally quiet.
examples.zh: 这座城市安静得有些异常。

senses.def: to test somebody in order to find out how much they already know or can do before they start learning or doing something
senses.zh: （学习或做某事前的）预先测试

senses.def: a test that you take to find out how much you already know or can do before learning or doing something
senses.zh: （学习或做某事前的）预先测试

senses.def: a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason; an excuse

examples.en: The incident was used as a pretext for intervention in the area.
examples.zh: 这次事件被用作干涉那个地区的借口。

examples.en: He left the party early on the pretext of having work to do.
examples.zh: 他借口有事要处理，早早离开了聚会。

examples.en: People were being arrested on the flimsiest of pretexts.
examples.zh: 人们以最站不住脚的借口被捕。

examples.en: The case for war was made on a false pretext.
examples.zh: 战争的理由是基于虚假的借口。

examples.en: Under the pretext of checking her identity, the man had copied down her credit card details.
examples.zh: 那个男的以检查她的身分为借口抄下了她信用卡的详细资料。

examples.en: Be careful not to give him a pretext to report you.
examples.zh: 小心别给他一个举报你的借口。

synonyms.words: explanation ▪ grounds ▪ basis ▪ excuse ▪ motive ▪ justification ▪ pretext

intro.en: These are all words for a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指事情发生或做某事的原因、理由、解释。

items.def: a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done; a fact that makes it right or fair to do something:
items.zh: 指某事发生或做某事的原因、理由、解释、道理

examples.en: He said no but he didn’t give a reason.
examples.zh: 他说不行，但没有说明原因。

items.def: a statement, fact or situation that tells you why something has happened; a reason given for something:
items.zh: 指解释、说明、阐述

examples.en: The most likely explanation is that his plane was delayed.
examples.zh: 最可能的解释是他的飞机晚点了。

items.def: (rather formal) a good or true reason for saying, doing or believing something:
items.zh: 指说、做或相信某事的充分理由、根据

examples.en: You have no grounds for complaint.
examples.zh: 你没有理由抱怨。

items.def: (rather formal) the reason why people take a particular action:
items.zh: 指原因、缘由

examples.en: On what basis will this decision be made?
examples.zh: 将基于何种原因作出这一决定呢？

items.def: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour; a good reason that you give for doing something that you want to do for other reasons:
items.zh: 指为自己行为所作的辩护、借口、理由

examples.en: Late again! What’s your excuse this time?
examples.zh: 又迟到了！你这次有什么借口？

items.def: a reason that explains somebody’s behaviour:
items.zh: 指动机、原因

examples.en: There seemed to be no motive for the murder.
examples.zh: 这起谋杀案看不出有什么动机。

items.def: (rather formal) a good reason why something exists or is done:
items.zh: 指事物存在或做某事的正当理由

examples.en: I can see no possible justification for any further tax increases.
examples.zh: 我看不出还能提出什么理由来加税了。

items.def: (rather formal) a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason:
items.zh: 指为掩盖做某事（通常为不好的事）的真正理由而找的借口、托辞

examples.en: He left the party early on the pretext of having to work.
examples.zh: 他借口有事要处理，早早离开了聚会。

senses.def: in or connected with the time before a court case begins

examples.en: He testified at a pretrial hearing.
examples.zh: 他在审判前的听证会上作证。

senses.def: to try to make something pretty, often with the result that it looks worse or false

examples.en: attempts to prettify nature
examples.zh: 试图美化自然

senses.def: in an attractive way

examples.en: She laughed prettily.
examples.zh: 她笑得很妩媚。

examples.en: The rooms are simply but prettily furnished.
examples.zh: 这些房间布置得简单但赏心悦目。

senses.def: the quality of being pretty

examples.en: the prettiness of youth
examples.zh: 青春之美

examples.en: We just sat there admiring the prettiness of the town square.
examples.zh: 我们只是坐在那里欣赏城镇广场的美丽。

senses.def: to some extent; fairly

examples.en: The game was pretty good.
examples.zh: 这个游戏相当不错。

examples.en: I'm pretty sure I'll be going.
examples.zh: 我相当肯定会去的。

examples.en: It's pretty hard to explain.
examples.zh: 这事很难解释清楚。

examples.en: I'm going to have to find a new apartment pretty soon.
examples.zh: 我很快就得找个新住处了。

senses.def: very

examples.en: That performance was pretty impressive.
examples.zh: 那场表演很出色。

examples.en: Things are looking pretty good!
examples.zh: 形势看来很不错！

examples.en: The idea sounds pretty cool.
examples.zh: 这个想法听起来很酷。

examples.en: We were pretty disappointed with the quality of the food.
examples.zh: 我们对食物的质量非常失望。

senses.def: to be in a good situation, especially when others are not
senses.zh: （尤指在他人处境不好时）处境好

examples.en: With profits at record levels, the company’s certainly sitting pretty this year.
examples.zh: 由于利润创历史新高，该公司今年的表现肯定不错。

senses.def: almost; almost completely

examples.en: One dog looks pretty much like another to me.
examples.zh: 在我看来，狗长得都差不多。

examples.en: He goes out pretty well every night.
examples.zh: 他几乎每晚都外出。

examples.en: The first stage is pretty near finished.
examples.zh: 第一阶段已经接近完成。

examples.zh: 你穿那件连衣裙真漂亮！

examples.en: She's very attractive, though not conventionally pretty.
examples.zh: 她很有魅力，虽然不是传统意义上的漂亮。

senses.zh: 赏心悦目的；动听的；美观的；精致的

examples.en: a pretty garden
examples.zh: 赏心悦目的花园

examples.en: That's a pretty flower—what's it called?
examples.zh: 那花很漂亮，叫什么名字？

examples.en: The canal looked prettiest at night.
examples.zh: 晚上的运河看起来最漂亮。

examples.en: He was hired to make the company pretty and then sell it off.
examples.zh: 他被雇佣是为了让公司变得漂亮，然后把它卖掉。

examples.zh: 她美得像一幅画。

intro.zh: 以上各词均形容人好看。

items.def: (most often used of a woman or girl) very pleasant to look at:
items.zh: （尤指女子或女孩）漂亮的，美丽的

examples.en: She looked stunningly beautiful that night.
examples.zh: 她那天晚上美极了。

senses.zh: “漂亮男孩”弗洛伊德：查尔斯·亚瑟·弗洛伊德（1901-34）是一名美国罪犯，在大萧条期间抢劫了中西部的银行，并曾一度成为第一公敌。一些美国人钦佩他，因为他把钱捐给了穷人，但他还谋杀了约十名男子，其中包括两名联邦调查局官员。他最终在俄亥俄州的一个野外被联邦调查局杀害。

to exist or be very common at a particular time or in a particular place

examples.en: We were horrified at the conditions prevailing in local prisons.
examples.zh: 地方监狱的普遍状况让我们震惊。

examples.en: Those beliefs still prevail among certain social groups.
examples.zh: 那些信念在某些社会群体中仍很盛行。

senses.def: to be accepted, especially after a struggle or an argument

examples.en: Justice will prevail over tyranny.
examples.zh: 正义必将战胜暴虐。

examples.en: Fortunately, common sense prevailed.
examples.zh: 幸而常识占了上风。

senses.def: to defeat an opponent, especially after a long struggle
senses.zh: （尤指长时间斗争后）战胜，挫败

examples.en: In a one-sided final, Spain prevailed against title-holder Croatia 40–34.
examples.zh: 在一场实力悬殊的决赛中，西班牙队以40:34挫败了卫冕的克罗地亚队。

examples.en: They wasted two penalties but still prevailed 2–1.
examples.zh: 他们浪费了两个点球，但仍然以 2-1 获胜。

senses.def: to persuade somebody to do something

examples.en: I'm sure he could be prevailed upon to give a talk.
examples.zh: 我相信能说服他来做一次报告。

senses.def: to persuade somebody to do something

examples.en: I'm sure he could be prevailed upon to give a talk.
examples.zh: 我相信能说服他来做一次报告。

senses.def: the fact of existing or being very common at a particular time or in a particular place

examples.en: an increase in the prevalence of obesity in many countries
examples.zh: 许多国家肥胖症患病率上升

senses.def: that exists or is very common at a particular time or in a particular place
senses.zh: 流行的；普遍存在的；盛行的

examples.en: a prevalent view
examples.zh: 普遍的观点

examples.en: These prejudices are particularly prevalent among people living in the North.
examples.zh: 这些偏见在北方人中尤为常见。

examples.en: The disease is even more prevalent in Latin America.
examples.zh: 这种疾病在拉丁美洲更为流行。

senses.def: to avoid giving a direct answer to a question in order to hide the truth
senses.zh: 支吾搪塞；闪烁其词；吞吞吐吐

examples.en: Stop prevaricating and come to the point.
examples.zh: 别吞吞吐吐的，有话快说吧。

senses.def: the act of not giving a direct answer to a question in order to hide the truth
senses.zh: 支吾搪塞；闪烁其词；吞吞吐吐

examples.en: She accused him of prevarication.
examples.zh: 她指责他搪塞。

examples.en: The report was full of lies and prevarications.
examples.zh: 这篇报道不是颠倒黑白就是含糊其辞。

senses.def: to stop somebody from doing something; to stop something from happening

examples.en: The accident could have been prevented.
examples.zh: 这次事故本来是可以预防的。

examples.en: Maddie would have joined the army if an injury had not prevented her.
examples.zh: 要不是受伤的话，玛迪本来会参军的。

examples.en: The government took steps to prevent a scandal.
examples.zh: 政府采取措施防止丑闻发生。

examples.en: He is prevented by law from holding a licence.
examples.zh: 法律不准他持有执照。

examples.en: Nothing would prevent him from speaking out against injustice.
examples.zh: 什么都不能阻止他鸣不平。

examples.en: Nothing would prevent him speaking out against injustice.
examples.zh: 什么也阻挡不了他为不平之事鸣冤叫屈。

senses.def: that can be stopped from happening
senses.zh: 可防止的，可预防的，可阻止的

examples.en: preventable diseases/accidents
examples.zh: 可预防的疾病／事故

senses.def: the act of stopping something bad from happening

examples.en: accident/crime prevention
examples.zh: 防止事故／犯罪

examples.en: the prevention of disease
examples.zh: 疾病的预防

examples.en: a fire prevention officer
examples.zh: 消防官员

examples.en: a diabetes prevention programme
examples.zh: 糖尿病预防计划

senses.def: it is better to stop something bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
senses.zh: 预防优于补救；防患于未然是上策

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start looking after your heart now.
examples.zh: 防病比治病好，所以从现在开始照顾好你的心脏。

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start taking care of yourself.
examples.zh: 治病不如防病，所以从现在开始照顾好你自己。

senses.def: it is better to stop something bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
senses.zh: 预防优于补救；防患于未然是上策

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start looking after your heart now.
examples.zh: 防病比治病好，所以从现在开始照顾好你的心脏。

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start taking care of yourself.
examples.zh: 治病不如防病，所以从现在开始照顾好你自己。

senses.def: it is better to stop something bad from happening rather than try to deal with the problems after it has happened
senses.zh: 预防优于补救；防患于未然是上策

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start looking after your heart now.
examples.zh: 防病比治病好，所以从现在开始照顾好你的心脏。

examples.en: Prevention is better than cure, so start taking care of yourself.
examples.zh: 治病不如防病，所以从现在开始照顾好你自己。

senses.def: intended to try to stop something that causes problems or difficulties from happening

examples.en: preventive medicine
examples.zh: 预防医学

examples.en: The police were able to take preventive action and avoid a possible riot.
examples.zh: 警方得以及时采取防范措施，避免了可能发生的骚乱。

senses.def: connected with the time before a child learns to speak
senses.zh: （幼儿）前语言期的，习得语言能力前的

examples.en: preverbal communication
examples.zh: 前语言期交流

senses.def: an occasion at which you can see a film, a show, etc. before it is shown to the general public

examples.en: a press preview (= for journalists only)
examples.zh: 招待新闻界的预展

examples.en: a special preview of our winter fashion collection
examples.zh: 我们冬季时装系列的特别预展

examples.en: On today’s show, we’ll have exclusive previews of some of the best new music.
examples.zh: 在今天的展会上，我们将有机会独家试听一些最好的音乐新作。

senses.def: a description in a newspaper or a magazine that tells you about a film, a television programme, etc. before it is shown to the public
senses.zh: （报刊上有关电影、电视节目等的）预先评述，预告

examples.en: Turn to page 12 for a preview of next week's programmes.
examples.zh: 下周节目预告请见第 12 页。

senses.def: a series of short scenes from a film or television programme, shown in advance to advertise it
senses.zh: 指电影或电视节目的预告片

senses.def: a chance to see what something will be like before it happens or is shown

examples.en: Click on the print preview button.
examples.zh: 点击打印预览按钮。

senses.def: to see a film, a television programme, etc. before it is shown to the general public and write an account of it for a newspaper or magazine

examples.en: The exhibition was previewed in last week's issue.
examples.zh: 本刊上周对展览作了预评。

senses.def: to give somebody a short account of something that is going to happen, be studied, etc.

examples.en: The professor previewed the course for us.
examples.zh: 教授为我们扼要介绍了这门课程。

senses.def: happening or existing before the event or object that you are talking about

examples.en: No previous experience is necessary for this job.
examples.zh: 这一工作无需相关的经验。

examples.en: The car has had only one previous owner.
examples.zh: 这辆车只有一位前车主。

examples.en: She is his daughter from a previous marriage.
examples.zh: 她是他与前妻生的女儿。

examples.en: I was unable to attend because of a previous engagement.
examples.zh: 我因有约在先，无法出席。

examples.en: The judge will take into consideration any previous convictions.
examples.zh: 任何前科法官都将予以考虑。

examples.en: We dealt with this in a previous chapter.
examples.zh: 我们在前一章中讨论过这个问题。

examples.en: We had met on two previous occasions.
examples.zh: 我们以前见过两次面。

examples.en: Most previous studies have focused on the elderly.
examples.zh: 之前的大多数研究都集中在老年人身上。

examples.en: Today's teens are more health conscious than previous generations.
examples.zh: 今天的青少年比前几代人更加注重健康。

senses.def: immediately before the time you are talking about

examples.en: the previous year/month/week/night
examples.zh: 前一年；前一个月；前一周；前一夜

examples.en: I couldn't believe it when I heard the news. I'd only seen him the previous day.
examples.zh: 听到这消息时我不敢相信，我就在前一天还见到过他。

examples.en: He went jogging on Friday, despite the doctor’s warnings the previous day.
examples.zh: 尽管医生前一天刚警告过他，可他周五还是去慢跑了。

senses.def: before a particular time or event

examples.en: Previous to this, she'd always been well.
examples.zh: 这以前，她身体一向很好。

senses.def: at a time before the time that you are talking about

examples.en: The building had previously been used as a hotel.
examples.zh: 这座楼房早先曾用作旅馆。

examples.en: As previously reported, the couple separated in May.
examples.zh: 正如之前报道的那样，这对夫妇于五月分居。

examples.en: The book contains a number of photographs not previously published.
examples.zh: 这本书包含许多以前未出版的照片。

examples.en: I had visited them three days previously.
examples.zh: 三天前我曾探访过他们。

examples.en: a previously unknown species
examples.zh: 以前未知的物种

senses.def: an animal, a bird, etc. that is hunted, killed and eaten by another

examples.en: The lion will often stalk its prey for hours.
examples.zh: 狮子经常悄然跟踪猎物达几个小时。

examples.en: birds of prey (= birds that kill for food)
examples.zh: 猛禽

senses.def: a person who is harmed or tricked by somebody, especially for dishonest purposes

examples.en: Socially isolated young people are easy prey for extremists.
examples.zh: 社会孤立的年轻人很容易成为极端分子的猎物。

senses.def: to be killed and eaten by another animal or bird

examples.en: Many small birds and rodents fall prey to the domestic cat.
examples.zh: 许多小鸟和啮齿动物成为家猫的猎物。

senses.def: to be harmed or affected by something bad

examples.en: Since the attack, he had fallen prey to irrational fears.
examples.zh: 自从袭击发生以来，他一直陷入非理性的恐惧之中。

examples.en: She knew she must not fall prey to his charm.
examples.zh: 她清楚自己绝不可以被他迷住。

examples.en: The new government has fallen prey to corruption and fraud.
examples.zh: 新一届政府深受腐败与欺诈之苦。

senses.def: to make somebody think and worry about it all the time

examples.en: The thought that he could have helped more preyed on his mind.
examples.zh: 他本可以帮助更多人，这个念头萦绕在他的心头。

examples.en: It's been preying on my mind ever since it happened.
examples.zh: 事情发生后我的内心就一直在受折磨。

senses.def: to be killed and eaten by another animal or bird

examples.en: Many small birds and rodents fall prey to the domestic cat.
examples.zh: 许多小鸟和啮齿动物成为家猫的猎物。

examples.en: It's been preying on my mind ever since it happened.
examples.zh: 事情发生后我的内心就一直在受折磨。

senses.def: to make somebody think and worry about it all the time

examples.en: The thought that he could have helped more preyed on his mind.
examples.zh: 他本可以帮助更多人，这个念头萦绕在他的心头。

examples.en: It's been preying on my mind ever since it happened.
examples.zh: 事情发生后我的内心就一直在受折磨。

senses.def: to hunt and kill another animal for food

examples.en: Hawks prey on rodents and small birds.
examples.zh: 老鹰捕食啮齿动物和小鸟。

senses.def: to harm somebody who is weaker than you, or make use of them in a dishonest way to get what you want

examples.en: Scammers have been preying on inexperienced investors.
examples.zh: 诈骗者一直在欺骗缺乏经验的投资者。

senses.def: to hunt and kill another animal for food

examples.en: Hawks prey on rodents and small birds.
examples.zh: 老鹰捕食啮齿动物和小鸟。

examples.zh: 诈骗者一直在欺骗缺乏经验的投资者。

senses.def: president
a present that you give somebody, for example for their birthday
connected with or like a penis
connected with male sexual activity
having a penis
a condition in which a man’s penis
the amount of money that you have to pay for something

examples.en: Boat for sale, price £8 000
examples.zh: 出售小船，价格 8 000 英镑

examples.en: house/oil/share prices
examples.zh: 房价；油价；股价

examples.en: rising/falling prices
examples.zh: 攀升／下跌的价格

examples.en: to increase/lower/reduce prices
examples.zh: 提高/降低/减少价格

examples.en: We will have to raise ticket prices.
examples.zh: 我们将不得不提高票价。

examples.en: The company has announced that it is cutting prices.
examples.zh: 该公司宣布正在降价。

examples.en: In the past year, house prices have fallen.
examples.zh: 过去一年，房价有所下跌。

examples.en: The price of crude oil has risen over the last few months.
examples.zh: 过去几个月原油价格有所上涨。

examples.en: to charge a high/reasonable/low price for something
examples.zh: 索价很高／适中／很低

examples.en: to pay/charge a price for something
examples.zh: 为某物付费／收费

examples.en: He managed to get a good price for the car.
examples.zh: 他终于把汽车卖了个好价钱。

examples.en: Retail prices for food at the supermarket rose just under two per cent in the first quarter.
examples.zh: 第一季度超市食品零售价格上涨了不到百分之二。

examples.en: Can you give me a price for the work (= tell me how much you will charge)?
examples.zh: 请问做这件工作要多少钱？

examples.en: Children over five must pay (the) full price for the ticket.
examples.zh: 五岁以上的儿童须买全票。

examples.en: I'm only buying it if it's the right price (= a price that I think is reasonable).
examples.zh: 只有价钱合理我才会买这东西。

examples.en: How much are these? They don't have a price on them.
examples.zh: 这些东西卖多少钱？它们都没有标价。

examples.en: Most new technology comes down in price with time.
examples.zh: 大多数新技术的价格都会随时间推移而下降。

examples.en: a rise/an increase/a fall/a drop in price
examples.zh: 价格上涨/上涨/下跌/下跌

examples.en: They sell quality art supplies at discount prices.
examples.zh: 他们打折销售优质艺术品。

examples.en: I don't think you'll be able to sell it for that price.
examples.zh: 我认为你卖不出这个价格。

examples.en: price rises/increases/hikes/cuts
examples.zh: 加价；价格急涨；减价

senses.def: the unpleasant things that you must do or experience in order to achieve something or as a result of achieving something

examples.en: Criticism is part of the price of leadership.
examples.zh: 挨批评是当领袖要付出的代价之一。

examples.en: Loneliness is a high price to pay for independence in your old age.
examples.zh: 孤独是老年独力生活要付出的高昂代价。

examples.en: Giving up his job was a small price to pay for his children's happiness.
examples.zh: 为了他子女的幸福，放弃工作实在不算什么。

examples.en: The team paid a heavy price for its lack of preparation.
examples.zh: 这支队伍由于准备不足而付出了沉重的代价。

examples.en: Being recognized wherever you go is the price you pay for being famous.
examples.zh: 出名所付出的代价是不管你走到哪里，都会被人认出来。

examples.en: His success came at a high price.
examples.zh: 他的成功代价高昂。

senses.def: the numbers that tell you how much money you will receive if the horse that you bet on wins the race

examples.en: Six to one is a good price for that horse.
examples.zh: 那匹马有六比一的赔率很不错。

senses.def: whatever the cost or the difficulties may be
senses.zh: 不惜任何代价；无论如何

examples.en: We want peace at any price.
examples.zh: 为了争取和平，我们不惜任何代价。

senses.def: costing a lot of money

examples.en: You can buy strawberries all year round, but at a price.
examples.zh: 草莓一年到头都买得到，不过很贵。

examples.en: Food is available, at a price.
examples.zh: 食物可以买到，不过出价要高。

senses.def: involving something unpleasant

examples.en: He'll help you—at a price!
examples.zh: 他会帮助你的，但要付出代价！

senses.def: extremely valuable or important
senses.zh: 无价的；极珍贵的；极重要的

senses.def: so good or useful that the cost does not seem too much

examples.en: To buy all the recommended equipment is expensive, but as an investment for the future it is cheap at the price.
examples.zh: 购买所有推荐的设备是昂贵的，但作为对未来的投资，它的价格很便宜。

senses.def: you can persuade anyone to do something by giving them more money or something that they want
senses.zh: 重赏之下，必有勇夫；人皆有价；有钱能使鬼推磨

senses.def: used to say that no amount of money would persuade you to do or to sell something
senses.zh: 无论如何也不；给多少钱也不

examples.en: I wouldn't work for her again—not at any price!
examples.zh: 我再也不替她做事了，给多少钱也不做！

senses.def: to suffer because of bad luck, a mistake or something you have done

examples.en: He looked terrible this morning. I think he's paying the penalty for all those late nights.
examples.zh: 他今天上午脸色很不好，我想这是他一直熬夜造成的。

examples.en: They're now paying the price for past mistakes.
examples.zh: 他们现在正为过去的错误付出代价。

examples.en: She thinks that any inconvenience is a price worth paying for living in such a beautiful place.
examples.zh: 她认为生活在如此美丽的地方，任何不便都是值得付出的代价。

senses.def: an amount of money that is offered for capturing or killing somebody
senses.zh: 缉拿（或杀害）某人的悬赏金

examples.en: Ever since he killed the gang’s leader, there has been a price on his head.
examples.zh: 自从他杀死了帮派头目之后，他的人头就被悬赏了。

senses.def: to say how much money something valuable is worth

examples.en: They haven't yet put a price on the business.
examples.zh: 他们还没有给这笔生意开价。

examples.en: You can't put a price on that sort of loyalty.
examples.zh: 那样的忠心是无法用金钱衡量的。

examples.en: You can't put a price on happiness.
examples.zh: 你不能以金钱来衡量幸福。

senses.def: used to say that you think that something you have achieved may not be worth all the problems and difficulties it causes
senses.zh: （认为得不偿失）…不值得，…有什么用？

examples.en: What price fame and fortune?
examples.zh: 名利的代价何其大。

senses.def: used to say that something seems unlikely
senses.zh: （认为可能性不大）…可能吗，…不可能吧

examples.en: What price England winning the World Cup?
examples.zh: 英格兰队夺得世界杯冠军，这可能吗？

senses.def: to fix the price of something at a particular level

examples.en: The main courses are all reasonably priced.
examples.zh: 几道主菜都价格合理。

examples.en: These goods are priced too high.
examples.zh: 这些货品定价过高。

examples.en: Their printers are competitively priced.
examples.zh: 他们的打印机价格很有竞争力。

examples.en: The tickets are priced at $100 each.
examples.zh: 每张票定价 100 美元。

examples.en: A dominant firm will price aggressively in markets where it faces new competitors.
examples.zh: 在市场上占主导地位的公司面临新的竞争者时会采取进取性市场定价。

senses.def: to write or stick tickets on goods to show how much they cost
to compare the prices of different types of the same thing

examples.en: We priced various models before buying this one.
examples.zh: 我们比较了多种型号的价格以后才买了这一款。

senses.def: to charge such a high price for your goods, services, etc. that nobody wants to buy them
senses.zh: 因索价过高而无人问津

examples.en: Some leading UK firms are pricing themselves out of the market.
examples.zh: 英国的一些大公司因要价过高而无人问津。

senses.def: whatever the cost or the difficulties may be
senses.zh: 不惜任何代价；无论如何

examples.en: We want peace at any price.
examples.zh: 为了争取和平，我们不惜任何代价。

senses.def: costing a lot of money

examples.en: You can buy strawberries all year round, but at a price.
examples.zh: 草莓一年到头都买得到，不过很贵。

examples.en: Food is available, at a price.
examples.zh: 食物可以买到，不过出价要高。

senses.def: involving something unpleasant

examples.en: He'll help you—at a price!
examples.zh: 他会帮助你的，但要付出代价！

senses.def: extremely valuable or important
senses.zh: 无价的；极珍贵的；极重要的

senses.def: so good or useful that the cost does not seem too much

examples.en: To buy all the recommended equipment is expensive, but as an investment for the future it is cheap at the price.
examples.zh: 购买所有推荐的设备是昂贵的，但作为对未来的投资，它的价格很便宜。

senses.def: you can persuade anyone to do something by giving them more money or something that they want
senses.zh: 重赏之下，必有勇夫；人皆有价；有钱能使鬼推磨

senses.def: used to say that no amount of money would persuade you to do or to sell something
senses.zh: 无论如何也不；给多少钱也不

examples.en: I wouldn't work for her again—not at any price!
examples.zh: 我再也不替她做事了，给多少钱也不做！

items.idm: pay the/a penalty/price (for something/for doing something)

senses.def: to suffer because of bad luck, a mistake or something you have done

examples.en: He looked terrible this morning. I think he's paying the penalty for all those late nights.
examples.zh: 他今天上午脸色很不好，我想这是他一直熬夜造成的。

examples.en: They're now paying the price for past mistakes.
examples.zh: 他们现在正为过去的错误付出代价。

examples.en: She thinks that any inconvenience is a price worth paying for living in such a beautiful place.
examples.zh: 她认为生活在如此美丽的地方，任何不便都是值得付出的代价。

senses.def: an amount of money that is offered for capturing or killing somebody
senses.zh: 缉拿（或杀害）某人的悬赏金

examples.en: Ever since he killed the gang’s leader, there has been a price on his head.
examples.zh: 自从他杀死了帮派头目之后，他的人头就被悬赏了。

senses.def: to say how much money something valuable is worth

examples.en: They haven't yet put a price on the business.
examples.zh: 他们还没有给这笔生意开价。

examples.en: You can't put a price on that sort of loyalty.
examples.zh: 那样的忠心是无法用金钱衡量的。

examples.en: You can't put a price on happiness.
examples.zh: 你不能以金钱来衡量幸福。

senses.def: used to say that you think that something you have achieved may not be worth all the problems and difficulties it causes
senses.zh: （认为得不偿失）…不值得，…有什么用？

examples.en: What price fame and fortune?
examples.zh: 名利的代价何其大。

senses.def: used to say that something seems unlikely
senses.zh: （认为可能性不大）…可能吗，…不可能吧

examples.en: What price England winning the World Cup?
examples.zh: 英格兰队夺得世界杯冠军，这可能吗？

items.idm: price yourself/something out of the market

senses.def: to charge such a high price for your goods, services, etc. that nobody wants to buy them
senses.zh: 因索价过高而无人问津

examples.en: Some leading UK firms are pricing themselves out of the market.
examples.zh: 英国的一些大公司因要价过高而无人问津。

intro.en: These words all refer to the amount of money that you have to pay for something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指价值、价钱。

items.def: the amount of money that you have to pay for an item or service:
items.zh: 指商品或服务的价格、价钱

examples.en: house prices
examples.zh: 房屋价格

items.def: the amount of money that you need in order to buy, make or do something:
items.zh: 指购买、制造某物或做某事所需的成本、费用、花费

examples.en: A new computer system has been installed at a cost of £80 000.
examples.zh: 新的计算机系统已安装，费用为 8 万英镑。

items.def: how much something is worth in money or other goods for which it can be exchanged:
items.zh: 指价值

examples.en: The winner will receive a prize to the value of £1 000.
examples.zh: 获胜者将得到价值为 1 000 英镑的奖品。

items.def: the money that you spend on something; something that makes you spend money:
items.zh: 指所花费用、花钱的东西、开销

examples.en: The garden was transformed at great expense.
examples.zh: 花园改建花了一大笔费用。

items.def: the financial value of somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指人或物的价值

examples.en: He has a personal net worth of $10 million.
examples.zh: 他有价值 1 000 万美元的个人净资产。

senses.def: to charge such a high price for your goods, services, etc. that nobody wants to buy them
senses.zh: 因索价过高而无人问津

examples.en: Some leading UK firms are pricing themselves out of the market.
examples.zh: 英国的一些大公司因要价过高而无人问津。

price yourself/something out of the mark.word: price yourself/something out of the market

senses.def: an upper limit set by a government on the price of something

examples.en: The price cap on bus fares will come into effect in April.
examples.zh: 巴士票价上限将于四月生效。

senses.def: limits that a government puts on the price of goods at particular times, such as when there is not enough of something, when there is a war, etc.
senses.zh: （物品短缺或战时等的）物价控制，价格管制

senses.def: the practice of companies agreeing not to sell goods below a particular price
senses.zh: 价格垄断（公司之间协议不低于某价位销售货品）

senses.def: the action or practice of increasing prices a lot, especially in order to take advantage of sudden high demand

examples.en: Drug and medical supplies companies were accused of price gouging in the early stages of the pandemic.
examples.zh: 药品和医疗用品公司被指控在大流行的早期阶段哄抬价格。

senses.def: a list of the prices of some ordinary goods and services which shows how much these prices change each month
a list of the prices of the goods or services that are offered by a company
one of the possible prices that a company can charge for a product or service in order to create a high demand for it

examples.en: They don't want to cheapen the brand by going with a lower price point for their new car.
examples.zh: 他们不想通过降低新车的价格来降低品牌的价格。

senses.def: a label on something that shows how much you must pay

examples.en: I got a shock when I looked at the price tag.
examples.zh: 看到价格标签，我大吃一惊。

examples.en: There is a £50 million price tag on the team's star player.
examples.zh: 这个球队的明星球员身价为 5 000 万英镑。

senses.def: a situation in which companies or shops keep reducing the prices of their products and services in order to attract customers away from their competitors
senses.zh: 价格战（以减价来吸引顾客）

examples.en: All the large supermarket chains are currently locked in a price war.
examples.zh: 目前各大连锁超市都陷入了价格战。

senses.def: extremely valuable or important
senses.zh: 无价的；极珍贵的；极重要的

examples.en: a priceless collection of antiques
examples.zh: 价值连城的古文物收藏

examples.en: priceless information
examples.zh: 极有价值的信息

examples.en: Our family photos are priceless.
examples.zh: 我们的家庭照极其珍贵。

senses.def: extremely funny
senses.zh: 滑稽的；极可笑的；令人捧腹的

examples.en: You should have seen his face—it was priceless!
examples.zh: 你真该见识见识他那副尊容，可笑极了！

intro.en: These words all describe something that is worth a lot of money or very important to somebody.
intro.zh: 以上各词均用以形容物品值钱、宝贵。

items.def: worth a lot of money:
items.zh: 指值钱的、贵重的

examples.en: The thieves took three pieces of valuable jewellery.
examples.zh: 窃贼盗走了三件贵重的首饰。

items.def: rare and worth a lot of money; loved or valued very much:
items.zh: 指珍稀的、珍贵的、宝贵的

examples.en: a precious Chinese vase, valued at half a million pounds
examples.zh: 价值 50 万英镑的稀世中国花瓶

items.def: extremely valuable; loved or valued very much:
items.zh: 指无价的、极珍贵的、极宝贵的

examples.en: a priceless collection of antiques
examples.zh: 价值连城的古文物收藏

items.def: too valuable or special to be replaced
items.zh: 指因贵重或独特而不能替代的

examples.zh: 菜单可能看起来很贵，但实际上物有所值。

intro.en: These words all describe something that costs a lot of money.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示昂贵、花钱多。

examples.en: I can’t afford it—it’s just too expensive for me.
examples.zh: 我买不起，对我来说这太贵了。

items.def: (rather formal) costing a lot of money, especially more than you want to pay:

examples.en: You want to avoid costly legal proceedings if you can.
examples.zh: 可能的话，你应该避免昂贵的法律诉讼。

items.def: too expensive; costing more than it is worth:

examples.en: ridiculously overpriced designer clothes
examples.zh: 贵得离谱的名牌衣服

items.def: (informal) expensive:
items.zh: 指昂贵的、价格高的

examples.en: Houses in the village are now too pricey for local people to afford.
examples.zh: 如今该村镇的房价太高，当地人根本买不起。

items.def: [not usually before noun] (British English英式英语) expensive:

examples.en: Everything’s so dear now, isn’t it?
examples.zh: 现在什么东西都那么贵，是不是？

examples.zh: 他把气球扎爆了。

examples.zh: 用大头针在纸上扎洞。

examples.zh: 她一听到他的名字，耳朵就立刻竖了起来。

examples.en: I walked along, ears pricked for the slightest noise.
examples.zh: 我沿着路走着，竖起耳朵来倾听最轻微的声音。

examples.en: I'm going to give your finger a little prick with this needle.

senses.def: a slight pain caused by a sharp point or something that feels like a sharp point

examples.en: He could feel the hot prick of tears in his eyes.

examples.en: He prickled (= became angry) at the suggestion that it had been his fault.
examples.zh: 一听说过错在他，他马上火儿了。

examples.en: The hedgehog curled up in a prickly ball.

examples.zh: 看到儿子毕业她充满了自豪。

examples.zh: 当人们停下来欣赏他的花园时，他感到一阵自豪。

examples.zh: 他们对自己的工作有很强的自尊感。

examples.zh: 他们的公平声誉是值得骄傲的。

examples.en: We take great pride in offering the best service in town.
examples.zh: 我们以能够提供全城最好的服务而自豪。

examples.en: I looked with pride at what I had achieved.
examples.zh: 回顾过去的成就，我感到十分光荣。

senses.def: a person or thing that makes people feel pleased or satisfied

examples.zh: 新体育场是这个城市的骄傲。

senses.def: the feeling of respect that you have for yourself
