senses.zh: 真爱尔啤酒（用传统方法制作，木桶储存，不充气）

senses.def: property in the form of land or buildings

examples.en: My father sold real estate.
examples.zh: 我父亲经营过房地产。

senses.def: the business of selling houses or land for building
senses.zh: 房地产业；房地产销售业

examples.en: to work in real estate
examples.zh: 经营房地产

senses.def: (especially on a web page) space that is useful or valuable
senses.zh: （尤指网页上）有用的空间，有价值的空间

examples.en: A company's home page is its most valuable real estate.
examples.zh: 一家公司的主页是其最有价值的网上空间。

examples.en: You can increase screen real estate by moving the taskbar to the right of the screen.
examples.zh: 将任务栏移到屏幕右侧可以增加屏幕的使用空间。

senses.def: a person whose job is to sell houses and land for people
actually happening or existing in life, not in books, stories or films
senses.zh: 真实的；实际发生的；现实生活中的

examples.en: a novel based on real-life events
examples.zh: 以真实事件为素材的小说

examples.en: a real-life Romeo and Juliet
examples.zh: 现实生活中的罗密欧与朱丽叶

examples.en: a real-life drama
examples.zh: 取材于现实生活的戏剧

senses.def: any number that is not an imaginary number
an old form of tennis
senses.zh: 庭院网球（使用硬球的旧式室内网球运动）

senses.def: the fact that there is only a very short time between a computer system receiving information and dealing with it

examples.en: To make the training realistic the simulation operates in real time.
examples.zh: 为使训练真实，模拟是实时运行的。

examples.en: real-time missile guidance systems
examples.zh: 实时导弹制导系统

senses.def: existing in the real world and not specially invented for a particular purpose
senses.zh: 存在于现实世界的；真实的

examples.en: Teachers need to prepare their students to deal with real-world situations outside the classroom.
examples.zh: 教师应该让学生做好应对课堂以外的现实世界的准备。

senses.def: ordinary objects used in a class for teaching purposes
senses.zh: 实物教具（用于教学的日常用品）

senses.def: to change the position or direction of something slightly

examples.en: The road was realigned to improve visibility.
examples.zh: 道路做了调整，以提高能见度。

examples.en: The physiotherapist massaged the shoulder to realign the joint.
examples.zh: 物理治疗师按摩肩膀以重新调整关节。

senses.def: to make changes to something in order to adapt it to a new situation
senses.zh: 对…进行调整；使适应新形势

examples.en: The company has been forced to realign its operations in the area.
examples.zh: 公司被迫对这一领域的经营做了调整。

senses.def: to change your opinions, policies, etc. so that they are the same as those of another person, group, etc.
senses.zh: 改变观点，改变策略（以与别人相同）

examples.en: The rebel MPs have realigned themselves with the opposition party.
examples.zh: 几个造反的下院议员已与反对党站在一起。

senses.def: the act of changing the position or direction of something slightly
senses.zh: 稍微改变某物的位置或方向的行为

examples.en: the realignment of a main road
examples.zh: 主要道路的重新调整

senses.def: the act of making changes to something in order to adapt it to a new situation
senses.zh: 改变自己的观点、政策等，使其与另一个人、团体的观点、政策等相同的行为。

examples.en: the realignment of personal goals
examples.zh: 个人目标的调整

senses.def: the act of changing your opinions, policies, etc. so that they are the same as those of another person, group, etc.
senses.zh: 改变观点，改变策略（以与别人相同）

examples.en: political realignments
examples.zh: 政治重组

senses.def: a way of seeing, accepting and dealing with situations as they really are without being influenced by your emotions or false hopes
senses.zh: 务实作风；现实主义方式

examples.en: There was a new mood of realism among the leaders at the peace talks.
examples.zh: 参加和平谈判的领导人之间有着一种务实的新气氛。

senses.def: the quality of being very like real life

examples.en: the gritty realism of the new drama serial
examples.zh: 新连续剧的坚韧现实主义

senses.def: a style in art or literature that shows things and people as they are in real life
senses.zh: （文艺的）现实主义风格，现实主义

examples.en: realism in Dutch art
examples.zh: 荷兰艺术中的现实主义

examples.en: the Soviet adoption of socialist realism in art
examples.zh: 苏联在艺术上采取的社会主义现实主义

senses.def: a person who accepts and deals with a situation as it really is and does not try to pretend that it is different

examples.en: I'm a realist—I know you can't change people overnight.
examples.zh: 我是个务实的人，我知道人不可能一夜之间被改变。

senses.def: a writer, painter, etc. whose work represents things as they are in real life
senses.zh: 现实主义作家（或画家等）

senses.def: accepting in a sensible way what it is actually possible to do or achieve in a particular situation
senses.zh: 现实的；实际的；实事求是的

examples.en: a realistic assessment/approach/view
examples.zh: 实事求是的评估／方法／观点

examples.en: We have to be realistic about our chances of winning.
examples.zh: 我们必须实事求是地估计我们获胜的可能性。

examples.en: It is not realistic to expect people to spend so much money.
examples.zh: 期望人们花那么多的钱是不实际的。

examples.en: It would not be realistic for the Government to demand a pay freeze in the sector at this point.
examples.zh: 政府目前要求该行业冻结工资是不现实的。

senses.def: sensible and appropriate; possible to achieve
senses.zh: 明智的；恰如其分的；能够实现的

examples.en: a realistic prospect/chance/possibility
examples.zh: 现实的前景／机会／可能性

examples.en: a realistic alternative/option
examples.zh: 现实的选择

examples.en: The important thing is to have realistic expectations about what you can and can't accomplish.
examples.zh: 重要的是对你能完成什么和不能完成什么抱有现实的期望。

examples.en: We must set realistic goals.
examples.zh: 我们必须制订可实现的目标。

examples.en: a realistic target
examples.zh: 切实的目标

examples.en: If you want to retain good employees, you have to pay a realistic salary.
examples.zh: 要留住好员工，必须支付合理的薪水。

senses.def: representing things as they are in real life

examples.en: a realistic portrayal/depiction/picture
examples.zh: 逼真的描绘

examples.en: She made a very realistic drawing of a horse.
examples.zh: 她画了一匹马，非常逼真。

examples.en: We try to make these training courses as realistic as possible.
examples.zh: 我们努力使这些训练课程尽可能地贴近实际情况。

examples.en: The realistic graphics really bring the game to life.
examples.zh: 逼真的图形确实让游戏变得栩栩如生。

senses.def: used to say what you think can actually be achieved in a particular situation
senses.zh: （表明你认为实际实现的可能性）如实地，实际地

examples.en: Realistically, there is little prospect of a ceasefire.
examples.zh: 实事求是地讲，停火的希望很渺茫。

senses.def: in a way that shows somebody accepts in a sensible way what it is actually possible to do or achieve

examples.en: How many can you realistically hope to sell?
examples.zh: 实事求是地讲，你希望能卖出多少？

examples.en: Kate spoke realistically about the task ahead.
examples.zh: 凯特如实地谈了面临的任务。

senses.def: in a way that represents things as they are in real life

examples.en: a fireplace with realistically glowing coals
examples.zh: 有逼真的炉火闪耀的壁炉

senses.def: the true situation and the problems that actually exist in life, in contrast to how you would like life to be

examples.en: She refuses to face reality.
examples.zh: 她不肯面对现实。

examples.en: You're out of touch with reality.
examples.zh: 你脱离了现实。

examples.en: The reality is that there is not enough money to pay for this project.
examples.zh: 实际情况是没有足够的钱花在这个项目上。

examples.en: They seemed to have the perfect marriage but the reality was very different.
examples.zh: 他们的婚姻看似完美，但现实却大不相同。

examples.en: I'm having a hard time adjusting to the reality of this situation.
examples.zh: 我很难适应这种情况的现实。

examples.en: He needs to accept the reality that his time in this job is over.
examples.zh: 他需要接受这样的现实：他在这份工作上的时间已经结束了。

senses.def: a thing that is actually experienced or seen, in contrast to what people might imagine
senses.zh: 事实；实际经历；见到的事物

examples.en: Will time travel ever become a reality?
examples.zh: 时光旅行真的会成为现实吗？

examples.en: The paperless office is still far from being a reality.
examples.zh: 无纸化办公还远未成为现实。

examples.en: As children they experienced the harsh realities of life.
examples.zh: 他们在童年时经历了严酷的生活。

examples.en: This decision reflects the realities of the political situation.
examples.zh: 这一决定反映了政治形势的真实情况。

examples.en: Politicians should not ignore economic realities for short-term political gain.
examples.zh: 政治家不应为了短期政治利益而忽视经济现实。

examples.en: It took five years to make her idea a reality.
examples.zh: 她花了五年时间才把这个想法变成现实。

examples.en: Money is the key to turning dreams into a reality.
examples.zh: 金钱是将梦想变为现实的关键。

senses.def: television/shows, etc. that use real people (not actors) in real situations, presented as entertainment

examples.en: the reality show ‘Survivor’
examples.zh: 真人秀节目《幸存者》

senses.def: used to say that a situation is different from what has just been said or from what people believe

examples.en: Outwardly she seemed confident but in reality she felt extremely nervous.
examples.zh: 表面上看，她显得信心十足，而实际上她紧张得要命。

examples.en: In reality, human beings and dinosaurs never lived on earth at the same time.
examples.zh: 事实上，人类和恐龙从未同时生活在地球上。

examples.en: The media portray her as happy and successful, but in reality she has a difficult life.
examples.zh: 媒体把她描述得快乐而成功，而事实上她过着艰难的生活。

senses.def: used to say that a situation is different from what has just been said or from what people believe

examples.en: Outwardly she seemed confident but in reality she felt extremely nervous.
examples.zh: 表面上看，她显得信心十足，而实际上她紧张得要命。

examples.en: In reality, human beings and dinosaurs never lived on earth at the same time.
examples.zh: 事实上，人类和恐龙从未同时生活在地球上。

examples.en: The media portray her as happy and successful, but in reality she has a difficult life.
examples.zh: 媒体把她描述得快乐而成功，而事实上她过着艰难的生活。

senses.def: an occasion when you are reminded of how things are in the real world, rather than how you would like things to be
senses.zh: （提醒人面对现实而不再想当然的）现实感检验

examples.en: It’s time for a reality check—you’re never going to finish that book.
examples.zh: 是时候审视一下现实了——你永远也读不完那本书。

senses.def: television shows that are based on real people (not actors) in real situations, presented as entertainment

examples.en: a reality TV star
examples.zh: 一个真人秀电视明星

senses.def: possible to achieve or make happen

examples.en: realizable objectives
examples.zh: 可实现的目标

senses.def: that can be sold and turned into money
senses.zh: 可兑现的；可变为现金的

examples.en: realizable assets
examples.zh: 可变现资产

senses.def: the process of becoming aware of something

examples.en: As realization dawned, he went pale.
examples.zh: 当他意识到这一点时，他的脸色变得苍白。

examples.en: the sudden realization of what she had done
examples.zh: 突然意识到她自己究竟干了些什么

examples.en: There is a growing realization that changes must be made.
examples.zh: 越来越多的人认识到改革势在必行。

senses.def: the process of achieving a particular aim, etc.

examples.en: It was the realization of his greatest ambition.
examples.zh: 这就实现了他的宏伟抱负。

examples.en: the realization of political goals
examples.zh: 政治目标的实现

senses.def: the act of selling something that you own, such as property, in order to get the money that you need for something
the act of producing a sound, play, design, etc.; or the thing that is produced
senses.zh: 发声；（戏剧）演出；设计成果

senses.def: to understand or become aware of a particular fact or situation
senses.zh: 理解；领会；认识到；意识到

examples.en: I didn’t realize (that) you were so unhappy.
examples.zh: 我没有察觉到你那么不开心。

examples.en: The moment I saw her, I realized something was wrong.
examples.zh: 我一看到她，就觉得不太对劲。

examples.en: I finally came to realize that he would never change.
examples.zh: 我最后终于意识到他永远不会改变。

examples.en: It is important to realize that there are still potential problems.
examples.zh: 重要的是要认识到仍然存在潜在的问题。

examples.en: I don't think you realize how important this is to her.
examples.zh: 我认为你没有意识到这对她是多么重要。

examples.en: They hadn't realized just how much time it would take.
examples.zh: 他们没有意识到这需要多少时间。

examples.en: Many families fail to realize the importance of a well-balanced diet
examples.zh: 许多家庭没有意识到均衡饮食的重要性。

examples.en: Only later did she realize her mistake.
examples.zh: 只是到了后来她才意识到自己的错误。

examples.en: I hope you realize the seriousness of this crime.
examples.zh: 我希望你能认识到这一罪行的严重性。

examples.en: The situation was more complicated than they had at first realized.
examples.zh: 形势比他们最初意识到的更为复杂。

examples.en: They managed to leave without any of us realizing.
examples.zh: 我们谁也没注意，他们悄悄走了。

examples.en: There was a cheer when it was realized that everyone was safely back.
examples.zh: 人们意识到大家都已平安归来的时候便发出了一阵欢呼声。

senses.def: to achieve something important that you very much want to do

examples.en: to realize your dream
examples.zh: 实现梦想

examples.en: We try to help all students realize their full potential (= be as successful as they are able to be).
examples.zh: 我们努力帮助所有的学生充分发挥他们的潜力。

examples.en: She never realized her ambition of becoming a professional singer.
examples.zh: 她从未实现成为一名职业歌手的志向。

examples.en: He has fully realized the promise which he showed.
examples.zh: 他已经完全实现了他所做出的承诺。

examples.en: I've finally realized a lifelong ambition.
examples.zh: 我终于实现了毕生的愿望。

senses.def: if somebody’s fears are realized

examples.en: His worst fears were realized when he saw that the door had been forced open.
examples.zh: 他一看门被撬了，就知道最担心的事还是发生了。

senses.def: to sell things that you own, for example property, in order to get the money that you need for something
to be sold for a particular amount of money

examples.en: The paintings realized $2 million at auction.
examples.zh: 这些绘画在拍卖会上以 200 万美元卖出。

senses.def: to produce something that can be seen or heard, based on written information or instructions
senses.zh: 把（概念等）具体表现出来

examples.en: The stage designs have been beautifully realized.
examples.zh: 舞台设计得到了完美的体现。

senses.group: make something real 使成为现实

realize the error of your ways: @@@LINK=see, realize, etc. the error of your ways

senses.def: to change the way money or materials are shared between different people, groups, projects, etc.

examples.en: Government funds were reallocated to the new local authorities.
examples.zh: 政府资金被重新分配给新的地方当局。

senses.def: the act of changing the way money or materials are shared between different people, groups, projects, etc.

examples.en: a reallocation of resources
examples.zh: 资源的重新分配

senses.def: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.en: That's a really good idea.
examples.zh: 这是一个非常好的想法。

examples.en: It's really hard to find a decent job these days.
examples.zh: 现在找一份像样的工作真的很难。

examples.en: It all went really well.
examples.zh: 一切都很顺利。

examples.en: This is a really nice place.
examples.zh: 这是一个非常好的地方。

examples.en: Things are looking really bad for him.
examples.zh: 他的情况看起来很糟糕。

examples.en: It's really important that I speak with her right away.
examples.zh: 我马上和她说话真的很重要。

examples.en: a really hot fire
examples.zh: 好热的炉子

examples.en: I'm really sorry.
examples.zh: 我十分抱歉。

examples.en: She was driving really fast.

senses.def: a cause or an explanation for something that has happened or that somebody has done

examples.en: He said no but he didn't give a reason.
examples.zh: 他说不行，但没有说明原因。

examples.en: She gave no reasons for her decision.
examples.zh: 她没有对她的决定作出任何解释。

examples.en: I have no particular reason for doubting him.
examples.zh: 我没有什么特别的理由怀疑他。

examples.en: There were a number of reasons behind her departure.
examples.zh: 她离开的背后有很多原因。

examples.en: We aren't going for the simple reason that we can't afford it.
examples.zh: 我们不去，只是因为我们负担不起。

examples.en: Job satisfaction is the main reason people remain in jobs or careers.
examples.zh: 工作满意度是人们留在工作或职业生涯的主要原因。

examples.en: The only reason your parents are doing this is because they care so much for you.
examples.zh: 你的父母这样做的唯一原因是他们非常关心你。

examples.en: Give me one good reason why I should help you.
examples.zh: 我为什么要帮你？给我一个充分的理由。

examples.en: I'd like to know the reason why you're so late.
examples.zh: 我想知道你为什么迟到那么长时间。

examples.en: For some reason (= one that I don't know or don't understand) we all have to come in early tomorrow.
examples.zh: 出于某种原因，我们大家明天都不得不早点儿来。

examples.en: For this reason, it's important to have friends who will support you.
examples.zh: 因此，拥有支持你的朋友是很重要的。

examples.en: These rules are there for a very good reason.
examples.zh: 这些规则的存在是有充分理由的。

examples.en: The man attacked me for no apparent reason.
examples.zh: 那个人不知何故攻击我。

examples.en: Sometimes I cry for no reason at all.
examples.zh: 有时我会无缘无故地哭泣。

examples.en: She resigned for personal reasons.
examples.zh: 她出于个人原因而辞职。

examples.en: For obvious reasons the data is not complete.
examples.zh: 由于显而易见的原因，数据并不完整。

examples.en: He wants to keep them all in his office for reasons best known to himself.
examples.zh: 他想把他们都留在他的办公室里，原因只有他自己知道。

examples.en: people who, for whatever reason, are unable to support themselves
examples.zh: 那些因为种种原因不能自立的人

examples.en: For reasons of security the door is always kept locked.
examples.zh: 为了保证安全，门总是锁着的。

examples.en: ‘Why do you want to know?’ ‘No reason’ (= I do not want to say why).
examples.zh: “你为什么想知道？”“不为什么。”

examples.en: ‘Why did she do that?’ ‘She must have her reasons’ (= secret reasons which she does not want to tell).
examples.zh: “她为什么那么做？”“她一定有她的理由。”

examples.en: He was excused by reason of (= because of) his age.
examples.zh: 他因为其年龄而得以免除。

senses.def: a fact that makes it right or fair to do something

examples.en: They have reason to believe she is lying.
examples.zh: 他们有理由相信她在撒谎。

examples.en: We have every reason (= have very good reasons) to feel optimistic.
examples.zh: 我们完全有理由感到乐观。

examples.en: You have no reason to accuse him of laziness.
examples.zh: 你没有理由指责他懒惰。

examples.en: She has good reason to be concerned.
examples.zh: 她有充分的理由担心。

examples.en: There is no reason at all to doubt it.
examples.zh: 完全没有理由怀疑这一点。

examples.en: There is no reason why we should agree to this.
examples.zh: 我们没有理由同意这点。

examples.en: This result gives us all the more reason for optimism.
examples.zh: 这个结果使我们更有理由保持乐观。

examples.en: He has every reason for feeling excited.
examples.zh: 他完全有理由感到兴奋。

examples.en: She complained, with reason (= rightly), that she had been underpaid.
examples.zh: 她抱怨给她的报酬太低，这是有道理的。

senses.def: the power of the mind to think in a logical way, to understand and have opinions, etc.

examples.en: Only human beings are capable of reason (= of thinking in a logical way, etc.).
examples.zh: 只有人类才有理性思考的能力。

examples.en: to lose your reason (= become mentally ill)
examples.zh: 神经失常

examples.en: the conflict between faith and reason
examples.zh: 信仰与理性的冲突

senses.def: what is possible, practical or right

examples.en: I can't get her to listen to reason.
examples.zh: 我没法跟她讲道理。

examples.en: Why can't they see reason?
examples.zh: 他们为什么不明事理？

examples.en: Look, you're supposed to be the voice of reason here.
examples.zh: 听着，你应该是这里能发出理性声音的人。

examples.en: Keith appears to be open to reason (= to be willing to accept sensible advice).
examples.zh: 基思似乎对理性持开放态度（=愿意接受明智的建议）。

examples.en: He's looking for a job and he's willing to do anything within reason.
examples.zh: 他在找工作，而且只要是正当的事他都愿意做。

senses.def: it must be clear to any sensible person who thinks about it
senses.zh: 这是人人都清楚的；这是明摆着的

examples.en: It stands to reason that they'll leave if you don't pay them enough.
examples.zh: 这是明摆着的，你不给他们足够的报酬，他们就走人。

examples.en: It stands to reason that she wouldn't want them to find out about her personal problems.
examples.zh: 她不想让他们知道她的个人问题，这是自然的。

senses.zh: 毫无道理；无规律可循；莫名其妙

examples.zh: 突然，他的心情无缘无故地变了。

examples.en: There's no rhyme or reason to the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 新的营业时间毫无道理。

examples.zh: 她断定她准是把包落在火车上了。

examples.en: They couldn't fire him, he reasoned. He was the only one who knew how the system worked.
examples.zh: 他推断他们不会解雇他。他是唯一知道这套系统如何运转的人。

examples.en: They reasoned, correctly, that the enemy would not attempt an attack at night.
examples.zh: 他们作出了正确推断，敌人不会企图发动夜袭。

examples.zh: 他说不行，但没有说明原因。

items.def: a statement, fact or situation that tells you why something has happened; a reason given for something:
items.zh: 指解释、说明、阐述

examples.en: The most likely explanation is that his plane was delayed.
examples.zh: 最可能的解释是他的飞机晚点了。

items.def: (rather formal) a good or true reason for saying, doing or believing something:
items.zh: 指说、做或相信某事的充分理由、根据

examples.en: You have no grounds for complaint.
examples.zh: 你没有理由抱怨。

items.def: (rather formal) the reason why people take a particular action:
items.zh: 指原因、缘由

examples.en: On what basis will this decision be made?
examples.zh: 将基于何种原因作出这一决定呢？

items.def: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour; a good reason that you give for doing something that you want to do for other reasons:
items.zh: 指为自己行为所作的辩护、借口、理由

examples.en: Late again! What’s your excuse this time?
examples.zh: 又迟到了！你这次有什么借口？

items.def: a reason that explains somebody’s behaviour:
items.zh: 指动机、原因

examples.en: There seemed to be no motive for the murder.
examples.zh: 这起谋杀案看不出有什么动机。

items.def: (rather formal) a good reason why something exists or is done:
items.zh: 指事物存在或做某事的正当理由

examples.en: I can see no possible justification for any further tax increases.
examples.zh: 我看不出还能提出什么理由来加税了。

items.def: (rather formal) a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason:
items.zh: 指为掩盖做某事（通常为不好的事）的真正理由而找的借口、托辞

examples.en: He left the party early on the pretext of having to work.
examples.zh: 他借口有事要处理，早早离开了聚会。

senses.def: to try and find the answer to a problem by using your power to think in a logical way
senses.zh: 通过思考想出对策；推理出（结果）

examples.en: Reason it out for yourself!
examples.zh: 你自己推理一下吧！

senses.def: to talk to somebody in order to persuade them to be more sensible

examples.en: I tried to reason with him, but he wouldn't listen.
examples.zh: 我尽量跟他讲道理，可他就是不听。

senses.def: fair, practical, and sensible
senses.zh: 公平的；合理的；有理由的；明智的

examples.en: It is reasonable to assume that he knew beforehand that this would happen.
examples.zh: 有理由认为，他事先就知道会发生这样的事。

examples.en: As life expectancy increases, it is reasonable to expect that the retirement age will increase too.
examples.zh: 随着预期寿命的增加，预计退休年龄也会增加是合理的。

examples.en: It seems reasonable to conclude that their claims are unfounded.
examples.zh: 似乎可以合理地得出结论，他们的主张毫无根据。

examples.en: Is it not reasonable for the government to look for savings and efficiencies?
examples.zh: 政府追求节约和效率难道不合理吗？

examples.en: Be reasonable! We can't work late every night.
examples.zh: 要讲道理呀！我们不能每天晚上都加班呀。

examples.en: The prosecution has to prove beyond (a) reasonable doubt that he is guilty of murder.
examples.zh: 控方必须毫无疑义地证明他犯有谋杀罪。

examples.en: We have reasonable grounds for believing that you are responsible.
examples.zh: 我们有理由相信你有责任。

examples.en: Any reasonable person would have done exactly as you did.
examples.zh: 任何有头脑的人都会完全像你那样去做的。

examples.en: You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the information that you provide is correct.
examples.zh: 您必须采取一切合理步骤确保您提供的信息正确。

examples.en: It seems a perfectly reasonable request to make.
examples.zh: 这看起来是一个非常合理的请求。

examples.en: If companies expect work during personal time, it's only reasonable to allow personal time at work.
examples.zh: 如果公司希望员工在私人时间也工作，那么允许员工在工作时间干私活才是合理的。

examples.en: I considered the evidence in order to decide what is fair and reasonable in the circumstances.
examples.zh: 我考虑了证据，以决定在这种情况下什么是公平合理的。

senses.def: acceptable and appropriate in a particular situation
senses.zh: 可以接受的；合乎情理的；公道的

examples.en: The police apparently thought this explanation perfectly reasonable.
examples.zh: 警方显然认为这个解释完全合理。

examples.en: The judge said they had a reasonable expectation of privacy relating to the information concerned.
examples.zh: 法官说，他们对有关信息的隐私问题有合理的期望。

examples.en: He made us a reasonable offer for the car.
examples.zh: 他给我们出的车价公平合理。

examples.en: You must submit your claim within a reasonable time.
examples.zh: 你必须在适当的时间内提出要求。

examples.en: It can even be done as a class project in a reasonable amount of time.
examples.zh: 它甚至可以作为课堂项目在合理的时间内完成。

examples.en: The adviser must take reasonable care to ensure that the information is correct
examples.zh: 顾问必须采取合理的谨慎措施以确保信息正确

senses.def: not too expensive

examples.en: We sell good-quality food at reasonable prices.
examples.zh: 我们以公道的价格出售优质食品。

examples.en: He believes NASA can reach Mars at a reasonable cost.
examples.zh: 他相信美国宇航局能够以合理的成本到达火星。

examples.en: If the price is reasonable, we'll buy it.
examples.zh: 要是价格公道，我们就买。

senses.def: fairly good, but not very good
senses.zh: 不错的；还算好的；过得去的

examples.en: Most people here have a reasonable standard of living.
examples.zh: 这里大部分人生活水平还不错。

examples.en: The hotel was reasonable, I suppose (= but not excellent).
examples.zh: 我觉得这家酒店还可以。

examples.en: There's a reasonable chance that he'll come.
examples.zh: 他还是有可能来的。

examples.en: The furniture is in reasonable condition.
examples.zh: 家具的状况还过得去。

intro.en: These words all describe a product or service that costs little money or less money than you expected.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指产品或服务花钱少或低于预期。

items.def: costing little money or less money than you expected; charging low prices. Cheap can also be used in a disapproving way to suggest that something is of poor quality as well as low in price:
items.zh: cheap 亦可作贬义，指价低质劣

items.def: (of prices, goods or services) as cheap as or cheaper than those offered by other companies; able to offer goods or services at competitive prices.
items.zh: 指价格、产品或服务收费方面具有竞争力

items.def: [only before noun] (used especially in advertising) cheap because it offers only a basic level of service.
items.zh: 指仅提供基本服务因而价格低廉

items.def: cheap enough for most people to afford.
items.zh: 指多数人买得起或负担得来的

items.def: (of prices) not too expensive.
items.zh: 指价格不太高、公道的

items.def: (rather formal) cheap. Inexpensive is often used to mean that something is good value for its price. It is sometimes used instead of cheap, because cheap can suggest that something is of poor quality.
items.zh: inexpensive 常含物有所值之义，有时用以代替 cheap，因为 cheap 可有质量低劣的含义。

senses.def: the fact of being fair, practical and sensible

examples.en: The court must determine the reasonableness of the costs claimed.
examples.zh: 法院必须确定索赔费用的合理性。

examples.en: She spoke with an air of sweet reasonableness.
examples.zh: 她说话时带着一种甜蜜合理的神情。

senses.def: to a degree that is fairly good but not very good

examples.en: The instructions are reasonably straightforward.
examples.zh: 用法说明还算简单易懂。

examples.en: She seems reasonably happy in her new job.
examples.zh: 她在新的工作岗位上好像还挺开心。

senses.def: in a logical and sensible way
senses.zh: 合情合理地；明智地；通情达理地

examples.en: We tried to discuss the matter calmly and reasonably.
examples.zh: 我们试图冷静且通情达理地来讨论这个问题。

senses.def: in a fair way

examples.en: He couldn't reasonably be expected to pay back the loan all at once.
examples.zh: 公平合理地讲，不可能指望他一下子归还全部借款。

examples.en: The apartments are reasonably priced (= not too expensive).
examples.zh: 这些公寓房价格合理。

senses.def: to fit the parts of something together again after it has been taken apart

examples.en: We had to take the table apart and reassemble it upstairs.
examples.zh: 我们只好先把桌子拆开，到楼上再组装起来。

senses.def: to meet together again as a group after a break

examples.en: The class reassembled after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后，全班同学又集合起来。

senses.def: to make other people recognize again your right or authority to do something, after a period when this has been in doubt

examples.en: She found it necessary to reassert her position.
examples.zh: 她觉得有必要重申她的立场。

senses.def: to start to have an effect again, after a period of not having any effect

examples.en: He thought about giving up his job, but then common sense reasserted itself.
examples.zh: 他曾想放弃这份工作，但后来还是理智占了上风。

senses.def: to state again, clearly and definitely, that something is true

examples.en: He reasserted that all parties should be involved in the talks.
examples.zh: 他再次声明各方均应参加会谈。

examples.en: Traditional values have been reasserted.
examples.zh: 传统价值观再次得到肯定。

senses.def: the act of making other people recognize again your right or authority to do something, after a period when this has been in doubt

examples.en: an aggressive reassertion of authority
examples.zh: 积极地重申权威

senses.def: the act of stating again, clearly and definitely, that something is true

examples.en: This repeated reassertion that the debate is over clearly shows that it is not over at all.
examples.zh: 反复重申辩论已经结束，这清楚地表明辩论根本没有结束。

senses.def: to think again about something to decide if you need to change your opinion of it

examples.en: After reassessing the situation, she decided to do nothing.
examples.zh: 重新评估情况后，她决定什么也不做。

senses.def: the act of thinking again about something to decide if you need to change your opinion of it

examples.en: Students were allowed to hand in corrected work again for reassessment.
examples.zh: 学生被允许再次提交更正的作业以进行重新评估。

examples.en: She decided that a complete reassessment of her career was due.
examples.zh: 她决定对自己的职业生涯进行彻底的重新评估。

senses.def: to give somebody a different duty, position or responsibility
senses.zh: 重新委派，再次指派（任务、职位、责任等）

examples.en: After his election defeat he was reassigned to the diplomatic service.
examples.zh: 落选之后，他又被派到外交部门工作。

senses.def: to give something to a different person or organization; to change the status of something
senses.zh: 重新分配…（给某人或机构）；重新指定

examples.en: The case was reassigned to a different court.
examples.zh: 这桩案件已交由另一法院审理。

senses.def: the act of giving somebody a different duty, position or responsibility
senses.zh: 再指派（工作）;再指定（职位）

examples.en: Her reassignment is part of a new global restructuring.
examples.zh: 她的调动是新的全球重组的一部分。

senses.def: the act of giving something to a different person or organization; the act of changing the status of something
senses.zh: （将某物）给其他人;（以不同方式）再分配

examples.en: a reassignment of duties
examples.zh: 职责重新分配

senses.def: the fact of giving advice or help that takes away a person’s fears or doubts

examples.en: to give/provide/offer reassurance
examples.zh: 表明肯定的态度

examples.en: Teenagers need love, encouragement and reassurance from their parents.
examples.zh: 青少年需要父母的爱、鼓励和安慰。

examples.en: She is very insecure and constantly seeks reassurance that he loves her.
examples.zh: 她非常没有安全感，不断寻求他爱她的保证。

senses.def: something that is said or done to take away a person’s fears or doubts
senses.zh: 能消除疑虑的话（或行动）；保证

examples.en: We have been given reassurances that the water is safe to drink.
examples.zh: 我们得到保证说这水适合饮用。

senses.def: to say or do something that makes somebody less frightened or worried

examples.en: They tried to reassure her, but she still felt anxious.
examples.zh: 他们设法让她放心，可她还是焦虑不安。

examples.en: The doctor reassured him that there was nothing seriously wrong.
examples.zh: 医生安慰他说，没什么大毛病。

examples.en: She needed to be reassured of his love for her.
examples.zh: 她需要证实他是爱她的。

senses.def: in a way that makes you feel less worried or uncertain about something
senses.zh: 令人感到宽慰的；令人放心的

examples.en: She smiled reassuringly.
examples.zh: 她微微一笑，让人心里踏实。

examples.en: ‘We’ll take good care of you,’ he said reassuringly.
examples.zh: “我们会好好照顾你的。”他安慰道。

senses.def: to make you feel a particular emotion again or to make you remember something again
senses.zh: 勾起，唤起，再次引发（感情、回忆等）

examples.en: The place reawakened childhood memories.
examples.zh: 这地方唤起了童年的回忆。

senses.def: not attractive; causing strong dislike
senses.zh: 无吸引力的；令人厌恶的

examples.en: rebarbative modern buildings
examples.zh: 丑陋的现代建筑。

senses.def: an amount of money that is paid back to you because you have paid too much

examples.en: She's claiming a 100% tax rebate.
examples.zh: 她正在索要百分之百的退税。

senses.def: an amount of money that is taken away from the cost of something, before you pay for it
senses.zh: 折扣，返还（退还的部分货价）

examples.en: Buyers are offered a cash rebate.
examples.zh: 购买者享受现金折扣。

examples.en: The maximum cash rebate available is about $4 800.
examples.zh: 最大的现金折扣约为 4,800 美元。

senses.def: a first name for girls
(1892-1983) an English writer and journalist. She wrote many novels, including The Thinking Reed
senses.zh: 丽贝卡·韦斯特（Rebecca West）：（1892-1983）英国作家和记者。她写了许多小说，包括《思考的里德》（1936年），《喷泉泛滥》（1956年）和《鸟儿掉下来》（1966年），但由于她作为记者的工作而写的书而被人们所铭记。其中包括有关间谍伯吉斯和麦克林的《叛国罪的意义》（The Treason，1949年）和有关纽伦堡审判的《粉末火车》（A Train of Powder，1955年）。韦斯特与作家HG威尔斯（HG Wells）有着悠久的恋情。她于1959年当上贵妇。

senses.def: a person who fights against the government of their country
senses.zh: 反政府的人；叛乱者；造反者

examples.en: rebel forces
examples.zh: 叛乱武装

examples.en: Armed rebels advanced towards the capital.
examples.zh: 武装叛乱分子向首都推进。

examples.en: Some parts of the country fell into rebel hands.
examples.zh: 该国的一些地区落入叛军之手。

senses.def: a person who opposes somebody in authority over them within an organization, a political party, etc.

examples.en: A number of Tory rebels are planning to vote against the government.
examples.zh: 一些保守党人倒戈，计划投票反对政府。

examples.en: The Education Secretary has made further concessions to the back-bench rebels.
examples.zh: 教育部长对持反对意见的后座议员作出了进一步的让步。

senses.def: a person who does not like to obey rules or who does not follow generally accepted standards of behaviour, dress, etc.

examples.en: I've always been the rebel of the family.
examples.zh: 我在家里向来是个叛逆者。

examples.en: He was a rebel in his teens but he’s a respectable citizen these days.
examples.zh: 他十几岁的时候是一个叛逆者，但现在他是一个受人尊敬的公民。

senses.def: to fight against or refuse to obey an authority, for example a government, a system, your parents, etc.

examples.en: He later rebelled against his strict religious upbringing.
examples.zh: 他后来背叛了他所受的严格的宗教教育。

examples.en: Most teenagers find something to rebel against.
examples.zh: 大多数青少年都有反抗意识。

examples.en: In 1215 the barons rebelled against the king.
examples.zh: 1215年，贵族们反抗国王的统治。

examples.en: The colonies rebelled and declared their independence.
examples.zh: 各殖民地起来反抗并宣布独立。

senses.def: the US film (1955) which made James Dean
senses.zh: 叛逆无故：美国电影（1955年），詹姆斯·迪恩（James Dean）出名。他扮演一个年轻人，他抗拒父母的权威并与警察发生纠纷。这部电影使许多美国父母感到震惊，因为这部电影显示来自好家庭的孩子对自己的舒适生活方式不满意。

senses.def: an attempt by some of the people in a country to change their government, using violence

examples.en: The north of the country rose in rebellion against the government.
examples.zh: 这个国家的北方地区发生了反对政府的叛乱。

examples.en: The army put down the rebellion.
examples.zh: 军队镇压了叛乱。

senses.def: opposition to authority within an organization, a political party, etc.

examples.en: Some members are in rebellion against proposed cuts in spending.
examples.zh: 一些成员反对削减开支的提议。

examples.en: The prime minister faces a rebellion from junior members of her party.
examples.zh: 首相面临着党内下级成员的反对。

senses.def: opposition to authority; being unwilling to obey rules or accept normal standards of behaviour, dress, etc.

examples.en: Teenage rebellion often starts in the home.
examples.zh: 青少年的叛逆常常始于家庭。

examples.en: rebellion against their parents
examples.zh: 他们与父母对抗

examples.en: The band refused to go on stage and rebellion began to stir in the audience.
examples.zh: 乐队拒绝上台，激起了观众的敌对情绪。

senses.def: unwilling to obey rules or follow generally accepted standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
senses.zh: 反叛的；叛逆的；桀骜不驯的

examples.en: rebellious teenagers
examples.zh: 叛逆的青少年

examples.en: He has always had a rebellious streak.
examples.zh: 他总是有点叛逆。

senses.def: opposed to the government of a country; opposed to those in authority within an organization
senses.zh: 叛乱的；造反的；反对权威的

examples.en: rebellious cities/factions
examples.zh: 叛乱的城市；反对派别

examples.en: Rebellious MPs are threatening to vote against the government.
examples.zh: 叛逆的议员威胁要投票反对政府。

senses.def: in a way that shows that you are unwilling to obey rules or follow generally accepted standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
senses.zh: 反叛地；叛逆地；桀骜不驯地

examples.en: ‘I don't care!’ she said rebelliously.
examples.zh: “我不在乎！”她桀骜不驯地说道。

senses.def: in a way that is opposed to the government of a country or to those in authority within an organization
senses.zh: 叛乱的；造反的；反对权威的

examples.en: He incited the people to rise up rebelliously against the king.
examples.zh: 他煽动人民起来反抗国王。

senses.def: the fact of being unwilling to obey rules or follow generally accepted standards of behaviour, dress, etc.
senses.zh: 桀骜不驯;难以控制;难对付

examples.en: teenage rebelliousness
examples.zh: 青少年的叛逆

senses.def: the fact of being opposed to the government of a country or to those in authority within an organization
senses.zh: 叛乱的；造反的；反对权威的

examples.en: His growing rebelliousness got him transferred in 1950 to a labour camp.
examples.zh: 1950 年，他日益增长的叛逆情绪导致他被转移到劳改营。

senses.def: a period of new life, growth or activity

examples.en: the seasonal cycle of death and rebirth
examples.zh: 死而复生的四季轮回

examples.en: The company underwent a rebirth five years ago and is now a market leader.
examples.zh: 该公司五年前经历了重生，现在已成为市场领导者。

examples.en: the rebirth of a ferry link between Liverpool and Ireland
examples.zh: 利物浦和爱尔兰之间的渡轮航线的重生

senses.def: a spiritual change when a person’s faith becomes stronger or they move to another religion
senses.zh: （信仰加强或皈依另一宗教后精神上的）新生，再生

senses.def: a type of psychotherapy
senses.zh: 呼吸重生法，再生疗法（通过控制呼吸重新体验出生的心理疗法）

senses.def: the act of starting a computer, smartphone, etc. again immediately after you have switched it off

examples.en: After a reboot, the program started working again.
examples.zh: 重启后，程序又开始运行了。

senses.def: something, especially a series of films or TV programmes, that has been started again or made successful again
senses.zh: （电影或电视节目的）重拍或重拍版

examples.en: the trailer for the ‘Spider Man’ reboot
examples.zh: 《蜘蛛侠》重启的预告片

senses.def: if you reboot
to make something, especially a series of films or TV programmes, start again or become successful again
senses.zh: 使（电影或电视系列节目）重新开始；使再获成功

examples.en: This film is the producer's second attempt to reboot the franchise.
examples.zh: 这部电影是制片人第二次尝试重启该系列。

examples.en: The government is desperately trying to reboot the country's economy.
examples.zh: 政府正竭尽全力重振国家经济。

examples.en: The talented boxer is trying to reboot his career following his recovery from injury.
examples.zh: 这位天才拳击手伤愈后正试图重新开始他的职业生涯。

senses.def: to become active or popular again

examples.en: With the coming of television, old legends such as those of Robin Hood and King Arthur were reborn.
examples.zh: 随着电视的出现，罗宾汉和亚瑟王等古老的传说重生。

senses.def: to be born again

examples.en: If you were reborn as an animal, which animal would you be?
examples.zh: 如果你转世成为动物，你愿意做哪种动物？

senses.def: having become active again

examples.en: a reborn version of social democracy
examples.zh: 一种社会民主主义的翻版

senses.def: having experienced a complete spiritual change

examples.en: After the workshop I felt reborn and full of hope.
examples.zh: 工作坊结束后，我感到重获新生，充满希望。

senses.def: to bounce

examples.en: The ball rebounded from the goalpost and she headed it in.
examples.zh: 球从门柱反弹，她头球破门。

senses.def: if something that you do rebounds
to rise again after they have fallen

examples.en: Share prices rebounded after Friday’s losses.
examples.zh: 股价在周五下跌后反弹。

senses.def: (of a person) to have an illness again, especally after stopping taking medicine; (of an illness) to happen again

examples.zh: 我很高兴收到你的来信。

examples.zh: 她收到了许多支持的信息。

examples.zh: 几名乘客受了重伤。

examples.zh: 最近出版的一本书

examples.zh: 最近发布的一份报告

examples.zh: 该公司最近宣布了裁员五分之一的计划。

examples.zh: 她最近完成了一项对参与者的后续研究。

examples.zh: 最近举行了公开会议来讨论这些提案。

examples.en: The company has recently signed a deal with a major bank.
examples.zh: 该公司最近与一家大银行签署了一项协议。

senses.def: a container for putting something in

examples.en: In the backyard there was a large receptacle for catching rainwater.
examples.zh: 后院有一个大容器，用来收集雨水。

examples.en: The seas have been used as a receptacle for a range of industrial toxins.
examples.zh: 海洋成了各种有毒工业废料的大容器。

senses.def: a device in a wall that you put a plug
the area inside the entrance of a hotel, an office building, etc. where guests or visitors go first when they arrive

examples.zh: 到达后请立即到接待处报到。

examples.zh: 你可以在接待处留言。

examples.zh: 我们约定 6:30 在接待处会面。

senses.def: a formal social occasion to welcome somebody or celebrate something
senses.zh: 接待仪式；欢迎会；招待会

examples.zh: 婚礼后你们要举行大型招待会吗？

examples.zh: 他们在白宫为日本贸易代表团举行招待会。

examples.zh: 评论家和观众的反应充其量是冷淡的

examples.zh: 乐队受到民众的狂热欢迎。

examples.zh: 由于他呼吁增加教育经费，代表们向他报以热烈的欢迎。

examples.zh: 我的电话接收效果很差。

examples.en: Television reception is very good in this area.
examples.zh: 这一地区的电视接收效果很好。

senses.def: the act of receiving or welcoming somebody

examples.zh: 当地人提供设施接收来自战区的儿童。

senses.zh: （为 4 至 5 岁儿童开设的）学前班，预备班

examples.zh: 我儿子在预备班。

senses.def: an act of catching the ball when it is thrown forward

examples.zh: 四分卫发现他接球后跑动 22 码达阵。

examples.zh: 博物馆正在修建新的来宾接待室。

examples.zh: 议会进入漫长的夏季休会期。

examples.en: The court is in recess until October.
examples.zh: 法庭休庭至十月。

examples.zh: 法官宣布短暂休庭。

examples.zh: 他课间休息时不愿跟我玩耍。

examples.en: I believe kids need more recess time.
examples.zh: 我认为小孩需要更多的课间休息时间。

examples.zh: 放书的壁橱

senses.def: the part of a place that is furthest from the light and hard to see or get to

examples.en: He stared into the dark recesses of the room.
examples.zh: 他盯着房间里黑暗的角落。

examples.en: The doubt was still there, in the deep recesses of her mind.
examples.zh: 在她的内心深处依然存有疑虑。

examples.zh: 听证会周末暂停。

senses.zh: 把…放进壁龛（或壁橱）；将…嵌入墙壁

examples.zh: 灯应嵌入天花板。

examples.en: recessed shelves
examples.zh: 凹进墙壁的格子架

examples.zh: 你如何评价时下经济萎缩对制造业的影响？

examples.zh: 经济正处于严重的衰退之中。

examples.zh: 引导国家走出经济萎缩的政策

examples.en: These industries have been hard hit by recession.
examples.zh: 这些行业受到经济衰退的严重打击。

examples.zh: 他把剃刀插在插座上，给它充电。

examples.en: The drill takes about three hours to recharge.
examples.zh: 钻机充满电大约要三个小时。

senses.zh: 恢复体力；恢复精力；休整

examples.zh: 鸡汤的做法

examples.zh: 素菜食谱

examples.zh: 烹饪书

examples.zh: 您需要仔细遵循食谱。

examples.zh: 她最终说服了她的母亲分享这个食谱。

examples.zh: 这个食谱需要120克黄油。

examples.zh: 来自顶级厨师的 100 道美味食谱合集

examples.en: I tried some recipes from this book.
examples.zh: 我尝试了这本书中的一些食谱。

examples.en: The dish is made to a (= according to) traditional Italian recipe.
examples.zh: 这道菜是用传统的意大利做法制成的。

examples.en: The jam is based on a 14th century recipe.
examples.zh: 这种果酱是根据 14 世纪的配方制作的。

senses.def: a method or an idea that seems likely to have a particular result

examples.en: His plans are a recipe for disaster.
examples.zh: 他的计划后患无穷。

examples.en: What's her recipe for success?
examples.zh: 她成功的秘诀是什么？

examples.en: a recipe for failure/chaos/trouble
examples.zh: 失败/混乱/麻烦的秘诀

senses.def: a person who receives something

examples.zh: 领奖者

senses.def: involving two people or groups who agree to help each other or behave in the same way to each other

examples.en: The two colleges have a reciprocal arrangement whereby students from one college can attend classes at the other.
examples.zh: 两所学院有一项互惠协定，允许学生跨院选课。

examples.en: a reciprocal relationship between citizens and the state
examples.zh: 公民与国家之间的互惠关系

examples.en: Anita had a reciprocal arrangement with her brother—each would take care of the other’s children if the need arose.
examples.zh: 安妮塔与她的兄弟达成了互惠安排——如果有需要，双方都会照顾对方的孩子。

senses.zh: 相互动词，交互动词（如 Paul and Claire kissed 中的 kiss）

senses.def: in a way that involves two people or groups helping each other or behaving in the same way to each other

examples.en: a reciprocally beneficial alliance where both parties give and receive emotional support
examples.zh: 双方给予和接受情感支持的互惠联盟

senses.def: to behave or feel towards somebody in the same way as they behave or feel towards you

examples.en: Her passion for him was not reciprocated.
examples.zh: 她对他的热情没有得到回应。

examples.en: They wanted to reciprocate the kindness that had been shown to them.
examples.zh: 他们想要报答受到过的盛情。

examples.en: He smiled but his smile was not reciprocated.
examples.zh: 他露出微笑，可他的微笑没有得到回应。

examples.en: He chose to reciprocate the gift with a sample of his own art.
examples.zh: 他选择用自己的艺术作品作为回报。

examples.en: I wasn't sure whether to laugh or to reciprocate with a remark of my own.
examples.zh: 我不知道是该笑一笑还是该说点什么作为回应。

examples.zh: 往复运动

a public performance of music or poetry, usually given by one person or a small group
senses.zh: 音乐演奏会；诗歌朗诵会

examples.en: to give a piano recital
examples.zh: 举办钢琴演奏会

examples.en: a recital by the Grieg Trio
examples.zh: 格里格三重奏演奏会

examples.en: They put on a song recital in honour of Mozart’s 250th birthday.
examples.zh: 他们为庆祝莫扎特诞辰250周年举办了一个专场演唱会。

examples.en: They both launched into a recital of their misfortunes.
examples.zh: 他们俩开始讲述自己的不幸经历。

examples.zh: 我们用歌曲和朗诵来娱乐。

examples.en: At that time children were encouraged to learn poems for recitation.
examples.zh: 当时鼓励孩子们学习诗歌背诵。

senses.def: an act of talking or writing about a series of things

examples.en: She continued her recitation of the week's events.
examples.zh: 她接着逐一讲述这一周发生的事。

to say a poem, piece of literature, etc. that you have learned, especially to an audience

examples.en: Each child had to recite a poem to the class.
examples.zh: 每个孩子都得在班上背诵一首诗。

examples.en: She recited what she had learned.
examples.zh: 她背诵了她所学的内容。

examples.en: ‘I wandered lonely as a cloud,’ he recited.
examples.zh: “我像一朵云一样孤独地徘徊，”他背诵道。

senses.def: to say a list or series of things

examples.en: They recited all their grievances to me.
examples.zh: 他们把所受的委屈都告诉了我。

examples.en: She could recite a list of all the kings and queens.
examples.zh: 她能一一说出所有的国王和王后的名字。

senses.def: showing a lack of care about danger and the possible results of your actions
senses.zh: 鲁莽的；不计后果的；无所顾忌的

examples.en: He showed a reckless disregard for his own safety.
examples.zh: 他全然不顾个人安危。

examples.en: She was a good rider, but reckless.
examples.zh: 她是个好骑手，但太鲁莽。

examples.en: to cause death by reckless driving
examples.zh: 鲁莽驾驶造成死亡

examples.en: She threw herself into the game with reckless abandon.
examples.zh: 她不计后果地投入到游戏中。

examples.en: He had always been reckless with money.
examples.zh: 他花钱总是大手大脚。

senses.def: in a way that shows a lack of care about danger and the possible results of your actions
senses.zh: 鲁莽的；不计后果的；无所顾忌的

examples.en: He admitted driving recklessly.
examples.zh: 他承认鲁莽驾驶。

examples.en: She had fallen hopelessly and recklessly in love.
examples.zh: 她恋爱了，爱得无所顾忌，无法自拔。

senses.def: behaviour that shows a lack of care about danger and the possible results of your actions
senses.zh: 表现出对危险和行为可能导致的后果漠不关心的行为

examples.en: He was full of boyish recklessness and irresponsibility.
examples.zh: 他充满了孩子气的鲁莽和不负责任。

senses.def: to think something or have an opinion about something

examples.en: I reckon (that) I’m going to get that job.
examples.zh: 我认为我会得到那份工作。

examples.en: He'll be famous one day. What do you reckon (= do you agree)?
examples.zh: 总有一天，他会成为名人的。你觉得呢？

examples.en: It's worth a lot of money, I reckon.
examples.zh: 我想这值很多钱。

examples.en: ‘They'll never find out.’ ‘You reckon?’ (= I think you may be wrong about that)
examples.zh: “他们永远不会发现。”“是吗？”

senses.def: to be generally considered to be something
senses.zh: 被普遍认为是；被看作是

examples.en: Children are reckoned to be more sophisticated nowadays.
examples.zh: 人们认为今天的孩子比过去世故。

examples.en: It was generally reckoned a success.
examples.zh: 大家都认为那是一次成功。

senses.def: to expect to do something

examples.en: We reckon to finish by ten.
examples.zh: 我们预计十点钟以前结束。

examples.en: He wasn’t reckoning to pay so much.
examples.zh: 他没想到要付出这么多。

senses.def: to calculate an amount, a number, etc.

examples.en: I could see him reckoning the cost as I spoke.
examples.zh: 当我说话时，我可以看到他正在计算成本。

examples.en: The age of the earth is reckoned at about 4.6 billion years.
examples.zh: 估计地球的年龄大约为 46 亿年。

examples.en: My debts were reckoned at $12 000.
examples.zh: 我的债务估计为 12000 美元。

examples.en: They reckon (that) their profits are down by at least 20%.
examples.zh: 他们估计利润至少下降了 20%。

examples.en: It is generally reckoned that about half of all job vacancies are never advertised publicly.
examples.zh: 人们普遍认为，所有职位空缺中约有一半从未公开刊登广告。

examples.en: The journey was reckoned to take about two hours.
examples.zh: 路上估计要花大约两个小时。

examples.en: The trip was reckoned to take over two days.
examples.zh: 这次旅行估计要花两天多。

examples.en: Miyazaki is still a name to conjure with among anime fans.
examples.zh: 宫崎骏在日本动漫迷中仍是一个大名鼎鼎的名字。

examples.zh: 他来自泰纳布鲁厄赫，这个名字真够拗口的！
