examples.zh: 她完全信任他。

senses.def: an extra player who plays in a team when one of the other players is injured or not available to play
a team that is below the level of the main team
an extra military force, etc. that is not part of a country’s regular forces, but is available to be used when needed

examples.en: the Army Reserve
examples.zh: 预备役部队

examples.en: the reserve police
examples.zh: 预备役警察

senses.def: the lowest price that somebody will accept for something, especially something that is sold at an auction

examples.en: The painting failed to reach to its reserve and was withdrawn from the sale.
examples.zh: 这幅画未能达到其保留价，因此被从拍卖中撤回。

senses.def: available to be used in the future or when needed

examples.en: The money was being kept in reserve for their retirement.
examples.zh: 他们把钱存着以备退休后使用。

examples.en: 200 police officers were held in reserve.
examples.zh: 200 名警察随时待命。

senses.def: to ask for a seat, table, room, etc. to be available for you or somebody else at a future time
senses.zh: 预订，预约（座位、席位、房间等）

examples.en: I'd like to reserve a table for three for eight o'clock.
examples.zh: 我想预订八点钟供三人用餐的桌位。

examples.en: I've reserved a room in the name of Jones.
examples.zh: 我以琼斯的名字预订了一个房间。

senses.def: to keep something for somebody/something, so that it cannot be used by any other person or for any other reason

examples.en: These seats are reserved for special guests.
examples.zh: 这些座位是留给贵宾的。

examples.en: The team captain reserved special praise for his players after the match.
examples.zh: 赛后队长对队员们特别表扬。

examples.en: She said this in the tone of voice she reserved for addressing small children.
examples.zh: 她用对小孩子说话的语气说这句话。

senses.def: to have or keep a particular power
senses.zh: 拥有，保持，保留（某种权力）

examples.en: The management reserves the right to refuse admission.
examples.zh: 管理部门有权拒绝接收。

examples.en: All rights reserved (= nobody else can publish or copy this).
examples.zh: 版权所有。

senses.def: to not decide or make a judgement about something until a later time

examples.en: I'd prefer to reserve judgement until I know all the facts.
examples.zh: 在我了解所有事实之前，我宁愿不做判断。

examples.en: Three judges have decided to reserve their decision until a later date.
examples.zh: 三名法官决定稍后再做出决定。

senses.def: available to be used in the future or when needed

examples.en: The money was being kept in reserve for their retirement.
examples.zh: 他们把钱存着以备退休后使用。

examples.en: 200 police officers were held in reserve.
examples.zh: 200 名警察随时待命。

senses.def: to not decide or make a judgement about something until a later time

examples.en: I'd prefer to reserve judgement until I know all the facts.
examples.zh: 在我了解所有事实之前，我宁愿不做判断。

examples.en: Three judges have decided to reserve their decision until a later date.
examples.zh: 三名法官决定稍后再做出决定。

senses.def: to not decide or make a judgement about something until a later time

examples.en: I'd prefer to reserve judgement until I know all the facts.
examples.zh: 在我了解所有事实之前，我宁愿不做判断。

examples.en: Three judges have decided to reserve their decision until a later date.
examples.zh: 三名法官决定稍后再做出决定。

senses.def: a regional bank that operates according to the policies of the Federal Reserve System
a central bank

examples.en: The South African Reserve Bank cut interest rates last year.
examples.zh: 南非储备银行去年降息。

examples.en: The senator proposed that the reserve bank should offer online banking services.
examples.zh: 参议员建议储备银行提供网上银行服务。

senses.def: a word that has a special meaning to a computer program, and so cannot be used in other ways when entering data
senses.zh: 保留词，保留字（编程语言中已被赋予特定意义的单词）

senses.def: a soldier, etc. who is a member of the reserves
senses.zh: 预备役军人；后备军战士

senses.def: a natural or artificial lake where water is stored before it is taken by pipes to houses, etc.

examples.en: The water content of the country's reservoirs had fallen to less than 50% of their capacity.
examples.zh: 这个国家的水库蓄水量已降至不足其库容量的50%。

examples.en: They got up early and went for a swim in the reservoir.
examples.zh: 他们一大早就起床到水库游泳去了。

senses.def: a large amount of something that is available to be used

examples.en: We can tap into the vast reservoir of information available on the internet
examples.zh: 我们可以开发利用因特网上丰富的信息储备。

senses.def: a place in an engine or a machine where a liquid is kept before it is used

examples.en: an oil reservoir
examples.zh: 油槽

senses.def: to change a machine, an instrument or a control so that it gives a different time or number or is ready to use again

examples.en: You need to reset your watch to local time.
examples.zh: 你需要把表调整到当地时间。

examples.en: I’ve reset the heating to stay on all day.
examples.zh: 我已将暖气重置为全天开启。

senses.def: to place something in the correct position again

examples.en: to reset a broken bone
examples.zh: 重接断骨

senses.def: the act of making a machine or instrument ready to use again, usually by returning it to its original settings

examples.en: If you are still having problems, it may be a good idea to perform a factory reset (= return a device to its original settings).
examples.zh: 如果你依然有问题，恢复出厂设置也许是个好办法。

examples.en: Make sure you back up all your data before doing a reset.
examples.zh: 重置前确保备份所有数据。

senses.def: a fundamental change made to a way of doing something

examples.en: The MD has called for a reset of company strategy.
examples.zh: 总经理要求重新部署公司战略。

senses.def: to push the reset button

examples.en: When the game is over, press reset to start a new game.
examples.zh: 游戏结束后，按重置键开始新游戏。

senses.def: to make an important change in your life, career, etc. by starting again with a fresh approach

examples.en: Working from home during Covid gave many people a chance to press reset and make changes in their lives.
examples.zh: 新冠疫情期间居家工作使许多人有机会重新开始，改变自己的生活。

senses.def: to push the reset button

examples.en: When the game is over, press reset to start a new game.
examples.zh: 游戏结束后，按重置键开始新游戏。

senses.def: to make an important change in your life, career, etc. by starting again with a fresh approach

examples.en: Working from home during Covid gave many people a chance to press reset and make changes in their lives.
examples.zh: 新冠疫情期间居家工作使许多人有机会重新开始，改变自己的生活。

senses.def: a button that you press on a machine or instrument to make it ready to use again, usually by returning it to its original settings
senses.zh: 重设按钮；重启键；重置键

examples.en: The reset button will restart the game.
examples.zh: 重启按钮将重新启动游戏。

senses.def: to help people go and live in a new country or area; to go and live in a new country or area
senses.zh: 帮助…定居他国（或别的地区）；到他国（或别的地区）定居

examples.en: Many of the refugees were resettled in Britain and Canada.
examples.zh: 许多难民被安置到英国和加拿大。

senses.def: to start to use an area again as a place to live

examples.en: The region was only resettled 200 years later.
examples.zh: 这一地区 200 年以后才重新有人居住。

senses.def: to make yourself comfortable in a new position

examples.en: The birds flew around and then resettled on the pond.
examples.zh: 鸟儿飞来飞去，然后落在池塘边上。

senses.def: the act or process of helping people go and live in a new country or area; the act of going to live in a new country or area
senses.zh: 移民；移居；重新安置；重新定居

examples.en: the resettlement of refugees
examples.zh: 难民的重新安置

examples.en: a resettlement agency
examples.zh: 居民安置机构

examples.en: This process of settlement and resettlement along the banks of the river continued into the nineteenth century.
examples.zh: 这种沿河岸定居和移居的过程一直持续到19世纪。

senses.def: to change the shape or structure of something
senses.zh: 改变…的形状（或结构）；重塑；改组

examples.en: exercises to reshape your body
examples.zh: 重塑身体的练习

examples.en: Their policies set out to reshape the welfare system.
examples.zh: 他们的政策着手重塑福利制度。

examples.en: Tides and storms inexorably reshaped the land.
examples.zh: 潮汐和暴风雨无情地改变了这片土地的面貌。

senses.def: a change in the jobs that a group of people do, for example in a government

examples.en: a Cabinet reshuffle
examples.zh: 内阁改组

senses.def: to change around the jobs that a group of people do, for example in a government
senses.zh: 改组；进行岗位调整；更改职责配置

examples.en: The prime minister eventually decided against reshuffling the Cabinet.
examples.zh: 首相最终决定反对改组内阁。

examples.en: After a six-game losing streak the coach decided to reshuffle the starting line-up.
examples.zh: 六连败后，教练决定调整首发阵容。

senses.def: to live in a particular place

examples.en: He returned to Britain in 1939, having resided abroad for many years.
examples.zh: 他在国外居住多年以后，于 1939 年回到了英国。

examples.en: Their passports do not give them the right to reside in Britain.
examples.zh: 他们的护照并不赋予他们在英国居住的权利。

senses.def: to be in somebody/something; to be caused by something

examples.en: The poem’s main interest resides in the use of dialect.
examples.zh: 这首诗的主要兴趣在于方言的使用。

examples.en: The source of the problem resides in the fact that the currency is too strong.
examples.zh: 问题的根源在于货币过于坚挺。

senses.def: to belong to somebody/something

examples.en: The ultimate authority resides with the board of directors.
examples.zh: 最高权力属于董事会。

senses.def: to belong to somebody/something

examples.en: The ultimate authority resides with the board of directors.
examples.zh: 最高权力属于董事会。

senses.def: a house, especially a large or impressive one
senses.zh: 住所；住房；（尤指）宅第，豪宅

examples.en: a desirable family residence for sale (= for example, in an advertisement)
examples.zh: 待售的理想家居

examples.en: 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister’s official residence.
examples.zh: 唐宁街 10 号是英国首相的官邸。

senses.def: the state of living in a particular place

examples.en: They were not able to take up residence in their new home until the spring.
examples.zh: 他们到第二年春天才住进了新家。

examples.en: Please state your occupation and place of residence.
examples.zh: 请说明你的职业和住址。

examples.en: The flag flies when the Queen is in residence.
examples.zh: 女王驻跸在这里时有国旗飘扬。

senses.def: permission to live in a country that is not your own

examples.en: They have been denied residence in this country.
examples.zh: 这个国家不给他们居住资格。

examples.en: a residence permit
examples.zh: 居留许可证

senses.def: having an official position in a particular place such as a college or university
senses.zh: （在大学等处）有正式职位，常驻

examples.en: creative writing classes given by the writer in residence
examples.zh: 由驻校作家开设的创意写作课程

senses.def: having an official position in a particular place such as a college or university
senses.zh: （在大学等处）有正式职位，常驻

examples.en: creative writing classes given by the writer in residence
examples.zh: 由驻校作家开设的创意写作课程

senses.def: a building for university or college students to live in
permission to live in a country that is not your own

examples.en: She has been granted permanent residency in Britain.
examples.zh: 她获准在英国永久居住。

senses.def: the period of time that an artist, a writer or a musician spends working for a particular institution
senses.zh: （艺术家、作家、音乐家为某机构工作的）驻留时间，驻留期

senses.def: the state of living in a particular place

examples.en: a residency requirement for students
examples.zh: 要求学生住校

senses.def: the period of time when a doctor working in a hospital receives special advanced training
senses.zh: 高级专科住院医生实习期

senses.def: the official house of somebody such as an ambassador
a person who lives in a particular place or who has their home there

examples.en: a resident of the United States
examples.zh: 美国的居民

examples.en: The proposals sparked concern among local residents.
examples.zh: 这些建议引起了当地居民的关切。

senses.def: a person who is staying in a hotel

examples.en: The hotel restaurant is open to non-residents.
examples.zh: 旅店的餐馆对外开放。

senses.def: a doctor working in a hospital in the US who is receiving special advanced training
senses.zh: （美国的）高级专科住院实习医生

senses.def: living in a particular place

examples.en: the town’s resident population (= not tourists or visitors)
examples.zh: 镇上的居民

examples.en: to be resident abroad/in the UK
examples.zh: 住在国外／英国

examples.en: Tom's our resident expert (= our own expert) on foreign movies.
examples.zh: 汤姆可是我们的外国电影专家。

senses.def: a person from another country who has permission to stay in the US
senses.zh: （获准在美国居留的）外籍居民，外侨

senses.def: suitable for living in; consisting of houses rather than factories or offices

examples.en: a quiet residential area
examples.zh: 安静的住宅区

senses.def: requiring a person to live at a particular place; offering living accommodation
senses.zh: 需要在某地居住的；提供住宿的

examples.en: a residential language course
examples.zh: 需要住校的语言课程

examples.en: a residential home for the elderly
examples.zh: 老人院

examples.en: residential care for children
examples.zh: 提供食宿的儿童福利院服务

senses.def: a group of people who live in a particular area and join together to discuss the problems of that area
senses.zh: 居民委员会；居民联合会

senses.def: left at the end of a process

examples.en: There are still a few residual problems with the computer program.
examples.zh: 电脑程序还有一些残留问题。

examples.en: residual income (= money that is left from your income after you have paid tax and other costs)
examples.zh: 税后收入

senses.def: left from the money and property of a person who has died after all debts, gifts, etc. have been paid

examples.en: a residuary bequest
examples.zh: 剩余遗赠

senses.def: left at the end of a process
a small amount of something that remains at the end of a process

examples.en: pesticide residues in fruit and vegetables
examples.zh: 残留在水果和蔬菜中的杀虫剂

senses.def: the part of the money, property, etc. of a person who has died that remains after all the debts, gifts, etc. have been paid

examples.en: The residue of the estate was divided equally among his children.
examples.zh: 剩余遗产被他的孩子平分了。

senses.def: something that remains after a reaction or process has taken place
senses.zh: （化学反应的）残基，残渣，残留物；（某种进程的）残体

senses.def: to officially tell somebody that you are leaving your job, an organization, etc.

examples.en: She was forced to resign due to ill health.
examples.zh: 由于身体不好，她被迫辞职。

examples.en: He resigned as manager after eight years.
examples.zh: 八年后，他辞去了经理的职务。

examples.en: Two members resigned from the board in protest.
examples.zh: 董事会的两名成员辞职以示抗议。

examples.en: Some judges have threatened to resign over this issue.
examples.zh: 一些裁判威胁要为此事辞职。

examples.en: My father resigned his directorship last year.
examples.zh: 我父亲去年辞去了董事的职务。

senses.def: to accept something unpleasant that cannot be changed or avoided

examples.en: She resigned herself to her fate.
examples.zh: 她只好听天由命了。

examples.en: We had to resign ourselves to making a loss on the sale.
examples.zh: 我们只好接受销售造成的亏损。

senses.def: the act of giving up your job or position; the occasion when you do this

examples.en: a letter of resignation
examples.zh: 辞职信

examples.en: There were calls for her resignation from the board of directors.
examples.zh: 有人要求她从董事会辞职。

examples.en: Further resignations are expected.
examples.zh: 预计还会有人辞职。

examples.en: The defeat led to his resignation as team manager.
examples.zh: 这次失败导致他辞去球队经理职务。

senses.def: a letter, for example to your employers, to say that you are giving up your job or position

examples.en: to offer/hand in/tender your resignation
examples.zh: 呈递／上交／提交辞职信

examples.en: We haven't received his resignation yet.
examples.zh: 我们还没有收到他的辞呈。

senses.def: the quality of being willing to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation that you cannot change

examples.en: They accepted their defeat with resignation.
examples.zh: 他们无可奈何地承认失败。

senses.def: in a way that calmly accepts something unpleasant or difficult that you cannot change

examples.en: ‘I suppose you're right,’ she said resignedly.
examples.zh: “看来你是对的。”她无奈地说。

senses.def: the ability of people or things to recover quickly after something unpleasant, such as shock, injury, etc.
senses.zh: 快速恢复的能力；适应能力

examples.en: He showed great courage and resilience in fighting back from a losing position to win the game.
examples.zh: 他在从落后局面反击赢得比赛中表现出极大的勇气和韧性。

senses.def: the ability of a substance to return to its original shape after it has been bent, stretched or pressed

examples.en: the natural beauty and resilience of wool
examples.zh: 羊毛的自然美和韧性

senses.def: able to recover quickly after something unpleasant such as shock, injury, etc.
senses.zh: 可迅速恢复的；适应能力强的

examples.en: He'll get over it—young people are amazingly resilient.
examples.zh: 他会克服的，年轻人的适应力惊人。

examples.en: These plants are very resilient to rough handling.
examples.zh: 这些植物对粗暴搬运非常有抵抗力。

senses.def: returning to its original shape after being bent, stretched, or pressed
senses.zh: 有弹性（或弹力）的；能复原的

senses.def: in a way that shows the ability to resist being badly affected after something unpleasant such as shock, injury, etc.
senses.zh: 弹性：以某种方式显示出抵御受到诸如震动，伤害等不愉快影响的严重影响的能力。

examples.en: Even the most sensitive teenager can emerge resiliently from disappointment.
examples.zh: 即使是最敏感的青少年也能从失望中恢复过来。

senses.def: a sticky substance that is produced by some trees and is used in making varnish
an artificial substance similar to resin
producing, consisting of or smelling of resin

examples.en: the resinous scent of pine trees
examples.zh: 松脂的香气

senses.def: to refuse to accept something and try to stop it from happening

examples.en: They are determined to resist pressure to change the law.
examples.zh: 他们决心顶住要求改革法律的压力。

examples.en: People naturally resist change.
examples.zh: 人生来就抗拒变革。

examples.en: The bank strongly resisted cutting interest rates.
examples.zh: 银行强烈反对降低利率。

examples.en: Residents who oppose the plans are threatening to resist.
examples.zh: 反对该计划的居民威胁要抵制。

senses.def: to fight back when attacked; to use force to stop something from happening

examples.en: He tried to pin me down, but I resisted.
examples.zh: 他试图按住我，但我奋力反抗。

examples.en: She was charged with resisting arrest.
examples.zh: 她被控拒捕。

senses.def: to stop yourself from having something you like or doing something you very much want to do

examples.en: I finished the cake. I couldn't resist it.
examples.zh: 我忍不住把整块蛋糕都吃了。

examples.en: The Chancellor resisted the temptation to raise business taxes.
examples.zh: 财政大臣克制住提高营业税的诱惑。

examples.en: I found the temptation to miss the class too hard to resist.
examples.zh: 我抵挡不住逃课的诱惑。

examples.en: She could hardly resist the urge to turn and run.
examples.zh: 她几乎抑制不住转身跑掉的冲动。

examples.en: He couldn't resist showing off his new car.
examples.zh: 他忍不住炫耀起了他的新车。

senses.def: to not be harmed or damaged by something

examples.en: A healthy diet should help your body resist infection.
examples.zh: 健康饮食有助于身体抗感染。

examples.en: The castle was built to resist attack.
examples.zh: 这座城堡是为抵抗攻击而建的。

senses.def: dislike of or opposition to a plan, an idea, etc.; the act of refusing to obey

examples.en: As with all new ideas it met with resistance.
examples.zh: 和所有的新观念一样，它受到了抵制。

examples.en: There has been a lot of resistance to this new law.
examples.zh: 这项新的法规已经遭到强烈抵制。

examples.en: Resistance to change has nearly destroyed the industry.
examples.zh: 对变革的抵制几乎毁了这个行业。

senses.def: the act of using force to oppose somebody/something

examples.en: There were a number of episodes of armed resistance during the early years of occupation.
examples.zh: 占领初期发生了多起武装抵抗事件。

examples.en: The defenders put up a strong resistance.
examples.zh: 保卫者顽强地抵抗。

examples.en: The demonstrators offered little or no resistance to the police.
examples.zh: 示威者几乎没有对警察作任何反抗。

senses.def: the power not to be affected by something

examples.en: AIDS lowers the body's resistance to infection.
examples.zh: 艾滋病降低了身体的抗感染能力。

senses.def: a force that stops something moving or makes it move more slowly

examples.en: wind/air resistance (= in the design of planes or cars)
examples.zh: 风阻；空气阻力

senses.def: the opposition of a substance or device to the flow of an electrical current
a secret organization that resists the authorities, especially in a country that an enemy has control of
senses.zh: （尤指敌占区的）秘密抵抗组织

examples.en: resistance fighters
examples.zh: 秘密抵抗战士

examples.en: The Resistance was/were not going to surrender.
examples.zh: 抵抗运动不会投降。

senses.def: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing something

items.idm: (choose, follow, take, etc.) the line/path of least resistance

senses.def: (to choose, etc.) the easiest way of doing something
not affected by something; able to resist something

examples.en: plants that are resistant to disease
examples.zh: 抗病植株

examples.en: Mosquitoes are becoming resistant to insecticides.
examples.zh: 蚊子对杀虫剂产生了抗药性。

senses.def: opposing something and trying to stop it happening

examples.en: Elderly people are not always resistant to change.
examples.zh: 上了年纪的人并不总是抵制变革。

senses.def: not damaged by the thing mentioned

examples.en: disease-resistant plants
examples.zh: 抗病植株

examples.en: fire-resistant materials
examples.zh: 耐火材料

senses.def: a person who resists somebody/something
that can be resisted
able to survive or deal with the action or effect of something
relating to electrical resistance
a measure of the electrical resistance
a device that has resistance
the act of taking an exam or a test again, usually after failing it the first time

examples.en: Students are only allowed one resit.
examples.zh: 学生只有一次补考机会。

senses.def: to take an exam or a test again, usually after failing it the first time
to make something bigger or smaller, especially an image on a computer screen
senses.zh: 改变（尤指计算机图像等）的大小

senses.def: to learn new skills so that you can do a new job; to teach somebody new skills
senses.zh: （为新工作）学习新技能；教（某人）新技能

senses.def: strong and determined

examples.en: His resolute leadership was admired by many.
examples.zh: 他果断的领导能力受到许多人的钦佩。

examples.en: He became even more resolute in his opposition to the plan.
examples.zh: 他更加坚决地反对这个计划。

examples.en: Her voice sounded calm and resolute.
examples.zh: 她的声音听起来平静而坚定。

senses.def: in a way that is strong and determined

examples.en: They remain resolutely opposed to the idea.
examples.zh: 他们仍然坚决反对这个观点。

examples.en: She resolutely refuses to talk about it.
examples.zh: 她坚决拒绝谈论这件事。

senses.def: the quality of being strong and determined
a definite decision to do or not to do something

examples.en: Have you made any New Year's resolutions (= for example, to give up smoking from 1 January)?
examples.zh: 你有什么新年计划吗？

examples.en: She made a resolution to visit her relatives more often.
examples.zh: 她决定要多走走亲戚。

senses.def: a formal statement of an opinion agreed on by a committee or a council, especially by means of a vote

examples.en: to pass/adopt/approve a resolution
examples.zh: 通过／采纳／批准决议

examples.en: The UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution calling for a halt to hostilities.
examples.zh: 联合国安理会一致通过决议，呼吁各方停止对抗。

senses.def: the act of solving or settling a problem, argument, etc.

examples.en: dispute/conflict resolution
examples.zh: 争端／冲突的解决

examples.en: The government is pressing for an early resolution of the dispute.
examples.zh: 政府正在不断敦促早日解决这起纠纷。

examples.en: Hopes of a peaceful resolution to the conflict were fading.
examples.zh: 和平解决冲突的希望正在消失。

senses.def: the quality of being resolute

examples.en: The reforms owe a great deal to the resolution of one man.
examples.zh: 这些改革主要归功于一个人的坚定决心。

examples.en: Her resolution never faltered.
examples.zh: 她的决心从未动摇过。

examples.en: She showed great resolution in her dealings with management.
examples.zh: 她与管理人员打交道时态度十分坚决。

senses.def: the power of a computer screen, printer, etc. to give a clear image, depending on the size of the dots

examples.en: The graphics look fine, even at low resolution.
examples.zh: 图形看起来不错，尽管分辨率很低。

examples.en: The higher the resolution, the sharper the image.
examples.zh: 分辨率越高，图像越清晰。

examples.en: a monitor capable of a 1 024 by 768 pixel resolution
examples.zh: 1,024×768 像素的显示器

senses.def: to find an acceptable solution to a problem or difficulty

examples.en: to resolve an issue/a dispute/a conflict/a crisis
examples.zh: 解决问题／争端／冲突／危机

examples.en: Attempts are being made to resolve the problem of security in schools.
examples.zh: 正在努力采取措施解决学校安全问题。

examples.en: Both sides met in order to try to resolve their differences.
examples.zh: 双方会晤以努力解决分歧。

examples.en: We hope to resolve the matter as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 我们希望尽快解决此事。

examples.en: Everything is being done to resolve the situation.
examples.zh: 正在采取一切措施来解决这一问题。

examples.en: The dispute has not been fully resolved.
examples.zh: 争议尚未完全解决。

examples.en: Be patient and the situation may resolve itself.
examples.zh: 要有耐心，情况可能会自行解决。

senses.def: to make a definite decision to do something

examples.en: He resolved not to tell her the truth.
examples.zh: 他决定不告诉她真相。

examples.en: He resolved to do something to help the children he had met.
examples.zh: 他决定做点什么来帮助他遇到的孩子们。

examples.en: She resolved that she would never see him again.
examples.zh: 她决心再也不见他了。

examples.en: We had resolved on making an early start.
examples.zh: 我们已经决定早点动身。

senses.def: to reach a decision by means of a formal vote
senses.zh: （经正式投票）作出决定，作出决议；表决

examples.en: It was resolved that the matter be referred to a higher authority.
examples.zh: 经过表决，决定把这件事提交给上级主管部门。

examples.en: They resolved that the matter be referred to a higher authority.
examples.zh: 他们经过表决，决定把这件事提交给上级主管部门。

examples.en: The committee unanimously resolved that the party chairman should step down.
examples.zh: 委员会一致决定党主席辞职。

examples.en: The Supreme Council resolved to resume control over the national press.
examples.zh: 最高委员会作出决议恢复对国家新闻机构的控制。

examples.en: The board of directors has called a meeting to resolve on the merger.
examples.zh: 董事会已召开会议以解决合并事宜。

senses.def: a determined desire to achieve something

examples.en: The difficulties in her way merely strengthened her resolve.
examples.zh: 她所遇到的困难只是让她更加坚定。

examples.en: It was a test of his stamina and resolve.
examples.zh: 这是对他毅力和决心的考验。

examples.en: She did not weaken in her resolve.
examples.zh: 她的决心并没有减弱。

examples.en: The government reiterated its resolve to uncover the truth.
examples.zh: 政府重申一定要查个水落石出。

senses.def: to separate or to be separated into its parts

examples.en: to resolve a complex argument into its basic elements
examples.zh: 把一个复杂的论点分解成几个基本要点

senses.def: to gradually turn into a different form when it is seen or heard more clearly
senses.zh: 逐渐变为（另一种形式）；显现（为）

examples.en: The orange light resolved itself into four lanterns.
examples.zh: 橙色的光亮逐渐变成了四盏灯。

senses.def: to gradually become or be understood as something
senses.zh: 逐步变成；逐渐被理解为

examples.en: The discussion eventually resolved itself into two main issues.
examples.zh: 讨论后来集中在两大主要议题上。

senses.def: the quality of being resonant

examples.en: Her voice had a strange and thrilling resonance.
examples.zh: 她的声音洪亮，有一种奇特的震撼人心的效果。

senses.def: the sound or other vibration
the power to bring images, feelings, etc. into the mind of the person reading or listening; the images, etc. produced in this way
senses.zh: 激发联想的力量；引起共鸣的力量；引起的联想（或共鸣）

senses.def: deep, clear and continuing for a long time
senses.zh: 嘹亮的；响亮的；回响的；悠扬的

examples.en: a deep resonant voice
examples.zh: 深沉而响亮的声音

senses.def: causing sounds to continue for a long time

examples.en: resonant frequencies
examples.zh: 谐振频率

senses.def: having the power to bring images, feelings, memories, etc. into your mind
senses.zh: 引起联想的；产生共鸣的

examples.en: a poem filled with resonant imagery
examples.zh: 充满了让人浮想联翩的意象的诗歌

examples.en: Everything was resonant with new meaning.
examples.zh: 一切都充满了新的意义。

senses.def: in a way that brings images, feelings, memories, etc. into your mind
senses.zh: 引起联想的；产生共鸣的

examples.en: I was amazed that a book written in 1937 could speak to me so clearly and so resonantly.
examples.zh: 我很惊讶一本写于 1937 年的书能如此清晰、如此共鸣地对我说话。

senses.def: used to describe how a sound continues deeply and clearly for a long time
senses.zh: 共振地：用来描述声音在很长一段时间内持续深入清晰地传播的方式

senses.def: to make a deep, clear sound that continues for a long time
senses.zh: 产生共鸣；发出回响；回荡

examples.en: Her voice resonated through the theatre.
examples.zh: 她的声音在剧场里回响。

senses.def: to be filled with sound; to make a sound continue longer

examples.en: The body of the violin acts as a resonating chamber and makes the sound louder.
examples.zh: 小提琴琴身相当于一个共鸣箱，把声音放大。

examples.en: The room resonated with the chatter of 100 people.
examples.zh: 屋里充满了 100 人唧唧喳喳的声音。

senses.def: to remind somebody of something; to be similar to what somebody thinks or believes
senses.zh: 使产生联想；引起共鸣；和…的想法（或观念）类似

examples.en: These issues resonated with the voters.
examples.zh: 这些问题引起了投票者的共鸣。

examples.en: His speech resonated with the fears and suspicions of his audience.
examples.zh: 他的演讲引起了听众的恐惧和怀疑。

senses.def: to be full of a particular quality or feeling

examples.en: She makes a simple story resonate with complex themes and emotions.
examples.zh: 她使一部情节简单的小说充满了复杂的主题和情感。

senses.def: a device for making sound louder and stronger, especially in a musical instrument
a place where a lot of people go on holiday

examples.en: seaside/mountain resorts
examples.zh: 海滨/山区度假村

examples.en: They spent a month at a fashionable ski resort in Switzerland.
examples.zh: 他们在瑞士一个时尚的滑雪胜地呆了一个月。

examples.en: a popular tourist resort
examples.zh: 受欢迎的旅游胜地

examples.en: a popular holiday resort
examples.zh: 受欢迎的旅游胜地

examples.en: the resort town of Byron Bay
examples.zh: 度假小镇拜伦湾

examples.en: destination resorts such as Atlantis in the Bahamas
examples.zh: 巴哈马亚特兰蒂斯之类的度假胜地

senses.def: the act of using something, especially something bad or unpleasant, because nothing else is possible

examples.en: There are hopes that the conflict can be resolved without resort to violence.
examples.zh: 冲突有望不需要诉诸武力而得到解决。

senses.def: the first or last course of action that you should or can take in a particular situation
senses.zh: 应急措施；可首先（或最后）采取的手段

examples.en: Strike action should be regarded as a last resort, when all attempts to negotiate have failed.
examples.zh: 罢工应该是最后一着，在所有的谈判努力都告失败时才使用。

examples.en: In the last resort (= in the end) everyone must decide for themselves.
examples.zh: 最后人人都得自己作决定。

senses.def: to make use of something, especially something bad, as a means of achieving something, often because there is no other possible solution

examples.en: They felt obliged to resort to violence.
examples.zh: 他们觉得有必要诉诸暴力。

examples.en: They achieved their demands without having to resort to force.
examples.zh: 他们无需诉诸武力就达到了自己的要求。

examples.en: We had to resort to another loan from the bank.
examples.zh: 我们不得不向银行求助另一笔贷款。

examples.en: We may have to resort to using untrained staff.
examples.zh: 我们也许只能使用未受过训练的员工了。

senses.def: to fill a place with sound

examples.en: Laughter resounded through the house.
examples.zh: 笑声在屋里回荡。

examples.en: The tragedy resounded around the world.
examples.zh: 这一惨案传遍了全世界。

senses.def: to be filled with sound
senses.zh: 回荡着声音；回响着声音

examples.en: The street resounded to the thud of marching feet.
examples.zh: 街道上回荡着行进步伐的铿锵声。

examples.en: The room resounded with screams and shouts.
examples.zh: 房间里响起了尖叫声和叫喊声。

senses.def: in a complete and extreme way

examples.en: The federal party was resoundingly defeated.
examples.zh: 联邦党惨败。

senses.def: a supply of something that a country, an organization or a person has and can use, especially to increase their wealth

examples.en: the exploitation of minerals and other natural resources
examples.zh: 矿产和其他自然资源的开发

examples.en: They promote the use of renewable resources like soybean oil.
examples.zh: 他们推广使用像豆油这样的可再生资源。

examples.en: water/mineral/energy resources
examples.zh: 水/矿产/能源

examples.en: The school does the best it can with limited resources (= money).
examples.zh: 这所学校资金有限，只能尽力而为。

examples.en: a valuable/precious/scarce resource
examples.zh: 有价值的/宝贵的/稀缺的资源

examples.en: Think carefully about how you allocate resources.
examples.zh: 要慎重考虑如何分配资源的问题。

examples.en: We agreed to pool our resources (= so that everyone gives something).
examples.zh: 我们同意把我们的资源集中起来。

examples.en: Police have had to devote more resources to these cases.
examples.zh: 警方不得不投入更多资源来处理这些案件。

senses.def: something that can be used to help achieve an aim, especially a book, equipment, etc. that provides information for teachers and students
senses.zh: 有助于实现目标的东西；资料

examples.en: The website is an invaluable educational resource.
examples.zh: 该网站是宝贵的教育资源。

examples.en: This is an online resource for anyone interested in digital design.
examples.zh: 这是一个可供任何对数字设计感兴趣的人使用的线上资源。

examples.en: The library is a vast resource for historians of medieval France.
examples.zh: 该图书馆是中世纪法国历史学家的巨大资源。

examples.en: Time is your most valuable resource, especially in examinations.
examples.zh: 时间是你最宝贵的东西，尤其是在考试中。

examples.en: resource books for teachers
examples.zh: 教师参考书

examples.en: a library resource centre
examples.zh: 图书馆资源中心

senses.def: personal qualities such as courage and imagination that help you deal with difficult situations

examples.en: He has no inner resources and hates being alone.
examples.zh: 他没有什么精神力量，因而害怕独处。

examples.en: She is someone of considerable personal resources.
examples.zh: 她才华横溢。

senses.def: to provide something with the money or equipment that is needed

examples.en: Schools in the area are still inadequately resourced.
examples.zh: 本地区的学校仍然没有足够的资金。

senses.def: a person who knows a lot about a particular subject, who may be employed to perform a task or provide information
senses.zh: 对某一特定主题了解很多的人，可能受雇执行任务或提供信息

examples.en: The successful applicant will serve as a resource person for member organizations.
examples.zh: 成功的申请者将担任成员组织的顾问。

senses.def: good at finding ways of doing things and solving problems, etc.
senses.zh: 机敏的；足智多谋的；随机应变的

examples.en: These women were strong, resourceful and courageous.
examples.zh: 这些女性坚强、足智多谋且勇敢。

senses.def: in a way that solves problems and manages things well
the quality of being good at finding ways of doing things and solving problems, etc.
senses.zh: 机敏的；足智多谋的；随机应变的

examples.en: situations that will test your resourcefulness to the utmost
examples.zh: 最大限度考验你的足智多谋的情况

senses.def: if a character that has been killed in a video game respawns or is respawned, that character appears again in the game
senses.zh: （电子游戏中的人物）重生，复活

examples.en: On level five of the game, enemies respawn very quickly.
examples.zh: 在游戏的第五关，敌人重生得非常快。

examples.en: Characters in the game can be respawned when they are killed.
examples.zh: 游戏中的角色被杀死后可以重生。

senses.def: a strong feeling of approval of somebody/something because of their good qualities or achievements

examples.en: I have the utmost respect for her and her work.
examples.zh: 我对她和她的工作充满敬意。

examples.en: They feel a deep and mutual respect for each other.
examples.zh: 他们彼此深深地感受到一种相互尊重。

examples.en: It was a noble effort that deserves respect.
examples.zh: 这是一种值得尊敬的崇高付出。

examples.en: She soon earned the respect of her colleagues.
examples.zh: 她很快赢得了同事们的尊重。

examples.en: You did a great job. Respect! (= used to praise somebody)
examples.zh: 你做得很出色。了不起！

senses.def: polite behaviour towards or care for somebody/something that you think is important

examples.en: to show a lack of respect for authority
examples.zh: 蔑视权威

examples.en: They have a deep respect for the natural world.
examples.zh: 他们非常尊重大自然。

examples.en: He has no respect for her feelings.
examples.zh: 他根本不尊重她的感情。

examples.en: Everyone has a right to be treated with respect.
examples.zh: 人人有权受到尊重。

examples.en: A two-minute silence was held as a mark of respect.
examples.zh: 人们静默两分钟以示尊敬。

examples.en: Out of respect for my friend, I didn't say anything.
examples.zh: 出于对朋友的尊重，我什么也没说。

senses.def: a particular aspect or detail of something

examples.en: In this respect we are very fortunate.
examples.zh: 在这方面，我们是很幸运的。

examples.en: This has been a difficult year in many respects.
examples.zh: 从很多方面来说，今年都是艰难的一年。

examples.en: There was one respect, however, in which they differed.
examples.zh: 然而，他们在一点上有分歧。

senses.def: about; relating to

examples.en: A writ was served on the firm in respect of their unpaid bill.
examples.zh: 公司由于欠账而收到了传票。

senses.def: in payment for something

examples.en: money received in respect of overtime worked
examples.zh: 得到的加班费

senses.def: to visit somebody or to send a message of good wishes as a sign of respect for them

examples.en: Many came to pay their last respects (= by attending somebody's funeral).
examples.zh: 许多人前来参加葬礼向逝者告别。

senses.def: used when you are going to disagree, usually quite strongly, with somebody
senses.zh: （通常在表示强烈不同意之前说）恕我直言

examples.en: With all due respect, the figures simply do not support you on this.
examples.zh: 恕我直言，这些数字根本不能支持你的观点。

examples.en: With all due respect, I think you've misunderstood what he said.
examples.zh: 我无意冒犯，但我认为你误解了他的话。

senses.def: in connection with

examples.en: The two groups were similar with respect to income and status.
examples.zh: 这两组在收入和地位方面是相似的。

senses.def: to have a very good opinion of somebody/something; to admire somebody/something

examples.en: I respect Jack's opinion on most subjects.
examples.zh: 在大多数事情上，我尊重杰克的意见。

examples.en: She was a much loved and highly respected teacher.
examples.zh: 她是位深受爱戴和尊敬的老师。

examples.en: She had always been honest with me, and I respect her for that.
examples.zh: 她一直对我很诚实——我非常敬重她这一点。

senses.def: to be careful about something; to make sure you do not do something that might be considered wrong
senses.zh: 慎重对待；谨慎从事；尊重

examples.en: Employers must respect employees' privacy.
examples.zh: 雇主必须尊重雇员的隐私。

examples.en: to respect other people’s property
examples.zh: 不侵犯别人的财产

examples.en: I respect your right to disagree.
examples.zh: 我尊重你保留不同意见的权利。

examples.en: She promised to respect our wishes.
examples.zh: 她保证尊重我们的愿望。

senses.def: to agree not to break a law, principle, etc.

examples.en: The new leader has promised to respect the constitution.
examples.zh: 新的领导人承诺遵守宪法。

examples.en: The government has promised to respect human rights.
examples.zh: 政府已承诺尊重人权。

senses.def: a British political party, started by Salma Yakoob and George Monbiot, that was active between 2004 and 2016. Respect's candidate George Galloway joined after he was forced to leave the Labour Party
senses.zh: 尊重：由萨尔玛·雅各布（Salma Yakoob）和乔治·蒙比奥特（George Monbiot）发起的英国政党，活跃于2004年至2016年。受尊敬的候选人乔治·加洛韦（George Galloway）因批评托尼·布莱尔（Tony Blair）和乔治·W·布什（George W Bush）入侵伊拉克而被迫离开工党，因此加入。该党反对战争，支持传统的社会主义思想。

senses.def: about; relating to

examples.en: A writ was served on the firm in respect of their unpaid bill.
examples.zh: 公司由于欠账而收到了传票。

senses.def: in payment for something

examples.en: money received in respect of overtime worked
examples.zh: 得到的加班费

senses.def: to visit somebody or to send a message of good wishes as a sign of respect for them

examples.en: Many came to pay their last respects (= by attending somebody's funeral).
examples.zh: 许多人前来参加葬礼向逝者告别。

items.idm: with respect | with all due respect

senses.def: used when you are going to disagree, usually quite strongly, with somebody
senses.zh: （通常在表示强烈不同意之前说）恕我直言

examples.en: With all due respect, the figures simply do not support you on this.
examples.zh: 恕我直言，这些数字根本不能支持你的观点。

examples.en: With all due respect, I think you've misunderstood what he said.
examples.zh: 我无意冒犯，但我认为你误解了他的话。

senses.def: in connection with

examples.en: The two groups were similar with respect to income and status.
examples.zh: 这两组在收入和地位方面是相似的。

senses.def: the fact of being considered socially acceptable

examples.en: middle-class notions of respectability
examples.zh: 中产阶级对体面的看法

examples.en: The country has again achieved international respectability after years of isolation.
examples.zh: 被孤立了几年之后，该国又重新赢得了国际声望。

examples.en: The theory has now gained scientific respectability.
examples.zh: 该理论现在已经获得了科学上的承认。

senses.def: considered by society to be acceptable, good or correct
senses.zh: 体面的；得体的；值得尊敬的

examples.en: a highly respectable neighbourhood
examples.zh: 非常体面的街区

examples.en: a respectable married man
examples.zh: 正派的已婚男子

examples.en: Go and make yourself look respectable.
examples.zh: 去把自己弄得体面点儿。

senses.def: fairly good; that there is no reason to be ashamed of

examples.en: It was a perfectly respectable result.
examples.zh: 这是个非常好的结果。

examples.en: Economic growth has averaged at a respectable 2.5 per cent.
examples.zh: 经济增长率平均为2.5%，相当不错。

senses.def: in a way that is considered by society to be acceptable, good or correct
senses.zh: 体面的；得体的；值得尊敬的

examples.en: respectably dressed
examples.zh: 衣着体面

senses.def: fairly well; in a way that gives you no reason to be ashamed

examples.en: The party performed respectably in the election, gaining 20% of the vote.
examples.zh: 该党在选举中表现出色，获得了20%的选票。

items.idm: be no respecter of persons, age, class, etc.

senses.def: to treat everyone in the same way, without being influenced by their importance, wealth, etc.

examples.en: Death is no respecter of persons.
examples.zh: 死神不区分贫富贵贱。

senses.def: showing or feeling respect

examples.en: The onlookers stood at a respectful distance.
examples.zh: 旁观者站在一定的距离之外，以示尊敬。

examples.en: We were brought up to be respectful of authority.
examples.zh: 我们从小就学会了尊重权威。

senses.def: in a way that shows respect

examples.en: He listened respectfully.
examples.zh: 他恭敬地听着。

examples.en: I would respectfully agree with this comment.
examples.zh: 我会恭敬地同意这个评论。

senses.def: belonging or relating separately to each of the people or things already mentioned

examples.en: They are each recognized specialists in their respective fields.
examples.zh: 他们在各自的领域都被视为专家。

examples.en: the respective roles of men and women in society
examples.zh: 男女在社会中各自的角色

senses.def: in the same order as the people or things already mentioned
senses.zh: 分别；各自；顺序为；依次为

examples.en: Julie and Mark, aged 17 and 19 respectively
examples.zh: 朱莉和马克，年龄分别为 17 岁和 19 岁

senses.def: the act of breathing

examples.en: Blood pressure and respiration are also recorded.
examples.zh: 血压和呼吸也做了记录。

senses.def: a process by which organisms
a piece of equipment that makes it possible for somebody to breathe over a long period when they are unable to do so naturally

examples.en: She was put on a respirator.
examples.zh: 给她戴上了人工呼吸器。

senses.def: a device worn over the nose and mouth to allow somebody to breathe in a place where there is a lot of smoke, gas, etc.
connected with breathing

examples.en: the respiratory system
examples.zh: 呼吸系统

examples.en: respiratory diseases
examples.zh: 呼吸道疾病

examples.en: the respiratory rate
examples.zh: 呼吸频率

senses.def: to breathe

examples.en: Terrestrial amphibians respire through their skin.
examples.zh: 陆地两栖动物通过皮肤呼吸。

senses.def: a piece of equipment for measuring how much air somebody’s lungs will hold
a short break or escape from something difficult or unpleasant

examples.en: The drug brought a brief respite from the pain.
examples.zh: 药物暂时缓解了疼痛。

examples.en: There was no respite from the suffocating heat.
examples.zh: 闷热的天气根本没有缓解。

examples.en: She continued to work without respite.
examples.zh: 她连续工作，没有休息。

examples.en: respite care (= temporary care arranged for somebody who is old, ill, etc. so that the people who usually care for them can have a rest)
examples.zh: 暂时托管（为老人、病人等提供短期照料以使长期照顾者获得短暂休息）

senses.def: a short delay allowed before something difficult or unpleasant must be done

examples.en: His creditors agreed to give him a temporary respite.
examples.zh: 他的债权人同意给他一个喘息的机会。

synonyms.words: break ▪ respite ▪ time out ▪ breathing space

intro.en: These are all words for a short period of time spent relaxing.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示短暂的休息。

items.def: a period of relaxing, sleeping or doing nothing after a period of activity:
items.zh: 指休息、睡眠

examples.en: We stopped for a well-earned rest.
examples.zh: 我们停下来做个应有的休息。

items.def: a short period of time when you stop what you are doing and rest or eat:
items.zh: 指间歇、休息

examples.en: Let’s take a break.
examples.zh: 咱们休息一会儿吧。

items.def: a short break from something difficult or unpleasant:
items.zh: 指从困境或不愉快、不舒适的状态中得到暂缓、暂停

examples.en: The drug brought a brief respite from the pain.
examples.zh: 药物暂时缓解了疼痛。

items.def: (especially North American English尤用于美式英语, informal) time for resting or relaxing away from your usual work or studies:
items.zh: 指暂停工作或学习的时间

examples.en: Take time out to relax by the pool.
examples.zh: 去游泳池边歇一歇吧。

items.def: a short rest in the middle of a period of mental or physical effort:
items.zh: 指脑力或体力活动期间的短暂休息、喘息时间

examples.en: This delay gives the party a breathing space in which to sort out its policies.
examples.zh: 这一延误使该党有了喘息之机来厘定其政策。

senses.def: brightly coloured in an impressive way

examples.en: He glimpsed Sonia, resplendent in a red dress.
examples.zh: 他瞥了索尼娅一眼，见她一身红衣，光彩照人。

examples.en: the resplendent tail of the male peacock
examples.zh: 雄孔雀灿烂的尾巴

senses.def: in way that is brightly coloured and impressive
to give a spoken or written answer to somebody/something

examples.en: I asked him his name, but he didn't respond.
examples.zh: 我问他叫什么名字，可他没回答。

examples.en: The government did not respond to our questions.
examples.zh: 政府没有回答我们的问题。

examples.en: She never responded to my letter.
examples.zh: 她从来没给我回过信。

examples.en: ‘I'm not sure,’ she responded.
examples.zh: “我不肯定。”她答道。

examples.en: When asked about the company's future, the director responded that he remained optimistic.
examples.zh: 问到公司的未来的时候，经理回答说他依然乐观。

examples.en: He responded with a question.
examples.zh: 他回答了一个问题。

senses.def: to do something as a reaction to something that somebody has said or done

examples.en: How did they respond to the news?
examples.zh: 他们对这则消息有什么反应？

examples.en: to respond to a call/need/demand
examples.zh: 响应电话/需要/要求

examples.en: The public is responding positively to these changes.
examples.zh: 公众对这些变化反应积极。

examples.en: to respond favourably/enthusiastically
examples.zh: 积极地/热情地回应

examples.en: The government responded by banning all future demonstrations.
examples.zh: 政府的反应是今后禁止一切示威活动。

examples.en: The audience responded with enthusiasm.
examples.zh: 观众反应热烈。

senses.def: to react quickly or in the correct way to something/somebody
senses.zh: 反应灵敏；作出正确反应

examples.en: The car responds very well to the controls.
examples.zh: 这辆汽车操纵自如。

examples.en: You can rely on him to respond to a challenge.
examples.zh: 你可以信赖他，他懂得应付挑战。

examples.en: Our company is small enough to respond quickly.
examples.zh: 我们公司规模较小，可以快速做出反应。

examples.en: He tried to move but his body wouldn't respond.
examples.zh: 他想动一下，但身体却没有任何反应。

senses.def: to improve as a result of a particular kind of treatment
senses.zh: 有改进；见起色；显出效果

examples.en: The infection did not respond to the drugs.
examples.zh: 这些药物对感染没有起作用。

senses.def: a person who answers questions, especially in a survey
senses.zh: 回答问题的人；（尤指）调查对象

examples.en: 60 per cent of the respondents agreed with the suggestion.
examples.zh: 回复调查的人中 60% 同意这项建议。

senses.def: a person who is accused of something
a spoken or written answer

examples.en: She made no response.
examples.zh: 她没作任何回答。

examples.en: We have asked for a meeting and we are awaiting a response.
examples.zh: 我们已要求召开会议，正在等待答复。

examples.en: I received an immediate response to my request.
examples.zh: 我的请求得到了即时回复。

examples.en: Here's a quick response to your question.
examples.zh: 这是对您的问题的快速答复。

examples.en: I am writing in response to your enquiry.
examples.zh: 我写信答复你的询问。

examples.en: Jack just nodded in response.
examples.zh: 杰克只是点头回应。

examples.en: We sent out over 1 000 letters but the response rate has been low (= few people replied).
examples.zh: 我们寄出了 1 000 多封信，但回信寥寥。

senses.def: a reaction to something that has happened or been said

examples.en: The news provoked an angry response.
examples.zh: 这条消息引起了人们的愤怒。

examples.en: to elicit/trigger/evoke a response
examples.zh: 引起/触发/引起反应

examples.en: When I suggested changes, I got a very positive response.
examples.zh: 当我提出改变的建议时，我得到了非常积极的回应。

examples.en: I knocked on the door but there was no response.
examples.zh: 我敲了门，可是没有回应。

examples.en: There has been little response to our appeal for funds.
examples.zh: 我们请求资金援助，但几乎没有回应。

examples.en: The product was developed in response to demand.
examples.zh: 这种产品是为满足需求而开发的。

senses.def: a part of a church service that the people sing or speak as an answer to the part that the priest sings or speaks
senses.zh: （礼拜仪式中的）答唱咏，启应经

examples.en: The congregation sang the responses.
examples.zh: 会众用歌声回应。

senses.def: the length of time that a person or system takes to react to something

examples.en: The average response time to emergency calls was 9 minutes.
examples.zh: 紧急救助电话的平均回应时间是 9 分钟。

senses.def: a duty to deal with or take care of somebody/something, so that you may be blamed if something goes wrong

examples.en: to be in a position of responsibility
examples.zh: 身居要位

examples.en: It's time for someone to take responsibility and get the job done.
examples.zh: 该有人负起责任把活儿干完了。

examples.en: She assumed responsibility for recruitment.
examples.zh: 她负责招聘。

examples.en: We are recruiting a sales manager with responsibility for the European market.
examples.zh: 我们正在招聘负责欧洲市场的销售经理。

examples.en: They have responsibility for ensuring the rules are enforced.
examples.zh: 他们有责任确保制度的执行。

examples.en: The responsibility for doing this rests with the department managers.
examples.zh: 这样做的责任在于部门经理。

examples.en: It is their responsibility to ensure the rules are enforced.
examples.zh: 他们有责任确保制度的执行。

examples.en: parental rights and responsibilities
examples.zh: 父母的权利和义务

examples.en: She is no longer able to fulfil her responsibilities.
examples.zh: 她不再能够履行她的职责。

examples.en: I did it on my own responsibility (= without being told to and being willing to take the blame if it had gone wrong).
examples.zh: 我做的这件事，由我自己负责。

senses.def: blame for something bad that has happened

examples.en: The bank refuses to accept responsibility for the mistake.
examples.zh: 银行拒绝为这一错误承担责任。

examples.en: Nobody has claimed responsibility for the bombing.
examples.zh: 没有人声称对爆炸事件负责。

examples.en: It is for the court to decide who bears responsibility.
examples.zh: 应由法院决定谁承担责任。

examples.en: We take full responsibility for any errors in the text.
examples.zh: 我们对文本中的任何错误承担全部责任。

senses.def: a moral duty to do something or to help or take care of somebody because of your job, position, etc.

examples.en: We want to instil a sense of personal responsibility in children.
examples.zh: 我们希望向孩子们灌输个人责任感。

examples.en: She feels a strong sense of responsibility towards her employees.
examples.zh: 她对自己的雇员有很强的责任感。

examples.en: We have a responsibility to our shareholders.
examples.zh: 我们对股东负有责任。

examples.en: I think we have a moral responsibility to help these countries.
examples.zh: 我认为我们在道义上有责任帮助这些国家。

examples.en: The media has abdicated its responsibility to report the facts.
examples.zh: 媒体已经放弃了报道事实的责任。

senses.def: having the job or duty of doing something or taking care of somebody/something, so that you may be blamed if something goes wrong

examples.en: Mike is responsible for designing the entire project.
examples.zh: 迈克负责设计全部工程。

examples.en: Even where parents no longer live together, they each continue to be responsible for their children.
examples.zh: 即使父母不再共同生活，他们也要继续分别对子女负责。

examples.en: The management team is directly responsible for the day-to-day operations of the company.
examples.zh: 管理团队直接负责公司的日常运营。

examples.en: I'd like to talk to whoever is responsible here.
examples.zh: 我想和这里的负责人谈谈。

senses.def: being able to be blamed for something

examples.en: Who's responsible for this mess?
examples.zh: 是谁弄得这么乱？

examples.en: He is mentally ill and cannot be held responsible for his actions.
examples.zh: 他有精神病，不能对自己的行为负责。

examples.en: We will ensure that anyone found responsible for the accident is held accountable.
examples.zh: 我们将确保追究对事故负责的任何人的责任。

examples.en: Everything will be done to bring those responsible to justice.
examples.zh: 将竭尽全力把罪魁祸首绳之以法。

examples.en: You mustn't feel responsible in any way.
examples.zh: 你不应该以任何方式感到有责任。

senses.def: being the cause of something

examples.en: Cigarette smoking is responsible for about 90 per cent of deaths from lung cancer.
examples.zh: 大约 90% 的肺癌死亡是由吸烟导致的。

examples.en: He believes that man-made carbon dioxide is directly responsible for global warming.
examples.zh: 他认为人造二氧化碳是造成全球变暖的直接原因。

examples.en: Hormonal changes may be partly responsible for these mood swings.
examples.zh: 荷尔蒙的变化可能是这些情绪波动的部分原因。

senses.def: that you can trust and rely on
senses.zh: 可信任的；可信赖的；可靠的

examples.en: The child should be accompanied by a parent or other responsible adult.
examples.zh: 儿童应由父母或其他成年责任人陪同。

examples.en: We need to teach our children to act as responsible citizens.
examples.zh: 我们需要教导我们的孩子成为负责任的公民。

examples.en: the importance of using medicines in a responsible manner
examples.zh: 以负责任的方式使用药物的重要性

examples.en: Clare has a mature and responsible attitude to work.
examples.zh: 克莱尔对待工作成熟而可信赖。

examples.en: The firm specializes in socially responsible investments.
examples.zh: 该公司专门从事社会责任投资。

examples.en: They are not very responsible with money.
examples.zh: 他们花钱有些大手大脚。

senses.def: needing somebody who can be trusted and relied on; involving important duties
senses.zh: 责任重大的；需要可靠的人负责的

examples.en: a responsible position
examples.zh: 重要岗位

senses.def: having to report to somebody/something with authority or in a higher position and explain to them what you have done

examples.en: The Council of Ministers is responsible to the Assembly.
examples.zh: 内阁须向议会负责。

senses.group: to somebody in authority 对主管者

senses.def: in a sensible way that shows you can be trusted
senses.zh: 明事理地；认真负责地；可信赖地

examples.en: to act responsibly
examples.zh: 办事认真负责

senses.def: reacting quickly and in a positive way

examples.en: Firms have to be responsive to consumer demand.
examples.zh: 公司必须对顾客的需求作出积极反应。

examples.en: a flu virus that is not responsive to treatment
examples.zh: 治疗无效的流感病毒

examples.en: The company is highly responsive to changes in demand.
examples.zh: 该公司对需求的变化反应特别迅速。

senses.def: reacting with interest or enthusiasm

examples.en: The club is responsive to new ideas.
examples.zh: 俱乐部对新的想法都表示欢迎。

examples.en: a responsive and enthusiastic audience
examples.zh: 反应热烈又热情的观众

senses.def: used to describe a website, etc. that changes to suit the kind of device you are using, for example by changing the size of the text or the way that items are arranged on the screen
senses.zh: （网站等）响应式设计的，自适应的（可根据使用者的装置以适当的样式呈现内容）

senses.def: quickly and in a positive way

examples.en: A simple email could meet many patients' needs more responsively and at lower cost.
examples.zh: 一封简单的电子邮件可以更快地以更低的成本满足许多患者的需求。

senses.def: with interest or enthusiasm

examples.en: They listened respectfully and responsively to every participant.
examples.zh: 他们尊重并认真地倾听每一位参与者的发言。

senses.def: the ability to react quickly and in a positive way to something

examples.en: a lack of responsiveness to client needs
examples.zh: 对客户的需求反应冷淡

senses.def: an interested and enthusiastic reaction to somebody/something
senses.zh: 响应能力：对某人/某事的兴趣和热情的反应

examples.en: His letters express his profound responsiveness to nature and beauty.
examples.zh: 他的信表达了他对自然和美的深刻反应。

senses.def: the act of changing the colour of something, especially a car, by spraying
to change the colour of something, especially a car, by spraying
the part of something that remains

examples.en: Take what you want and throw the rest away.
examples.zh: 把你想要的拿走，其余的丢掉。

examples.en: The country enjoys friendly relations with the rest of the world.
examples.zh: 该国与世界其他国家保持友好关系。

examples.en: How would you like to spend the rest of the day?
examples.zh: 后半天你打算怎么过？

examples.en: I'm not doing this job for the rest of my life.
examples.zh: 我不会一辈子干这种工作。

senses.group: remaining part/people/things 剩余的部分／人／事物

senses.def: the people or things that remain; the others
senses.zh: 其余的人；其他事物；其他

examples.en: The first question was difficult, but the rest were pretty easy.
examples.zh: 第一个问题很难，但其余的都相当简单。

examples.en: Don't blame Alex. He's human, like the rest of us.
examples.zh: 不要责怪亚历克斯。他和我们大家一样，也是人。

senses.group: remaining part/people/things 剩余的部分／人／事物

senses.def: a period of relaxing, sleeping or doing nothing after a period of activity

examples.en: I had a good night's rest.
examples.zh: 我睡了一宿好觉。

examples.en: We stopped for a well-earned rest.
examples.zh: 我们停下来做个应有的休息。

examples.en: to have/take a rest from all your hard work
examples.zh: 放下繁重的工作，休息一下

examples.en: Try to get some rest—you have a busy day tomorrow.
examples.zh: 休息一下吧，你明天还要忙一天呢。

examples.en: There are no matches tomorrow, which is a rest day, but the tournament resumes on Monday.
examples.zh: 明天是休息日，没有比赛，但星期一继续比赛。

senses.group: period of relaxing 休息时间

senses.def: an object that is used to support or hold something

examples.en: an armrest (= for example on a seat or chair)
examples.zh: 座椅扶手

senses.def: a period of silence between notes; a sign that shows a rest
used at the end of a list to mean everything else that you might expect to be on the list

examples.en: He wants a big house and an expensive car and all the rest of it.
examples.zh: 他想要大房子、豪华汽车，如此等等。

senses.def: used to say that the actual amount or number of something is much higher than somebody has stated
senses.zh: （比所说的）还要多；远不止此数

examples.en: ‘It cost 250 pounds…’ ‘And the rest, and the rest!’
examples.zh: “这要花 250 英镑…”“不止这些，不止！”

senses.def: not moving

examples.en: At rest the insect looks like a dead leaf.
examples.zh: 这种昆虫不动时看上去像一片枯叶。

senses.def: dead and therefore free from trouble or worry. People say ‘
senses.zh: （委婉说法，与 dead 同义）安息，长眠

examples.en: She now lies at rest in the churchyard.
examples.zh: 她现在长眠在教堂墓地里。

senses.def: to stop moving

examples.en: The car crashed through the barrier and came to rest in a field.
examples.zh: 汽车闯过护栏，在一块田里停了下来。

examples.en: His eyes came to rest on Clara's face.
examples.zh: 他的目光停留在克拉拉的脸上。

examples.en: The ball rolled down the hill and came to rest against a tree.
examples.zh: 球滚下山，撞在一棵树上停了下来。

senses.def: apart from that; considering other matters

examples.en: The book has some interesting passages about the author's childhood. For the rest, it is extremely dull.
examples.zh: 这本书中关于作者童年的一些章节倒还有意思。除此之外，便无聊至极。

senses.def: used to tell somebody to stop talking about something because they are annoying you

examples.en: Give it a rest! You’ve been complaining all day.
examples.zh: 让它休息一下吧！你整天都在抱怨。

senses.def: to stop doing something for a while
to bury somebody. People say ‘
senses.zh: （委婉说法，与 bury 同义）安葬

examples.en: George was laid to rest beside his parents.
examples.zh: 乔治被安葬在他父母墓旁。

senses.def: to stop something by showing it is not true

examples.en: The announcement finally laid all the speculation about their future to rest.
examples.zh: 通告最终消除了一切有关他们的未来的推测。

senses.def: used when somebody is complaining that they have a lot of work to do
senses.zh: （有人抱怨工作太多时说）恶人绝无平安

senses.def: to do or say something to make somebody stop worrying about something
used when you are telling a story to say that you do not need to tell the end of it, because everyone knows it already
senses.zh: 结局是尽人皆知的；结果如何不必赘述

senses.def: to relax, sleep or do nothing after a period of activity or illness; to not use a part of your body for some time

examples.en: The doctor told me to rest.
examples.zh: 医生叫我休息。

examples.en: He won't rest (= will never be satisfied) until he finds her.
examples.zh: 他非得找到她才会安心。

examples.en: He had to rest his injured knee for six weeks.
examples.zh: 他不得不让受伤的膝盖休息六个星期。

examples.en: Rest your eyes every half an hour.
examples.zh: 每过半小时让眼睛休息一下。

senses.def: to leave a player out of a team for a short period of time

examples.en: The striker has been rested ahead of the final this weekend.
examples.zh: 这名前锋在本周末的决赛之前已经被安排离队。

examples.en: The manager chose to rest some of her star players for the midweek game.
examples.zh: 主教练选择让一些明星球员离队，不参加在周中举行的比赛。

senses.def: to support something by putting it on or against something; to be supported in this way

examples.en: Rest your head on my shoulder.
examples.zh: 把头靠在我肩上。

examples.en: He rested his chin in his hands.
examples.zh: 他双手托着下巴。

examples.en: Their bikes were resting against the wall.
examples.zh: 他们的自行车靠在墙上。

examples.en: I settled back, my hands resting in my lap.
examples.zh: 我往后一靠，把双手放在腿上。

senses.def: if you let a matter rest

examples.en: The matter cannot rest there—I intend to sue.
examples.zh: 这件事不能就此了结，我打算提出诉讼。

examples.en: And there the matter rested until an interested journalist uncovered the file.
examples.zh: 事情就这样搁置了，直到一位感兴趣的记者发现了这份文件。

senses.def: to be buried. People say ‘
senses.zh: （委婉说法，与 be buried 同义）安息，长眠

examples.en: She rests beside her husband in the local cemetery.
examples.zh: 在当地的墓地里，她长眠在她丈夫的墓旁。

examples.en: May he rest in peace.
examples.zh: 愿他安息吧。

senses.def: to relax and stop worrying

examples.en: You can rest easy—I'm not going to tell anyone.
examples.zh: 你尽管放心，我不会告诉任何人的。

examples.en: I can sleep easy knowing that she's safely home.
examples.zh: 知道她安全回家了，我就可以安心入睡了。

senses.def: used to show respect when you are talking about somebody who is dead
senses.zh: （对死者表示敬意）魂归天国，安息主怀

senses.def: used to emphasize that what you say is true or will definitely happen
senses.zh: （强调所言确凿无误）尽管放心

examples.en: You may rest assured that we will do all we can to find him.
examples.zh: 你就放心吧，我们会千方百计找到他。

senses.def: used to say that you do not need to say any more about something because you think that you have proved your point
senses.zh: 我的论证到此为止（已经足够）

senses.def: used by lawyers in court to say that they have finished presenting their case
senses.zh: （律师在法庭上）对案情陈述完毕

examples.en: The prosecution rests its case.
examples.zh: 控方对案情陈述完毕。

synonyms.words: break ▪ respite ▪ time out ▪ breathing space

intro.en: These are all words for a short period of time spent relaxing.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示短暂的休息。

items.def: a period of relaxing, sleeping or doing nothing after a period of activity:
items.zh: 指休息、睡眠

examples.en: We stopped for a well-earned rest.
examples.zh: 我们停下来做个应有的休息。

items.def: a short period of time when you stop what you are doing and rest or eat:
items.zh: 指间歇、休息

examples.en: Let’s take a break.
examples.zh: 咱们休息一会儿吧。

items.def: a short break from something difficult or unpleasant:
items.zh: 指从困境或不愉快、不舒适的状态中得到暂缓、暂停

examples.en: The drug brought a brief respite from the pain.
examples.zh: 药物暂时缓解了疼痛。

items.def: (especially North American English尤用于美式英语, informal) time for resting or relaxing away from your usual work or studies:
items.zh: 指暂停工作或学习的时间

examples.en: Take time out to relax by the pool.
examples.zh: 去游泳池边歇一歇吧。

items.def: a short rest in the middle of a period of mental or physical effort:
items.zh: 指脑力或体力活动期间的短暂休息、喘息时间

examples.en: This delay gives the party a breathing space in which to sort out its policies.
examples.zh: 这一延误使该党有了喘息之机来厘定其政策。

senses.def: used to emphasize that what you say is true or will definitely happen
senses.zh: （强调所言确凿无误）尽管放心

examples.en: You may rest assured that we will do all we can to find him.
examples.zh: 你就放心吧，我们会千方百计找到他。

senses.def: used to say that you do not need to say any more about something because you think that you have proved your point
senses.zh: 我的论证到此为止（已经足够）

senses.def: used by lawyers in court to say that they have finished presenting their case
senses.zh: （律师在法庭上）对案情陈述完毕

examples.en: The prosecution rests its case.
examples.zh: 控方对案情陈述完毕。

senses.def: an area next to an important road where people can stop their cars to rest, eat food, etc.
a period spent resting or relaxing in order to improve your physical or mental health

examples.en: His new job was almost a rest cure after the stresses of the army.
examples.zh: 他经历了在军队的压力后，新工作几乎就是一种静养。

senses.def: a place where old or sick people are cared for
(in parts of Asia and Africa) a house or hut
senses.zh: （亚洲和非洲部分地区，尤指野外的）客栈，旅舍

senses.def: to depend or rely on somebody/something

examples.en: All our hopes now rest on you.
examples.zh: 现在我们所有的希望都寄托在你的身上。

senses.def: to look at somebody/something

examples.en: Her eyes rested on the piece of paper in my hand.
examples.zh: 她的目光落在我手里的一张纸上。

senses.def: to be based on something

examples.en: The whole argument rests on a false assumption.
examples.zh: 全部论证都是基于一个错误的假设。

examples.en: Our trade policy rests firmly on the foundation of free and open markets.
examples.zh: 我们的贸易政策完全以自由公开的市场为基础。

senses.def: an area next to an important road where people can stop their cars to rest, eat food, etc.
to depend or rely on somebody/something

examples.en: Her eyes rested on the piece of paper in my hand.
examples.zh: 她的目光落在我手里的一张纸上。

senses.def: if it rests with somebody to do something

examples.en: It rests with management to justify their actions.
examples.zh: 管理部门应当为他们的行动说出个道理来。

examples.en: The final decision rests with the doctors.
examples.zh: 要由医生作出最后决定。

senses.def: to feel so satisfied with what you have already achieved that you do not try to do any more
senses.zh: 满足于既得成就；不思进取

senses.def: the act of starting again, or of making something start again, after it has stopped

examples.en: He is in jail awaiting the restart of his trial for fraud.
examples.zh: 他正在监狱中等待重新开始欺诈罪的审判。

senses.def: to start again, or to make something start again, after it has stopped

examples.en: to restart a game
examples.zh: 重新开始游戏

examples.en: The doctors struggled to restart his heart.
examples.zh: 医生竭力重新起搏他的心脏。

examples.en: The engine did not restart and the plane dived to the ground.
examples.zh: 发动机没能重新启动，飞机栽向地面。

senses.def: to say something again or in a different way, especially so that it is more clearly or strongly expressed

examples.en: They restated their belief in the existence of a ‘hidden agenda’.
examples.zh: 他们重申他们相信背后另有“隐秘意图”。

senses.def: the act of saying something again or in a different way, especially so that it is more clearly or strongly expressed
a place where you can buy and eat a meal

examples.en: We're going to try this Italian restaurant that just opened.
examples.zh: 我们打算去这家刚开张的意大利餐馆吃吃看。

examples.en: They stopped at a fast-food restaurant on the way to the concert.
examples.zh: 他们在去音乐会的路上在一家快餐店停了下来。

examples.en: We had a meal in a restaurant.
examples.zh: 我们在餐厅吃了顿饭。

examples.en: We went to my favourite restaurant to celebrate.
examples.zh: 我们到我最喜欢的餐馆里庆祝了一番。

examples.en: a restaurant chain/owner
examples.zh: 餐饮连锁店；餐馆老板

senses.def: a coach on a train in which meals are served
a person who owns and manages a restaurant
that makes you feel relaxed and peaceful
senses.zh: 闲适宁静的；使人感到悠闲的

examples.en: a hotel with a restful atmosphere
examples.zh: 气氛闲适幽雅的旅馆

examples.en: I find this music very restful.
examples.zh: 我觉得这音乐很平静。

senses.def: a grave
senses.zh: 长眠之地，安息处（grave 的委婉说法）

examples.en: her final/last resting place
examples.zh: 她的长眠之处

senses.def: a place where you can rest
the act of giving back something that was lost or stolen to its owner
senses.zh: 归还（真正物主）；归还（赃物等）

examples.en: the restitution of property seized under Communist rule
examples.zh: 归还共产党统治下没收的财产

senses.def: payment, usually money, for some harm or wrong that somebody has suffered

examples.en: to make restitution for the damage caused
examples.zh: 赔偿所造成的损失

examples.en: The company has a legal duty to make restitution to passengers for any inconvenience caused.
examples.zh: 这家公司法律上有义务对给乘客造成的任何不便进行赔偿。

senses.def: unable to stay still, or unwilling to be controlled, especially because you feel bored or not satisfied
senses.zh: 难驾驭的；焦躁不安的；不耐烦的

examples.en: The crowd was growing increasingly restive.
examples.zh: 人群变得越来越不安。

examples.en: The news was relayed to the restive citizens.
examples.zh: 这个消息被传达给了不安的公民。

senses.def: the state of being unable to stay still, or a desire not to be controlled, especially because you feel bored or not satisfied
senses.zh: 难驾驭的；焦躁不安的；不耐烦的

senses.def: unable to stay still or be happy where you are, because you are bored or need a change

examples.en: The audience was becoming restless.
examples.zh: 观众开始不耐烦了。

examples.en: After five years in the job, he was beginning to feel restless.
examples.zh: 这份工作干了五年以后，他开始厌烦了。

examples.en: The children always get restless on long trips.
examples.zh: 孩子们在长途旅行中总是焦躁不安。

examples.en: She was in a restless mood.
examples.zh: 她心情焦躁不安。

examples.en: Lydia had always been a restless child.
examples.zh: 莉迪亚一直是个不安分的孩子。

senses.def: without real rest or sleep
senses.zh: 没有真正休息的；没有睡眠的

examples.en: a restless night
examples.zh: 不眠之夜

examples.en: He woke from a restless sleep.
examples.zh: 他从不安的睡眠中醒来。

senses.def: in a way that shows you are unable to stay still or be happy where you are, because you are bored or need a change

examples.en: He moved restlessly from one foot to the other.
examples.zh: 他心神不宁，双脚不停地倒着重心。

senses.def: without resting or sleeping properly
senses.zh: 没有真正休息的；没有睡眠的

examples.en: She tossed restlessly until she finally fell asleep.
examples.zh: 她翻来覆去，直到终于睡着了。

senses.def: the state of being unable to stay still or be happy where you are, because you are bored or need a change

examples.en: the restlessness of youth
examples.zh: 年轻人的躁动

senses.def: the state of being unable to rest or sleep properly

examples.en: She was suffering from headaches and restlessness at night.
examples.zh: 她感到头痛，夜间烦躁不安。

senses.def: to fill something with new or different things to replace those that have been used, sold, etc.; to get a new supply of something
senses.zh: 更新（旧物品）；补充（货源）；再补给

examples.en: Environmentalists are planning to restock the river with fish.
examples.zh: 环保人士正计划在河里再放养一批鱼。

senses.def: the work of repairing and cleaning an old building, a painting, etc. so that its condition is as good as it originally was

examples.en: restoration work
examples.zh: 修复工作

examples.en: The palace is closed for restoration.
examples.zh: 王宫因整修而停止开放。

senses.def: the act of bringing back a system, a law, etc. that existed previously

examples.en: the restoration of diplomatic relations between the two countries
examples.zh: 两国恢复外交关系

examples.en: the restoration of democracy/the monarchy
examples.zh: 民主制度／君主政体的恢复

senses.def: the act of returning something to its correct place, condition or owner

examples.en: the restoration of the Elgin marbles to Greece
examples.zh: 埃尔金大理石雕塑品之交还希腊

senses.def: the time in Britain after 1660 when, following a period with no king or queen, Charles II became king
senses.zh: 王政复辟时期（1660 年，英国经历了一段无王时期后，查理二世登基为王）

examples.en: Restoration comedy/poetry (= written during and after this time)
examples.zh: 王政复辟时期的喜剧／诗歌

senses.def: a type of comedy play written during and after the Restoration
making you feel strong and healthy again
senses.zh: 恢复健康的；促使康复的

examples.en: the restorative power of fresh air
examples.zh: 新鲜空气的康复功效

senses.def: connected with treatment that repairs the body or a part of it

examples.en: restorative dentistry/surgery
examples.zh: 整形牙科／外科

senses.def: a thing that makes you feel better, stronger, etc.
senses.zh: 有助于恢复健康的事物；滋补品

examples.en: Sleep is the best restorative there is.
examples.zh: 睡眠是最好的恢复方式。

senses.def: a system of justice that focuses on helping criminals to change by establishing a relationship with their victims and with the wider community
senses.zh: 恢复性司法，修复式正义

examples.en: The study advised greater use of restorative justice to replace prison sentences.
examples.zh: 该研究建议更多地使用恢复性司法来取代监禁。

senses.def: to bring back a situation or feeling that existed before

examples.en: The measures are intended to restore public confidence in the economy.
examples.zh: 这些举措旨在恢复公众对经济的信心。

examples.en: Order was quickly restored after the riots.
examples.zh: 暴乱过后秩序很快得到了恢复。

examples.en: Such kindness restores your faith in human nature (= makes you believe most people are kind).
examples.zh: 这样的善心使人又一次感到人性善良。

examples.en: The operation restored his sight (= made him able to see again).
examples.zh: 手术使他恢复了视力。

examples.en: Peace has now been restored to the area.
examples.zh: 该地区现已恢复和平。

senses.def: to bring somebody/something back to a former condition, place or position

examples.en: He is now fully restored to health.
examples.zh: 他现在完全恢复了健康。

examples.en: We hope to restore the garden to its former glory (= make it as beautiful as it used to be).
examples.zh: 我们想把这花园变得和过去一样美丽。

examples.en: This cream claims to restore your skin to its youthful condition.
examples.zh: 这款面霜声称可以使您的皮肤恢复年轻状态。

senses.def: to repair a building, work of art, piece of furniture, etc. so that it looks as good as it did originally

examples.en: Her job is restoring old paintings.
examples.zh: 她的工作是修复旧画。

examples.en: The house has been lovingly restored to the way it looked in 1900 when it was built.
examples.zh: 这座房子经过精心修复，恢复了 1900 年建成时的样子。

senses.def: to bring a law, tradition, way of working, etc. back into use

examples.en: to restore ancient traditions
examples.zh: 恢复古老的传统

examples.en: Some people argue that the death penalty should be restored.
examples.zh: 有些人主张恢复死刑。

senses.def: to give something that was lost or stolen back to somebody

examples.en: The police have now restored the painting to its rightful owner.
examples.zh: 警察已经把这幅油画归还给了它的合法主人。

senses.def: a person whose job is to repair old buildings, works of art, etc. so that they look as they did when new
to stop somebody/something from doing something, especially by using physical force

examples.en: The prisoner had to be restrained by the police.
examples.zh: 警方只好强行制住囚犯。

examples.en: He placed a restraining hand on her arm.
examples.zh: 他拉住她的胳膊制止她。

examples.en: They have obtained an injunction restraining the company from selling the product.
examples.zh: 他们已经得到阻止这家公司出售这一产品的禁销令。

examples.en: I had to restrain her from hitting out at passers-by.
examples.zh: 我得强行制止她袭击路人。

senses.def: to stop yourself from feeling an emotion or doing something that you would like to do
senses.zh: 约束（自己）；控制（自己）；忍住

examples.en: John managed to restrain his anger.
examples.zh: 约翰努力压制住自己的怒气。

examples.en: I restrained the urge to punch him.
examples.zh: 我抑制住了自己的冲动，没用拳头打他。

examples.en: She had to restrain herself from crying out in pain.
examples.zh: 她只得忍住疼痛，不哭出来。

examples.en: I was tempted to answer back, but I restrained myself.
examples.zh: 我想还嘴，但忍住了。

senses.def: to stop something that is growing or increasing from becoming too large

examples.en: The government is taking steps to restrain inflation.
examples.zh: 政府正在采取措施控制通货膨胀。

examples.en: Economic growth first induced, then restrained population growth.
examples.zh: 经济增长首先促进人口增长，然后抑制人口增长。

senses.def: an official order given by a judge which demands that something must or must not be done. A restraining order
a rule, a fact, an idea, etc. that limits or controls what people can do
senses.zh: 约束力；管制措施；制约因素

examples.en: The government has imposed export restraints on some products.
examples.zh: 政府对一些产品实行了出口控制。

examples.en: social restraints on drinking alcohol
examples.zh: 社会对饮酒的限制

senses.def: the act of controlling or limiting something because it is necessary or sensible to do so

examples.en: The unions are unlikely to accept any sort of wage restraint.
examples.zh: 工会不大可能接受任何形式的工资限制。

examples.en: They said that they would fight without restraint (= completely freely) for what they wanted.
examples.zh: 他们说他们将为理想而战斗到底。

senses.def: the quality of behaving calmly and with control

examples.en: The police appealed to the crowd for restraint.
examples.zh: 警方呼吁群众保持克制。

examples.en: He exercised considerable restraint in ignoring the insults.
examples.zh: 他表现出相当的克制，没去理会种种侮辱。

senses.def: the use of physical force to control somebody who is behaving in a violent way

examples.en: the physical restraint of prisoners
examples.zh: 对囚犯的人身限制

senses.def: a type of seat belt

examples.en: Children must use an approved child restraint or adult seat belt.
examples.zh: 儿童必须使用经过认可的儿童安全带或成人座椅安全带。

intro.en: These are all words for something that limits what you can do or what can happen.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示限制或限定。

items.def: the greatest or smallest amount of something that is allowed:
items.zh: 指极限、限量、限额

examples.en: The EU has set strict limits on pollution levels.
examples.zh: 欧盟对污染程度作了严格的限定。

items.def: (rather formal) a rule or law that limits what you can do:
items.zh: 指限制规定、限制法规

examples.en: There are no restrictions on the amount of money you can withdraw.
examples.zh: 取款没有限额。

items.def: (often in compounds) the act of limiting or managing something; a method of doing this:
items.zh: （常构成复合词）指限制、约束、管理、管制

examples.en: arms control
examples.zh: 军备控制

items.def: (rather formal) a fact or decision that limits what you can do:
items.zh: 指限制、限定、约束

examples.en: We have to work within severe constraints of time and money.
examples.zh: 我们必须在时间紧迫、资金紧张的限制下工作。

items.def: (rather formal) a decision, a rule, an idea, etc. that limits what you can do; the act of limiting something because it is necessary or sensible to do so:
items.zh: 指约束力、管制措施、制约因素、控制、限制

examples.en: The government has imposed export restraints on some products.
examples.zh: 政府对一些产品实行了出口控制。

items.def: the act or process of limiting something; a rule, fact or condition that limits something:
items.zh: 指限制、控制、起限制作用的规则、事实或条件

examples.en: They would resist any limitation of their powers.
examples.zh: 他们会抵制对他们权力的任何限制。

senses.def: to limit the size, amount or range of something

examples.en: Speed is restricted to 30 mph in towns.
examples.zh: 在城里车速不得超过每小时 30 英里。

examples.en: We restrict the number of students per class to ten.
examples.zh: 我们将每个班的学生人数限定为十人。

examples.en: Fog severely restricted visibility.
examples.zh: 浓雾严重影响了能见度。

examples.en: Having small children tends to restrict your freedom.
examples.zh: 有了小孩往往会限制你的自由。

senses.def: to stop somebody/something from moving or acting freely

examples.en: The long skirt restricted her movements.
examples.zh: 长裙妨碍了她的行动。

senses.def: to control something with rules or laws

examples.en: Access to the club is restricted to members only.
examples.zh: 俱乐部仅对会员开放。

senses.def: to allow yourself or somebody to have only a limited amount of something or to do only a particular kind of activity

examples.en: I restrict myself to one cup of coffee a day.
examples.zh: 我控制自己每天只喝一杯咖啡。

examples.en: Why don't you restrict yourself to setting down the facts?
examples.zh: 你为什么不限制自己陈述事实呢？

examples.en: We restrict ourselves to one takeaway meal a week.
examples.zh: 我们限制自己每周只能吃一顿外卖。

senses.def: a rule or law that limits what you can do or what can happen

examples.en: import/speed/travel restrictions
examples.zh: 进口／速度／旅行限制

examples.en: to impose/place a restriction on something
examples.zh: 对某事实行限制

examples.en: The government has agreed to lift restrictions on press freedom.
examples.zh: 政府已经同意撤销对新闻自由的限制。

examples.en: There are no restrictions on the amount of money you can withdraw.
examples.zh: 取款没有限额。

senses.def: the act of limiting or controlling somebody/something

examples.en: sports clothes that prevent any restriction of movement
examples.zh: 宽松的运动服

examples.en: A diet to lose weight relies on calorie restriction in order to obtain results.
examples.zh: 节食减肥依赖于热量限制才能取得效果。

senses.def: a thing that limits the amount of freedom you have

examples.en: the restrictions of a prison
examples.zh: 监狱的种种约束

examples.zh: 军备控制

examples.zh: 我们必须在时间紧迫、资金紧张的限制下工作。
