examples.zh: 我们可以把辩论更深入一步。

senses.def: a raised area, usually in a theatre, etc. where actors, dancers, etc. perform

examples.en: There were more than 50 people on stage in one scene.
examples.zh: 有一场戏中舞台上的人有 50 多个。

examples.en: Half the band walked off stage.
examples.zh: 乐队一半人员走下了舞台。

examples.en: The audience threw flowers onto the stage.
examples.zh: 观众把鲜花抛向舞台。

examples.en: The main character then takes the stage (= comes onto it).
examples.zh: 主人公随后上台。

examples.en: Rose exits stage left (= to the left hand side of the stage).
examples.zh: 罗斯从左侧退出舞台（= 到舞台的左侧）。

senses.def: the theatre and the world of acting as a form of entertainment

examples.en: The screenplay was originally written for the stage.
examples.zh: 剧本最初是为舞台而写的。

examples.en: His parents didn't want him to go on the stage (= to be an actor).
examples.zh: 他父母不想让他当演员。

examples.en: She was a popular star of stage and screen (= theatre and cinema/movies).
examples.zh: 她是观众喜爱的舞台银幕两栖明星。

examples.en: a stage play/musical/show
examples.zh: 舞台剧／音乐剧／演出

senses.def: an area of activity where important things happen, especially in politics
senses.zh: （政治等活动的）领域；（政治）舞台

examples.en: She was forced to the centre of the political stage.
examples.zh: 她被推到了政治舞台的中心。

examples.en: The country is now a major player on the world stage.
examples.zh: 该国在当今世界舞台上扮演着重要角色。

examples.en: Germany is playing a leading role on the international stage.
examples.zh: 德国在国际政治舞台上扮演着重要角色。

senses.def: a stagecoach
to make it possible for something to happen; to make something likely to happen
senses.zh: 使某事成为可能；为某事铺平道路

examples.en: Family problems in childhood can set the stage for stress in adult life.
examples.zh: 童年时期的家庭问题可能为成年生活带来压力。

examples.en: The thrilling semi-finals set the stage for what should be a great game.
examples.zh: 半决赛尚且激动人心，决赛将更扣人心弦了。

senses.def: to organize and present a play or an event for people to see

examples.en: to stage a play/an event/an exhibition
examples.zh: 举办戏剧表演／活动／展览

examples.en: The local theatre group is staging a production of ‘Hamlet’.
examples.zh: 当地剧团在上演《哈姆雷特》。

examples.en: Birmingham has bid to stage the next national athletics championships.
examples.zh: 伯明翰申办下届全国田径锦标赛。

senses.def: to organize and take part in action that needs careful planning, especially as a public protest

examples.en: to stage a protest/demonstration/rally
examples.zh: 组织抗议／示威／集会

examples.en: to stage a sit-in/strike/walkout
examples.zh: 举行静坐/罢工/罢工

examples.en: Generals staged a coup in 1964, beginning 21 years of military dictatorship.
examples.zh: 军队将领在 1964 年发动政变，开始了 21 年的军事独裁统治。

senses.def: to make something happen

examples.en: The dollar staged a recovery earlier today.
examples.zh: 今天早些时候，美元出现回升。

examples.en: After five years in retirement, he staged a comeback to international tennis.
examples.zh: 退役五年之后，他重返国际网坛。

senses.def: to make it possible for something to happen; to make something likely to happen
senses.zh: 使某事成为可能；为某事铺平道路

examples.en: Family problems in childhood can set the stage for stress in adult life.
examples.zh: 童年时期的家庭问题可能为成年生活带来压力。

examples.en: The thrilling semi-finals set the stage for what should be a great game.
examples.zh: 半决赛尚且激动人心，决赛将更扣人心弦了。

senses.def: a note in the text of a play telling actors when to come on to or leave the stage, what actions to perform, etc.
senses.zh: 舞台指示（剧本中关于演员上下场、表演动作等的说明）

examples.en: The stage direction reads, ‘Exit left’.
examples.zh: 舞台指示上写着：“向左出口”。

examples.en: Shakespeare's famous stage direction: ‘Exit, pursued by a bear.’
examples.zh: 莎士比亚著名的舞台指示：“退场，一只熊紧追在后。”

examples.en: As the stage directions indicate, it is early morning in Moscow.
examples.zh: 按舞台说明所示，那是莫斯科的清晨。

senses.def: the entrance at the back of a theatre used by actors, staff, etc.
senses.zh: 剧场后门（供演职人员进出）

examples.en: A crowd of fans was waiting outside the stage door.
examples.zh: 一大群歌迷在舞台门外等候。

examples.en: Fans hung around the stage door hoping to meet the band.
examples.zh: 粉丝们逗留在剧场后门希望能见乐队一面。

senses.def: nervous feelings felt by performers before they appear in front of an audience
senses.zh: 怯场（演员出场前的紧张不安）

examples.en: Even experienced actors can suffer from stage fright.
examples.zh: 即使富有经验的演员也会怯场。

senses.def: on the left side of a stage in a theatre, as seen by an actor facing the audience
senses.zh: （演员面对观众时的）舞台左侧

senses.def: to act as stage manager
to arrange and carefully plan an event that the public will see, especially in order to give a particular impression
senses.zh: 精心安排，周密策划（公共活动）

examples.en: The entire sequence of events was stage-managed by the government.
examples.zh: 整个事件的发生都是由政府精心策划的。

senses.def: the person who is responsible for the stage, lights, scenery
a name that an actor uses instead of his or her real name

examples.en: David Harries adopted the stage name Dixon Hare when he became a full-time actor.
examples.zh: 戴维·哈里斯成为专职演员后用了狄克逊·黑尔作为艺名。

senses.def: on the right side of a stage in a theatre, as seen by an actor facing the audience
senses.zh: （演员面对观众时的）舞台右侧

senses.def: enjoying the theatre a lot and wishing very much to become an actor
senses.zh: 醉心舞台渴望当演员的

senses.def: words that are spoken quietly by an actor to the audience and that the other people on stage are not supposed to hear
senses.zh: 低声旁白（演员避开台上其他角色说给观众听的）

senses.def: words that are spoken quietly by somebody but that they in fact want everyone to hear
senses.zh: 故意让所有人听见的悄悄话

examples.en: ‘I knew this would happen,’ she said in a stage whisper.
examples.zh: “我早知道会出这样的事。”她轻声说给所有人听。

senses.def: a large carriage

examples.en: Stagecoaches were often attacked by robbers and bandits.
examples.zh: 驿马车经常遭到强盗和强盗的袭击。

examples.en: They travelled by stagecoach as far as York.
examples.zh: 他们乘公共马车最远到达约克。

examples.en: Travel by stagecoach was uncomfortable and often hazardous.
examples.zh: 坐驿站马车出行并不舒服，而且经常会有危险。

senses.def: skill in presenting plays in a theatre
senses.zh: 舞台表演技巧；剧场表演艺术

senses.def: a person whose job is to help move scenery
senses.zh: 舞台工作人员（负责移动布景、准备道具等）

senses.def: a party that a woman has with her (usually female) friends just before she gets married
senses.zh: 婚礼前夕为新娘举行，只有女性朋友参加的）告别单身聚会

examples.en: His fiancée had gone to a bar in town for her stagette.
examples.zh: 他的未婚妻去镇上的一家酒吧参加舞台表演。

senses.def: not natural, as if it is being acted by somebody in a play
senses.zh: 不自然的；做作的；演戏似的

senses.def: an economic situation where there is high inflation
senses.zh: 滞胀（高通胀与低就业率或经济低迷并存）

senses.def: a weak unsteady way of walking, as if you are about to fall
senses.zh: 走路摇摇晃晃，好像快要摔倒一样

examples.en: to walk with a stagger
examples.zh: 步履蹒跚

senses.def: to walk with weak unsteady steps, as if you are about to fall
senses.zh: 摇摇晃晃地走；蹒跚；踉跄

examples.en: The injured woman staggered to her feet.
examples.zh: 受伤的女人摇摇晃晃地站起身来。

examples.en: He staggered home, drunk.
examples.zh: 他喝醉酒，踉跄着回了家。

examples.en: We seem to stagger from one crisis to the next.
examples.zh: 我们仿佛在接连不断的危机中举步维艰。

examples.en: The company is staggering under the weight of a £10m debt.
examples.zh: 公司在 1 000 万英镑债务的重压下步履艰难。

examples.en: I managed to stagger the last few steps.
examples.zh: 我好不容易跌跌撞撞走了这最后几步。

senses.def: to shock or surprise somebody very much

examples.en: Her remarks staggered me.
examples.zh: 她的话让我震惊。

examples.en: The inspectors were staggered at the level of incompetence among senior staff.
examples.zh: 公司高级职员的不称职让视察员们觉得不可思议。

examples.en: It staggers me that the government is doing nothing about it.
examples.zh: 政府对此竟然不采取任何措施，我觉得不可思议。

senses.def: to arrange for events that would normally happen at the same time to start or happen at different times

examples.en: There were so many runners that they had to stagger the start.
examples.zh: 参加赛跑的选手很多，他们不得不把起跑点错开。

senses.def: in a way that is so great, shocking

examples.en: staggeringly beautiful/expensive
examples.zh: 美／贵得惊人

senses.def: an area where soldiers and equipment are gathered before a military operation

examples.en: a staging area for training exercises
examples.zh: 士兵操练的集结待命区

senses.def: a place where people gather to organize an activity or a trip
senses.zh: （组织活动或旅行的）集合处，行动指挥中心

examples.en: The church was used as a staging area for the flood relief effort.
examples.zh: 这个教堂当时被用作抗洪救灾的指挥中心。

senses.def: a place where people, planes, ships, etc. regularly stop during a long journey
senses.zh: 中途站（或机场、停靠码头）

senses.def: stagnant

examples.en: Few fish survive in the stagnant waters of the lake.
examples.zh: 很少有鱼能够在死水湖中生存。

senses.def: not developing, growing or changing
senses.zh: 停滞的；不发展的；无变化的

examples.en: a stagnant economy
examples.zh: 停滞的经济

examples.en: a stagnant population
examples.zh: 人口停滞

examples.en: The housing market has been largely stagnant over the past few months.
examples.zh: 过去几个月，房地产市场基本停滞。

senses.def: to stop developing or making progress

examples.en: Profits have stagnated.
examples.zh: 利润原地踏步。

examples.en: I feel I'm stagnating in this job.
examples.zh: 我觉得，干这份工作我没有长进。

examples.en: Businesses must adapt to change or stagnate.
examples.zh: 企业必须适应变化，否则就会停滞不前。

senses.def: to be or become stagnant

examples.en: The water in the pond was stagnating.
examples.zh: 池塘里的水逐渐变成了死水。

senses.def: the fact of no longer developing or making progress

examples.en: a period of economic stagnation
examples.zh: 经济停滞期

senses.def: the fact of not moving and therefore smelling unpleasant

examples.en: water/air stagnation
examples.zh: 水/空气停滞

senses.def: not natural, as if it is being acted by somebody in a play
senses.zh: 不自然的；做作的；演戏似的

examples.en: He fell to the ground writhing in stagy agony.
examples.zh: 他倒在地上，痛苦地扭动着。

senses.def: not fun or interesting; boring and old-fashioned
senses.zh: 没意思的；古板的；一本正经的

examples.en: The museum is trying to get rid of its staid image.
examples.zh: 这家博物馆正努力摆脱古板的形象。

senses.def: to leave a mark that is difficult to remove on something; to be marked in this way

examples.en: I hope it doesn't stain the carpet.
examples.zh: 希望它别把地毯弄脏。

examples.en: This carpet stains easily.
examples.zh: 这块地毯不耐脏。

examples.en: The juice from the berries stained their fingers red.
examples.zh: 浆果汁把他们的手指染成了红色。

senses.def: to change the colour of something using a coloured liquid

examples.en: to stain wood
examples.zh: 给木料上色

examples.en: Stain the specimen before looking at it under the microscope.
examples.zh: 先把标本染色，再放到显微镜下观察。

examples.en: They stained the floors dark brown.
examples.zh: 他们把地板涂成了深棕色。

examples.en: The floors had been stained dark brown.
examples.zh: 地板被涂成了深棕色。

senses.def: to damage the opinion that people have of something

examples.en: The events had stained the city's reputation unfairly.
examples.zh: 这些事件使该市背上了不应有的恶名。

senses.def: a dirty mark on something, that is difficult to remove

examples.en: a blood/a coffee/an ink stain
examples.zh: 血渍；咖啡渍；墨痕

examples.en: stubborn stains (= that are very difficult to remove)
examples.zh: 顽固的污渍

examples.en: How can I get this stain out?
examples.zh: 我怎么才能把这点污渍除去？

examples.en: The carpet has been treated so that it is stain-resistant (= it does not stain easily).
examples.zh: 这地毯已经过处理，不易挂污。

senses.def: a liquid used for changing the colour of wood or cloth

examples.en: wood stain
examples.zh: 木材染色剂

examples.en: Apply two coats of white stain.
examples.zh: 涂两层白色。

senses.def: something that damages a person’s reputation, so that people think badly of them

examples.en: He left the court without a stain on his character.
examples.zh: 他经法庭一役，人格丝毫无损。

examples.en: The scandal left a dark stain on his reputation.
examples.zh: 这个丑闻给他的名声留下了污点。

synonyms.words: stain ▪ fingerprint ▪ streak ▪ speck ▪ blot ▪ smear ▪ spot

intro.en: These are all words for a small area of dirt or another substance on a surface.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指污点、斑点、污迹。

items.def: a small area of dirt, a spot or a cut on a surface that makes it look less good:
items.zh: 污点；污渍；斑点；疤痕

examples.en: The kids left dirty marks all over the kitchen floor.
examples.zh: 孩子们把厨房的地板弄得污迹斑斑。

items.def: a dirty mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid:
items.zh: 指污点、污渍

examples.en: blood stains
examples.zh: 血迹

items.def: a mark on a surface made by the pattern of lines on the end of a person’s finger, often used by the police to identify criminals:
items.zh: 指指纹、指印

examples.en: Her fingerprints were all over the gun.
examples.zh: 那支枪上布满了她的指纹。

items.def: a long, thin mark or line that is a different colour from the surface it is on:
items.zh: 指条纹、条痕

examples.en: She had streaks of grey in her hair.
examples.zh: 她头上已是白发绺绺。

items.def: a very small mark, spot or piece of a substance on something:
items.zh: 指小点、污点

examples.en: There isn’t a speck of dust anywhere in the house.
examples.zh: 整间房子一尘不染。

items.def: a spot or dirty mark left on something by a substance such as ink or paint being dropped on a surface
items.zh: 指污点、墨渍

items.def: a mark made by something such as oil or paint being spread or rubbed on a surface
items.zh: 指污迹、油渍、污渍、污点

items.def: a small dirty mark on something:
items.zh: 指污迹、污渍、污点

examples.en: There were grease spots all over the walls.
examples.zh: 墙上满是油渍。

senses.def: pieces of coloured glass that are put together to make windows showing pictures or special designs, especially in churches
a type of steel that does not rust

examples.en: knives made of stainless steel
examples.zh: 不锈钢刀具

senses.def: on, of or for stairs

examples.en: the stair carpet
examples.zh: 楼梯地毯

examples.en: The carpet was held in place by brass stair rods.
examples.zh: 地毯用黄铜楼梯毯棍固定住。

senses.def: a set of steps built between two floors inside a building

examples.en: We had to carry the piano up three flights of stairs.
examples.zh: 我们不得不抬着钢琴上了三段楼梯。

examples.en: He climbed the stairs to his bedroom.
examples.zh: 他爬上楼梯去自己的卧室。

examples.en: The children ran up the stairs.
examples.zh: 孩子们跑上楼去。

examples.en: He remembered passing her on the stairs.
examples.zh: 他记得在楼梯上与她擦肩而过。

examples.en: at the bottom/top of the stairs
examples.zh: 在楼梯下端／顶端

senses.def: one of the steps in a set of stairs

examples.en: How many stairs are there up to the second floor?
examples.zh: 上到第三层一共有多少磴楼梯？

senses.def: a set of stairs inside a building including the banisters

examples.en: The house had a panelled hall and a fine oak stair.
examples.zh: 房子的门厅装有镶板墙裙，楼梯是用高级栎木建造的。

senses.def: in the part of a house where the servants lived in the past
in the part of a house where the servants lived in the past
a set of stairs inside a building including the banisters

examples.en: a marble/stone/wooden staircase
examples.zh: 大理石／石头／木楼梯

senses.def: a piece of equipment in the form of a seat that somebody can sit on to be moved up and down stairs, used by people who find it difficult to walk up and down stairs without help, especially in their own home
senses.zh: （尤指家用）座椅式升降器（供无法步行上下楼的人使用）

senses.def: a set of stairs inside or outside a building
the space in a building in which the stairs are built
senses.zh: 楼梯井（建筑物内楼梯占用的空间）

senses.def: money that somebody invests in a company

examples.en: a 20 per cent stake in the business
examples.zh: 那家公司 20% 的股份

examples.en: a controlling/majority/minority stake
examples.zh: 控股/多数/少数股权

senses.def: a part or share in a business, plan, etc. that will bring you money or other benefits if it succeeds
senses.zh: （在公司、计划等中的）利益，利害关系

examples.en: She has a personal stake in the success of the play.
examples.zh: 这出戏成功与否对她个人有重大利害关系。

examples.en: Many young people no longer feel they have a stake in society.
examples.zh: 很多年轻人不再觉得他们与社会休戚相关。

examples.en: He has a personal stake in the outcome of the war.
examples.zh: 战争的结果与他有切身的利害关系。

senses.def: something that you risk losing, especially money, when you try to predict the result of a race, game, etc., or when you are involved in an activity that can succeed or fail

examples.en: How much was the stake (= how much did you bet)?
examples.zh: 下了多少注？

examples.en: They were playing cards for high stakes (= a lot of money).
examples.zh: 他们当时正在打扑克，赌注很高。

examples.en: With only two points separating the top five players, the stakes are high as they enter the final round.
examples.zh: 前五名选手仅相差两分，进入最后一轮的赌注很高。

senses.def: a wooden or metal post that is pointed at one end and pushed into the ground in order to support something, mark a particular place, etc.

examples.en: Tall plants can be secured by tying them to stakes.
examples.zh: 高大的植物可以通过将它们绑在木桩上来固定。

senses.def: a wooden post that somebody could be tied to in former times before being burnt to death (= killed by fire)

examples.en: Joan of Arc was burnt at the stake.
examples.zh: 圣女贞德被处以火刑。

senses.def: the money that is paid to the winners in horse racing
used in the names of some horse races
senses.zh: （用于某些赛马赛事的名称）…赛

senses.def: that can be won or lost, depending on the success of a particular action
senses.zh: 成败难料；得失都可能；有风险

examples.en: We cannot afford to take risks when people's lives are at stake.
examples.zh: 在性命攸关的事情上，不容我们有闪失。

examples.en: The prize at stake is a place in the final.
examples.zh: 这次如果获胜，便能进入决赛。

senses.def: to be prepared to do anything in order to defend your opinions or beliefs
senses.zh: 为坚持自己的观点（或信仰）甘冒一切危险；为维护自己的观点（或信仰）不惜赴汤蹈火

examples.en: He would have gone to the stake for his belief in his daughter’s innocence.
examples.zh: 他会因为相信女儿的清白而被送上火刑柱。

senses.def: used to say how much of a particular quality a person has, as if they were in a competition in which some people are more successful than others
senses.zh: （评论一个人的某种品质高或低）要是比…的话，论…

examples.en: John doesn't do too well in the personality stakes.
examples.zh: 论人格魅力，约翰很一般。

examples.en: She was determined to win in the fashion stakes.
examples.zh: 她决意要在时装比赛中获胜。

senses.def: to suddenly move from your house and go to live somewhere else

examples.en: He pulled up stakes and went back to France.
examples.zh: 他撤回赌注并返回法国。

senses.def: to risk money or something important on the result of something

examples.en: He staked £25 on the favourite (= for example, in horse racing).
examples.zh: 他在那匹众人看好的马上押了 25 英镑。

examples.en: She staked her political career on tax reform, and lost.
examples.zh: 她把自己的政治前程押在税制改革上，结果赌输了。

examples.en: That's him over there—I'd stake my life on it (= I am completely confident).
examples.zh: 就是那边那个人，我敢拿脑袋打赌。

senses.def: to support something with a stake

examples.en: to stake newly planted trees
examples.zh: 用木桩支撑新植的树

examples.en: The young trees should be staked after planting.
examples.zh: 幼树种植后应进行立桩。

senses.def: to say or show publicly that you think something should be yours
senses.zh: 公开宣布自己（对某物）的所有权；向公众表示某物应属于自己

examples.en: Adams staked his claim for a place in the Olympic team with his easy win yesterday.
examples.zh: 亚当斯昨天轻松获胜，这无异于告诉人们奥运代表队中应有他的位置。

senses.def: that can be won or lost, depending on the success of a particular action
senses.zh: 成败难料；得失都可能；有风险

examples.en: We cannot afford to take risks when people's lives are at stake.
examples.zh: 在性命攸关的事情上，不容我们有闪失。

examples.en: The prize at stake is a place in the final.
examples.zh: 这次如果获胜，便能进入决赛。

items.idm: go to the stake over/for something

senses.def: to be prepared to do anything in order to defend your opinions or beliefs
senses.zh: 为坚持自己的观点（或信仰）甘冒一切危险；为维护自己的观点（或信仰）不惜赴汤蹈火

examples.en: He would have gone to the stake for his belief in his daughter’s innocence.
examples.zh: 他会因为相信女儿的清白而被送上火刑柱。

senses.def: used to say how much of a particular quality a person has, as if they were in a competition in which some people are more successful than others
senses.zh: （评论一个人的某种品质高或低）要是比…的话，论…

examples.en: John doesn't do too well in the personality stakes.
examples.zh: 论人格魅力，约翰很一般。

examples.en: She was determined to win in the fashion stakes.
examples.zh: 她决意要在时装比赛中获胜。

senses.def: to suddenly move from your house and go to live somewhere else

examples.en: He pulled up stakes and went back to France.
examples.zh: 他撤回赌注并返回法国。

senses.def: to say or show publicly that you think something should be yours
senses.zh: 公开宣布自己（对某物）的所有权；向公众表示某物应属于自己

examples.en: Adams staked his claim for a place in the Olympic team with his easy win yesterday.
examples.zh: 亚当斯昨天轻松获胜，这无异于告诉人们奥运代表队中应有他的位置。

senses.def: to say or show publicly that you think something should be yours
senses.zh: 公开宣布自己（对某物）的所有权；向公众表示某物应属于自己

examples.en: Adams staked his claim for a place in the Olympic team with his easy win yesterday.
examples.zh: 亚当斯昨天轻松获胜，这无异于告诉人们奥运代表队中应有他的位置。

senses.def: to clearly mark the limits of something that you claim is yours
senses.zh: 清楚地界定自认为属于自己的东西

senses.def: to state your opinion, position, etc. on something very clearly
senses.zh: 明确阐述自己的看法（或立场等）

examples.en: The president staked out his position on the issue.
examples.zh: 总统明确阐述了他在这个问题上的立场。

senses.def: to watch a place secretly, especially for signs of illegal activity

examples.en: Detectives had been staking out the house for several weeks.
examples.zh: 警探们已对这所房子监视了几个星期。

senses.def: a situation in which police watch a building secretly to find evidence of illegal activities

examples.en: an armed stake-out of the building
examples.zh: 对建筑物进行武装监视

senses.def: a person or company that is involved in a particular organization, project, system, etc., especially because they have invested money in it
senses.zh: （某组织、工程、体系等的）参与人，参与方，利益相关者

examples.en: All our employees are stakeholders in the company.
examples.zh: 我们所有的员工都是公司的利益共享人。

examples.en: The government has said it wants to create a stakeholder economy in which all members of society feel that they have an interest in its success.
examples.zh: 政府表示希望建立一种人人参与的经济模式，让社会全体成员觉得其繁荣将给每个人带来利益。

senses.def: a person who holds all the bets placed on a game or race and who pays the money to the winner
a type of private pension plan
senses.zh: 利益相关者养老金：2001年在英国引入的一种私人养老金计划。利益相关者养老金必须符合政府设定的某些标准并且对养老金公司可以收取的费用进行了限制。他们必须允许人们根据工作情况在不同的时间支付不同的金额，并且如果他们转移工作，也必须保持相同的计划。

senses.def: a long pointed piece of rock hanging down from the roof of a cave
a piece of rock pointing upwards from the floor of a cave
no longer fresh and therefore unpleasant to eat

examples.en: This bread's going stale.
examples.zh: 面包不新鲜了。

examples.en: There was one piece of stale chocolate cake left in the tin.
examples.zh: 烤盘里还剩一块不新鲜的巧克力蛋糕。

senses.def: no longer fresh; smelling unpleasant
senses.zh: 不新鲜的；污浊的；难闻的

examples.en: The atmosphere was stale with cigarette smoke.
examples.zh: 烟味令空气污浊。

examples.en: The room smelt of stale sweat.
examples.zh: 房间里闻着有股汗臭味。

examples.en: The room smelled musty and stale.
examples.zh: 这个房间闻起来有股发霉的陈味儿。

senses.def: something that is stale
senses.zh: 陈腐的；没有新意的；老掉牙的

examples.en: stale jokes
examples.zh: 老掉牙的笑话

examples.en: Their marriage had gone stale.
examples.zh: 他们的婚姻已了无热情。

senses.def: a person who is stale
senses.zh: （因持续做某事时间太长）厌倦的，腻烦的

examples.en: After ten years in the job, she felt stale and needed a change.
examples.zh: 在那个岗位干了十年之后，她觉得腻了，需要换换工作。

examples.en: The cast is changed regularly to stop the actors from getting stale.
examples.zh: 演员阵容会定期更换，以防止演员变得陈旧。

senses.def: a disagreement
senses.zh: （辩论或竞赛中出现的）僵局，僵持局面

examples.en: The talks ended in (a) stalemate.
examples.zh: 谈判陷入僵局，无果而终。

examples.en: proposals aimed at breaking (= ending) the political stalemate
examples.zh: 旨在打破（=结束）政治僵局的提案

examples.en: The strike has once again reached stalemate.
examples.zh: 罢工再次陷入僵局。

senses.def: a situation in which a player cannot successfully move any of their pieces and the game ends without a winner

examples.en: The match ended in (a) stalemate
examples.zh: 比赛以平局告终

senses.def: the fact of not being fresh and tasting or smelling unpleasant
senses.zh: 过时：不新鲜，不品尝或闻起来不愉快

examples.en: Herb mixtures can help to eliminate mustiness and staleness.
examples.zh: 香草混合物有助于消除霉味和陈味。

senses.def: the fact that something has been said or done too many times before and is no longer interesting or exciting
senses.zh: 陈腐的；没有新意的；老掉牙的

examples.en: She needed something to break the staleness of her routine.
examples.zh: 她需要一些东西来打破陈腐的日常生活。

senses.def: the policies and beliefs of Stalin, especially that the Communist party should be the only party and that the central government should control the whole political and economic system

following or connected with the policies and beliefs of Stalin, especially that the Communist party should be the only party and that the central government should control the whole political and economic system

examples.en: a Stalinist regime
examples.zh: 斯大林主义政权

senses.def: a person who follows the policies and beliefs of Stalin, especially that the Communist party should be the only party and that the central government should control the whole political and economic system
a thin stem
senses.zh: （叶）柄；（花）梗；（果实的）柄；（植物的）茎，秆

examples.en: flowers on long stalks
examples.zh: 长茎上的花

examples.en: celery stalks
examples.zh: 芹菜茎

examples.en: He ate the apple, stalk and all.
examples.zh: 他把那个苹果吃了个干净，连梗都没剩下。

senses.def: a long, thin structure that supports something, especially an organ in some animals, and joins it on to another part

examples.en: Crabs have eyes on stalks.
examples.zh: 螃蟹的眼睛长在肉柄上。

senses.def: to move slowly and quietly towards an animal or a person, in order to kill, catch or harm it or them
senses.zh: 偷偷接近，潜近（猎物或人）

examples.en: The lion was stalking a zebra.
examples.zh: 狮子偷偷接近斑马。

examples.en: He stalked his victim as she walked home, before attacking and robbing her.
examples.zh: 她步行回家时，他偷偷地接近然后下手袭击，并且抢劫了她。

senses.def: to illegally follow and watch somebody over a long period of time, in a way that is annoying or frightening

examples.en: She claimed that he had been stalking her over a period of three years.
examples.zh: 她声称，三年来他一直在盯她的梢。

senses.def: to walk in an angry or proud way
senses.zh: 怒冲冲地走；趾高气扬地走

examples.en: He stalked off without a word.
examples.zh: 他一言未发，怒冲冲地走了。

examples.en: The actress stalked out of a press conference when asked if she had a weight problem.
examples.zh: 当被问及是否有体重问题时，这位女演员大步走出新闻发布会。

examples.en: Snatching up her bag, she stalked out of the room.
examples.zh: 她拎起包，大步走出了房间。

senses.def: to move through a place in an unpleasant or threatening
senses.zh: 令人厌恶地穿过；威胁地通过

examples.en: The gunmen stalked the building, looking for victims.
examples.zh: 这些持枪歹徒凶神恶煞般地打楼里走过，寻找袭击的目标。

examples.en: Fear stalks the streets of the city at night.
examples.zh: 夜间，这座城市的大街小巷笼罩着恐怖气氛。

senses.def: a person who follows and watches another person over a long period of time in a way that is annoying or frightening
a person who follows an animal quietly and slowly, especially in order to kill or capture it
a person or thing that is used to hide the real purpose of a particular course of action
senses.zh: 用以掩人耳目的人（或物）；用以掩蔽的事物

senses.def: a politician who competes against the leader of their party in order to see how much support the leader has; a stronger candidate can then compete against the leader more seriously
senses.zh: （为试探对手支持率而推出的）掩护性候选人

senses.def: a table or small shop with an open front that people sell things from, especially at a market
senses.zh: （尤指集市上的）货摊，摊位，售货亭

examples.en: He works on a market stall in the Square.
examples.zh: 他在广场上的一个集市售货亭工作。

examples.en: They have a fish stall on the market.
examples.zh: 他们在市场上有一个鱼摊。

examples.en: Drinks were being sold from makeshift stalls at the side of the road.
examples.zh: 路边的临时摊位正在出售饮料。

senses.def: a section inside a farm building that is large enough for one animal to be kept in

examples.en: We had to muck out stalls and groom the horses.
examples.zh: 我们必须得打扫马厩，刷洗马匹。

senses.def: a small area in a room, surrounded by glass, walls, etc., that contains a shower or toilet
senses.zh: （房间内的）小隔间，淋浴室，洗手间

examples.en: a bathroom stall
examples.zh: 洗手间的淋浴区

senses.def: the seats that are nearest to the stage in a theatre

examples.en: the front row of the stalls
examples.zh: 正厅第一排

senses.def: the seats at the front of a church where the choir
senses.zh: （教堂内）唱诗班和牧师的座位

senses.def: a situation in which a vehicle’s engine suddenly stops because it is not getting enough power
senses.zh: （车辆发动机的）熄火；（车辆的）抛锚

senses.def: a situation in which an aircraft loses speed and goes steeply downwards

examples.en: The plane went into a stall.
examples.zh: 这架飞机进入失速状态。

senses.def: to stop suddenly because of a lack of power or speed; to make a vehicle or an engine do this

examples.en: The car stalled and refused to start again.
examples.zh: 汽车熄火打不着了。

examples.en: I kept stalling.
examples.zh: 我一直在拖延。

examples.en: I stalled the car three times during my driving test.
examples.zh: 我考驾照时车子熄了三次火。

senses.def: to try to avoid doing something or answering a question so that you have more time

examples.en: They are still stalling on the deal.
examples.zh: 他们仍在拖时间，而不急于达成协议。

examples.en: ‘What do you mean?’ she asked, stalling for time.
examples.zh: “你这是什么意思？”她问，故意拖延着时间。

examples.en: The opposition party was angered by the Prime Minister’s stalling tactics.
examples.zh: 首相的拖延策略激怒了反对党。

examples.en: He asked them all kinds of pointless questions, stalling for time.
examples.zh: 他向他们提了各种毫无意义的问题来拖延时间。

senses.def: to make somebody wait so that you have more time to do something
senses.zh: 拖住（以赢得时间做某事）

examples.en: See if you can stall her while I finish searching her office.
examples.zh: 你看能不能拖住她，我好把她的办公室搜查完。

senses.def: to stop something from happening until a later date; to stop making progress

examples.en: There have been several attempts to revive the stalled peace plan.
examples.zh: 重新启动搁置的和平方案的尝试已有多次。

examples.en: Discussions have once again stalled.
examples.zh: 讨论再次停顿下来。

senses.def: a person who sells things from a stall
a fully grown male horse, especially one that is used for breeding
a loyal
senses.zh: （政党等组织的）忠诚拥护者，坚定分子

examples.en: a Labour/Tory stalwart
examples.zh: 工党/保守党的坚定支持者

examples.en: They have been stalwarts of the local amateur dramatic society for over 30 years.
examples.zh: 三十多年来，他们一直是当地业余戏剧协会的中坚力量。

senses.def: always showing support and able to be relied on, even in a difficult situation

examples.en: stalwart supporters
examples.zh: 忠实的拥护者

senses.def: physically strong
a small, thin male part in the middle of a flower that produces pollen
a village in north-east England. A famous battle took place there in 1066, when the forces of King Harold II
senses.zh: 斯坦福桥：英格兰东北部的一个村庄。1066年，哈罗德二世国王的军队在黑斯廷斯战役前三周击败了挪威国王哈拉尔德·哈德拉拉德的侵略军，在那里展开了一场著名的战斗。

senses.def: a well-known football stadium in Fulham
senses.zh: 斯坦福桥：位于伦敦西富勒姆的著名足球场。这是切尔西足球俱乐部的主场。

senses.def: (1781-1826) an English politician. He is best known for buying Singapore
senses.zh: 斯坦福·莱佛士（Stanford Raffles）：（1781-1826）一位英国政客。他以1819年为东印度公司收购新加坡以及将该岛发展为商业中心而闻名。那里著名的莱佛士酒店以他的名字命名。他还是Java（1815-17）和Sumatra（1818-23）的州长，并撰写了Java历史（1817）。1826年，莱佛士成为伦敦动物园的第一任总统。1817年，他被任命为骑士。

senses.def: the physical or mental strength that enables you to do something difficult for long periods of time

examples.en: It takes a lot of stamina to run a marathon.
examples.zh: 跑马拉松需要很大的耐力。

examples.en: exercises aimed at increasing stamina
examples.zh: 旨在增强耐力的练习

senses.def: to speak with difficulty, repeating sounds or words and often stopping, before saying things correctly

examples.en: Many children stammer but grow out of it.
examples.zh: 很多小孩口吃，但长大后就改过来了。

examples.en: ‘W-w-what?’ he stammered.
examples.zh: “什…什…什么？”他结巴着说。

examples.en: She was barely able to stammer out a description of her attacker.
examples.zh: 她只能勉强结结巴巴地说一说袭击她的人是什么模样。

senses.def: a problem that somebody has in speaking in which they repeat sounds or words or often stop, before saying things correctly

examples.en: She spoke with a stammer.
examples.zh: 她结结巴巴地说话。

examples.en: As a child, he had a dreadful stammer.
examples.zh: 小时候，他有严重的口吃。

senses.def: a person who stammers
senses.zh: 口吃者，说话结结巴巴的人

senses.def: a small piece of paper with a design on it that you buy and stick on an envelope

examples.en: a 67p stamp
examples.zh: 一枚 67 便士的邮票

examples.en: Could I have three first-class stamps, please?
examples.zh: 请给我拿三张第一类邮件的邮票。

examples.en: He has been collecting stamps since he was eight.
examples.zh: 他从八岁开始集邮。

examples.en: a stamp album
examples.zh: 集邮册

examples.en: The Post Office has issued a commemorative stamp to mark the event.
examples.zh: 邮局发行了纪念邮票以纪念这一事件。

senses.def: a tool for printing the date or a design or mark onto a surface

examples.en: a date stamp
examples.zh: 日期戳

senses.def: a design or words made by stamping something onto a surface

examples.en: The passports, with the visa stamps, were waiting at the embassy.
examples.zh: 那些护照都加盖了签证章，在大使馆等待领取。

examples.en: The project has the government's stamp of approval.
examples.zh: 工程已获得政府批准。

senses.def: a small piece of paper with a design on it, stuck on a document to show that a particular amount of money has been paid

examples.en: a TV licence stamp
examples.zh: 电视收视许可证印花

senses.group: proof of payment 付款证明

senses.def: the mark or sign of a particular quality or person

examples.en: All his work bears the stamp of authority.
examples.zh: 他的一切工作都具有权威性。

senses.def: a kind or class, especially of people

examples.en: men of a different stamp
examples.zh: 另一类人

senses.def: an act or sound of stamping

examples.en: The stamp of hoofs alerted Isabel.
examples.zh: 马蹄声引起了伊莎贝尔的警觉。

senses.def: to put your foot down heavily and noisily on the ground

examples.en: I tried stamping my feet to keep warm.
examples.zh: 我跺了一阵脚想暖和暖和。

examples.en: Sam stamped his foot in anger.
examples.zh: 萨姆气得直跺脚。

examples.en: He stamped the snow off his boots.
examples.zh: 他把靴子上的雪踩掉。

examples.en: The audience were stamping and cheering.
examples.zh: 观众又是跺脚，又是欢呼。

examples.en: She stamped her foot impatiently.
examples.zh: 她不耐烦地跺脚。

senses.def: to walk with loud heavy steps

examples.en: She turned and stamped out of the room.
examples.zh: 她扭身嗵嗵地走出了房间。

examples.en: The children came stamping down the stairs.
examples.zh: 孩子们跺着脚走下楼梯。

senses.def: to print letters, words, a design, etc. onto something using a special tool
senses.zh: 在…上盖（字样或图案等）；把（字样或图案等）盖在…上

examples.en: The box was stamped with the maker's name.
examples.zh: 盒子上盖有制作者的印章。

examples.en: Wait here to have your passport stamped.
examples.zh: 请在这里等候给护照盖章。

examples.en: I'll stamp the company name on your cheque.
examples.zh: 我来给你的支票盖上公司的章。

examples.en: The maker's name was stamped in gold on the box.
examples.zh: 盒子上盖有制作者的金字印章。

senses.def: to make a feeling show clearly on somebody’s face, in their actions, etc.

examples.en: Their faces were stamped with hostility.
examples.zh: 他们的神情充满敌意。

examples.en: The crime had revenge stamped all over it.
examples.zh: 从各方面看这次犯罪都是复仇行为。

examples.en: Terror was stamped across her face.
examples.zh: 她的脸上写满了恐惧。

senses.group: show feeling/quality 显露感情／性质

senses.def: to show that somebody has a particular quality

examples.en: Her success has stamped her as one of the country's top riders.
examples.zh: 她的成功表明她是全国最出色的骑手之一。

senses.group: show feeling/quality 显露感情／性质

senses.def: to stick a stamp on a letter or package
to cut and shape an object from a piece of metal or plastic using a special machine or tool

examples.en: The hinges are stamped out of sheets of metal.
examples.zh: 铰链由金属板冲压而成。

senses.def: the hobby of collecting stamps from different countries
a person who collects stamps from different countries as a hobby
a tax in the UK on some legal documents
to put your foot down with force on something

examples.en: The child stamped on the spider.
examples.zh: 小孩踩了那只蜘蛛一脚。

examples.en: She stamped on my toe!
examples.zh: 她踩到我的脚趾了！

senses.def: to stop something from happening or stop somebody from doing something, especially by using force or authority

examples.en: All attempts at modernization were stamped on by senior officials.
examples.zh: 旨在实现现代化的努力统统受到高级官员的压制。

senses.def: to make something have an important effect or influence on something
senses.zh: 在…上打上…印记；把…铭刻在…中

examples.en: She stamped her own interpretation on the role.
examples.zh: 她给那个角色注入了自己的诠释。

examples.en: His personality was indelibly stamped on the final product.
examples.zh: 他的个性在最终产品上留下了不可磨灭的印记。

senses.def: to get rid of something that is bad, unpleasant or dangerous, especially by using force or a lot of effort
senses.zh: （尤指通过武力或不懈努力）消除，消灭，镇压

examples.en: to stamp out racism
examples.zh: 消灭种族主义

senses.def: to put out a fire by bringing your foot down heavily on it

examples.en: He stamped out the flames before they spread any further.
examples.zh: 他踩灭火焰，以免蔓延。

senses.def: an envelope
senses.zh: （写上姓名地址且贴有邮票的）回邮信封

examples.en: Please enclose a stamped addressed envelope to get your test results.
examples.zh: 请附姓名地址邮资俱全的信封，以便把化验结果寄给你。

senses.def: a situation in which a group of people or large animals such as horses suddenly start running in the same direction, especially because they are frightened or excited
senses.zh: （人群的）奔逃，蜂拥；（兽群的）惊跑，狂奔

examples.en: A stampede broke out when the doors opened.
examples.zh: 门一开，人们蜂拥而出。

senses.def: a situation in which a lot of people are trying to do or achieve the same thing at the same time

examples.en: Falling interest rates has led to a stampede to buy property.
examples.zh: 不断下降的利率引发了一场购房热。

senses.def: to run in a stampede

examples.en: a herd of stampeding elephants
examples.zh: 一群狂奔的大象

examples.en: A huge bunch of kids came stampeding down the corridor.
examples.zh: 一大群孩子顺着走廊涌了过来。

examples.en: The cattle started to stampede, as if they could sense the danger.
examples.zh: 牛群仿佛感觉到危险，开始狂奔起来。

senses.def: to make somebody rush into doing something without giving them time to think about it

examples.en: I refuse to be stampeded into making any hasty decisions.
examples.zh: 我不愿仓促行事，草率作决定。

senses.def: a place that somebody likes and where they often go

examples.en: This bar used to be one of my brother’s old stamping grounds.
examples.zh: 这个酒吧曾经是我哥哥以前常去的地方之一。

senses.def: a very enthusiastic fan of somebody/something

examples.en: She got caught up in a social media spat with stans of the actor.
examples.zh: 她在社交媒体上与这位演员的粉丝发生了口角。

senses.def: to be a very enthusiastic fan of somebody/something
senses.zh: 成为某人/某事的狂热粉丝

examples.en: She's a total legend and she keeps on giving us more reasons to stan her forever.
examples.zh: 她是一个彻头彻尾的传奇人物，她不断给我们更多的理由来永远支持她。

examples.en: How many people can say they stan for an inventor?
examples.zh: 有多少人可以说自己是发明家？

examples.en: I thought I couldn't stan harder, but then he came up with that brilliant put-down.
examples.zh: 我以为我不能再坚持得更卖力了，但后来他却说出了那句绝妙的贬低的话。

senses.def: a first name for boys, short for Stanley
(1927-91) a US jazz musician who played the saxophone
senses.zh: 斯坦·盖兹（Stan Getz）：（1927-91）是一位美国爵士音乐家，曾演奏萨克斯风。他曾是“西海岸酷派”爵士乐的领导者，他的成功包括《初秋》（1948年），《伊帕内玛的女孩》（1963年）和《我记得你》（1991年）。盖茨（Getz）与本尼·古德曼（Benny Goodman），伍迪·赫曼（Woody Herman）和其他著名乐队合作。他获得了三项艾美奖（1962、1964和1991），并于1986年入选爵士名人堂。

senses.def: the opinions that somebody has about something and expresses publicly

examples.en: What is the newspaper's stance on the war?
examples.zh: 那家报纸对这场战争持什么立场？

examples.en: He is known for his anti-abortion stance.
examples.zh: 他以反对堕胎的立场而闻名。

examples.en: Judges are increasingly taking a tougher stance on rape.
examples.zh: 法官对强奸案的态度越来越强硬。

senses.def: the way in which somebody stands, especially when playing a sport
senses.zh: （尤指体育运动中的）站立姿势

examples.en: Widen your stance (= move your feet wider apart) for greater stability when hitting the ball.
examples.zh: 击球时两腿分开一些，这样站得更稳。

senses.def: to stop the flow of something, especially blood
a long thin vertical
to be on your feet; to be in a vertical

examples.en: She was too weak to stand.
examples.zh: 她虚弱得站都站不住。

examples.en: a bird standing on one leg
examples.zh: 单腿独立的鸟

examples.en: Don't just stand there—do something!
examples.zh: 别光站着，干点什么！

examples.en: I was standing only a few feet away.
examples.zh: 当时我就站在几英尺远的地方。

examples.en: We all stood around in the corridor waiting.
examples.zh: 我们分散站在过道里等着。

examples.en: to stand on your head/hands (= to be upside down, balancing on your head/hands)
examples.zh: 用头／用手倒立

examples.en: Stand still while I take your photo.
examples.zh: 我给你照相，站着别动。

examples.en: We stood talking for a few minutes.
examples.zh: 我们站着聊了几分钟。

examples.en: People stood waiting for a bus in the rain.
examples.zh: 人们在雨中站着等公共汽车。

examples.en: After the earthquake, only a few houses were left standing.
examples.zh: 地震后只剩几座房子没倒。

senses.group: on feet/be vertical 站立；直立

senses.def: to get up onto your feet from another position

examples.en: Everyone stood when the president came in.
examples.zh: 总统进来时大家都起立。

examples.en: We stood up in order to get a better view.
examples.zh: 我们站起身来以便看得更清楚。

examples.en: I tried to stand up and found myself in agony.
examples.zh: 我试图站起身来，却发现疼痛难忍。

senses.group: on feet/be vertical 站立；直立

senses.def: to put something/somebody in a vertical

examples.en: Stand the ladder up against the wall.
examples.zh: 把梯子靠墙立好。

examples.en: I stood the little girl on a chair so that she could see.
examples.zh: 我让小女孩站到椅子上，好让她看得见。

senses.def: used especially in negative sentences and questions to emphasize that you do not like somebody/something
senses.zh: （尤用于否定句和疑问句，强调不喜欢）容忍，忍受

examples.en: I can't stand his brother.
examples.zh: 他弟弟让我受不了。

examples.en: I can't stand the sight of blood.
examples.zh: 一看见血我就难受。

examples.en: I can't stand it when you do that.
examples.zh: 你那么做，我受不了。

examples.en: She couldn't stand being kept waiting.
examples.zh: 叫她等着，她会受不了。

examples.en: She couldn't stand to be kept waiting.
examples.zh: 她无法忍受继续等待。

examples.en: I can't stand people interrupting all the time.
examples.zh: 我不能容忍老有人打岔。

examples.en: How do you stand him being here all the time?
examples.zh: 他老在这儿，你怎么受得了呢？

senses.def: used especially with can/could
senses.zh: （尤与 can／could 或 will 连用）经受，承受，经得起

examples.en: His heart won't stand the strain much longer.
examples.zh: 他的心脏对这种压力承受不了多久。

examples.en: Modern plastics can stand very high and very low temperatures.
examples.zh: 新型塑料能承受很高和很低的温度。

examples.en: It can stand being dropped from a great height without breaking.
examples.zh: 它可以承受从高处掉落而不会破裂。

examples.en: Can you stand me touching your hand or is it too sore?
examples.zh: 你能忍受我碰你的手吗？或者你的手太痛了吗？

examples.en: I can't stand to see him suffer any more.
examples.zh: 我无法忍受看到他再受苦。

senses.def: to be in a particular place
senses.zh: 位于（某处）；坐落在；被放在

examples.en: The castle stands on the site of an ancient battlefield.
examples.zh: 那座城堡坐落在一片古战场上。

examples.en: An old oak tree once stood here.
examples.zh: 以前这儿长着一棵老橡树。

examples.en: Books stood in piles in the corner.
examples.zh: 墙角竖放着一摞摞的书。

senses.group: be in place/condition 位置；状态

senses.def: to be in a particular condition or situation

examples.en: The house stood empty for a long time.
examples.zh: 那所房子空了好长一段时间。

examples.en: 'You're wrong about the date—it was 2008.’ ‘I stand corrected (= accept that I was wrong).'
examples.zh: “你把日期搞错了，是 1988 年。” “你说得对，是我搞错了。”

examples.en: You stand accused of a terrible crime.
examples.zh: 你被指控犯有可怕的罪行。

examples.en: You never know where you stand with her—one minute she's friendly, the next she'll hardly speak to you.
examples.zh: 你从来拿不准你和她的关系如何，她一会儿跟你亲热，一会儿连话也不大跟你说。

examples.en: As things stand, there is little chance of a quick settlement of the dispute.
examples.zh: 照目前的形势，尽快解决争端的可能微乎其微。

senses.group: be in place/condition 位置；状态

senses.def: to be a candidate in an election

examples.en: He stood for election in Colchester.
examples.zh: 他在科尔切斯特参加了竞选。

examples.en: He stood for parliament (= tried to get elected as an MP).
examples.zh: 他竞选过议会议员。

examples.en: She stood unsuccessfully as a candidate in the local elections.
examples.zh: 她参加过地方选举，但未能当选。

examples.en: Her friends persuaded her to stand.
examples.zh: 她的朋友们劝她站起来。

senses.def: to be a particular height

examples.en: The tower stands 30 metres high.
examples.zh: 塔高 30 米。

senses.group: be at height/level 高度；水平

senses.def: to be at a particular level, amount, height, etc.
senses.zh: 达特定水平（或数量、高度等）

examples.en: Interest rates stand at 3 per cent.
examples.zh: 利率为 3%。

examples.en: The world record then stood at 6.59 metres.
examples.zh: 当时的世界纪录是 6.59 米。

senses.group: be at height/level 高度；水平

senses.def: to be in a particular place, especially while waiting to go somewhere

examples.en: The train standing at platform 3 is for London, Victoria.
examples.zh: 停在第 3 站台的火车开往伦敦维多利亚站。

senses.group: of car/train, etc. 汽车、火车等

senses.def: to remain still, without moving or being moved

examples.en: Mix the batter and let it stand for twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 搅好面糊后，放上二十分钟。

examples.en: standing pools of rainwater
examples.zh: 雨水洼

senses.def: if an offer, a decision, etc. made earlier stands

examples.en: My offer still stands.
examples.zh: 我的出价仍然算数。

examples.en: The world record stood for 20 years.
examples.zh: 那项世界纪录 20 年未被打破。

senses.def: to be in a situation where you are likely to do something

examples.en: You stand to make a lot from this deal.
examples.zh: 你很可能会从这笔生意中大赚一笔。

examples.en: Who stands to benefit the most?
examples.zh: 谁将受益最大？

examples.en: to stand to gain/lose something
examples.zh: 忍受获得/失去某些东西

senses.group: be likely to do something 很可能

senses.def: to have a particular attitude or opinion about something or towards somebody
senses.zh: （对某事）持某种态度，有某一观点，采取某种立场

examples.en: Where do you stand on private education?
examples.zh: 你对私立教育持什么观点？

senses.def: to buy a drink or meal for somebody
senses.zh: 花钱请（某人喝饮料或吃饭）；买…请客

examples.en: He stood drinks all round.
examples.zh: 他请客，让大家喝了饮料。

examples.en: She was kind enough to stand us a meal.
examples.zh: 她真好，请我们吃了饭。

senses.def: an attitude towards something or an opinion that you make clear to people

examples.en: He has avoided taking a firm stand.
examples.zh: 他故意不表明立场。

examples.en: The judge takes a tough stand on corruption.
examples.zh: 法官对腐败采取强硬立场。

examples.en: I admire their principled stand against the war.
examples.zh: 我欣赏他们有原则的反战立场。

senses.def: a strong effort to defend yourself or your opinion about something

examples.en: They are willing to take a stand and defend what they believe in.
examples.zh: 他们愿意进行抵抗，捍卫自己的信仰。

examples.en: We must make a stand against job losses.
examples.zh: 我们必须采取措施，防止失业。

examples.en: the rebels’ desperate last stand
examples.zh: 反叛者最后的疯狂抵抗

senses.def: a table or structure that goods are sold from, especially in the street or at a market

examples.en: a lemonade/hot dog/newspaper stand
examples.zh: 柠檬味汽水／热狗售卖亭；报摊

examples.en: She sells fruit from a roadside stand.
examples.zh: 她在路边摊上卖水果。

examples.en: The magazine sold out as soon as it hit the stands (= went on sale).
examples.zh: 该杂志一上架就卖光了。

senses.group: for showing/holding something 展示；摆放

senses.def: a table or a vertical
senses.zh: （展示或推介物品的）桌，台，摊位

examples.en: a display/an exhibition stand
examples.zh: 展位

examples.en: Oxford University Press’s stand at the book fair
examples.zh: 牛津大学出版社在书展上的展位

senses.group: for showing/holding something 展示；摆放

senses.def: a piece of equipment or furniture that you use for holding a particular type of thing

examples.en: a bicycle/microphone/cake stand
examples.zh: 自行车停靠架；麦克风架；蛋糕座

senses.group: for showing/holding something 展示；摆放

senses.def: a large sloping structure at a stadium with rows where people sit or stand to watch the game

examples.en: We had seats in the east stand.
examples.zh: 我们在东看台有座位。

senses.def: the place in court where people stand to give evidence

examples.en: He took the stand as the first witness.
examples.zh: 他第一个出庭做证。

senses.def: the period of time in which two people who are batting
senses.zh: 两个击球员同时在场上并跑动得分的阶段；双人配对

examples.en: Clinch and Harris shared an opening stand of 69.
examples.zh: 克林奇和哈里斯两位击球员，比赛一开始时搭档，共得 69 分。

senses.def: a place where taxis, buses, etc. park while they are waiting for passengers
senses.group: for taxis/buses, etc. 出租车、公共汽车等

senses.def: a group of plants or trees of one kind

examples.en: a stand of pines
examples.zh: 松树丛

senses.def: a piece of land that you can buy and use for building a house, etc. on

examples.en: A developer bought the land and divided it into stands.
examples.zh: 开发商买下这块土地将其分为多块建筑用地。

note.en: Idioms containing stand are at the entries for the nouns and adjectives in the idioms, for example stand on ceremony is at ceremony.
note.zh: 含 stand 的习语，都可在该等习语中的名词及形容词相关词条找到，如 stand on ceremony 在词条 ceremony 下。

synonyms.words: get up ▪ stand up ▪ rise ▪ get to your feet ▪ be on your feet

intro.en: These words all mean to be in a vertical position with your weight on your feet, or to put yourself in this position.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含站立、直立、站起来之义。

items.def: to be in a vertical position with your weight on your feet:
items.zh: 指站立、直立

examples.en: She was too weak to stand.
examples.zh: 她虚弱得站都站不住。

items.def: to get into a standing position from a sitting, kneeling or lying position:
items.zh: 指从坐、跪或躺的姿势站起来

examples.en: Please don’t get up!
examples.zh: 请不要站起来！

items.def: to be in a standing position; to stand after sitting:
items.zh: 指站立、起立

examples.en: Stand up straight!
examples.zh: 立正！

items.def: (formal) to get into a standing position from a sitting, kneeling or lying position:
items.zh: 指从坐、跪或躺的姿势站起来

examples.en: Would you all rise, please, to welcome our visiting speaker.
examples.zh: 请大家起立，欢迎我们的演讲嘉宾。

items.def: to stand up after sitting, kneeling or lying:
items.zh: 指坐、跪或躺后站起来

examples.en: I helped her to get to her feet.
examples.zh: 我扶着她让她站起来。

items.def: to be standing up:
items.zh: 指站着

examples.en: I’ve been on my feet all day.
examples.zh: 我已经站了一整天。

synonyms.words: dislike ▪ can’t stand ▪ despise ▪ can’t bear ▪ loathe ▪ detest

intro.en: These words all mean to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含厌恶、讨厌、憎恶之义。

items.def: to have a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/​something. Although hate is generally a very strong verb, it is also commonly used in spoken or informal English to talk about people or things that you dislike in a less important way, for example a particular type of food:
items.zh: 尽管 hate 通常为语气很强的动词，但亦常用于口语或非正式英语中，谈论不太喜欢的人或物，如某种食物等

items.def: (rather formal) to not like somebody/​something. Dislike is a rather formal word; it is less formal, and more usual, to say that you don't like somebody/​something, especially in spoken English:
items.zh: dislike 为相当正式的用语，don’t like 则较非正式，而且较常用，尤其在英语口语中

items.def: (rather informal) used to emphasize that you really do not like somebody/​something:
items.zh: 强调不喜欢、受不了、不能容忍

examples.en: I can’t stand his brother.
examples.zh: 他弟弟让我受不了。

items.def: to dislike and have no respect for somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指鄙视、蔑视、看不起

examples.en: He despised himself for being so cowardly.
examples.zh: 他为自己如此怯懦而看不起自己。

items.def: used to say that you dislike something so much that you cannot accept or deal with it:
items.zh: 指无法承受、应付不了

examples.en: I can’t bear having cats in the house.
examples.zh: 家里有猫我可受不了。

items.def: to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They loathe each other.
examples.zh: 他们相互讨厌。

items.def: (rather formal) to hate somebody/​something very much:
items.zh: 指厌恶、憎恨、讨厌

examples.en: They absolutely detest each other.
examples.zh: 他们完全是相互憎恨。

senses.def: to have the possibility of succeeding or achieving something
senses.zh: 有可能成功；有机会获得

examples.en: The driver didn't stand a chance of stopping in time.
examples.zh: 司机根本不可能及时刹车。

examples.en: He doesn't stand a chance of winning against such an experienced player.
examples.zh: 他不可能打败这样一位经验丰富的选手。

senses.def: to be independent or not connected with other people, organizations or ideas

examples.en: These islands are too small to stand alone as independent states.
examples.zh: 这些岛屿太小，不能成为独立的国家。

examples.en: The problems that research is designed to solve do not stand alone, but are part of a wider context.
examples.zh: 研究旨在解决的问题并不是孤立的，而是更广泛背景的一部分。

senses.def: to be not near other objects or buildings

examples.en: The arch once stood alone at the entrance to the castle.
examples.zh: 拱门曾经孤零零地矗立在城堡的入口处。

senses.def: used as a command to soldiers who are already standing at ease
senses.zh: （对士兵的命令用语）原地休息

senses.def: to refuse to move back; to refuse to change your opinions
senses.zh: 坚定不移；不让步；坚持自己的观点

senses.def: to behave formally

examples.en: Please don't stand on ceremony (= Please be natural and relaxed) with me.
examples.zh: 请别跟我讲客套。

examples.en: I won't stand on ceremony.
examples.zh: 我不会讲客套。

senses.def: to demand to be treated with the respect that you think that you deserve
senses.zh: 要求受到应有的礼遇；保持尊严

examples.en: Our teacher never stands on her dignity with us, but treats us all as friends and colleagues.
examples.zh: 我们的老师从不以自己的尊严对待我们，而是把我们所有人当作朋友和同事。

examples.en: She was never one to stand on her dignity.
examples.zh: 她从来就不是个端架子的人。

senses.def: to be independent and able to take care of yourself

examples.en: When his parents died he had to learn to stand on his own two feet.
examples.zh: 他的父母去世后他不得不学会自立。

senses.def: to refuse to change your mind about a decision you have made or an opinion you have
senses.zh: 固执己见；拒不改变决定

senses.def: to be useful or helpful to somebody when needed
senses.zh: （需要时）对某人有用，对某人有利

examples.en: Your languages will stand you in good stead when it comes to finding a job.
examples.zh: 你懂得几种语言，找工作时就会显出优势。

senses.def: to show that you are proud and able to deal with anything

examples.en: Suddenly he seemed to stand taller.
examples.zh: 忽然间他显得更高了。

senses.def: to prove to be good, popular, etc. over a long period of time

examples.en: Whether this new technology will stand the test of time remains to be seen.
examples.zh: 这种新技术能否经得起时间的考验仍需拭目以待。

senses.def: to say publicly that you support somebody or you agree with something

examples.en: Everyone needs to stand up and be counted in order to make them see the strength of our conviction.
examples.zh: 每个人都需要站出来，让他们看到我们信念的力量。

senses.def: able to be operated on its own without being connected to a larger system
to be obviously different from somebody/something
senses.zh: 与…明显不同；显然有别于

examples.en: The brand’s originality makes it stand apart from other brands.
examples.zh: 该品牌的独特创意使其与其他品牌截然不同。

senses.def: to move to one side

examples.en: She stood aside to let us pass.
examples.zh: 她站到一边让我们过。

senses.def: to not get involved in something
senses.zh: 不参与；不介入；置身事外

examples.en: Don't stand aside and let others do all the work.
examples.zh: 不要袖手旁观，工作都让别人去做。

senses.def: to stop doing a job so somebody else can do it
senses.zh: 退居一旁；让位于他人；靠边

senses.def: to move back from a place

examples.en: The police ordered the crowd to stand back.
examples.zh: 警察命令人群往后退。

senses.def: to be located away from something
senses.zh: 位于离…有一段距离的地方

examples.en: The house stands back from the road.
examples.zh: 房子离公路有一段距离。

senses.def: to think about a situation as if you are not involved in it

examples.en: It's time to stand back and look at your career so far.
examples.zh: 现在你该从旁观者的角度来审视一下自己迄今的职业生涯了。

senses.def: to prevent somebody from getting or achieving something

examples.en: Only one game stood between him and victory.
examples.zh: 只要再赢一场比赛他就能胜出。

senses.def: to be present while something bad is happening but not do anything to stop it

examples.en: How can you stand by and see him accused of something he didn't do?
examples.zh: 你怎么能眼睁睁看着他遭人诬陷呢？

examples.en: Surely the world cannot stand idly by and let this country go through the agony of war yet again?
examples.zh: 国际社会当然不能袖手旁观，让这个国家再度经历战争的伤痛吧？

senses.def: to be ready for action

examples.en: The troops are standing by.
examples.zh: 部队随时待命出动。

senses.def: to help somebody or be friends with them, even in difficult situations

examples.zh: 她的著名歌曲《忠于你的男人》

senses.def: to still believe or agree with something you said, decided or agreed earlier
senses.zh: 仍然遵守诺言（或协议等）

examples.zh: 她依旧恪守她说过的每一句话。

senses.def: to leave a job or position

examples.zh: 他退下来好为年轻人让路。

examples.zh: 小队被命令退下。

senses.def: a period when people, especially soldiers, relax after a period of duty or danger
senses.zh: 停工休息期；（尤指士兵的）休整期

senses.def: to be an abbreviation or symbol of something

examples.en: ‘The book's by T.C. Smith.’ ‘What does the ‘T.C.’ stand for?’
examples.zh: “这部书是 T.C. 史密斯写的。”“T.C. 是什么的缩写？”

senses.def: to support or represent something

examples.en: I hated the organization and all it stood for (= the ideas that it supported).
examples.zh: 我厌恶那个组织，也厌恶它的一切主张。

senses.def: to not let somebody do something or something happen

examples.en: I'm not standing for it any longer.
examples.zh: 这种事我再也不能容忍了。

senses.def: to take somebody’s place

examples.en: My assistant will stand in for me while I'm away.
examples.zh: 我不在期间，由我的助手代替我。

senses.def: a person who does somebody’s job for a short time when they are not available

examples.en: I acted as Tom’s stand-in when he was away.
examples.zh: 汤姆不在时我替他顶班。

examples.en: the stand-in captain
examples.zh: 替补队长

senses.def: a person who replaces an actor in some scenes in a film, especially dangerous ones
senses.zh: （尤指影视中做危险动作的）替身演员

examples.en: Most of the stunts are performed by stand-ins.
examples.zh: 大部分特技由替身演员完成。

senses.def: a situation in which no agreement can be reached

examples.en: a stand-off between the union and the management
examples.zh: 工会与管理层之间的对峙

senses.def: a player who plays behind the scrum half
not friendly towards other people
senses.zh: 冷淡的；冷漠的；不友好的

senses.def: to be much better or more important than somebody/something

examples.en: Four points stand out as being more important than the rest.
examples.zh: 有四点比其余各点更为重要。

senses.def: to be easily seen or noticed

examples.en: The lettering stood out well against the dark background.
examples.zh: 那种字体的文字在深色背景下十分醒目。

examples.en: She's the sort of person who stands out in a crowd.
examples.zh: 她是那种在人群中很显眼的人。

senses.def: be near somebody and watch them

examples.en: I don't like you standing over me while I'm cooking.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢做饭时你在一旁盯着我。

senses.def: the state of being ready to fight or attack
stand-up

examples.en: When did you start doing stand-up?
examples.zh: 你什么时候开始表演脱口秀的？

senses.def: a person who performs stand-up
senses.zh: 独角喜剧演员；脱口秀演员

examples.en: She started out as a stand-up.
examples.zh: 她出道时是个脱口秀演员。

senses.def: to get up onto your feet

examples.en: The children stood up when the teacher walked into the room.
examples.zh: 老师走进教室时孩子们起立。

senses.def: to be on your feet

examples.en: There were no seats left so I had to stand up.
examples.zh: 没有座位了，所以我只好站着。

examples.en: You'll look taller if you stand up straight.
examples.zh: 站直身子，你会显得高些。

senses.def: to deliberately not meet somebody you have arranged to meet, especially somebody you are having a romantic relationship with
senses.zh: （尤指恋人）故意失约使某人空等，放某人鸽子

examples.en: I've been stood up!
examples.zh: 人家让我空等一场！

senses.def: to remain true, relevant or acceptable even when tested, examined closely, etc.

examples.en: His argument simply doesn't stand up to close scrutiny.
examples.zh: 他的论点完全经不起仔细推敲。

examples.en: I'm afraid this document will never stand up in a court of law.
examples.zh: 恐怕这份文件在法庭上是根本站不住脚的。

senses.def: stand-up

examples.en: a stand-up act
examples.zh: 单人说笑表演

examples.en: a stand-up comedian
examples.zh: 单口喜剧演员

senses.def: a stand-up
worn, used, etc. in a vertical

examples.en: a stand-up collar
examples.zh: 立领

examples.en: The stand-up edging prevents soil from falling on the path.
examples.zh: 直立式边缘可防止土壤掉落在道路上。

senses.def: held, used, etc. while standing up

examples.en: a stand-up meeting
examples.zh: 站会

examples.en: Working at a stand-up desk instead of sitting down all day really helped my back problems.
examples.zh: 在站立式办公桌上工作而不是整天坐着，确实对我的背部问题有帮助。

senses.def: to support or defend somebody/something

examples.en: Always stand up for your friends.
examples.zh: 任何时候都要支持自己的朋友。

examples.en: You must stand up for your rights.
examples.zh: 你必须维护自己的权利。

examples.en: She had learnt to stand up for herself.
examples.zh: 她学会了自我保护。

senses.def: to resist somebody; to not accept bad treatment from somebody without complaining
senses.zh: 抵抗；勇敢反对；不甘忍受某人的欺负（或不公平对待）

examples.en: It was brave of her to stand up to those bullies.
examples.zh: 她不向那几个坏蛋屈服，真是勇敢。

senses.def: to remain in good condition despite rough treatment

examples.en: The carpet is designed to stand up to a lot of wear and tear.
examples.zh: 这种地毯设计得十分耐用。

senses.def: to be very obvious or easy to notice

examples.en: It stood out a mile that she was lying.
examples.zh: 很明显她在撒谎。

senses.def: to be very easy to notice in an unpleasant way

examples.en: The blue building stood out like a sore thumb among the whitewashed villas.
examples.zh: 蓝色的建筑在粉刷成白色的别墅中显得格外显眼。

examples.en: If you wear a suit to the party, you’ll stand out like a sore thumb.
examples.zh: 如果你穿西装去参加聚会，你会很引人注目。

stand/stick out like a sore thumb.word: stand/stick out like a sore thumb

senses.def: to make people think about something in a completely different way
senses.zh: 使人完全改变思路；使人从反面思考

senses.def: a level of quality, especially one that people think is acceptable

examples.en: There has been a fall in living standards.
examples.zh: 生活水平有所下降。

examples.en: safety/quality standards
examples.zh: 安全/质量标准

examples.en: Who sets the standard for water quality?
examples.zh: 水质标准由谁来制定？

examples.en: A number of Britain's beaches fail to meet European standards on cleanliness.
examples.zh: 英国有几处海滩不符合欧洲的清洁标准。

examples.en: to improve/raise standards
examples.zh: 提升标准

examples.en: He failed to reach the minimum standard and did not qualify.
examples.zh: 他未能达到最低标准，因而不具备资格。

examples.en: We aim to maintain high standards of customer care.
examples.zh: 我们的宗旨是始终以高标准为顾客服务。

examples.en: The standard of this year's applications is very low.
examples.zh: 今年的申请标准很低。

examples.en: The quality of the image was below the standard I had hoped for.
examples.zh: 图像质量低于我希望的标准。

examples.en: The work was done to a professional standard.
examples.zh: 这项工作是按照专业标准完成的。

examples.en: Her work is not up to standard (= of a good enough standard).
examples.zh: 她的工作不合格。

senses.group: level of quality 品质标准

senses.def: a level of quality that is normal or acceptable for a particular person or in a particular situation
senses.zh: 正常的水平；应达到的标准

examples.en: You'd better lower your standards if you want to find somewhere cheap to live.
examples.zh: 要想找个便宜的地方住，你最好降低要求。

examples.en: It was a simple meal by Eddie's standards.
examples.zh: 在埃迪看来，那不过是一顿便饭。

examples.en: The equipment is slow and heavy by modern standards.
examples.zh: 按现代标准，那台设备又慢又笨重。

examples.en: His latest film is well below his usual standards.
examples.zh: 他的最新电影远远低于他通常的标准。

senses.group: level of quality 品质标准

senses.def: a level of behaviour that somebody considers to be morally acceptable

examples.en: a man of high moral standards
examples.zh: 道德水准高的人

examples.en: Some people have no standards.
examples.zh: 有些人没有道德水准。

examples.en: The government must uphold basic standards of decency.
examples.zh: 政府必须维护基本的礼仪标准。

examples.en: My grandparents are always complaining about falling standards.
examples.zh: 我的祖父母总是抱怨标准下降。

examples.en: the advertising standards watchdog
examples.zh: 广告标准监管机构

senses.group: level of behaviour 行为标准

senses.def: a unit of measurement that is officially used; an official rule used when producing something
senses.zh: 法定度量衡标准；法定含量；技术规范；产品规格

examples.en: a reduction in the weight standard of silver coins
examples.zh: 银币法定重量标准的降低

examples.en: industry standards
examples.zh: 工业标准

senses.group: unit of measurement 度量衡标准

senses.def: a flag that is used during official ceremonies, especially one connected with a particular military group
senses.zh: 仪式上使用的旗帜；（尤指）军旗

examples.en: the royal standard
examples.zh: 王旗。

senses.def: a song that has been recorded by many different singers
senses.zh: （很多歌手录制过的）经典曲目

senses.def: average or normal rather than having special or unusual features
senses.zh: 普通的；正常的；通常的；标准的

examples.en: the standard rate of tax (= paid by everyone)
examples.zh: 标准税率

examples.en: It is standard practice to search visitors as they enter the building.
examples.zh: 对进入这栋建筑物的来访者进行搜查是例行做法。

examples.en: DNA was extracted by a standard procedure.
examples.zh: 通过标准程序提取DNA。

examples.en: Touch screens are now a standard feature on most devices.
examples.zh: 触摸屏现在是多数设备的标准配置。

examples.en: A standard letter was sent to all candidates.
examples.zh: 给所有求职者均寄去了一封标准函。

examples.en: The format of the show is fairly standard.
examples.zh: 节目编排中规中矩。

examples.en: Front airbags come as standard on all models.
examples.zh: 所有款式都标配前排安全气囊。

senses.def: following a particular standard set, for example, by an industry
senses.zh: （符合）标准的；按一定规格制作的

examples.en: standard sizes of clothes
examples.zh: 服装的标准尺寸

examples.en: Washing machines have standard measurements to fit under kitchen units.
examples.zh: 洗衣机具有标准尺寸，可安装在厨房设备下方。

examples.en: The stations were built to a simple, almost standard design.
examples.zh: 车站都是按照同一个简单的近于标准化的设计建成的。

examples.en: Our charges are standard throughout the country.
examples.zh: 我们的收费标准全国统一。

senses.def: read by most people who are studying a particular subject

examples.en: the author of the standard textbook on the topic
examples.zh: 该主题标准教科书的作者

senses.def: believed to be correct and used by most people

examples.en: Standard English
examples.zh: 规范的英语

senses.def: a leader in a political group or campaign
a way of travelling on a train or ship that costs less and is less comfortable than first class
connected with the less expensive way of travelling on a train, ship, etc.

examples.en: standard-class carriages/passengers
examples.zh: 二等座车厢／乘客

senses.def: a fixed amount of money that you can earn free of tax
senses.zh: 工资免税标准；工资免税额

senses.def: the amount by which measurements in a set vary from the average for the set
a method of measuring how accurate an estimate is
senses.zh: 标准误差（用于衡量估计的准确性）

senses.def: (in Scotland) an exam that was taken in a particular subject at a lower level than Highers
senses.zh: 标准级别考试（学生通常在 16 岁时参加，2014 年为国家资格认证体系所取代）

senses.def: the basic equipment that is given to all the members of a particular group, especially in the army, navy
senses.zh: （尤指陆军、海军等的）基本配置，标准配置

examples.en: CS gas has been standard issue in the police force for some time.
examples.zh: 催泪瓦斯成为警察的标配已有一段时间了。

examples.en: Tans and perfect teeth are standard issue in this movie.
examples.zh: 晒黑的皮肤和完美的牙齿是这部电影的标准配置。

senses.def: provided as part of the basic equipment that is given to all the members of a particular group, especially in the army, navy
senses.zh: （尤指陆军、海军等的装备）基本配置的，标准配置的

examples.en: They were protected by standard-issue body armour.
examples.zh: 他们有标配防弹服护身。

examples.en: It's a standard-issue action movie.
examples.zh: 那是部标准的动作片。

senses.def: a tall lamp that stands on the floor
the amount of money and level of comfort that a particular person or group has

examples.en: Their standard of living is very low.
examples.zh: 他们的生活水平很低。

examples.en: As a result of the redundancies, most families suffered a fall in their standard of living.
examples.zh: 由于裁员，大多数家庭的生活水平下降。

examples.en: the fall in their standard of living caused by redundancy
examples.zh: 裁员导致生活水平下降

examples.en: a decent standard of living
examples.zh: 体面的生活水平

senses.def: a large US oil company established in 1870 by John D Rockefeller
senses.zh: 标准油：约翰·洛克菲勒（John D Rockefeller）于1870年成立的美国大型石油公司。1911年，美国最高法院裁定限制贸易，并将其分为34家独立公司。其中一些公司后来成为埃克森美孚和Amoco。

senses.def: a set of instructions on how to perform a routine business activity

examples.en: The authority urged the business community to follow standard operating procedures strictly in order to ensure safe working conditions.
examples.zh: 当局敦促商界严格遵守标准操作程序，以确保安全的工作条件。

examples.en: This was a serious breach of standard operating procedure.
examples.zh: 这是严重违反标准操作程序的行为。

senses.zh: 标准普尔（Standard＆Poor's）：一家国际公司于1941年以目前的形式成立，但历史可以追溯到1860年。它位于纽约，在许多其他国家设有办事处。它发布有关公司的信息并给予他们信用评级（即是否能够偿还借入的钱以及将钱借给他们的安全性的判断）。

senses.def: the official time of a country or an area
the process of making objects or activities of the same type have the same features or qualities; the process of making something standard

examples.en: the standardization of components
examples.zh: 组件标准化

senses.def: to make objects or activities of the same type have the same features or qualities; to make something standard
senses.zh: 使标准化；使符合标准（或规格）

examples.en: a standardized contract/design/test
examples.zh: 标准化合同／设计／考试

senses.def: a person or thing that can always be used if needed, for example if somebody/something else is not available or if there is an emergency

examples.en: I always keep a pizza in the freezer as a standby.
examples.zh: 我总会在冰箱里放一个比萨饼以备不时之需。

examples.en: a standby electricity generator
examples.zh: 备用发电机

examples.en: Wilson has been called into the squad as a standby.
examples.zh: 威尔逊已被征召入队作为替补。

examples.en: A dark suit is a useful standby for any formal occasion.
examples.zh: 深色西装是任何正式场合的有用备用品。

senses.def: ready to do something immediately if needed or asked
senses.zh: 随时可以投入行动；处于待命状态；招之即来

examples.en: The emergency services were put on standby after a bomb warning.
examples.zh: 接到炸弹警报后，各应急服务机构进入待命状态。

examples.en: As the level of the water rose, villages were put on evacuation standby.
examples.zh: 随着水位上升，村庄进入疏散待命状态。

examples.en: The troops are on 24-hour standby (= ready to move at any time of the day or night).
examples.zh: 部队待命24小时（接到命令后24小时内可行动）。

senses.def: ready to travel or go somewhere if a ticket or something that is needed suddenly becomes available
senses.zh: 候补座位（如临时有票或具备其他必要条件便可立即出发的）

examples.en: He was put on standby for the flight to New York.
examples.zh: 这班飞往纽约的班机，他候补待位。

senses.def: a standby
senses.zh: （机票、音乐会门票等）最后时刻出售的

senses.def: ready to do something immediately if needed or asked
senses.zh: 随时可以投入行动；处于待命状态；招之即来

examples.zh: 接到炸弹警报后，各应急服务机构进入待命状态。

examples.en: As the level of the water rose, villages were put on evacuation standby.
examples.zh: 随着水位上升，村庄进入疏散待命状态。

examples.en: The troops are on 24-hour standby (= ready to move at any time of the day or night).
examples.zh: 部队待命24小时（接到命令后24小时内可行动）。

senses.def: ready to travel or go somewhere if a ticket or something that is needed suddenly becomes available
senses.zh: 候补座位（如临时有票或具备其他必要条件便可立即出发的）

examples.en: He was put on standby for the flight to New York.
examples.zh: 这班飞往纽约的班机，他候补待位。

senses.def: a person who is standing, for example in a bus or at a concert
senses.zh: 站立者；站立乘客；站票观众

senses.def: a situation in which the referee
senses.zh: 强制性数八，站立数八（一名拳击手未被击倒但似乎无法继续比赛的情况下，裁判中断比赛并进行数秒，直至数到八）

senses.def: an instruction that you give to your bank to pay somebody a fixed amount of money from your account on the same day each week/month, etc.
senses.zh: （客户给银行的）定期支付指示，经常性支付授权

examples.en: to set up a standing order
examples.zh: 设定经常性支付授权

examples.en: to pay by standing order
examples.zh: 采用定期转账的方式付款

senses.def: an order for something that is repeated every week, month, etc.
senses.zh: 长期协议订单；长期订购

examples.en: The restaurant placed a standing order for a side of beef every month.
examples.zh: 餐厅每个月都会定期订购一份牛肉。

senses.def: a military order that must always be obeyed

examples.en: We had a standing order never to go out on patrol alone.
examples.zh: 我们有一个长期命令，绝对不能单独外出巡逻。

senses.def: a rule that says how a parliament, committee, etc. should operate
senses.zh: （议会、委员会等的）议事规则，工作规定

examples.en: The council's standing orders require you to withdraw from the meeting while the matter is discussed.
examples.zh: 理事会的常规命令要求您在讨论此事时退出会议。

senses.def: space for people to stand in, especially in a theatre, sports ground, etc.
senses.zh: （尤指剧场、体育场等）站立的空间

examples.en: standing room for 12 000 supporters
examples.zh: 可容纳 12 000 名支持者站立的空间

examples.en: It was standing room only at the concert (= all the seats were sold).
examples.zh: 音乐会只剩站票了。

senses.def: a tall stone that was shaped and put in position by prehistoric
an area of water that is not moving, usually one that smells bad and is not good to drink

examples.en: Some people were drinking from polluted wells or standing water because they had no alternative.
examples.zh: 有些人因为别无选择而只能饮用受污染的井水或死水。

examples.en: Mosquitoes can breed in standing water.
examples.zh: 蚊子会在死水中滋生。

senses.def: very easy to notice because of being better, more impressive, etc. than others in a group

examples.en: the standout track on this album
examples.zh: 这张专辑里最突出的那首歌

senses.def: a person or thing that is very easy to notice because they are or it is better, more impressive, etc. than others in a group

examples.en: The songs on the album are good though none is a standout.
examples.zh: 专辑中的歌曲都不错，但没有哪一首是出彩的。

senses.def: a pipe that is connected to a public water supply and used to provide water outside a building
senses.zh: 公用水管（用于在户外公共场所供水）

senses.def: an opinion or a way of thinking about ideas or situations

examples.en: a political/theoretical standpoint
examples.zh: 政治／理论观点

examples.en: We must approach the problem from a different standpoint.
examples.zh: 我们必须从不同的立场来探讨这一问题。

examples.en: He is writing from the standpoint of someone who knows what life is like in prison.
examples.zh: 他从一个了解监狱生活的人的立场写作。

senses.def: a situation in which all activity or movement has stopped

examples.en: The security alert brought the airport to a standstill.
examples.zh: 安全警戒使机场陷入停顿状态。

examples.en: The roadworks brought the traffic to a standstill.
examples.zh: 道路维修使交通陷入了停顿。

examples.zh: 火车完全停了下来。

senses.zh: 斯坦利·鲍德温（Stanley Baldwin）：（1867-1947）英国保守党政客，在1920年代和1930年代三度出任总理。他的政府制定了击败1926年大罢工的法律。他还处理了爱德华八世国王退位的难题。他于1937年成为伯爵。

senses.def: a large British company, established in 1856, that sells stamps to people who collect them. It has a very large stamp shop in London, and organizes auctions
senses.zh: 斯坦利·吉本斯（Stanley Gibbons）：一家大型英国公司，成立于1856年，向出售邮票的人出售邮票。它在伦敦有一个非常大的邮票店，并组织拍卖（将公共物品卖给为他们提供最多钱的人的公共活动）。它还发布了其著名的邮票目录。

senses.def: (1919-2009) a teacher from Brooklyn
senses.zh: 斯坦利·卡普兰（Stanley Kaplan）：（ 1919-2009年）布鲁克林的一位老师，他创立了卡普兰组织。他首先在父母的家中教学生，其中许多人来自移民家庭。

senses.def: a very sharp knife with a short blade

senses.def: (1928-1999) a US film director, known for his great attention to detail. His best-known films include Spartacus
senses.zh: 斯坦利·库布里克（Stanley Kubrick）：（1928-1999）美国电影导演，以对细节的关注着称。他最著名的电影包括《斯巴达克斯》（1960年），《洛丽塔》（1962年），《奇异博士》（1963年），2001年：《太空漫游》（1968年），《发条橙子》（1971年），巴里·林登（1975年），《光辉》（1980年）和Eyes Wide Shut（1999）。

senses.def: (1915-2000) one of the most famous English football players of all time. He played on the wing
senses.zh: 斯坦利·马修斯（Stanley Matthews）：（1915-2000）有史以来最著名的英国足球运动员之一。他在机翼上打球，并以其将球带过对手并传到球门区域的技巧而闻名。还记得他在50岁之前一直是职业球员。他为英格兰效力了54次，并且是第一位当选骑士的足球运动员（1965年）。

senses.def: (1891-1959) an English artist. He is most famous for his unusual religious paintings, especially the series of pictures of Christ appearing at Cookham, the village on the Thames
senses.zh: （1891-1959）是一位英国艺术家。他以他非同寻常的宗教绘画而闻名，尤其是在出现在斯宾塞出生的伦敦以西的泰晤士河畔的库克姆（Cookham）上出现的一系列基督像。他的风格被描述为“原始写实主义”，因为他的许多画作看起来都是未经正式培训并试图以写实风格作画的艺术家的作品。1958年，他被任命为骑士。

senses.def: an airport in Essex
senses.zh: 斯坦斯特德机场：伦敦东北部埃塞克斯（Essex）的机场。直到1990年代，它还是一个很小的机场，成为伦敦的第三座机场。由诺曼·福斯特（Norman Foster）设计的新机场大楼于1991年开业。

senses.def: a US television series first shown on NBC
senses.zh: 《星际迷航》（Star Trek）：1960年代在美国全国广播公司（NBC）上首次亮相的美国电视连续剧，后来成为一个受人们欢迎的节目（对特定人群而言非常时髦）。这是关于“星际飞船”号航天飞机的，其船员包括詹姆斯·柯克船长，斯波克先生，“波恩斯”·麦考伊和“斯科特”·斯科特。他们在1979年至1991年之间制作了六部《星际迷航》电影。后来与不同演员的电视连续剧《星际迷航：下一代》于1988年开始，还有更多电影和其他衍生产品，例如旅行者号和深空9号。

senses.def: the main performer or person who provides entertainment in a show
a very successful US film (1977), directed by George Lucas, about a war in space. The story is about Luke Skywalker and Han Solo, who fight the evil Darth Vader
senses.zh: 《星球大战》：一部非常成功的美国电影（1977年），由乔治·卢卡斯执导，内容涉及太空战争。这个故事是关于卢克·天行者和汉·索罗，他们与邪恶的达斯·维达战斗以营救莱娅公主。相同的角色还出现在其他几部电影中，包括《帝国反击战》（1980），《绝地归来》（1983）和第1集（1999）。罗纳德·里根总统将“星球大战”一词用于他的战略防御计划，他还称苏联为“邪恶帝国”，这是电影中的用词。

examples.zh: 博物馆正努力摆脱其或多或少有点刻板的形象。

intro.en: These words all mean to look at somebody/​something for a long time.
intro.zh: 以上各词均含盯着看、凝视、注视之义。

items.def: to look at somebody/​something for a long time, especially with surprise or fear, or because you are thinking:
items.zh: 尤指吃惊、害怕或深思地盯着看、凝视、注视

examples.en: I screamed and everyone stared.
examples.zh: 我尖叫一声，众人都盯着我看。

items.def: (rather formal) to look steadily at somebody/​something for a long time, especially with surprise or love, or because you are thinking:
items.zh: 尤指吃惊、爱恋或深思地凝视、注视、盯着

examples.zh: 我们都惊异地注视着马可。

items.zh: 尤指看不清楚时仔细看、端详

examples.en: I looked at her and she glared stonily back.
examples.zh: 我看了她一眼，她便冷冷地回瞪我。

intro.en: These are all words for an act of looking, when you turn your eyes in a particular direction.
intro.zh: 以上各词均表示看的动作。

items.zh: 指看、瞧

examples.en: Here, have a look at this.
examples.zh: 来，看一看这个。

examples.zh: 她偷偷看了看表。

examples.en: She felt embarrassed under his steady gaze.
examples.zh: 她在他凝视的目光下感到很尴尬。

examples.en: She gave the officer a blank stare and shrugged her shoulders.
examples.zh: 她面无表情地盯着那个军官，耸了耸肩。

items.def: a look at somebody/​something for a very short time, when you do not see the person or thing completely:
items.zh: 指一瞥、一看

examples.en: He caught a glimpse of her in the crowd.
examples.zh: 他在人群里一眼瞥见了她。

items.def: a long, angry look at somebody/​something:
items.zh: 指长久的怒视、瞪眼

examples.en: She fixed her questioner with a hostile glare.
examples.zh: 她带着敌意瞪着向她提问的人。

senses.def: to look into somebody’s eyes for a long time until they feel embarrassed and are forced to look a way
