examples.en: The idea is to increase ‘stickiness’—the time a customer spends on the site.
examples.zh: 这个想法是为了增加“粘性”——客户在网站上花费的时间。

senses.def: a piece of material that can be stuck to the skin to protect a small wound or cut; this material
something that people do not agree on and that prevents progress in a discussion

examples.en: This was one of the major sticking points in the negotiations.
examples.zh: 这是谈判中主要的难点之一。

senses.def: a small freshwater
a person who thinks that a particular quality or type of behaviour is very important and expects other people to think and behave in the same way
senses.zh: 非常看重（某品质或行为）的人

examples.en: a stickler for punctuality
examples.zh: 非常注重守时的人

senses.def: an attractive pin that is worn on a tie to keep it in place, or as a piece of jewellery
made of or covered in a substance that sticks to things that touch it

examples.en: sticky fingers covered in jam
examples.zh: 粘满果酱的黏糊糊的手指

examples.en: There's a dish of mango with sweet sticky rice.
examples.zh: 有一道菜是芒果甜糯米饭。

examples.en: Stir in the milk to make a soft but not sticky dough.
examples.zh: 把牛奶搅进去，和成软而不黏的面团。

examples.en: Her arms were covered in a sticky substance that could only be blood.
examples.zh: 她的手臂沾满了粘稠的物质，那只能是血。

senses.def: with glue

examples.en: sticky tape
examples.zh: 透明胶带

senses.def: hot and slightly wet

examples.en: a sticky, humid afternoon
examples.zh: 一个粘稠潮湿的下午

examples.en: The air was hot and sticky.
examples.zh: 空气湿热难耐。

senses.def: feeling hot and uncomfortable

examples.en: She felt hot and sticky after six hours on the bus.
examples.zh: 坐了六个小时后，她感到又热又粘。

senses.def: difficult or unpleasant
senses.zh: 难办的；棘手的；让人为难的

examples.en: I always seem to get into sticky situations on holiday.
examples.zh: 我好像总是在假期里陷入窘境。

examples.en: Their relationship is going through a sticky patch and they’ve decided to have counselling.
examples.zh: 他们的关系正经历一个棘手的时期，他们决定接受咨询。

senses.def: so interesting and well organized that the people who visit it stay there for a long time
senses.zh: 用户黏着度高的；富有吸引力的

senses.def: something unpleasant that happens to somebody, for example punishment or a violent death, usually because of their own actions
senses.zh: 不愉快的结局；可悲的下场

examples.en: He'll come to a sticky end one of these days if he carries on like that.
examples.zh: 如果他继续那样下去，总有一天会落得个可悲的下场。

senses.def: to be likely to steal something
senses.zh: 好偷东西的；有顺手牵羊的毛病

senses.def: a difficult situation
a small piece of sticky paper that you use for writing a note on, and that can be easily removed

examples.en: Never write your password on a sticky note!
examples.zh: 千万不要将密码写到便利贴上！

senses.def: something unpleasant that happens to somebody, for example punishment or a violent death, usually because of their own actions
senses.zh: 不愉快的结局；可悲的下场

examples.en: He'll come to a sticky end one of these days if he carries on like that.
examples.zh: 如果他继续那样下去，总有一天会落得个可悲的下场。

senses.def: to be likely to steal something
senses.zh: 好偷东西的；有顺手牵羊的毛病

senses.def: a difficult situation
a type of rice grown especially in South-East Asia, which is sticky when cooked

examples.en: Sticky rice is much prized in Laos and is considered to be good for health.
examples.zh: 糯米在老挝很受重视，被认为对健康有益。

senses.def: clear plastic tape that is sticky on one side, used for sticking things together
a cake made with dates

examples.en: I had sticky toffee pudding for dessert, and it was really filling!
examples.zh: 我吃了粘稠的太妃糖布丁作为甜点，真的很饱！

senses.def: to try to find out information about other people's private lives in a way that is annoying or rude

examples.en: I don't mean to stickybeak, but when is he going to leave?
examples.zh: 我不是要多管闲事，但是他什么时候要离开呢？

senses.def: a person who tries to find out information about other people’s private lives in a way that is annoying or rude
senses.zh: 爱打听的人；好探听隐私的人；包打听

senses.def: difficult to bend or move

examples.en: a sheet of stiff black cardboard
examples.zh: 一张黑色硬纸板

examples.en: Scrub away any residue with a stiff brush.
examples.zh: 用硬刷子把残留物擦洗掉。

examples.en: The windows were stiff and she couldn't get them open.
examples.zh: 窗户紧，她开不了。

senses.group: difficult to bend/move 不易弯曲／活动

senses.def: when a person or a part of their body is stiff

examples.en: I'm really stiff after that bike ride yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天骑了那趟自行车，我觉得浑身酸痛。

examples.en: I've got a stiff neck.
examples.zh: 我脖子发僵。

senses.def: thick; difficult to stir

examples.en: Whisk the egg whites until stiff.
examples.zh: 把蛋清打稠。

senses.def: more difficult or severe than usual
senses.zh: 困难的；艰难的；严厉的；激烈的

examples.en: It was a stiff climb to the top of the hill.
examples.zh: 费了好大劲才爬到山顶。

examples.en: The company faces stiff competition from its rivals.
examples.zh: 公司遇到对手的激烈竞争。

examples.en: The new proposals have met with stiff opposition.
examples.zh: 新提案遭到强烈的反对。

examples.en: She offered stiff resistance to a thief attempting to snatch her bag.
examples.zh: 当小偷试图抢走她的包时，她进行了坚决的抵抗。

examples.en: Firms face stiff penalties for breaking the rules.
examples.zh: 公司违反规则要受重罚。

examples.en: a stiff breeze/wind (= one that blows strongly)
examples.zh: 强风

senses.def: not friendly or relaxed

examples.en: The speech he made to welcome them was stiff and formal.
examples.zh: 他那番欢迎他们的话讲得生硬刻板。

senses.def: costing a lot or too much

examples.en: There's a stiff $30 entrance fee to the exhibition.
examples.zh: 展览会的入场费高达 30 美元。

senses.def: strong; containing a lot of alcohol

examples.en: a stiff whisky
examples.zh: 烈性威士忌

examples.en: ‘What you need is a stiff drink,’ he told her.
examples.zh: “你需要的是一杯烈酒，”他告诉她。

senses.def: to keep calm and hide your feelings when you are in pain or in a difficult situation
senses.zh: （面对痛苦或困境）不动声色，沉着而不外露

examples.en: He was taught to keep a stiff upper lip and never to cry in public.
examples.zh: 他被教导要保持​​上嘴唇紧绷，永远不要在公共场合哭泣。

examples.en: Their reaction contrasts sharply with the stiff upper lip of the English.
examples.zh: 他们的反应与英国人的僵硬的上唇形成鲜明对比。

senses.def: very much; to an extreme degree

examples.en: be bored/scared/worried stiff
examples.zh: 非常厌烦／害怕／担心

senses.def: very cold and hard because the water has become ice

examples.en: The clothes on the washing line were frozen stiff.
examples.zh: 挂在晾衣绳上的衣服冻硬了。

examples.en: I came home from the game frozen stiff (= very cold).
examples.zh: 我看完比赛回到家里，都快冻僵了。

senses.def: the body of a dead person
to cheat somebody or not pay them what you owe them, especially by not leaving any money as a tip
senses.zh: 诈骗；不还钱；（尤指）不给小费

examples.en: These people are taxed on the tips they make. When you stiff ’em, you cost them money.
examples.zh: 这些人根据自己的小费纳税。当你僵化他们时，你就损失了他们的钱。

senses.def: to keep calm and hide your feelings when you are in pain or in a difficult situation
senses.zh: （面对痛苦或困境）不动声色，沉着而不外露

examples.en: He was taught to keep a stiff upper lip and never to cry in public.
examples.zh: 他被教导要保持​​上嘴唇紧绷，永远不要在公共场合哭泣。

examples.en: Their reaction contrasts sharply with the stiff upper lip of the English.
examples.zh: 他们的反应与英国人的僵硬的上唇形成鲜明对比。

senses.def: to push away a player who is trying to stop you, with your arm straight
proud and refusing to change
to make yourself or part of your body straight and still, especially because you are angry or frightened
senses.zh: （使身体部位）变僵硬，变僵直，绷紧（尤指因气愤或害怕）

examples.en: She stiffened with fear.
examples.zh: 她吓呆了。

examples.en: I stiffened my back and faced him.
examples.zh: 我挺直了腰杆面对着他。

senses.def: to become, or to make something become, difficult to bend or move

examples.en: My muscles had stiffened up after the climb.
examples.zh: 爬上去以后我肌肉都发僵了。

examples.en: stiffened muscles
examples.zh: 发僵的肌肉

senses.def: to make an attitude or idea stronger or more powerful; to become stronger

examples.en: The threat of punishment has only stiffened their resolve (= made them even more determined to do something).
examples.zh: 惩罚的威胁益发坚定了他们的决心。

senses.def: to make something, such as cloth, hard and unable to bend
in a way that is formal, and not friendly or relaxed

examples.en: ‘Thank you,’ she replied stiffly.
examples.zh: “谢谢。”她生硬地回答。

examples.en: She sat down stiffly on a chair by the wall, aware that they were looking at her.
examples.zh: 她僵硬地坐在靠墙的椅子上，意识到他们正在看着她。

senses.def: in a slow and uncomfortable way
senses.zh: 僵硬地：缓慢而不舒服地

examples.en: He got up stiffly to put more logs on the fire.
examples.zh: 他僵硬地站起来，去往火上添更多的木头。

senses.def: in a way that is hard and difficult to bend or move
senses.zh: 不易弯曲（或活动）的；硬的；挺的

examples.en: The key turned stiffly in the lock.
examples.zh: 钥匙在锁里转动不灵活。

senses.def: difficulty in moving because of pain in your muscles
senses.zh: 僵硬：由于肌肉疼痛而难以移动

examples.en: pain and stiffness in her legs
examples.zh: 她两腿的酸痛僵硬

senses.def: the fact of not being friendly or relaxed

examples.en: his military stiffness and reserve
examples.zh: 他的军事僵硬和矜持

senses.def: the fact of being hard and difficult to bend or move
senses.zh: 不易弯曲（或活动）的；硬的；挺的

examples.en: It's difficult to sew because of the stiffness of the fabric.
examples.zh: 由于布料的硬度，缝制起来很困难。

senses.def: the fact of being more difficult or severe than usual
senses.zh: 困难的；艰难的；严厉的；激烈的

examples.en: the stiffness of the competition
examples.zh: 竞争的激烈程度

senses.def: an erection
to prevent something from happening; to prevent a feeling from being expressed

examples.en: She managed to stifle a yawn.
examples.zh: 她忍住了哈欠。

examples.en: They hope the new rules will not stifle creativity.
examples.zh: 他们希望新规则不会压制创新。

examples.en: The government failed to stifle the unrest.
examples.zh: 政府没有制止住动乱。

examples.en: She pressed her hand against her mouth to stifle her sobs.
examples.zh: 她用手捂住嘴，忍住抽泣。

examples.en: Stifling her impatience, she waited another half an hour.
examples.zh: 她强忍着不耐烦，又等了半个小时。

senses.def: to feel unable to breathe, or to make somebody unable to breathe, because it is too hot and/or there is no fresh air
senses.zh: （使）窒息，无法自如地呼吸，感觉窒闷

examples.en: I felt I was stifling in the airless room.
examples.zh: 在那间闷气的房间里我感觉都快憋死了。

examples.en: Most of the victims were stifled by the fumes.
examples.zh: 多数受害者是因烟雾窒息而死的。

senses.def: in a way that makes you feel unable to breathe, because it is too hot and/or there is no fresh air
senses.zh: （使）窒息，无法自如地呼吸，感觉窒闷

examples.en: The room was stiflingly hot.
examples.zh: 房间里热得让人喘不上气来。

senses.def: negative feelings that people have about particular circumstances or characteristics that somebody may have

examples.en: the social stigma of alcoholism
examples.zh: 酗酒在社会上的恶名

examples.en: There is no longer any stigma attached to being divorced.
examples.zh: 离婚不再是什么丢脸的事。

senses.def: the part in the middle of a flower where pollen
marks that look like the wounds made by nails on the body of Jesus Christ, believed by some Christians to have appeared as holy marks on the bodies of some saints
senses.zh: 圣伤，圣痕（据信出现在某些圣徒身上，与耶稣身上钉子留下的伤痕相似）

senses.def: the act of describing or considering somebody/something in a way that unfairly suggests that they are bad or do not deserve respect

examples.en: Such headlines result in the stigmatization of entire communities.
examples.zh: 此类头条新闻导致整个社区受到污名化。

senses.def: to describe or consider somebody/something in a way that unfairly suggests that they are bad or do not deserve respect
a set of steps that help people climb over a fence or gate in a field, etc.
senses.zh: （供人翻越田地等处所设的围栏、栅栏门等的）台阶，梯磴

senses.def: a shoe with a very high narrow heel; the heel on such a shoe
a small knife with a narrow pointed blade
continuing until a particular point in time and not finishing

examples.en: I am very happy that you all are still alive and well.
examples.zh: 我很高兴你们都还健在。

examples.en: Tickets are still available for the 8 o'clock performance.
examples.zh: 8 点演出的票还有。

examples.en: He's still very young and has a lot to learn.
examples.zh: 他还年轻，要学的还很多。

examples.en: She still has a chance to win the title.
examples.zh: 她还有赢得冠军的机会。

examples.en: If you still need help next week, contact me.
examples.zh: 如果下周你还需要帮助，就联系我。

examples.en: I wrote to them last month and I'm still waiting for a reply.
examples.zh: 我上个月给他们写了信，到现在还在等回音。

examples.en: There's still time to change your mind.
examples.zh: 你还有时间改变主意。

senses.def: despite what has just been said

examples.en: Although he promised faithfully to come, I still didn't think he would.
examples.zh: 尽管他忠实地答应会来，但我仍然认为他不会来。

examples.en: We searched everywhere but we still couldn't find it.
examples.zh: 我们四处找，但还是没找到。

examples.en: The weather was cold and wet. Still, we had a great time.
examples.zh: 天气又冷又潮，不过我们仍旧玩得很开心。

examples.en: I know it's not rational, but I still feel terribly guilty.
examples.zh: 我知道这很不理智，但我还是非常内疚。

examples.en: He was wounded but he was still able to paint.
examples.zh: 他受了伤，但仍能作画。

senses.def: used for making a comparison stronger

examples.en: The next day was warmer still.
examples.zh: 第二天更暖和了。

examples.en: If you can manage to get two tickets that's better still.
examples.zh: 要是你能设法弄到两张票，那就更好了。

senses.def: even more

examples.en: There was still more bad news to come.
examples.zh: 随后还传来了其他的坏消息。

senses.def: used to say that it is too soon to be sure how a situation will develop

examples.en: It's still early days. We don't know if the play will be a success.
examples.zh: 现在还为时尚早。不知道这部剧能否成功。

senses.def: and certainly not

examples.en: No explanation was offered, still less an apology.
examples.zh: 连个解释都不给，就更不用说道歉了。

examples.en: He’s too shy to ask a stranger the time, much less speak to a room full of people.
examples.zh: 他太害羞了，不敢向陌生人询问时间，更不用说和一屋子人说话了。

senses.def: not moving; calm and quiet
senses.zh: 静止的；平静的；安静的；寂静的

examples.en: A fallen tree floated in the still water.
examples.zh: 一棵倒下的树漂浮在静止的水中。

examples.en: Keep still while I brush your hair.
examples.zh: 我给你梳头时你不要动。

examples.en: The kids found it hard to stay still.
examples.zh: 孩子们觉得待着不动很难做到。

examples.en: Can't you sit still?
examples.zh: 你就不能老老实实坐一会儿吗？

examples.en: We stayed in a village where time has stood still (= life has not changed for many years).
examples.zh: 我们待在一个时间似乎凝滞了的村子里。

senses.def: a still

examples.en: At this time cinema began to influence both still photography and painting.
examples.zh: 此时，电影开始影响静态摄影和绘画。

senses.def: with no wind

examples.en: a still summer’s day
examples.zh: 无风的夏日

examples.en: the still night air
examples.zh: 夜间宁静的空气

senses.def: not containing bubbles of gas; not fizzy
senses.zh: 不含碳酸气的；不起泡的

examples.en: still mineral water
examples.zh: 无汽矿泉水

senses.def: the voice of God or your conscience
senses.zh: 上帝的教示；良心的呼唤

senses.def: a person who seems to be quiet or shy may surprise you by knowing a lot or having deep feelings
senses.zh: 静水流深；木讷寡言者也许胸藏丘壑

senses.def: a photograph of a scene from a film or video
senses.zh: （电影或视频的）定格画面，剧照

examples.en: a publicity still from his new movie
examples.zh: 他的新电影的宣传剧照

examples.en: The police studied the stills from the security video.
examples.zh: 警方研究了安全视频中的剧照。

senses.def: a piece of equipment that is used for making strong alcoholic drinks

examples.en: a whisky still
examples.zh: 威士忌蒸馏器

senses.def: the time during the night when it is quiet and calm
senses.zh: 万籁俱寂的夜晚；夜阑人静

senses.def: to become calm and quiet; to make something calm and quiet

examples.en: The wind stilled.
examples.zh: 风停了。

examples.en: She spoke quietly to still the frightened child.
examples.zh: 她轻声安慰受到惊吓的孩子。

examples.en: to still somebody’s doubts/fears
examples.zh: 消除某人的疑虑／恐惧

examples.en: His words stilled my fears.
examples.zh: 他的话消除了我的恐惧。

items.idm: it's still early days | it's early days (yet)

senses.def: used to say that it is too soon to be sure how a situation will develop

examples.en: It's still early days. We don't know if the play will be a success.
examples.zh: 现在还为时尚早。不知道这部剧能否成功。

senses.def: and certainly not

examples.en: No explanation was offered, still less an apology.
examples.zh: 连个解释都不给，就更不用说道歉了。

examples.en: He’s too shy to ask a stranger the time, much less speak to a room full of people.
examples.zh: 他太害羞了，不敢向陌生人询问时间，更不用说和一屋子人说话了。

senses.def: the voice of God or your conscience
senses.zh: 上帝的教示；良心的呼唤

senses.def: a person who seems to be quiet or shy may surprise you by knowing a lot or having deep feelings
senses.zh: 静水流深；木讷寡言者也许胸藏丘壑

senses.def: the time during the night when it is quiet and calm
senses.zh: 万籁俱寂的夜晚；夜阑人静

senses.def: a person who seems to be quiet or shy may surprise you by knowing a lot or having deep feelings
senses.zh: 静水流深；木讷寡言者也许胸藏丘壑

senses.def: the art of painting or drawing arrangements of objects such as flowers, fruit, etc.; a painting, etc. like this

examples.en: She prefers still life to landscape painting.
examples.zh: 她喜欢静物画胜过风景画。

examples.en: a still life in oils
examples.zh: 一幅静物油画

senses.def: a birth in which the baby is born dead
born dead

examples.en: a stillborn baby
examples.zh: 死产儿

senses.def: not successful; not developing

examples.en: The proposal was stillborn.
examples.zh: 该提议胎死腹中。

senses.def: the quality of being quiet and not moving

examples.en: The sound of footsteps on the path broke the stillness.
examples.zh: 小路上的脚步声打破了宁静。

senses.def: one of a set of posts that support a building so that it is high above the ground or water
senses.zh: （支撑建筑物高出地面或水面的）桩子，支柱

examples.en: The houses are built on stilts to prevent flooding during the rainy season.
examples.zh: 这些房屋建在高跷上，以防止雨季洪水泛滥。

senses.def: one of two long pieces of wood that have a step on the side that you can stand on, so that you can walk above the ground

examples.en: a circus performer on stilts
examples.zh: 马戏团里踩高跷的演员

senses.def: not natural or relaxed; too formal

examples.en: We made stilted conversation for a few moments.
examples.zh: 我们不自然地客套了一会儿。

senses.def: if somebody speaks or writes stiltedly
senses.zh: 固执己见：如果某人说话或写作固执己见，他们的说话或写作方式自然或放松

senses.def: a type of English cheese with blue lines of mould
senses.zh: 斯蒂尔顿奶酪（一种英国干酪，有蓝色霉纹，味浓）

senses.def: a drug or substance that makes you feel more active and gives you more energy

examples.en: Coffee and tea are mild stimulants.
examples.zh: 咖啡和茶是轻度兴奋剂。

senses.def: an event or activity that encourages more activity
to make something develop or become more active; to encourage something

examples.en: The exhibition has stimulated interest in her work.
examples.zh: 展览增进了人们对她作品的兴趣。

examples.en: The article can be used to stimulate discussion among students.
examples.zh: 这篇文章可用来活跃学生的讨论。

examples.en: a government package designed to stimulate economic growth
examples.zh: 旨在刺激经济增长的政府一揽子计划

senses.def: to make somebody interested and excited about something

examples.en: Parents should give children books that stimulate them.
examples.zh: 父母应给孩子能启发他们的书。

examples.en: Both men and women are stimulated by erotic photos (= sexually).
examples.zh: 色情照片对男女都有刺激作用。

examples.en: The conference stimulated him to study the subject in more depth.
examples.zh: 这次会议促使他更深入地研究那个课题。

senses.def: to make a part of the body function
senses.zh: 促进（身体某部分）的功能

examples.en: The women were given fertility drugs to stimulate the ovaries.
examples.zh: 那些妇女得到了促进卵巢功能的生育药。

senses.def: the act of encouraging of something so that it develops or becomes more active
senses.zh: 刺激：鼓励某事物以使其发展或变得更加活跃的行为

examples.en: the stimulation of economic growth
examples.zh: 刺激经济增长

senses.def: the act of making somebody interested and excited about something by engaging their mind or their physical senses

examples.en: Kids' interest is often caught by visual stimulation.
examples.zh: 孩子们的兴趣往往是通过视觉刺激来吸引的。

examples.en: intellectual/sensory/sexual/physical stimulation
examples.zh: 智力/感官/性/身体刺激

senses.def: the act of making a part of the body function
senses.zh: 促进（身体某部分）的功能

examples.en: stimulation of the ovaries
examples.zh: 刺激卵巢

senses.def: something that helps somebody/something to develop better or more quickly
senses.zh: 促进因素；激励因素；刺激物

examples.en: Books provide children with ideas and a stimulus for play.
examples.zh: 书不仅给孩子们提供想法，而且使他们玩得更有意思。

examples.en: The new tax laws should act as a stimulus to exports.
examples.zh: 新税法应该能促进出口。

examples.en: This development also acted as a stimulus for Britain to modernize her air force.
examples.zh: 这一发展也刺激了英国空军现代化。

senses.def: something that produces a reaction in a human, an animal or a plant
senses.zh: （使生物产生反应的）刺激，刺激物

examples.en: sensory/verbal/visual stimuli
examples.zh: 感官／言语／视觉刺激

examples.en: The animals were conditioned to respond to auditory stimuli (= sounds).
examples.zh: 经过训练，那些动物对声音形成了条件反射。

senses.def: to touch your skin or make a very small hole in it so that you feel a sharp pain

examples.en: I was stung on the arm by a wasp.
examples.zh: 我的胳膊给黄蜂蜇了一下。

examples.en: Be careful of the nettles—they sting!
examples.zh: 小心给荨麻扎着，荨麻有刺！

senses.def: to feel, or to make somebody feel, a sharp pain in a part of their body

examples.en: I put some antiseptic on the cut and it stung for a moment.
examples.zh: 我在割破的地方抹了点抗菌剂，一时间十分刺痛。

examples.en: My eyes were stinging from the smoke.
examples.zh: 烟熏得我眼睛疼。

examples.en: Tears stung her eyes.
examples.zh: 她流泪流得眼睛疼。

senses.def: to make somebody feel angry or upset

examples.en: He was stung by their criticism.
examples.zh: 他们的批评使他心烦意乱。

examples.en: They launched a stinging attack on the government.
examples.zh: 他们对政府进行了猛烈的抨击。

examples.en: Their cruel remarks stung her into action.
examples.zh: 他们伤人的话激怒了她，使她采取了行动。

examples.en: He was stung into answering in his defence.
examples.zh: 他被激怒了，不得不作出回应为自己辩护。

senses.def: to charge somebody more money than they expected; to charge somebody who did not expect to pay
senses.zh: 对（某人）敲竹杠；敲诈；欺诈

examples.en: I got stung for a £100 meal.
examples.zh: 我挨宰了，一顿饭吃了 100 英镑。

examples.en: How much did they sting you for?
examples.zh: 他们骗了你多少钱？

senses.def: to borrow money from somebody

examples.en: Can I sting you for a couple of pounds?
examples.zh: 我可以蜇你几磅吗？

senses.def: the sharp pointed part of an insect or creature that can go into the skin leaving a small, painful and sometimes poisonous wound
senses.zh: （昆虫的）螫针，刺；（植物的）刺，刺毛

examples.en: the sting of a bee
examples.zh: 蜜蜂的螫针

examples.en: The scorpion has a sting in its tail.
examples.zh: 蝎子尾巴上有螫针。

examples.en: The scorpion has a sting that can be deadly.
examples.zh: 蝎子的螫针可以致命。

senses.def: a wound that is made when an insect, a creature or a plant stings

examples.en: A wasp or bee sting is painful but not necessarily serious.
examples.zh: 被黄蜂或蜜蜂蜇一下疼是疼，但未必碍事。

senses.def: any sharp pain in your body or mind

examples.en: the sting of salt in a wound
examples.zh: 伤口上撒盐引起的剧痛

examples.en: There was a sting of sarcasm in his voice.
examples.zh: 他的声音里带着一丝讽刺。

examples.en: She felt the sting of tears in her eyes.
examples.zh: 她感觉眼睛被泪水刺得发痛。

examples.en: He smiled at her, trying to take the sting out of his words (= trying to make the situation less painful or difficult).
examples.zh: 他冲她微微一笑，想使他的话不至于刺痛她。

examples.en: the hot sting of tears
examples.zh: 泪水引起的火辣辣的刺痛

senses.def: a clever secret plan by the police to catch criminals
senses.zh: （警察为抓捕罪犯而设的）圈套

examples.en: The FBI conducted a sting operation to catch heroin dealers in Detroit.
examples.zh: 联邦调查局设了圈套在底特律抓捕海洛因贩子。

examples.en: She was arrested in an undercover sting operation.
examples.zh: 她被秘密诱捕。

senses.def: a clever plan by criminals to cheat people out of a lot of money
an unpleasant feature that comes at the end of a story, an event, etc. and makes it less good, successful, etc.
an unpleasant feature that comes at the end of a story, an event, etc. and makes it less good, successful, etc.

synonyms.words: ache ▪ burn ▪ sting ▪ tingle ▪ itch ▪ throb

intro.en: These are all words that can be used when part of your body feels painful.
intro.zh: 以上各词均可指身体部位感到疼痛。

items.def: (of part of your body) to feel painful; (of an action) to cause pain:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）感到疼痛、（某一动作）引起疼痛

examples.en: My feet hurt.
examples.zh: 我脚疼。

items.def: to feel a continuous pain that is not severe:
items.zh: 指（持续地）疼痛、隐痛

examples.en: I’m aching all over.
examples.zh: 我周身疼痛。

items.def: (of part of your body) to feel very hot and painful:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）火辣辣地痛、发烫

examples.en: Our eyes were burning from the chemicals in the air.
examples.zh: 空气中弥漫的化学物质熏得我们的眼睛火辣辣地痛。

items.def: to make somebody feel a sharp burning pain or uncomfortable feeling in part of their body; (of part of your body) to feel this pain:
items.zh: 指（使）身体部位感觉刺痛、灼痛

examples.en: My eyes were stinging from the smoke.
examples.zh: 烟熏得我眼睛疼。

items.def: (of part of your body) to feel as if a lot of small sharp points are pushing into the skin there:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）感到刺痛

examples.en: The cold air made her face tingle.
examples.zh: 冷空气冻得她的脸发痛。

items.def: to have an uncomfortable feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch; to make your skin feel like this:
items.zh: （使）发痒

examples.en: I itch all over.
examples.zh: 我浑身痒。

items.def: (of part of your body) to feel pain as a series of regular beats:
items.zh: 指（身体部位）有规律地抽动、抽痛

examples.en: His head throbbed painfully.
examples.zh: 他的头一抽一跳地痛。

senses.def: the fact of not being willing to give something or enough of something; the fact of not being generous with money
senses.zh: 不愿给予某物或某物足够的事实；不慷慨地用货币代名词的意思（2）

senses.def: a wild plant with leaves that have pointed edges, are covered in fine hairs and sting
a large, wide, flat sea fish that has a long tail with a sharp sting
senses.zh: 魟鱼，魔鬼鱼（大型扁宽海鱼，尾长，有尖刺）

senses.def: not given or giving willingly; not generous, especially with money

examples.en: You're stingy! (= not willing to spend money)
examples.zh: 你真小气！

examples.en: Don't be so stingy with the cream!
examples.zh: 别那么舍不得放奶油！

examples.en: It was a stingy offer and he turned it down.
examples.zh: 报价很小气，他回绝了。

senses.def: to have a strong, unpleasant smell

examples.en: Her breath stank of garlic.
examples.zh: 她嘴里有股大蒜味。

examples.en: It stinks of smoke in here.
examples.zh: 这儿有股烟味。

examples.en: Don't go in there—it stinks.
examples.zh: 别进去——那里很臭。

senses.def: to seem very bad, unpleasant or dishonest
senses.zh: 让人觉得很糟糕；令人厌恶；似乎有不正当行为

examples.en: The whole business stank of corruption.
examples.zh: 这件事从头到尾都有腐败嫌疑。

examples.en: ‘What do you think of the idea?’ ‘I think it stinks.’
examples.zh: “你觉得这个主意怎么样？”“我觉得是个馊主意。”

senses.def: a very unpleasant smell

examples.en: The room was filled with the stink of sweat and urine.
examples.zh: 房间里弥漫着难闻的汗味和尿味。

senses.def: a lot of trouble and anger about something

examples.en: The whole business caused quite a stink.
examples.zh: 整件事引起了轩然大波。

examples.en: We'll kick up a stink (= complain a lot and cause trouble) if they try to close the school down.
examples.zh: 假如他们想关闭这所学校，我们就要大闹一场。

examples.en: The parents of the pupils say they'll kick up a stink if the school roof isn't repaired before the winter.
examples.zh: 学生家长说如果冬天以前学校屋顶还没修好的话，他们就要大闹一场。

senses.def: a container that produces a very bad smell when it is broken. Stink bombs
senses.zh: 臭弹（破碎时发出恶臭，用于恶作剧）

senses.def: to fill a place with a strong, unpleasant smell
senses.zh: 使充满臭味（或难闻气味）

examples.en: She stinks out the whole house with her incense and candles.
examples.zh: 她的香和蜡烛让整个房子都散发着臭味。

senses.def: a person or thing that is very unpleasant or difficult

examples.en: It’s been a real stinker of a day.
examples.zh: 这一天真让人受不了。

senses.def: having an extremely bad smell
extremely unpleasant or bad
senses.zh: 令人厌恶的；糟糕透顶的

senses.def: a period of time that you spend working somewhere or doing a particular activity
senses.zh: 从事某项工作（或活动）的时间

examples.en: He did a stint abroad early in his career.
examples.zh: 他刚参加工作时在国外干过一段时间。

examples.en: He hated his two-year stint in the Navy.
examples.zh: 他憎恨在海军服役的那两年。

examples.en: I’ve done my stint in the kitchen for today.
examples.zh: 我今天已经在厨房干完活了。

senses.def: to provide or use only a small amount of something

examples.en: She never stints on the food at her parties.
examples.zh: 她举办聚会吃的东西从不小气。

examples.en: We don't need to stint ourselves—have some more!
examples.zh: 我们没必要节省，多吃点！

senses.def: an amount of money that is paid regularly to somebody, especially a priest, as wages or money to live on
senses.zh: （尤指神职人员的）生活津贴，薪俸；献仪

examples.en: a monthly stipend
examples.zh: 月俸

examples.en: a summer internship with a small stipend
examples.zh: 薪水微薄的暑期实习

examples.en: The church pays him an annual stipend of $17 000.
examples.zh: 教会每年支付他17000美元的津贴。

senses.def: (in the UK) a magistrate
to paint or draw something using small marks

examples.en: a stippled effect
examples.zh: 点画效果。

senses.def: to state clearly and definitely that something must be done, or how it must be done

examples.en: A delivery date is stipulated in the contract.
examples.zh: 合同中规定了交货日期。

examples.en: The job advertisement stipulates that the applicant must have three years' experience.
examples.zh: 招聘广告明确要求应聘者必须有三年工作经验。

examples.en: The policy stipulates what form of consent is required.
examples.zh: 保险单规定了需要哪种知情同意书。

senses.def: a clear and definite statement that something must be done, or about how it must be done

examples.en: The only stipulation is that the topic you choose must be related to your studies.
examples.zh: 唯一的要求是你选择的题目必须和你的研究科目相关。

senses.def: to move a liquid or substance around, using a spoon or something similar, in order to mix it completely

examples.en: She stirred her tea.
examples.zh: 她搅了搅茶。

examples.en: Stir the paint before you use it.
examples.zh: 使用前先把油漆搅和一下。

examples.en: The vegetables are stirred into the rice while it is hot.
examples.zh: 趁米饭热时把蔬菜拌进去。

examples.en: Stir in the milk until the sauce thickens.
examples.zh: 把牛奶搅进去，直到酱汁变稠为止。

senses.def: to move, or to make something move, slightly

examples.en: She heard the baby stir in the next room.
examples.zh: 她听见婴儿在隔壁动弹。

examples.en: A slight breeze was stirring the branches.
examples.zh: 微风吹动着树枝。

examples.en: A noise stirred me from sleep.
examples.zh: 响声把我从睡梦中惊醒。

senses.def: to move, or to make somebody move, in order to do something

examples.en: You haven't stirred from that chair all evening!
examples.zh: 你坐在那把椅子上一晚上没动了！

examples.en: Come on, stir yourself. You're late!
examples.zh: 快，快走吧。你要迟到了！

examples.en: Their complaints have finally stirred him into action.
examples.zh: 他们的抱怨最终促使他采取了行动。

senses.def: to make somebody excited or make them feel something strongly

examples.en: It's a book that really stirs the imagination.
examples.zh: 这是一本真正能够激发想象力的书。

examples.en: She was stirred by his sad story.
examples.zh: 他那悲惨的故事打动了她。

examples.en: The preachers were stirred to new zeal.
examples.zh: 传教士们被激起了新的热情。

senses.def: to begin to be felt
senses.zh: 开始感到；逐渐产生；萌动；被唤起

examples.en: A feeling of guilt began to stir in her.
examples.zh: 她心里渐渐生出了内疚感。

examples.en: New optimism was stirring throughout the country.
examples.zh: 新的乐观情绪正在全国各地兴起。

senses.def: to try to cause trouble

examples.en: You're just stirring it!
examples.zh: 你这不是搬弄是非吗！

senses.def: to make somebody excited

examples.en: The atmosphere in a theatre never failed to stir her blood.
examples.zh: 剧院里的气氛总是让她热血沸腾。

senses.def: to begin to move; to hurry
excitement, anger or shock that is felt by a number of people
senses.zh: （一些人感到的）激动，愤怒，震动

examples.en: Her resignation caused quite a stir.
examples.zh: 她的辞职引起很大震动。

examples.en: The discovery caused something of a stir among physicists.
examples.zh: 这个发现在物理学家当中引起了几分轰动。

examples.en: There was quite a stir about the book.
examples.zh: 关于这本书有过一阵不小的轰动。

senses.def: the action of stirring

examples.en: Could you give the rice a stir?
examples.zh: 你把米饭搅一搅好吗？

senses.def: to make somebody excited

examples.en: The atmosphere in a theatre never failed to stir her blood.
examples.zh: 剧院里的气氛总是让她热血沸腾。

senses.def: to begin to move; to hurry

intro.en: These words all refer to substances, qualities, ideas or feelings combining or being combined.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指物质、品质、想法或情感的混合、掺和、融合。

items.def: to combine two or more substances, qualities, ideas or feelings, usually in a way that means they cannot easily be separated; to be combined in this way:
items.zh: 指（使）两种或以上物质、品质、想法或情感等混合、掺和、融合

examples.en: Mix all the ingredients together in a bowl.
examples.zh: 把所有的配料放入碗里混合在一起。

items.def: to move a liquid or substance around, using a spoon or something similar, in order to mix it completely:
items.zh: 指搅动、搅和、搅拌（液体或物质）

examples.en: She stirred her tea.
examples.zh: 她搅了搅茶。

items.def: to combine or be combined. Mingle can be used to talk about sounds, colours, feelings, ideas, qualities or substances. It is used in written English to talk about how a scene or event appears to somebody or how they experience it:
items.zh: mingle 可用以指声音、颜色、情感、想法、品质或物质等交织在一起，用于书面语表示对某一场景或事件的感受或经历

items.def: to mix two or more substances or flavours together; to be mixed together:
items.zh: 指（使）两种或以上物质或味道混合、掺和

examples.en: Blend the flour with the milk to make a smooth paste.
examples.zh: 把面粉和牛奶调成均匀的面糊。

senses.def: to make somebody excited

examples.en: The atmosphere in a theatre never failed to stir her blood.
examples.zh: 剧院里的气氛总是让她热血沸腾。

senses.def: to begin to move; to hurry
feeling unhappy or upset because of having spent a long time in the same place or situation and being prevented from leaving

examples.en: Some passengers go a little stir-crazy on long-haul flights.
examples.zh: 有些乘客在长途航班上会有点疯狂。

senses.def: a hot dish made by stir-frying
to cook thin pieces of vegetables or meat quickly by moving them around with a spoon, etc. in very hot oil

examples.en: stir-fried chicken
examples.zh: 油爆鸡

senses.def: to encourage somebody to do something; to make somebody feel they must do something
to make people feel strong emotions

examples.en: to stir up hatred
examples.zh: 激起仇恨

examples.en: Going back there stirred up a lot of memories for her.
examples.zh: 回到那里唤起了她很多回忆。

senses.def: to try to cause arguments or problems

examples.en: to stir up a debate
examples.zh: 挑起争论

examples.en: Whenever he's around, he always manages to stir up trouble.
examples.zh: 只要有他在，他就总要挑起点事来。

examples.en: We've got enough problems without you trying to stir things up.
examples.zh: 我们麻烦事儿已经够多的了，你就别再挑拨是非了。

senses.def: to make something move around in water or air

examples.en: The wind stirred up a lot of dust.
examples.zh: 风吹起大量尘土。

senses.def: a town in central Scotland. It has an important place in Scottish history. It has a very old castle where the kings and queens of Scotland used to live. Scottish forces defeated the English in two important battles, Stirling Bridge (1297) and the Battle of Bannockburn
senses.zh: 斯特灵（苏格兰中部城镇。在苏格兰历史上有重要地位。城中一座古堡曾是苏格兰国王和女王的王宫。苏格兰军队为控制城堡和跨越福斯河的桥梁，在斯特灵桥和班诺克本这两场重要的战役中击败了英格兰人）

senses.def: a person who likes causing trouble, especially between other people, by spreading secrets
senses.zh: 喜欢制造事端的人；（尤指）好拨弄是非者

senses.def: one of the metal rings that hang down on each side of a horse’s saddle

examples.en: He put his feet in the stirrups.
examples.zh: 他把脚伸进马镫里。

examples.en: She stood up in her stirrups to see where the others had gone.
examples.zh: 她脚踩马镫站起身来，想看看其他人都到哪里去了。

senses.def: the third of three small bones in the middle ear
senses.zh: 镫骨（三个最小的骨头之一，从耳膜携带声音到内耳中）

senses.def: tight trousers with a narrow piece of cloth at the bottom of each leg that fits under the foot
senses.zh: 女式紧身踩脚裤；健美裤

senses.def: one of the small lines of thread

examples.en: Try to keep the stitches small and straight.
examples.zh: 针脚要尽量缝得小而直。

examples.en: Put a stitch in the corner of the pocket to keep it in place.
examples.zh: 在口袋角那儿缝一针把它固定住。

senses.def: one of the small circles of wool that you make around the needle when you are knitting

examples.en: to drop a stitch (= to lose one that you have made)
examples.zh: 漏一针

examples.en: The knitting should be 120 stitches wide.
examples.zh: 编织宽度应为 120 针。

examples.en: to cast stitches on/off (= to add or remove them)
examples.zh: 缝上/拆下针

senses.def: a particular style of sewing

examples.en: chain stitch
examples.zh: 链式线步

examples.en: The edge was sewn with blanket stitch.
examples.zh: 边上用的是锁缝针法。

senses.def: a short piece of thread

examples.en: The cut needed eight stitches.
examples.zh: 这道伤口需要缝八针。

examples.en: I had six stitches in my foot after the accident.
examples.zh: 事故发生后我的脚缝了六针。

examples.en: I’m having my stitches out today.
examples.zh: 我的伤口今天拆线。

examples.en: I’m getting my stitches out today.
examples.zh: 我今天要拆线。

senses.def: a sudden pain in the side of your body, usually caused by running or laughing
senses.zh: 肋部突然的疼痛（多由奔跑或笑引起）；岔气

examples.en: Can we slow down? I've got a stitch.
examples.zh: 我们慢一点好不好？我岔气了。

senses.def: laughing a lot

examples.en: The play had us in stitches.
examples.zh: 那出戏让我们笑得前仰后合。

senses.def: to be wearing no clothes
it is better to deal with something immediately because if you wait it may become worse or more difficult and cause extra work
senses.zh: 及时缝一针能省九针；小洞及时补，免遭大洞苦

senses.def: to use a needle and thread

examples.en: Her wedding dress was stitched by hand.
examples.zh: 她的婚纱是手工缝制的。

examples.en: A pocket was stitched to the front of the jacket.

Britain's most famous prehistoric
senses.zh: 巨石阵：英国最著名的史前纪念碑，在英格兰南部的索尔兹伯里平原上。它由两个大的站立的石头圈组成，一个圈在另一个圈内。内圈由拱形组成，拱形是将一块石头铺在另外两个上面。其中有些下降了，但有些仍然存在。巨石阵建于公元前3000至1500年。没有人知道为什么要建造它，但是许多人认为这是研究恒星和行星或崇拜太阳的原因，因为穿过它中心的线会直接指向夏至或落日的位置在冬至。许多人去巨石阵举行盛夏的庆祝活动，现在这是一年中仅有的一次允许公众靠近石头的日子之一。巨石阵于1986年被列为世界遗产。

examples.zh: 你要尽量不让肌肉和关节太吃力。

examples.en: The ground here cannot take the strain of a large building.
examples.zh: 这块地承受不住大型建筑的压力。

examples.en: The cable has a 140kg breaking strain (= it will break when it is stretched or pulled by a force greater than this).
examples.zh: 这种缆索的断裂应变力为 140 千克。

senses.def: an injury to a part of your body, such as a muscle, that is caused by using it too much or by twisting

examples.en: a calf/groin/leg strain
examples.zh: 腿肚子／腹股沟／腿部拉伤

examples.en: muscle strain
examples.zh: 肌肉劳损

senses.def: a particular type of plant or animal, or of a disease caused by bacteria, etc.
senses.zh: （动、植物的）系，品系，品种；（疾病的）类型

examples.en: a new strain of mosquitoes resistant to the poison
examples.zh: 对这种毒药有抗药性的新品种蚊子

examples.en: This is only one of the many strains of the disease.
examples.zh: 这种病有许多类型，这只是其中之一。

examples.en: H5N1 is a strain of avian influenza.
examples.zh: H5N1 是一种禽流感病毒。

senses.group: type of plant/animal/disease 动植物／疾病种类

senses.def: a particular feature of the character of a person or group, or a quality in their manner
senses.zh: 个性特点；性格倾向；秉性

examples.en: He had a definite strain of snobbery in him.
examples.zh: 他这个人明显有一股势利小人的气味。

senses.def: the sound of music being played or sung

examples.en: She could hear the strains of Mozart through the window.
examples.zh: 她听见从窗户飘出的莫扎特的旋律。

examples.en: He heard the familiar strains of a tango coming from the club.
examples.zh: 他听到俱乐部里传来熟悉的探戈曲调。

senses.def: if a system or service creaks under the strain
senses.zh: 因负担过重而效率低下；由于压力过大而运转不灵

senses.def: to injure yourself or part of your body by making it work too hard

examples.en: to strain a muscle
examples.zh: 拉伤肌肉

examples.en: You’ll strain your back carrying those heavy suitcases.
examples.zh: 提着那些沉重的手提箱你会拉伤你的背部。

senses.def: to make an effort to do something, using all your mental or physical strength

examples.en: I strained my ears (= listened very hard) to catch what they were saying.
examples.zh: 我竖起耳朵去听他们在说些什么。

examples.en: Necks were strained for a glimpse of the stranger.
examples.zh: 大家伸长了脖子想看一看这个陌生人。

examples.en: People were straining to see what was going on.
examples.zh: 人们翘首企足看发生了什么事。

examples.en: He burst to the surface, straining for air.
examples.zh: 他冲出水面，使劲吸气。

examples.en: Bend gently to the left without straining.
examples.zh: 轻轻向左弯，不要用力。

senses.def: to try to make something do more than it is able to do

examples.en: The sudden influx of visitors is straining hotels in the town to the limit.
examples.zh: 游客突然涌入，城里的旅馆全都爆满。

examples.en: His constant complaints were straining our patience.
examples.zh: 他没完没了的抱怨让我们忍无可忍。

examples.en: The dispute has strained relations between the two countries (= made them difficult).
examples.zh: 这场争端使两国关系紧张起来。

examples.en: Her latest version of events strained their credulity still further.
examples.zh: 她对事件的最新说法进一步增加了他们的可信度。

senses.group: stretch to limit 使达到极限

senses.def: to push hard against something; to pull hard on something

examples.en: She strained against the ropes that held her.
examples.zh: 她使劲挣了挣拴着她的绳子。

examples.en: The dogs were straining at the leash, eager to get to the park.
examples.zh: 几条狗用力拽着皮带，急于要去公园。

senses.def: to pour food, etc. through something with very small holes in it, for example a sieve

examples.en: Use a colander to strain the vegetables.
examples.zh: 把蔬菜放在漏筐里控控水。

examples.en: Strain the juice from the cherries into a small saucepan.
examples.zh: 将樱桃汁滤入小锅中。

examples.en: Strain off any excess liquid.
examples.zh: 滤掉多余的液体。

senses.group: separate solid from liquid 过滤

examples.en: Like all youngsters, he's straining at the leash to leave home.
examples.zh: 跟所有年轻人一样，他也急于离开家生活。

senses.group: separate solid from liquid 过滤

intro.en: These are all words for the feelings of worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指生活上的心理压力、精神紧张。

items.def: difficulties and feelings of worry that are caused by the need to achieve something or to behave in a particular way:
items.zh: 指为达到某一目标或有某种行为表现而产生的心理压力、紧张

examples.en: She was unable to attend because of the pressures of work.
examples.zh: 由于工作紧张，她不能出席。

items.def: pressure or worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life:
items.zh: 精神压力；心理负担；紧张

examples.en: stress-related illnesses
examples.zh: 与精神压力有关的疾病

items.def: a feeling of worry and stress that makes it impossible to relax:
items.zh: 指情绪上的紧张、烦躁

examples.en: nervous tension
examples.zh: 神经紧张

items.def: pressure on somebody/​something because they have too much to do or manage; the problems or worry that this produces:
items.zh: 指压力、重负、重压之下出现的问题、担忧

examples.en: I found it a strain looking after four children.
examples.zh: 我觉得照料四个孩子挺累的。

synonyms.words: wound ▪ hurt ▪ bruise ▪ sprain ▪ pull ▪ strain

intro.en: These words all mean to harm yourself or somebody else physically, especially in an accident.
intro.zh: 以上各词主要指在事故中伤害、使受伤。

items.def: to harm yourself or somebody else physically, especially in an accident:
items.zh: 尤指在事故中伤害、使受伤

examples.en: He injured his knee playing hockey.
examples.zh: 他打曲棍球时弄伤了膝盖。

items.def: [often passive] (rather formal) to injure part of the body, especially by making a hole in the skin using a weapon:
items.zh: 指使身体受伤，尤指用武器伤害

examples.en: 50 people were seriously wounded in the attack.
examples.zh: 这次攻击中有 50 人受重伤。

items.def: to cause physical pain to somebody/​yourself; to injure somebody/​yourself:
items.zh: 指（使）疼痛、受伤

examples.en: Did you hurt yourself?
examples.zh: 你伤着自己了吗？

items.def: to make a blue, brown or purple mark (= a bruise) appear on the skin after somebody has fallen or been hit; to develop a bruise
items.zh: 指摔伤、撞伤、（使）出现瘀伤

items.def: to injure part of your body, especially your ankle, wrist or knee, by suddenly twisting it, causing pain and swelling
items.zh: 指扭伤（踝、腕、膝）

items.def: to damage a muscle, etc., by using too much force
items.zh: 指拉伤、扭伤（肌肉等）

items.def: to injure yourself or part of your body by making it work too hard:
items.zh: 指损伤、拉伤、扭伤

examples.en: Don’t strain your eyes by reading in poor light.
examples.zh: 别在光线不足的地方看书把眼睛给伤了。

examples.en: a tea strainer
examples.zh: 滤茶器

senses.zh: 海峡；（连结两大水域的）水道

examples.en: the Strait(s) of Gibraltar
examples.zh: 直布罗陀海峡

senses.def: a very difficult situation especially because of lack of money
senses.zh: （尤指经济拮据引起的）困境，境况窘迫

examples.en: The factory is in dire straits.
examples.zh: 工厂岌岌可危。

examples.en: She found herself in desperate financial straits.
examples.zh: 她发觉自己经济状况极为窘迫。

examples.en: The business is in dire financial straits.
examples.zh: 这家公司处于严重的财务困境中。

senses.def: having strict or old-fashioned ideas about people’s moral behaviour
senses.zh: （在道德行为上）拘谨保守的，古板的

senses.def: without enough money or as much money as there was before
senses.zh: 经济拮据的；穷困的；经济状况恶化的

examples.en: The family of eight was living in straitened circumstances.
examples.zh: 这个八口之家日子过得很拮据。

senses.def: a piece of clothing like a jacket with long arms that can be tied together, used to control a person who is violent and thought to be likely to harm themselves or others
senses.zh: 约束衣，紧身衣（有时用以束缚精神病患者）

senses.def: a thing that stops something from growing or developing

examples.en: The government has been caught in the straitjacket of debt.
examples.zh: 政府债务缠身。

senses.def: a single thin piece of thread

examples.en: He pulled at a loose strand of wool in his sweater.
examples.zh: 他拉扯毛衣里的一缕松散的羊毛。

examples.en: a few strands of dark hair
examples.zh: 几绺黑发

examples.en: She wore a single strand of pearls around her neck.
examples.zh: 她脖子上戴着单串珍珠。

senses.def: one of the different parts of an idea, a plan, a story, etc.
senses.zh: （观点、计划、故事等的）部分，方面

examples.en: We heard every strand of political opinion.
examples.zh: 各派的政治观点我们都听到了。

examples.en: The author draws the different strands of the plot together in the final chapter.
examples.zh: 作者在最后一章把不同的情节线索归拢到了一起。

senses.def: the land along the edge of the sea or ocean, or of a lake or river
to leave somebody in a place from which they have no way of leaving

examples.en: The strike left hundreds of tourists stranded at the airport.
examples.zh: 这场罢工使成百上千的游客滞留在机场。

senses.def: to make a boat, fish, whale

examples.en: The ship was stranded on a sandbank.
examples.zh: 船在沙洲上搁浅了。

senses.def: unusual or surprising, especially in a way that is difficult to understand

examples.en: A strange thing happened this morning.
examples.zh: 今天上午发生了一件怪事。

examples.en: He had a strange feeling that he had seen her somewhere before.
examples.zh: 他有种奇怪的感觉，好像以前在哪儿见过她。

examples.en: This may seem strange but it's the truth.
examples.zh: 这似乎很怪，却是事实。

examples.en: It’s strange (that) we haven’t heard from him.
examples.zh: 奇怪，我们一直没有他的消息。

examples.en: It's strange how childhood impressions linger.
examples.zh: 童年的印象经久不忘，真是不可思议。

examples.en: That's strange—the front door's open.
examples.zh: 怪事，正门开着。

examples.en: There was something strange about her eyes.
examples.zh: 她的眼睛有些异常。

examples.en: She was looking at me in a very strange way.
examples.zh: 她用十分异样的目光看着我。

examples.en: I'm looking forward to the exam, strange as it may seem.
examples.zh: 别人可能感到奇怪，我在盼望这场考试。

examples.en: Strange to say, I don't really enjoy television.
examples.zh: 说来奇怪，我不大喜欢看电视。

senses.def: not familiar because you have not been there before or met the person before

examples.en: I am still a stranger in a strange land.
examples.zh: 我仍然是异乡的异乡人。

examples.en: She woke up in a strange bed in a strange room.
examples.zh: 醒来时她发现自己躺在一个陌生房间里一张陌生的床上。

examples.en: Never accept lifts from strange men.
examples.zh: 千万别搭陌生男人的车。

examples.en: At first the place was strange to me.
examples.zh: 起先我对这个地方不熟悉。

senses.def: to not feel comfortable in a situation; to have an unpleasant physical feeling
senses.zh: 感觉不自在；感觉不舒服

examples.en: She felt strange sitting at her father's desk.
examples.zh: 坐在父亲的书桌前，她感觉不自在。

examples.en: It was terribly hot and I started to feel strange.
examples.zh: 酷热难当，我逐渐感到不舒服。

senses.def: used to show that ‘funny’ is being used with the meaning of ‘strange’
used to say that things that actually happen are often more surprising than stories that are invented
senses.zh: 现实比虚构更不可思议

senses.def: to not feel comfortable in a situation; to have an unpleasant physical feeling
senses.zh: 感觉不自在；感觉不舒服

examples.en: She felt strange sitting at her father's desk.
examples.zh: 坐在父亲的书桌前，她感觉不自在。

examples.en: It was terribly hot and I started to feel strange.
examples.zh: 酷热难当，我逐渐感到不舒服。

senses.def: used to show that ‘funny’ is being used with the meaning of ‘strange’
used to say that things that actually happen are often more surprising than stories that are invented
senses.zh: 现实比虚构更不可思议

senses.def: in an unusual or surprising way
senses.zh: 异常地；奇怪地；不可思议地

examples.en: She's been acting very strangely lately.
examples.zh: 近来她举止十分反常。

examples.en: The house was strangely quiet.
examples.zh: 房子里静得出奇。

examples.en: strangely shaped rocks
examples.zh: 奇形怪状的岩石

examples.en: Strangely enough, I don't feel at all nervous.
examples.zh: 真奇怪，我一点也不紧张。

senses.def: the fact of being unusual or surprising, especially in a way that is difficult to understand

examples.en: the sheer strangeness of this classic film
examples.zh: 这部经典电影的奇异之处

senses.def: the fact of not being familiar because you have not been there before or met the person before

examples.en: the strangeness of her surroundings
examples.zh: 她周围的环境很奇怪

senses.def: the risk to children from people that they do not know who might approach them, seen as something that children should be aware of
senses.zh: 不知道谁可能接近他们的人给儿童带来的风险，被视为儿童应该意识到的事情

examples.en: The children were all warned about stranger danger.
examples.zh: 孩子们都被警告注意陌生人的危险。

senses.def: a prison in central Manchester
senses.zh: 奇怪的路：在英格兰曼彻斯特中部的监狱。这是1990年的新闻，当时许多囚犯参加了针对那里恶劣条件的暴力抗议活动。一人死亡，监狱严重受损，必须将其重建。有关事件的报告建议对英国监狱进行重大改进。

senses.def: to kill somebody by pressing their throat and neck hard, especially with your fingers

examples.en: to strangle somebody to death
examples.zh: 把某人掐死

examples.en: The victim had been strangled with a scarf.
examples.zh: 受害人被人用围巾勒死了。

examples.en: Whenever he starts going on about football, I could cheerfully strangle him.
examples.zh: 每当他开始谈论足球时，我都会高兴地掐死他。

senses.def: to prevent something from growing or developing

examples.en: The current monetary policy is strangling the economy.
examples.zh: 现行货币政策抑制了经济的发展。

examples.en: ‘Oh, no!’ she cried, strangling a sob.
examples.zh: “哦，不！”她大声喊道，强忍着抽泣。

examples.en: This project should have been strangled at birth.
examples.zh: 这个项目早该被扼杀在摇篮里。

senses.def: a strong hold around somebody’s neck that makes it difficult for them to breathe

examples.en: Both arms were around his neck in a stranglehold.
examples.zh: 双臂掐住了他的脖子。

senses.def: complete control over something that makes it impossible for it to grow or develop well

examples.en: The company now had a stranglehold on the market.
examples.zh: 这家公司现在垄断了市场。

examples.en: attempts to break the US stranglehold on the industry
examples.zh: 试图打破美国对该行业的束缚

senses.def: a person who kills somebody by pressing their throat hard
made so narrow by pressure that blood etc. cannot pass through it

examples.en: a strangulated hernia
examples.zh: 绞窄性疝

senses.def: sounding as though the throat is being pressed hard, usually because of fear or worry
senses.zh: 嗓子被扼住似的，哽塞的（通常由于恐惧或担忧）

examples.en: He gave a strangulated squawk.
examples.zh: 他像嗓子被勒住似的嘎叫了一声。

senses.def: the act of killing somebody by pressing their throat hard; the state of being killed in this way

examples.en: to die of slow strangulation
examples.zh: 被缓慢勒死

senses.def: the act of preventing something from growing or developing

examples.en: the strangulation of the human spirit
examples.zh: 对人的精神压制

senses.def: a narrow piece of leather, cloth or other material that is used to fasten something, keep something in place, carry something or hold onto something

examples.en: the shoulder straps of her dress
examples.zh: 她连衣裙上的肩带

examples.en: a watch with a leather strap
examples.zh: 皮表带的手表

senses.def: to fasten somebody/something in place using a strap

examples.en: He strapped the knife to his leg.
examples.zh: 他把刀绑到腿上。

examples.en: Everything had to be strapped down to stop it from sliding around.
examples.zh: 所有东西必须绑定，免得来回滑动。

examples.en: Are you strapped in (= wearing a seat belt in a car, plane, etc.)?
examples.zh: 您系好安全带了吗？

senses.def: to wrap long, narrow pieces of material around a wound or an injured part of the body

examples.en: I have to keep my leg strapped up for six weeks.
examples.zh: 我的腿必须打六星期绷带。

senses.def: without straps
having straps

examples.en: white strappy sandals
examples.zh: 白色条带凉鞋

senses.def: a trick or plan that you use to gain an advantage or to trick an opponent
senses.zh: （为取胜或迷惑对手的）计策，计谋

examples.en: to adopt a clever stratagem
examples.zh: 采取巧妙的策略

examples.en: He deployed various cunning stratagems.
examples.zh: 他施展了各种狡猾的计谋。

senses.def: done as part of a plan that is meant to achieve a particular purpose or to gain an advantage
senses.zh: 根据全局而安排的；战略性的

examples.en: strategic planning
examples.zh: 全局性规划

examples.en: a strategic decision to sell off part of the business
examples.zh: 卖掉企业一部分的战略决策

examples.en: Cameras were set up at strategic points (= in places where they would be most effective) along the route.
examples.zh: 在沿途一些最佳位置架设了摄像机。

senses.def: connected with getting an advantage in a war or other military situation

examples.en: Malta was of vital strategic importance during the war.
examples.zh: 在那次战争中，马耳他的战略意义至为关键。

examples.en: a strategic alliance
examples.zh: 战略联盟

examples.en: the strategic bombing of communication centres
examples.zh: 对通讯中心的战略轰炸

senses.def: intended to be fired at an enemy’s country rather than used in a battle

examples.en: strategic missiles
examples.zh: 战略导弹

senses.def: in a way that is meant to achieve a particular purpose or to gain an advantage
senses.zh: 根据全局而安排的；战略性的

examples.en: a strategically placed microphone
examples.zh: 安放在最佳位置的麦克风

examples.en: to think strategically
examples.zh: 战略性地思考

senses.def: in a way that is connected with getting an advantage in a war or other military situation

examples.en: a strategically important target
examples.zh: 具有重大战略意义的目标

senses.def: a person who shows skill at planning things, especially military activities
senses.zh: 战略家；善于筹划部署的人

examples.en: a military strategist
examples.zh: 军事战略家

examples.en: a brilliant political strategist
examples.zh: 杰出的政治策略家

senses.def: a plan that is intended to achieve a particular purpose

examples.en: the government’s economic strategy
examples.zh: 政府的经济策略

examples.en: We need to devise an effective long-term strategy.
examples.zh: 我们需要设计一个有效的长期策略。

examples.en: Often, individuals employ multiple coping strategies because one particular strategy is not sufficient
examples.zh: 通常，个人会采用多种应对策略，因为一种特定策略是不够的

examples.en: to adopt/implement/pursue a strategy
examples.zh: 采取／贯彻／实施策略

examples.en: to develop a strategy for dealing with unemployment
examples.zh: 制订解决失业问题的对策

examples.en: It's all part of an overall strategy to gain promotion.
examples.zh: 这都不过是一个向上爬的完整计划的一部分。

senses.def: the process of planning something or putting a plan into operation
senses.zh: 策划；规划；部署；统筹安排

examples.en: Poor marketing strategy was blamed for the failure of the service to catch on.
examples.zh: 营销策略不当被认为是该业务没能打开局面的原因。

senses.def: the skill of planning the movements of armies in a battle or war; an example of doing this

examples.en: military strategy
examples.zh: 军事战略

examples.en: defence strategies

examples.zh: 街头运动是非正式的，基于人们想玩的任何运动。

examples.zh: 对于街上的男人和女人来说，真正重要的是什么？

examples.en: a charity that helps street children
examples.zh: 帮助流浪儿童的慈善组织

senses.def: ordinary clothes that people wear in public

examples.en: She took off her uniform and changed into street clothes.
examples.zh: 她脱下制服换上便装。

senses.def: a quality that makes somebody acceptable to young people, especially those who live in cities and have experienced the problems of real life
senses.zh: 街头信誉（尤指尝过生活艰辛的城市年轻人推崇的特质）

examples.en: Those clothes do nothing for your street cred.
examples.zh: 穿那些衣服对你的街头信誉可没好处。

examples.en: His spell in prison gained him a lot of street cred.
examples.zh: 他的铁窗生涯使他赢得了极高的街头声望。

senses.def: prepared or cooked food sold in a street or public place, to be eaten immediately

examples.en: The street food in the night markets is one of the highlights of any visit to the city.
examples.zh: 夜市的街头小吃是这座城市的亮点之一。

examples.en: The chef has created a menu inspired by traditional street foods.
examples.zh: 厨师根据传统街头食品的灵感创作了一份菜单。

senses.def: equipment such as road signs, street lights, etc. placed at the side of a road
senses.zh: 街道设施（如路标、路灯等）

senses.def: a game like ice hockey
senses.zh: 街头曲棍球：像冰球这样的游戏，在硬质表面上进行，穿着直排轮滑鞋

senses.def: a light at the top of a tall post in the street

examples.en: There are no street lights in the village.
examples.zh: 村里没有路灯。

examples.en: It was getting dark and the street lights had come on.
examples.zh: 天色渐暗，路灯已经亮了。

senses.def: an outdoor party, usually held on a street that has been closed to traffic, for all the people who live on the street or in the neighbourhood

examples.en: They celebrated the royal wedding with a huge street party.
examples.zh: 他们举办了一场盛大的街头派对来庆祝皇室婚礼。

senses.def: people who have no home and who live outside in a town

senses.zh: 适应都市生活的；有都市人的精明劲儿的

senses.zh: 都市生活诀窍，都市人的精明，街头智慧（应对大都市生活的困难和危险所需的知识和经验）

examples.en: drugs with a street value of over £1 million
examples.zh: 黑市价值超过 100 万英镑的毒品

examples.en: Beth is streets ahead of all the other students in her year.
examples.zh: 贝丝比同年级的所有其他学生领先很多。

senses.def: the appearance or a picture of a street or area of streets

examples.en: They will develop pedestrian-friendly streetscapes.
examples.zh: 他们将开发适合行人的街景。

examples.en: streetscape photos
examples.zh: 街景照

senses.def: a person working as a prostitute
informal clothes of a style worn by young people in cities, especially those who are fans of a particular type of music, sport, culture, etc.
senses.zh: 街头潮服（尤指迷恋某类音乐、体育运动、文化等的城市年轻人的衣着风格）

examples.en: He's well known for his trendy urban streetwear, mainly in black.
examples.zh: 他以其时尚的都市街头服饰（主要是黑色）而闻名。

examples.en: It's an Australian surf and streetwear brand.
examples.zh: 这是一个澳大利亚冲浪和街头服饰品牌。

senses.def: having the knowledge and experience that is needed to deal with the difficulties and dangers of life in a big city
senses.zh: 适应都市生活的；有都市人的精明劲儿的

examples.en: Kids seem much more streetwise these days.
examples.zh: 如今的孩子们比以前精明了。

senses.def: the quality of being physically strong

examples.en: He pushed against the rock with all his strength.
examples.zh: 他用全力推那块石头。

examples.en: It may take a few weeks for you to build up your strength again.
examples.zh: 可能需要几个星期你才能恢复体力。

examples.en: She gradually regained strength in her legs.
examples.zh: 她逐渐恢复了腿部力量。

examples.en: He had a physical strength that matched his outward appearance.
examples.zh: 他的体力与外形相称。

examples.en: She didn't have the strength to walk any further.
examples.zh: 她再也走不动了。

senses.group: being physically strong 强壮；牢固

senses.def: the ability that something has to resist force or hold heavy weights without breaking or being damaged

examples.en: the strength of a rope
examples.zh: 绳子的强度

examples.en: The panels are reinforced with steel for extra strength.
examples.zh: 面板采用钢材加固以增加强度。

senses.group: being physically strong 强壮；牢固

senses.def: the quality of being brave and determined in a difficult situation
senses.zh: 毅力；坚强决心；意志力量

examples.en: During this ordeal he was able to draw strength from his faith.
examples.zh: 在这次磨难中，他得以从自己的信仰中吸取力量。

examples.en: She has a remarkable inner strength.
examples.zh: 她有非凡的意志力。

examples.en: You have shown great strength of character.
examples.zh: 你表现得很有毅力。

senses.def: the power and influence that somebody/something has

examples.en: Political power depends upon economic strength.
examples.zh: 政治权力取决于经济实力。

examples.en: Their superior military strength gives them a huge advantage.
examples.zh: 他们军事实力较强，占有巨大优势。

examples.en: to negotiate from a position of strength
examples.zh: 以实力地位谈判

examples.en: The rally was intended to be a show of strength by the socialists.
examples.zh: 社会主义者组织这次集会意在显示力量。

senses.def: how strong or deeply felt an opinion or a feeling is

examples.en: the strength of public opinion
examples.zh: 公众舆论的强烈程度

examples.en: This view has recently gathered strength (= become stronger or more widely held).
examples.zh: 这种观点近来已为更多人接受了。

examples.en: I was surprised by the strength of her feelings.
examples.zh: 她感情之强烈让我吃惊。

examples.en: I have been overwhelmed by the strength of feeling that people have about this issue.
examples.zh: 人们对这个问题的强烈感受让我不知所措。

senses.def: a quality or an ability that a person or thing has that gives them an advantage

examples.en: The ability to keep calm is one of her many strengths.
examples.zh: 能够保持冷静是她的多项长处之一。

examples.en: the strengths and weaknesses of an argument
examples.zh: 一个论点的有力之处与薄弱之处

examples.en: The new weapon's strength lies in its accuracy.
examples.zh: 新武器的优点在于它的准确性。

senses.def: how strong a natural force or a signal is

examples.en: the strength of the sun
examples.zh: 太阳的强度

examples.en: wind strength
examples.zh: 风力

examples.en: the strength and direction of the tide
examples.zh: 潮水的流速与方向

examples.en: The phone company aims to improve signal strength within buildings.
examples.zh: 电话公司打算提升建筑物内部的信号强度。

senses.def: how strong a particular taste or substance is

examples.en: Add more curry powder depending on the strength required.
examples.zh: 按所要求的口味轻重再加点咖喱粉。

examples.en: a range of beers with different strengths (= with different amounts of alcohol in them)
examples.zh: 各种不同度数的啤酒

examples.en: a packet of double-strength mints
examples.zh: 一包双倍薄荷糖

examples.en: These wines vary in strength between 11° and 15°.
examples.zh: 这些酒的浓度在 11 度到 15 度之间。

senses.def: how strong a country’s currency is in relation to other countries’ currencies

examples.en: the relative strength of the dollar against the euro
examples.zh: 美元兑欧元的相对强弱

examples.en: The euro has continued to gain strength.
examples.zh: 欧元继续走强。

examples.en: the continuing strength of the pound
examples.zh: 英镑的持续坚挺

senses.def: the number of people in a group, a team or an organization

examples.en: The strength of the workforce is about to be doubled from 3 000 to 6 000.
examples.zh: 职工人数将翻一番，由 3 000 人增加到 6 000 人。

examples.en: The team will be back at full strength (= with all the best players) for the next match.
examples.zh: 这支队在下场比赛将恢复最佳的阵容。

examples.en: The Korean team was not up to strength for the final.
examples.zh: 韩国队决赛时人员不齐。

examples.en: The protesters turned out in strength (= in large numbers).
examples.zh: 抗议者大量聚集。

examples.en: These cuts have left the local police force under strength (= with fewer members than it needs).
examples.zh: 这几次裁减造成地方警力不足。

senses.group: number in group 群体人数多寡

senses.def: to become more and more successful
senses.zh: 越来越兴旺发达；不断取得成功

examples.en: Since her appointment the department has gone from strength to strength.
examples.zh: 自她上任以来，这个部门越来越兴旺了。

senses.group: number in group 群体人数多寡

senses.def: because somebody has been influenced or persuaded by something
senses.zh: 凭借（或根据）某事物；在某事物的影响下

examples.en: I got the job on the strength of your recommendation.
examples.zh: 由于您的推荐，我得到了那份工作。

examples.en: She hopes to secure a recording contract on the strength of these songs.
examples.zh: 她希望凭借这些歌曲获得录制合同。

senses.group: number in group 群体人数多寡

senses.def: the quality of being strong because you have a great variety of good people, ideas, etc. that can contribute to the success of something
senses.zh: 板凳深度深；团队无弱兵

examples.en: The French team does not have the strength in depth that the Australians have.
examples.zh: 法国队的板凳深度不如澳大利亚队。

senses.group: number in group 群体人数多寡

senses.def: being in a group gives you more power

examples.en: There's strength in numbers, so encourage your friends and family to join us.
examples.zh: 人多力量大，鼓励你的亲朋好友参加吧。

senses.group: number in group 群体人数多寡

senses.zh: （危难时的）可依靠的人，主心骨

examples.en: He was a tower of strength to his sisters when their father died.
examples.zh: 父亲死后，他成了姊妹们的支柱。

senses.zh: （危难时的）可依靠的人，主心骨

examples.zh: 父亲死后，他成了姊妹们的支柱。

examples.en: The French team does not have the strength in depth that the Australians have.
examples.zh: 法国队的板凳深度不如澳大利亚队。

senses.def: to become more powerful or effective; to make somebody/something more powerful or effective

examples.en: Her position in the party has strengthened in recent weeks.
examples.zh: 最近几个星期以来，她在党内的地位得到巩固。

examples.en: The move is clearly intended to strengthen the president's position as head of state.
examples.zh: 这一举措显然意在巩固总统作为国家元首的地位。

examples.en: The new evidence will strengthen their case.
examples.zh: 新的证据将使他们的论据更为充分。

examples.en: The new manager has strengthened the side by bringing in several younger players.
examples.zh: 新教练通过引进几名年轻队员加强了队伍的实力。

senses.def: to become physically stronger
senses.zh: 增强（体质等）；使变得强壮

examples.en: The exercises are designed to strengthen your stomach muscles.
examples.zh: 这些运动旨在增强你的腹部肌肉。

examples.en: Repairs are necessary to strengthen the bridge.
examples.zh: 这座桥需要加固。

senses.def: to make a feeling, an opinion or a relationship stronger; to become stronger
senses.zh: 加强，加深（感情、观念、关系）；（使）变得更深刻；（使）更坚定

examples.en: This temporary setback merely strengthened her resolve.
examples.zh: 这一时的挫折只加强了她的决心。

examples.en: Their attitude only strengthened his resolve to fight on.
examples.zh: 他们的态度反而使他坚定了继续战斗的决心。

examples.en: The experience of bereavement can strengthen family ties.
examples.zh: 丧亲之痛能够增强家人之间的感情。

examples.en: His determination only strengthened in the face of this opposition.
examples.zh: 在这样的反对之下，他的决心反而愈加坚定。

senses.def: to become stronger

examples.en: The wind had strengthened overnight.
examples.zh: 夜里，风更大了。

senses.def: to become stronger; to make a currency or an economy stronger

examples.en: Yesterday the pound strengthened against the dollar.
examples.zh: 昨天，英镑对美元的汇率上升了。

examples.en: The fall in unemployment is a sign of a strengthening economy.
examples.zh: 失业人数下降是经济走强的信号。

examples.en: The measures should help create jobs and strengthen the economy.
examples.zh: 这些措施应该会有助于创造就业机会、振兴经济。

senses.def: needing great effort and energy

examples.en: a strenuous climb
examples.zh: 艰难的攀登

examples.en: Avoid strenuous exercise immediately after a meal.
examples.zh: 刚吃完饭避免剧烈运动。

examples.en: How about a stroll in the park? Nothing too strenuous.
examples.zh: 在公园里散散步怎么样？不会太累的。

examples.en: Avoid tasks which require strenuous physical activity.
examples.zh: 避免从事繁重的体力活动。

senses.def: determined and showing great energy
senses.zh: 劲头十足的；奋力的；顽强的

examples.en: The ship went down although strenuous efforts were made to save it.
examples.zh: 尽管人们为营救这条船作了很大的努力，它还是沉了。

examples.en: The plan has met with strenuous opposition.
examples.zh: 该计划遭到了强烈反对。

senses.def: in a way that needs or uses great effort and energy

examples.en: He still works out strenuously every morning.
examples.zh: 他仍然每天早晨都刻苦锻炼。

senses.def: in a way that is determined and shows great energy

examples.en: The government strenuously denies the allegations.
examples.zh: 政府坚称那些说法不是事实。

senses.def: an infection of the throat
a type of bacteria, some types of which can cause serious infections and illnesses
pressure or worry caused by problems in somebody’s life or by having too much to do
senses.zh: 精神压力；心理负担；紧张

examples.en: emotional/mental stress
examples.zh: 情感／精神压力

examples.en: to suffer from stress
examples.zh: 有精神压力

examples.en: to relieve/reduce/alleviate stress
examples.zh: 缓解／降低／减轻压力

examples.en: Things can easily go wrong when people are under stress.
examples.zh: 人在压力之下，办事情就容易出差错。

examples.en: The incident has caused enormous stress and anxiety to my family.
examples.zh: 这件事给我的家人造成了巨大的压力和不安。

examples.en: We all sometimes struggle with the stresses and strains of daily life.
examples.zh: 我们有时都会与日常生活的压力和压力作斗争。

examples.en: How can we help young people cope with the stress of exams?
examples.zh: 如何帮助青少年应对考试压力？

examples.en: stress-related illnesses
examples.zh: 与精神压力有关的疾病

examples.en: stress management (= dealing with stress)
examples.zh: 对于压力的应对

examples.en: The release of the stress hormone cortisol is part of the human stress response.
examples.zh: 释放压力荷尔蒙皮质醇是人类的一种应激反应。

examples.en: Stress is often a factor in the development of long-term sickness.
examples.zh: 心理压力常常是形成长期疾病的一个因素。

examples.en: Few of us can understand the stresses of a job where an everyday mistake can cost lives.
examples.zh: 我们很少有人能够理解工作的压力，因为日常的错误可能会夺去生命。

senses.def: physical pressure put on something that can damage it or make it lose its shape

examples.en: When you have an injury you start putting stress on other parts of your body.
examples.zh: 一旦受伤，你便会让身体其他部位受力。

examples.en: Little is known about the effects of water stress on plants.
examples.zh: 人们对水分胁迫对植物的影响知之甚少。

examples.en: The building was condemned because of the damage caused by excessive heat stress.
examples.zh: 该建筑因过度热应激造成的损坏而受到谴责。

examples.en: Different organisms react differently to environmental stress (= damage to the environment caused by human activity or natural events).
examples.zh: 不同生物对环境刺激有不同的反应。

examples.en: a stress fracture of the foot (= one caused by such pressure)
examples.zh: 足部应力性骨折

senses.def: an extra force used when pronouncing a particular word or syllable

examples.en: We worked on pronunciation, stress and intonation.
examples.zh: 我们学习了语音、重读和语调。

examples.en: There's a stress on the second syllable.
examples.zh: 重音在第二音节。

examples.en: In ‘strategic’ the stress falls on the second syllable
examples.zh: strategic 一词的重音在第二音节。

senses.def: special importance given to something

examples.en: She lays great stress on punctuality.
examples.zh: 她十分注重守时。

examples.en: I think the company places too much stress on cost and not enough on quality.
examples.zh: 我认为公司对成本强调有余，而对质量重视不足。

senses.def: extra force used when making a particular sound in music
illness caused by difficult physical conditions
to give extra force to a word or syllable when saying it

examples.en: You stress the first syllable in ‘happiness’.
examples.zh: happiness 一词重读第一个音节。

examples.en: They might (and I stress the word 'might') do the right thing the next time.
examples.zh: 他们下次可能（我强调“可能”这个词）做正确的事。

senses.def: to emphasize a fact, an idea, etc.

examples.en: He stressed the importance of a good education.
examples.zh: 他强调了良好教育的重要性。

examples.en: She stressed the need for cooperation with the authorities.
examples.zh: 她强调了同当局合作的必要性。

examples.en: She is at pains to stress the cultural differences between the two countries.
examples.zh: 她极力强调两国之间的文化差异。

examples.en: I must stress that everything I've told you is strictly confidential.
examples.zh: 我必须强调，我告诉你的一切都要严加保密。

examples.en: I can't stress enough that security is of the highest importance.
examples.zh: 需要再三强调的是，安全是重中之重。

examples.en: ‘There is,’ Johnson stressed, ‘no real alternative.’
examples.zh: 约翰逊强调说：“别无真正能够替代的办法。”

examples.en: It must be stressed that this disease is very rare.
examples.zh: 必须着重指出，这种病非常罕见。

examples.en: I cannot stress too much how important this is.
examples.zh: 这事的重要性我怎么强调都不过分。

senses.def: to become or make somebody become too anxious or tired to be able to relax

examples.en: I just need to get some sleep and stop stressing.
examples.zh: 我只需要睡一会儿并停止压力。

examples.en: I try not to stress out when things go wrong.
examples.zh: 出问题时，我尽量不紧张。

examples.en: Driving in cities really stresses me (out).
examples.zh: 在城市里开车让我真的很紧张。

intro.en: These are all words for the feelings of worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life.
intro.zh: 以上各词均指生活上的心理压力、精神紧张。

items.def: difficulties and feelings of worry that are caused by the need to achieve something or to behave in a particular way:
items.zh: 指为达到某一目标或有某种行为表现而产生的心理压力、紧张

examples.en: She was unable to attend because of the pressures of work.
examples.zh: 由于工作紧张，她不能出席。

items.def: pressure or worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life:
items.zh: 精神压力；心理负担；紧张

examples.en: stress-related illnesses
examples.zh: 与精神压力有关的疾病

items.def: a feeling of worry and stress that makes it impossible to relax:
items.zh: 指情绪上的紧张、烦躁

examples.en: nervous tension
examples.zh: 神经紧张

items.def: pressure on somebody/​something because they have too much to do or manage; the problems or worry that this produces:
items.zh: 指压力、重负、重压之下出现的问题、担忧

examples.en: I found it a strain looking after four children.
examples.zh: 我觉得照料四个孩子挺累的。

intro.en: These words both mean to give extra force to a syllable, word or phrase when you are saying it.
intro.zh: 以上两词均含重读（音节、单词或短语）之义。

items.def: to give extra force to a word or syllable when saying it:
items.zh: 重读；用重音读

examples.en: You stress the first syllable in ‘happiness’.
examples.zh: happiness 一词重读第一个音节。

items.def: to give extra force to a word or phrase when saying it, especially to show that it is important:
items.zh: 指重读、强调（词或短语）、加强语气

examples.en: ‘Let nothing … nothing,’ he emphasized the word, ‘tempt you.’
examples.zh: 他强调说：“要抵制一切…一切的诱惑。”

senses.def: a hormone
senses.zh: 一种与身体对压力的反应有关的激素（=体内产生的影响细胞功能的化学物质）

examples.en: The drug works by blocking the action of stress hormones.
examples.zh: 该药物通过阻断应激激素的作用发挥作用。

senses.def: the symbols and used to show where the stress is placed on a particular word or syllable
having a regular rhythm of primary stresses
causing a lot of worry

examples.en: a stressful job
examples.zh: 造成沉重压力的工作

examples.en: It was a stressful time for all of us.
examples.zh: 对我们所有人来说，那是一段艰难的时期。

senses.def: to make something longer, wider or looser, for example by pulling it; to become longer, etc. in this way

examples.en: Is there any way of stretching shoes?
examples.zh: 有什么办法能把鞋撑大吗？

examples.en: Stop stretching your sleeves like that!
examples.zh: 别一个劲地抻袖子了！

examples.en: This sweater has stretched.
examples.zh: 这件毛衣给撑得变形了。

senses.def: to become bigger or longer when you pull it and return to its original shape when you stop

examples.en: The jeans stretch to provide a perfect fit.
examples.zh: 这条牛仔裤有弹性，可以完全贴身。

senses.def: to pull something so that it is smooth and tight

examples.en: Stretch the fabric tightly over the frame.
examples.zh: 把布在架子上绷紧。

examples.en: Striped awnings had been stretched across the courtyard.
examples.zh: 条纹雨篷被撑开架在院子上方。

examples.en: Make sure that the rope is stretched tight.
examples.zh: 务必要把绳子拉紧。

senses.def: to put your arms or legs out straight and contract your muscles

examples.en: He stretched and yawned lazily.
examples.zh: 他伸了伸懒腰，打了个哈欠。

examples.en: Andrea turned out the light and stretched full-length on the bed.
examples.zh: 安德烈亚关了灯，舒展全身躺到了床上。

examples.en: The exercises are designed to stretch and tone your leg muscles.
examples.zh: 这些活动目的在于伸展和增强你的腿部肌肉。

examples.en: It was impossible to bend or stretch my legs.
examples.zh: 我的腿无法弯曲或伸展。

senses.def: to put out an arm or a leg in order to reach something

examples.en: She stretched across the table for the butter.
examples.zh: 她伸手到桌子那头去拿黄油。

examples.en: She stretched up to reach the top shelf.
examples.zh: 她伸手向上去够顶层架子。

examples.en: I stretched out a hand and picked up the book.
examples.zh: 我伸出一只手，把书捡起来。

senses.group: reach with arm 伸手够着

senses.def: to spread over an area of land

examples.en: Fields and hills stretched out as far as we could see.
examples.zh: 放眼望去，田野山丘绵延不绝。

examples.en: The traffic jam seemed to stretch for miles.
examples.zh: 交通堵塞似乎绵延数英里。

examples.en: A line of cars stretched into the distance.
examples.zh: 车子的长龙一直排到很远。

examples.en: The flat landscape stretched to the horizon.
examples.zh: 平坦的风景一直延伸到地平线。

examples.en: Beyond the mountains stretches a vast desert.
examples.zh: 山峦后面是一片辽阔的沙漠。

senses.def: to continue over a period of time

examples.en: The town's history stretches back to before 1500.
examples.zh: 该镇的历史可以上溯到公元 1500 年以前。

examples.en: to stretch back years/decades/generations/centuries
examples.zh: 追溯到几年/几十年/几代人/几个世纪前

examples.en: The training stretches over a period of 16 months.
examples.zh: 培训持续16个月。

examples.en: Endless summer days stretched out before us.
examples.zh: 无尽的夏日在等待着我们。

examples.en: The talks look set to stretch into a second week.
examples.zh: 看来谈判十有八九要延续到下个星期了。

examples.en: The future stretched out endlessly in front of me.
examples.zh: 未来我前面的路还有很长很长。

senses.def: to be enough to buy or pay for something

examples.en: I need a new car, but my savings won't stretch to it.
examples.zh: 我需要一辆新车，但我的积蓄不够。

examples.en: There are lots of things I’d like to buy, but our budget just won’t stretch that far.
examples.zh: 我想买很多东西，但我们的预算不会那么长。

senses.def: to make use of a lot of your money, supplies, time, etc.

examples.en: The pandemic has stretched healthcare resources to the limit.
examples.zh: 大流行使医疗资源达到极限。

examples.en: We can't take on any more work—we're fully stretched as it is.
examples.zh: 我们不能再接受其他工作了，现在我们已经满负荷了。

examples.en: The budget is already stretched to breaking point.
examples.zh: 预算已经达到极限。

senses.def: to increase your lead over somebody in a game or competition

examples.en: A minute later, Kelly stretched their lead to eight points.
examples.zh: 一分钟后，凯莉把她们的领先优势扩大到了八分。

senses.def: to make use of all somebody’s skill, intelligence, etc.
senses.zh: 使竭尽所能；使全力以赴；使发挥出全部本领

examples.en: I need a job that will stretch me.
examples.zh: 我需要一份能让我充分发挥才智的工作。

examples.en: She was never really stretched at school.
examples.zh: 她在学校从来没有真正紧张过。

examples.en: The book really stretches your imagination.
examples.zh: 这本书确实拓展了你的想象力。

senses.def: to use something in a way that would not normally be considered fair, acceptable, etc.

examples.en: He admitted that he had maybe stretched the truth a little (= not been completely honest).
examples.zh: 他承认可能有点言过其实了。

examples.en: The play's plot stretches credulity to the limit.
examples.zh: 这出戏的剧情简直就是胡编滥造。

senses.def: to change the rules to suit a particular person or situation
senses.zh: 根据具体情况改变规则；通融

examples.en: Couldn't they just bend the rules and let us in without a ticket?
examples.zh: 难道他们就不能通融一下，让我们没票也进去吗？

senses.def: to go for a short walk after sitting for some time
senses.zh: （久坐之后）散散步，活动活动腿脚

examples.en: It was good to get out of the car and stretch our legs.
examples.zh: 我们下了车活动活动腿脚，真不错。

senses.def: to allow or do something that is not usually acceptable, especially because of a particular situation

examples.en: I was hoping they would stretch a point and let me stay on for a while.
examples.zh: 我希望他们能延长一点，让我继续呆一段时间。

senses.def: an area of land or water, especially a long one

examples.en: a particularly dangerous stretch of road
examples.zh: 特别危险的路段

examples.en: There are tailbacks along a 10-mile stretch of the motorway.
examples.zh: 高速公路上有 10 英里路段行驶缓慢。

examples.en: an unspoilt stretch of coastline
examples.zh: 一段未破坏原貌的海岸线

examples.en: You rarely see boats on this stretch of the river.
examples.zh: 这一河段船只罕见。

senses.group: area of land/water 土地；水域

senses.def: a continuous period of time

examples.en: They worked in four-hour stretches.
examples.zh: 他们工作四小时一班。

examples.en: She used to read for hours at a stretch (= without stopping).
examples.zh: 她以前看书常常连看几小时。

senses.group: period of time 一段时间

senses.def: a period of time that somebody spends in prison

examples.en: He did a ten-year stretch for fraud.
examples.zh: 他因欺诈罪服刑十年。

senses.group: period of time 一段时间

senses.def: an act of stretching out your arms or legs or your body and pulling the muscles tight; the state of being stretched

examples.en: We got out of the car and had a good stretch.
examples.zh: 我们下车好好舒展了一下身体。

examples.en: Only do these more difficult stretches when you are warmed up.
examples.zh: 要做了准备活动以后再做这些较难的伸展运动。

examples.en: Stay in this position and feel the stretch in your legs.
examples.zh: 保持这个姿势，体会腿部绷紧的感觉。

senses.def: the ability to be made longer or wider without breaking or tearing

examples.en: You need a material with plenty of stretch in it.
examples.zh: 你需要一种弹性很大的布料。

examples.zh: 弹力牛仔裤

senses.def: a straight part at the end of a racing track

examples.en: the finishing stretch
examples.zh: 最后的拉伸

examples.en: The campaign has entered its final stretch.
examples.zh: 竞选已进入最后冲刺阶段。

senses.def: using as much energy as possible, or the greatest possible amount of supplies
senses.zh: 竭尽全力；以最大财力物力

examples.en: Fire crews have been operating at full stretch.
examples.zh: 各消防队一直在全力以赴。

senses.def: used to say strongly that something is not true, even if you try to imagine or believe it
senses.zh: 任凭怎么想也不；再怎么说也不

examples.en: She could not, by any stretch of the imagination, be called beautiful.
examples.zh: 再怎么说，她也称不上漂亮。

examples.en: By no stretch of the imagination could the trip be described as relaxing.
examples.zh: 无论如何想象，这次旅行都不能用轻松来形容。

examples.zh: 他被人用担架抬走了。

examples.zh: 必须用担架抬的伤员

senses.zh: 担架：木制框架，布在该框架上展开并拉紧，准备绘画
